beats.title: The Funeral Leftovers
beats.modern: they served the funeral food at the wedding. THE SAME PLATTERS. two months apart. my uncle stole my mom AND he's a cheapskate.
beats.quote: Thrift, thrift, Horatio! The funeral bak’d meats Did coldly furnish forth the marriage tables.

beats.title: Something Rotten
beats.modern: Denmark is cooked. the whole server's corrupted.

beats.title: The Ghost Reveal
beats.modern: the night watch keeps clocking a figure on the wall. full armor. my DEAD FATHER'S walk. so tonight I pulled up, and it waved me away from the group for a one-on-one. chat. it's him. it's actually him. and the official snakebite story? fake. he was MURDERED.
beats.quote: Revenge his foul and most unnatural murder.

beats.title: Haste Me to Know It
beats.modern: say less. I must be on this revenge quest.
beats.quote: Haste me to know’t, that I, with wings as swift As meditation or the thoughts of love May sweep to my revenge.

beats.title: O My Prophetic Soul
beats.modern: I FUCKING KNEW IT. I CALLED IT. check the VOD chat, day one I said it was the uncle.
beats.quote: O my prophetic soul! Mine uncle!

beats.title: The Antic Disposition
beats.modern: listen up chat, I'm about to act SO unhinged. it's a bit. it's all a bit. do NOT break kayfabe.

beats.title: The Honeypot
beats.modern: Polonius has a THEORY, chat. the theory is I've gone mad from loving his daughter. the plan: release Ophelia into the lobby where I do my pacing, then hide with the king and watch the encounter. they are running a honeypot op on me. this family cannot stop hiding behind things.
beats.quote: At such a time I’ll loose my daughter to him.

beats.title: The Soliloquy Reflection
beats.modern: this actor just CRIED. real tears. over a queen that doesn't even EXIST. my dad got actually murdered and I've done jack shit for two months. I'm an NPC in my own revenge arc.
beats.quote: What’s Hecuba to him, or he to Hecuba, That he should weep for her?

beats.title: The Mousetrap
beats.modern: I can't just ask 'hey did you murder my dad.' so we're staging a play OF the murder with face cam on my uncle the whole time. Horatio, you're on reaction duty. if he flinches, CLIP IT.
beats.quote: The play’s the thing Wherein I’ll catch the conscience of the King.

beats.title: To Be or Not to Be
beats.modern: chat should I just kill myself? I'm so ready to rage quit... but nobody's ever respawned to drop a review of the death update. zero info. so I guess I keep suffering like a little bitch.
beats.quote: To be, or not to be, that is the question:

beats.title: The Cowardice Reflection
beats.modern: ran the numbers on my own brain, chat: 25% big brain plays, 75% being a fucking pussy. those are my stats.
beats.quote: Thus conscience does make cowards of us all,

beats.title: The Nunnery Breakup
beats.modern: we're done. delete your account. go join a convent. I'm blocking you on everything.
beats.quote: Get thee to a nunnery.

beats.title: The Prayer Scene
beats.modern: he's literally praying right now. I could end his whole career... but if he dies mid-prayer he respawns in HEAVEN?? no shot I'm giving this man the good ending. I'll grief him when he's sinning.

beats.title: The Curtain Incident
beats.modern: something moved behind the curtain so I took the shot. ...chat that was not a rat. that was my girlfriend's dad. F in chat for Polonius, my bad.
beats.quote: Dead for a ducat, dead!

beats.title: The Portrait Review
beats.modern: sat my mother down and would not let her leave. portrait review: my father, an actual god-tier king, next to the uncle, a mildewed ear of corn. 'THIS was your husband. and you swiped on THAT.' she's begging me to stop. then dad's ghost pops in MID-RANT with two notes: I'm behind on the revenge quest, and go easy on your mother. even the quest giver thinks I'm doing too much.
beats.quote: Here is your husband, like a mildew’d ear Blasting his wholesome brother.

beats.title: How All Occasions
beats.modern: this entire army is HYPED to die over a patch of grass worth five bucks, and I still haven't done ONE murder. everyone in this play is more locked in than me. actually embarrassing.

beats.title: Ophelia Unravels
beats.modern: news from the castle while they ship me off: Ophelia broke. she drifts through the halls singing about dead men and shrouds, handing flowers to the exact people who wrecked her. her father is dead behind a curtain and the boyfriend who did it got put on a boat. no jokes on this one, chat. this is my damage.
beats.quote: Good night, ladies; good night, sweet ladies; good night, good night.

beats.title: Laertes Kicks the Door
beats.modern: Laertes is BACK from Paris and he skipped every stage of grief except war. kicked the doors in with a mob chanting his name, told allegiance itself to go to hell, demanding answers about his father. bro speedran in one afternoon the quest I've been sitting on for months. genuinely embarrassing for me. respect.
beats.quote: Let come what comes; only I’ll be reveng’d Most throughly for my father.

beats.title: The Willow
beats.modern: she was hanging flower garlands on the willow over the brook and the branch snapped. the water took her. Ophelia is gone, chat. she never got her apology from me. not one word of it. take the nunnery clip down. take everything down.
beats.quote: Your sister’s drown’d, Laertes.

beats.title: The Skull Farmer
beats.modern: back in Denmark, and the first man I meet is digging a grave while SINGING, flipping old skulls out of the dirt like he's clearing inventory. I ask whose grave it is. 'mine, sir. I'm standing in it.' can't even be mad. the only honest man on this server works in the death business.
beats.quote: That skull had a tongue in it, and could sing once.

beats.title: The Letter Switcheroo
beats.modern: these two clowns escorted me to England carrying my execution order. so I rewrote it with THEIR names. don't run courier quests for my uncle. get griefed.

beats.title: Yorick
beats.modern: CHAT. I KNOW THIS SKULL. this is Yorick, he gave me piggyback rides when I was five. I am holding my babysitter's head right now. craziest lore drop of my life.
beats.quote: Alas, poor Yorick. I knew him, Horatio, a fellow of infinite jest, of most excellent fancy. He hath borne me on his back a thousand times;

beats.title: The Wager
beats.modern: a courtier named Osric just floated in under an enormous hat to announce the king has placed a BET on me: exhibition fencing, me against Laertes, six Barbary horses on the line. Laertes. whose father I killed. Horatio smells a setup. honestly? same. we're doing it anyway. whatever's coming was always coming, chat. lock in.
beats.quote: we defy augury. There’s a special providence in the fall of a sparrow.

beats.title: The Cup
beats.modern: MOM. MOM DO NOT DRINK THAT— ...she drank it. chat. chat she drank it.
beats.quote: It is the poison’d cup; it is too late.

beats.title: Fortinbras Ending
beats.modern: and then some Norwegian who did NOTHING all game walks in and takes the crown. biggest third-party of all time. bro looted an entire royal family.

beats.title: The Rest Is Silence
beats.modern: gg. stream's over. Horatio's got the channel.
beats.quote: The rest is silence.

beats.title: A Truth Universally Acknowledged
beats.modern: new stream, chat. rule one of my town: a rich single man moves in and every mother in ten miles instantly declares him the rightful property of one of her daughters. he hasn't unpacked. he has NO idea he's already engaged in five separate imaginations. welcome to Longbourn.
beats.quote: It is a truth universally acknowledged, that a single man in possession of a good fortune must be in want of a wife.

beats.title: Mom's Nerves
beats.modern: breaking news: a single guy with money rented the big house and mom has already married him to one of us. she just needs to pick which daughter. dad's entire contribution is roasting her nerves, which he calls his old friends of twenty years. five daughters, an inheritance that skips all of us, and mom running matchmaking like it's her full time job. it IS her full time job.
beats.quote: I have a high respect for your nerves. They are my old friends. I have heard you mention them with consideration these twenty years at least.”

beats.title: The Tolerable Incident
beats.modern: CLIP IT. this man looks at me, in my hearing range, and rates me 'tolerable.' TOLERABLE. not handsome enough to tempt HIM. sir, you have ten thousand a year and the personality of a damp wall. anyway I told everyone at the party and I tell it with a full damn reenactment now. it's my best material. he doesn't get to live this down.
beats.quote: “She is tolerable: but not handsome enough to tempt me; and I am in no humour at present to give consequence to young ladies who are slighted by other men.

beats.title: Jane Gets Two Dances
beats.modern: meanwhile Jane danced with Bingley TWICE. the only girl in the room he asked twice, chat. she's glowing, he's grinning, it's disgusting and I love it. mom narrated the whole thing at full commentary volume like it's a title match. Jane deserves every bit of this. Jane is the best person alive and that is not up for debate.

beats.title: Charlotte's Odds Take
beats.modern: my best friend just said, with her whole chest, that happiness in marriage is pure RNG. study his character for a year or marry him tomorrow, same odds. she says it's better to know as little as possible about the person beforehand. chat she is not joking. she never jokes about strategy. remember this take. it becomes extremely relevant.
beats.quote: Happiness in marriage is entirely a matter of chance.

beats.title: The Fine Eyes Leak
beats.modern: UPDATE. Mr. Tolerable got caught telling Caroline Bingley he's been meditating on a pretty woman's fine eyes. she starts fishing, ready to book a venue. he says MINE. Elizabeth Bennet's. she has been in damage control ever since and I am FEASTING. insults me in public, catches feelings in private. make it make sense, my guy.
beats.quote: I have been meditating on the very great pleasure which a pair of fine eyes in the face of a pretty woman can bestow.”

beats.title: The Mud Run
beats.modern: Jane got sick at the rich people's house, so I walked three miles of mud to go nurse her. arrived glowing and filthy. the sisters treated my dirty petticoat like a crime scene. walking, apparently, is a scandal if you're a woman with functioning legs. Jane needed me. I'd do it again and apologize less.
beats.quote: “To walk three miles, or four miles, or five miles, or whatever it is, above her ancles in dirt, and alone, quite alone!

beats.title: The Impossible Loadout
beats.modern: Caroline just posted the requirements for an 'accomplished woman.' music, singing, drawing, dancing, languages, plus a certain something in her walk. Darcy patches in extensive reading on top. so I tell him I'm no longer surprised he only knows six such women. I'm surprised he knows ANY. chat, nobody owns that loadout. it's not a woman, it's a wishlist.
beats.quote: A woman must have a thorough knowledge of music, singing, drawing, dancing, and the modern languages, to deserve the word;

beats.title: The Resentment Patch Notes
beats.modern: got him to publish his own patch notes tonight. known issue, will not fix: once his good opinion is lost, it's lost FOREVER. no appeals, no second chances. I point out that implacable resentment is quite the character flaw and he just nods and keeps it. this man speedran telling on himself and left the table thinking he won.
beats.quote: My good opinion once lost is lost for ever.”

beats.title: The Olive Branch Letter
beats.modern: lore drop, chat: dad's cousin Collins inherits our whole house when dad dies, because the law decided daughters don't count. he sent a letter offering an 'olive branch.' the olive branch is him. he is coming here to select a wife from among us like we're a tasting menu. four paragraphs of bowing to his patroness. dad is delighted. I feel ill.

beats.title: Wickham's Sob Story
beats.modern: the hot new officer just dropped LORE. says old Mr. Darcy left him a living in his will and our Darcy simply refused to honor it. godfather's dying wish, no legal recourse, tragic backstory, perfect delivery. and chat, he tells it SO well. so smoothly. a tiny voice in my head says it's a little too smooth for a man I met on Tuesday. I have muted her. next clip.
beats.quote: But the fact is, that we are very different sort of men, and that he hates me.”

beats.title: The Cringe Compilation
beats.modern: my family speedran humiliation at the ball tonight. Collins introduces himself to Darcy UNPROMPTED. mom announces Jane's wedding to a man who has not proposed, at full volume, with Darcy sitting opposite. Mary sings. then sings AGAIN. dad executes her in front of the room. if they had made an actual agreement to expose themselves they could not have played it cleaner. my family is a fucking cringe compilation and tonight was the season finale.
beats.quote: “That will do extremely well, child. You have delighted us long enough. Let the other young ladies have time to exhibit.”

beats.title: The Three Reasons Proposal
beats.modern: a man just proposed to me with a NUMBERED LIST. reason one: clergymen should model marriage. reason two: it will add to his happiness. reason three: his boss told him to. love did not make the list, chat. then I decline and he calls it flirting. says elegant females always say no first, to build suspense. sir. there is no suspense. the answer is the whole answer.
beats.quote: As I must, therefore, conclude that you are not serious in your rejection of me, I shall choose to attribute it to your wish of increasing my love by suspense, according to the usual practice of elegant females.”

beats.title: An Unhappy Alternative
beats.modern: mom's ruling: marry Collins or she never speaks to me again. dad looks at us both and delivers, completely deadpan, the counter ruling: if I DO marry him, HE never speaks to me again. an unhappy alternative, he calls it. I lose a parent either way. dad wins. dad always wins. mom is currently malfunctioning in the hallway.
beats.quote: Your mother will never see you again if you do not marry Mr. Collins, and I will never see you again if you do.”

beats.title: The Netherfield Rug Pull
beats.modern: they're GONE. the entire Bingley party packed up for London overnight. no goodbye, no return date, nothing. Caroline sends Jane a letter that is ninety percent perfume and ten percent knife: we're not coming back, and by the way, my brother would be just perfect for Darcy's little sister. Jane believes the perfume. I believe the knife. someone third partied my sister's whole love story, chat, and I have suspects.

beats.title: Charlotte Locks In
beats.modern: Charlotte accepted Collins. CHARLOTTE. three days after I turned him down. she looks me dead in the eye and says she's not romantic, never was, she just wants a comfortable home. and chat, she TOLD us. the take was posted months ago. this was never an upset, this is the most Charlotte play ever made, and I hate how much the math checks out. F in chat for romance.
beats.quote: I am not romantic, you know. I never was. I ask only a comfortable home;

beats.title: Dinner at Rosings
beats.modern: met Lady Catherine, Collins' boss and Darcy's aunt. she ran the dinner table like a deposition, told me I give my opinions very decidedly for so young a person, then demanded my age. I declined to say. she nearly rebooted. later she explained she would have been a great musician IF she had ever learnt. chat. she's leaving a five star review of a game she never installed.
beats.quote: There are few people in England, I suppose, who have more true enjoyment of music than myself, or a better natural taste. If I had ever learnt, I should have been a great proficient.

beats.title: The Fitzwilliam Leak
beats.modern: Darcy's cousin just leaked the logs without knowing what he was holding. Darcy has been congratulating himself on 'saving a friend' from an imprudent marriage. the friend is Bingley. the imprudent marriage is MY SISTER. this man personally rug pulled Jane's whole heart, filed it under wins, and moved on. are you shitting me. and in an hour I'm expected at tea. with him. acting normal.

beats.title: The Proposal Disaster
beats.modern: HE PROPOSED. Darcy. I had a headache and he just materialized in the parlour. opens with how he's struggled in vain, how my family is beneath him, how he loves me against his judgment, his character, and basically his will. chat, he made loving me sound like a chronic condition he's bravely managing. and he expected a YES. the audacity is off the damn charts.
beats.quote: “In vain have I struggled. It will not do. My feelings will not be repressed. You must allow me to tell you how ardently I admire and love you.”

beats.title: The Last Man Alive
beats.modern: so I emptied the whole tank. Jane. Wickham. the tolerable incident, month one. told him his proposal was ungentlemanlike, and that he is the last man in the world I could ever be prevailed on to marry. LAST, chat. behind strangers. behind COLLINS. he went pale, said I had said quite enough, and walked out. flawless victory. so why does the room feel like this.
beats.quote: I had not known you a month before I felt that you were the last man in the world whom I could ever be prevailed on to marry.”

beats.title: The Letter
beats.modern: he wrote me a letter, chat. it's all receipts. Wickham got paid for the living he 'lost,' burned through the money, then came back demanding more. denied, he tried to elope with Darcy's sister. she was FIFTEEN. her fortune was the target. I read it yelling this must be false, and the letter just sat there listing a witness I can personally interrogate. I have not interrogated him. because I know.
beats.quote: “This must be false! This cannot be! This must be the grossest falsehood!”--and

beats.title: The Ratio
beats.modern: chat. I just got ratioed by a piece of paper. my entire brand is reading people, and the first pretty soldier with a sad story played me start to finish, because he flattered me and Darcy didn't. I ran the audit on my own brain and the stats are ugly. till this moment I never knew myself. no bit this clip. it just hurts.
beats.quote: Till this moment, I never knew myself.”

beats.title: The Pemberley Tour
beats.modern: the aunt and uncle dragged me to PEMBERLEY. his house, chat. it is not a house, it is a biome. and his housekeeper, unprompted, unpaid, gives the review money cannot buy: best landlord, best master that ever lived, not one servant with a bad word. that's the character witness that actually counts. also I caught myself thinking I could have been the boss of all this, and had to go stand by a window.
beats.quote: There is not one of his tenants or servants but what will give him a good name.

beats.title: Twenty Yards
beats.modern: HE'S HERE. HE IS SUPPOSED TO BE GONE UNTIL TOMORROW. twenty yards, chat. TWENTY. both of us blue screened in front of his own house. I'm touring the estate of the man I rejected like some kind of stan, the optics are catastrophic. and then he's... polite? warm, even? asks after my family like the proposal never detonated? what the hell is this patch. I did not read these notes.

beats.title: Darcy 2.0
beats.modern: update from the grounds: the man who once called my family degrading just asked, unprompted, to be introduced to my aunt and uncle. the TRADE relatives, chat. then invited my uncle to fish his stream whenever he likes, tackle included. then asked me to meet his SISTER. tomorrow. I keep looking for the catch and there is no catch. he took the feedback. he actually took the feedback.

beats.title: The Lydia Emergency
beats.modern: STREAM EMERGENCY. two letters from Jane. Lydia has run off with WICKHAM. sixteen, no money, no wedding, last seen headed anywhere but Scotland while he outruns gambling debts. the man I defended on this very stream, chat, the VOD is right there and it is brutal. if this stands, the whole family sinks with her. nobody marries any of us after this. I have to get home NOW.
beats.quote: to inform us that she was gone off to Scotland with one of his officers; to own the truth, with Wickham! Imagine our surprise.

beats.title: Telling Him
beats.modern: Darcy walked in while I was still holding the letters and I just told him. everything. could not stop crying long enough to be strategic about it. she has no money, nothing that could make Wickham keep her. he went quiet, paced the room, and left. and here's the gut punch, chat: I finally know exactly what I want, in the same hour I watch it walk out the door.

beats.title: Found and Invoiced
beats.modern: uncle's letter is in. they're FOUND. not married, obviously, but a deal is on the table: Wickham marries her for terms so suspiciously small that dad keeps doing the math out loud. his read: Wickham would be a fool to take her under ten thousand pounds, so SOMEONE covered a number our family does not have. dad is doing arithmetic. I'm doing suspect profiling.
beats.quote: “Wickham’s a fool if he takes her with a farthing less than ten thousand pounds: I should be sorry to think so ill of him, in the very beginning of our relationship.”

beats.title: The Worst Secret Keeper
beats.modern: Lydia, mid brag about her own wedding, casually drops that MR. DARCY was standing in the church. then gasps that she promised so faithfully not to tell, like the vault didn't just blow open live on air. DARCY. AT THE WEDDING. why the hell was the final boss at my disaster sister's rushed wedding, chat. aunt Gardiner is receiving a letter from me within the hour.
beats.quote: “Oh, yes! he was to come there with Wickham, you know. But, gracious me! I quite forgot! I ought not to have said a word about it. I promised them so faithfully!

beats.title: The Silent Fixer
beats.modern: aunt's reply is in, and it was him. ALL of it. Darcy tracked them through London, bribed the intel out of an old contact, paid Wickham's debts, bought his commission, funded the whole marriage, and stood in that church as witness to the worst man he knows. then swore everyone to secrecy so I would never find out. nothing was to be done that he did not do himself. no credit. no announcement. for me. chat, I need a minute.
beats.quote: I fancy, Lizzy, that obstinacy is the real defect of his character, after all.

beats.title: Jane Wins
beats.modern: BINGLEY PROPOSED. Jane is doing the thing where she's too happy for sentences, keeps saying she doesn't deserve it and asking why everyone can't be this happy. she waited a YEAR through ghosting and designer psychological warfare and never once got mean about it. happiest creature in the world, she says. the good ending for the best person on the server. no I'm not crying, YOU'RE crying.

beats.title: Lady Catherine Pulls Up
beats.modern: LADY CATHERINE JUST PULLED UP TO MY HOUSE. uninvited. before breakfast settled. demands I promise never to marry her nephew, calls me an obstinate headstrong girl, asks if the shades of Pemberley are to be thus POLLUTED. I'm the pollution, chat. so I tell her I will act on my own happiness with zero reference to her or anyone else so wholly unconnected with me. she rage quit down the driveway. and here's the tell: you don't drive out here to block a thing you believe is impossible.
beats.quote: Are the shades of Pemberley to be thus polluted?”

beats.title: One Word
beats.modern: we walked. I thanked him for Lydia. he said he thought only of me. then, quietly: his affections and wishes are unchanged, but one word from me will silence him on the subject forever. chat. I did not give that word. I gave the other one. the last man in the world is now the only man, and I have never been this happy to lose an argument.
beats.quote: If your feelings are still what they were last April, tell me so at once. My affections and wishes are unchanged; but one word from you will silence me on this subject for ever.”

beats.title: Happier Than Jane
beats.modern: final update, chat, live from my new biome. I am the happiest creature in the world. other people have said it before, but no one with such justice. Jane only smiles. I LAUGH. and the stream ends where it started: a single man in possession of a good fortune, in want of a wife. turns out the wife was me. gg. logging off happy.
beats.quote: I am the happiest creature in the world. Perhaps other people have said so before, but no one with such justice. I am happier even than Jane; she only smiles, I laugh.

beats.title: The Morning Lineup
beats.modern: morning briefing to myself: today I will meet a nosy guy, an ungrateful guy, a hater, a fraud, and at least one snake. can't be mad at any of them. nobody taught them what good even is. also we're technically teammates, like teeth in the same mouth. teeth don't fight teeth. let's get it.
beats.quote: Betimes in the morning say to thyself, This day I shalt have to do with an idle curious man, with an unthankful man, a railer, a crafty, false, or an envious man;

beats.title: The Warm Bed Debate
beats.modern: 5am. bed: warm. me: emperor. the negotiation begins. 'but this is pleasing.' was I born to be PLEASED? the ants are up. the bees are on shift. the spiders are doing spider work without complaint. I am not losing a productivity battle to a spider. up.
beats.quote: Or was I made for this, to lay me down, and make much of myself in a warm bed?

beats.title: Snooze Button Eternity
beats.modern: reminder: you have been putting this off for YEARS. the gods gave you a deadline and you keep requesting extensions. the time limit is real, and unused minutes do not roll over. you either spend them calming your own soul or you die holding them.

beats.title: Good Tomorrow
beats.modern: caught myself scheduling my own character development: 'I'll be good tomorrow.' brother. you are procrastinating VIRTUE. be good today. tomorrow is not a place. nothing lives there.

beats.title: Star Routine
beats.modern: the Pythagoreans had one morning ritual: look up. the stars have been running the same flawless shift for all eternity. on time, zero drama, nothing hidden, no cover. that's the standard. look up, take notes, then go run your own orbit like that.

beats.title: The Best Revenge
beats.modern: someone did me dirty today. my revenge plan is elite: I am simply not going to become him. that's it. that's the whole revenge. undefeated strategy, zero cost, drives them insane.
beats.quote: 'The best kind of revenge is, not to become like unto them.'

beats.title: Emerald Status
beats.modern: whatever anyone says or does today, my job description does not change: be an emerald. keep the colour. the emerald does not check the replies. the emerald does not post a response. the emerald is green full time.
beats.quote: Whatsoever any man either doth or saith, I must still be an emerald, and I must keep my colour.

beats.title: Two Options Only
beats.modern: the menu for dealing with people has exactly two items: teach them better, or bear with them. there is no third option where you rage about them to the group chat. that dish is not served here. it feeds nobody.
beats.quote: All men are made one for another: either then teach them better, or bear with them.

beats.title: The Report
beats.modern: intel arrives: 'someone is talking trash about you, Caesar.' correct. that is what was reported. notice what was NOT reported: that I was harmed. the harm is an optional extra that I add myself, and I am declining it at checkout.
beats.quote: that he speaketh ill of thee, so much is reported. But that thou art hurt thereby, is not reported: that is the addition of opinion,

beats.title: Let Him Look To That
beats.modern: will someone despise me? his problem. will someone hate me? also his problem. my entire workload is making sure I never do or say anything that actually deserves it. everything past that point is somebody else's inbox.

beats.title: Quota Guy
beats.modern: met a shameless man today. ran the check: is it possible for the world to contain zero shameless men? no. it is not. so some must exist, and this is simply one of the ones that must exist. quota filled. inventory updated. no further emotion required.

beats.title: They Won't Change
beats.modern: hard truth from the imperial desk: people are going to keep doing what they do no matter how upset you get. the actual text of my note says they'd carry on even if you hanged yourself over it. so obviously don't. spend that energy staying unbothered instead. they hate that more.
beats.quote: What they have done, they will still do, although thou shouldst hang thyself.

beats.title: The Breath Guy
beats.modern: you cannot be angry at the man with catastrophic breath. that is simply the breath he has. it travels with him. either tell him kindly or endure it quietly. your rage changes zero parts per million of that air.

beats.title: Calm Is the Meta
beats.modern: anger feels like strength but it's a wound in a costume. both the angry man and the grieving man already took the hit and surrendered. real meekness, the genuine kind, is unconquerable. the closer you get to unbothered, the closer you get to actual power. those are the patch notes of the universe.
beats.quote: For the nearer everything is unto unpassionateness, the nearer it is unto power.

beats.title: Fig Tree Discourse
beats.modern: you're SHOCKED a shady man did a shady thing? that is being shocked a fig tree made figs. the doctor is not shocked by fever. the pilot is not shocked by a headwind. expected output from a known build. update your expectations, not your blood pressure.

beats.title: Mirror Check
beats.modern: before I rage at this man's flaws, quick internal audit of my own in the same category. ...audit complete. findings: extensive. rage cancelled on procedural grounds. carry on.

beats.title: Leave Right Now
beats.modern: do everything like a man who could get unplugged from life mid task. not as a downer. as a filter. it deletes fake priorities instantly. would I want to be caught doing THIS when the lights go out? if yes, proceed. if no, why am I doing it at all.
beats.quote: Whatsoever thou dost affect, whatsoever thou dost project, so do, and so project all, as one who, for aught thou knowest, may at this very present depart out of this life.

beats.title: Death Hangs Over Thee
beats.modern: you do not have thousands of years. the timer is live. it has always been live. whilst thou livest, whilst thou mayest, be good. that's the whole notification. tap to dismiss at your own risk.
beats.quote: Not as though thou hadst thousands of years to live. Death hangs over thee: whilst yet thou livest, whilst thou mayest, be good.

beats.title: Alexander and the Mule Guy
beats.modern: Alexander the Great and the man who groomed his mules are both dead, and death did the exact same thing to each of them. same dispersal. same atoms. same result screen. the leaderboard wipes at the end for everyone. plan accordingly.
beats.quote: Alexander of Macedon, and he that dressed his mules, when once dead both came to one.

beats.title: Nobody Beats the Game
beats.modern: the doctors who cured everyone? dead. the astrologers who predicted deaths professionally? dead, did not see it coming. Heraclitus, whose whole brand was fire? died full of water. lice got Democritus. nobody is beating this game. you sailed, you reached land. disembark with some grace.

beats.title: Leaves
beats.modern: your kids are leaves. your fans are leaves. the guys cursing you in private are leaves. the future generations who might remember your name? also leaves. wind blows, leaves drop, the tree makes new ones. stop clinging to individual leaves. love the tree.

beats.title: Funeral Attendance
beats.modern: real talk: however beloved you are, somebody at your funeral will be quietly relieved. even the wise get one mourner thinking 'finally, some rest from this pedagogue.' THAT is the audience you're postponing death for. be kind to them anyway. and leave the party graciously.

beats.title: Ashes or a Skeleton
beats.modern: coming soon: you, as ashes or a skeleton. maybe a name survives. probably not even that. and a name is what exactly? an empty sound. an echo produced by mouths that are also scheduled for deletion. build on something else.

beats.title: Three Acts
beats.modern: 'but the play is only three acts!' correct. in matter of life, three acts IS the whole play. the one who cast you sets the runtime, and you were never in the writers' room. take the bow, thank the producer, exit clean. gg.
beats.quote: As if the praetor should fairly dismiss him from the stage, whom he had taken in to act a while.

beats.title: Oblivion Speedrun
beats.modern: status report on the human condition: life is a dot. the body is a stream. the soul is a dream and a smoke. fame after death is oblivion with extra steps. the only thing that stays on your account is philosophy. everything else is a rented skin.
beats.quote: Our life is a warfare, and a mere pilgrimage. Fame after life is no better than oblivion.

beats.title: Remembered By Whom
beats.modern: you want to be remembered. by WHOM, exactly? the people who'd remember you are also dying. then their replacements die. memory is a relay race where every single runner is running into a grave. and even if the memory were immortal: what does a dead man do with a mention?

beats.title: Trending, Then Obsolete
beats.modern: top trending names of earlier eras: Camillus. Caeso. Volesius. ring any bells? none? they were THE guys. Scipio and Cato are fading. even Augustus is buffering. this is also the roadmap for whatever name you are grinding to make famous. all is vanity. log off and be just instead.

beats.title: The Pixel
beats.modern: zoom out with me. the whole earth: one point. the inhabited part: a corner of the point. your fan region: a crumb of the corner. and inside the crumb, not one person praises you consistently. hell of a kingdom to trade your peace for.

beats.title: Applause Deconstructed
beats.modern: the praise of many tongues is the clattering of many tongues. that's it. that's the entire feature. you are chasing a sound that mouths make. clap. clap. clap. congratulations on your sound.

beats.title: Future Followers
beats.modern: these guys cannot say one nice thing about anyone alive, but they are desperate to be praised by people who do not exist yet. that is exactly as unhinged as being sad that ancient strangers never complimented you. say it out loud and hear it.

beats.title: The Internal Retreat
beats.modern: everyone's booking country villas and seaside retreats to find peace. meanwhile the actual retreat has no travel time, no booking fee, and is open at 3am: your own soul. go inward, refresh, come back online. shortest commute in the empire.
beats.quote: At what time soever thou wilt, it is in thy power to retire into thyself, and to be at rest, and free from all businesses.

beats.title: Delete the Opinion
beats.modern: remove the opinion, and 'I have been wronged' disappears. remove 'I have been wronged,' and the wrong itself disappears. a two step uninstall, and both steps run inside your own head. nobody else has admin access. nobody ever did.
beats.quote: Let opinion be taken away, and no man will think himself wronged. If no man shall think himself wronged, then is there no more any such thing as wrong.

beats.title: Bitter Cucumber Protocol
beats.modern: cucumber is bitter? put it down. brambles on the path? step around them. that's the whole protocol. you do not also need to file a formal complaint with the universe titled 'why do brambles exist.' the carpenter's shop has wood shavings in it. keep walking.
beats.quote: Is the cucumber bitter? set it away. Brambles are in the way? avoid them. Let this suffice.

beats.title: Rock vs Waves
beats.modern: be the promontory. the waves hit it all day, every day, forever. the rock's entire strategy is to continue being a rock. no counterattack, no statement, no response video. and somehow the sea around it ends up calm. study that.

beats.title: Spring Water
beats.modern: 'they kill me, they cut my flesh, they curse my name.' okay. and the spring keeps running clear. throw dirt in it: dispersed. it cannot be dyed, cannot be infected. don't be a well you have to guard. be the spring that clears itself.

beats.title: The Worse Plague
beats.modern: posting from an actual plague year: the thing in the air attacks your breath. the corruption of the mind attacks the part of you that is actually YOU. only one of those can be caught from standing too close to fools. guard the mind first.

beats.title: Standing Outside
beats.modern: the things stressing you are standing outside the door. motionless. silent. completely unaware of your existence. the entire verdict against them is being written inside your own head, by you, on your own servers. you are the author of the stress fanfic. put the pen down.

beats.title: The Only Thing You Lose
beats.modern: live three thousand years or live thirty: you can only ever lose the moment you are currently in. that's the entire inventory. the past is not yours anymore. the future never was. the longest life and the shortest lose the exact same thing at the end: now.
beats.quote: If thou shouldst live three thousand, or as many as ten thousands of years, yet remember this, that man can part with no life properly, save with that little part of life, which he now lives:

beats.title: Change and Opinion
beats.modern: final answer on how reality works, in nine words: this world is mere change, and this life, opinion. everything out there is turnover. everything in here is a take. hold both loosely and you are untouchable.
beats.quote: This world is mere change, and this life, opinion.

beats.title: No New Content
beats.modern: there is nothing new. NOTHING. every scandal, every hater, every collapse: ancient stories, middle age stories, fresh stories, same stories. once you've seen the pattern you have seen the entire catalog. and honestly? most calming spoiler of all time.

beats.title: The Vespasian Feed
beats.modern: scroll back to the times of Vespasian: marrying, flexing, scheming, farming, feasting, hoarding, chasing office, dying. now scroll to Trajan: same feed, different accounts. every era is a repost, and every one of those posters is gone. keep that tab open in your mind.

beats.title: Spend It On Yourself
beats.modern: you are hoarding your attention for a future that is not real and an audience that is not born. this time that is now present, bestow it upon thyself. the future fans you're grinding for will be exactly as annoying as the current ones. the present is the only paycheck that clears.

beats.title: Do Less, Better
beats.modern: peace hack from the throne room: most of what we say and do is unnecessary. cut it and you get back hours AND tranquility, double reward. before every action, one question: is this necessary? and yes, it applies to thoughts too. unfollow your own spam.

beats.title: Call Me Ishmael
beats.modern: yo. new stream. I'm broke, I'm depressed, and yesterday I caught myself following a random funeral for fun. when it gets this bad I don't do anything drastic, I just go to sea. boat or bullet, chat, and I pick the boat every time. name's Ishmael. that's the whole bio.
beats.quote: Call me Ishmael.

beats.title: The Roommate
beats.modern: the inn is full, so the landlord sells me HALF a bed. my roommate rolls in at midnight from selling human heads, tattooed head to toe, and lights his tomahawk pipe IN the bed. I scream. the landlord vouches for him. and honestly? better to sleep with a sober cannibal than a drunken Christian. best sleep of my life.
beats.quote: Better sleep with a sober cannibal than a drunken Christian.

beats.title: The Counterpane Cuddle
beats.modern: chat I woke up and the cannibal is SPOONING me. full married couple hug. I genuinely cannot tell his tattooed arm from the patchwork quilt. we have known each other for nine hours.

beats.title: The Jonah Sermon
beats.modern: church stop before the voyage. the sermon is Jonah: the original guy who tried to sail out of God's coverage zone. booked passage to the literal edge of the known map, paid triple, acted so sus the sailors profiled him in one look. spoiler, chat: there is no logging off from God. the whale is the ban hammer.

beats.title: Married By Forehead
beats.modern: update: the head salesman and I are best friends now. one shared pipe and he presses his forehead to mine and declares us MARRIED. then he splits his life savings, thirty dollars, and just pours half into my pocket. so I did the theology math and helped him worship his little idol. day two of knowing this man.
beats.quote: he pressed his forehead against mine, clasped me round the waist, and said that henceforth we were married;

beats.title: The 777th Lay
beats.modern: salary negotiation. Bildad looks up from his BIBLE and offers me the 777th lay. that is one 777th of the profits, chat. he lowballs me with scripture still in his mouth. Peleg screams, threatens to swallow a live goat, and lands me the 300th. still robbery. blessed, certified robbery.
beats.quote: The seven hundred and seventy-seventh lay, Captain Peleg.”

beats.title: Elijah The Doomer
beats.modern: some dockside prophet named Elijah stops us: oh, you signed with AHAB? then he just riffs. the leg. a silver calabash. something off Cape Horn where the captain lay like dead for three days. then he wishes us luck like we're already ghosts. I hate how SPECIFIC the doomer lore is, chat.
beats.quote: when Captain Ahab is all right, then this left arm of mine will be all right; not before.”

beats.title: The Christmas Launch
beats.modern: we launch ON CHRISTMAS. old Bildad cannot let go of the ship, does five farewell laps, then delivers the greatest send off speech ever streamed: don't stave the boats, watch the cheese, the butter was twenty cents a pound, and beware of fornication at the islands. then three cheers and we plunge like fate into the lone Atlantic.
beats.quote: If ye touch at the islands, Mr. Flask, beware of fornication.

beats.title: The Captain Appears
beats.modern: first captain sighting after WEEKS at sea. chat, this man looks like he was cut off the stake mid burning. a white scar runs from his hair straight down under his collar like lightning split him. the leg is polished whale jawbone, slotted into a bored hole in the deck. he says nothing. we say nothing. crucifixion in his face. new fear unlocked.
beats.quote: He looked like a man cut away from the stake, when the fire has overrunningly wasted all the limbs without consuming them,

beats.title: Draught Of A Draught
beats.modern: yes chat, I paused the whale hunt arc for three streams to build a whale taxonomy. no I will not finish it. God keep me from ever completing anything. this whole book is a draft of a draft. small creators finish things. grand ones leave the last stone to posterity.
beats.quote: God keep me from ever completing anything.

beats.title: The Gold Doubloon
beats.modern: EMERGENCY ALL HANDS. Ahab nails a GOLD DOUBLOON to the mast: whoever spots a white whale with a crooked jaw and a wrinkled brow gets it. then the lore drops: that whale TOOK HIS LEG. it's Moby Dick. and now the whole crew is howling for its blood over grog, hands spliced on a revenge pact. we didn't sign up for this quest line, chat. we got patched into it.
beats.quote: it was Moby Dick that dismasted me; Moby Dick that brought me to this dead stump I stand on now.

beats.title: Strike The Sun
beats.modern: Starbuck tries the sane take: it's a dumb animal that bit you on instinct, and vengeance sells for zero barrels in Nantucket. Ahab responds with the most terrifying monologue I've ever heard live. everything is a pasteboard mask. strike through the mask. the whale is the wall. I'd strike the sun if it insulted me. chat, we don't work for a whaling company. we work for a grudge with a boat.
beats.quote: Talk not to me of blasphemy, man; I’d strike the sun if it insulted me.

beats.title: The Boss Wiki
beats.modern: posting the wiki on our raid boss. believers claim Moby Dick is UBIQUITOUS, encountered in two oceans at the same instant. others say immortal: plant a whole grove of spears in his flanks and he swims off unharmed. see him bleed? ghastly deception, he'll be spouting clean a hundred leagues away. you don't nerf this whale, chat. this whale nerfs you.
beats.quote: declaring Moby Dick not only ubiquitous, but immortal (for immortality is but ubiquity in time);

beats.title: The Whiteness
beats.modern: people ask why I'M scared of one whale. it's not the jaw, chat. it's the COLOR. white is brides and angels right up until it's a shark's belly in the dark, and then it is the worst color that exists. the void wears white. I can't explain it properly and that is exactly what keeps me up at night.
beats.quote: It was the whiteness of the whale that above all things appalled me.

beats.title: The Hate Spreadsheet
beats.modern: leaked the captain's nightly routine: charts of all four oceans on his table and piles of old logbooks, plotting one single whale's commute through the seasons. every night, new pencil lines. and the swinging lamp keeps drawing shadow lines on his forehead, like something is charting HIM back. this man has a spreadsheet for his hatred and it's almost done calculating.

beats.title: The First Lowering
beats.modern: FIRST HUNT. we sail straight into a squall chasing spouts. Queequeg lands a graze, the whale detonates the sea under us, boat swamped, night falls, no ship in sight. Starbuck lights one lantern on a pole and Queequeg holds it up all night: a man without faith, hopelessly holding up hope. at dawn a huge shape looms out of the mist. it's OUR OWN SHIP about to run us over. we dive, they fish us out. that was hunt number one, chat.
beats.quote: There, then, he sat, the sign and symbol of a man without faith, hopelessly holding up hope in the midst of despair.

beats.title: The Will
beats.modern: did a post match review: sailing full speed onto a whale in fog is apparently standard practice here. so I went below and drafted my will. Queequeg is my lawyer, my executor, AND my heir. I feel incredible now. every day from here is bonus content. I'm a quiet ghost with a clean conscience, chat.
beats.quote: “come along, you shall be my lawyer, executor, and legatee.”

beats.title: The White Ghost
beats.modern: false Moby alarm. instead we watch a KRAKEN surface: a cream colored pulpy acre with arms like a nest of anacondas and NO FACE. Starbuck, our most sensible man, says he'd rather have fought Moby Dick than have seen it. Ahab says nothing at all and turns the boat around. when the captain mutes himself, chat, start worrying.
beats.quote: exclaimed—“Almost rather had I seen Moby Dick and fought him, than to have seen thee, thou white ghost!”

beats.title: Both Pipes Smoked Out
beats.modern: Stubb logs our first kill without his pipe ever going out. the line screams around the loggerhead, smoke coming off the rope, hands getting flayed, and the man keeps puffing. then he churns the lance in like he's fishing a gold watch out of the whale. red tide everywhere. when it's over he taps his ashes onto the water: both pipes smoked out. coldest kill screen I have ever witnessed. F for the whale, unironically.
beats.quote: “Yes; both pipes smoked out!”

beats.title: Sermon To The Sharks
beats.modern: several thousand sharks are eating our whale overnight, so Stubb sends the ship's cook to the rail to PREACH at them. old Fleece leans over with a lantern and actually delivers: you can't help being sharks, but govern the shark inside you and you are an angel. the sharks keep chewing. greatest congregation of all time. zero converts.
beats.quote: You is sharks, sartin; but if you gobern de shark in you, why den you be angel;

beats.title: The Monkey Rope
beats.modern: today's task: Queequeg rides the dead whale in shark water while I hold his rope. except on THIS ship the rope is tied to BOTH of us. if he sinks, honor says I follow him down. my individuality is now a joint stock company of two, chat. my free will took a mortal wound this morning. and I only manage one end of the rope.
beats.quote: should poor Queequeg sink to rise no more, then both usage and honor demanded, that instead of cutting the cord, it should drag me down in his wake.

beats.title: Whale Skull Obstetrics
beats.modern: Tashtego fell INTO the whale's head while bailing it. then the hook tore and the whole head SANK with him inside. Queequeg dove, cut a hole in the sinking skull with a sword, reached in, and delivered him head first like a midwife. a running delivery, at depth, on the second try. obstetrics on a whale skull, chat. clip of the year and it's not close.
beats.quote: through the courage and great skill in obstetrics of Queequeg, the deliverance, or rather, delivery of Tashtego, was successfully accomplished,

beats.title: The Nursery
beats.modern: we got dragged into the calm center of a whale mega herd and it's a NURSERY. mothers and newborns hanging in glass clear water. the babies come up to the boat like puppies and Queequeg pets one on the forehead. a day old calf looks up through us like we're a bit of seaweed. I hunt these for money, chat. I'm having a whole moment about it.
beats.quote: Like household dogs they came snuffling round us, right up to our gunwales,

beats.title: The Ambergris Diddle
beats.modern: a French ship is towing two rotten whales, and Stubb clocks that one is full of AMBERGRIS. whale gold. so, scam of the century: through a fake interpreter he convinces their captain the corpses carry plague, they panic and cut both loose, and Stubb helpfully tows one away and digs six handfuls of perfume money out of it. then declines the victory wine: against my principles to drink with the man I've diddled. an absolute menace.
beats.quote: tell him it’s against my principles to drink with the man I’ve diddled.

beats.title: Pip
beats.modern: no jokes for this one. Pip jumped from the boat a second time, and this time Stubb kept chasing the whale. Pip floated alone in the open ocean, one small head in a million shoreless miles, until the ship stumbled on him by pure chance. his body came back. the rest of him didn't. the crew says he's mad now. I say the sea showed him something infinite and kept the part of him that saw it.
beats.quote: The sea had jeeringly kept his finite body up, but drowned the infinite of his soul.

beats.title: The Hand Squeeze
beats.modern: today's task: squeeze crystallized whale wax back into liquid. status report: I squeezed all morning until I fully lost the plot and started squeezing my coworkers' HANDS in the vat, gazing into their eyes like, why do we ever fight, chat. I would do this job forever. I saw a vision of angels and every single one had their hands in a jar of spermaceti. best shift of my life.
beats.quote: let us all squeeze ourselves into each other; let us squeeze ourselves universally into the very milk and sperm of kindness.

beats.title: Fire Watch
beats.modern: night shift at the blubber furnaces. the ship is glowing red like a floating hell and I zone out at the helm staring into the fire. I snap awake standing BACKWARDS. no compass in front of me, tiller inverted, seconds from capsizing everyone. spun around just in time. PSA, chat: look not too long in the face of the fire. there is a wisdom that is woe, but there is a woe that is madness.
beats.quote: There is a wisdom that is woe; but there is a woe that is madness.

beats.title: The Coin Readings
beats.modern: everyone keeps solo staring at the doubloon like it's a mirror. Ahab sees Ahab in it. Stubb runs zodiac math. Flask computes 960 cigars. the old Manxman reads doom, Fedallah bows to the sun sign, and then Pip shuffles up and drops the realest take on this ship: I look, you look, he looks; we look, ye look, they look. that's it. that's the whole game, chat.
beats.quote: “I look, you look, he looks; we look, ye look, they look.”

beats.title: The Sane Timeline
beats.modern: gam with the Samuel Enderby, whose captain lost an ARM to Moby Dick. he and Ahab cross ivory limbs like a toast. but catch the difference, chat: Captain Boomer LET IT GO. ain't one limb enough? he figures the whale isn't even malicious, just awkward. Ahab practically sprints us back to the Pequod. the sane ending exists. it's right there. our guy looked at it and left.
beats.quote: “Didn’t want to try to: ain’t one limb enough?

beats.title: The Coffin Demo
beats.modern: Queequeg caught a fever and calmly ordered his own COFFIN. tested it for comfort with his idol and a biscuit loadout like it's a demo unit, said it will do, and then, chat, DECIDED not to die. remembered an errand ashore. said a man who makes up his mind to live can't be killed by sickness, only by a whale, a gale, or something equally rude. got up. kept the coffin as a sea chest. legend behavior.
beats.quote: if a man made up his mind to live, mere sickness could not kill him:

beats.title: The Black Baptism
beats.modern: Ahab commissioned a custom harpoon for one specific whale and refused water for the quench. he asked the three harpooneers for BLOOD, tempered the barbs in it, and howled a baptism over the steel in the devil's name. I watched our captain forge a cursed item live on deck, chat. the stats are hate, hate, and hate.
beats.quote: “Ego non baptizo te in nomine patris, sed in nomine diaboli!”

beats.title: The Death Conditions
beats.modern: Fedallah posted Ahab's death conditions like patch notes. before you can die you must see TWO hearses on the open sea: the first not made by mortal hands, the second of wood grown in America. and only hemp can kill you. Ahab heard gallows, declared himself immortal on land and on sea, and laughed. chat. clip the prophecy. CLIP IT.
beats.quote: gloom—“Hemp only can kill thee.”

beats.title: Quadrant Smash
beats.modern: Ahab took his noon sun reading, stared at the quadrant, and asked it the only question he cares about: can you tell me where MOBY DICK is? it cannot. so he called it a foolish toy, cursed science by name, and stomped our navigation instrument to pieces with his ivory leg. we are now steering by dead reckoning and vibes, chat.
beats.quote: Science! Curse thee, thou vain toy; and cursed be all the things that cast man’s eyes aloft to that heaven,

beats.title: The Corpusants
beats.modern: TYPHOON. lightning everywhere, and then all three masts light up with pale fire. corpusants. three white flames like altar candles and the whole crew frozen underneath. and Ahab? Ahab plants a foot on Fedallah, grabs the lightning chains BAREHANDED, and cuts a promo on the storm itself: defiance is your right worship. he is flaming the WEATHER, chat. and the weather is listening.
beats.quote: I now know thee, thou clear spirit, and I now know that thy right worship is defiance.

beats.title: Starbuck At The Door
beats.modern: I should not have this clip. Starbuck went below to report the wind, saw the loaded muskets outside Ahab's door, and stood there doing the math. one touch and thirty men see home again, and Mary, and the boy. he leveled it at the door. he wrestled with an angel in that corridor, chat. then he racked the gun and walked away.
beats.quote: A touch, and Starbuck may survive to hug his wife and child again.—Oh

beats.title: Lord Of The Loadstone
beats.modern: the typhoon flipped our compass needles overnight. they point BACKWARDS. so Ahab forges a new needle from a sail needle and a lance head in front of everyone, does some wizard hand motions, and crowns himself lord of the level loadstone. the crew peeks one by one and slinks away. that wasn't morale I saw on their faces, chat. that was fear in all his fatal pride.
beats.quote: exclaimed,—“Look ye, for yourselves, if Ahab be not lord of the level loadstone! The sun is East, and that compass swears it!”

beats.title: Coffin Life Buoy
beats.modern: a man fell from the masthead at sunrise. the life buoy we dropped was so sun shrunk it sank right after him. so now we need a new float, and the only buoyant box aboard is Queequeg's coffin. Starbuck says it out loud like the ship needed to hear it: a life buoy of a coffin! rig it, carpenter. the foreshadowing is hanging off our stern now, chat.
beats.quote: “A life-buoy of a coffin!”

beats.title: The Rachel
beats.modern: a ship called the Rachel begs us to help. the captain's twelve year old SON is out there in a missing boat that Moby Dick dragged off. he offers money, offers anything, begs father to father. Ahab's answer: Captain Gardiner, I will not do it. even now I lose time. and we sail away from a man sweeping the sea for his child. no joke exists for this. F in chat isn't enough.
beats.quote: word—“Captain Gardiner, I will not do it. Even now I lose time.

beats.title: One Tear
beats.modern: one mild blue day before contact. Ahab leans over the rail, drops a single tear into the sea, then hands Starbuck forty years of regrets: the girl he widowed by marrying her, the boy he's never danced with. Starbuck begs him: turn the ship, Nantucket is right there in that eye. for one breath he wavers. then: what nameless, inscrutable, unearthly thing commands me? is it even Ahab lifting this arm? Starbuck walked away before the answer, chat. so did the answer.
beats.quote: “What is it, what nameless, inscrutable, unearthly thing is it; what cozening, hidden lord and master, and cruel, remorseless emperor commands me;

beats.title: There She Blows
beats.modern: DAY ONE. Ahab has himself hoisted up the mainmast and screams it before any lookout: There she blows! a hump like a snow hill! it is Moby Dick! then he claims the doubloon, his own prize money, because fate reserved it for him. three years of buildup, chat, and the boss just spawned. lock. in.
beats.quote: “There she blows!—there she blows! A hump like a snow-hill! It is Moby Dick!”

beats.title: Bitten In Two
beats.modern: Moby Dick took Ahab's whole boat in his mouth and BIT IT IN TWO. shook it first like a mildly cruel cat with a mouse, while Ahab grabbed the jawbone BAREHANDED trying to wrench it off us. then the whale circled his bobbing head in tightening rings until the Pequod herself charged in and broke the ring. day one final score: whale 1, humanity 0.
beats.quote: the White Whale now shook the slight cedar as a mildly cruel cat her mouse.

beats.title: Day Two Wipe
beats.modern: DAY TWO. all three boats wrecked in a single engagement. Ahab comes up clinging to half a hull with his ivory leg snapped to a splinter. and Fedallah is GONE, dragged under in Ahab's own line. the prophet got taken by his own prophecy, chat. Ahab's response is to promise to girdle the globe ten times and dive straight through it. Starbuck calls it devil's madness to his face. one day left on this timer.
beats.quote: His ivory leg had been snapped off, leaving but one short sharp splinter.

beats.title: The First Hearse
beats.modern: DAY THREE opens with Ahab taunting the ocean: no coffin and no hearse can be mine, hemp only can kill me! then the whale breaches and chat. CHAT. it's FEDALLAH. lashed to Moby Dick's back in last night's tangled lines, dead, eyes fixed on Ahab. a hearse not made by mortal hands. condition one just completed itself in front of us. the harpoon dropped out of Ahab's hand.
beats.quote: no coffin and no hearse can be mine:—and hemp only can kill me! Ha! ha!”

beats.title: The Second Hearse
beats.modern: he's done with the boats. Moby Dick turns and rams THE SHIP. the solid white forehead through the starboard bow, men knocked flat, ocean pouring in like a mountain flume. and Ahab, watching from the water, narrates his own prophecy: The ship! The hearse! the second hearse! its wood could only be American. condition two, chat. he knows he's allowed to die now.
beats.quote: “The ship! The hearse!—the second hearse!”

beats.title: From Hell’s Heart
beats.modern: the last clip of Captain Ahab. he turns his body from the sun and gives the whale everything: to the last I grapple with thee; from hell's heart I stab at thee; for hate's sake I spit my last breath at thee. the harpoon flies, the line runs foul, he stoops to clear it, and the loop takes him around the neck. gone before his own crew saw it happen. hemp, chat. it was hemp the whole time.
beats.quote: to the last I grapple with thee; from hell’s heart I stab at thee; for hate’s sake I spit my last breath at thee.

beats.title: The Sea Rolls Shut
beats.modern: the Pequod goes down with every soul aboard. Tashtego keeps hammering the flag to the mast even under the water, and a sky hawk gets its wing nailed to the spar and goes down wrapped in Ahab's flag. the ship dragged a piece of heaven under with her. then the whirlpool spins the last chip of her out of sight, and the sea rolls shut like it has rolled for five thousand years.
beats.quote: then all collapsed, and the great shroud of the sea rolled on as it rolled five thousand years ago.

beats.title: Another Orphan
beats.modern: so how am I live right now. the vortex pulled me to its center, and then Queequeg's coffin shot up out of the middle of it and floated to my side. my best friend's death bed held me for a day and a night. sharks slid past with padlocked mouths. the ship that finally found me? the Rachel, still sweeping the sea for her missing children. she only found another orphan. stream's over, chat. I'm the only one who got out to tell thee.
beats.quote: It was the devious-cruising Rachel, that in her retracing search after her missing children, only found another orphan.

beats.title: The Iceberg Pickup
beats.modern: new stream setup, chat: a ship frozen into the arctic. quick recap: I was chasing someone across the ice, my ride melted, this crew fished me out. I was 95 percent dead and I still asked where the ship was headed BEFORE boarding. if this thing was sailing south I was staying on the iceberg. oh, and yesterday the crew saw a giant man on a dog sledge heading north. that's him. that's my boy. settle in. this story will ruin your day.
beats.quote: “will you have the kindness to inform me whither you are bound?”

beats.title: The Pretty Present
beats.modern: lore drop: when I was five my mom found an angel orphan in a peasant cottage and just acquired her. the night before, she told me she had a pretty present for her Victor. chat. they gave me a HUMAN as a gift and little me interpreted it literally: mine to protect, love, cherish, forever. her name is Elizabeth. write that name down. it matters later.
beats.quote: “I have a pretty present for my Victor—tomorrow he shall have it.”

beats.title: Sad Trash
beats.modern: origin story. age thirteen, rainy day at an inn, I find a book by Cornelius Agrippa and my brain ignites. I show dad. his entire review: 'sad trash.' no explanation. so naturally I read the COMPLETE works out of spite. then at fifteen I watch lightning delete an entire oak tree in front of me, and a houseguest explains electricity and galvanism. parents: EXPLAIN the trash. two minutes of explanation and none of this happens.
beats.quote: “Ah! Cornelius Agrippa! My dear Victor, do not waste your time upon this; it is sad trash.”

beats.title: Mom's Last Wish
beats.modern: Elizabeth caught scarlet fever. mom insisted on nursing her herself. Elizabeth recovered. mom caught it. on her deathbed she joined our hands and said her firmest hope was our union. she planned our wedding WHILE DYING. then she was gone, calm and kind to the end. I left for university a few weeks later, grieving, and carrying one dangerous thought: why does death get to win. hold that thought, chat.
beats.quote: “my firmest hopes of future happiness were placed on the prospect of your union.

beats.title: The Two Professors
beats.modern: university onboarding. professor one, Krempe: asks what I've read, I name my alchemists, and he tells me every minute spent on those books is 'utterly and entirely lost.' ratio'd in office hours. professor two, Waldman: says modern scientists 'penetrate into the recesses of nature' and 'command the thunders of heaven.' chat. ONE lecture. one lecture and my whole build changed. I said it that night: more, far more, will I achieve. clip that. you'll want the receipt.
beats.quote: they can command the thunders of heaven, mimic the earthquake, and even mock the invisible world with its own shadows.”

beats.title: The Filthy Workshop
beats.modern: UPDATE. two years of grinding and I cracked it. the actual cause of life. I can animate dead matter. no, I will not share the method, this is not a tutorial channel. sourcing phase: charnel houses, the dissecting room, the slaughterhouse. the small parts were too fiddly so I scaled the build UP: eight feet tall, proportionally large. me, alone, at midnight, in an attic I genuinely call my workshop of filthy creation. zero red flags anywhere, chat.
beats.quote: After days and nights of incredible labour and fatigue, I succeeded in discovering the cause of generation and life; nay, more, I became myself capable of bestowing animation upon lifeless matter.

beats.title: The Yellow Eye
beats.modern: one in the morning. rain on the glass. candle's nearly out. HIS EYE OPENED. it's dull yellow and he's breathing hard. chat, I picked every feature to be beautiful. lustrous black hair. pearly teeth. and the finished whole is the worst thing I have ever seen. two years, my health, my family, all of it for this, and the second he breathed, the dream died in my chest. I'm leaving. I'm walking out of my own launch stream. what the fuck did I make.
beats.quote: I saw the dull yellow eye of the creature open; it breathed hard, and a convulsive motion agitated its limbs.

beats.title: The Bed Curtain
beats.modern: tried to sleep it off. dreamed I kissed Elizabeth and she turned into my mother's corpse. woke up and HE IS AT THE BED. holding the curtain open. staring down at me. jaw working, making sounds, one hand reaching out like a toddler reaching for dad. and I, the genius, the creator, the modern Prometheus: sprinted downstairs and hid in a courtyard until sunrise. day one of fatherhood, chat. perfect score.
beats.quote: He held up the curtain of the bed; and his eyes, if eyes they may be called, were fixed on me.

beats.title: The Empty Apartment
beats.modern: CLERVAL IS HERE. best friend, straight off the coach from home. I bring him back to my place in absolute terror, sprint up first, throw the door open like a kid checking for a spectre... empty. he's gone. an eight foot corpse man is simply LOOSE in Germany, and chat, I clapped. actual applause. gone means solved, right? anyway my body immediately filed for bankruptcy: nervous fever, several months, Henry nursed me the entire time. we do not deserve Clerval.

beats.title: William
beats.modern: letter from dad. reading it on stream, why not. ...chat. William is dead. my baby brother. someone strangled him in the park at Plainpalais and took the locket with mom's picture off his neck. he was playing hide and seek. Henry's ordering the horses. stream is going home to Geneva. no jokes today. F's in chat for William, and I mean it.
beats.quote: “William is dead!—that sweet child, whose smiles delighted and warmed my heart, who was so gentle, yet so gay! Victor, he is murdered!

beats.title: Storm Receipts
beats.modern: midnight, massive storm, I walk to the spot where William died. lightning flash. HE'S THERE. him. my creature, two years off the grid, standing at my brother's murder site. he did it, chat. I know it in my spine. and I can tell NO ONE, because 'the eight foot man I built from corpses did it' is a sentence that ends with me in an asylum. so I'm going home to sit at the family table and say nothing. the silence starts now and I already hate it.
beats.quote: Nothing in human shape could have destroyed the fair child.

beats.title: The Locket Trial
beats.modern: they arrested JUSTINE for it. our Justine. she half raised William. the evidence: mom's locket, found in her pocket. chat, he PLANTED it. my creature framed a sleeping girl for his murder. Elizabeth stood up in open court and vouched with her whole soul, and the crowd hated Justine MORE for it. I sat there holding the actual answer and said nothing, because the answer sounds insane. the ballots came back all black. condemned.
beats.quote: The tortures of the accused did not equal mine; she was sustained by innocence, but the fangs of remorse tore my bosom and would not forgo their hold.

beats.title: The False Confession
beats.modern: we visited her cell the night before. she told us the truth: she DID confess, because her priest threatened her with hellfire until she signed a lie. an innocent girl bullied into writing her own guilt. she spent her last night comforting US. 'live, and be happy, and make others so.' they hanged her in the morning. that's two dead, chat. William, then Justine. both mine. I built the thing that did this because I wanted to be a god so badly.
beats.quote: “I did confess, but I confessed a lie.

beats.title: The Glacier Interview
beats.modern: climbed the glacier to feel something and HE found ME, vaulting ice crevices at superhuman speed. I charged him. he dodged, effortless, and then hit me with the hardest line I've ever taken on stream: I should have been your Adam, I am your fallen angel instead. he says he was born GOOD and misery made him this. he wants one hour. so we're in a mountain hut, he lit the fire, and I'm about to hear my son's side of the story. strangest collab of my life.
beats.quote: Remember that I am thy creature; I ought to be thy Adam, but I am rather the fallen angel, whom thou drivest from joy for no misdeed.

beats.title: The Ember Grab
beats.modern: ok chat, his side. day one of being alive: light hurt, dark scared him, hunger had no name, he sat down and cried. then he found a fire some beggars left and was so delighted he GRABBED THE LIVE EMBERS with his bare hand. his review: how strange, that the same cause should produce such opposite effects. he speedran the scientific method off one burn. I skipped his tutorial and he built it himself.
beats.quote: In my joy I thrust my hand into the live embers, but quickly drew it out again with a cry of pain.

beats.title: The Village Speedrun
beats.modern: he walks into a village hoping for breakfast. children shriek, a woman faints, and the whole town instantly picks up rocks. full mob, zero dialogue attempted. he escapes to a low wooden hovel stuck to the back of a cottage, barely tall enough to sit up in, and calls it an agreeable asylum. chat, an entire server jumped him for having a face, and his patch notes said 'nice shed.' I'm listening to this in the hut feeling my organs drop.

beats.title: The Secret Santa Arc
beats.modern: he's been watching the cottage family through a chink in the wall for months. update from inside the wall: they're POOR. the young ones skip meals so the blind old father can eat. so what does the 'monster' do? stops stealing their food that instant, lives on berries, and starts chopping their firewood at night, anonymously. the girl opens the door, finds a mystery wood pile, and Felix gets a whole day off. chat. my creature invented secret santa. and I left him in a forest to die.

beats.title: The Pool Jumpscare
beats.modern: months of admiring the beautiful cottage family, and then he catches his reflection in a clear pool. he tells me he started BACK from it. could not believe the reflection was him. imagine learning what you look like from a pond, at full adult size, alone. imagine finding out you're the jumpscare. I chose every part of that face, chat. I picked it off tables. mute the jokes for a second.
beats.quote: when I became fully convinced that I was in reality the monster that I am, I was filled with the bitterest sensations of despondence and mortification.

beats.title: The Woodland Library
beats.modern: he found a lost suitcase of books in the woods and gave himself a liberal arts degree. the syllabus: Werther for the sadness, Plutarch for the greatness, and Paradise Lost, which he read as NONFICTION. straight documentary. his takeaway: like Adam, created and connected to nothing, except Adam got a god who answered, and an Eve. so he identifies with Satan instead. at least Satan had friends, chat. his words. the reading is unfortunately airtight.
beats.quote: Like Adam, I was apparently united by no link to any other being in existence;

beats.title: The Build Log
beats.modern: the coat he grabbed the night he was born? mine. in the pocket: my LAB JOURNAL. four months of build notes, in my handwriting, including exactly how repulsive I found him while I was assembling him. he read his own creation written up as a horror story. 'hateful day when I received life' is his review of my diary. chat, the craziest lore drop of his life was learning his dad kept receipts of the disgust. I have no defense. keep the clip.
beats.quote: ‘Hateful day when I received life!’

beats.title: The Blind Man Gambit
beats.modern: the plan, one year in the making: talk to the blind father while the family is out. and it WORKS. the old man can't see him, only hear him, and tells him the hearts of men are full of brotherly love and charity. the first kind words of his entire existence, chat. then the door opens. Agatha faints. Safie runs. and Felix beats him off his own father with a stick. he could have torn Felix in half. he took the blows and crawled back to the wall.
beats.quote: the hearts of men, when unprejudiced by any obvious self-interest, are full of brotherly love and charity.

beats.title: The Cottage Bonfire
beats.modern: the family MOVED OUT. abandoned the whole cottage over one look at him. his single thread to the human race, cut by the humans. so he howled in the woods all night, waited for the moon to go down, and danced around the cottage with a burning branch until it was all flame. then the declaration, his words: everlasting war against the species. plus one name at the top of the list. mine. the redemption arc is gone, chat, and I'm the one who bricked it.
beats.quote: I, like the arch-fiend, bore a hell within me,

beats.title: The Rescue Reward
beats.modern: on the road to Geneva he sees a girl slip into a river. heavy current. he dives, wrestles the water, drags her out alive. then her guardian arrives, grabs her, and SHOOTS HIM. a bullet in the shoulder for a completed rescue. he spent weeks alone in the woods digging around a musket ball. his words: this was then the reward of my benevolence. chat, every time I build a counterargument, the story eats it.
beats.quote: “This was then the reward of my benevolence!

beats.title: The Fatal Surname
beats.modern: then the part I already knew. a beautiful boy runs past his hiding spot. his idea: a child is too young to be prejudiced, maybe THIS one can be his friend. the boy screams monster, ogre, and then drops the fatal word: his papa is M. FRANKENSTEIN. my name flipped the switch. my little brother died for my surname. and the locket went into a sleeping girl's dress so mankind's own laws would finish the job. that girl was Justine. there's no joke here. there is no joke here.
beats.quote: ‘I too can create desolation; my enemy is not invulnerable;

beats.title: The Bride Commission
beats.modern: his terms: build him a wife. as hideous as him, his words, so they can vanish to the wilds of South America and live on acorns and berries. I said no. he said, I am malicious because I am miserable. and chat, I hate that the logic holds. option A: he works at my destruction until I curse the hour of my birth. option B: I build her and they disappear forever. I consented. I am now taking commissions. what could possibly go wrong with monster number two.
beats.quote: I am malicious because I am miserable. Am I not shunned and hated by all mankind?

beats.title: The Save the Date
beats.modern: wife number two, half assembled, and I'm spiraling at the bench: what if she hates him? what if they BREED? a race of devils, propagated forever, signed me. then I look up. he's AT THE WINDOW. ghastly grin. watching. and I tore her to pieces in front of him. he howled and vanished... then broke into my house at midnight to deliver exactly one line. 'I shall be with you on your wedding-night.' and left. that's it. that's the whole visit. chat, he sent me a save the date.
beats.quote: “It is well. I go; but remember, I shall be with you on your wedding-night.”

beats.title: The Irish Beach
beats.modern: rowed out at 3am and dumped the... remains... in the sea. the wind took me, I drifted all night, landed in Ireland, and got arrested ON THE BEACH. a man was strangled here last night. black finger marks on the neck. his signature. they walked me to the body for the reaction test, and chat. it's Henry. it's CLERVAL. the man who nursed me through months of fever, dead for knowing me. that's three. I woke up two months later in an Irish prison, raving.
beats.quote: “Have my murderous machinations deprived you also, my dearest Henry, of life?

beats.title: Armed at the Altar
beats.modern: wedding day. I married Elizabeth, chat. childhood promise fulfilled, mom's wish fulfilled, the happiest day still available to me. and I did it carrying PISTOLS AND A DAGGER, because 'I shall be with you on your wedding-night' obviously means me. he kills ME tonight. I've accepted it. so we sailed across the lake in perfect weather, and I sat next to my brand new wife running threat assessments behind my eyes. keep her safe, survive the night, deal with him. solid plan. airtight plan.

beats.title: The Wedding Night
beats.modern: I sent her to our room so she wouldn't have to see the fight. that's the decision I made. I patrolled the halls with the pistol. every corridor. every corner. then the scream. from our room. chat, it was never me. it was NEVER me. she's thrown across the bed and she's not moving, and he's at the window, grinning, pointing at her with one finger. I fired. I hit lake water. Elizabeth is gone. chat. Elizabeth is gone.
beats.quote: She was there, lifeless and inanimate, thrown across the bed, her head hanging down and her pale and distorted features half covered by her hair.

beats.title: The Last Straw
beats.modern: the news stopped my father's heart in slow motion. he died in my arms within days. that's five, if you're keeping count. and they put ME in a madhouse for months, for saying the truth out loud. when I got out I did it properly: magistrate, full deposition, dates, evidence, calm delivery. he listened. he even shuddered in the right places. and then he soothed me, quote, as a nurse does a child. understood. no more institutions, chat. I'll be the consequence myself.

beats.title: The Graveyard Oath
beats.modern: knelt at the family plot. William, my father, Elizabeth, all in one place, and me still standing. I kissed the ground and swore, by the night and the spirits, to hunt him until one of us dies in the fight. and out of the dark: LAUGHTER. huge, fiendish, echoing off the mountains. then his whisper right at my ear: I am satisfied, miserable wretch. you have determined to live. chat. he WANTED the vow. my revenge quest is his favorite show. we begin.
beats.quote: “I am satisfied, miserable wretch! You have determined to live, and I am satisfied.”

beats.title: The Dead Hare
beats.modern: months of pursuit across Russia, and here's the thing: he leaves me MESSAGES. carved into tree bark, cut into stone. 'my reign is not yet over.'
