'follow me.' and when I'm starving in the snow, he leaves FOOD. an actual dead hare with a note: eat and be refreshed, come on, my enemy. chat, he is keeping me alive so the chase doesn't end. I'm being kited across the planet by my own creation and he's dropping supply crates. and I eat the hare. what else is there.
beats.quote: You will find near this place, if you follow not too tardily, a dead hare; eat and be refreshed. Come on, my enemy; we have yet to wrestle for our lives,

beats.title: The Ice Split
beats.modern: I HAD HIM. one mile between us on the frozen ocean, dogs at full sprint. then the sea split the ice with a sound like an earthquake and put open water between us. my dogs died. my raft shrank under me for hours. and then this ship appeared, which is where you came in, chat. so now you're caught up. Walton, you're in the will: if I die, he does not escape. swear it. put the steel in, and I will hover near and aim it for you.
beats.quote: swear to me, Walton, that he shall not escape, that you will seek him and satisfy my vengeance in his death.

beats.title: The Mutiny Speech
beats.modern: the sailors came down in a delegation: swear we turn south the moment the ice frees us, captain. reasonable. men are dying. and then I, a man who cannot stand unassisted, ROSE off this bed and gave the speech of my life. be men, or be MORE than men. this ice cannot withstand you if you say it shall not. they left shaking with hype, chat. one skill remains on this account and it's turning frostbitten sailors into believers. then I fell over. worth it.
beats.quote: Oh! Be men, or be more than men. Be steady to your purposes and firm as a rock. This ice is not made of such stuff as your hearts may be;

beats.title: The Final Clip
beats.modern: last clip, chat. the surgeon says hours. so, exit interview with myself: reviewing the whole run, I mostly do not find my conduct blamable, which tells you the patient is still sick. Walton got my actual final patch notes: seek happiness in tranquility and avoid ambition, even the innocent looking science kind. that's the whole cautionary tale. I touched the deepest mystery there is and it cost me every person I loved. the dead are here now. they look happy to see me. gg. it's Walton's channel now.
beats.quote: Seek happiness in tranquillity and avoid ambition, even if it be only the apparently innocent one of distinguishing yourself in science and discoveries.

beats.title: The Funeral Pile
beats.modern: Walton here. final upload. I walked in on HIM, eight feet of grief hunched over the body, begging a dead man for a pardon. he's done: no more victims, his series is wound to its close. the plan is an ice raft north, then a funeral pile, ashes into the sea. 'he is dead who called me into being.' then he went out the window onto the ice and the dark took him. no body. no sequel. F in chat for everybody.
beats.quote: I shall ascend my funeral pile triumphantly and exult in the agony of the torturing flames.

beats.title: The Title Card
beats.modern: chat the title card just spoiled the WHOLE run. it says two lovers die. it says it in the INTRO. they put my death in the opening cinematic. two families beefing so long nobody remembers why, and me and some girl I haven't met yet are the price. enjoy the stream I guess.
beats.quote: A pair of star-cross’d lovers take their life;

beats.title: The Thumb War
beats.modern: pulling up the clip: a Capulet bit his thumb at my cousin's boys. that's it. that's the whole provocation. swords OUT in the street, old man Capulet screaming for his longsword while his wife offers him a crutch instead. now the Prince says the next brawl is a death sentence. this server is one report away from a wipe.
beats.quote: Do you bite your thumb at us, sir?

beats.title: The Rosaline Arc
beats.modern: day forty of the Rosaline arc. she took a chastity vow, chat. she has sworn off the entire genre. Benvolio keeps saying 'just look at other girls' like I'm not the most loyal simp on this platform. I am in love forever with a woman who has me on read. this is my life now.
beats.quote: Why, then, O brawling love! O loving hate!

beats.title: The Party Crash
beats.modern: Benvolio's galaxy brain plan: sneak into the CAPULET party tonight, enemy headquarters, so I can compare Rosaline to other girls and get over her. he swears he'll make my swan look like a crow. fine. I'm going, but purely to stare at Rosaline. masks on. what could go wrong at the rival guild's house party.
beats.quote: Compare her face with some that I shall show, And I will make thee think thy swan a crow.

beats.title: The Queen Mab Filibuster
beats.modern: I said 'I had a weird dream' and Mercutio has been going for FIVE MINUTES about a tiny fairy who drives a hazelnut chariot over sleeping people's noses. nobody asked. he's still going. chat he's describing her WAGON PARTS now. I love this man so much. also I have a genuinely horrible feeling about tonight. anyway, party time.
beats.quote: O, then, I see Queen Mab hath been with you.

beats.title: First Sight
beats.modern: HOLD ON. hold the whole stream. who the hell is THAT. Rosaline who? I don't know a Rosaline. delete the last forty days of VODs. meanwhile some guy clocked my voice through the mask and is screaming for his rapier, and the HOST shut him down at his own party to protect my vibe. thanks king. nothing is ruining tonight.
beats.quote: Did my heart love till now? Forswear it, sight! For I ne’er saw true beauty till this night.

beats.title: Kiss by the Book
beats.modern: went up and opened with the holy pilgrim material. she MATCHED it, chat. took my metaphor and countered it mid-verse. we built a whole sonnet together in real time and then I kissed her. then I found a technicality and kissed her again. she says I kiss 'by the book.' best stream of my life.
beats.quote: Then move not while my prayer’s effect I take. Thus from my lips, by thine my sin is purg’d.

beats.title: The Reveal
beats.modern: the Nurse just hit me with the lore drop from hell: she's a CAPULET. the boss's only daughter. and her cam caught the mirror moment, her finding out I'm a Montague: 'my only love sprung from my only hate.' matchmaking put me in the one house I can't touch and dropped the love of my life inside it.
beats.quote: My only love sprung from my only hate! Too early seen unknown, and known too late!

beats.title: The Balcony Lurk
beats.modern: update: I hopped the orchard wall. this is kill on sight territory. she's on her balcony talking to herself and chat, it's about ME. she's asking the night sky why my name has to be the one problem, telling me to deny my father. she has no idea I'm in the bushes. do I say something. DO I SAY SOMETHING.
beats.quote: O Romeo, Romeo, wherefore art thou Romeo? Deny thy father and refuse thy name.

beats.title: The Marriage Speedrun
beats.modern: I said something. she didn't scream, she basically PROPOSED: if I'm serious, send word tomorrow and she'll marry me. tomorrow. I met her six hours ago. and neither of us can end the call. she keeps coming back to the window, I keep not leaving. 'parting is such sweet sorrow.' we are not beating the down bad allegations.
beats.quote: If that thy bent of love be honourable, Thy purpose marriage, send me word tomorrow,

beats.title: Ratioed by a Monk
beats.modern: took it to my priest at dawn. Friar Lawrence immediately pulled the receipts: weren't you crying about Rosaline YESTERDAY? the tear stains are still on your face? ratioed by a monk before breakfast. but he said yes, because he thinks this wedding might end the whole family war. one condition: go wisely and slow. chat I have never done anything slow in my life.
beats.quote: Holy Saint Francis! What a change is here! Is Rosaline, that thou didst love so dear, So soon forsaken?

beats.title: The Wedding
beats.modern: WEDDING STREAM. day two of knowing each other. the officiant's toast was 'these violent delights have violent ends,' which is an unhinged thing to say at a wedding, king of vibes as always. don't care. we're married. secret married. nobody in either family knows. the run is going PERFECTLY.
beats.quote: These violent delights have violent ends, And in their triumph die; like fire and powder, Which as they kiss consume.

beats.title: Mercutio Down
beats.modern: Tybalt called me out and I just took it, chat. I can't fight my wife's cousin and nobody knows that's what he is. so Mercutio answered for me. Tybalt got him UNDER MY ARM while I was breaking it up. he's dying and still doing bits: 'ask for me tomorrow and you shall find me a grave man.' punning on the way out. he cursed both our houses. he's gone. my best friend died carrying my secret.
beats.quote: Ask for me tomorrow, and you shall find me a grave man.

beats.title: Fortune's Fool
beats.modern: Tybalt came back doing a victory lap while Mercutio was still warm and something in me just fucking snapped. it's done. he's down. and now it lands: I killed my wife's cousin on day two of the marriage. 'O, I am fortune's fool.' Benvolio is screaming at me to run. clip it, chat. that's the run dying right there.
beats.quote: O, I am fortune’s fool!

beats.title: The Ban
beats.modern: verdict: not execution. banished from Verona. the Friar keeps calling that MERCY and I'm face down on his floor telling him there is no world outside these walls. every cat, dog, and carrion fly gets to look at Juliet and I don't. yes chat, I know a temp ban beats a perma. no, I will not be behaving rationally about it.
beats.quote: There is no world without Verona walls, But purgatory, torture, hell itself.

beats.title: The Lark Argument
beats.modern: one night as actual married people and now we're arguing about a bird. she says nightingale, meaning I can stay. I say lark, meaning I leave or I die at sunrise. so I offered to just stay and die and she INSTANTLY switched sides: it is the lark, GO. last thing she says while I climb down is that I look like a dead man at the bottom of a tomb. cool. cool cool. see you soon, wife.
beats.quote: It was the lark, the herald of the morn, No nightingale.

beats.title: Juliet Cam: The Meltdown
beats.modern: Juliet here. dad announced I'm marrying Paris on THURSDAY. I said no one time and he went full caps lock: hang, beg, starve, die in the streets. mom is done with me. and the Nurse, my day one, my whole childhood, just told me to forget Romeo because Paris has nicer eyes. everyone in this house is blocked. the Friar is the last name on my list.
beats.quote: Hang thee young baggage, disobedient wretch!

beats.title: Juliet Cam: The Plan
beats.modern: the Friar's plan, and I need you to hear the WHOLE thing: I drink this vial and read as dead for 42 hours. no pulse, no breath. they bury me in the family crypt, Romeo gets a letter explaining everything, he's waiting when I respawn, and we leave for Mantua together. the entire plan has exactly one point of failure and it's 'Romeo gets a letter.' give me the vial.
beats.quote: Take thou this vial, being then in bed, And this distilled liquor drink thou off,

beats.title: Juliet Cam: Bottoms Up
beats.modern: alone. vial in hand. brain speedrunning every worst case: what if it's actual poison. what if I wake up early, sealed in the dark with a hundred years of ancestors and Tybalt two days into decomposing, and lose my mind before anyone comes. okay. okay okay okay. Romeo, this one's for you. chugging.
beats.quote: Romeo, Romeo, Romeo, here’s drink! I drink to thee.

beats.title: The News
beats.modern: Balthasar just rode in from Verona. chat. Juliet's dead. he watched them lay her in the family crypt. no letter from the Friar, no explanation, nothing. ...'then I defy you, stars.' I'm buying horses. I'm going home tonight. chat is spamming something in all caps and I am not reading it. this stream is over, I just haven't ended it yet.
beats.quote: Is it even so? Then I defy you, stars!

beats.title: The Pharmacist
beats.modern: found an apothecary so broke his shop decor is one stuffed alligator. selling this stuff is a death sentence in Mantua and he still took the forty ducats. 'my poverty, but not my will consents.' told him the gold is the real poison and to go buy food. one vial, strong enough for twenty men. you already know what it's for. don't ask me anything else.
beats.quote: My poverty, but not my will consents.

beats.title: The Lost Letter
beats.modern: the editors are inserting this clip so the VOD makes sense: the Friar's letter, the one explaining the fake death, never left Verona. the courier stopped at a plague house and the town sealed him inside. quarantine. 'I could not send it, here it is again.' the message that fixes everything, returned to sender. Romeo is already on the road. chat knew. only chat knew.
beats.quote: I could not send it,—here it is again,— Nor get a messenger to bring it thee, So fearful were they of infection.

beats.title: Paris at the Tomb
beats.modern: Paris is at her tomb with flowers. of course he is. he thinks I'm here to desecrate it. I begged him, chat. tempt not a desperate man. walk away. I like you better than I like me. he swung anyway. ...he's down. his last request was to be laid next to her, so I'm carrying him in myself. everyone this feud touches ends up in this room.
beats.quote: Good gentle youth, tempt not a desperate man.

beats.title: Thus With a Kiss
beats.modern: she doesn't look dead. that's the thing, chat. her lips are still red. death took her and couldn't leave a single mark on her. ...I know what chat is typing. I'm not reading it. eyes, look your last. arms, take your last embrace. here's to my love. gg.
beats.quote: O true apothecary! Thy drugs are quick. Thus with a kiss I die.

beats.title: Juliet Cam: Four Minutes
beats.modern: I wake up ON TIME. the plan worked PERFECTLY on my end. and he's right here. cup still in his hand. he drank all of it, chat. didn't leave one friendly drop for me. his lips are still warm. WARM. I missed him by minutes. ...the guards are coming up the stairs. it's okay. this part is easy. happy dagger.
beats.quote: O churl. Drink all, and left no friendly drop To help me after? I will kiss thy lips.

beats.title: The Golden Statues
beats.modern: final clip on the channel. the watch found them. the Prince read Romeo's last letter out loud so both fathers heard the whole story at once, standing over everything their beef cost. handshake, over the bodies. they're building the two of them golden statues, side by side, each raised by the other's father. the war patch shipped. it only cost the two players who never wanted to fight. stream offline. F in chat, forever.
beats.quote: For never was a story of more woe Than this of Juliet and her Romeo.

beats.title: The Room Situation
beats.modern: chat we've been SCAMMED. the landlady promised south rooms with a view over the river. we got north rooms facing a courtyard, and the dinner meat has definitely already been soup. now Charlotte and I are locked in a politeness duel over who gets the view neither of us has. she insists I take it. I insist she takes it. nobody wins. that's the whole game.

beats.title: I Have a View
beats.modern: an old man just leaned across the dinner table INTO our private argument and offered us his rooms. him and his son George have the views, and he's like, take them, we'll swap. Charlotte is treating this like an attempted mugging. the son says it's obvious we should have the rooms, there's nothing else to say. correct?? but apparently truth is rude here.
beats.quote: “I have a view, I have a view.”

beats.title: Unequal to the Bath
beats.modern: update: the vicar brokered the room swap. Charlotte, in defeat, demanded to thank Mr. Emerson PERSONALLY, full ceremony. instead the son walks in and announces his father is in his bath. chat. her entire diplomacy build has no counter for bath. one word and every barbed civility came out wrong end first. George wins the lobby.
beats.quote: Miss Bartlett was unequal to the bath. All her barbed civilities came forth wrong end first.

beats.title: The Question Mark
beats.modern: Charlotte just did a security sweep of her new room, checked where the cupboards lead, looked for secret entrances, normal chaperone things. and pinned over the washstand she found a big sheet of paper with one ENORMOUS question mark scrawled on it. nothing else. she stared at it by candlelight until it became menacing, then filed it between blotting paper like evidence. what does it MEAN, chat.
beats.quote: she saw, pinned up over the washstand, a sheet of paper on which was scrawled an enormous note of interrogation. Nothing more.

beats.title: My Guide Stole My Guidebook
beats.modern: toured with Miss Lavish today, a novelist who confiscated my guidebook because we will simply drift. we drifted into the wrong quarter for an hour. then she spotted a man she calls her local colour box, sprinted across the square, and VANISHED down a side street. with my guidebook. I'm now alone in a huge cold church and I cannot remember one fact about it.

beats.title: Built by Faith Indeed
beats.modern: found the Emersons inside the church. a lecturer is telling his tour group Santa Croce was built by faith, and old Mr. Emerson yells across the chapel that it just means the workmen weren't paid properly. then he starts fact checking a fresco, out loud, at volume. the entire congregation filed out in silence. this man heckles CHURCHES.
beats.quote: Built by faith indeed! That simply means the workmen weren’t paid properly.

beats.title: The Everlasting Yes
beats.modern: the old man cornered me with a side quest, chat. his son is sad because the things of the universe don't fit. he wants ME to help George realize that beside the everlasting Why there is a Yes. a man handed me his son's entire soul and I panicked and suggested stamp collecting. then I laughed. WHY did I laugh.
beats.quote: Make him realize that by the side of the everlasting Why there is a Yes—a transitory Yes if you like, but a Yes.”

beats.title: The Beethoven Report
beats.modern: rainy afternoon, so I played Beethoven for the pension. the vicar's review just dropped: if I ever start LIVING the way I PLAY, it will be very exciting for everybody. chat what is that supposed to mean. I play like victory and live like an apology and he said it to my face, politely, over tea. clipped forever.
beats.quote: “If Miss Honeychurch ever takes to live as she plays, it will be very exciting both for us and for her.”

beats.title: Man Down in the Piazza
beats.modern: I went out alone at dusk because I wanted something to HAPPEN. two Italians were arguing over five lire by the loggia. one of them turned and looked at me like he had a message for me, and then blood came out of his mouth. stabbed. I fainted straight into George Emerson's arms. I asked the game for content and it sent a death.
beats.quote: She had complained of dullness, and lo! one man was stabbed, and another held her in his arms.

beats.title: The Photo Situation
beats.modern: George walked me home and mid conversation he YEETED something into the river. my photographs. the ones I dropped when I fainted. they were covered in the dying man's blood and he didn't know what to do with them, so they've gone out to sea. then he goes quiet and says something tremendous has happened and he means to find out what it is. sir, the tremendous thing was a murder. right? chat. right?
beats.quote: “For something tremendous has happened; I must face it without getting muddled. It isn’t exactly that a man has died.”

beats.title: I Shall Want to Live
beats.modern: we stopped at the parapet and I did damage control, made him swear never to tell the pension gossips I fainted. he barely registered it. I said how quickly these accidents happen, and then one returns to the old life. he said: I don't. I shall probably want to live. chat I came to manage a PR incident and this man is having a whole rebirth over the Arno.
beats.quote: “I shall want to live, I say.”

beats.title: The Allegation
beats.modern: souvenir shopping with our chaplain Mr. Eager. I defended the Emersons for exactly one sentence and he snapped and announced, in the shop, that Mr. Emerson MURDERED HIS WIFE. in the sight of God. no details, no evidence, will not elaborate. Charlotte defused the situation by purchasing a picture of the Leaning Tower. hardest lore drop of the trip and we just kept shopping.
beats.quote: For that man has murdered his wife in the sight of God.”

beats.title: War Not With the May
beats.modern: carriage ride into the hills. our driver brought his girlfriend, claimed she was his sister, and drove one handed the whole climb. Mr. Eager caught them kissing and held a tribunal on a moving carriage. the girl got ejected. old Emerson called it defeat, we have parted two people who were happy, then started quoting a poet: don't go fighting against the Spring. I'm supposed to disapprove. I keep almost clapping.
beats.quote: “Do we find happiness so often that we should turn it off the box when it happens to sit there?

beats.title: The Violet Terrace
beats.modern: I asked the driver, in broken Italian, where the good men were. he walked me through the bushes and the ground GAVE WAY and I fell out of the wood onto an open terrace covered end to end in violets, blue running downhill like water. and standing at the edge of it was not the vicar. it was George. he looked at me like I'd fallen out of heaven, stepped forward, and kissed me. and then Charlotte's voice. calling my name. brown against the view.
beats.quote: He saw radiant joy in her face, he saw the flowers beat against her dress in blue waves. The bushes above them closed. He stepped quickly forward and kissed her.

beats.title: The Tribunal
beats.modern: Charlotte convened a hearing in her room by candlelight. agenda: how do we SILENCE him. she has met his type before, apparently they collect exploits. my motion to simply talk to George myself: denied. then she cried out for a real man to avenge me, we are only two women, and started pulling her rings off like armor. verdict: the eight o'clock train to Rome. we are fleeing the country over a kiss.
beats.quote: “Oh, for a real man! We are only two women, you and I.

beats.title: The Guilt Trip
beats.modern: midnight packing, and Charlotte deployed her ultimate: how will you ever forgive me. chat she ran the FULL routine. she's a failure, she's old and uninteresting, she's only fit to pack my things, my mother will never forgive her. by the end I was consoling HER, and somehow I swore to never tell anyone what happened. not even mom. I got out hugged and out negotiated in the same move.

beats.title: The Permission Rounds
beats.modern: timeskip, chat. home in England. new character: Cecil Vyse, currently on proposal attempt number three. lore from the drawing room: he asked my mother's permission first, then asked my LITTLE BROTHER for his blessing, and Freddy said no. to his face. then had to laugh like it was a joke. my whole family ran a council vote on my love life while I sat in the garden.
beats.quote: “I said to Cecil, ‘Take her or leave her; it’s no business of mine!’”

beats.title: The Gothic Statue
beats.modern: I said yes. engagement arc is live. Cecil is tall, refined, well read, well connected, and the best description anyone has for him is medieval, like a Gothic statue. chat. a Gothic statue. the kind of saint that guards a cathedral door. things that guard doors do not let things through. anyway, I'm happy. this is me being happy.
beats.quote: He was medieval. Like a Gothic statue.

beats.title: The Permission Kiss
beats.modern: my fiancé just asked, out loud, with words, whether he may kiss me. I said of course you may, you might have before, I can't exactly run at you. so he approached, visibly wished he could retreat, and his gold glasses got SMUSHED flat between our faces. that was it. that was our first kiss. eyewear was harmed. he's been replaying a cooler version in his head ever since. so have I. a very different version.
beats.quote: As he touched her, his gold pince-nez became dislodged and was flattened between them.

beats.title: The Tenants
beats.modern: garden ball game, and Freddy drops it mid tackle: the villa down the road has new tenants. name of Emerson. friends of CECIL. chat, appreciate my position here. I fled Florence. I crossed a continent. I got engaged. I built a whole new save file. and my own fiancé has imported the exact boy I was fleeing into the house down the road.
beats.quote: “Emerson. I’ll bet you anything you like.”

beats.title: Victory for the Comic Muse
beats.modern: confronted Cecil and it's worse than betrayal, it's a BIT. he met two strangers in the National Gallery, learned they wanted a cottage, and planted them in the villa purely to grief our snob landlord. he's SO proud. keeps announcing he won a great victory for the Comic Muse. babe. you didn't win anything. you spawned my past onto the map as a joke on a man you don't even like.
beats.quote: I, even I, have found tenants for the distressful Cissie Villa. Don’t be angry! Don’t be angry! You’ll forgive me when you hear it all.”

beats.title: The Honeychurch Taint
beats.modern: meet the in laws stream. Cecil's mother hosted a dinner of the grandchildren of famous people, and I played Schumann. the after hours review, which I was definitely not supposed to hear: Lucy is becoming wonderful. she is purging off the Honeychurch taint. the TAINT, chat. my family is a taint she is purging. then I woke up screaming from a nightmare and she kissed me goodnight like everything is fine. it's fine. everything is fine.
beats.quote: she is purging off the Honeychurch taint, most excellent Honeychurches, but you know what I mean.

beats.title: Come and Have a Bathe
beats.modern: my brother Freddy just met George Emerson for the first time. the complete introduction, verbatim: how d'ye do? come and have a bathe. that's it. no names, no weather, straight to pond. George said all right. the vicar rated it the best conversational opening he's ever heard. men found a cheat code and it's water.
beats.quote: “How d’ye do? Come and have a bathe.”

beats.title: The Sacred Lake Incident
beats.modern: took mom and Cecil on a genteel walk and rounded the corner into my brother, our VICAR, and George playing naked football with their own clothes. screaming. soaked. the vicar's waistcoat was lying in the path like a casualty. George, wearing essentially a hat, looked me dead in the eye and went hullo, Miss Honeychurch! mom said better bow. so I bowed, chat. I BOWED.
beats.quote: Barefoot, bare-chested, radiant and personable against the shadowy woods, he called: “Hullo, Miss Honeychurch! Hullo!”

beats.title: The Boiler
beats.modern: Charlotte's boiler is being replaced, so mom wants her to STAY WITH US. I fought it in open court: we're full, Minnie can sleep in the bath, I don't like Charlotte, I admit it's horrid of me. mom's closing argument: you two have each other and the woods, poor Charlotte has only plumbers. motion carried. the single person alive who knows about Italy is moving into my house.
beats.quote: “I suppose Miss Bartlett must come, since she boils eggs so well,”

beats.title: Chapter Two
beats.modern: Sunday tennis, and Cecil insists on reading a trashy Florence romance at us. the author is Miss Lavish. chapter two: a heroine on a hillside carpeted with violets, and Antonio steals up behind her and simply enfolds her in his manly arms. that's MY hillside, chat. Cecil is reading my own secret out loud, to me AND to George, and thinks the funny part is the prose. then in the shrubbery on the way in, George did it again.
beats.quote: “‘There came from his lips no wordy protestation such as formal lovers use. No eloquence was his, nor did he suffer from the lack of it. He simply enfolded her in his manly arms.’”

beats.title: You Told the Novelist
beats.modern: summoned Charlotte. asked how the violets, the hillside, and Florence in the distance got into Eleanor Lavish's novel. she cracked in under a minute: she told her. over tea in Rome. the woman who swore me to eternal silence, who wouldn't let me tell MY OWN MOTHER, briefed a professional novelist. and her official response is that SHE will never forgive Eleanor. she leaked my secret and she's claiming the victim slot. unreal.
beats.quote: “Then never—never—never more shall Eleanor Lavish be a friend of mine.”

beats.title: The Setting Down
beats.modern: nobody else would handle George, so I did it myself, Charlotte as witness. told him to leave and never come back. he ignored the script ENTIRELY. said Cecil is for society and cultivated talk and should know no one intimately, least of all a woman. that he's the type that's kept Europe back a thousand years, forming me, telling me what's ladylike. then he said he has loved me since that man died, and left. I won the room and lost the argument.
beats.quote: “You cannot live with Vyse. He’s only for an acquaintance. He is for society and cultivated talk. He should know no one intimately, least of all a woman.”

beats.title: The Breakup
beats.modern: same evening. gave Cecil back the ring. told him he's the sort who can't know anyone intimately. that he understands beautiful things but doesn't know how to use them, that he wraps himself in art and books and music and was trying to wrap me up too. chat, I dumped my fiancé using the other man's speech, word for word, hours after throwing the other man out of the house. Cecil doesn't know the source. I know the source.
beats.quote: you may understand beautiful things, but you don’t know how to use them; and you wrap yourself up in art and books and music, and would try to wrap up me.

beats.title: Cecil Takes the L
beats.modern: he took it... gracefully?? no rage, no begging. he said it's true, every word, it is a revelation, it is I. thanked me SOLEMNLY for showing him what he really is. shook my hand. lit my candle for me. on the stairs he looked genuinely noble for the first time all year. nothing in his love became him like the leaving of it. why is his best content the logout screen.
beats.quote: “I must actually thank you for what you have done—for showing me what I really am. Solemnly, I thank you for showing me a true woman.

beats.title: Operation Greece
beats.modern: the elderly Alan sisters are touring Greece, and I have DEMANDED to join them. everyone assumes it's about my broken engagement. it is not about my broken engagement. I am in love with exactly one person, so the plan is to put the entire nation of Greece between us, chaperoned by two old ladies and their special digestive bread. flawless plan. no notes. nothing about this is a muddle.
beats.quote: ‘Italy is only an euphuism for Fate.’”

beats.title: How She Went Under
beats.modern: old Mr. Emerson told me how his wife really died. George caught typhoid at twelve, and the chaplain told her it was a judgement for never baptizing him. George recovered. she went under, thinking about sin. THAT is the wife he murdered in the sight of God. the rumor came from the same man who caused the grief. and I helped pass it around.
beats.quote: He made her think about sin, and she went under thinking about it.”

beats.title: You Love George
beats.modern: I mentioned Cecil isn't coming to Greece and this old man in a borrowed study just said it, out loud: you love George. body and soul, plainly, directly, as he loves you. I argued. he kept going. you can transmute love, ignore it, muddle it, but you can never pull it out of you. the poets are right, love is eternal. chat I've been lying to everyone in my life for months and the final boss was a sick old man being kind. never stood a chance in hell.
beats.quote: “You love the boy body and soul, plainly, directly, as he loves you, and no other word expresses it.

beats.title: Truth Counts
beats.modern: I broke down. told him the tickets are bought, everyone trusts me, it's all arranged. he said we fight for more than love or pleasure. there is Truth. Truth counts. and I heard my own voice say: you kiss me. I will try. that's the clip, chat. the whole year was never a travel stream. it was this.
beats.quote: “Yes, for we fight for more than Love or Pleasure; there is Truth. Truth counts, Truth does count.”

beats.title: The Same Room
beats.modern: epilogue stream. we're MARRIED. we ran off to the same pension, and George says this was his old room, the one from the very first night, the one with the view. he's on the floor with his head in my lap while I mend his sock. my family isn't speaking to us. the river is loud. the cab drivers are still menaces. worth it. all of it.
beats.quote: All the fighting that mattered had been done by others—by Italy, by his father, by his wife.

beats.title: Did She Mean It
beats.modern: final lore drop. that Sunday at the rectory, Charlotte KNEW Mr. Emerson was in the study. she saw him and went to church anyway. the room swap cop. the Rome extraction squad. the midnight tribunal judge. she left the door open on purpose and let the one man who could talk sense at me do it. George thinks that far down, below all speech and behaviour, she always hoped for us. we can never thank her. she'd deny everything. F in chat for Charlotte, the most repressed wingman of all time.
beats.quote: But I do believe that, far down in her heart, far below all speech and behaviour, she is glad.”

beats.title: The Waistcoat Rabbit
beats.modern: chat my sister's book has no pictures and no dialogue. zero content. I'm bored out of my mind. wait. WAIT. a rabbit just ran past in a WAISTCOAT. he checked a pocket watch. he said he's late. I'm following him. he went down a hole. going in. no exit strategy. we'll figure it out live.
beats.quote: “Oh dear! Oh dear! I shall be late!”

beats.title: Still Falling
beats.modern: update: still falling. it's been ten minutes. this hole has BOOKSHELVES in the walls. grabbed a jar of marmalade on the way down. empty. worst loot spawn ever. got so bored I started debating whether cats eat bats. do bats eat cats? unclear. aaand I've landed on a pile of sticks. totally fine. the rabbit's getting away, let's move.
beats.quote: “Do cats eat bats? Do cats eat bats?”

beats.title: Mystery Consumables
beats.modern: found a tiny door to the most beautiful garden you've ever seen. can't fit. then a bottle spawns labeled DRINK ME. I DID check it wasn't marked poison first, I'm not stupid. now I'm ten inches tall and the key is on top of a glass table I can't climb. and here's a cake that says EAT ME. if it grows me, I reach the key. if it shrinks me, I slide under the door. either way I win. eating the mystery cake, chat.
beats.quote: round the neck of the bottle was a paper label, with the words “DRINK ME,” beautifully printed on it in large letters.

beats.title: Curiouser and Curiouser
beats.modern: curiouser and curiouser. I'm nine feet tall now. I literally said GOODBYE to my own feet. they're so far away I'm planning to mail them new boots every Christmas. hit my head on the ceiling, still can't fit through the door, and I cried so hard there's now a pool four inches deep flooding the hall. told myself a great girl like you, stop crying. did not stop.
beats.quote: “Curiouser and curiouser!”

beats.title: Swimming in My Own Tears
beats.modern: the fan I picked up was cursed. shrank me back down to nothing. dropped it just in time or I'd have blinked out of existence. then I slipped, and chat, I am now swimming in the pool of tears I cried when I was nine feet tall. instant karma. there's a mouse in here. I brought up my cat. twice. then dogs. it's swimming away from me. gg, no social skills in any universe.
beats.quote: “I shall be punished for it now, I suppose, by being drowned in my own tears!

beats.title: Everybody Has Won
beats.modern: a dodo just invented a sport. run in a circle, start whenever you want, stop whenever you want. after half an hour he yells the race is over and rules that EVERYBODY has won and all must have prizes. the prizes came out of MY pocket. and my prize? my own thimble, presented back to me in a formal ceremony. they cheered. this economy is fully fake, chat.
beats.quote: “We beg your acceptance of this elegant thimble;”

beats.title: Wearing the House
beats.modern: the White Rabbit mistook me for his housemaid and ordered me to fetch his gloves. inside his house: another bottle. no label this time. drank it anyway. I have learned NOTHING this stream. immediate consequences: I am now bigger than the building. one arm out the window, one foot up the chimney. I don't live in the house. I AM the house.

beats.title: There Goes Bill
beats.modern: they're sending Bill the lizard down the chimney to evict me. chat. my foot is already IN the chimney. I hear scratching... one clean kick. THERE GOES BILL. the entire crowd outside is narrating his flight path. he's alive. his official testimony: something came at him and he went up like a rocket. that something was my foot. F in chat for Bill.
beats.quote: you—all I know is, something comes at me like a Jack-in-the-box, and up I goes like a sky-rocket!”

beats.title: Who Are You
beats.modern: a caterpillar on top of a mushroom, three inches tall, smoking a hookah, just opened with 'who are YOU?' and chat... I don't know. I've been six different sizes since breakfast. I told him I can't explain myself because I'm not myself. he said that's not confusing. WE ARE THE SAME HEIGHT RIGHT NOW, SIR. then he told me to keep my temper. keeping it. barely.
beats.quote: “Keep your temper,” said the Caterpillar.

beats.title: Serpent Allegations
beats.modern: the caterpillar's exit advice: one side makes you taller, the other makes you shorter. ONE SIDE OF WHAT. THE MUSHROOM IS ROUND. bit the right side and my chin slammed into my foot. bit the left and my neck shot up above the TREES. now a pigeon is beating me up in the air screaming SERPENT. I said I'm a little girl. she said 'a likely story.' ratio'd by a bird.
beats.quote: “One side will make you grow taller, and the other side will make you grow shorter.”

beats.title: The Baby Is a Pig
beats.modern: a duchess just threw her baby at me, full overhand toss, and left to play croquet with the Queen. so I have a baby now. it keeps grunting. it has a snout. its eyes are getting weirdly small. CHAT. the baby is a PIG. it was a pig the whole time?? set it down and it trotted off into the woods. honestly? way more handsome as a pig than it ever was as a baby.
beats.quote: “it would have made a dreadfully ugly child: but it makes rather a handsome pig, I think.”

beats.title: We're All Mad Here
beats.modern: asked a floating cat for directions. 'depends a good deal on where you want to get to.' I don't much care where. 'then it doesn't matter which way you go.' genuinely unbeatable logic. his review of the whole region: we're all mad here. I'm mad. you're mad. then he vanished slowly, tail first, until only the GRIN was left. a grin. hovering. no cat attached. most unsettling NPC on the server.
beats.quote: “we’re all mad here. I’m mad. You’re mad.”

beats.title: The Riddle Has No Answer
beats.modern: found a tea party. massive table, three guys crammed into one corner screaming NO ROOM at me. there was room. sat down. the Hatter opens with a riddle: why is a raven like a writing desk? chat and I grinded this for ten minutes. gave up. asked for the answer. he hasn't the slightest idea. NEITHER DOES THE HARE. the riddle never had an answer. they farm wasted time here.
beats.quote: “Why is a raven like a writing-desk?”

beats.title: Beef With Time
beats.modern: lore drop: the Hatter has a personal beef with TIME. capital T. he sang at the Queen's concert, she screamed HE'S MURDERING THE TIME, OFF WITH HIS HEAD, and Time rage quit on him. it is now six o'clock forever. permanent tea time. no washing up, they just rotate seats as the clean cups run out. an infinite tea loop. this table is a punishment.
beats.quote: ‘He’s murdering the time! Off with his head!’”

beats.title: Painting the Roses Red
beats.modern: made it into the garden AND the gardeners are panic painting white roses red by hand. they planted the wrong rose tree. if the Queen finds out, everyone gets beheaded. chat, it's a landscaping error. the penalty for wrong flowers here is DEATH. they're speedrunning the paint job and... trumpets. she's coming. all three just threw themselves flat on their faces.
beats.quote: if the Queen was to find it out, we should all have our heads cut off, you know.

beats.title: The Nonsense Counter
beats.modern: the Queen of Hearts asked whose cards were lying face down. I said how should I know, none of my business. she went full crimson and screamed OFF WITH HER HEAD. and chat, I just said 'Nonsense!' as loud as I could. and she went QUIET. the final boss has one move and the counter is not flinching. also I stuffed the three condemned gardeners into a flower pot. the soldiers searched for two minutes and gave up. saved.
beats.quote: “Nonsense!” said Alice, very loudly and decidedly, and the Queen was silent.

beats.title: Flamingo Croquet
beats.modern: croquet patch notes: your mallet is a LIVE FLAMINGO. your ball is a LIVE HEDGEHOG. the arches are soldiers on all fours who stand up and wander off in the middle of your shot. every time I line up a swing, my flamingo twists around and looks me dead in the eye. nobody waits for turns. the Queen sentences someone to death roughly once a minute. the real wonder is that anyone's left alive. worst ranked mode ever shipped.

beats.title: Can't Behead a Head
beats.modern: the Queen ordered the Cheshire Cat executed. one problem: the cat is currently ONLY a floating head. the executioner says you can't cut off a head unless there's a body to cut it off from. the King says anything with a head can be beheaded, stop talking nonsense. the Queen says if it isn't sorted immediately, EVERYONE gets executed. peak governance. the head listened to the whole debate and quietly faded out. no body, no head, no case.
beats.quote: you couldn’t cut off a head unless there was a body to cut it off from:

beats.title: The Kayfabe Reveal
beats.modern: HOLD ON. HUGE LORE DROP. the gryphon just told me the executions are fake. direct quote: 'they never executes nobody.' NOBODY has ever actually been beheaded here. the Queen screams off with their head all day long and it has never once happened. the entire kingdom is kayfabe. every death threat this whole stream was a bit. I was scared of a tutorial boss.
beats.quote: “It’s all her fancy, that: they never executes nobody, you know.

beats.title: Reeling and Writhing
beats.modern: this turtle introduced himself by sobbing 'once, I was a real Turtle' and then went silent for a full minute. school lore: his teacher was called Tortoise because he TAUGHT US. the subjects: Reeling and Writhing, then Ambition, Distraction, Uglification and Derision. ten hours of lessons the first day, nine the next, because that's why they're called lessons. they LESSEN. the whole education system is a pun and he's weeping about it. so is the gryphon. I'm taking notes.
beats.quote: “We called him Tortoise because he taught us,”

beats.title: The Lobster Quadrille
beats.modern: they're performing the Lobster Quadrille AT me. two large crying reptiles dancing in circles around my body, stepping on my toes, singing about throwing lobsters into the sea and swimming after them. will you, won't you, will you, won't you, will you join the dance. I did not join the dance. the song has been stuck in my head for nine years and it has been four minutes.
beats.quote: Will you, won’t you, will you, won’t you, will you join the dance?

beats.title: The Tart Trial
beats.modern: COURT STREAM. the charge: the Knave allegedly stole the Queen's tarts. the evidence: the tarts. sitting right there on a table in the middle of the courtroom. fully recovered. looking delicious. the judge is the King, crown balanced on top of a judge wig. the jury is twelve small animals frantically writing their own names down so they don't forget them before the verdict. airtight proceedings incoming, I can feel it.
beats.quote: “The Queen of Hearts, she made some tarts, All on a summer day: The Knave of Hearts, he stole those tarts, And took them quite away!”

beats.title: The Teacup Bite
beats.modern: first witness: the Hatter, who brought his teacup to the stand. the King's opening line: give your evidence, and don't be nervous, or I'll have you executed on the spot. witness protection at its absolute finest. my man got so nervous he bit a chunk out of his own TEACUP instead of his bread and butter. and kept going. I have never related to anyone harder.
beats.quote: “and don’t be nervous, or I’ll have you executed on the spot.”

beats.title: The Oldest Rule
beats.modern: they called the next witness. it's ALICE. me?? jumped up so fast I flipped the entire jury box, twelve jurors sprawling like spilled goldfish. then the King reads from his notebook: rule forty two, all persons more than a mile high must leave the court. sir. you wrote that JUST NOW. I watched you. he claims it's the oldest rule in the book. then it ought to be rule ONE. he went pale and shut the book. VOD receipts, your honour.
beats.quote: “It’s the oldest rule in the book,” said the King.

beats.title: Begin at the Beginning
beats.modern: surprise evidence: an unsigned letter that is NOT in the Knave's handwriting. the King's ruling: if you didn't sign it, that only makes it worse, an honest man would have signed his name. the court APPLAUDED. then he tells the Rabbit how to read it out, and I quote: begin at the beginning, go on till you come to the end, then stop. the poem means NOTHING. I offered sixpence to anyone who can explain it. the jury wrote that down too.
beats.quote: “Begin at the beginning,” the King said gravely, “and go on till you come to the end: then stop.”

beats.title: A Pack of Cards
beats.modern: the Queen just said it. SENTENCE FIRST, VERDICT AFTERWARDS. I said stuff and nonsense. she screamed off with my head. nobody moved. and chat, I'm back to full size, so I stood up and said it: you're nothing but a pack of cards. the whole deck rose into the air and flew at my face and... I'm on the riverbank. my head's in my sister's lap. it was a dream. the whole stream was a dream. gg chat. best nap of my life. same hole tomorrow?
beats.quote: “You’re nothing but a pack of cards!”

beats.title: The Cold Open
beats.modern: new stream, chat. Middlemarch: one small English town, and every ambition it cannot fit. tonight's thesis: some people spawn with Saint Theresa stats in a map with no epic quests. no guild, no cause, nowhere to put all that fire. remember this. it explains literally everyone you are about to meet.
beats.quote: Here and there a cygnet is reared uneasily among the ducklings in the brown pond, and never finds the living stream in fellowship with its own oary-footed kind.

beats.title: Meet Miss Brooke
beats.modern: meet Dorothea Brooke: nineteen, gorgeous, dresses plain ON PURPOSE, quotes Pascal from memory, and files fashion under 'occupation for Bedlam.' she is playing life on hard mode for the achievement. chat already loves her. chat should be terrified for her.
beats.quote: Miss Brooke had that kind of beauty which seems to be thrown into relief by poor dress.

beats.title: The Husband Spec Sheet
beats.modern: her dream husband, chat, and I am quoting the spec sheet: a SORT OF FATHER who could teach her HEBREW. not tall. not rich. Hebrew. the hot young baronet who agrees with everything she says never had a chance.
beats.quote: The really delightful marriage must be that where your husband was a sort of father, and could teach you even Hebrew, if you wished it.

beats.title: The Emerald Loophole
beats.modern: she renounces her dead mother's jewels for religious reasons... except the emeralds. those she keeps, justifying it live as mystic religious joy. fastest speedrun ever of wanting a thing and finding the lore for it. Celia asks if she will actually wear them in public: 'I cannot tell to what level I may sink.' ICE. COLD.
beats.quote: All the while her thought was trying to justify her delight in the colors by merging them in her mystic religious joy.

beats.title: Marrying Pascal
beats.modern: target acquired: Casaubon. fifty ish, dried out, has been writing one enormous book since forever. she is monologuing in the woods RIGHT NOW: 'It would be like marrying Pascal.' ma'am. he is not Pascal. he is a footnote with a pulse. chat is spamming warnings and she has notifications off.
beats.quote: It would be like marrying Pascal.

beats.title: The Proposal Letter
beats.modern: the proposal letter just dropped and it is the least romantic document ever written. he says she is 'adapted to supply aid in graver labors and to cast a charm over vacant hours.' that is a job listing, chat. she reads it, falls on her knees SOBBING with joy, and writes back yes. F.
beats.quote: adapted to supply aid in graver labors and to cast a charm over vacant hours;

beats.title: Town Chat Reacts
beats.modern: the town chat is cooking him ALIVE. Sir James: 'he is no better than a mummy.' Mrs. Cadwallader: 'a great bladder for dried peas to rattle in.' someone says he has one foot in the grave; she says he means to draw it out again. no notes. wedding is still on.
beats.quote: “She says, he is a great soul.—A great bladder for dried peas to rattle in!”

beats.title: Will Enters the Server
beats.modern: new character: Will Ladislaw, Casaubon's broke artist cousin, sketching under a tree. he meets Dorothea, decides no girl with actual passion would ever marry Casaubon, waits for everyone to leave, and LAUGHS OUT LOUD at the entire situation. clip that laugh, chat. this man is going to matter.
beats.quote: There could be no sort of passion in a girl who would marry Casaubon.

beats.title: Rosamond Locks On
beats.modern: meanwhile in town: Dr. Lydgate, new, talented, related to a baronet. Rosamond Vincy trades ONE look with him and plans the wedding, the house, and the visits to his highborn relatives on the ride home. the scouting report says she wants a man of talent 'delightful to enslave.' Lydgate has no idea he is already in the cart.
beats.quote: a man of talent, also, whom it would be especially delightful to enslave:

beats.title: Fred's Opening Stats
beats.modern: Rosamond's brother Fred: charming, in debt, betting his whole build on inheriting from crusty old uncle Featherstone, and in love with Mary Garth. Rosamond reports that Mary said she would not marry him if he asked. Fred: 'She might have waited till I did ask her.' down bad and PROUD of it.
beats.quote: “She might have waited till I did ask her.”

beats.title: The Laure Lore Drop
beats.modern: lore drop, chat. Lydgate's first love was a Paris actress who stabbed her husband ON STAGE. ruled an accident. he chased her across France to propose anyway. her confession, verbatim: 'my foot really slipped'... then... 'I meant to do it.' he wearied her. that was the whole reason. Lydgate learned NOTHING from this. remember it.
beats.quote: “I did not plan: it came to me in the play—I meant to do it.”

beats.title: Crying in Rome
beats.modern: six weeks married. Casaubon is off at the Vatican doing homework. Dorothea is alone in a Rome apartment sobbing so hard she cannot even name a reason, telling herself the desolation is her own spiritual poverty. it is not, queen. it is week SIX.
beats.quote: I am sorry to add that she was sobbing bitterly,

beats.title: The Roar of Silence
beats.modern: the text just looked dead into the camera, chat: nobody calls a crying newlywed a tragedy because it is too common. but if we could truly feel all the ordinary pain around us, 'we should die of that roar which lies on the other side of silence.' the rest of us walk around well wadded with stupidity. chat went quiet. yeah. same.
beats.quote: we should die of that roar which lies on the other side of silence.

beats.title: The German Patch
beats.modern: Will drops the nuke on Dorothea: the Germans already did Casaubon's research, and Casaubon CANNOT READ GERMAN. twenty years grinding a quest another guild completed and published. she married him to serve a great mind, chat. she just found out the great mind is farming a dead map.
beats.quote: If Mr. Casaubon read German he would save himself a great deal of trouble.”

beats.title: Fred Griefs the Garths
beats.modern: Fred's horse flipping scheme went to zero and the bill lands on his cosigner: Mary's dad. so Mrs. Garth's savings for her son's apprenticeship? gone. Mary's savings? also gone. and Fred finally sees his own character screen: 'a pitiful rascal who was robbing two women of their savings.' correct assessment. no rerolls, Fred.
beats.quote: “I must give you the ninety-two pounds that I have put by for Alfred’s premium,”

beats.title: Why Always Dorothea
beats.modern: chat keeps spamming DOROTHEA DOROTHEA and honestly the text calls us all out: but why always Dorothea? fine. real talk: the mummy has an inner life too. he is 'spiritually a-hungered like the rest of us.' still insufferable. but it hits different now, does it not.
beats.quote: Dorothea—but why always Dorothea? Was her point of view the only possible one with regard to this marriage?

beats.title: Fit in the Library
beats.modern: mid cold war with Dorothea, Casaubon collapses on the library steps gasping for air. she is up on a stool holding him: 'Can you lean on me, dear?' ten minutes ago she was furious with him. that is marriage, chat. Lydgate is inbound.
beats.quote: “Can you lean on me, dear?”

beats.title: The Feather-Touch Engagement
beats.modern: Lydgate swore off romance after the murder actress. then Rosamond drops her little chain, he picks it up, she has real tears in her eyes, and 'that moment of naturalness was the crystallizing feather-touch: it shook flirtation into love.' he came to drop off a message, chat. he left ENGAGED. thirty minutes. speedran his own doom.
beats.quote: That moment of naturalness was the crystallizing feather-touch: it shook flirtation into love.

beats.title: Featherstone's Last Offer
beats.modern: 3 AM at Stone Court. dying old Featherstone wakes Mary: he made TWO wills and wants her to burn one. she refuses. he offers her all the cash in the box, take it, tell no one. she refuses again: 'I will not let the close of your life soil the beginning of mine.' morning comes. he is dead, one hand clasping the keys, the other lying on the pile of money. he tried to take it with him, chat.
beats.quote: I will not let the close of your life soil the beginning of mine.

beats.title: The Two Wills
beats.modern: the will reading. whole family assembled like crows in mourning wear. first will: Fred gets ten thousand! the room holds its breath. second will, the real one: revoked. EVERYTHING goes to a stranger named Rigg, plus charity almshouses. 'Nobody present had a farthing; but Mr. Trumbull had the gold-headed cane.' Fred just got third partied by a man nobody has met and some hypothetical old men.
beats.quote: Nobody present had a farthing; but Mr. Trumbull had the gold-headed cane.

beats.title: The Ban Hammer
beats.modern: Dorothea tried to get Will treated fairly and Casaubon, in the dark, in bed: 'It is not for you to interfere between me and Mr. Ladislaw.' then Will politely refuses to leave town, so Casaubon BANS him from the manor. they lie awake for hours not speaking. patch notes: jealousy added, communication removed.

beats.title: Come, My Dear, Come
beats.modern: Lydgate told him today: your heart could stop at any time. Casaubon froze her out all evening. so Dorothea waits in the dark corridor for hours in case he needs her. he comes up with his candle, sees her, and just: 'Come, my dear, come. You are young, and need not to extend your life by watching.' she takes his hand. no joke on this one, chat. sometimes the mummy is a person.
beats.quote: “Come, my dear, come. You are young, and need not to extend your life by watching.”

beats.title: The Dead Hand Request
beats.modern: bedtime. 'Before I sleep, I have a request to make, Dorothea.' he wants a blind promise that she will carry out his wishes AFTER HE DIES. no details. sign now, find out later, bound forever. she stalls: she cannot pledge herself 'to do I know not what.' chat, whatever you do: DO NOT SIGN.
beats.quote: whether you will avoid doing what I should deprecate, and apply yourself to do what I should desire.”

beats.title: Too Late in the Garden
beats.modern: she walked down to the garden to say yes, chat. she could not bring herself to crush him. he is in the summer house, head down on the table. 'I am come, Edward; I am ready.' nothing. 'Wake, dear, wake!... I am come to answer.' But Dorothea never gave her answer. he is gone. and now she will never know what she almost promised away.
beats.quote: “Wake, dear, wake! Listen to me. I am come to answer.” But Dorothea never gave her answer.

beats.title: The Codicil Drop
beats.modern: post credits grief, chat: Casaubon left a codicil. if Dorothea ever marries Will Ladislaw, she loses everything. understand: NOBODY was thinking about that pairing. now the entire county is thinking about it. mans got jealous from inside the coffin and accidentally made the ship canon. Celia relays the town verdict: 'you might as well marry an Italian with white mice!'
beats.quote: Mrs. Cadwallader said you might as well marry an Italian with white mice!

beats.title: The Egg Speech
beats.modern: Mr. Brooke runs for Parliament. the opposition hoists a PUPPET of him above the crowd and hires a ventriloquist to echo his speech in real time. every line comes back in Punch voice. then the eggs start flying. direct hits on candidate and puppet both. campaign: over. ratio: complete. five stars, no notes.
beats.quote: “You shall have the Bill, Mr. Brooke, per electioneering contest, and a seat outside Parliament as delivered, five thousand pounds, seven shillings, and fourpence.”

beats.title: The Painful Assist
beats.modern: Farebrother, who is in love with Mary himself, rides out to plead FRED'S case to her. Mary: never if he becomes a clergyman... but she will never love anyone else either. Farebrother secures the win for another man, says God bless you, and rides home alone. the most painful assist in league history.
beats.quote: I certainly never will be his wife if he becomes a clergyman.

beats.title: Blackmail Joins the Chat
beats.modern: a loud stranger in black strolls up to Bulstrode, the richest and holiest banker in town, and greets him like an old cellmate: 'By Jove, Nick, it's you!' Bulstrode turns the color of a corpse. chat. the banker has a PAST. and this man is a subscription he cannot cancel.
beats.quote: “By Jove, Nick, it’s you!

beats.title: The Gray Horse
beats.modern: Lydgate said no more riding. so Rosamond waits until he leaves town and rides again with his fancy cousin. the horse spooks at a falling tree. she loses the baby. and afterwards she stays 'mildly certain' the ride made no difference. Lydgate is discovering the boss mechanic, chat: she never takes damage and she never changes course.
beats.quote: the gentle gray, unprepared for the crash of a tree that was being felled on the edge of Halsell wood, took fright, and caused a worse fright to Rosamond, leading finally to the loss of her baby.

beats.title: What Can I Do
beats.modern: he finally tells her: we are in debt, they are coming to inventory the furniture, I need you. Rosamond turns her neck, looks at a vase, and says 'What can I do, Tertius?' four words at a temperature of absolute zero. the text calls them a mortal chill and I felt it through the screen.
beats.quote: “What can I do, Tertius?”

beats.title: Will's Origin Story
beats.modern: Raffles corners Will: 'was your mother's name Sarah Dunkirk?' turns out Will's mom ran away as a girl because the family business was fencing stolen goods. she chose broke over dirty. Will walks home in the dark feeling like he had dirt thrown on him in public. it gets worse, chat. so much worse.
beats.quote: He felt as if he had had dirt cast on him amidst shouts of scorn.

beats.title: Keep Your Money
beats.modern: the reveal: Bulstrode's first wife was Will's GRANDMOTHER. Bulstrode hid that her runaway daughter was alive, so the whole fortune came to him. now, sweating, he offers Will five hundred a year to square it with God. Will is broke, in love, and fully aware of both: 'You shall keep your ill-gotten money.' good night, sir. LEGEND behavior.
beats.quote: You shall keep your ill-gotten money.

beats.title: Uncle Godwin Replies
beats.modern: Rosamond secretly wrote to Lydgate's rich uncle begging for money. the reply arrives, addressed to Lydgate, and it opens by telling him not to send his wife to do his begging. then it gets meaner for a full page. Lydgate goes white. Rosamond reads it and is quietly disappointed... in HIM. chat, I cannot.
beats.quote: “DEAR TERTIUS,—Don’t set your wife to write to me when you have anything to ask.

beats.title: The Sudden Thousand
beats.modern: yesterday Bulstrode told Lydgate to go bankrupt with dignity. today, out of NOWHERE, he is writing him a cheque for a thousand pounds. Lydgate is saved and grateful. chat. look at the timing. why is a blackmailed man suddenly generous the night his blackmailer lies sick upstairs? pin this cheque to the board.
beats.quote: I esteem it right that I should incur a small sacrifice rather than leave you unaided.

beats.title: The Wine-Cooler Key
beats.modern: doctor's orders for Raffles: strict opium doses, absolutely no alcohol. Bulstrode... forgets to tell the housekeeper when the doses must stop. and when she begs brandy for the sinking patient, a key slides through the crack of the door: 'That is the key of the wine-cooler.' by morning Raffles is in 'the sleep which streams deeper and deeper into the gulf of death.' he never technically did anything, chat. that is the horror of it.
beats.quote: “That is the key of the wine-cooler. You will find plenty of brandy there.”

beats.title: The Town Meeting
beats.modern: public meeting. Hawley stands up: refute what the dead man said or RESIGN everything. Bulstrode plays the persecution card and the room detonates. he can barely stand. and Lydgate, who everyone now knows took a thousand pounds right before Raffles died, is the one who has to walk him out. arm in arm. in front of the whole town. two reputations, one clip.
beats.quote: As to Christian or unchristian, I repudiate your canting palavering Christianity;

beats.title: What Do We Live For
beats.modern: the whole town has convicted Lydgate by vibes. Dorothea, at dinner: 'people are almost always better than their neighbors think they are.' and then the line, chat: 'What do we live for, if it is not to make life less difficult to each other?' the men start explaining caution to her. she has already stopped listening. GO.
beats.quote: What do we live for, if it is not to make life less difficult to each other?

beats.title: Look Up, Nicholas
beats.modern: Harriet Bulstrode hears everything her husband is. she locks her door, sobs out her old life, takes off every ornament, puts on plain black, and goes DOWN to him. a hand on his hand: 'Look up, Nicholas.' they cry together. she never asks. he never denies. loyalty with its eyes open, chat. hardest clip of the season.
beats.quote: “Look up, Nicholas.”

beats.title: The Believer's Cheque
beats.modern: Dorothea hears Lydgate's side and simply believes him. he rides off saying she has 'a heart large enough for the Virgin Mary.' then she writes a cheque for a thousand pounds so he owes Bulstrode NOTHING, and plans to hand it over tomorrow. at his house. where his wife is. chat... chat, Will visits that house.
beats.quote: “This young creature has a heart large enough for the Virgin Mary.

beats.title: The Walk-In
beats.modern: she walks in unannounced and there it is: Will and Rosamond on the sofa, hands clasped, voices low. Dorothea goes full queen: 'Excuse me, Mrs. Lydgate, the servant did not know that you were here.' drops the letter. exits. do not be fooled by the walk speed, chat. that was a critical hit taken directly to the chest.
beats.quote: “Excuse me, Mrs. Lydgate, the servant did not know that you were here.

beats.title: The Longest Night
beats.modern: she cries herself to sleep on the floor. wakes at dawn and does the impossible thing: asks what she can do for the OTHER three people in the wreck. opens her curtains: a man with a bundle, a woman with a baby, the world getting up to work and endure. she is 'a part of that involuntary, palpitating life.' new dress. back to that house. she is going BACK, chat.
beats.quote: she felt the largeness of the world and the manifold wakings of men to labor and endurance.

beats.title: Rosamond's One Good Deed
beats.modern: Rosamond, of all people on this server, cracks: 'You are thinking what is not true... he was telling me how he loved another woman... no other woman existed for him beside you.' the one selfless act of her entire run, perfectly timed, and it flips the whole board. even NPCs get one heroic frame, chat.
beats.quote: He said yesterday that no other woman existed for him beside you.

beats.title: The Storm Proposal
beats.modern: Will came to say goodbye forever. lightning hits, hands clasp, 'we can never be married,' he reaches for his hat... and Dorothea BREAKS: 'I hate my wealth.' she is giving up the estate, chat. the codicil can keep it. seven hundred a year and she will learn what everything costs. GG Casaubon. your jealousy clause just funded their wedding.
beats.quote: “I don’t mind about poverty—I hate my wealth.”

beats.title: Stone Court Endgame
beats.modern: Mary tells Fred the ending he never earned the easy way: run Stone Court, be prudent, save every year, become somebody. and this time she says it straight: 'It is all true, Fred, and I am happy because of it, because I love you best.' immediately interrupted by her little brother demanding their cake. perfect. change nothing.
beats.quote: “It is all true, Fred, and I am happy because of it—because I love you best,”

beats.title: The Basil Plant
beats.modern: epilogue drop: Lydgate gets rich, hates himself, dies at fifty. he once called Rosamond his basil plant, because basil 'flourished wonderfully on a murdered man's brains.' she asked why he had chosen her, then, and won the exchange. she always won the exchange. F in chat for Tertius. the most expensive tears ever picked up off a carpet.
beats.quote: He once called her his basil plant; and when she asked for an explanation, said that basil was a plant which had flourished wonderfully on a murdered man’s brains.

beats.title: Where They Landed
beats.modern: Dorothea never regrets it. Will makes Parliament; she funds the fight from the wings. and the town's final review of its finest person: a nice woman would not have married EITHER husband. Middlemarch remains undefeated at missing the point.
beats.quote: Many who knew her, thought it a pity that so substantive and rare a creature should have been absorbed into the life of another,

beats.title: Unvisited Tombs
beats.modern: last screen, chat. no statue, no title, no page in the histories. but 'things are not so ill with you and me as they might have been' half because of people exactly like her: hidden lives, unhistoric acts, unvisited tombs. that is the stream. that is the whole point. gg. go be somebody's unhistoric act.
beats.quote: that things are not so ill with you and me as they might have been, is half owing to the number who lived faithfully a hidden life, and rest in unvisited tombs.

the-strange-case-of-dr.title: The strange case of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde
the-strange-case-of-dr.author: Robert Louis Stevenson

beats.title: The Juggernaut Clip
beats.modern: Sunday walk stream with my cousin Enfield. he points at this sketchy door and drops the worst story I've ever heard. 3am, empty street, and a small man tramples a CHILD. walks over her like she's terrain. the crowd corners him, so he ducks behind that door and comes back with a cheque signed by someone else. someone famous. Enfield says it wasn't like a man, it was like some damned Juggernaut. and chat: the cheque CLEARED.
beats.quote: It wasn’t like a man; it was like some damned Juggernaut.

beats.title: The Name Drop
beats.modern: I broke my own rule and asked the trampler's name. Enfield can't even describe the guy. says there's something wrong with him, something detestable, but he can't point to it. the name though: Hyde. chat, I kept my lawyer face on. inside I was screaming. I know that name. I know exactly where I've seen it, and I wish I didn't.
beats.quote: It was a man of the name of Hyde.”

beats.title: The Disappearance Clause
beats.modern: home. safe. here it is, the document I hate most in my files: the will of Dr. Henry Jekyll, my client, beloved genius, leaving everything to one 'Edward Hyde.' and it gets worse. if Jekyll DISAPPEARS for three months, Hyde just steps into his whole life, no questions asked. chat, who writes disappearance into a will?? I used to think it was madness. now I fear it is disgrace.

beats.title: Mr. Seek
beats.modern: new arc, chat: I'm staking out the door. before office hours. lunch. midnight. all lights, all hours. if he be Mr. Hyde, I shall be Mr. Seek. yes, I workshopped that. no, I will not be taking feedback on the pun.
beats.quote: “If he be Mr. Hyde,” he had thought, “I shall be Mr. Seek.”

beats.title: Satan's Signature
beats.modern: HE SHOWED UP. small, plain, and every cell in my body said run before he got within ten feet. I asked to see his face and he just... showed me. chat, I can't explain what's wrong with it. nothing is technically wrong with it. he snarled like an animal, volunteered his home address unprompted (weird flex, noted for the file), and vanished inside. if I ever read Satan's signature on a face, it is on that one.
beats.quote: God bless me, the man seems hardly human! Something troglodytic, shall we say?

beats.title: Trust Me Bro
beats.modern: cornered Jekyll after his dinner party. mentioned the will and the colour left his face like someone pulled a plug. he says I don't understand his position, it's 'a very strange one,' but the moment he chooses, he can be rid of Mr. Hyde. then he makes ME promise to get Hyde his inheritance if anything happens to him. chat, this is textbook blackmail. I've seen it a hundred times. I promised anyway. I hate everything about this.
beats.quote: the moment I choose, I can be rid of Mr. Hyde.

beats.title: The Carew Clip
beats.modern: chat. a maid watched a murder from her window last night. a beautiful white haired old gentleman stops to ask directions, polite as anything. and the small man he's talking to just EXPLODES. clubs him to the ground and keeps swinging until the bones are audibly breaking. like an ape having a tantrum, she said. she fainted at the window. and here's the part that ices my blood: she recognized the attacker. Mr. Hyde.
beats.quote: and at that Mr. Hyde broke out of all bounds and clubbed him to the earth.

beats.title: That's My Cane
beats.modern: police came for ME at dawn, chat. the victim was carrying a letter with my name on it. I made the ID at the station: Sir Danvers Carew. member of Parliament. my client. then they showed me the murder weapon, a heavy cane snapped in half by the force. and I knew it instantly. I gave Jekyll that cane. years ago. as a gift. pouring a gin. don't talk to me for a minute.

beats.title: The Sworn Oath
beats.modern: went to Jekyll. he looks half dead and SWEARS to God, unprompted, that he will never set eyes on Hyde again, that it's all over, that Hyde is 'quite safe.' then he hands me a farewell note from Hyde. touching. one problem: Poole says nothing was delivered today except circulars. so the note never came through the front door, chat. it came from inside the laboratory. cool. everything's fine.
beats.quote: “I swear to God I will never set eyes on him again.

beats.title: The Handwriting Check
beats.modern: showed the Hyde note to Guest, my head clerk. the man is a handwriting nerd, absolutely locked in. halfway through the analysis, a dinner invite from Jekyll arrives. Guest lays the two papers side by side and goes very quiet. same handwriting, chat. THE SAME HAND, just sloped the other way. and my brain serves up the only 'sane' conclusion left: Henry Jekyll forged a letter to protect a murderer. that's the sane one. I locked it in my safe and told nobody.
beats.quote: “Henry Jekyll forge for a murderer!”

beats.title: Do Not Open Yet
beats.modern: time skip, chat. Hyde vanished off the map. Jekyll got two golden months, then shut his door in my face. and Lanyon is DYING. the healthiest man I know, death warrant written on his face, says he's had a shock. mention Jekyll and he shakes. two weeks later he's gone. he left me an envelope: not to be opened till the death or disappearance of Dr. Henry Jekyll. that word again, chat. DISAPPEARANCE.
beats.quote: “not to be opened till the death or disappearance of Dr. Henry Jekyll.”

beats.title: The Window Slam
beats.modern: walk stream with Enfield. we found Jekyll sitting at his window like a prisoner taking air. got him chatting, he even smiled. and then the smile was struck off his face, and what replaced it... I'm not describing it. I'm not clipping it. the window slammed. we walked out of that court and neither of us said a word. God forgive us. God forgive us.
beats.quote: “God forgive us, God forgive us,”

beats.title: Not His Voice
beats.modern: Poole just showed up at MY door, white as paper, saying foul play. so we went. every servant in the house is huddled around the hall fire like sheep. we go out to the cabinet door, Poole announces me, and a voice answers that it cannot see anyone. chat. Poole turns and asks me: was that my master's voice? twenty years he's served him. it was not his voice. Poole thinks his master was murdered eight days ago, and whatever is in that room now... stayed.
beats.quote: “Have I been twenty years in this man’s house, to be deceived about his voice?

beats.title: The Masked Thing
beats.modern: it gets worse. all week the thing in the cabinet has been crying night and day for a chemical it cannot get pure enough, throwing every sample back: find the OLD batch. one note starts as polite doctor correspondence and ends 'for God's sake, find me some of the old.' and Poole SAW it once. masked. digging through crates. it cried out like a rat and bolted upstairs. he swears on his bible it was Hyde.
beats.quote: Sir, if that was my master, why had he a mask upon his face?

beats.title: Down With the Door
beats.modern: Poole takes the axe, I take the kitchen poker. we listen at the door one last time. light little footsteps pacing, up and down, up and down. not Jekyll's walk. Poole says once, he heard it WEEPING. like a lost soul, chat. I gave fair warning. the voice begged for mercy, for God's sake, mercy. and that voice is not Jekyll's. it's Hyde's. DOWN WITH THE DOOR, POOLE.
beats.quote: “Ah, that’s not Jekyll’s voice—it’s Hyde’s!”

beats.title: The Wrong Clothes
beats.modern: door's down. and the room is... cozy? fire lit, kettle singing, tea laid out for one. and in the middle of the floor, still twitching: Hyde. crushed vial in his hand. he took his own exit as we were breaking through. chat, he's drowning in Jekyll's clothes. clothes made for a man twice his size. we tore the place apart, every closet, the cellar. there is no Jekyll here. dead or alive. no Jekyll.
beats.quote: Utterson knew that he was looking on the body of a self-destroyer.

beats.title: Dead Men's Mail
beats.modern: on the desk, addressed to me: a new will. Hyde's name is out. mine is in. the dead man on the carpet spent days locked in here with the document that disinherits him and never burned it. plus a note from Jekyll dated TODAY, telling me to read Lanyon's sealed letter first, then his own confession. he was alive in this room this morning, chat. I'm going home. we read everything tonight. the whole case ends tonight.

beats.title: The Midnight Errand
beats.modern: Lanyon's envelope. dead man's mail, opened live, chat. January 9th, he gets a letter from Jekyll BEGGING: drop everything, even an emperor's bedside. break into my cabinet. steal drawer E, powders, phial, notebook. carry it home. at midnight a man will come for it, alone. 'my life, my honour, my reason, are all at your mercy; if you fail me to-night, I am lost.' Lanyon assumed his old friend had lost his mind. he went anyway.
beats.quote: Lanyon, my life, my honour, my reason, are all at your mercy; if you fail me to-night, I am lost.

beats.title: The Midnight Visitor
beats.modern: midnight. a knock. Lanyon answers with a hand on the gun in his pocket. a tiny man is on the doorstep, swimming in clothes five sizes too big, vibrating with panic. he sees the drawer and SOBS with relief. 'have you got it? have you got it?' mixes the chemicals on the spot. the glass boils, goes purple, fades to green. then he offers Lanyon a choice: walk away and stay sane... or watch.
beats.quote: “Have you got it?” he cried. “Have you got it?”

beats.title: Behold
beats.modern: Lanyon stayed. of course he stayed. the little man raises the glass and says you denied transcendental medicine, you derided your superiors. BEHOLD. one gulp. then screaming, swelling, the face going black and MELTING, reshaping. and when it stops, standing there pale and gasping like a man back from the dead: HENRY JEKYLL. chat. HYDE IS JEKYLL. the murderer half of London is hunting is my best friend. that is the shock. Lanyon watched this and it killed him.
beats.quote: you who have denied the virtue of transcendental medicine, you who have derided your superiors—behold!”

beats.title: Truly Two
beats.modern: Jekyll's confession now, chat. his own hand, his own voice. thesis statement: man is not truly one, but truly two. good and evil, polar twins, chained together in one body, struggling forever. every philosopher in history wrote essays about this. Henry Jekyll looked at the oldest problem in the human soul and said, I can fix that. in a LAB.
beats.quote: man is not truly one, but truly two.

beats.title: Meet Edward Hyde
beats.modern: he built the potion and drank it alone at night. no trial run, no antidote, no backup. racking agony, grinding bones... and then he's smaller. younger. FREE. tenfold more wicked and loving every second of it. he finds a mirror expecting horror, and chat, he feels WELCOME. 'this, too, was myself.' everyone else who ever looked at Hyde recoiled on sight, because Hyde is the only creature on earth that is pure evil. Jekyll looked at him and said hello.
beats.quote: I was conscious of no repugnance, rather of a leap of welcome. This, too, was myself.

beats.title: Waking Up Wrong
beats.modern: then it stopped asking permission. one morning Jekyll wakes up in his own bed, no potion taken, and looks down at the hand lying on the bedclothes. lean. corded. hairy. not his hand. the hand of Edward Hyde. he went to bed Henry Jekyll and woke up the monster, chat. the costume started putting itself on while he SLEPT.
beats.quote: It was the hand of Edward Hyde.

beats.title: Out Roaring
beats.modern: the Carew murder, from inside the monster. Jekyll had quit. white knuckled it for months, then caved in one weak hour and took a dose. 'my devil had been long caged, he came out roaring.' the old gentleman's only crime was being polite to a stranger.
