Jekyll says he broke him the way a sick child breaks a plaything, and felt GLEE. then he changed back, wept, prayed, and ground the laboratory key under his heel. never again, he swore. chat, we know how never again went.
beats.quote: My devil had been long caged, he came out roaring.

beats.title: The Park Bench
beats.modern: he didn't even need the potion to fall, chat. sunny January day, park bench, Jekyll feeling smug about his charity work. and mid thought, the shudder hits. clothes hanging off shrunken limbs. a corded, hairy hand on his knee. Edward Hyde, in DAYLIGHT, in Regent's Park. a wanted murderer who cannot go home, because the cure is locked in his own cabinet behind his own servants. one minute rich and beloved. the next: hunted, houseless, thrall to the gallows. now you know why Lanyon got that letter.
beats.quote: I looked down; my clothes hung formlessly on my shrunken limbs; the hand that lay on my knee was corded and hairy. I was once more Edward Hyde.

beats.title: The Last Powder
beats.modern: last page. the salt ran out, chat. every new batch fails. the original supply had an impurity, and the impurity was the magic. it can never be made again. he wrote this on the final dose, racing the change, knowing Hyde wakes up in his place forever. no bit here. 'I bring the life of that unhappy Henry Jekyll to an end.' that's the end of the confession. that's the end of my friend. stream's over. go home. hug somebody.
beats.quote: Here then, as I lay down the pen and proceed to seal up my confession, I bring the life of that unhappy Henry Jekyll to an end.

beats.title: Twenty-Nine and Unsought
beats.modern: chat. it's my 29th birthday and I woke up before dawn to cry on a schedule. in my family an unmarried woman at 29 is a failed save file. and the sting isn't being an old maid. it's that nobody ever ASKED. not once. no man has ever wanted the Valancy run. anyway mom can't see red eyes at breakfast or the interrogation starts, so. quiet crying only.

beats.title: The Blue Castle
beats.modern: lore drop: I have a second home nobody knows about. a blue castle in Spain. been building it in my head since I was five. turrets, fountains, nightingales, a rotating cast of imaginary boyfriends. one at a time, I'm not unhinged. current build: reddish hair, twisted smile, mysterious past. when I outgrow a lover he just quietly despawns. things are very convenient in Blue Castles.

beats.title: The Picnic Dialogue Tree
beats.modern: rain cancelled the clan picnic, so here's the NPC dialogue I'm skipping this year. uncle Wellington: 'not thinking of getting married yet?' plus signature bellow. aunt Alberta: skin like roses and cream, prettiest girl in Canada, did you know. and uncle Benjamin's riddle about me and a mouse. he has run it FIFTY TIMES. I can't even boo him, chat. he's rich, childless, and I'm possibly in the will.
beats.quote: “The mouse wishes to harm the cheese and Doss wishes to charm the he’s.”

beats.title: The Mystery Author
beats.modern: the one thing keeping me sane: nature books by a guy called John Foster. no face reveal, no bio, the publisher won't leak a word. total anon. the librarian thinks the books are about bugs. they are not about bugs, chat. they're about a door I never got to walk through. I've read Thistle Harvest four times and mom still rations my library visits like it's contraband.

beats.title: Fear Is the Original Sin
beats.modern: opened the new Foster book and a paragraph one-shotted me: fear is the original sin. almost all evil comes from someone being afraid of something. that's my whole build, chat. so I walked to the heart doctor ALONE. no family council. first solo quest of my life. and mid-exam his phone rings, his son's hurt in Montreal, and the man SPRINTS out the door with a club bag. never said the diagnosis. I got speedrun-abandoned in an empty office.
beats.quote: “Fear is the original sin,”

beats.title: The Rosebush Incident
beats.modern: my rosebush hasn't bloomed once in five years. healthiest bush on the street. zero flowers. today something snapped and I went at it with a garden knife like an unpaid intern with a grudge. mom came out mid-massacre asking if I've gone crazy. maybe! rose trees should BLOOM. consider this a performance review.

beats.title: The Death Timer
beats.modern: the letter came. angina, last stages, might die any moment, a year max if I'm careful. no cure. I read it once and the whole world lost its textures. there are girls laughing at the train station outside my window and none of it is real. I'm twenty-nine, I have never lived a single day, and now there's a hard timer on the run.

beats.title: The Three A.M. Patch
beats.modern: 3am. the wisest and most accursed hour of the clock. new patch, effective immediately: I've been trying to please other people all my life and failed. from now on I please myself. no more pretending anything, ever. mother can pout for WEEKS, not my problem. first change deployed: hurled the potpourri jar out the window. it smashed gloriously against the old carriage shop. I'm sick of the fragrance of dead things.
beats.quote: “I’ve been trying to please other people all my life and failed,”

beats.title: The Greatest Happiness
beats.modern: family dinner. uncle James launches a table topic: name the greatest happiness. answers: being a beloved wife and mother. travel in Europe. loving service for others. me, clearly and distinctly: the greatest happiness is to sneeze when you want to. full server silence. so uncle Benjamin panic-deploys his old maid riddle and I answer it FOR him, word for word, fifty repetitions deep, and inform him it's a fatal mistake to try to be funny if you don't succeed. the man bluescreened.
beats.quote: “One is happy and careless and the other is cappy and hairless,”

beats.title: The Snobocracy Speech
beats.modern: now they're carving up Barney Snaith and poor Cissy Gay at the dinner table. zero receipts, pure vibes. and something in me went off. told them the only crime Barney has ever been guilty of is minding his own business, which IS unforgivable in their little snobocracy. yes I coined snobocracy live. no notes. then I stood up, thanked aunt Alberta for dinner, and told her the salad dressing needs more salt and a dash of cayenne. exit clip of the year.
beats.quote: As for Barney Snaith, the only crime he has been guilty of is living to himself and minding his own business.

beats.title: The Housekeeper Application
beats.modern: Roaring Abel says Cissy can barely move and there's NOBODY to look after her. she's dying, chat. dying alone in a farmhouse because this whole God-fearing town decided one baby without a ring puts you outside the walls forever. Abel just needs a housekeeper and no 'decent woman' will take the job. so I asked him: will I do? chat spamming question marks. yes. I'm serious. quest accepted.

beats.title: Let Us Be Calm
beats.modern: the clan crisis meeting, as reported back to me. uncle Benjamin opening with 'let us be calm. let us be PERFECTLY calm.' mom testifying that I said, quote, I've been keeping up appearances all my life, now I'm going in for realities, appearances can go hang. GO HANG, she repeated, like reading a war crime into the record. and the closer: cousin Stickles asked who'd rub her back at night and I said 'oh darn.' actual swearing. the family is treating this as confirmed demonic possession.
beats.quote: ‘I’ve been keeping up appearances all my life. Now I’m going in for realities. Appearances can go hang!’

beats.title: The Salt Codfish Quest
beats.modern: HE STOPPED THE CAR. Barney Snaith. alleged jailbird, alleged forger, alleged everything, owner of one very loud vehicle named Lady Jane. his eyes are violet up close. he asked if he could get us anything from town. chat. in my dream castle I've sent knights on quests for twenty years. moonlit errands. dragon stuff. and my mouth, live and unsupervised, said: salt codfish. I asked the mystery man of Muskoka for SALT CODFISH. clip it. put it on my grave.

beats.title: The Asparagus Yeet
beats.modern: uncle James came to drag me home and called my boss a drunken blasphemous old scoundrel. while my boss was on the porch. Abel crossed the kitchen in ONE frame, grabbed him by the collar and the trousers, and yeeted him clean over the garden fence into the asparagus bed. coat-tails fully airborne. I have feared that man's judgment my entire life, chat, and he flew like patio furniture.

beats.title: The Forefinger Boss Fight
beats.modern: final boss pulled up: Dr. Stalling, the rector whose pointing forefinger has terrorized me since I was six. 'she entreats, but I COMMAND you to come home. get your hat and coat NOW.' and chat, I was folding. coat half on, soul half out. then the Foster line fired in my head like a system alert: fear is the original sin. respec complete. told him mother doesn't need me, Cissy does, I'm staying. the finger lowered. you cannot shake a finger forever.

beats.title: The Dance Extraction
beats.modern: 11pm at the backwoods dance: whiskey arrived and the whole lobby turned hostile. a big drunk one grabbed me. 'you've got to give us each a turn and a kiss to boot.' I'm being dragged into the mob, actively regretting my choices, when his jaw gets deleted by a punch from OFFSCREEN. Barney. out the window, over the sill, hand in hand, full sprint through the pines with a posse howling behind us. I have never run in my life. apparently I can MOVE.

beats.title: The Lightning Flash
beats.modern: status update from a dead car in the moonlight: we ran out of gas, and somewhere between him leaning on the door and me looking up, I fell in love. no loading screen. lightning flash. and here's the thing, chat. I don't need him to love me back. I'm rich now. death can't cheat me out of anything anymore. I have LOVED. that's the whole achievement.

beats.title: The Gas Stop Ratio
beats.modern: guess whose car pulled over to lend us gas. uncle Wellington. with OLIVE. she leans in with the missionary voice: come home, Doss, all will be forgiven, there are nights I cannot sleep for thinking of you. so I leaned in too and told her I've been sitting here three hours with Barney Snaith and he hasn't even TRIED to kiss me. and I wouldn't have minded if he had. her face buffered for a full second. uncle Wellington drove off yelling 'hussy.' RATIO.
beats.quote: I’ve been sitting here for three hours with Barney Snaith and he hasn’t even tried to kiss me. I wouldn’t have minded if he had, Olive.”

beats.title: Cissy’s Story
beats.modern: Cissy told me everything. a rich college boy at the summer hotel. she loved him. when trouble came he offered marriage out of pity and she refused, because he didn't love her anymore, and that felt worse than the shame. her baby lived one year. she said she was glad when she learned she was dying. days later she died at sunrise holding my hand, smiling at something past my shoulder. whatever she saw made up for everything. F for Cissy Gay.

beats.title: The Proposal
beats.modern: chat I did it. he pulled up to the gate, asked if there was anything he could do for me, and I said: yes. will you marry me. showed him the doctor's letter, laid out the run: months left, I'm crazy about you, I want to spend the endgame on your island. his terms: never ask about his past, never touch his mail, no lies between us ever. accepted. his closing line: 'I've always thought you were a bit of a dear.' WEDDING ARC UNLOCKED.
beats.quote: “Will you marry me?”

beats.title: The Overalls Wedding
beats.modern: married. tiny shabby parlour, me in the green dress, him in overalls. clean ones. he dressed up. no veil, no flowers, no guests, no cake. teenage me had storyboarded white silk and a flower girl and orange blossoms. current me looked at the two of us in the crooked little mirror over the mantel and understood: it was Barney. that was all that mattered. for whatever's left of this run, Barney.

beats.title: The Castle Is Real
beats.modern: he walks me down to the shore and points across the water. an island. two enormous pines holding hands over a little house, lilac mist, pale young moon behind it. chat. CHAT. it's my castle. the one I've been building in my head since I was five. it's REAL and I live here now. he lifted me out of the canoe and kissed me. first kiss. age twenty-nine. worth the wait. 'welcome home, dear.'
beats.quote: “Oh, my Blue Castle!”

beats.title: The Rosebush Redemption
beats.modern: STOP THE STREAM. walked past the old house and the rosebush, the one I knifed half to death and got labeled insane for, is COVERED in crimson roses. five years of nothing, one act of violence, full bloom. me and that bush ran the exact same patch, chat. cut away everything that wasn't working and FLOWER.

beats.title: The Marriage Bomb
beats.modern: walked into a full lobby of Stirlings and dropped it: married last Tuesday. to Barney Snaith. uncle Benjamin bounced out of his chair. cousin Gladys fainted on schedule. uncle James went nuclear: shameless creature, lost to all decency, washing his hands of me, never wants to see my face again. so I asked what he's got left for when I commit murder. pace your rage, uncle. exit line on my way out: the trouble with you people is you don't laugh enough.
beats.quote: “What have you left to say when I commit murder?”

beats.title: The Moonlight Nickname
beats.modern: he calls me Moonlight now. MOONLIGHT. twenty-nine years as Doss and this man looked at me and picked moonlight. he asked if I'd want the millionaire's palace across the lake. no thanks. I'd have to carry a house like that everywhere on my back like a snail. I like a house I can love and cuddle and boss. it's magnificent, but it isn't my Blue Castle.

beats.title: The Storm Night
beats.modern: he went for a woods tramp and the worst blizzard of the winter spawned directly on top of him. I spent the whole night at the window watching white static where the lake used to be, dying a hundred deaths. noon: he strolls around the point like nothing happened. slept in a lumber shanty. called it a baby storm. and chat, log this detail: when I saw him coming, something in my chest restarted. like I died and came back to life. it's on the exam later.

beats.title: The Switch Incident
beats.modern: I never want to watch this clip again. crossing the rails, through train incoming, and my pretty foolish shoe heel jams in the switch. STUCK. I'm screaming at him to run and he's on his knees slashing my shoelace saying NEVER. ripped me clear with the train's wind on our faces. then, sitting there shaking, the horrible math: that was more excitement than most people get in a lifetime. the kind that's supposed to kill me. it didn't even wobble me. chat. was the diagnosis wrong.

beats.title: The Wrong Letter Reveal
beats.modern: went to Dr. Trent and handed him his own letter. his face fell out of his face. it was meant for a MISS JANE STERLING of Port Lawrence. same day, similar name, wrong envelope. she got my letter. I got her death sentence. my actual diagnosis: pseudo-angina. never fatal. cured by treatment, or 'a shock of joy.' I'll live to a hundred, chat, and it's the worst news of my life. I trapped Barney into marrying a dying woman who is not going to die.
beats.quote: “Good heavens! This is the letter I meant for old Miss Jane Sterling.

beats.title: The Purple Pill Dad
beats.modern: there is a screaming purple limo parked next to Lady Jane and a round little man asking for 'Mr. Redfern's house.' chat. it's the face from the pill bottles. DOC REDFERN. purple pills, bitters, liniment, hair vigor. Barney is Bernard Snaith Redfern. his son. his heir. and when I asked how rich, he said MILLIONS, waving his diamond at my castle: 'and Bernie chucks them for that.' I married a millionaire's son by accident. today keeps happening to me.
beats.quote: “Yes, I understand Bernie’s been calling himself Snaith. Well, it’s his middle name—was his poor mother’s. Bernard Snaith Redfern—that’s him.

beats.title: Bluebeard’s Chamber
beats.modern: I went into the locked room. not for secrets. I just needed a pen to write the goodbye note. chat. on the desk: fresh page proofs. WILD HONEY. by JOHN FOSTER. my husband is John Foster. the author who saved my life is the man I'm leaving. I wrote the note anyway, offered him the divorce, and laid the pearls on top. the 'beads' he gave me for Christmas. they're worth fifteen thousand dollars. I can't keep them. locked the door behind me.
beats.quote: So Barney was John Foster!

beats.title: The Millionaire Flip
beats.modern: told the family everything, flat: wrong letter, not dying, Barney only married me out of pity, I've left him. zero sympathy in the room. then I said the words 'Dr. Redfern's son' and mom's eyes changed frequency. 'not the Purple Pill man?' uncle Benjamin's mouth snapped shut and reopened with 'ten times over.' a millionaire, ten times over. chat, watch this clan speedrun forgiveness any% in real time.
beats.quote: Foster—“Dr. Redfern is a millionaire!”

beats.title: I Want My Wife
beats.modern: next day. a dreadful old car takes the corner onto Elm street at speed and someone hatless attacks our doorbell like it owes him money. 'IS MY WIFE HERE.' uncle Benjamin, suddenly my butler, ushering him into the parlour, rubbing his hands, dropping husband riddles in the kitchen. mom went up to fetch me. I said I can't see him. uncle Benjamin, THROUGH THE KEYHOLE: he says he won't leave till he's seen you. Barney never said that. the man is fully improvising dialogue for us.
beats.quote: “Is my wife here?”

beats.title: The Turpentine Lore Drop
beats.modern: full lore dump. he grew up the loneliest rich kid in Montreal. boys held him underwater at school until he read his dad's pill ads out loud. college nickname: After Using. then he overheard his fiancée, the beautiful Ethel Traverse, explain their engagement to a friend: his money will gild the pills and sweeten the bitters, but she smells TURPENTINE whenever he comes near. so he ghosted the entire planet for eleven years. chat, everyone in this story was one overheard sentence away from a different life.
beats.quote: “‘His money will gild the Pills and sweeten the Bitters,’

beats.title: The Rage Check
beats.modern: he said I'm in the very core of his heart, held there like a jewel. and I still couldn't believe it. pity, obviously. acting. so I said so. and this man went VOLCANIC. white-faced, silk-voiced fury: I'm tired of him, my Stirling pride can't stomach the pills, fine for a dying lark but a LIFETIME with Doc Redfern's son is beneath me. and I started laughing, chat. you do not rage like that out of pity. HE MEANS IT. confirmed via anger. we're back.
beats.quote: Girl, you’re in the very core of my heart. I hold you there like a jewel.

beats.title: Olive’s Leaked Letter
beats.modern: post-credits: cousin Olive's letter to her fiancé, leaked to the stream. 'it's really disgusting that Doss's crazy adventures should have turned out like this. it makes one feel that there is no use in behaving properly.' banger admission, Olive. also in the letter: dad Redfern gave us TWO MILLION as a wedding present, and the clan now says 'my son-in-law, Bernard Redfern' in public. she closes by noting I'm laughing at them all in my sleeve. correct, Olive. sharpest read of your life.
beats.quote: It makes one feel that there is no use in behaving properly.

beats.title: The Real Honeymoon
beats.modern: last clip of the season. cats shipped to cousin Georgiana, who won custody over three competing aunts. we stood under the pines for one long look at the Blue Castle in the sunset, and yes I cried. 'don't cry, Moonlight. we'll be back next summer. and now we're off for a real honeymoon.' Italy. Egypt. the Alhambra. none of it will touch this island and we both know it. gg chat. the castle was real the whole time.
beats.quote: “Don’t cry, Moonlight. We’ll be back next summer. And now we’re off for a real honeymoon.”

little-women.title: Little Women; Or, Meg, Jo, Beth, and Amy
little-women.author: Louisa May Alcott

beats.title: Broke Christmas
beats.modern: welcome back to the March family stream, chat. status: BROKE. no presents this Christmas, the money goes to the army, and dad's away at the war. four sisters, one dollar each. Meg wants pretty things, Beth wants sheet music, Amy wants drawing pencils, and I want a book, obviously. mom proposed sacrifice. we counter proposed shopping. we're workshopping it.
beats.quote: Christmas won't be Christmas without any presents]

beats.title: The Little Women Letter
beats.modern: mom read dad's letter from camp on stream tonight. zero complaints in it, just cheerful army talk, and then the last paragraph hits: work hard while we wait, so when he comes back he can be fonder and prouder than ever of his little women. entire chat sniffling. Amy sobbed a whole apology into mom's shoulder. I'm not crying. my eyes are just doing that.
beats.quote: when I come back to them I may be fonder and prouder than ever of my little women."

beats.title: The Breakfast Giveaway
beats.modern: Christmas morning. we waited an HOUR for breakfast, and mom walks in like 'there's a poor woman down the street with a newborn, six kids in one bed, no fire. give them your breakfast?' one minute of silence. then we boxed the whole spread and carried it over. the kids called us angel children while they ate. first time in my LIFE anyone's called me an angel. bread and milk never tasted better, chat.
beats.quote: "Funny angels in hoods and mittens,"

beats.title: The Curtain Boy
beats.modern: party report: I hid in a curtained alcove because my dress has a scorch mark on the back, and there was ALREADY a boy hiding in it. the shy rich kid from next door. we introduced ourselves like diplomats. 'I'm not Miss March, I'm only Jo.' 'I'm not Mr. Laurence, I'm only Laurie.' bonded instantly over hating our government names. he used to thrash kids who called him Dora. new duo unlocked, chat. clip it.
beats.quote: "I'm not Mr. Laurence, I'm only Laurie."

beats.title: Snowball Diplomacy
beats.modern: the boy next door has been sick and shut up in that huge house for a WEEK, so I ran foreign policy: threw a snowball at his window and yelled 'are you sick?' now we're negotiating. he says it's dull as tombs up there, nobody visits, grandpa reads him books he hates. I said you know US. he said will you come, PLEASE. going to ask mom and breach the mansion. diplomacy, chat.
beats.quote: "How do you do? Are you sick?"

beats.title: Beth Kisses the Boss
beats.modern: old Mr. Laurence gave Beth a PIANO. his dead granddaughter's piano. and Beth, the child who is scared of doorbells, said she'd go thank him now before she got frightened thinking about it, walked into his study, and KISSED the most terrifying old man in the neighborhood. he set her on his knee like he'd got his own granddaughter back. we watched from the window like it was a moon landing. Meg says the world is ending.
beats.quote: "Well, I do believe the world is coming to an end!"

beats.title: The Lime Massacre
beats.modern: school scandal, chat. pickled limes are the contraband currency of Amy's class, and she got ratted out holding two dozen. the teacher made her throw them out the window TWO BY TWO while the street kids feasted below, then hit her palm in front of the whole class. she held out her hand and didn't flinch. she's twelve. first time anyone ever struck her, and to her it was as deep as being knocked down. justice for the lime queen.
beats.quote: Now take these disgusting things two by two, and throw them out of the window."

beats.title: She Burned My Book
beats.modern: AMY. BURNED. MY BOOK. my manuscript, chat. years of work, the only copy, torched because I wouldn't take her to the theatre. I shook her till her teeth rattled. she tried a sorry at dinner and I said the quiet thing loud: I will never forgive you as long as I live. I have never been this angry in my entire life and I do not want to be talked down.
beats.quote: "You wicked, wicked girl! I never can write it again, and I'll never forgive you as long as I live."

beats.title: Rotten Ice
beats.modern: we weren't speaking, so when Amy followed us to the river, I heard Laurie yell 'keep near the shore' and did not pass it on. she went for the smooth ice in the middle. chat, she went THROUGH. one second she's skating, then it's just a little blue hood in black water and my legs wouldn't move. Laurie kept his head, I dragged a fence rail, we got her out. I let spite nearly drown my sister. no bit for this one.
beats.quote: "No matter whether she heard or not, let her take care of herself."

beats.title: The Conservatory Leak
beats.modern: dispatch from Meg's fortnight with the rich friends: she's sitting behind the flowers at the dance and overhears the moms running commentary. our mom has 'plans' to bag the rich boy next door for one of us, apparently, and Meg would be 'so nice if she was only got up in style.' they're going to lend her a dress and 'have fun about it afterward.' she cried herself to sleep. rich people start the group chat the SECOND you leave the room.
beats.quote: "Mrs M. has made her plans, I dare say, and will play her cards well, early as it is.

beats.title: The Hedge Post Office
beats.modern: club news: our secret literary society (we're all Dickens characters, don't worry about it) admitted Laurie, and his acceptance speech came with INFRASTRUCTURE. he built a post office in the hedge between our houses. padlocks, a key for each family, room for letters, manuscripts, books, and bundles. even grandpa Laurence sends mystery packages through it now. I have a weird feeling that box is going to matter later, chat. writer's instinct.

beats.title: Salt Instead of Sugar
beats.modern: I hosted a dinner party today. results: asparagus boiled to string, bread burnt black, a lobster hammered out of its shell by force, potatoes raw, and, the centerpiece, strawberries served with SALT instead of sugar plus cream that had gone sour. our guest tasted one spoonful and drank water. I laughed till I cried, which was lucky, because the other option was just crying. also the canary died this week and the funeral is this afternoon. the no chores experiment is CONCLUDED.
beats.quote: "Salt instead of sugar, and the cream is sour,"

beats.title: The Croquet Cheat
beats.modern: croquet turned GEOPOLITICAL. the English guest nudged his ball through the wicket with his toe, I SAW IT, then told me Yankees are tricky when I called it out. so I went and stood in the nettles until I could speak without starting a second revolution, came back cool, and won the game with a clean stroke while his teammate's ball sat there untouched. sportsmanship is just rage with better aim, chat.
beats.quote: "We don't cheat in America, but you can, if you choose,"

beats.title: Castles in the Air
beats.modern: dream sharing circle on the hill. Laurie: Germany, music, fame. Meg: a lovely house full of luxury and 'pleasant people' (sure, Meg). Amy: Rome, art, best artist in the whole world. Beth: to stay home safe with father and mother and take care of the family. that's it. that's her whole castle. and me? I want to write books, get rich and famous, and do something splendid that won't be forgotten after I'm dead. manifesting on main, chat.
beats.quote: I want to do something splendid before I go into my castle,--something heroic or wonderful, that won't be forgotten after I'm dead.

beats.title: Your Sister
beats.modern: read a story aloud to my sisters tonight, real casual, face hidden behind the paper. they liked it. Meg cried at the romantic part. then Beth asked who wrote it, and I sat up and said: 'your sister.' CHAT. I'M PUBLISHED. no pay yet, the man 'doesn't pay beginners,' but it is PRINT, and someday this is how I support myself and help the girls. first W of the arc.
beats.quote: "Your sister."

beats.title: Two Lines
beats.modern: a telegram came, chat. two lines. 'Your husband is very ill. Come at once.' mom went white and the whole world changed in one minute. she's on the first train to Washington. no jokes this stream. help me pack.
beats.quote: "Your husband is very ill. Come at once.

beats.title: My One Beauty
beats.modern: mom needed money for the trip, so I sold the one thing I own that's actually worth something. walked into a shop with all my hair, walked out with twenty five dollars and a crop. the family SCREAMED. 'your one beauty!' I told them my head feels deliciously light and my vanity needed the haircut. ...it's midnight. Meg just caught me crying into my pillow. not about dad. about my HAIR. I contain multitudes, chat.
beats.quote: "O Jo, how could you? Your one beauty."

beats.title: The Baby Died
beats.modern: Beth's been visiting the poor Hummels all week while the rest of us dodged the chore. tonight she came home wrong. the baby died, chat. in her lap, before the mother got back with the doctor. scarlet fever. Beth's never had it, and she's already got the headache and the sore throat. her first thought was to protect Amy from catching it. I stayed home writing while she carried that alone. nurse duty starts now.
beats.quote: Oh, Jo, the baby's dead!"

beats.title: The Fever Turns
beats.modern: the doctor said midnight would decide it, better or worse. at two I looked at her face and every trace of pain was gone, and I thought that was the end, chat. I kissed her forehead and whispered goodbye. then Hannah woke, checked her, and threw her apron over her head: the fever TURNED. she's sleeping. actually sleeping. breathing easy. and at dawn, bells at the door, and Laurie whispering 'girls, she's come! she's come!' mom's home. we sat on the stairs and just held on.
beats.quote: "The fever's turned; she's sleepin' nat'ral; her skin's damp, and she breathes easy.

beats.title: Amy's Last Will
beats.modern: meanwhile in quarantine exile at our aunt's: Amy, age twelve, has drafted her LAST WILL AND TESTIMENT (her spelling), because 'life is uncertain' and she wants no ill feeling over her tomb. she left me her plaster rabbit and a written apology for burning my book. Laurie witnessed it with a straight face, and then she added a codicil: her curls to be cut off and given round to her friends. her greatest sacrifice, chat, and she means every word. I'm laughing and crying at the same time.
beats.quote: I felt that I ought to do it, for life is uncertain and I don't want any ill-feeling over my tomb."

beats.title: The Forged Love Letter
beats.modern: SCANDAL AT HOME. Meg got a love letter signed by Mr. Brooke and ANSWERED it, and then a second note claimed he never wrote any. four minutes of forensics: both were Laurie, running romance psyops because I wouldn't tell him a secret. mom took him into the parlor alone for half an hour, and nobody knows what was said in there, but he came out a penitent man. do NOT catfish my sister, chat. get griefed.
beats.quote: "I can no longer restrain my passion, and must know my fate before I return.

beats.title: Dad Drop
beats.modern: CHRISTMAS MIRACLE, CHAT. Laurie pokes his head in going 'here's another Christmas present for the March family' and it's DAD. muffled to the eyes, home from the war. total stampede: I nearly fainted, Brooke kissed Meg 'entirely by mistake' (sure), Amy tripped over a stool and hugged his BOOTS, and Beth, weak legged, wrapped in a blanket Beth, RAN into his arms. biggest drop in stream history.
beats.quote: "Here's another Christmas present for the March family."

beats.title: Aunt March Backfires
beats.modern: comedy of the CENTURY. Meg was mid rejection speech at Brooke when Aunt March hobbled in and ORDERED her not to marry him: poor tutor, no money, marry rich or you're out of my will. instant reverse psychology. Meg, who was eighty percent out the door, announced she'll marry whom she pleases. aunt rage quit. Brooke heard everything from the hall. and I walked in expecting to celebrate a banished lover and found my sister ON HIS KNEE. worst jump scare of my career, chat.
beats.quote: "I shall marry whom I please, Aunt March, and you can leave your money to any one you like,"

beats.title: First Kiss for Marmee
beats.modern: Meg's wedding day. no procession, no show. dad did the service and his voice broke, the groom's hands shook, and Meg looked straight up at him and said 'I will' like it was the easiest thing she's ever done. the second it was official she yelled 'the first kiss for Marmee!' and hugged mom before her own husband. Hannah sobbed that the cake ain't hurt a mite. I did NOT cry, chat. Laurie was watching me not cry, which made it worse.
beats.quote: "The first kiss for Marmee!"

beats.title: The Hundred Dollar Check
beats.modern: CHAT. I entered a newspaper contest with my most unhinged sensation story (duels, an elopement, ends in an earthquake) and a check for a HUNDRED DOLLARS just fell out of an envelope into my lap. I stared at it like it was a snake, then cried. dad says 'you can do better than this, aim at the highest, never mind the money.' respectfully: the money is sending Beth and mom to the seaside for a month. sensation sells and my family eats.
beats.quote: "You can do better than this, Jo. Aim at the highest, and never mind the money."

beats.title: The Jelly Won
beats.modern: report from my sister's newlywed cottage: she spent all day fighting currant jelly that refused to jell. one batch on the floor, one burning, kitchen a crime scene. and THAT is the day her husband brings a friend home to dinner unannounced. no dinner exists. she told him to take his guest to mother's, he laughed at the exact wrong moment, and she quit the field entirely. first married fight, chat: jelly. the jelly won.
beats.quote: "The--the jelly won't jell and I don't know what to do!"

beats.title: Twins by Jupiter
beats.modern: MEG HAD TWINS, chat. a boy and a girl. Laurie took one look and went 'twins, by Jupiter!' then begged someone to take them before he dropped them laughing. Amy put a blue ribbon on the boy and a pink one on the girl, French fashion, so we can tell them apart. names: Margaret, called Daisy... and for the boy, Laurie proposed DEMIJOHN, Demi for short. it stuck instantly. it's permanent now. I'm an aunt. new party members unlocked.
beats.quote: "Name him Demijohn, and call him 'Demi' for short,"

beats.title: Europe Goes to Amy
beats.modern: Aunt Carrol is going to Europe and taking a niece. it's Amy. AMY. Europe was MY quest, chat, I've been farming it my whole life. but apparently I once said 'favors burden me' and 'I hate French' in front of the wrong aunt, and she wrote it all down. my own mouth cost me the trip. Amy has all the fun and I have all the work, and knowing exactly whose fault it is somehow makes it worse.
beats.quote: "It's always so. Amy has all the fun and I have all the work. It isn't fair, oh, it isn't fair!"

beats.title: Strategic Retreat
beats.modern: roster news: I'm going to New York for the winter. teaching gig at a boarding house, fresh material for the writing. those are the official patch notes. the real ones, quietly: Laurie is getting too fond of me, and I don't feel it back. mom agrees we're not suited. two hot tempers and two strong wills in one lifetime contract, no thank you. so I'm leaving the lobby before he says something we can't take back. strategic retreat, chat.
beats.quote: "It may be vain and wrong to say it, but--I'm afraid--Laurie is getting too fond of me."

beats.title: The Coal Hod Professor
beats.modern: New York log, day one: there's a German professor in this boarding house. I watched him take a heavy coal hod out of a tiny servant girl's hands and carry it all the way up because 'the little back is too young to haf such heaviness.' poor as a church mouse, raising two orphan nephews, two buttons off his coat, a patch on one shoe, kindest eyes I've ever seen. he's almost forty, chat. this is NOT content. I just think he's neat.
beats.quote: "'It goes better so. The little back is too young to haf such heaviness.'

beats.title: Burning the Gunpowder
beats.modern: the Professor burned a sensation paper right in front of me and said he'd like to send all the rest after it, not knowing I write that exact rubbish for rent money. so I went upstairs and reread my stories wearing his moral spectacles. verdict: trash, and getting worse. I fed three months of work into the stove and nearly set the chimney on fire. better to burn the house down than let other people blow themselves up with my gunpowder. no, chat, you can't have the VODs. they're cinders.
beats.quote: I'd better burn the house down, I suppose, than let other people blow themselves up with my gunpowder,"

beats.title: The Refusal
beats.modern: it happened. Laurie said it all, chat. loved me since day one, gave up billiards for me, waited, everything. and I told him the truth: I can't say yes truly, so I won't say it at all. he swore I'd love somebody someday and he'd have to stand by and watch it. I said I'll never marry you, and the sooner you believe it the better for both of us. his face. chat, his face. I feel like I murdered something innocent.
beats.quote: "I can't say 'Yes' truly, so I won't say it at all.

beats.title: Beth's Secret
beats.modern: Beth told me today. on the warm rocks at the seaside, her head in my lap. she's known for a good while, chat. she's not getting better, and she gave up hoping back in the autumn, and she carried it alone all this time so she wouldn't frighten anybody. she says she's glad I finally see it. I asked how she could shut me out and bear it all alone. no bit tonight. just my sister, being braver than me again.
beats.quote: "Jo, dear, I'm glad you know it. I've tried to tell you, but I couldn't."

beats.title: Lazy Laurence
beats.modern: Amy update from Nice: she found Laurie deep in his sad boy Europe arc, six months of lounging, gossip, and being petted by silly people, and took him APART. new nickname: 'Lazy Laurence.' direct quote, delivered calm as a surgeon: 'well, I despise you.' he tried charm; she itemized his wasted money, talent, and time straight to his face. he ended up going 'I will be good, oh, I will be good' like a scolded child. my little sister does not miss, chat.
beats.quote: "Well, I despise you."

beats.title: Take My Place
beats.modern: found Beth awake by the fire holding a poem I wrote about her, asking if she'd really been all that to me. all that and more, chat. then she gave me her one assignment: take her place. be everything to father and mother when she's gone. she said love is the only thing we carry with us when we go, and it makes the end easy. I said I'd try. I would trade every book I'll ever write to not be needed for this.
beats.quote: You must take my place, Jo, and be everything to father and mother when I'm gone.

beats.title: The Tide Goes Out
beats.modern: spring came, and the birds came back, and Beth went with the tide. in the dark hour before dawn, on the chest where she drew her first breath, she quietly drew her last. no famous last words. one loving look. one little sigh. in the morning the fire was out and the room was very still. chat, I have no bit. my sister is gone, and the world kept its spring anyway.
beats.quote: in the dark hour before the dawn, on the bosom where she had drawn her first breath, she quietly drew her last, with no farewell but one loving look, one little sigh.

beats.title: The Same Boat
beats.modern: meanwhile in Switzerland: Laurie and Amy, one rowboat, the Alps watching. she takes an oar, they row in perfect time, and she says 'how well we pull together, don't we?' and he answers, no speech, no moonlight, mid lake at noon: 'so well that I wish we might always pull in the same boat. will you, Amy?' 'yes, Laurie.' very low. chat, I checked my heart for a bruise and found none. they fit. they actually fit.
beats.quote: "So well that I wish we might always pull in the same boat. Will you, Amy?"

beats.title: Truth Is the Secret
beats.modern: mom told me to write something for US, not for a market. something got into that story, chat. grief, mostly. dad mailed it to a magazine WITHOUT ASKING (parents meta gaming my career) and it hit: paid, reprinted in the newspapers, letters from strangers. his verdict: there is truth in it, that's the secret. I finally wrote with my heart instead of my rate card. Beth taught me the style. she just isn't here to read it.
beats.quote: "There is truth in it, Jo, that's the secret; humor and pathos make it alive, and you have found your style at last.

beats.title: He Said My Wife
beats.modern: woke up on the sofa to a GHOST kissing me awake. Laurie, back from Europe. two minutes in he says 'my wife' mid sentence, then tries to walk it back with 'oh, the dickens! now I've done it.' THEY GOT MARRIED, chat. six weeks ago, in Paris, at the consul's, quiet, because even in their happiness they didn't forget Beth. he knelt on the floor and promised 'never to do it again.' my old boy is my brother now. the audacity is fully healed. so are we, I think.
beats.quote: "You've gone and got married!"

beats.title: Going A-Wooing
beats.modern: KNOCK AT THE DOOR and it's my Professor. from New York. in a new suit of black, hair actually brushed, gold sleeve buttons, dressed like a man who came courting and I am NOT imagining it. the family absorbed him in one evening: babies rifling his pockets, dad locked in deep philosophical conversation, Laurie running suspicious brotherly surveillance and getting charmed anyway. then we both dove for my dropped ball of yarn and smacked heads. this is my romance arc, chat. head trauma and knitting.
beats.quote: "Dear old fellow! He couldn't have got himself up with more care if he'd been going a-wooing,"

beats.title: Under the Umbrella
beats.modern: he was leaving. going west. we're in the street, rain everywhere, and he sees me crying and asks 'heart's dearest, why do you cry?' and I, undignified creature, sob out 'because you are going away.' chat, he LIT UP. said he has nothing but much love to give and came to see if I could care for it. proposed in the mud under one old umbrella, hands too full of parcels to kneel. I said yes before he finished. the girl who was never marrying anyone would like to issue a formal correction.
beats.quote: "Jo, I haf nothing but much love to gif you; I came to see if you could care for it, and I waited to be sure that I was something more than a friend.

beats.title: A Wilderness of Boys
beats.modern: Aunt March died. F, genuinely: she loved me in her porcupine way. and she left me PLUMFIELD. the whole estate. Laurie assumed I'd sell it. absolutely not, chat. we're opening a school for boys. a good, happy, homelike school, me running it, Fritz teaching. rich pupils to fund it, a ragamuffin or two for the soul. the family laughed until they nearly needed a doctor. I'm dead serious. Plumfield my own, and a wilderness of boys to enjoy it with me.
beats.quote: "Boys. I want to open a school for little lads,--a good, happy, homelike school, with me to take care of them, and Fritz to teach them."

beats.title: Harvest Time
beats.modern: apple harvest at Plumfield, the whole family under the tree. Meg has her little home and her John. Amy has her art and her lord. I have a yard full of boys, a gray professor, and no complaints. never wrote the great book yet, chat, but I can wait: the material keeps improving. mom looked at all of us, kids and grandkids piled in her lap, and said she could never wish us a greater happiness than this. gg. thanks for watching the March arc. stream's over.
beats.quote: "O, my girls, however long you may live, I never can wish you a greater happiness than this!"

beats.title: The Dad Rule
beats.modern: ok chat, house rule from my dad before we start: don't judge anybody, they didn't all get your spawn point. I've run that rule my whole life and my only reward is every weirdo on the east coast trauma dumping in my DMs. anyway. this summer broke the rule. this summer broke everything.
beats.quote: “Whenever you feel like criticizing anyone,” he told me, “just remember that all the people in this world haven’t had the advantages that you’ve had.”

beats.title: The Eighty-Dollar Shoebox
beats.modern: setup tour: I'm paying eighty a month for a cardboard box wedged between two actual palaces. the one on my right is a full French castle clone with a marble pool and forty acres of lawn. belongs to some guy named Gatsby. never met him. love the consoling proximity of millionaires, chat.

beats.title: Tom's Book Report
beats.modern: dinner at my cousin Daisy's. her husband Tom, old money, ex football, built like a vending machine, just went OFF about a race science book he's reading. 'it's all scientific stuff, it's been proved.' nobody asked, Tom. Daisy is winking at me like it's hostage footage. one dinner in and I already want to log off the East.
beats.quote: The idea is if we don’t look out the white race will be—will be utterly submerged.

beats.title: The Fifth Guest
beats.modern: phone rings mid dinner. Tom vanishes. Daisy vanishes. Jordan leans in: 'Tom's got some woman in New York.' the mistress is calling the LANDLINE. at DINNER. then they come back and Daisy does a whole bit about a nightingale on the lawn while the phone rings AGAIN. my honest instinct was to call the police.
beats.quote: “Tom’s got some woman in New York.”

beats.title: Beautiful Little Fool
beats.modern: no bit for this one. Daisy told me what she said when her daughter was born, Tom God knows where: 'I'm glad it's a girl. and I hope she'll be a fool. that's the best thing a girl can be in this world, a beautiful little fool.' then she smirked, like being this hollow is a private club her and Tom belong to. chat I don't think anyone in that house is okay.
beats.quote: And I hope she’ll be a fool—that’s the best thing a girl can be in this world, a beautiful little fool.’

beats.title: Green Light Sighting
beats.modern: CHAT. my millionaire neighbor just materialized on his lawn at midnight. no party, no guests. he stretched both arms toward the water, toward one tiny green light across the bay, and I swear the man was trembling. I blinked and he DESPAWNED. what is his deal. what is the green light. I need the lore.
beats.quote: alone—he stretched out his arms toward the dark water in a curious way,

beats.title: The Eyes of Eckleburg
beats.modern: map update: between here and the city there's a wasteland where ashes grow like wheat. and looming over the whole zone, a rotting billboard of two giant blue eyes in yellow glasses. some optometrist's dead ad, retinas one yard high, just watching. most cursed loading screen in America. remember the eyes, chat. they're going to matter.
beats.quote: The eyes of Doctor T. J. Eckleburg are blue and gigantic—their retinas are one yard high.

beats.title: Meet My Girl
beats.modern: Tom physically hauled me off the train at the ash heaps to 'meet his girl.' at her husband's garage, chat. he small talked the husband about a car deal while setting up the hookup with the wife over his head. I asked if the husband suspects anything. Tom: 'he's so dumb he doesn't know he's alive.' this man is the final boss of audacity.
beats.quote: “Wilson? He thinks she goes to see her sister in New York. He’s so dumb he doesn’t know he’s alive.”

beats.title: The Open Hand
beats.modern: apartment party, hour six, everyone plastered. Myrtle starts chanting Daisy's name at Tom. Daisy! Daisy! Dai— and he broke her nose. open hand, one motion, like swatting a fly. blood on the towels, women screaming over the furniture, and the party just kept going around it. I got my hat off the chandelier and left. clip deleted. no rewatch.
beats.quote: Making a short deft movement, Tom Buchanan broke her nose with his open hand.

beats.title: The Party Machine
beats.modern: neighbor status report: the house is a permanent festival. a Rolls Royce shuttle to the city, a whole orchestra pit and not some five piece band, a machine that juices two hundred oranges if a butler presses the button two hundred times. every Monday eight servants repair the damage. nobody's invited, chat. everyone just spawns in.
beats.quote: In his blue gardens men and girls came and went like moths among the whisperings and the champagne and the stars.

beats.title: Host Status Unknown
beats.modern: finally inside one of the parties. host status: UNKNOWN. live theories at my table: he killed a man once. no, German spy. no, American army, but LOOK at him when he thinks nobody's watching. everyone has lore, nobody has canon. hundreds of guests drinking a ghost's champagne. Gatsby is an ARG and we're all playing it.
beats.quote: “You look at him sometimes when he thinks nobody’s looking at him. I’ll bet he killed a man.”

beats.title: The Books Are Real
beats.modern: found a very drunk man in owl glasses auditing the LIBRARY. 'the books are real! pages and everything! I thought they'd be a nice durable cardboard!' he's been drunk for a week and came in to sober up, and instead he's fact checking the mansion like it's set dressing. honestly? mood. this whole place feels like a build somebody rendered yesterday.
beats.quote: “Absolutely real—have pages and everything. I thought they’d be a nice durable cardboard.

beats.title: I'm Gatsby
beats.modern: CHAT. I just spent twenty minutes telling the war vet at my table how I still haven't met this mysterious Gatsby. he let me finish. then: 'I'm Gatsby.' I DESCRIBED THE STREAMER TO THE STREAMER. and that smile of his... it's like the game rendered a smile just for you, max settings, then snapped off. also he says 'old sport.' who says old sport.
beats.quote: “I thought you knew, old sport. I’m afraid I’m not a very good host.”

beats.title: The Backstory Speedrun
beats.modern: car ride lore dump. his story: rich Middle West family, all dead. 'educated at Oxford,' said like the words were hot. lived like a rajah collecting rubies. then soloed a German offensive so hard every Allied government mailed him medals. 'even Montenegro!' I asked what part of the Middle West. he said San Francisco. it's fanfic, chat... and then he pulled the ACTUAL Montenegro medal out of his pocket??
beats.quote: “I am the son of some wealthy people in the Middle West—all dead now.

beats.title: Molar Cufflinks
beats.modern: lunch with Gatsby's business associate. the man's cufflinks are human molars, chat. real ones. 'finest specimens.' and once he leaves, Gatsby drops it fully casual: 'he's the man who fixed the World's Series back in 1919.' played with the faith of fifty million people like a burglar blowing a safe. why isn't he in jail? 'they can't get him, old sport. he's a smart man.' what business is my neighbor in.
beats.quote: “He’s the man who fixed the World’s Series back in 1919.”

beats.title: The Louisville Files
beats.modern: Jordan just dropped five YEARS of lore. Louisville, 1917: Daisy and a young officer named JAY GATSBY, inseparable, then he ships out. cut to the night before her wedding to Tom: Daisy drunk for the first time in her life, clutching a letter, 'tell 'em Daisy's change' her mine.' they put her in a cold bath, pried the letter away in pieces, hooked the pearls back on her neck. next day she married Tom without a shiver. chat. CHAT.
beats.quote: ’Gratulate me,” she muttered. “Never had a drink before, but oh how I do enjoy it.”

beats.title: It Was Her Dock
beats.modern: FULL LORE UNLOCKED. the mansion. the parties. the light. he bought that house because Daisy lives across the bay. the green light is HER DOCK. five years of throwing parties for hundreds of strangers, hoping she'd wander in one night. and the big ask, after all that? I invite her to tea and he 'comes over.' that's the whole heist. the most down bad man in recorded history, and I'm his wingman now.
beats.quote: He had waited five years and bought a mansion where he dispensed starlight to casual moths—so that he could “come over” some afternoon to a stranger’s garden.

beats.title: Five Years Next November
beats.modern: reunion day. man ghosted through my house, went back out into the rain, and knocked on my front door like he just pulled up. now he's leaning on the mantel doing his best relaxed pose and knocks my clock off with his head. catches it. apologizes to the clock. Daisy: 'we haven't met for many years.' Gatsby, instantly: 'five years next November.' bro. you cannot have the timer memorized. you cannot say the timer OUT LOUD.
beats.quote: “We haven’t met for many years,” said Daisy, her voice as matter-of-fact as it could ever be. “Five years next November.”

beats.title: The Shirt Avalanche
beats.modern: now he's throwing his entire wardrobe at us. silk, flannel, coral, apple green, a literal avalanche of shirts piling up on the table. and Daisy buried her face in them and started SOBBING. 'they're such beautiful shirts. it makes me sad because I've never seen such beautiful shirts before.' chat, she is not crying about the shirts. nobody in history has cried about shirts.
beats.quote: “They’re such beautiful shirts,” she sobbed, her voice muffled in the thick folds.

beats.title: Quest Marker Down
beats.modern: he pointed into the mist: 'you always have a green light that burns all night at the end of your dock.' and I watched the patch notes go live on his face. the quest marker he chased for five years just turned back into a regular dock light. she's standing right next to him, and somehow that's the nerf. his count of enchanted objects went down by one.
beats.quote: “You always have a green light that burns all night at the end of your dock.”

beats.title: James Gatz of North Dakota
beats.modern: real backstory unlocked. his name is James Gatz. North Dakota farm kid. at seventeen he rowed out to warn a millionaire's yacht about the wind and introduced himself as JAY GATSBY, a character he'd had fully built for years, just waiting for the server to open. he didn't rebrand, chat. he created a whole new account and mained it until it became him.
beats.quote: The truth was that Jay Gatsby of West Egg, Long Island, sprang from his Platonic conception of himself.

beats.title: The Rollback Plan
beats.modern: the actual plan: Daisy tells Tom 'I never loved you,' four years get deleted by one sentence, and they get married from her house in Louisville like it's 1917 again. I said, gently: you can't repeat the past. he looked at me like I'd blasphemed. 'can't repeat the past? why of course you can!' he thinks the last five years is a bug he can patch. chat, there is no rollback. there's never been a rollback.
beats.quote: “Can’t repeat the past?” he cried incredulously. “Why of course you can!”

beats.title: Tom Sees It
beats.modern: hottest day of the year, lunch at the Buchanans'. Daisy just looked at Gatsby and said 'you always look so cool.' that was the confession, chat. out loud, at the table, in front of everyone. and Tom SAW it. his whole face rebooted. later, waiting for the cars, Gatsby says the truest thing anyone's said all summer: 'her voice is full of money.' that's the jingle in it. and now we're all driving to town together. this ends badly.
beats.quote: “Her voice is full of money,” he said suddenly.

beats.title: The Plaza Showdown
beats.modern: PLAZA HOTEL. hundred degrees, no ice, wedding music bleeding through the floor. Gatsby full sends: 'your wife doesn't love you. she's never loved you. she loves me.' Tom counters with receipts: the 'drugstores,' the bootlegging, Wolfshiem. and Daisy, the whole point of the war, cracks in the middle: 'I did love him once... but I loved you too.' and THAT'S the hit that lands. 'you loved me TOO?' too was never in his script, chat. five years of plan and no patch for too.
beats.quote: “Your wife doesn’t love you,” said Gatsby. “She’s never loved you. She loves me.”

beats.title: The Victory Lap
beats.modern: Tom won so hard he sent them home TOGETHER. in Gatsby's car. 'go on. he won't annoy you.' that's a finishing move, chat. he's not even worried anymore. oh, and I remembered mid wreckage that it's my birthday today. I'm thirty. we drove home through the cooling twilight, and the road already knew something we didn't.
beats.quote: So we drove on toward death through the cooling twilight.

beats.title: The Death Car
beats.modern: jokes off. Myrtle ran out into the road, ran AT the yellow car like she knew it. it came out of the dark, hit her, wavered, and disappeared around the bend. it didn't stop, chat. it didn't even slow down. she died right there on the road she'd lived over for eleven years. the papers will call it the death car. it's Gatsby's car.
beats.quote: The “death car” as the newspapers called it, didn’t stop; it came out of the gathering darkness, wavered tragically for a moment, and then disappeared around the next bend.

beats.title: Watching Over Nothing
beats.modern: found Gatsby hiding in the bushes outside Daisy's house. asked him who was driving. it was Daisy, chat. IT WAS DAISY. and he says, instantly, like it's obvious: 'but of course I'll say I was.' he's going to eat the whole thing for her. and through the pantry window? Daisy and Tom at the kitchen table over cold chicken, heads together, looking exactly like teammates. he's out there guarding her window till dawn. watching over nothing.
beats.quote: “Yes,” he said after a moment, “but of course I’ll say I was.

beats.title: The First Nice Girl
beats.modern: he told me everything before sunrise. Louisville, 1917: a broke kid in an officer's uniform, the one costume that hid his stats, in love with a girl who had never once heard the word rent. he knew he was in her house on a glitch. he stayed anyway. then the war, and she vanished back into that rich, full life and left him nothing. 'he felt married to her, that was all.' the name, the mansion, the shirts. all of it was one long walk back to that porch.
beats.quote: She vanished into her rich house, into her rich, full life, leaving Gatsby—nothing.

beats.title: The Only Compliment
beats.modern: last thing I ever yelled across that lawn: 'they're a rotten crowd. you're worth the whole damn bunch put together.' the only compliment I ever gave him. I disapproved of the man from beginning to end and I meant every word anyway. both things true, all the way down. and that smile came out one more time, like we'd been in cahoots on it forever. glad I said it, chat. gladdest I've ever been about anything.
beats.quote: “You’re worth the whole damn bunch put together.”

beats.title: God Sees Everything
beats.modern: meanwhile, the garage, all night: Wilson, destroyed, telling his neighbor how he took Myrtle to the window before she died. 'you may fool me, but you can't fool God.' and chat, he was pointing at the BILLBOARD. the giant faded eyes over the ash heaps. 'God sees everything,' he keeps repeating. 'that's an advertisement,' says the neighbor. he's not hearing it. a broken man just cast an optometrist ad as God, and at dawn he started walking.
beats.quote: “I told her she might fool me but she couldn’t fool God.

beats.title: The Pool
beats.modern: he waited by the pool for her call. first swim of the whole summer. he never once used that pool, chat. the call never came. Wilson came instead, on foot, all day, with a revolver. the chauffeur heard the shots and thought nothing of them. we found the mattress still drifting, tracing a thin red circle in the water. Wilson in the grass a little way off. I don't have a bit. there's no bit.
beats.quote: he had lost the old warm world, paid a high price for living too long with a single dream.

beats.title: The Tennis Shoes Call
beats.modern: trying to fill a funeral for a man who hosted hundreds every weekend. the phone rings. Klipspringer! the boarder! the guy who LIVED here free all summer! finally, I think, a mourner. no, chat. he can't make it, there's a picnic in Greenwich, but could the butler mail him the tennis shoes he left here. his TENNIS SHOES. I hung up mid address. the party lobby held thousands. the funeral lobby is me.
beats.quote: “What I called up about was a pair of shoes I left there.

beats.title: The Schedule
beats.modern: his dad came out from Minnesota. showed me a beat up copy of Hopalong Cassidy with a schedule pencilled inside the back cover, dated 1906. rise 6:00. dumbbell exercise. study needed inventions. 'no more smokeing.' 'be better to parents.' a farm kid grinding a self improvement build in the back of a cowboy book. 'Jimmy was bound to get ahead,' his dad keeps saying, holding it like treasure. chat, I'm not okay.
beats.quote: “Jimmy was bound to get ahead. He always had some resolves like this or something.

beats.title: Owl Eyes Shows Up
beats.modern: three cars in the rain. me, his father, the minister, a few servants, the postman from West Egg. hundreds drank his champagne every weekend, chat. hundreds. then one more car pulls up, and it's Owl Eyes. the drunk from the library. the only guest who ever checked whether anything in that house was real. he wiped his glasses and delivered the one true eulogy: 'the poor son-of-a-bitch.' amen to that.
beats.quote: “The poor son-of-a-bitch,” he said.

beats.title: Careless People
beats.modern: ran into Tom on Fifth Avenue and got the confirmation: HE told Wilson whose car it was. pointed a grieving man with a revolver at Gatsby's house, then packed and left. and he cried telling me this, over a box of dog biscuits, so I'm supposed to call it suffering. Daisy never sent a flower. careless people, Tom and Daisy. they smashed up things and creatures and retreated back into their money and let other people clean up the mess.
beats.quote: They were careless people, Tom and Daisy—they smashed up things and creatures and then retreated back into their money or their vast carelessness,

beats.title: Boats Against the Current
beats.modern: last night on the beach before I log off the East forever. thinking about the first time he picked out that green light and how close the dream must have looked. it was already behind him, chat. maybe it's behind all of us. tomorrow we run faster, stretch our arms out further... and one fine morning... so we beat on. boats against the current. borne back ceaselessly into the past. stream over. good night, old sports.
beats.quote: Gatsby believed in the green light, the orgiastic future that year by year recedes before us.

beats.title: Going Live From The Garret
beats.modern: yo chat. live from a garret the size of a cupboard, five flights up, four months behind on rent. every exit is a stealth section past the landlady's open kitchen door. rather than talk to her I will creep down the stairs like a cat. I owe everyone money and I'm planning... something. we'll get to it.

beats.title: The Rehearsal
beats.modern: dry run, chat. there's this pawnbroker: tiny, sixty, mean, neck like a hen's leg, rich off everyone's misery. I pawn dad's watch, but the REAL quest is recon. the layout, the keys, which pocket. and mid-scan my brain goes 'so the sun will shine like this THEN too.' chat. why did my brain say THEN. what is THEN.
beats.quote: “So the sun will shine like this then too!”

beats.title: Bar Guy Lore Drop
beats.modern: a drunk clerk at the tavern is giving me his full tragic backstory unprompted. mans sold his wife's STOCKINGS for drink. not the shoes. the stockings. and then he says the realest thing I've ever heard: he drinks so that he may suffer twice as much. Marmeladov, you are the most honest man on this server.
beats.quote: I drink so that I may suffer twice as much!”

beats.title: Nowhere To Turn
beats.modern: he keeps going. his wife married him because she was a widow with three kids and literally zero other options. then he leans in and asks if I understand what it means to have absolutely nowhere left to turn. the whole bar is laughing at him, chat. I'm not laughing.
beats.quote: Do you understand, sir, do you understand what it means when you have absolutely nowhere to turn?

beats.title: The Thirty Roubles
beats.modern: his daughter Sonia. stepmom, sick and desperate, said 'you eat and drink here and do nothing.' so at six she put on her cape and went out, and at nine she came back and laid thirty roubles on the table in silence. then lay down facing the wall. the stepmom spent the whole night kissing her feet. and he watched it all, drunk. chat, this family is being eaten alive and one girl is paying the bill.

beats.title: The Letter
beats.modern: mom's letter dropped, chat. two ounces, tiny handwriting. Dunya is ENGAGED. to Luzhin, 45, two government posts, 'already made his fortune,' a man who said out loud he wanted a poor bride so the wife looks upon her husband as her benefactor. mom writes it like it's charming. Dunya paced all night, prayed at the ikon, said yes in the morning. the tuition money is ME, chat. my sister is the payment plan.
beats.quote: a man ought not to be indebted to his wife, but that it is better for a wife to look upon her husband as her benefactor.

beats.title: It Shall Not Be
beats.modern: no. NO. Sonia got a yellow ticket, Dunya gets a lawyer with a benefactor complex. same trade, better paperwork. everyone sacrificing themselves for ME while I lie on this couch like an NPC. it shall not be, chat. I won't accept it. ...accept it with WHAT, big man? what's your counter-offer? exactly. nothing. fuck the excuses. something must be done NOW.
beats.quote: It shall not be, so long as I am alive, it shall not, it shall not! I won’t accept it!”

beats.title: The Horse Dream
beats.modern: nightmare: I'm seven again. a drunk crams six grown men into a cart hitched to one little mare and screams 'she'll gallop.' she can't. so they whip her, eyes, nose, everything, and when she still can't, he finishes her with a crowbar. dream-me pushes through the crowd and kisses her bleeding head. dad pulls me away: they're drunk, it's not our business. woke up soaked, chat. and I know exactly what my brain was trying to show me.

beats.title: Quest Abandoned
beats.modern: said the plan out loud for the first time. an axe, chat. an actual axe. me, her skull, sticky warm blood. my brain has been quietly building this for a MONTH. said it and nearly threw up. quest abandoned. I literally prayed on the bridge: show me my path, I renounce that accursed dream. uninstalled. free. lightest I've felt all summer.
beats.quote: “can it be, can it be, that I shall really take an axe, that I shall strike her on the head, split her skull open...

beats.title: The Seven O'Clock Leak
beats.modern: three hours, chat. THREE HOURS after I renounce everything, I cut through the Haymarket, completely out of my way, and overhear that Lizaveta, the pawnbroker's sister, is invited out tomorrow at exactly seven. meaning the old woman will be home ALONE. I didn't seek this intel. the universe just set a quest marker on my map. I walked home like a man condemned. no will left. it's decided.

beats.title: Simple Arithmetic
beats.modern: flashback clip: months ago, a random student in a tavern pitching MY exact plan to an officer. kill the useless old leech, take the money, fund a hundred fresh starts. one death, a hundred lives, simple arithmetic. officer: 'would you kill her yourself?' student: 'of course not.' and that, chat, is the entire difference between chat theorycrafting a build and someone actually queueing up with it.
beats.quote: One death, and a hundred lives in exchange--it’s simple arithmetic!

beats.title: The Run
beats.modern: it happened. chat, it happened and I'm not making it a bit. seven o'clock. the axe was in a noose under my coat. she turned to the window with my fake pledge and I don't remember deciding. my arms decided. she didn't even cry out loud. there's blood like an overturned glass and my hands won't stop shaking. I'm not clipping this. there's no clipping this.

beats.title: Lizaveta Came Home
beats.modern: the front door was open. Lizaveta came home. the gentlest person in this entire city, and she didn't scream, didn't guard her face, just held out one empty hand like a child asking me to stop. chat. the plan was ONE harmful old woman for a hundred good deeds. the arithmetic died in that room with her. two bodies. the second one refutes everything.

beats.title: The Latch
beats.modern: I'm trapped INSIDE the flat, chat, holding the door hook, while two randoms ring the bell a dozen times. one of them is a law student doing detective cosplay in real time: 'the hook's on from inside, someone's HOME.' brother please log off. they go fetch the porter, I slip down, duck into the freshly painted empty flat below, and walk out the gate. nobody saw me. nobody saw me. say it with me, chat: nobody saw me.

beats.title: Fainting At The Precinct
beats.modern: day one and the police SUMMON me. full panic. turns out it's my landlady suing over an IOU. unrelated side quest, debt collection. I'm giggling with relief, signing forms, when the officers start discussing THE CASE five feet away. next thing I know I'm in a chair with someone holding water. yes chat. I fainted. in a police station. the day after. and they noticed. stealth build, zero composure stat.

beats.title: Loot Buried, Never Counted
beats.modern: hid it all under a big stone in a random courtyard and walked away laughing like a maniac. buried my tracks. and here's the part where you scream at the screen: I never counted it. never even opened the purse. all those agonies for loot I refuse to LOOK at. so what the hell was the run for, chat? genuinely asking. chat? anyone?

beats.title: Baiting Zametov
beats.modern: found Zametov, the police clerk, at a café and did the most unhinged bit of my life. leaned in close, dead-eyed, whispered exactly how I'D have hidden the loot. stone, courtyard, touch nothing for years. and then: 'and what if it was I who murdered the old woman and Lizaveta?' his face went whiter than the tablecloth. then I laughed like it's all a joke. chat I am speedrunning my own arrest for content.
beats.quote: “And what if it was I who murdered the old woman and Lizaveta?”

beats.title: Back To The Flat
beats.modern: went back to the flat, chat. the actual flat. workmen are repapering the walls, lilac flowers over everything that happened. I rang the old cracked bell again and again just to feel the exact dread one more time. then asked them 'why have you washed away the blood?' and offered to explain everything at the police station. from the outside, how does this look. don't answer. I know. I can't stop.

beats.title: Marmeladov Down
beats.modern: crowd on the street, a rich man's carriage, someone under the hooves. chat, it's HIM. Marmeladov. the bar guy. drunk, crushed, unrecognizable. I'm shouting that I know him, I'm paying for the doctor, carry him home. his kids are about to watch this. someone run ahead for Sonia. worst possible lore continuation.

beats.title: Sonia Daughter Forgive
beats.modern: he came to for one minute. saw Sonia at the door, in the gaudy work clothes his drinking bought, and used his last strength: 'Sonia! Daughter! Forgive!' and fell reaching for her. he died in her arms. chat.
beats.quote: “Sonia! Daughter! Forgive!”

beats.title: Thy Servant Rodion
beats.modern: gave the widow my last twenty for the funeral. yes, mom's money. all of it. and on the dark staircase little Polenka chased me down, arms like sticks, hugged me and promised to pray for me all the rest of her life. chat, something switched back ON. my life didn't die with that old woman. I'm alive. I want to LIVE. what a feeling after a week in the grave.
beats.quote: “I’ll pray for you all the rest of my life,”

beats.title: Mom Walked In
beats.modern: opened my door: MOM AND DUNYA. sitting on my sofa. they'd waited ninety minutes, they rushed me crying with joy, and I stood there like a corpse. couldn't lift my arms to hug them. then the floor came up. yes chat, fainted AGAIN, in front of my mother. she traveled two days to see her golden boy. she got this.

beats.title: My Article Gets Quoted
beats.modern: the investigator, Porfiry. round little guy, smiles constantly. casually cites an ARTICLE I published: mankind splits into ordinary material and extraordinary men who have an inner right to step over obstacles. Napoleon rules. and chat, on camera, in front of the detective, I DEFENDED THE THESIS. expanded it. gave examples. then he asked if I believe in Lazarus rising from the dead and I said literally yes. clip that. that's evidence now. he was never asking as a fan.
beats.quote: But extraordinary men have a right to commit any crime and to transgress the law in any way, just because they are extraordinary.

beats.title: Called Out IRL
beats.modern: a stranger just looked me dead in the eyes on the street and said, quiet and clear: 'murderer.' then walked off like he'd said good morning. chat. WHO IS HE. what does he know, and HOW. I stood frozen for ten minutes, then went home and lay down like a dead man. the server knows. somehow the server already knows.
beats.quote: “Murderer!”

beats.title: The Laughing Dream
beats.modern: dream: back in the flat. she's under a cloak in the corner. I swing the axe and she doesn't die. she LAUGHS. shakes with silent laughter, hiding it, and the harder I hit the louder the flat laughs with her, and the stairwell fills with silent staring people. tried to scream, woke up. and chat, there is a MAN in my doorway. real. watching me sleep. 'Svidrigailov, allow me to introduce myself.' Dunya's stalker from the letter. HIM.

beats.title: Bathhouse Eternity
beats.modern: Svidrigailov talks to me like we're old friends and it's freaking me out. says his dead wife visits him. says maybe eternity isn't vast at all. just one little room, like a village bathhouse, black with grime, spiders in every corner, forever. I asked how he can't imagine anything JUSTER than that. chat, the scary part isn't the spider room. the scary part is I couldn't counter it.
beats.quote: what if it’s one little room, like a bath house in the country, black and grimy and spiders in every corner, and that’s all eternity is?

beats.title: Luzhin Gets Uninstalled
beats.modern: the Luzhin summit went PERFECTLY. he spent it explaining Dunya should be grateful he chose a bride with a ruined reputation. Dunya stood up: 'Pyotr Petrovitch, go away.' he threatened to never come back. chat, that's not the threat you think it is. then he ITEMIZED HIS EXPENSES on the way out. the trunk shipped for free, you absolute shithead. blocked, unmatched, griefed out of the family. Dunya carried.
beats.quote: I have been led on account of that into expenses....”

beats.title: The Bow
beats.modern: I kissed Sonia's foot, chat. she jumped back like I'd lost it. maybe I have. so I told her the truth: I did not bow down to you, I bowed down to all the suffering of humanity. she's eighteen and carrying a dead man's whole family on a yellow ticket. everyone treats her like dirt. she is the strongest person in this city and nobody claps for her. so I did.
beats.quote: “I did not bow down to you, I bowed down to all the suffering of humanity,”

beats.title: Lazarus Come Forth
beats.modern: asked her to read me the raising of Lazarus. one candle-end, her voice shaking, cold with ecstasy. dead four days, and he came forth. the book itself says what we are, chat, word for word: the murderer and the harlot, reading the eternal book together. I keep snagging on one detail. four days dead. and he walked out. hold that thought for me.
beats.quote: the murderer and the harlot who had so strangely been reading together the eternal book.

beats.title: The Third-Party Confession
beats.modern: Porfiry has me in the office getting psychologically COOKED. he's smiling, circling, I can feel a trap loading. and then the door bursts open and Nikolay, a housepainter, drops to his knees: 'I am guilty! mine is the sin! I am the murderer.' confesses to MY murders. unprompted. Porfiry's entire combo dropped on the floor. chat, I just got saved by the biggest third-party in Petersburg history, and the man isn't even lying for profit. he WANTS to suffer.
beats.quote: “I am guilty! Mine is the sin! I am the murderer,”

beats.title: The Planted Hundred
beats.modern: Luzhin's revenge play: at the funeral dinner he publicly accuses SONIA of stealing a hundred roubles. and it's IN HER POCKET, chat. he planted it while 'kindly' giving her ten. the room turns on her. and then his own roommate Lebeziatnikov stands up: I SAW him slip it into her pocket, I'll take my oath. caught. live. in front of everyone. get griefed, Luzhin. that's twice.

beats.title: Take A Good Look
beats.modern: I told Sonia. couldn't say the words. I said 'guess,' and then 'take a good look.' and her face slowly became Lizaveta's face, chat. the same childish terror, the same little hand held out. she guessed. and then she HUGGED me. 'what have you done to yourself?' to MYSELF. and: there's no one in the whole world unhappier than me. I confess to two murders and this woman's first move is grief FOR me. I don't have a stat for what she is.
beats.quote: “What have you done--what have you done to yourself?”

beats.title: The Redemption Quest
beats.modern: her patch for my corrupted save, word for word: go to the crossroads, bow, kiss the earth you defiled, and say out loud to all the world 'I am a murderer.' then God will send you life again. that's the quest, chat. public. humiliating. no skips, no stealth route. I told her I'm not doing it. I keep hearing it anyway. on loop.
beats.quote: stand at the cross-roads, bow down, first kiss the earth which you have defiled and then bow down to all the world and say to all men aloud, ‘I am a murderer!’

beats.title: The Ball Is Over
beats.modern: Katerina Ivanovna is dying on Sonia's bed. consumption, three kids, evicted mid-memorial-dinner, made the children dance in the street for coins until she broke. she hands them over: take them all, I've had enough. the ball is over. refuses the priest. says God must forgive her without one, he knows how she suffered. and if he won't, she doesn't care. chat, she's right, and nobody in this story will say it. so I will.
beats.quote: I hand them over to you, I’ve had enough! The ball is over.”

beats.title: The Wall Has Ears
beats.modern: AT THE DEATHBED, Svidrigailov pulls me aside. he'll fund the orphans, fifteen hundred each. because, he smiles, the dead woman wasn't 'a louse, like some old pawnbroker.' chat. those are MY words. from MY confession. to SONIA. he lodges one wall away from her room. he heard everything. the villain has my whole VOD downloaded and he's quoting my own clips back at me. 'how do you know?' I could barely breathe it out.
beats.quote: “How do you know?”

beats.title: You Are The Murderer
beats.modern: Porfiry came to my room. no warrant, no tricks, tea-time voice. I asked him who the murderer is. he leaned in and whispered: why, YOU, Rodion Romanovitch. you are the murderer. then he didn't arrest me. told me to walk in and confess myself, it'll shave the sentence. said don't disdain life. seek and ye shall find. chat, the final boss just handed me the controller and told me to finish the level myself.
beats.quote: You are the murderer,”

beats.title: Dunya Does Not Miss
beats.modern: Svidrigailov locked my SISTER in a flat with him. blackmail, the overheard confession, five locked rooms, 'no one would believe you.' Dunya pulled out a REVOLVER. first shot grazed his scalp. he stood there and told her to shoot again. misfire. two paces. she threw the gun down. and something in him actually broke, chat. he laid the key on the table and let her go. Dunya faced the demon of this story with two bullets and beat him with NEITHER.
beats.quote: “I know you will shoot, you pretty wild creature. Well, shoot away!”
