beats.title: Going To America
beats.modern: no jokes on this clip. that same night Svidrigailov gave away all his money, wandered the rain till dawn, and walked up to a watchman in a little copper Achilles helmet. 'where are you off to?' 'to America.' and he pulled the trigger. chat, that's the endgame of the man who dared everything and believed in nothing. I keep thinking I was two patches away from that build.
beats.quote: When you are asked, you just say he was going, he said, to America.”

beats.title: Kissing The Pavement
beats.modern: I did the quest, chat. knelt in the middle of the Haymarket and kissed the filthy earth. bliss and rapture, genuinely. crowd's verdict: 'he's boozed.' roasted mid-redemption. the words 'I am a murderer' died right there in my throat. but at the second bow I spotted Sonia fifty paces off, hiding behind a shanty. she followed me the whole way. she'll follow me to the ends of the earth. okay. station. let's finish this.
beats.quote: “He’s boozed,”

beats.title: It Was I
beats.modern: I almost bailed TWICE. small-talked the loud lieutenant about nihilists and midwives, and then he drops it, casually: Svidrigailov shot himself this morning. my last exit, gone. I walked out. and Sonia was standing in the yard, pale, just LOOKING at me. I turned around. walked back up. and said it, chat, softly and distinctly, on the record: it was I killed the old pawnbroker woman and her sister Lizaveta with an axe and robbed them. stream's over. clip everything.
beats.quote: “It was I killed the old pawnbroker woman and her sister Lizaveta with an axe and robbed them.”

beats.title: Eight Years
beats.modern: sentencing patch notes: eight years, Siberia, second-class convict. the detail that broke the whole courtroom: I confessed everything in perfect order, and the purse under the stone had 317 roubles in it. untouched. never opened. the lawyers could not compute a robber who wouldn't check his loot. chat, I could have told them. it was never about the money. I still can't tell you what it was about. that's the sentence under the sentence.

beats.title: Mom Never Knew
beats.modern: mom died, chat. brain fever. they never told her where I am. but she was redecorating my room for a homecoming I never scheduled, and in her delirium she said things that proved she knew everything. all along. knew, and kept setting the table anyway. moms always know. F. just F.

beats.title: The Plague Dream
beats.modern: fever dream from the prison hospital: a plague where everyone infected becomes CONVINCED they alone have the truth. every single person, an extraordinary man. nobody can agree what evil even is. armies attack themselves mid-march. the world burns down not from malice, chat, from CERTAINTY. I finally saw my article from the outside. run it on one man, you get me. run it on everyone, you get the end of the world.

beats.title: The Riverbank
beats.modern: she came to the riverbank at dawn and sat down beside me. no words. and something seized me and THREW me at her feet, chat. I wept and held her knees, and for one second she was frightened, and then her whole face was infinite happiness. she knew. seven years left. we're counting them like seven days. I'm not fixed. but I'm alive, and it finally started.

beats.title: A New Story
beats.modern: last clip. her New Testament is under my pillow, the one she read Lazarus from. haven't opened it yet. but the narrator says it himself: this is the beginning of a new story, the gradual renewal of a man, his passing from one world into another. that's a different stream, chat. this one's done. gg. thanks for watching the whole VOD. Sonia's got the channel.
beats.quote: But that is the beginning of a new story--the story of the gradual renewal of a man, the story of his gradual regeneration, of his passing from one world into another,

beats.title: Day One Of The Grind
beats.modern: chat we are LIVE from Marseilles, 1815. captain died mid-voyage so I docked the ship myself. nineteen years old, cargo intact, owner already hinting the captain chair is mine. engaged to the most beautiful girl in the Catalans. life is genuinely perfect right now. remember this timestamp.

beats.title: The Group Chat Of Evil
beats.modern: found this VOD way too late, chat. a table at the bar: the purser who wants my job, the guy who wants my fiancée, my drunk neighbor. Danglars writes an anonymous tip calling me a traitor. with his LEFT hand, so the writing can't be traced. then goes 'haha jk' and crumples it where Fernand can reach it. CLIP IT. clip every second of it.
beats.quote: I have always had more dread of a pen, a bottle of ink, and a sheet of paper, than of a sword or pistol.”

beats.title: The Wedding Raid
beats.modern: it's my BETROTHAL FEAST. Mercédès is right there. we are an hour from married. and soldiers knock three times and arrest me mid-toast, in the name of the law. I tell everyone it's a little mix-up, I'll probably be back before dessert. chat. I was not back before dessert.
beats.quote: “Edmond Dantès,” replied the magistrate, “I arrest you in the name of the law!”

beats.title: The DA Speedruns A Cover-Up
beats.modern: the prosecutor reads my file, sees I'm obviously innocent, literally says I'm free. then he asks who the letter I was carrying is addressed to. I say the name. his face crashes to desktop. the recipient is HIS DAD, a conspirator. so he burns the only evidence 'for my protection' and coaches me to deny it exists. chat why is my get-out-of-jail card on fire.
beats.quote: “Oh, if he knows the contents of this!” murmured he, “and that Noirtier is the father of Villefort, I am lost!”

beats.title: Welcome To The Château d'If
beats.modern: they load me in a boat at night and won't say where we're going. 'look round you.' it's the Château d'If. the island supermax. no judge, no sentence, no logout button. I tried to jump overboard and got a carbine on my temple for it. I'm nineteen. server admin abuse of the highest order.
beats.quote: “There are only,” said the gendarme, “a governor, a garrison, turnkeys, and good thick walls.

beats.title: The Hunger Strike Arc
beats.modern: four years in solitary, chat. I stopped counting at two. new plan, the only unban left: throw every meal out the window and let the hunger finish it. day six I can't see anymore. no jokes on this one. there was no chat in that cell. there was nothing.
beats.quote: It was the twilight of that mysterious country called Death!

beats.title: New Sound In The Walls
beats.modern: I am actively dying and I hear SCRATCHING inside the wall. not rats. rhythmic. tool on stone. chat, somebody is DIGGING. I start eating again immediately, chatting up the jailer so he won't hear it. never been this locked in over a noise in my life.

beats.title: Co-op Mode Unlocked
beats.modern: THE FLOOR JUST CAVED IN and an old man climbed out of the hole into my cell. chat I am hugging a stranger who breached my floor and it's the best thing that has ever happened on this stream. say hi to Abbé Faria, the 'mad priest' of the château. he is not mad. he's the smartest human alive.

beats.title: The Worst GPS In History
beats.modern: update on my new roommate: he dug FIFTY FEET with a chisel made from a bed clamp. one problem. he was aiming for the outer wall and the open sea. he curved wrong. six years of tunneling, and he surfaced in... another locked cell. mine. F in the wall for Faria. we're already drafting tunnel two.
beats.quote: instead of taking an ellipsis of forty feet, I made it fifty.

beats.title: The Detective Episode
beats.modern: Faria asks me five questions about my arrest and solves the whole thing on the spot. who gains if I lose the captaincy? Danglars. who wanted my girl? Fernand. who writes left-handed? Danglars. and my 'kind' prosecutor? the letter was addressed to HIS OWN FATHER. he buried me to bury the family secret. I FUCKING SEE IT NOW, chat. three separate men third-partied my whole life in one day.
beats.quote: This Noirtier was his father!”

beats.title: Prison University
beats.modern: new arc: the old man is teaching me EVERYTHING. mathematics, physics, history, three or four languages. six months in I'm speaking Spanish, English, and German. most productive dungeon stay in recorded history. shoutout to my entire education system: one dying priest in a hole.
beats.quote: At the end of a year Dantès was a new man.

beats.title: The Mad Priest's Secret
beats.modern: Faria just went 'my treasure is real and half of it is yours.' chat, this treasure talk is EXACTLY why the whole prison calls him mad. so I'm nodding along like you do with a sick relative. sure man. big treasure. we'll look at it tomorrow, no rush. hold that thought, chat. hold it tight.
beats.quote: No, be assured, I am not mad. This treasure exists, Dantès, and if I have not been allowed to possess it, you will.

beats.title: The Loot Drop Of All Time
beats.modern: it's real. IT'S REAL. a Renaissance cardinal's fortune buried on a deserted island called Monte Cristo. two million Roman crowns. thirteen million francs. escape together and half is mine; if he dies here, all of it. then he calls me the son of his captivity and I'm sobbing into his one working arm. he's not my cellmate, chat. he's my dad.
beats.quote: “Two millions of Roman crowns; nearly thirteen millions of our money.”2

beats.title: F In Chat For Faria
beats.modern: the third attack takes him. his last words are for me: 'Monte Cristo, forget not Monte Cristo.' I pour the whole vial down his throat and count drops with my heartbeat. nothing works. I sit with him till dawn, still doubting while the light comes up. the only person on earth who loves me is a body I can't even close the eyes of.
beats.quote: said,—“Monte Cristo, forget not Monte Cristo!”

beats.title: The Sack Swap
beats.modern: they sewed Faria into a burial sack. so here's the wildest play ever attempted on this stream: I move his body to my bed and sew MYSELF into the sack. the gravediggers carry me out, tie something heavy to my feet, swing me — 'one, two, three' — and YEET me off the cliff. chat, the château doesn't have a graveyard. the sea is the cemetery of the Château d'If.
beats.quote: The sea is the cemetery of the Château d’If.

beats.title: Spawn Point: Open Ocean
beats.modern: thirty-six pounds of iron dragging me to the bottom. rip the sack with the knife, cut the rope off my legs at the exact second my lungs quit, and BREACH. storm overhead, fortress behind me, and one stat that never decayed in fourteen years: best swimmer in Marseilles. first checkpoint is a league of black water. LET'S GO.

beats.title: Fourteen Years
beats.modern: smugglers fished me out. I take the helm and ask the deckhand the date, real casual, like I just forgot. February 28th. 1829. chat. I went in at nineteen. I'm thirty-three. fourteen years, day for day. I don't know if anyone I love is alive. Danglars. Fernand. Villefort. the dungeon oath still stands, and it just collected fourteen years of interest.
beats.quote: It was fourteen years, day for day, since Dantès’ arrest.

beats.title: Checking The Loot Table
beats.modern: Monte Cristo island. pried the chest open with a pickaxe and went motionless. three compartments: stacked gold coin, bars of raw gold, and a layer of diamonds, pearls and rubies that sounds like HAIL when you run your hands through it. I sprinted around the rocks screaming at seagulls, chat. the richest man alive is currently a barefoot guy on an empty island.
beats.quote: He was alone—alone with these countless, these unheard-of treasures! Was he awake, or was it but a dream?

beats.title: The Debrief
beats.modern: put on a priest disguise and interviewed my old neighbor, who has no clue it's me. the patch notes from while I was 'away': my father died of hunger. of HUNGER, chat. nine days. blessing me with his last breath. meanwhile Danglars is a millionaire baron and Fernand is a count and a general. the men who wrote the letter are thriving. stream's taking a short break.
beats.quote: ‘If you ever see my Edmond again, tell him I die blessing him.’”

beats.title: The Bride Rerolled
beats.modern: and Mercédès? eighteen months of waiting. my father died in her arms. no body, no letter, nothing to bury. then she married Fernand. the SAME church we booked, chat. the priest voice I was doing nearly cracked on 'only a change of bridegrooms.' I can't even be angry at her. I can be angry at everyone else.
beats.quote: “there was only a change of bridegrooms.”

beats.title: The Red Purse Save
beats.modern: first quest isn't revenge, it's a rescue. my old boss Morrel, the ONE man who fought for me for fourteen years, is at his desk with a loaded pistol and a clock running out on his debts. then his daughter bursts in holding a red silk purse: every debt receipted, plus a diamond labeled as her dowry. the pistol drops. anonymous donor, chat. no idea who.

beats.title: Rebrand Announcement
beats.modern: and then a brand-new Pharaon sails into harbor, fully loaded, because I had the entire SHIP secretly rebuilt. Morrel's weeping, the whole pier is chanting. that was the last good deed under the old name, chat. 'farewell kindness, humanity, and gratitude.' the reward arc is complete. new name, new build. the vengeance patch drops in Paris.
beats.quote: “farewell kindness, humanity, and gratitude! Farewell to all the feelings that expand the heart!

beats.title: Bandit Aggro Deleted
beats.modern: ten years later. new identity: the Count of Monte Cristo. tonight in Rome, bandits grabbed a young French viscount at Carnival and priced his head at four thousand piastres. I stroll into their catacombs, twenty carbines pointed at me, and the bandit KING takes his hat off and apologizes. the hostage I'm freeing? Albert de Morcerf. Fernand's son. yes chat. I just rescued my enemy's kid, free of charge. the run is ON.
beats.quote: “not so bad for a man who is to be shot at seven o’clock tomorrow morning.”

beats.title: Server Entrance
beats.modern: Paris. Albert's breakfast party. the son of the man who ruined me, plus half of young Paris, in one room, actively debating whether I exist. the clock strikes half past ten and the butler announces me ON the chime. fourteen years in a cell teaches you one stat above all, chat: timing.
beats.quote: “Punctuality,” said Monte Cristo, “is the politeness of kings, according to one of your sovereigns, I think; but it is not the same with travellers.

beats.title: The Ex Sees Through Everything
beats.modern: all of Paris is fooled. then the countess de Morcerf walks into the salon, sees me, and grabs the door-post to stay upright. Mercédès knew INSTANTLY, chat. she says nothing. I say nothing. we perform a full minute of flawless aristocratic small talk while both our heart rates redline. hardest 'everything is fine' kayfabe ever streamed. do NOT break it.

beats.title: Infinite Money Glitch
beats.modern: opened an account with Baron Danglars today. he leans back all smug: 'were you even to require a MILLION—' a million? chat I carry that in my pocket-book. I fan out treasury bonds like trading cards, set year-one spending at six million, and order half a million delivered by ten tomorrow morning. his pupils, chat. I watched greed physically dilate the man.
beats.quote: A million? Excuse my smiling when you speak of a sum I am in the habit of carrying in my pocket-book or dressing-case.”

beats.title: Haydée Lore Drop
beats.modern: meet Haydée. her father was Ali Pasha of Yanina. betrayed and murdered by a French officer he trusted, and his wife and daughter were sold as slaves. I bought her freedom. she lives with me under one rule: never say her father's name in Paris. why? because the officer who sold her is HERE, chat, wearing a title he bought with his master's blood. that card stays face down. for now.
beats.quote: “He is here, and here,” said she, touching her eyes and her heart.

beats.title: The Chemistry Seminar
beats.modern: Madame de Villefort, the prosecutor's wife, keeps steering our chats toward poison. purely academic interest, chat. so I explain, purely academically, how one milligram a day builds immunity until you can share a carafe of water and only ONE of you dies. she took mental NOTES. am I the villain-arc supplier now? anyway. remember this timestamp too.
beats.quote: at the end of a month, when drinking water from the same carafe, you would kill the person who drank with you, without your perceiving, otherwise than from slight inconvenience, that there was any poisonous substance mingled with this water.”

beats.title: NPC Deployment
beats.modern: I hired actors, chat. a fake Italian major, and for his long-lost 'son' — a charming young criminal named Benedetto, now playing 'Prince Andrea Cavalcanti' complete with allowance, wardrobe, and a tearful reunion I scripted myself. Paris society devours him. Danglars is already eyeing him for his daughter. the DLC character is not random, chat. wait for the reveal. WAIT for it.

beats.title: The Telegraph Hack
beats.modern: today I bought a telegraph operator a retirement garden for twenty-five thousand francs, and in exchange he wiggled three wrong signals down the line to Paris. fake news: the Spanish pretender escaped! Danglars panic-dumps his Spanish bonds. next morning: whoops, signal misread, fog. one million francs, evaporated. chat, I just learned how a gardener gets rid of the dormice that eat his peaches.
beats.quote: “I have just discovered how a gardener may get rid of the dormice that eat his peaches.”

beats.title: Dinner Party From Hell
beats.modern: I bought the house at Auteuil. a very specific house. tonight I hosted Danglars' wife and prosecutor Villefort and gave the garden tour: 'fun fact — digging under this very tree, my man found a box holding the skeleton of a newborn.' Villefort's arm is TREMBLING in mine. because twenty years ago he buried his affair baby right there. and the affair, chat? she's holding my other arm.
beats.quote: “How? is it not a crime to bury a living child in a garden?”

beats.title: It Started
beats.modern: people are dying in the Villefort house, chat. Valentine's grandmother went down with 'tetanus symptoms,' and the doctor privately names the real mechanic: brucine. poison. and then he and Villefort agree to bury the diagnosis and just... watch the house. remember who took notes at my chemistry seminar. this is out of my hands now. I hate that I built the hands.
beats.quote: Madame de Saint-Méran succumbed to a powerful dose of brucine or of strychnine, which by some mistake, perhaps, has been given to her.”

beats.title: Wrong Glass
beats.modern: the lemonade was dosed for grandpa Noirtier — except a year of his own medicine made the old man immune. so Barrois, the loyal servant, drinks it instead and dies on the floor mid-errand. the doctor runs the syrup-of-violets test: green. confirmed poison, victim number three. then he looks the prosecutor dead in the eye: 'people die very suddenly in your house.' the leaderboard is public now, chat.
beats.quote: People die very suddenly in your house, M. de Villefort.”

beats.title: One
beats.modern: Caderousse broke into my house tonight, knife first. his old cellmate Benedetto tipped him the job — then stabbed him on his way out the window. as he lay dying he asked who I am. I took off the priest wig, chat. let him see all the way back to 1815. he understood in his last second. I looked at the body and said one word. one.

beats.title: The Receipts Drop
beats.modern: Fernand — sorry, 'Count de Morcerf' — faces the Chamber of Peers over Yanina. surprise witness: a veiled Greek woman with DOCUMENTS. her birth record. the bill of her own sale. Haydée points at him across the chamber: assassin, with his master's blood still on his brow. he flees the room without one word of defense. verdict: guilty, unanimous. the title he built on a corpse just got repossessed live, chat.
beats.quote: Assassin, assassin, assassin, you have still on your brow your master’s blood! Look, gentlemen, all!’

beats.title: Glove Accepted
beats.modern: Albert connected the dots on who fed the press the Yanina story and jumped me at the Opera, screaming, glove out, full lobby watching. I take the glove and inform him I'll return it wrapped around a bullet. pistols at eight a.m. Maximilian asks what I'm going to do. chat, I've rehearsed this for a decade. the son pays the father's bill. that IS the design.
beats.quote: “I consider your glove thrown, and will return it to you wrapped around a bullet.

beats.title: The Visitor At Midnight
beats.modern: there is a veiled woman in my study at midnight and she opens with six words: 'Edmond, you will not kill my son.' EDMOND. chat, twenty-three years, and one syllable of my real name from HER knocks the pistol out of my hand. Mercédès knew from day one. she watched me circle her whole family and held the secret until tonight.
beats.quote: “Edmond, you will not kill my son!”

beats.title: The Avenger Gets Ratioed
beats.modern: I hit her with the full log: my father starving to death, my fourteen years in the dark, her wedding. she answers with one line — she has seen the man she loved about to murder her son. and I fold, chat. 'the lion was daunted; the avenger was conquered.' Albert lives. which means at eight a.m. I stand on that field and let a furious twenty-two-year-old shoot me. the run's final boss is me.
beats.quote: The lion was daunted; the avenger was conquered.

beats.title: The Public Apology
beats.modern: dueling ground, eight a.m. my will is written, chat. Albert gallops in — and instead of picking up a pistol, he THANKS me. publicly. declares his father's treachery justified everything I did, in front of every witness in Paris. his mother told him the whole story overnight. the kid chose truth over his own bloodline. duel cancelled. I get to live, and I genuinely don't know what to do with that.
beats.quote: you were justified in revenging yourself on my father, and I, his son, thank you for not using greater severity.”

beats.title: Game Over, Fernand
beats.modern: Fernand storms my house demanding the duel his son cancelled. he doesn't even know why Albert apologized. so I excuse myself, change costumes, and walk back in dressed as a sailor from 1815. one look. one name out of his mouth — 'Edmond Dantès!' — and he crawls home to watch his wife and son leave with nothing but each other. a single gunshot from his window as their coach pulls away. two.
beats.quote: “Edmond Dantès!”

beats.title: My Little Bro Loves WHO?
beats.modern: Maximilian breaks down in my study: he's in love, and she's dying, and her name is VALENTINE DE VILLEFORT. chat. my sworn little brother — son of the one man who fought for me — loves the daughter of the man who threw me in the hole. I heard myself ROAR it: 'that daughter of an accursed race!' then I look at his face. fine. new rule for the endgame: the house falls, the girl doesn't.
beats.quote: “you love Valentine,—that daughter of an accursed race!”

beats.title: Night Shift
beats.modern: the poisoner's next target is Valentine. so I rented the house next door and I have been living inside her WALL, chat, taste-testing every glass she reaches for. four days, zero sleep. tonight I caught her hand mid-reach: 'now you may drink.' yes, she woke up to a count in her bedroom explaining he's her night-shift security. she took it well. all things considered.
beats.quote: He told me your life was his, and I have promised him that you shall live.”

beats.title: Hold Your Fs
beats.modern: worst moment of the whole stream: old Noirtier's eyes go full alarm, Maximilian sprints up the staircase three at a time, and the words come down the stairwell like a blade: 'Valentine is dead.' chat. HOLD your Fs. hold them. I know something this house does not know. but Maximilian doesn't know it either — and I have to stand here and let his heart rip in half for the trap to close.
beats.quote: “Valentine is dead!”

beats.title: Bank Run
beats.modern: Danglars is finished, chat. margin-called from five directions, at least three of them mine. so the baron 'borrows' five million from the hospital charity fund, pockets my receipt, drafts a goodbye note to his wife, and checks his passport: 'good, it is available for two months longer.' he RUNS. run, baron. you cannot outrun a man with a fourteen-year head start on patience.

beats.title: The Benefactor Reveal
beats.modern: Maximilian wants to die and I am DONE with the mask. who am I? the only man alive with the right to say his father's son shall not die today. I sent the red purse. I sent the new Pharaon. I am the Edmond Dantès who held him on my knee when he was a baby. he drops like his strings were cut, chat, and the whole Morrel family is on their knees, and the iron-hearted man is crying on stream.
beats.quote: Morrel—because I am the Edmond Dantès who nursed you, a child, on my knees.”

beats.title: Live Courtroom Nuke
beats.modern: Benedetto's murder trial. asked to state his name, my planted 'prince' stands up and announces he was born at Auteuil, buried alive by his own father — and his father is the PROSECUTOR. Villefort. prosecuting him. RIGHT NOW. proofs? 'look at M. de Villefort, and then ask me for proofs.' and Villefort just confesses. in open court. everything is true, he says, and walks out of his own courtroom a finished man. three.
beats.quote: “Well, then, look at M. de Villefort, and then ask me for proofs.”

beats.title: I Went Too Far
beats.modern: Villefort drags me up his stairs by the wrist. 'there, Edmond Dantès — are you well avenged?' his wife poisoned herself. and she took their nine-year-old boy with her. I tried everything to bring the child back, chat. everything. nothing. Villefort's mind snapped in the garden, digging for a son who isn't there. no joke on this one. tonight I looked at a dead child and doubted the entire run. God grant I have not done too much already.
beats.quote: “There, Edmond Dantès!” he said, pointing to the bodies of his wife and child, “see, are you well avenged?”

beats.title: Menu Prices May Vary
beats.modern: Danglars' final dungeon: Vampa's bandits scooped him up outside Rome, five stolen millions and all. room and board? completely free. FOOD, however, is sold separately. one roast chicken: one hundred thousand francs. 'we never joke,' says Peppino, solemn as a Quaker. the man who let my father starve is going to buy back every single meal at collector prices. pettiest system I have ever designed, chat. zero regrets.
beats.quote: “What! A hundred thousand francs for a fowl!”

beats.title: The Final W Is Forgiveness
beats.modern: day five. Danglars is on his knees begging, and something in me moves. 'do you repent?' 'yes! I repent!' I drop the cloak and tell him everything he sold, name by name — and then I forgive him, chat, because I hope to be forgiven. the five million goes back to the hospitals. he stumbles out free at dawn and kneels at a stream to drink, and his hair has turned completely white. scoreboard: two dead, one mad, one white. and I don't feel like a god anymore.
beats.quote: fortune—I am he whose father you condemned to die of hunger—I am he whom you also condemned to starvation, and who yet forgives you, because he hopes to be forgiven—I am Edmond Dantès!”

beats.title: Wait And Hope
beats.modern: final episode, island epilogue. Maximilian took what he believed was his exit... and wakes up to Valentine. ALIVE. smiling at him. I TOLD you to hold your Fs, chat. the death was staged down to the pill. I leave the kids the fortune and one letter, and sail into the sunrise with Haydée — who loves me, and I think I'm allowed to be happy? me? last message from your streamer: all human wisdom fits in two words. wait and hope. gg, chat. stream's over.
beats.quote: until the day when God shall deign to reveal the future to man, all human wisdom is summed up in these two words,—‘Wait and hope.’—Your

beats.title: The Window Seat
beats.modern: chat I have found the one spot in this house nobody can reach me. behind the curtain, feet up, bird book open, rain going sideways outside. meanwhile my aunt is doing family time with her three actual children and I have been officially excluded from privileges intended for happy little children. cool. me and the arctic seabirds are having a great night.

beats.title: Book To The Head
beats.modern: my cousin John informs me the books are HIS, the house is HIS, and I should be out begging in the street. then he throws the book at my head. I'm bleeding. so I called him a Roman emperor to his face and went for him. guess which one of us is getting locked in a room. not him.

beats.title: Locked In The Red Room
beats.modern: they put me in the room the dead uncle actually died in. red curtains, white bed, mirror doing things mirrors should not do. then a light slides across the wall and my brain goes: that's him, he's coming. I screamed. my aunt's response was another hour in there with the door locked. chat I passed out on the floor.

beats.title: The Hell Interview
beats.modern: tall man in black shows up and immediately asks a ten year old where the wicked go after death. I said hell. he asked how I plan to avoid it. I said stay healthy and don't die. chat he did NOT like that answer. wrong lobby, my guy.
beats.quote: Do you know where the wicked go after death?”

beats.title: My Reference Check
beats.modern: my aunt is doing my reference check IN FRONT OF ME. tells the man my worst fault is lying. I have never lied to that woman once. he nods along and says liars end up in the fire lake, and he'll have the teachers watch me. so my whole reputation is preloaded before I've even walked in the door.

beats.title: The Clapback
beats.modern: ten years of swallowing it and today it just came out. told her I don't love her, I dislike her worst of anybody alive, and I'll tell every single person who asks exactly what she did to me. she went white. she offered me WATER. chat I won. that's the first fight I have ever won in my life.
beats.quote: “How dare I, Mrs. Reed? How dare I? Because it is the truth.

beats.title: Lowood Institution
beats.modern: new server. stone building in a fog pit, girls coughing in the verandah, and a bible verse over the door about letting your light shine. I am already starving. there's a girl on a bench absolutely locked into a book, so I do the bravest thing I have ever done and ask what it's about. her name is Helen. remember that name.

beats.title: Helen Takes The Beating
beats.modern: teacher screamed at Helen for dirty fingernails. the water was FROZEN. that's why. then she makes Helen go fetch the bundle of sticks she's about to be hit with, and hits her a dozen times, and Helen doesn't move a muscle. my hands were shaking and I wasn't even the one getting hit. she cried after. once. on the way back.

beats.title: Helen's Cope Philosophy
beats.modern: asked Helen how she takes it. she says it's weak and silly to say you can't bear what you have to bear. chat she is thirteen years old. I said the teacher is cross and cruel and she went silent rather than agree with me. I do not have this build installed. I would be griefing that classroom daily.
beats.quote: it is weak and silly to say you cannot bear what it is your fate to be required to bear.”

beats.title: The Hair Inspection
beats.modern: the man who owns the school walks in, spots a girl with naturally curly hair, and orders it shaved off. his actual reasoning: we are not to conform to nature. makes the whole front row turn around so he can rate their braids. thirty seconds later his wife and daughters walk in wearing velvet, fur, ostrich plumes and FRENCH CURLS.
beats.quote: “All those top-knots must be cut off.”

beats.title: Public Enemy Number One
beats.modern: I dropped my slate. so he stands me on a high stool in front of the entire school and announces I'm a liar, a castaway, and everyone should shun me. half an hour up there, nobody allowed to speak to me all day. then Helen walked past and smiled at me. that's it. that's all she did. I stopped shaking.
beats.quote: this girl, who might be one of God’s own lambs, is a little castaway:

beats.title: Fever Season
beats.modern: typhus came through like a patch nobody asked for. forty-five girls out of eighty down at once. rules gone, nobody watching us, and we are eating BETTER now because there are fewer mouths. the garden is exploding with flowers this spring and we are picking them to put in coffins.

beats.title: Good-night, Helen
beats.modern: climbed into her bed at midnight. her forehead is cold. she tells me not to grieve, she's going home, she has faith, she'll see me again there. then she asks if I'm warm. I said yes. we said good-night. chat I woke up being carried back to the dorm and she was already gone. her stone says Resurgam. I will rise again.
beats.quote: “I am very happy, Jane; and when you hear that I am dead, you must be sure and not grieve:

beats.title: A New Servitude
beats.modern: eight years in this building and I burned through my entire patience in one afternoon standing at a window. asked for liberty. nothing. asked for change. nothing. so I lowered the ask until it was small enough to actually get: a new job somewhere else. then I put an ad in the paper. that is the whole plan, chat.
beats.quote: “Then,” I cried, half desperate, “grant me at least a new servitude!”

beats.title: The Gytrash On The Ice
beats.modern: walking to town at dusk and I hear hooves. a huge dog comes out of the hedge first and my brain instantly goes: fairy tale monster, we're done. then a man on a horse. then both of them go down on the ice. I ask if he's hurt and he tells me to stand aside. rude. stayed anyway till he could stand. he asks who I am. I'm the governess. HIS governess, as it turns out.

beats.title: Do You Think Me Handsome
beats.modern: my employer sits me down by the fire, catches me staring at his face, and asks point blank whether I think he's handsome. chat I said no. out loud. before my brain could get to my mouth. he has not shut up about it since and I don't think he ever will.
beats.quote: “You examine me, Miss Eyre,” said he: “do you think me handsome?”

beats.title: The Balcony Story
beats.modern: lore drop on the little French girl I teach. he was funding an opera dancer. apartment, carriage, diamonds, the whole loadout. one night he's sitting on her balcony and watches her come in with another man, and the two of them roast his face for entertainment. he ended it on the spot, shot the guy in the arm at dawn, and kept the kid anyway.

beats.title: Fire In The Master Bedroom
beats.modern: heard a laugh outside my door at 2am. then smoke. his curtains are ON FIRE and he is sleeping straight through it. I emptied every jug in two rooms onto the man. he wakes up drenched asking if I plotted to drown him. then he goes up to the third floor alone, comes back grey, and tells me not to say one word to anybody.
beats.quote: “In the name of all the elves in Christendom, is that Jane Eyre?”

beats.title: Slander Hour
beats.modern: sat in the corner of the drawing room while the rich guests ran a full segment on how governesses are a nuisance. said it knowing I was in the room. added they hope it does me good. then the beautiful one bragged about tormenting hers until the poor woman broke. and this is the woman everyone says he's marrying.
beats.quote: one word to say of the whole tribe; they are a nuisance.

beats.title: The Fortune Teller Was Him
beats.modern: a fortune teller turned up at the house and spent twenty minutes prying personal information out of me. then she pulled the costume off. IT WAS HIM. my employer put on a disguise and interrogated me in my own house for fun. I told him it wasn't right. he asked to be forgiven. I said I'd think about it.

beats.title: Something In The Attic
beats.modern: guest is bleeding out upstairs at 3am. shoulder cut AND bitten. surgeon finds teeth marks in two separate places. the man keeps repeating that she drank his blood and said she'd drain his heart. my employer tells him to shut up and never say it again. then leaves me alone with him for two hours, sponge in hand, locked door behind me.
beats.quote: “She sucked the blood: she said she’d drain my heart,” said Mason.

beats.title: The Deathbed Confession
beats.modern: aunt is dying and she finally coughs it up: my uncle in Madeira wrote asking to adopt me and make me rich, and she wrote back that I died of fever at school. she sat on that for years. called it her revenge. I told her she has my full and free forgiveness. she wouldn't take a kiss. died at midnight still hating me.
beats.quote: I wrote to him; I said I was sorry for his disappointment, but Jane Eyre was dead:

beats.title: Equal At God's Feet
beats.modern: he thinks I'll just stand here and watch him marry her. I'm not an automaton. I'm not a machine with no feelings. poor, plain, small, nobody, all of it true. I still have exactly as much soul as him and I said it to his face while shaking.
beats.quote: Do you think, because I am poor, obscure, plain, and little, I am soulless and heartless? You think wrong!—I

beats.title: I Am No Bird
beats.modern: he calls me a wild bird tearing its own feathers off trying to get out. I told him I'm not a bird and there's no net on me. then he says the bride he actually means is ME. chat. CHAT. he proposed and I STILL made him turn his face into the moonlight so I could read it for lies.
beats.quote: “I am no bird; and no net ensnares me; I am a free human being with an independent will,

beats.title: The Tree Got Struck
beats.modern: best night of my life and the sky immediately lost it. wind ripping down the laurel walk, thunder right on top of us, soaked before we made the door. next morning Adèle runs in to tell me the giant chestnut we were sitting under got hit by lightning and split clean in half. no notes. flawless omen. anyway.

beats.title: The Thing That Tore The Veil
beats.modern: chat something came into my room the night before the wedding. not a servant. tall, black hair down her back, something white and straight. she took MY VEIL, put it on her own head, looked in the mirror, then ripped it in two and stamped on it. held her candle over my face until I blacked out. he says I dreamed it. the veil is still on the floor in two halves.
beats.quote: “Of the foul German spectre—the Vampyre.”

beats.title: Objection At The Altar
beats.modern: we are AT the altar. a lawyer stands up and says there is a previous marriage. the wife is alive. she is living in the house. I didn't faint, I didn't cry, I just looked at him and he didn't deny a single syllable of it. wedding cancelled. clerk sent home. carriage back to the coach house.
beats.quote: Mr. Rochester has a wife now living.”

beats.title: Meet The Wife
beats.modern: he marched the entire wedding party up to the third floor to LOOK at her. fifteen years married. windowless room, a keeper stirring a pot, and her running back and forth in the dark. she came at him and he wrestled her down while telling the room to compare the two of us. he says he was cheated into it. I have never been colder in my life.
beats.quote: she is my wife, whom I married fifteen years ago,—Bertha Mason by name;

beats.title: I Care For Myself
beats.modern: he wants me abroad with him as his wife except not his wife. every part of me is screaming yes. he keeps asking who in the world would even be hurt by it. me. I would. nobody is coming to look after me, so that job is mine, and I am not quitting it tonight of all nights.
beats.quote: reply—“I care for myself. The more solitary, the more friendless, the more unsustained I am, the more I will respect myself.

beats.title: Out Before Sunrise
beats.modern: left before dawn. twenty shillings, a bundle, shoes in my hand. stopped outside his door because I could hear him pacing in there, awake all night, waiting for morning so he could send for me. one sentence through that door and I could have stayed forever. I put my hand on the lock. then I took it off and kept walking.

beats.title: Circling Houses
beats.modern: day three. no money, no food, sleeping in the heather. tried to trade my handkerchief for a bread roll and got looked at like a thief. walked to the parsonage for help and the clergyman was away. chat I have circled houses like a starving dog all afternoon and I still cannot make my mouth ask.

beats.title: The Doorstep
beats.modern: knocked at the last lit window on the moor. the servant called me a vagrant, offered me a penny, warned me about housebreakers and bolted the door. so I sat down in the rain and said out loud, fine, I can die here, I still believe in God. and a voice right beside me in the dark said: not tonight. rise, and come in.
beats.quote: “I can but die,” I said, “and I believe in God. Let me try to wait His will in silence.”

beats.title: Twenty Thousand
beats.modern: my uncle in Madeira died and left me everything. I had mentally budgeted for maybe four thousand. it is TWENTY. and the man delivering this news says it like he's reading a grocery list, then calls it a trifle. I asked three separate times if he'd misread the figures. he says it's written out in words, not numbers.

beats.title: They're My Cousins
beats.modern: the man who scraped me off a doorstep is named St. John EYRE Rivers. same name. his mother was my father's sister. the three people who took in a starving stranger off the moor are my actual blood cousins. found through my own name written on a scrap of paper. chat I have a FAMILY. I have never had one of those.

beats.title: Splitting It Four Ways
beats.modern: twenty thousand on my own would crush me. five each between the four of us and I get a house and three relatives out of the deal. they fought me on it for weeks. I put it to arbitration and WON. I have never had a brother or a sister. apparently they cost fifteen thousand pounds and it is worth every penny.

beats.title: Come Die In India With Me
beats.modern: he does not love me. he said it out loud, calm as anything: I'm built for labour, not for love. so come to India, marry him, work in that climate until it kills me, for God. chat he has been studying me for ten months like a spreadsheet before making this offer. I said I'd come as his sister. not allowed, apparently.
beats.quote: “God and nature intended you for a missionary’s wife. It is not personal, but mental endowments they have given you: you are formed for labour, not for love.

beats.title: The Voice
beats.modern: I was one word away from saying yes to him. hand on my head, whole house asleep, and I asked heaven to show me the path. then I heard my name. three times. not in the room, not in the house, not in the air. it was HIS voice and he sounded like he was in pain. ran outside shouting where are you and the hills just handed it back to me.
beats.quote: “Jane! Jane! Jane!”—nothing more.

beats.title: Thornfield Is Gone
beats.modern: got to the inn and asked about the house. burnt to the ground at harvest time. started at dead of night, the whole building was one sheet of flame before the engines got out from town. the man telling me this stood there and watched it happen. that's why none of my letters were ever answered.

beats.title: The Roof
beats.modern: she set my old bed on fire first. he got every servant out of the building, then went back up for HER. by then she was on the roof, black hair streaming against the flames, shouting loud enough to hear a mile off. he called her name and went toward her. she jumped. the innkeeper watched the whole thing happen.

beats.title: He Is Stone-Blind
beats.modern: he refused to leave until everyone else was out. then the staircase came down on him. one eye knocked out, one hand crushed and amputated on the spot, then the other eye failed. stone-blind, thirty miles away in a house in the woods with two old servants and a dog. the innkeeper says plenty of people think he'd be better off dead. I'm ordering the chaise.

beats.title: Her Very Fingers
beats.modern: carried the water tray in myself. the DOG knew me before he did. he takes the glass, stops, listens, says this is you, Mary, isn't it. I said Mary's in the kitchen. then he caught my hand and he knew, and all he could get out was my name. twice. that's all he could say.
beats.quote: “Jane Eyre!—Jane Eyre,” was all he said.

beats.title: Reader, I Married Him
beats.modern: married him. me, him, the parson and the clerk. nobody else in the building. walked into the kitchen afterward and told the cook, who said have you, Miss? well, for sure, and went straight back to basting the chicken. John grinned at me ear to ear. that's the whole ceremony, chat. that's the wedding.
beats.quote: Reader, I married him.

beats.title: Ten Years In
beats.modern: ten years married. I was his eyes and he was everything else. then two years in he asks whether I'm wearing a blue dress, and I WAS, the sight was coming back in one eye. enough to see our son's face and clock that the boy got his eyes, the old ones, from before all this. chat I hold myself supremely blest. stream's done. go read it properly.

beats.title: The Horse Fell On Me
beats.modern: stream starts here, chat. narrator gets thrown by a horse, cracks his head on the pavement, wakes up in a private asylum being treated for insanity. doctor eventually signs him off as cured. he pays the bill smiling and tells the man he'll get even for the mistake. the doctor LAUGHS. clip that. we are absolutely coming back to it.

beats.title: Do Not Read Act Two
beats.modern: there is a play going around that eats people. act one is fine. boring, even. he finishes it, feels something go wrong upstairs, and throws the book in the fire. it falls open on the hearth. he catches ONE line of act two and he's on his knees dragging it out of the coals. reads it twice. weeps. laughs. chat, act one is banal on purpose. that's the trap.

beats.title: The Government Death Booth
beats.modern: April 1920. the state opens its first Lethal Chamber on Washington Square. white marble, six columns, bronze door, a statue of the Fates out front. the governor cuts the ribbon on a suicide booth like it's a new library wing, and the crowd claps politely and goes home. patch notes: dying is now a public service.
beats.quote: “There a painless death awaits him who can no longer bear the sorrows of this life.

beats.title: Repairer Of Reputations
beats.modern: upstairs lives Mr. Wilde. no ears (wax ones, painted shell pink, held on by wire), no fingers on the left hand, and he keeps a cat purely so it can open his face. business model: he owns people. bookkeepers, ministers, the editor-in-chief of a major daily. five hundred on payroll. asked how he disciplines them, he says he invites them up for a little chat. chat, do NOT go up for the little chat.

beats.title: The Writ Of Execution
beats.modern: Wilde calls a man out of the shadows. the guy hits the floor begging — he was in a madhouse, he'd FORGOTTEN the King, please not again — and Wilde jumps on his throat until he stops. then reads his file aloud like a review. embezzler. forger. then hands him a brand new knife, a floor plan of the neighbours' rooms, and a signed order. and the man just shuffles off to do it.
beats.quote: I signed my first writ of execution with my name Hildred-Rex.

beats.title: Midnight In The Park
beats.modern: park bench, midnight, and he tells his cousin very calmly that he visited the doctor last night and the interview was final. then reads out the other three names that still need interviewing. one of them is the cousin. one of them is the cousin's fiancée. then he draws the knife and demands the crown. Louis just stands there white, watching his family turn into a coronation.

beats.title: King For Ten Minutes
beats.modern: he gets the crown on. white silk robe, Yellow Sign, dawn about to break, two hemispheres about to shake. then a groan in the dark hall. the cat has torn Wilde's throat out. his emperor, his empire, his whole life is lying on a carpet in a rented room. police take him biting and screaming. and then, at the bottom of the page, one line of editor's note.

beats.title: The Lily Turns To Stone
beats.modern: new story, same cursed book somewhere in the room. sculptor named Boris has a basin of clear liquid. drops in an Easter lily. foam, then colours rolling over the surface, then a shaft of pure sunlight comes UP from the bottom. that beam is the signal, that's when you're allowed to reach in. he pulls out the lily and it's flawless marble, blue-veined, still faintly warm in the heart. he thinks the sunbeam is the thing's life leaving.

beats.title: The Fever Says The Name
beats.modern: Geneviève is burning up and babbling. Boris holds her down gently and calls his best friend in to help. she opens her eyes, looks straight into her husband's face, and says the other man's name. that's it. that's the whole friendship, gone in one syllable. Alec can't move, can't speak, face on fire. then a hand lands on his shoulder and Boris turns to him with no blood left in his face at all.

beats.title: What Jack Found
beats.modern: Jack tells it in as few words as he can. Boris kept working on the Fates, and the third figure — the one staring out over the world — had grown his own face. near midnight a door opened and someone ran. they were too late. she was at the bottom of the marble pool with her hands crossed on her breast. then Boris shot himself through the heart.

beats.title: The Rabbit Came Back
beats.modern: the maid keeps complaining someone is pranking her. the marble rabbit is gone and a live one is loose in the house. the marble fish are gone and two live ones are flopping on the dining room floor. he goes to check the marble lily and lifts a real flower off the table, fresh, fragrant. then he understands, and he RUNS. the doors fly open and Geneviève lifts her flushed face off the marble and opens her eyes.

beats.title: He Walked Past Twice
beats.modern: the organist leaves the loft. white face, black coat, out the little side door, gone. under sixty seconds later the SAME man comes out from behind the pipes and walks the SAME way. there was no time to loop back. and when he's level with me he turns and sends a look of hate across the whole church, right into my eyes. a stranger. I have never been hated like that in my life.

beats.title: Hunted Across Paris
beats.modern: he's ahead of me on the sunny street. then he's down a chestnut alley by the river. then he's sitting on a bench at the Rond-point with mothers and children all around him, an ordinary Sunday lounger, and his face is still doing that. I get all the way to the Arc and he walks in from the other direction and brushes past me. no haste. no fatigue. nothing human in him at all.

beats.title: I Slept Through The Sermon
beats.modern: I back down the courtyard facing him, aiming for the far gate. I hit the archway and it isn't an archway, it's a vault — the great doors are shut, the dark is on his side. ...and then chairs scrape and the congregation stands and I am still in the pew. I never left. I slept through the sermon. except now I know his face, and I know where my weakness sent him, and I know my body sat here while he hunted my soul down that alley.

beats.title: The Church Becomes Carcosa
beats.modern: I crawl for the door and the organ detonates over my head. light floods everything, the altar goes, the arches go, the people go. black stars hanging in the sky. wet wind off the lake of Hali on my face. the towers of Carcosa rising behind the moon. and as I fall, the King in Yellow leans in and whispers it straight into my soul.
beats.quote: “It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God!”

beats.title: My Canvas Went Rotten
beats.modern: new story. painter, a model called Tessie, and a night-watchman standing in the churchyard below. I look at his face once and my brain just says: coffin worm. I go back to the easel and the flesh tones have gone sallow. I scrape it. it spreads. turpentine. it spreads. the whole figure is drinking the rot up like a sponge. three weeks of work, gangrenous, because I looked out of a window.

beats.title: Tessie Dreams A Hearse
beats.modern: Tessie's had the same dream three times. she wakes up standing at her open window — once soaked through with rain. a hearse comes down the empty street and the driver turns and looks up at her. so where am I in this, I ask, laughing. "you were in the coffin. but you were not dead." then she glances out my window at the watchman, screams, and says that's him. that's the driver. his face looked like it had been dead a long time.

beats.title: The Finger Came Off
beats.modern: the bellboy — ex-army, bugler, actually got shot at a real battle — tells me he swung on the watchman once. says the head was cold and mushy. then the thing grabbed his wrists, and when he twisted the soft fist one of the fingers came off in his hand. then he ran. he can't tell me why he ran. after he leaves I go to the window and check. middle finger, right hand. missing.

beats.title: Have You Found It
beats.modern: walking home at dawn I pass the watchman and he mutters something at me. I'm furious, I go up, I lie there for an hour and my brain finally decodes it, slow, like remembering something I was never told. same six words, three times, like a notification I cannot clear.
beats.quote: “Have you found the Yellow Sign?”

beats.title: The Gift On My Lapel
beats.modern: I give Tessie a gold chain with a cross. she gives me a little box: black onyx clasp, a gold symbol inlaid that is not Arabic, not Chinese, not any script any human ever wrote. she found it in the street, advertised it, nobody ever claimed it. and chat — she found it the same day she had the first hearse dream. I pinned it on. I promised her I'd wear it always.

beats.title: She Opened The Book
beats.modern: there's a book on my top shelf bound in snakeskin that I did not buy and did not put there. I say don't touch it. so of course she takes it and runs, laughing, and my wrists are sprained so I can't stop her. half an hour later I find her white and silent by a window, book open at the second part. too late. and then I sit down on the rug beside her and read the whole damn thing myself, front to back.

beats.title: Dead For Months
beats.modern: wheels in the fog. the gate. the bolts rot at his touch. he comes into the room and I cannot see him, I can only feel the cold soft grip, and he tears the Yellow Sign off my coat and hits me in the face. Tessie makes one small sound and she's gone. neighbours break in and find one living and two dead, and the doctor points at the heap on the floor and says the quiet part.
beats.quote: “I have no theory, no explanation. That man must have been dead for months!”

beats.title: The Falcon Wore A Bell
beats.modern: guy's lost on the Breton moors, sun going down, no house in any direction. a falcon drops a hare right in front of him — and the bird is leashed and belled. someone OWNS it. a girl walks up, hoods it, collects the hare, barely nods at him. he asks the way back to town. she looks at him with something close to pity and says coming in takes hours, and leaving can take centuries.
beats.quote: “The moor is wild and desolate. It is easy to enter, but sometimes they who enter never leave it.

beats.title: First Catch The Falcon
beats.modern: she's teaching him falconry in a French that died four hundred years ago and she doesn't know it's dead. holds up one finger, dead serious: first one must catch the falcon. "I am caught," he says. she laughs and warns him his training will be difficult, since he is noble. already tamed, he says. jessed and belled. chat this is the smoothest anybody has ever been on this stream.
beats.quote: “First one must catch the falcon.”

beats.title: The Date On The Stone
beats.modern: a viper comes across the warm rock. she grabs his arm — not scared for herself, scared for HIM — so he kisses her, and while he's kissing her it bites his ankle twice. he throws her clear, crushes its head, and goes down. wakes up: no hawks, no garden, no castle. just ruins with trees growing through them. he falls to his knees at a broken shrine and reads her name, and that she died young for love of Philip, a stranger, in 1573. her glove on the icy slab is still warm.

beats.title: Paler Than The Clown
beats.modern: short one from the prose-poem stretch. the Clown looks in the mirror and says if fair means beautiful, who can compete with me in my white mask. so I turn and ask Death, who is standing right there. Death says: me. I'm paler. and the Clown just sighs "you are very beautiful" and turns away from the glass. that's it. that's the whole clip.
beats.quote: “Who can compare with me?” said Death, “for I am paler still.”

beats.title: The Cat With The Garter
beats.modern: broke painter, five flights up, feeds a starving cat the last of his milk. then he clocks what's around her neck: a rose silk garter, embroidered, silver clasp with the mint mark. and he spends the entire evening reading it aloud to the cat like a case file. five eyelets. the fifth one worn through. therefore, he concludes, a well-rounded form. sir. that is a stranger's leg wear and you are running forensics on it.

beats.title: Behind The Bed Curtain
beats.modern: he carries the cat back to the north wing. dark room, clothes flung everywhere, one rose garter on the floor matching the one on the cat. he pulls the bed curtain back and the candle shakes in his hand: eyes open, smiling, gold hair. it's her. it's the Sylvia from Elven. he says her name twice into the silence. then he understands, and he kisses her anyway, and the cat purrs on his knee till the sky goes grey.
beats.quote: “Sylvia, it is I.”

beats.title: Seven Francs A Rat
beats.modern: siege of Paris arc. Trent steps outside and there's a kid on the corner with a rope holding his rags together and a warm dead rat hanging off it. going rate is two francs a quarter at the market. kid tries to charge him seven and lies about why. Trent calls the scam, throws him a franc anyway, and walks off while the kid brains another one at the mouth of the sewer. that's dinner. that's the economy now.

beats.title: Here Fell The First Shell
beats.modern: the Quarter is burning, the street is a heap of smoking bricks, and there's a child calmly writing on a wall with a bit of cinder. Trent climbs over two dead concierges and up to a door hanging off its hinges. walls gaped, floor torn. he sinks down by the bed — and two arms come round his neck in the dark. and from the pillow beside them a baby cries. "they brought it; it is mine." ours, he says.
beats.quote: “HERE FELL THE FIRST SHELL.”

beats.title: Do Not Ask About Me
beats.modern: American kid, three days in Paris, meets a girl in the Luxembourg and very politely asks to be presented to her family. she goes pale and tells him her parents are dead. then gives him her name — Valentine Tissot — and asks one favour: never speak about me to anyone. I want to stay a mystery, it's a caprice. chat it is not a caprice.

beats.title: Faster Faster
beats.modern: train out of the city, both of them hanging out the window, and she's shouting faster, faster, out of the land, out of the WORLD. he pulls her in and kisses her and she cries no, not that, I promised, I'm not worthy — and it goes straight through him without landing, because he genuinely cannot hear what she's confessing. so she stops trying. she looks out at the sunlight on the fields and says it.
beats.quote: “Is this the world? Then I have never known it.”

beats.title: Nobody Knows Her Name
beats.modern: every art student in the Quarter bows to her. she bows back. that is the entire relationship, for all of them, forever. nobody has her name so they named her after the sign outside her building: RUE BARRÉE, road closed. two of the lads have already thrown themselves at her and been iced with the same polite smile. Clifford's official position: he fears to tread where they rush in.

beats.title: Fifty Francs For A Rose
beats.modern: she wants the rose bush. it's fifty francs. she buys two francs of pansies instead, and when she turns around there's a tear in her eye and Selby is standing right there having watched all of it. so he panics, studies the sky for five straight minutes, then buys out the ENTIRE flower market at asking price. then quietly tells the gardener to send the rose bush along with her pansies and never say who it came from.

beats.title: The Proposal
beats.modern: Clifford actually asks her to marry him. she takes a long time to answer. says no man has ever offered her that before. then she looks out over Paris in the sunshine and tells him what her life is: alone, nothing, no friend she can keep in honour, and the only love on offer ending on the boulevard once the passion dies. then she thanks him, pulls a petal off the rose at her breast, presses it into her book, and says she can't.

beats.title: The Barrier Said Her Name
beats.modern: Selby, absolutely gone, loses his cane, gets outflanked by his own right leg, and walks face-first into a barrier across a torn-up street. black letters on it: RUE BARRÉE. so obviously he climbs the building. window sills, pipes, cornices, into her balcony. she opens the window. and the room is tiny and white and poor and so clean it hurts, and he catches his own face in her mirror and sobers up like a slap. no words, either of them. she presses a rose and lays it beside him. then she carries the lamp down and unbolts the door for him.

beats.title: Seventeen Steps
beats.modern: man hasn't seen me in months and opens with "you've put on seven and a half pounds." then he asks how many stairs lead up to this room. chat I have climbed those stairs hundreds of times. I do not know. he does. seventeen. because he counts everything, permanently, including me.
beats.quote: “You see, but you do not observe.

beats.title: The Guy In The Mask
beats.modern: client walks in six foot six wearing an actual black mask, calls himself Count Von Kramm. Holmes just shuts his eyes and looks bored. so the man rips the mask off and announces he is the King of Bohemia. Holmes, eyes still closed: yeah, I had your full name before you opened your mouth. the mask was decoration the entire time.
beats.quote: “I am the King. Why should I attempt to conceal it?”

beats.title: Best Man Speedrun
beats.modern: Holmes tails her to a church and gets grabbed at the door by the groom, because the license is invalid without a witness in the next three minutes. so my friend, undercover, in disguise, accidentally becomes best man at the wedding of the woman he is currently investigating. the bride tipped him a sovereign. he is putting it on his watch chain.
beats.quote: It was the most preposterous position in which I ever found myself in my life,

beats.title: Fire In The Building
beats.modern: my one job: stand at the window, wait for the hand signal, throw in the smoke rocket, shout fire. so I shout fire. and then the ENTIRE STREET shouts fire, because every loafer, guardsman and flower girl out there is on his payroll. she runs straight to a sliding panel above the bell pull. now we know where the photograph lives.

beats.title: She Read The Whole Play
beats.modern: we turn up at eight in the morning. maid on the steps, smiling: madam left on the 5:15, never returning. she had clocked the fake clergyman, put on men's clothes, followed us home, said good night to Holmes ON THE STREET, and left him a letter about how well he played it. he is just standing there holding it.
beats.quote: HOLMES,—You really did it very well. You took me in completely.

beats.title: The Only Payment He Wanted
beats.modern: the king offers him an emerald snake ring off his own finger. Holmes says he would value something else more highly. her photograph. then he bows, walks straight past the royal handshake without looking at it, and leaves. he beat kings all year. she beat him once and he took the souvenir home.

beats.title: Every Ginger In London
beats.modern: the ad promises four pounds a week to any red headed man. Fleet Street is wall to wall gingers. every shade: straw, lemon, brick, Irish setter, clay. our client gets shoved to the front, and the interviewer takes his hair in both hands and YANKS to prove it isn't a wig. he passes the audition by screaming.
beats.quote: Fleet Street was choked with red-headed folk,

beats.title: The League Is Dissolved
beats.modern: the job was copying out the encyclopaedia by hand. letter A. ten to two. never leave the room, not once, or you forfeit everything. eight weeks of Abbots, Archery, Armour, Attica, four gold coins every Saturday. then one morning the door is locked and there is a little card nailed to it. that is the entire notice. no patch notes.
beats.quote: “THE RED-HEADED LEAGUE IS DISSOLVED.

beats.title: The Knees Of His Trousers
beats.modern: Holmes walks to the pawn shop, whacks the pavement with his stick three times, knocks, asks the assistant how to get to the Strand, thanks him and walks off. I ask what he needed to see. not the man's face. his TROUSER KNEES. worn through, wrinkled, filthy. from months of digging.
beats.quote: “The knees of his trousers.”

beats.title: The Hand Out Of The Floor
beats.modern: we are crouched in a bank vault in total darkness with my revolver cocked on a crate. one of the flagstones lifts and a white hand comes THROUGH THE FLOOR, fingers feeling around. Holmes has him by the collar before he is fully out. and the man, in handcuffs, politely requests that we address him as sir, because his grandfather was a royal duke.
beats.quote: “You may not be aware that I have royal blood in my veins.

beats.title: In One Door Of The Cab
beats.modern: she is telling us about her wedding morning. the groom puts her and her mother in one cab and takes a second one himself. they arrive first. his cab pulls up. they wait. nobody gets out. the driver swears he watched the man climb in with his own eyes. empty carriage. no groom. she has been sitting with that for a week.

beats.title: The Typewriter Snitched
beats.modern: every love letter from the missing fiancé was typed, even the signature. Holmes spotted the same chewed e and the same tailless r in all four, plus fourteen more tells. so he wrote to the stepfather and got a typed reply. same machine. then he steps over, turns the key in the door, and tells the man he has caught him.
beats.quote: “I let you know, then, that I have caught him!”

beats.title: He Was The Boyfriend
beats.modern: here it is. the fiancé WAS the stepfather. tinted glasses, glued on whiskers, voice dropped to a whisper, and the girl is short sighted. he invented a boyfriend and romanced his own stepdaughter to keep real suitors away, with her mother helping. all of it to keep her hundred a year in his house. absolute freak behaviour, chat.

beats.title: The Hunting Crop
beats.modern: Holmes tells him straight: legally, nobody can touch you. then he unlocks the door and mentions that there happens to be a hunting crop right here and he thinks he will treat himself. the man is down the stairs, out the hall door and sprinting up the road before Holmes gets a hand on it. fastest exit I have ever witnessed.
beats.quote: there never was a man who deserved punishment more.

beats.title: He Died Saying Rat
beats.modern: the son is at the inquest. what did your father say before he died? he says: something about a rat. that is it. that is the dying message. he assumed the old man was delirious. the coroner assumed the son was lying. the whole county assumed murder. chat, hold onto that word.

beats.title: The Word Was Ballarat
beats.modern: Holmes flattens a map of Victoria on the table and puts his hand over half of it. read that. I read: ARAT. he lifts his hand. BALLARAT. the dying man was not raving about vermin, he was naming the town his killer came out of. the son only caught the last two syllables. two syllables and the whole case flips.

beats.title: Twenty Years Rent Free
beats.modern: the old millionaire finally talks. thirty years back he was a highway robber in Australia, held up a gold convoy, put a pistol to the driver's head, and let him live. that driver spent twenty years memorising his face, found him in London, moved his whole family onto the man's best land and never paid a shilling. one act of mercy on infinite compound interest.

beats.title: But For The Grace
beats.modern: he waited behind a tree, listened to the man plan to marry his daughter off like livestock, and something in him snapped. he confesses, signs it, and Holmes puts the paper in his pocket instead of handing it to police, because the man has months to live and the innocent son can be cleared another way. then, after the old man shuffles out, Holmes says the quiet part.
beats.quote: ‘There, but for the grace of God, goes Sherlock Holmes.’”

beats.title: Five Pips In The Mail
beats.modern: envelope from India. no letter inside. five dried orange pips bounce out onto his uncle's breakfast plate. the old man goes the colour of putty and says three letters: K. K. K. the nephew asks what it means. one word back. Death. then he goes upstairs and burns every paper he owns.
beats.quote: ‘My God, my God, my sins have overtaken me!’

beats.title: Too Late For Openshaw
beats.modern: I open the paper at breakfast and his name is in it. our client. pulled out of the river near Waterloo. he sat in that chair last night asking for help, Holmes sent him home with instructions, and now he is a paragraph about unsafe landing stages. I have never seen Holmes look like that. he does not say sorry. he says it is personal now.
beats.quote: “That hurts my pride, Watson,”

beats.title: Their Own Trademark Back
beats.modern: he tears an orange apart at the table, counts five pips into an envelope, writes S. H. for J. O. on the inside of the flap and addresses it to the captain of their ship. same omen. same delivery method. their own death notice, posted ahead of them so it is sitting there waiting when they dock.
beats.quote: let us put their own devilish trade-mark upon them.

beats.title: The Sea Third Partied Him
beats.modern: the envelope never gets delivered. the gales that autumn were the worst in years and the ship simply never arrives anywhere. no port, no trial, no arrest, no gallows, nothing we get to watch. the Atlantic third partied the whole damn case and left us nothing to look at.

beats.title: The Old Man In The Den
beats.modern: I am in an opium den fetching somebody's husband and a wrecked old man by the fire plucks my coat and whispers to walk past him and then look back. I look back. the wrinkles are gone, the dead eyes are lit, it is HOLMES, and he is grinning at my face. then he sags straight back into a drooling nobody mid sentence.

beats.title: He Brought A Sponge
beats.modern: police have a hideous beggar in a cell for murdering a missing gentleman. Holmes asks them to open the door quietly, opens his bag, and produces a bath sponge. two hard scrubs while the man sleeps: the scar comes off, the twisted lip comes off, the red wig comes away. the murderer and the victim are the same man.
beats.quote: The man’s face peeled off under the sponge like the bark from a tree.

beats.title: The Beggar Was The Husband
beats.modern: he was a reporter on two pounds a week who tried begging for one article and worked out he could make that in a DAY with paint on his face. so he quit journalism. seven hundred a year, a house in the country, a wife, two kids, and every morning he changed into a monster in a room above an opium den. she had no idea what business he did in the City.
beats.quote: It was a long fight between my pride and the money, but the dollars won at last,

beats.title: Five Pillows
beats.modern: the inspector asks how on earth he reaches his results. Holmes tells him: by sitting on five pillows and getting through an ounce of shag. that is the method. no chase, no fight, one man cross legged on a pile of cushions in a cloud of smoke until sunrise. then he suggests we drive back for breakfast.
beats.quote: “by sitting upon five pillows and consuming an ounce of shag.

beats.title: The Hat Knew Too Much
beats.modern: somebody dropped a battered hat in the street on Christmas morning. from the hat alone: highly intelligent, was well off three years ago, drinking now, haircut this week, uses lime cream, no gas laid on in the house, and his wife has stopped loving him. I said my dear Holmes. he said nobody has brushed it in weeks. that is the tell.
beats.quote: This may account also for the obvious fact that his wife has ceased to love him.”

beats.title: Something In The Goose
beats.modern: the commissionaire bursts in holding out his palm. his wife was dressing the Christmas goose we picked up off the street and there in its crop is the Countess of Morcar's blue carbuncle. the stone that has been in every paper for a week. thousand pound reward, worth twenty times that. it was inside a bird.

beats.title: Wrong Bird
beats.modern: the plan was: pry the goose's beak open, push the gem down its throat, walk the bird to Kilburn and cut it out there. he takes the white one with the barred tail. gets to his mate, they open it up, nothing. sprints back to the yard. there were TWO barred tails and his sister could never tell them apart. the whole flock went to market that morning.

beats.title: Get Out
beats.modern: long silence. just the man sobbing and Holmes tapping the table with his fingertips. then he stands, opens the door, and says get out. no police, no charge, and the man is gone down the stairs in about four seconds flat. the innocent man walks free anyway, and Holmes reckons the fear was the whole sentence.
beats.quote: “No more words. Get out!”

beats.title: It Was The Speckled Band
beats.modern: a scream in the middle of a storm. her twin sister comes out of her room white faced, swaying like a drunk, hands out for help, and drops. she gets her arms round her and the last thing her sister ever says is that it was the band, the speckled band. then she stabs a finger at the stepfather's door and the convulsion takes the rest.
beats.quote: It was the band! The speckled band!’

beats.title: He Bent The Poker
beats.modern: the stepfather kicks our door in to threaten us. calls Holmes a busybody, a meddler, then picks the iron poker off the hearth and bends it into a curve with his bare hands to make the point, and throws it down. he leaves. Holmes picks it up and quietly straightens it back out. says nothing else about it.
beats.quote: “See that you keep yourself out of my grip,”

beats.title: Sitting In The Dark
beats.modern: we are sitting in the dead sister's bedroom in total blackness. no light, no talking, no moving. half an hour of straining at nothing. then a soft hiss, like steam out of a kettle. Holmes is off the bed lashing at the bell rope with his cane, yelling do you see it, do you see it, and I see NOTHING. then the scream starts up in the next room.

beats.title: The Band Was A Snake
beats.modern: we open his door. he is sitting upright in his chair, eyes locked on the ceiling, wearing a yellow speckled band round his head. and then the band MOVES. it was never a scarf. it was a swamp adder he posted down a dummy bell rope onto his stepdaughter's bed every night, and tonight Holmes hit it with a cane and it went home furious.
beats.quote: Violence does, in truth, recoil upon the violent, and the schemer falls into the pit which he digs for another.

beats.title: The Ceiling Came Down
beats.modern: the engineer hears the levers clank and works out that the room he is locked in IS the press. the ceiling starts coming down. iron floor, iron roof, one minute until he is a shapeless pulp. he is lying there choosing which way hurts less to die when he catches a thin line of yellow light between two boards. the walls are wood. he throws himself through.

beats.title: He Took My Thumb
beats.modern: he is out the window hanging by his fingertips from the sill, thirty feet up, and the man comes at him with a damn cleaver. one swing. he feels a dull pain, his grip goes, he drops into the garden and runs. then the dizziness hits. he looks at his hand and his thumb is simply gone. faints face down in the rose bushes.
beats.quote: “‘You are mad, Elise!’

beats.title: What Did I Gain
beats.modern: the client totals up his week: lost a thumb, lost a fifty guinea fee, and what exactly did he gain out of it. Holmes says experience. says he only has to put it into words and he will be excellent company for the rest of his life. sir. the man has nine fingers now.
beats.quote: I have lost my thumb and I have lost a fifty-guinea fee, and what have I gained?”

beats.title: She Left Before The Soup
beats.modern: married at noon. at the wedding breakfast the bride says she feels suddenly unwell and goes up to her room. maid says she grabbed a coat and a bonnet and went straight back down. a footman watched a lady walk out of the house and decided it could not possibly be her. it was. gone from her own wedding party inside ten minutes.

beats.title: Meet Mr And Mrs Moulton
beats.modern: Holmes has had cold woodcock, a pheasant and cobwebby wine laid out for five people and will not say why. bell rings. he walks in a couple and introduces them as Mr and Mrs Francis Hay Moulton. the lady, he adds, you have already met. our client goes rigid and stares at the carpet, because that is his wife from this morning.

beats.title: Her Dead Husband In Pew One
beats.modern: she tells it herself. she is at the altar rails and glances back, and the husband she buried in her own head, the miner she secretly married in a camp years ago and was told died, is sitting in the first pew looking at her. she nearly hits the floor. he puts a finger to his lips. she drops her bouquet over to him and he hands it back with a note folded inside.
beats.quote: I thought it was his ghost at first;

beats.title: He Would Not Stay
beats.modern: Holmes invites the jilted lord to stay and eat the supper he laid on for exactly this. the man says that is asking a little too much, sweeps a bow at the whole room, and stalks out. so the rest of us ate his pheasant and drank his wine, and Holmes toasted the Americans, and nobody mentioned him again all night.

beats.title: Fifty Grand On A Crown
beats.modern: a name he refuses to say out loud walks into the bank needing fifty thousand by tonight. collateral: the Beryl Coronet. thirty nine enormous beryls, national treasure, cannot be replaced, would cause a public scandal if it got so much as scratched. he sets it on the desk like a coat. and the banker takes it HOME. to his house. where people live.

beats.title: Caught Bending It
beats.modern: two in the morning he hears a noise, peeps round the dressing room door, and there is his son in shirt and trousers holding the coronet and wrenching at it with both hands. he screams thief. the boy drops it, goes white as death, and will not say one word. a gold corner with three stones in it is missing. he calls the police on his own son that night without asking a single question.

beats.title: You Owe Him An Apology
beats.modern: Holmes hands the missing gold corner across the table and then tells the banker there is one debt left, and it is not money. the boy went out barefoot into the snow, fought the real thief for the crown, snapped it getting it back, then took a theft charge in total silence rather than name the girl. she had already run off with the man.
beats.quote: who has carried himself in this matter as I should be proud to see my own son do,

beats.title: Cut Your Hair Or No Job
