beats.modern: governess interview. a hundred a year, four times the going rate. duties: mind one child, wear any dress they hand you, sit exactly where they tell you to sit, and cut your hair short before you arrive. she says no to the hair. he loses interest instantly and asks to see other candidates. chat, the hair WAS the job.

beats.title: Sit There And Laugh
beats.modern: so the actual job is: put on the electric blue dress, sit in the chair at the big front window with your back to the road, and laugh at his stories. an hour of it. then change back. two days later, again. she wants to know what is behind her, so she hides a shard of broken mirror in her handkerchief, and dabs her eyes mid laugh, and looks.

beats.title: My Own Hair In The Drawer
beats.modern: she tries her keys on the one locked drawer in her room and the very first one opens it. inside, one item. a coil of chestnut hair. she digs her own cut off hair out of the bottom of her trunk and lays them side by side. same tint, same thickness, identical. somebody else's head, in a locked drawer, in the house she is living in.
beats.quote: It was my coil of hair.

beats.title: The Dog Had Not Been Fed
beats.modern: the prisoner is gone through the skylight, the father comes back up the stairs, sees the three of us in his locked room, and runs off to let the dog loose. mastiff. not fed for two days. we get to the hall and hear the baying, then a scream, then a sound I am not going to describe. I go round the corner and shoot it off his throat, and its teeth are still locked in when it drops.

beats.title: The Client Nobody Will Name
beats.modern: chat I'm a lawyer. I have one job: get a rich foreign client to sign property papers. so far every single person in this town has crossed themselves at me and then stopped speaking. the innkeeper suddenly cannot understand the German he was fluent in ten minutes ago. his wife looked at him like I'd already died. five stars, no notes, definitely not walking into anything.

beats.title: For Your Mother's Sake
beats.modern: the landlady got on her KNEES to beg me not to travel tonight. apparently at midnight all the evil things in the world get full sway. I explained that I have a business appointment. she put a crucifix round my neck, said it was for my mother's sake, and walked out. chat I'm Church of England, we do not do this. I'm still wearing it.

beats.title: For The Dead Travel Fast
beats.modern: driver says my ride isn't coming, sir, better go on to the next town, better still go tomorrow. and then a black carriage comes out of the dark behind us with four black horses and a driver whose eyes catch red in the lamplight. one of the passengers whispers a line of German poetry and crosses himself. I looked it up. it means the dead travel fast. cool. cool cool cool.
beats.quote: (“For the dead travel fast.”)

beats.title: The Wolf Ring
beats.modern: driver keeps stopping and walking off into the dark for no reason. then the moon comes out and chat there is a RING of wolves around the carriage. silent. teeth out. silent is so much worse. I'm screaming and banging the side of the coach, and then I hear his voice, and he just sweeps his arms like he's shooing pigeons and they fall back. my driver has admin privileges on wolves. nobody is explaining anything to me.

beats.title: Enter Freely Of Your Own Will
beats.modern: old man, dressed head to foot in black, not one speck of colour on him, holding a lamp. and he will NOT come to meet me. he stands there like a statue until I step over the threshold by myself, and the SECOND I do he's all over me, grabbing my hand, carrying my bags, nay sir you are my guest. handshake cold as a dead man's. chat I think I just consented to something.
beats.quote: “Welcome to my house! Enter freely and of your own will!”

beats.title: Children Of The Night
beats.modern: itemising my host while he watches me eat, because he has dined already and does not sup. ears pointed at the tops. teeth sticking out over the lip. hair growing in the PALMS of his hands. breath that made me physically gag when he leaned in. then the wolves start up down in the valley and his eyes go bright and he tells me to listen. it's his favourite song.
beats.quote: “Listen to them--the children of the night. What music they make!”

beats.title: No Reflection
beats.modern: shaving. hand lands on my shoulder. good-morning. chat I did not see him walk in BECAUSE HE IS NOT IN THE MIRROR. the whole room is in there. everything except him. then I nick my chin and he goes for my throat with real murder in his face, and stops dead the instant his hand touches the crucifix. then he throws my mirror out the window. no I do not know how I am meant to shave now.

beats.title: The Castle Is A Prison
beats.modern: did a full survey of the property this morning, because that is my actual profession. doors, doors, doors, every one of them locked and bolted. the only way out of this building is the windows, and the windows open onto a thousand foot drop. I came here to close a real estate deal and I have become stock.
beats.quote: The castle is a veritable prison, and I am a prisoner!

beats.title: The Family History Rant
beats.modern: asked one polite question about the local area. two hours later he is STILL going, pacing, crushing furniture in his hands, listing every war his bloodline won since Attila. was it not this Dracula indeed. bro is reading me his own patch notes out loud. then he goes very quiet and says the warlike days are over and blood is too precious now. chat he did not say that the way a normal person says that.
beats.quote: Blood is too precious a thing in these days of dishonourable peace;

beats.title: The Wall Crawl
beats.modern: leaned out my window and saw my client come out of HIS window. face down. cloak spread out around him like wings. and then he went down the outside of the castle over a thousand foot drop, fingers and toes in the gaps between the stones, fast. like a lizard. chat. like a lizard.

beats.title: Three Women In The Moonlight
beats.modern: fell asleep in a room he told me not to sleep in. woke up not alone. three women, moonlight behind them, no shadows on the floor. laughing like glass being played. two dark, one fair, and the fair one kneels over me and licks her teeth. and chat, here's the part I'll never say out loud: I wanted it. I lay there with my eyes shut waiting to feel the bite. I am engaged. I'm so sorry, Mina.

beats.title: This Man Belongs To Me
beats.modern: then the Count arrives and I have never seen rage like it in a human face. grabs her by the throat and HURLS her across the room. and the words aren't get away from my guest. the words are this man belongs to me. so that's my status confirmed, chat. I'm not a prisoner. I'm inventory. then she laughs in his face and tells him he has never loved anyone. brutal ratio on the ancient warlord.
beats.quote: “How dare you touch him, any of you? How dare you cast eyes on him when I had forbidden it? Back, I tell you all! This man belongs to me!

beats.title: The Bag
beats.modern: one of them asks if they get nothing tonight, and points at the bag he dropped on the floor. the bag is moving. he nods. she opens it. chat I heard a sound come out of that bag and I am not going to write down what it was. then the horror took me and I went under. I hope I went under before.

beats.title: Post-Dated Letters
beats.modern: he asked me very sweetly to write three letters home. one saying my work is nearly done. one saying I leave tomorrow. one saying I've already reached Bistritz safe. then he gave me the dates to put on them. June 12. June 19. June 29. chat he just handed me my expiry date and had me write it out in my own handwriting.
beats.quote: “The first should be June 12, the second June 19, and the third June 29.”

beats.title: Fifty Boxes Of Dirt
beats.modern: climbed down the wall the way he does, found a stairway, found a ruined chapel, found fifty wooden boxes packed with fresh dug earth. and in one of them, lying on the dirt, is my client. eyes open. no pulse. no breath. not dead, not asleep, just switched off. I got close enough to search him for the key and the dead eyes still had hate in them. I left very fast.

beats.title: Speed The Parting Guest
beats.modern: tested him. said fine, no carriage, I'll walk home tonight. and he goes ALL gracious, welcome the coming speed the parting guest, and starts opening the front door onto a wall of wolves. red jaws already coming through the gap. so I said please shut the door, I'll wait till morning, and covered my face so he wouldn't watch me cry. last thing I saw was him kissing his hand to me with a smile Judas would be proud of.
beats.quote: ‘Welcome the coming; speed the parting guest.’

beats.title: The Shovel
beats.modern: went back down to the box. he's in it and he looks YOUNGER. cheeks full, blood on the lips running down the chin. he's fed. and he is going to London on paperwork I filed to do that to a whole city. so I grabbed a workman's shovel and swung at his face with the edge. and the head turned, and the eyes opened on me, and I froze, and the blade just slipped off. gave him a gash above the forehead. chat remember that gash.

beats.title: The Precipice
beats.modern: boxes are loaded. the gypsies are gone. every door is locked and I am alone in this castle with those three women and he told them tomorrow night is theirs. so I'm going out the window and down the wall as far as I can get. if I fall, I fall as a man instead of whatever they would make of me. good-bye all. Mina.
beats.quote: At its foot a man may sleep--as a man.

beats.title: Three Proposals In One Day
beats.modern: stream cuts here. I don't remember months. I'll pick the story back up from everyone else's papers, because Mina typed the lot of them out and I've read every page. while I was in that castle: her best friend Lucy got THREE proposals in one day. an asylum doctor, a Texan, and a lord. she said yes to the lord and cried over the other two. that was the peak of her life, chat. genuinely the peak.

beats.title: The Ship That Steered Itself
beats.modern: a schooner comes into Whitby harbour through a storm with nobody steering, because the captain is TIED to the wheel. dead two days. tied his own hands with his teeth, crucifix wound through the cords. and the instant the hull hits sand a huge dog leaps off the deck and goes straight up the cliff into the churchyard and out of the light. cargo manifest, chat: fifty boxes of earth. my boxes. I filed that shipment.

beats.title: Something On The Bench
beats.modern: Mina wakes at night and Lucy's bed is empty. she runs the whole town barefoot up to the abbey and there's Lucy on their favourite bench in her nightdress, and something long and black is bending over her. Mina shouts her name and the thing lifts its head. white face. red eyes. by the time she gets up the last steps, Lucy is alone and there is not a living thing in sight.

beats.title: It Was Never The Pin
beats.modern: Mina pinned a shawl round Lucy's throat to keep the cold off her and thinks she pricked her doing it. next morning there are two little red points on Lucy's neck and a drop of blood on the nightdress. and Mina writes in her diary that she feels terrible for being so clumsy, and that at least it's too tiny to leave a scar. chat. it was not the pin. it was never the pin.

beats.title: Transfusion Roulette
beats.modern: Lucy keeps emptying out overnight. so the old Dutch professor starts pouring men into her. the fiancé first, straight from his arm into hers, colour coming back into her face while it drains out of his. then the doctor. then the Texan. then himself. four men, and she still runs dry by morning. and when he lifts her pillow he sees the red mark on her throat and does not say one word about it.

beats.title: Common Garlic
beats.modern: the professor turns up with a box of flowers shipped from Holland and Lucy laughs at him because it's GARLIC. he does not laugh. no trifling with me, I never jest. then he rubs it on every window sash, every door jamb, all round the fireplace, hangs a wreath of it round her neck, and tells her whatever happens do not open the window tonight. chat the best doctor in Europe is warding a bedroom.

beats.title: The Blood Is The Life
beats.modern: meanwhile in the asylum there's a patient who eats flies, then feeds the flies to spiders, then the spiders to sparrows, working his way up the chain. today he jumped his doctor with a dinner knife, opened his wrist, and lay flat on the floor lapping the blood off the carpet like a dog. then went off with the attendants completely calm, saying one thing over and over.
beats.quote: “The blood is the life!

beats.title: The Wolf At The Window
beats.modern: Lucy's mother gets frightened by the noise outside and climbs into bed with her daughter so they can be brave together. then a wolf's head comes THROUGH the window glass. mum grabs wildly at anything to hold onto, and what she grabs is the garlic wreath, and she tears it off Lucy's neck, and then she dies of fright right there on top of her. chat the only thing guarding that girl was ripped away by her mother's dying hands.

beats.title: Alone With The Dead
beats.modern: Lucy sends the four maids to the dining room for a glass of wine to steady them. goes to check on them. all four flat on the floor. someone put laudanum in the sherry. so she is now alone in a house with a smashed window, with her mother's body, with no help coming, and she can hear the wolf outside. and she sits down and writes the whole thing out anyway. that girl was braver than me.

beats.title: Kiss Me
beats.modern: at the very end her breathing changed and the gums pulled back and the teeth looked longer, and she opened her eyes and asked Arthur to kiss her in a voice that was not hers. and the old professor caught him by the neck and HURLED him across the room. not for your life. and then she came back for a moment, took the old man's hand, called him her true friend, asked him to guard Arthur and give her peace. and then she stopped.
beats.quote: “Arthur! Oh, my love, I am so glad you have come! Kiss me!”

beats.title: It Is The Man Himself
beats.modern: back live. I'm married, I'm recovered, we're walking down Piccadilly after a funeral. and I look across the road and there he is. in London. in daylight. staring at a girl in a big hat. and he is YOUNGER than he was in the castle, chat, he has grown DOWN. I grabbed Mina's arm so hard I hurt her. I nearly went down in the street.
beats.quote: “I believe it is the Count, but he has grown young.

beats.title: The Bloofer Lady
beats.modern: the London papers are running this as a cute little item. children on Hampstead Heath keep wandering off in the evening and turning up next morning saying they were with the bloofer lady. the other kids have started playing at BEING her, it's adorable, one correspondent says even a famous actress couldn't be so winning. also every single one of those children has two small wounds in the throat. Lucy is buried on that Heath.

beats.title: Come To Me, Arthur
beats.modern: we waited outside her tomb. a white figure comes up the avenue of yews carrying something dark at its chest. it's Lucy. it's her face with everything sweet burned out of it. she drops the child on the ground the way a dog drops a bone and walks at her fiancé with her arms open, calling him husband, saying her arms are hungry. and he OPENS HIS ARMS BACK. the professor got a crucifix between them with maybe half a second to spare.
beats.quote: “Come to me, Arthur. Leave these others and come to me. My arms are hungry for you. Come, and we can rest together. Come, my husband, come!”

beats.title: The Hammer Goes To Arthur
beats.modern: the professor could have done it himself. he gave the hammer to the man who loved her, and that was the kindness, and Arthur's hands did not shake once. he set the point over the heart and struck and the thing in the coffin screamed and writhed and he did not stop. and when it went still, chat, it was LUCY in there. her real face. sweet and calm. he put his head on the old man's shoulder and cried and thanked him for it.

beats.title: Come In, Lord And Master
beats.modern: the fly-eater is dying with his skull broken and he finally tells us why. the Count stood outside his window promising him rats. thousands of them, eyes blazing red, all those lives, all that blood, if he would just fall down and worship. and he opened the sash himself. said the words himself. chat we spent weeks sealing every door in that building and the door had already been opened from the inside.
beats.quote: ‘Come in, Lord and Master!’

beats.title: The Kitten And The Saucer
beats.modern: they broke down my own bedroom door. I was on the bed, drugged unconscious, breathing like a stupid animal. Mina was kneeling beside me with his hand on the back of her neck, her face forced down onto a cut he had opened in his own chest, made to DRINK. the doctor wrote it down as looking like someone shoving a kitten's nose into a saucer of milk. that's my wife. I was two feet away. asleep.

beats.title: Unclean
beats.modern: she saw her own blood on my nightshirt where she had touched me and she pulled back and said unclean, unclean, I must never kiss you again, I'm your worst enemy now, you should be afraid of me. and I told her no. I said God can punish me worse than this hour if I ever let anything come between us. chat I have never meant anything more in my life.
beats.quote: “Unclean, unclean! I must touch him or kiss him no more.

beats.title: The Wine-Press Speech
beats.modern: then she told us what he said to her while he did it. that he commanded nations and fought wars centuries before any of us were born. that we should have kept our energies closer to home. that she is his now, flesh of his flesh, his wine-press for a while and his companion after. that when his brain says come, she will cross land or sea to reach him. then he tore his own chest open with his nails. chat he didn't just bite her. he installed himself.
beats.quote: flesh of my flesh; blood of my blood; kin of my kin; my bountiful wine-press for a while;

beats.title: The Wafer Burns
beats.modern: the professor went to bless her forehead with a piece of the Host so nothing could touch her while we were out. it BURNED her. seared into the flesh like white-hot metal. she screamed and then pulled her own hair down over her face like a leper and said even the Almighty shuts her out now, she'll carry the mark until Judgment Day. chat that is the worst sound I have ever heard and it has been a year of sounds.
beats.quote: “Unclean! Unclean! Even the Almighty shuns my polluted flesh!

beats.title: Deleting His Spawn Points
beats.modern: here's the actual strategy, chat. he can only rest in his own imported holy dirt and there are fifty boxes of it. so we are not fighting him. we are opening every single box and laying a fragment of the Host inside. he chose that earth because it was sanctified; we sanctify it harder and it burns him out. every lid we screw back down is one less place in England he can log back in.

beats.title: My Revenge Is Just Begun
beats.modern: cornered him in the Piccadilly house. I got the kukri in and only opened his coat, and banknotes and gold came pouring out of the lining. then all five of us lifted our crosses and he COWERED, then dove under my arm and went through the window into the yard. got up unhurt. told us we look like sheep in a butcher's, that our girls are his already, that his revenge runs over centuries and time is on his side. then bolted the stable door behind him.
beats.quote: My revenge is just begun! I spread it over centuries, and time is on my side.

beats.title: Kill Me If I Turn
beats.modern: Mina made all five of us swear it. one at a time, on our knees in front of her. that if she changes, if it is better she dies than lives, we drive a stake through her and cut off her head without a moment's delay. the Texan went first and added that if he is ever even DOUBTFUL, he'll take it that the time has come. and then she turned and looked at me and asked if I had to promise too.
beats.quote: You must promise me, one and all--even you, my beloved husband--that, should the time come, you will kill me.”

beats.title: She Is The Tracker
beats.modern: here's what he didn't think through. he's inside her head, but the wire runs both ways. every sunrise and every sunset the professor puts her under and asks where she is, and she answers from inside his box: lapping waves. rushing water. creaking masts. chat my wife is the GPS. he is sailing home in a crate with a tracker he installed himself and he does not know.

beats.title: The Ring In The Snow
beats.modern: the professor gets Mina up to the pass, builds a fire, draws a circle in the snow and crumbles the Host round it, and she cannot step out of it. and then the mist comes and the three women are there. the exact three from my bedroom. they smile at her and call her sister, come to us, come. and she sits in that ring with the burn on her forehead and looks at them with pure horror. and the old man nearly wept, because horror means she's still ours.
beats.quote: “Come, sister. Come to us. Come! Come!”

beats.title: One Word On The Tomb
beats.modern: then he went into the castle alone and did to those three what Arthur did to Lucy. three times over. an old man, by himself, in the dark, and he admits the fair one was so beautiful he nearly couldn't. then he found the last tomb, bigger and grander than all of them, one word cut into it. empty. so he sealed it with the Host so the owner can never come home to it again.

beats.title: Sunset At The Gate
beats.modern: gypsies whipping a cart up the mountain road, sun going down behind the castle. we surround them. I got onto the cart and threw the box off the wheel and Quincey and I prised the lid with our knives while they cut at him. and he's in there, and his eyes find the sinking sun, and the hate in them turns to TRIUMPH. he thought he'd made it. my knife through the throat, Quincey's into the heart, and he went to dust in front of us.

beats.title: Quincey
beats.modern: and Quincey is on the ground with the blood coming through his fingers, and he doesn't say one word about himself. he struggles up and points at Mina's forehead. the burn is gone. gone clean. he says it was worth dying for this, that the snow is not more stainless than her forehead, that the curse has passed away. and then he smiled, and that was all.
beats.quote: “Now God be thanked that all has not been in vain! See! the snow is not more stainless than her forehead! The curse has passed away!”

beats.title: Seven Years On
beats.modern: seven years now. we all went through the flames and what some of us have had since is worth what it cost. our boy was born on the anniversary of the day Quincey died, and Mina quietly believes some of him came through into our son. the kid carries every one of our names stacked up in a row. we just call him Quincey. that's the whole file, chat. every page of it. good night.

beats.title: Nobody Was Watching The Kid
beats.modern: my father's first wife walked out on him and he went on TOUR with it. drove the whole province crying on command, doing the injured husband bit, adding new details every stop. chat he was ENJOYING it. new comic role unlocked. then word comes she died and he ran into the street shouting thank you God, and also sobbed like a baby. both stories are true. that's the man.

beats.title: He Forgot He Had A Son
beats.modern: and Mitya? three years old, still in the house. dad didn't abandon him out of spite. he forgot. genuinely forgot a child lived there. our servant Grigory picked the kid up because otherwise nobody was going to change his shirt. that's my brother's entire origin story, chat. raised by the help because our father's memory had a gap exactly the size of a son.

beats.title: Why I Went Monk Mode
beats.modern: chat everyone thinks I'm a fanatic. I'm not. I'm not even mystical. I just love people, and the house I grew up in was a sewer, so I found the one man who felt real and I went where he was. that's the whole conversion arc. no vision. no lightning. I met an old man and my entire heart went with him.

beats.title: The Only Save File I Have Of Her
beats.modern: I was four when my mother died. one frame survived. evening light, window open, the lamp lit under the icon, and her on her knees holding me up to the picture like she's handing me over for safekeeping. she's sobbing. she's screaming. she is beautiful. then a nurse grabs me out of her arms and the clip cuts. that's all I've got. I've replayed it my whole life.

beats.title: Dad Does A Bit At The Monastery
beats.modern: we bring the family to a holy elder to settle the money fight like adults. dad walks in, reads the room, and decides tonight is crowd work. announces to a saint's face that he is a professional buffoon and would like to introduce himself as such. chat he is not drunk. this is just his personality with an audience.

beats.title: Why Is Such A Man Alive
beats.modern: and then Mitya says it. out loud. inside a monastery. surrounded by monks. asks the room why our father is permitted to keep existing, whether he can be allowed to go on defiling the earth. says it flat, no shouting, finger pointed right at him. chat you do not say that about your father in a room full of witnesses. you especially do not say it weeks before he turns up dead.
beats.quote: “Why is such a man alive?”

beats.title: The Elder Bows To Mitya
beats.modern: then the elder stands up, crosses the room, and puts his forehead on the floor at my brother's feet. a saint. bowing to the man who just publicly wished his own father dead. Mitya yelled oh God, covered his face and ran out. nobody understood it. I understood it later. he wasn't blessing him. he was bowing to how much suffering was already on its way.

beats.title: The Bet In The Nettles
beats.modern: lore drop and it's a rough one. years ago a pack of drunks walking home find a homeless woman asleep in the weeds. one of them jokes about whether she even counts as a woman. everyone says no, gross, obviously not. my father says actually there's a certain something about it. months later the whole town knows she's pregnant and every finger in it points the same direction.

beats.title: The Battlefield Is My Chest
beats.modern: Mitya's confessing to me and he says the quiet part. calls himself an insect. says we ALL are, me included, and that thing is asleep in me too and will wake up. then he drops the line I can't get out of my head: a man can hold the highest beauty and the lowest filth at the same time and not let go of either one.
beats.quote: I can’t endure the thought that a man of lofty mind and heart begins with the ideal of the Madonna and ends with the ideal of Sodom.

beats.title: She Bowed To The Floor
beats.modern: Katya comes to his room alone because her father is short the money and she has nowhere left to go. Mitya says he thought about humiliating her. thought about it for five entire seconds. then handed her the note and bowed. and she put her forehead on the floor to him and ran. he nearly stabbed himself afterward. from joy, he says. chat that debt is the whole rest of this story.

beats.title: Three Days, Zero Roubles
beats.modern: so he's engaged to her, he's carrying three thousand roubles of her money, and he takes Grushenka to Mokroe instead. gypsies, champagne, the entire village drunk on his tab. three days. stripped bare at the end of it, but a hero. and he got nothing out of her but a laugh. she is, he says, still laughing.

beats.title: The Cook Has A Loophole
beats.modern: our cook opens his mouth at dinner and calmly argues that if enemies were about to kill you for being Christian you could just renounce it. verbally. no sin. because the instant you THINK of saying it you're already cut off, so the words add nothing. chat he found a theological exploit. dad is delighted. I'm watching a man patch morality out of his own life in real time.

beats.title: He Kicked Our Father
beats.modern: Mitya's convinced Grushenka is hiding in the house. she isn't. he goes through Grigory, through a door, through every room, finds nothing, and dad starts screaming that he's stealing. so Mitya grabs the two tufts of hair the old man has left, slams him down and boots him in the face. then announces to the room he'll be back to finish it. everyone heard. that's the point. everyone heard.

beats.title: The Kid Who Bit Me
beats.modern: random schoolkid starts throwing rocks at me for no reason. gets me in the back, gets my elbow, then runs up and sinks his teeth into my finger down to the bone. ten seconds. will not let go. I bandage my hand and ask him what I did to him. he bursts into tears and runs. chat I have never seen this child before in my life.

beats.title: So Much For Your Money
beats.modern: a boy watched his father get dragged through the square by the beard. so I bring the father two hundred roubles to make it right and he LIGHTS UP, planning a whole new life, a horse, a cart, moving the family out. then he stops. asks if I want to see a little trick. crumples the notes, throws them in the sand, and stomps them, screaming so much for your money.
beats.quote: “Tell those who sent you that the wisp of tow does not sell his honor,”

beats.title: Ivan Returns The Ticket
beats.modern: Ivan isn't arguing God doesn't exist. everyone gets that wrong. he says fine, suppose at the end it's all explained and the mother embraces the man who fed her child to dogs and the whole thing resolves into harmony. Ivan says he doesn't want in. one tortured kid is too high a ticket price. he's not rejecting God. he's declining entry.
beats.quote: It’s not God that I don’t accept, Alyosha, only I most respectfully return Him the ticket.”

beats.title: My Brother Wrote Fanfic
beats.modern: then Ivan goes: I wrote a poem. he didn't write it. composed it in his head, never put one line on paper, and has been holding it a full year waiting for exactly one listener. why should an author give up even one listener, he says. the premise: Christ comes back. Spain. sixteenth century. and gets arrested immediately.

beats.title: The Kiss
beats.modern: the old Inquisitor talks for an hour straight. tells the prisoner nobody ever wanted freedom, they wanted bread and someone to obey, and the church quietly fixed His mistake. then he waits. he wants an answer. anything. a curse would do. and the prisoner just walks over and kisses him on the mouth. that's the entire reply. the old man opens the door and says go, never come back. and he can't get the kiss out of his chest.
beats.quote: ‘Go, and come no more ... come not at all, never, never!’

beats.title: Ivan Leaves Town On Purpose
beats.modern: Ivan books it to Moscow knowing exactly what's sitting in that house. gets to the station, changes his mind about where he's going, and pays a peasant to ride back and tell dad he did NOT go where dad asked. rides all night. and somewhere before dawn he says out loud to nobody: I'm a scoundrel. chat he knew. he knew and he left anyway.

beats.title: The Cook Falls Down The Stairs
beats.modern: same day, Smerdyakov goes down the cellar steps and starts convulsing at the bottom. doctor says serious, might be worse tomorrow. they carry him to the lodge. Grigory is already flat on his back and useless. so on the exact night everything happens, both men who guard that house are conveniently offline. remember this beat, chat. remember who scheduled it.

beats.title: The Duel He Did Not Fight
beats.modern: before he was a holy elder he was an army officer who beat his servant in the face and then challenged a man to a duel over a woman. night before, it lands on him: he is about to kill someone who never wronged him. so he goes to the servant's room, in full uniform, and puts his forehead on the floor and asks forgiveness. then rides out to the duel free.

beats.title: Everyone Is Responsible For Everyone
beats.modern: the elder's whole system, one line: stop telling yourself the world is too broken and you're too small. take it on. make yourself answerable for every person alive and every sin in it. and the second you actually do it, you'll see it was already true. no exceptions clause. nobody else left to blame.

beats.title: The Saint Starts To Smell
beats.modern: my elder dies and by afternoon the body smells, and the whole town LOSES it. because everyone had privately decided a real saint wouldn't rot, so the smell reads as a verdict. monks who spent forty years being holy are gloating in the corridor. chat they were waiting. all of them. they had been waiting for a chance to be right about him.

beats.title: The Onion
beats.modern: story her cook told her when she was little. wicked woman dies, goes straight in the lake of fire, and her angel can only dig up one good deed in her whole life: she once gave a beggar an onion. God says fine, hold it out, if it holds she's saved. it's HOLDING. and then everyone else in the lake grabs her legs and she kicks them off screaming it's MY onion. snap. she's still burning.
beats.quote: ‘I’ve done nothing but give away one onion all my life, that’s the only good deed I’ve done.’

beats.title: I Fell Down And Kissed The Dirt
beats.modern: I walk out under the stars and something takes my legs out. I'm on the ground with my arms around the earth, crying on it, kissing it, promising out loud to love it forever, and I could not tell you why. I went down a kid who'd lost his faith three hours earlier. I got up as something else. I've never once forgotten that minute.

beats.title: The Gold Mines Pitch
beats.modern: he needs three thousand roubles today or he's finished, so he goes begging to a rich widow. she is THRILLED. tells him the money's as good as in his pocket, not three thousand, three MILLION. he's going to run gold mines, found institutions, lead the nation. he asks about the actual three thousand. she says oh no, I meant the gold mines. she never had the money. she gave him a career plan.

beats.title: At The Window With A Pestle
beats.modern: Mitya's in the garden looking in his father's bedroom window. old man in a brand new silk dressing gown, gold studs, hair done, waiting up for a woman who is not coming. and Mitya's staring at the profile. the nose. the mouth. the whole face he has hated his entire life, lit up nicely from the left. and his hand goes in his pocket for the brass pestle.

beats.title: Parricide
beats.modern: he's up on the fence when old Grigory catches his leg and screams PARRICIDE loud enough for the whole street. then the old man drops like he's been hit by lightning. and here's the detail that ruins Mitya forever: he climbs back down, kneels, and tries to wipe the blood off the man's face with a clean handkerchief. soaks it through. then runs anyway.

beats.title: Looking At The Bullet
beats.modern: he's back in town covered in blood, buys his pistols out of pawn, and loads one at a table while a man watches him do it. holds the bullet up to the candle first. says it's going in his brain so it's interesting to see what it looks like. writes two lines on a clean sheet of paper, pockets it, then says he loves life. he loves life, chat. he just intends to be done with it after one more night.

beats.title: Crashing Her Party
beats.modern: he gets to Mokroe and she's in a room with the officer from five years ago. the first one. the one she cried over for five years. and Mitya walks in and asks permission to stay till morning. that's it. no scene, no scream. calls it his last night and asks if he can just be in the room. chat that is a man who has already decided how his story ends.

beats.title: The Marked Deck
beats.modern: and then the innkeeper reaches behind the sofa cushion and pulls out his own unopened pack, because the great first love has been playing with a marked deck all night. Kalganov saw him switch cards twice. so the man calls Grushenka a harlot and Mitya picks him up off the floor and carries him into the next room like furniture. and the little one STILL walks out the door expecting her to follow him.

beats.title: Take Off Your Socks
beats.modern: they arrest him at the inn and the first thing they do is make him undress. coat, trousers, shirt, socks, in front of peasant witnesses, while two lawyers run their fingers along every seam looking for money sewn in. he keeps asking am I to stay naked and they keep saying we'll arrange something. chat they stopped treating him like an officer about four minutes in.

beats.title: The Thing Round My Neck
beats.modern: then he gives up his real secret and it's the worst one he has. the money was his. he'd been wearing fifteen hundred roubles sewn in a rag around his neck for a MONTH. Katya's money. exactly half of what she trusted him with, held back so he could tell himself he was only half a thief. the room laughed at him. it was the truest thing he said all night.

beats.title: Why Is The Babe Weeping
beats.modern: he passes out mid-interrogation and dreams a burnt-out village, women lined up in the cold, a baby screaming. he asks the driver why and the driver just says it's the babe weeping. and Mitya wakes up wanting to do something for every one of them, now, immediately, obstacles be damned. that's the exact second he stops being innocent-and-furious and starts being willing to go down for it.

beats.title: It Is Zhutchka
beats.modern: Ilusha is dying and part of it is that he thinks he killed a dog. and Kolya, fourteen years old, has had that exact dog found, trained and hidden for WEEKS, purely to time the reveal. tells it to beg. the kid sits bolt upright and says its name. chat he stood a lost dog up in front of a dying child like a magic trick. it worked perfectly. it was also the worst possible thing for him.

beats.title: Bury Me By The Big Stone
beats.modern: Ilusha tells his father he saw the new doctor's face and he already knows. then he asks him to get another boy afterward, a good one, name him Ilusha, love him instead. and to come sit by the big stone in the evenings. the three of them hold onto each other and nobody says anything. then out in the hallway his father tells me he does not want another boy.
beats.quote: “Father, don’t cry, and when I die get a good boy, another one

beats.title: Lise Wants The World To Burn
beats.modern: Lise tells me flat that she wants to do evil. quietly, for a long time, and then be found out and have everyone stand around pointing at her. she reads awful books she steals from her mother. she wants to destroy herself. and then the line that actually landed: everyone loves that my brother killed his father. they all say it's horrifying and secretly they love it. chat she's not wrong about them.

beats.title: The Money In The Sock
beats.modern: Smerdyakov rolls up his trouser leg, fishes around in his stocking, and lays three packets of hundred-rouble notes on the table. all three thousand of it. then tells Ivan it wasn't Mitya, it was him, and that Ivan is the real murderer because Ivan is the one who left town. chat my brother went in to prove himself innocent and got handed the money instead.
beats.quote: “It was only with you, with your help, I killed him, and Dmitri Fyodorovitch is quite innocent.”

beats.title: Ivan Has A Guest
beats.modern: and now there's a man sitting on Ivan's sofa. shabby jacket three years out of fashion, collar not quite clean, check trousers too tight, the exact type of poor relation who tells stories and takes a hand at cards and never quite gets the good seat. extremely polite. extremely reasonable. chat it isn't a man. it's Ivan's own brain wearing a threadbare scarf and it will not stop talking.

beats.title: He Hanged Himself
beats.modern: I run in to tell Ivan that Smerdyakov is dead. note on the table saying he ended it by his own will so no blame falls on anybody. and Ivan doesn't react. just says I knew. HE told me. just now. and I look around an empty room. chat the only man who could clear Mitya is on a nail in a wall and the only man who heard him confess is coming apart tonight.
beats.quote: “I destroy my life of my own will and desire, so as to throw no blame on any one.”

beats.title: Ivan Takes The Stand
beats.modern: Ivan gets called up, says he has nothing to tell them, walks four steps toward the door, stops, turns around, and dumps three thousand roubles on the table. says he got it yesterday from the murderer. says Smerdyakov did it and he told him to. then he turns on the gallery and informs the entire room that they all want their fathers dead and they only came for the show.
beats.quote: It was he, not my brother, killed our father. He murdered him and I incited him to do it

beats.title: Katya Produces A Letter
beats.modern: they haul Ivan out screaming and Katya stands up with a letter. Mitya wrote it drunk, two days before, spelling out how he'd kill our father for the money. she'd been sitting on it to protect him. then she watched Ivan destroy himself on the stand for Mitya's sake, and she chose Ivan. handed the court the rope herself. chat she loved him. that's exactly what made it fatal.

beats.title: Yes, Guilty
beats.modern: one hour of deliberation. the foreman stands up and says guilty. then again. and again, to every single question, no recommendation to mercy, nothing. the room goes dead silent because nobody expected it, not even the people who wanted it. and Mitya stands with his hands out and swears on the day of judgment he never touched his father's blood, forgives Katya, and asks them to pity Grushenka. twenty years in the mines.
beats.quote: “I swear by God and the dreadful Day of Judgment I am not guilty of my father’s blood! Katya, I forgive you!

beats.title: The Escape Plan
beats.modern: Katya's nursing Ivan through brain fever in her own house, ignoring the entire town's opinion of that, and she tells me the escape is already built. it was Ivan's. drawn up before the trial, third stop on the road to Siberia, the right people already spoken to. the brother who stood up in open court and blamed himself has quietly been arranging to steal Mitya out of Russia the whole time.

beats.title: Hurrah For Karamazov
beats.modern: Ilusha's funeral. twelve boys, one stone, and the only thing I actually know: a single good memory from childhood can hold a person together for the rest of their life, and this one, right here, might be theirs. then Kolya asks if we really all rise again and see each other. and somebody shouts Karamazov we love you and they all take it up. we go in to the funeral dinner hand in hand. gg chat.
beats.quote: “Karamazov, we love you!”

beats.title: The Wistaria Ad
beats.modern: chat. CHAT. I'm sitting in a miserable women's club in London reading the classifieds like a normal depressed housewife and there it is. small mediaeval castle. Italy. the whole month of April. addressed specifically to people who APPRECIATE wistaria and sunshine, which is me, that's my entire personality, nobody knows that about me. then I put the paper down and go stare at the rain because castles are for the rich.
beats.quote: To Those who Appreciate Wistaria and Sunshine.

beats.title: The Rainy Day Clause
beats.modern: my husband has spent our entire marriage telling me to save for a rainy day. ninety pounds. scraped out of my dress allowance pound by pound, which is why I dress like a perfect sight but am PREPARED. chat I am looking out the window at sooty rain hitting the omnibuses and doing the maths. this is the rainy day. he said it himself. receipts in chat.
beats.quote: “when there will be a rainy day, and you may be very glad to find you have a nest-egg.

beats.title: Talking To A Stranger
beats.modern: there's a sad woman across the table reading the exact same ad with the face of a disappointed Madonna. now, I have never once spoken to a stranger. I am shy to the point of being furniture. and my mouth just goes: are you reading about the mediaeval castle. chat I shocked myself harder than I shocked her.
beats.quote: “Are you reading about the mediaeval castle and the wistaria?”

beats.title: Rent It Hire It Have It
beats.modern: so I pitch her. two women, one castle, split the rent, one month, come home nicer than we left. she says but we don't know each other. I say we WILL. she says how do you mean, get it. rent it. hire it. HAVE it. chat I have never closed a deal in my life and I am closing this one.
beats.quote: “Rent it. Hire it. Have it.”

beats.title: Boots Made Of Sins
beats.modern: lore drop on my new friend's husband. he writes bestselling memoirs of kings' mistresses. one dead courtesan a year, like a franchise. she can't stomach a penny of it so she launders the whole income through the parish poor. the children of Hampstead are walking around in boots funded by centuries of adultery. she calls that purified. she is not convinced.
beats.quote: Their very boots were stout with sins.

beats.title: I Thought I Saw Keats
beats.modern: we advertise for two more women to split the rent and get exactly two replies, so no auditions. one's a duke's daughter. the other is sixty-five and personally knew every dead genius in England. so I ask if she knew Keats. she looks at me over her glasses and states that she was unacquainted with both Keats and Shakespeare. and then, chat, I keep going. I tell her I saw Keats. in Hampstead. crossing the road. she asks for references.
beats.quote: she had been unacquainted with both Keats and Shakespeare.

beats.title: Italy For Easter
beats.modern: third Sunday. I have fed this man the greatest Yorkshire pudding of his life purely so he'll be soft when I confess. he lights his cigar and announces he is thinking of taking ME to Italy for Easter. chat. CHAT. the silence in that room. I have already rented a castle in Italy behind his back and I have not written the speech yet.
beats.quote: “I am thinking of taking you to Italy for Easter.”

beats.title: Too Good For Too Long
beats.modern: we're pacing Victoria station an hour early, going on holiday, feeling like criminals. that's what a decade of being good does to you. we spoiled them so thoroughly that wanting one month to ourselves reads as theft. we're not people anymore, we're brow-beaten. nobody real is ever as good as we've been.
beats.quote: We’re brow-beaten—we’re not any longer real human beings.

beats.title: Beppo Drives
beats.modern: midnight. sheeting rain. zero Italian between us. a stranger has our suitcases and is whipping his horse round cliff bends with his back to the road, facing US, explaining something. we wave at him to TURN AROUND. he reads this as go faster. so he goes faster. we cling to each other repeating the only two words we know: San Salvatore.
beats.quote: the rocks leaped towards them, the little fly swayed, the suit-cases heaved,

beats.title: We Were Not Murdered
beats.modern: update: it was the castle. the suitcases are here. the men who grabbed them were porters. the terrifying lantern man is the gardener and he is lovely. we stand in the hall blinking at each other like two survivors, and I kiss her, because the first thing that happens in this house is going to be a kiss. she's Rose. I'm Lotty.
beats.quote: and their suit-cases were waiting for them; and they had not been murdered.

beats.title: Opening The Shutters
beats.modern: morning one. I wake up in a bed with nobody else in it for the first time in five years and pull the blankets any direction I want purely because I can. then I open the shutters. chat. the sea. the mountains asleep in the light. one enormous black cypress cutting through all of it. I am crying at a tree before breakfast and I regret nothing.
beats.quote: All the radiance of April in Italy lay gathered together at her feet.

beats.title: Naked Of Goodness
beats.modern: at home I was GOOD. relentlessly, professionally good, and I felt like a wrung-out rag every single day of it. here I'm doing nothing unselfish, nothing I don't want to do, and I feel like light. not one twinge. and when I try to picture my husband being furious in Hampstead he just shimmers, goes violet, and dissolves. can't even render him.
beats.quote: She was naked of goodness, and was rejoicing in being naked.

beats.title: The Girl On The Wall
beats.modern: the fourth sharer beat us here and she's sitting on the wall with her feet in the lilies being the most beautiful person I have ever physically seen. so I tell her. immediately. out loud. she says thank you, she's been making the most of it since birth. and Rose raises a finger and informs her it won't last. chat we have been in heaven ninety minutes and we are already being ourselves.
beats.quote: “I make the most of it. I’ve been doing that ever since I can remember.”

beats.title: Beds Without Husbands
beats.modern: the old lady has had the spare bed hauled out of her room on the grounds that it's foolish to have more beds than occupiers. so I ask, very reasonably, if we can have ours removed too, seeing as we haven't got any husbands here to put in them. chat the temperature in that dining room. in her day beds and husbands were never spoken of in the same breath and I did it in one sentence.
beats.quote: I don’t see any use in extra beds in one’s room if one hasn’t got husbands to put in them.

beats.title: Wistaria And Sunshine Delivered
beats.modern: we go down the steps and the periwinkles are being POURED down both sides like someone tipped them out. the pergola is wistaria falling over itself. then geraniums, marigolds actually burning, snapdragons, and terrace after terrace of peach blossom dropping away to the sea. wistaria and sunshine, the ad said. the ad undersold it.
beats.quote: Colour seemed flung down anyhow, anywhere; every sort of colour, piled up in heaps,

beats.title: Cups Of Acceptance
beats.modern: we climb down through the olives to the water and take off our shoes and stockings and hang our feet in the sea. two respectable married women of Hampstead. we stop talking. we stop saying the word heaven. we just sit there being filled up. our husbands would not recognise us.
beats.quote: They were just cups of acceptance.

beats.title: A Noise About Nothing
beats.modern: the beautiful one came here to be left alone and instead she's out under the stars discovering something worse. twenty-eight years of parties, of being adored by every man who ever saw her, and it might have been a noise about nothing. she has never had to think before. turns out it's difficult. she keeps falling asleep mid-thought.
beats.quote: it had suddenly seemed as if her life had been a noise all about nothing.

beats.title: Maccaroni Was My Husband
beats.modern: the old lady cannot eat the maccaroni. it slips, it wriggles off the fork, it hangs out of her mouth and destroys her dignity, and every time she eats it she thinks of her late husband, because he did all four of those things too. she ends up cutting it up with a KNIFE. chat that's an entire marriage on one plate.
beats.quote: He had during their married life behaved very much like maccaroni.

beats.title: I Saw Inside Her
beats.modern: the beautiful one says she has a headache. Rose wants to bring her tea. the old lady prescribes castor oil. I say she hasn't got a headache, she just wants to be left alone. they ask how I could possibly know that. because when I was out there just now I saw inside her. the table goes silent. the old lady decides I'm an idiot and rings the gong for more food.
beats.quote: “When I was out there just now I saw inside her.”

beats.title: Women's Heads
beats.modern: the beautiful one finally admits what she wants out of this month. to come to a conclusion. one. that's the whole ask. and the old lady looks her over and says what a young woman like her needs is a husband and children, and that women's heads weren't built for thinking anyway, so she should go to bed. sixty-five years of receipts and THAT is the advice.
beats.quote: Women’s heads weren’t made for thinking, I assure you.

beats.title: A Mean Dog
beats.modern: plot twist chat: I've written to Mellersh to come out here. yes. the man I ran away from. he'd planned to take me to Italy himself and I went behind his back, so honestly? I've been a mean dog. there are empty beds in this house and it is disgusting not to share. he has fed and housed me for years. Rose thinks I've lost my mind. I see him here.
beats.quote: “I’ve invited him to come and stay with us.”

beats.title: Improper Without Men
beats.modern: the duke's daughter comes to dinner in something shell-pink you can see clean through. asked what's underneath, she says nothing. at least, hardly anything. the old lady rules this highly improper, so I point out there are no men here, so how can it be, and honestly, have you noticed how hard it is to be improper without men? nobody answers me. the beautiful one smiles into her soup.
beats.quote: “I haven’t. At least, hardly anything,”

beats.title: The Bitter Wind
beats.modern: and then I told the whole table the truth and couldn't stop. living with somebody who doesn't love you is standing outside in a bitter wind with nothing on, knowing there'll never be anything on, getting colder and colder until it finishes you. that was my life. the old lady kept saying Really—. I wasn't complaining, chat. I was saying I've suddenly got well.
beats.quote: it—that’s what it was like, living with somebody who didn’t love one.”

beats.title: All Bosom
beats.modern: Rose's arc, and it hurts. she's alone on a rock aching for ONE person of her own to say look at this to. her husband stopped seeing her years ago. her baby died. so she sits there stuffed with love and nowhere to put it, and describes the feeling in the least romantic phrasing ever committed to English: all bosom.
beats.quote: There was something about San Salvatore that made her feel all bosom.

beats.title: The Bath Explodes
beats.modern: husband arrives. husband wants a hot bath. the stove has printed instructions on the wall using the word PERICOLOSO, and my husband speaks no Italian and does not read walls. he gets in. he turns off the tap. the stove detonates. he comes out of that bathroom at a full sprint in one towel, saying a word he has never said in his professional life.
beats.quote: “That damned bath!”

beats.title: How Do You Do
beats.modern: and who does he run directly into on the landing. the duke's daughter. the one person he crossed a continent to impress, whose family history he REHEARSED on the train, and he is standing there dripping in a towel. so he apologises for his language. she says she thought it most appropriate. then he formally introduces himself and shakes her hand. twice. legs out. voice like a church.
beats.quote: “I thought it most appropriate,”

beats.title: The Confession
beats.modern: pay day. the bills come and I have to tell him all of it. the advertisement, the fibs, my entire nest-egg spent on a castle he wasn't invited to. at home this would have taken him three days to say out loud. here he just asks what could possibly be more beneficial than a holiday like this. chat I nearly went through the floor.
beats.quote: “What can be more beneficial than such a holiday?”

beats.title: Crop Out All Green
beats.modern: the old lady cannot sit still. she came here to sit quietly in the sun and remember her dead famous friends, and instead she's trotting in and out without her stick feeling SAP RISE, and she is appalled by it. sixty-five years of dignity, and now she's frightened that at any moment she might crop out all green.
beats.quote: did Mrs. Fisher have a ridiculous feeling as if she were presently going to burgeon.

beats.title: The Wrong Telegram
beats.modern: Rose finally wrote to her husband. today a telegram comes and she runs up those steps red as a camellia because he came, he actually — it's from the landlord. asking if he may pay his respects this afternoon. chat I watched her face go white in real time while she smiled and said oh no, on the contrary. I'm going to have a visitor.
beats.quote: “A telegram has come for you,”

beats.title: Briggs Is Undone
beats.modern: the landlord turns out to be thirty, an orphan, and so charming he made the old lady laugh for the first time in her recorded life. then the duke's daughter walks out of a dark doorway into the sunset and it ends him where he stands. beads on his temples. drops the teaspoon. rolls a macaroon across the floor. he does not recover this stream.
beats.quote: he became silent, solemn, and with little beads on his temples.

beats.title: The Man At The Window
beats.modern: Rose goes to look at the firelight in the drawing room and there is a man standing at the window. it's her husband. she creeps across that room not breathing, whispers his name, and he spins round and stares at her like she's a stranger — and she already has her arms round his neck saying I always knew you would come. chat he did not know she was here. he had no idea. he kisses her anyway, and then he can't stop.
beats.quote: “I knew you would come—in

beats.title: The Save
beats.modern: here's what he actually came for: the duke's daughter. he publishes under a fake name, she has no idea he's married, and he is now sitting at dinner about to be introduced to his own wife by his crush. so I get in first and say fancy how quickly ROSE'S HUSBAND has got here. and she doesn't blink. she sits down and tells him she's sorry she's late on his very first evening. clutch play of the century.
beats.quote: “and me late your very first evening.”

beats.title: The Loyalty Of A Man
beats.modern: he catches her in the garden afterwards and says he wants to kiss her shoes. she offers her hand instead. he tells her he adored her before for being beautiful, and now he adores her for being as decent as a man — chat that's 1922 for you, that's the highest compliment he owns. she takes it. she takes it a bit wistfully.
beats.quote: “I want to kiss your shoes.”

beats.title: The Other Half Of Her Pair
beats.modern: I find the old lady alone by the fire not reading, because her great dead friends have stopped saying anything new, and she's sitting there wishing she'd had a son. so I kiss her and shove a footstool under her feet and she holds my cheek against hers. chat. I think I'm the other half of her pair. I see myself fetching that woman footstools for the rest of my life.
beats.quote: the loneliness of having outstayed one’s welcome in the world,

beats.title: I See Them Being The Briggses
beats.modern: Mellersh wants me to say the Arbuthnots. fine. the Arbuthnots. and the Carolines — and both of them nearly come out of their chairs, because you cannot possibly pair the daughter of the Droitwiches with a man named BRIGGS whom she met this afternoon. sorry if you don't like it, Mellersh. don't struggle. I see them being the Briggses.
beats.quote: “I see them being the Briggses,”

beats.title: The Acacias
beats.modern: last week. the wistaria's gone, the syringa's out, and the whole garden turns white and starts smelling of acacia. four strangers came here out of a newspaper advertisement and not one of us is going home as the woman who arrived. on the first of May we walk down the hill and out through the iron gates, and we can still smell them. gg. stream's over.
beats.quote: they still could smell the acacias.

beats.title: Day One On The Sivilize Server
beats.modern: so a widow adopted me and now I live in a house. bell rings, you eat. she mumbles over the food before anybody's allowed to touch it. she read me a whole lore drop about a guy named Moses and I was LOCKED IN until she let slip he's been dead a considerable long time. dropped the quest immediately. chat I don't take no stock in dead people.
beats.quote: I don’t take no stock in dead people.

beats.title: Guild Application Denied
beats.modern: Tom's starting a robber gang. blood signatures, the whole thing. then the rules committee hits a snag: every member needs a family the gang can murder if he snitches. I don't have one. they were about to CUT ME FROM THE ROSTER. so I offered up Miss Watson. they could kill her. unanimous yes. I'm in.
beats.quote: all at once I thought of a way, and so I offered them Miss Watson—they could kill her.

beats.title: Ransomed To Death
beats.modern: Ben asked Tom what ransoming actually is. Tom does not know. Tom has never known. but it's in the BOOKS so we've got to do it. ten minutes of debate later the official ruling is that ransom means you keep them till they die. Ben said that'll answer, why couldn't you said that before. these are my raid leaders.
beats.quote: “I don’t know. But that’s what they do. I’ve seen it in books; and so of course that’s what we’ve got to do.”

beats.title: The Elephant Raid
beats.modern: Tom's intel said Spanish merchants, two hundred elephants, six hundred camels, all loaded with diamonds and guarded by only four hundred soldiers. we ambushed with lath swords. it was a Sunday school picnic. primer class. we chased toddlers up a hollow and got doughnuts. Tom says the diamonds WERE there, we just have enemies called magicians who turned the whole thing into an infant Sunday school out of spite.
beats.quote: He said it was all done by enchantment.

beats.title: Liquidating My Account
beats.modern: found boot tracks in the snow with a cross of nails in the heel to keep off the devil. that's pap. he's back and he wants the six thousand. so I sprinted to the judge and tried to GIVE HIM my entire fortune. he thought I was joking. I said just take it and don't ask me nothing, then I won't have to lie. so he wrote it up as a sale. I got a dollar for it.
beats.quote: “Please take it,” says I, “and don’t ask me nothing—then I won’t have to tell no lies.”

beats.title: He Was In The Room
beats.modern: went up to my room with a candle and he was already sitting in the chair. window open, boot busted, two toes out and working. and his face, chat. not white the way a person is white. a white that makes your flesh crawl. tree-toad white. fish-belly white. hat on the floor with the top caved in like a lid. first thing he said was that my clothes were too starchy.
beats.quote: a white to make a body sick, a white to make a body’s flesh crawl—a tree-toad white, a fish-belly white.

beats.title: The Redemption Arc
beats.modern: new judge takes pap in, feeds him, talks temperance at him till he CRIES. pap does a whole speech holding out his hand, says look, this used to be the hand of a hog and now it's a man's hand. everybody sobbed. the judge's wife kissed it. that night he traded his new coat for a jug, rolled off the porch roof and broke his arm in two places. judge said you could maybe reform him with a shotgun.
beats.quote: There’s a hand that was the hand of a hog; but it ain’t so no more;

beats.title: Pap Reviews The Government
beats.modern: drunk uncle discovers politics. forty minutes on how the law is stealing his son and his money, then he pivots hard to a free man from Ohio with a gold watch who teaches at a college, speaks several languages, and can VOTE where he's from. pap announces he will never vote again as long as he lives and the country may rot. then he kicked a tub of salt pork with his bad foot, and the cussing that followed beat anything he'd ever done previous.

beats.title: The Angel Of Death
beats.modern: woke up to screaming. snakes on his legs. then devils have hold of him. then he crawls under the table begging the dead to let him alone, and cries. then he sees me, decides I am the Angel of Death, and comes at me with a knife. got me by the jacket. I came out of the jacket. he ran out of gas and said he would rest a minute and then kill me. I took the gun down and waited for sunrise.
beats.quote: He chased me round and round the place with a clasp-knife, calling me the Angel of Death,

beats.title: I Staged My Own Murder
beats.modern: axed the door open from the inside. shot a wild pig and cut its throat on the dirt floor. dragged a sack of rocks to the river so they'd think that was my body sinking. pulled out some of my own hair and stuck it to the bloody axe. slit the meal sack so it left a trail toward the lake for them to chase. only regret is Tom Sawyer wasn't here, he'd have thrown in the fancy touches.
beats.quote: Nobody could spread himself like Tom Sawyer in such a thing as that.

beats.title: Somebody Else Is On My Island
beats.modern: stalked a campfire for two days, finally crept up on the guy at dawn, and it's Jim. Miss Watson's Jim. he takes one look at me and hits his KNEES begging a ghost not to hurt him, says he always liked dead people and done all he could for them, please go get back in the river where you belong. sir. sir I'm not dead.

beats.title: Eight Hundred Dollars
beats.modern: Jim goes quiet, makes me swear twice, then says it: I run off. here's why. he heard Miss Watson through a door telling the widow she was selling him down to Orleans. she said she didn't want to. she said she couldn't resist, because he was worth eight hundred dollars. he didn't stay to hear the rest. people would call me a low-down abolitionist for keeping mum. I ain't telling.
beats.quote: “But mind, you said you wouldn’ tell—you know you said you wouldn’ tell, Huck.”

beats.title: The Floating House
beats.modern: a whole two-story house came drifting down the river in the night so obviously we boarded it through an upstairs window. there's a man in the far corner. Jim goes over, looks, comes back and says he's dead, shot in the back, been there days. then he says come in Huck but don't look at his face. so I didn't. remember this one, chat. it comes back at the very end.
beats.quote: “It’s a dead man. Yes, indeedy; naked, too. He’s ben shot in de back.

beats.title: Sarah Mary Williams George Elexander Peters
beats.modern: went into town in a dress to farm intel and gave three different names in one conversation. the woman clocked me and then ran the FILM: you threaded a needle wrong. you throw like a boy. you clapped your knees together to catch that lump of lead instead of spreading your skirt. she said she contrived the other tests just to make certain. absolutely cooked by a stranger in a shack in under an hour.

beats.title: Wrong Boat To Board
beats.modern: boarded a wrecked steamboat in a thunderstorm for fun. there's a man tied up on the floor and two guys standing over him arguing about whether to shoot him. and the one AGAINST shooting is scarier, because his plan is better: leave him tied, the wreck breaks up in two hours, he drowns, and technically nobody killed anybody. he called it good morals. I'm in the top bunk not breathing.
beats.quote: He’ll be drownded, and won’t have nobody to blame for it but his own self.

beats.title: Jim Reviews King Solomon
beats.modern: told Jim that Solomon was the wisest man who ever lived. Jim: absolutely not. man had a million wives, that's a boiler factory, a wise man builds one so he can SHUT IT DOWN when he wants rest. then he gets to the baby. you're gonna settle who owns a whole child by producing half a child? what's the use of half a dollar bill, can't buy nothing with it. I said you're missing the point. he said blame the point.
beats.quote: En what use is a half a chile? I wouldn’ give a dern for a million un um.”

beats.title: Trash
beats.modern: got separated in the fog all night and then told Jim he dreamed the whole thing. he BELIEVED me. spent ten minutes interpreting his own fake dream as a warning. then he sees the leaves and the busted oar all over the raft and goes quiet. says his heart was most broke thinking I was lost, and all I was thinking about was how to make a fool of him. that truck is trash. and trash is what people is that puts dirt on the head of their friends.
beats.quote: en trash is what people is dat puts dirt on de head er dey fren’s en makes ’em ashamed.”

beats.title: He's White
beats.modern: two men in a skiff, guns, asking is the man on your raft white or black. I'd spent all night talking myself into turning him in. I opened my mouth and nothing came out. hadn't the spunk of a rabbit. then I heard myself say he's white. then I sold them a whole smallpox story until they backed water so fast they left me forty dollars floating on a board to go away.
beats.quote: “He’s white.”

beats.title: The Wages Are The Same
beats.modern: felt rotten for not turning him in. then I ran the numbers: if I HAD turned him in, would I feel better? no. I'd feel exactly this bad. so what's the point of learning to do right, when doing right is troublesome and doing wrong is easy and the wages is just the same. couldn't answer that one. new policy: always do whichever comes handiest at the time.
beats.quote: what’s the use you learning to do right when it’s troublesome to do right and ain’t no trouble to do wrong, and the wages is just the same?

beats.title: We Went Past Cairo
beats.modern: Cairo was the whole run. reach Cairo, sell the raft, steamboat up into the free states, done. we passed it in the fog. in the DARK. we've been floating the wrong direction into deeper slave country for days and neither of us knew. clear Ohio water inshore and the old Muddy outside. Jim said poor folks can't have no luck and blamed the snakeskin. it was not the snakeskin.

beats.title: Third Partied By A Steamboat
beats.modern: upstream boat came at us in the dark. we lit the lantern. we assumed she'd sheer off. she did not sheer off. furnace doors open like a row of red-hot teeth and she came straight through the middle of the raft. Jim went over one side, me the other. I stayed under a minute and a half because a thirty-foot wheel needed room. surfaced. no Jim. and the boat started her engines back up, because nobody has ever cared about raftsmen.

beats.title: Emmeline's Content Pipeline
beats.modern: the dead daughter of this house ran a system: read the obituaries, write a poem about it same day, paste it in the scrap-book. there's one about a boy who fell down a well. it carefully rules out whooping-cough. rules out measles. rules out despised love. rules out stomach troubles. then confirms he died of the well. she was fourteen and there ain't no telling what she could have done by and by.

beats.title: I Ain't Going To Tell All That Happened
beats.modern: Sophia ran off with a Shepherdson and both families were to guns before breakfast. I was up a cottonwood watching. Buck and his cousin were pinned behind a woodpile doing fine until the men circled through the trees and came in from behind. the boys jumped for the river hurt and the men ran the bank shooting. I ain't going to tell all that happened. I pulled them out of the water after and covered their faces. I cried some over Buck. he was mighty good to me.
beats.quote: I ain’t ever going to get shut of them—lots of times I dream about them.

beats.title: No Home Like A Raft
beats.modern: got back and Jim grabbed me and hugged me. corn-dodgers and buttermilk and pork and cabbage and we didn't talk about the shooting for a while. other places feel cramped up and smothery. a raft don't. there ain't no home like a raft, after all.
beats.quote: We said there warn’t no home like a raft, after all.

beats.title: By Rights I Am A Duke
beats.modern: picked up two guys running from two separate mobs. inside one afternoon the younger one is sighing at the horizon going alas, the secret of my birth. turns out he is the rightful Duke of Bridgewater, wrongfully deprived, hunted of men, degraded to the companionship of felons on a raft. Jim bought it so completely he waited on him through dinner. will your Grace have some of this.
beats.quote: By rights I am a duke!”

beats.title: Ratio'd By The Bald One
beats.modern: the old bald one watched four hours of duke worship and then started crying too. bilgewater, can I trust you. I am the late Dauphin. the lost king of France, in blue jeans, on our raft. the duke tried to contest it, said at your age you'd have to be Charlemagne, and got told trouble done it. so now we do Your Majesty AND Your Grace, and we stand up until he says we can sit.
beats.quote: “Bilgewater, I am the late Dauphin!”

beats.title: The Reformed Pirate Speedrun
beats.modern: king walks into a revival cold and announces he's been a pirate in the Indian Ocean for thirty years, got robbed last night, and it's the BLESSEDEST thing that ever happened to him because he's changed now and he's going back to convert the other pirates. crowd sobbing. somebody yells let HIM pass the hat. eighty-seven dollars seventy-five cents, plus a jug he found under a wagon on the walk home. his review: heathens don't amount to shucks alongside pirates.
beats.quote: heathens don’t amount to shucks alongside of pirates to work a camp-meeting with.

beats.title: Hamlet From Memory
beats.modern: the duke's teaching the king Hamlet's soliloquy. he doesn't have the book. he's pulling it from recollection's vaults. what comes out is Hamlet and Macbeth and about four other plays in a blender: to be or not to be, that is the bare bodkin. Birnam Wood turns up. Duncan gets woken. Ophelia is told not to open her ponderous and marble jaws. the king learned it perfect and it became the pride of his life.
beats.quote: To be, or not to be; that is the bare bodkin

beats.title: Till One O'Clock
beats.modern: old Boggs rides in drunk for his monthly and starts cussing Colonel Sherburn in the street. whole town laughing, everybody says he never hurt nobody drunk or sober. Sherburn steps out and gives him a deadline. one o clock. not a threat, a schedule. they sent for his daughter. she was running down the street when Sherburn called his name. Boggs turned, saw the barrel come level, threw both hands up. two shots. she was sixteen.
beats.quote: “I’m tired of this, but I’ll endure it till one o’clock.

beats.title: The Idea Of You Lynching Anybody
beats.modern: mob tore his fence down and Sherburn walked out on the porch roof with a shotgun and said nothing until they went quiet. then he took the whole town apart. the average man's a coward. your juries won't hang murderers because they're scared of getting shot in the back in the dark. you didn't bring a man with you, you brought HALF a man and hung onto his coat-tail. now droop your tails and go home. they went home.
beats.quote: The average man’s a coward.

beats.title: The Royal Nonesuch
beats.modern: three nights only, fifty cents, ladies and children not admitted. curtain goes up and the king comes out on all fours, naked, painted in stripes like a rainbow. that is the entire show. they made him do it three times. it would make a cow laugh.

beats.title: Sold
beats.modern: curtain drops and the duke announces the tragedy runs two more nights due to pressing London engagements. the crowd works it out. crowd stands up furious. then a big respectable man jumps on a bench: hold on. we're sold. but do we want to be the laughing stock of this town forever? no. so we go home QUIET and we sell the rest of the town. everybody agreed with him. that's how night two sold out.
beats.quote: What we want is to go out of here quiet, and talk this show up, and sell the rest of the town!

beats.title: Shet De Do'
beats.modern: Jim's been moaning nights when he thinks I'm asleep. tonight he told me why. his little girl, four, just off scarlet fever. he told her to shut the door. she stood there smiling up at him. he yelled it. she stood there. so he hit her. went in the other room. came back and she was still in that open doorway crying. then the wind slammed the door behind her, ker-blam, and she never moved. she never moved, chat. the fever took her hearing and he didn't know.
beats.quote: Oh, she was plumb deef en dumb, Huck, plumb deef en dumb—en

beats.title: We Are His Brothers
beats.modern: king pumped a random kid on the riverbank for an hour, got a dead tanner's whole family tree, then walked into town and asked where Peter Wilks lives. they told him he died yesterday. he collapsed onto a stranger's shoulder and cried down his back. the duke, playing deaf and dumb, dropped his bag and burst out sobbing on cue. the town carried their luggage up the hill for them. it was enough to make a body ashamed of the human race.
beats.quote: It was enough to make a body ashamed of the human race.

beats.title: Funeral Orgies
beats.modern: the king keeps saying funeral ORGIES. the duke slips him a note reading obsequies, you old fool. so the king stands up in a room full of mourners and explains that orgies is actually the correct term in England now, from the Greek orgo meaning outside and the Hebrew jeesum meaning to plant, hence inter, hence a public funeral. he invented two languages live on stage. the doctor in the back just laughed in his face.
beats.quote: Orgies is better, because it means the thing you’re after more exact.

beats.title: I Put It In The Coffin
beats.modern: stole the gold back off them at two in the morning, then heard somebody on the stairs with nowhere to run. only hiding place in the room was the coffin. so I tucked six thousand dollars in gold under the lid, just past where his hands was crossed, which was cold enough to make me creep. then Mary Jane came in and knelt down and cried over the box with the money in it, and I slid out behind the door.

beats.title: Digging Him Up In A Thunderstorm
beats.modern: real brothers showed up, nobody could prove anything, so the whole town marched us to the graveyard at nine at night to check the dead man's tattoo. rain, lightning, a hundred shovels, nobody brought a lantern. they get the lid off and a flash lights the hole and a man screams there's the bag of gold on his breast. the guy holding my wrist let go to look. I have never run like that in my life.
beats.quote: “By the living jingo, here’s the bag of gold on his breast!”

beats.title: Forty Dirty Dollars
beats.modern: raft empty. Jim gone. a kid on the road tells me a stranger sold out his chance in him for forty dollars because he had to go upriver and couldn't wait. forty dollars, chat. two hundred was the posted reward and he took forty because he was in a hurry to get drunk. after everything we did for those two. a slave again all his life, amongst strangers, for forty dirty dollars.
beats.quote: Think o’ that, now! You bet I’d wait, if it was seven year.”

beats.title: All Right Then I'll Go To Hell
beats.modern: wrote the letter turning him in. felt washed clean for the first time in my life. then I sat there thinking about the trip. him standing my watch on top of his own so I could sleep. how glad he was when I came back out of the fog. calling me honey. saying I was the only friend old Jim has got. then I looked at that paper, and I knew I was deciding forever. all right then, I will go to hell. and tore it up.
beats.quote: “All right, then, I’ll go to hell”—and

beats.title: Anybody Hurt? No'm.
beats.modern: walked onto a farm hunting Jim and a woman ran out, hugged me, and called me Tom. so I'm Tom now. she asks why the boat was late. I say we blowed out a cylinder-head. she says good gracious, anybody hurt? and I say no ma'am. it only killed a Black man. and she says well, it's lucky, because sometimes people do get hurt. that's the whole country right there, chat. that's the river I've been floating down.

beats.title: I'll Help You Steal Him
