beats.modern: I'm hiding in the shingles listening to thirteen grown men when one grabs my leg and yells there's a snake here as big as a cow. they drag me out. plan A: throw me overboard. plan B: PAINT ME SKY BLUE and then throw me overboard. so I panic and give the fake name of the dead baby from the ghost story they just told. entire raft loses it. laughing saved my life.
beats.quote: 'Charles William Allbright, sir.'

beats.title: Steamboat A-Comin'
beats.modern: our whole town has one dream job and it's steamboatman. the village is DEAD all day: pigs on the sidewalk, clerks asleep in chairs, town drunk passed out by the skids. then somebody spots smoke on the point and yells and the corpse gets up. everybody sprints to the wharf. ten minutes of chaos, boat leaves, town flatlines again. this is our entire content schedule. one boat a day.
beats.quote: 'S-t-e-a-m-boat a-comin'!'

beats.title: The Kid Who Got The Job
beats.modern: one of our boys got hired on a boat and became instantly insufferable. finds a rusty bolt to scrub every time he docks, sits where we can all watch. drops boat jargon like we're too dumb to follow. has hair oil. has a WATCH. every girl in town folded immediately. then his boat blew up and honestly the mood improved for a week, and then he came home bandaged and famous and we had to admit the universe plays favorites.

beats.title: The Amazon Plan
beats.modern: new arc: I read that the government didn't finish exploring the Amazon, so I'm going to go finish it. myself. I have thirty dollars. it's fifteen hundred miles to New Orleans where I'll simply obtain a ship somehow. that is the entire plan. that's it. that's the whole thing. I have never been strong on the details part.
beats.quote: I had thirty dollars left; I would go and complete the exploration of the Amazon.

beats.title: Tell Me Where It Is
beats.modern: trying to get in with the giant tattooed mate so I volunteer to fetch him a capstan bar. he stops swearing. full system crash. stares at me for ten seconds straight while his brain reboots, then goes 'well, if this don't beat hell!' and walks off like I'm an unsolvable math problem. did not go to dinner. did not go to supper. touched grass alone for the rest of the day.
beats.quote: 'Well, if this don't beat hell!'

beats.title: I Signed The Contract
beats.modern: okay pivot. sieged this pilot for three days straight until he cracked and agreed to teach me twelve hundred miles of river for five hundred dollars, payable out of wages I do not have yet. signed it with the easy confidence of a man who thinks the job is 'keep boat in water.' it's wide. how hard can it be. chat if I'd known what I was agreeing to I'd never have started.
beats.quote: He agreed to teach me the Mississippi River from New Orleans to St. Louis for five hundred dollars,

beats.title: Peel An Apple
beats.modern: first time at the wheel and Bixby goes shave those steamships as close as you'd peel an apple. so I clawed us away to a safe margin like a sane person and got yanked off the wheel in disgrace and verbally skinned for cowardice. he then drives within a paint layer of every hull in the line, whistling. new personal rule: I will only pilot downstream, forever, and let brave men do the other direction.
beats.quote: 'Here, take her; shave those steamships as close as you'd peel an apple.'

beats.title: Boats Run All Night
beats.modern: went to bed. midnight, lantern in my face, watchman says turn out. I told him to stop bothering me and went back to sleep. chat. CHAT. I did not know that boats run all night. I knew they ran all night, I had simply never connected that to a human being getting out of a warm bed to do it. off-watch is offering me sugar in a rag. piloting is a JOB. horrifying discovery.
beats.quote: 'Come! turn out!'

beats.title: Pilot A Cow Down A Lane
beats.modern: pop quiz at midnight. name the first point above New Orleans. don't know. the next one. don't know. name ANY point I told you. cannot. he asks what I do know and I said nothing, for certain, which was the honest answer and the wrong one. got called the stupidest dunderhead he has ever encountered, so help him Moses, and informed that I don't know enough to pilot a cow down a lane.
beats.quote: You're the stupidest dunderhead I ever saw or ever heard of, so help me Moses!

beats.title: He Found The Plantation
beats.modern: it is pitch black. no stars. I cannot see the shore, I cannot see my hands, I am privately betting my life savings this man cannot find one specific plantation in this void. he rings the bell. nose touches land. a voice on the bank says gimme the carpet-bag, Mars' Jones. it was Jones's plantation. I decided it was pure luck that could never happen again. I believed that. I fully believed that.

beats.title: Hat Island At Night
beats.modern: engines off. drifting. eight pilots standing shoulder to shoulder behind Bixby in total silence and nobody is breathing. leadsman counting down: eight and a half, eight feet, seven and a half, six— we TOUCH BOTTOM. he screams for every ounce of steam, snatch her, snatch her, and she grinds through the sand and hangs on the edge of disaster for one entire second and then she's OVER. the roof nearly came off that pilot-house.
beats.quote: 'By the Shadow of Death, but he's a lightning pilot!'

beats.title: Learn Him Or Kill Him
beats.modern: new requirement dropped: memorize the exact depth and the exact marks at the shallowest point of all five hundred shoal places between St. Louis and New Orleans. every trip. and don't mix up trips, because they're never twice the same. I said when I can do that I'll be raising the dead for a living instead. he said drop that. he said when I say I'll teach a man the river I'll learn him or kill him.
beats.quote: And you can depend on it, I'll learn him or kill him.'

beats.title: Run Over It
beats.modern: left me alone at the wheel, hid behind a chimney to watch. I see a reef across the bows. I flee. it FOLLOWS me. I ring every bell on the boat and we climb a tree while passengers scatter like rats. he strolls in with a toothpick and fixes it in four words. then tells me to run straight over the reef. I said if I don't I wish I may die. we slid over it like oil. it was wind.

beats.title: The Sunset Costs Extra
beats.modern: here's what nobody tells you about mastering something. I used to watch the river turn to blood and gold at sunset and stand there speechless. now that same sunset reads as: wind tomorrow, floating log means rising water, that slanting mark is a reef that will kill somebody's boat. the whole thing is instrument readings now. I gained the river and lost the river. sometimes I wonder which side of that trade I'm on.
beats.quote: All the grace, the beauty, the poetry had gone out of the majestic river!

beats.title: The Sleepwalking Pilot
beats.modern: pilot X takes the wheel from Ealer on the worst night of the year and runs Helena crossing like it's noon. threads three reefs, drifts, cracks on steam, perfect. Ealer says it's the sweetest piloting ever done on this river and goes down for coffee. watchman: WHO is at the wheel. they sprint up. nobody there. boat steering herself down the middle of the Mississippi. the man was ASLEEP THE ENTIRE TIME.

beats.title: We Ran Over The Sounding Boat
beats.modern: we're creeping down on the buoy light in total darkness when Thornburg screams that's not the buoy, that's the SOUNDING BOAT. crash. wheel grinds it to matchsticks. two men gone. and then out of the black comes a voice saying I can make it, stand by with a rope, and they haul aboard the one guy I wanted humbled: Tom. cheering everywhere. the girl couldn't get enough of him. loathed her anyway.

beats.title: The Man Who Cannot Forget
beats.modern: steered for a pilot whose memory has no delete key. mention any name and he gives you the man's scar, his boat, the date it grounded, and his first wife's maiden name. he once started a funny story about a DOG. we got the dog's breed, the owner, the owner's family weddings and funerals, the obituary poetry, the hard winter, pork prices, the circus, equatorial Africa, and three sermons. four hours. the dog never came back.

beats.title: Oh Ben If You Love Me
beats.modern: the crossing has no bottom. I know it has no bottom. then Bixby asks how much water is in it in a certain TONE and disappears, and an audience of twenty quietly assembles under me, and my brain constructs dangers out of thin air. by the end I'm screaming into the tube: oh Ben, if you love me, back her. he's standing behind me smiling. the hurricane deck detonated with laughter. I heard that line for MONTHS.
beats.quote: 'Oh, Ben, if you love me, back her!

beats.title: King Without A Keeper
beats.modern: let me explain the flex. kings answer to parliament. parliament answers to voters. editors answer to patrons, preachers answer to the pews, writers answer to everybody. the captain gives five orders while we back out and then his reign is OVER. the moment we're in the river she's mine and the law of the United States says nobody may even suggest otherwise. a pilot was the only completely free human being on earth.
beats.quote: a pilot, in those days, was the only unfettered and entirely independent human being that lived in the earth.

beats.title: Trifling Investment Of Fact
beats.modern: okay so the river has shortened itself 242 miles in 176 years, average one and a third miles a year. run the math backwards and a million years ago the Lower Mississippi was 1,300,000 miles long and stuck out over the Gulf like a fishing rod. run it forwards and in 742 years Cairo and New Orleans will share a mayor. science is beautiful. massive returns of conjecture on almost no investment of fact.
beats.quote: There is something fascinating about science. One gets such wholesale returns of conjecture out of such a trifling investment of fact.

beats.title: Alphabetical Order
beats.modern: Stephen owes every pilot on this river money and dodges them for a living. he owes young Yates a full month's wages and has been ducking him for so long he started ambushing YATES to apologize about it. today he gathers the whole billiard room, says he owes maybe forty thousand dollars, says he has finally found a method to pay every last cent. hope in Yates's eyes. then: alphabetical order. and he leaves.
beats.quote: 'I am going to pay them off in alphabetical order!'

beats.title: Where'd You Get Them Shoes
beats.modern: new boss. Brown. walks me through his onboarding process: stares at me for a quarter of an hour, asks if I'm Bigsby's cub, asks where I was born, and when I say Missouri says I'd have been better off staying there. then asks where I got my shoes. makes me HOLD UP MY FOOT. inspects it, scratches his head, says well I'll be dod derned, and goes back to the wheel. I still don't know what that was about.
beats.quote: 'Where'd you get them shoes?'

beats.title: I Kill Brown Every Night
beats.modern: legally I can't touch a pilot on duty. federal offense. so instead of going over the river in my head at bedtime like a good student, I kill Brown. every night. for months. and not lazily, chat, not the same way twice: fresh designs, new environments, escalating ghastliness. it's the only assignment I've ever been ahead on.
beats.quote: I killed Brown every night for months;

beats.title: The Stool
beats.modern: Brown calls my little brother a liar in front of me. I said you lie, yourself. he orders Henry out, then grabs a ten-pound lump of coal and goes after him, and I got between them with a heavy stool and laid him out. then, since I was already going to prison, I kept going with my fists for a while. meanwhile: nobody at the wheel, steamboat doing fifteen miles an hour down the river.

beats.title: I'm Deuced Glad Of It
beats.modern: captain closes both doors. asks did I strike first. yes sir. with what. a stool, sir. hard? middling. did it knock him down. he fell, sir. did I follow it up. yes sir. pounded him? one might call it that. long pause. then: I'm deuced glad of it, never repeat that I said it, you have committed a great crime, don't do it again on this boat — but lay for him ASHORE and I'll pay the expenses.
beats.quote: 'I'm deuced glad of it! Hark ye, never mention that I said that.

beats.title: The Night Before
beats.modern: Brown won't sail with me anymore so the captain puts me on a different boat, the Lacey, two days behind. last night Henry and I sat on a freight pile on the levee till midnight talking about, of all subjects, steamboat disasters. we agreed that if we ever got caught in one we'd stay with the boat and help. the water that would make the steam that would do it was fifteen hundred miles upriver while we talked. Henry remembered that promise.

beats.title: The Barber's Chair
beats.modern: the captain was in the barber's chair getting shaved. the explosion took the entire floor in front of him and left the chair sitting on the edge of nothing. he is unhurt. the barber is unhurt. the barber is standing with one toe hanging over open space, still stirring the lather, still saying absolutely nothing.

beats.title: Ealer Went Back For His Flute
beats.modern: Ealer saw the chimneys going up in front of him and knew exactly what it was, so he buried his face in his coat lapels and clamped both hands over it — because everyone who breathed that steam died, all of them, no exceptions. he had time. he was in the air. lands forty feet down on the unexploded boilers. then, once the steam cleared, he climbed back up and patiently collected every one of his chessmen and all the joints of his flute.

beats.title: Henry Swam Back
beats.modern: Henry was thrown clear into the river with Mr. Wood and they struck out for shore, only a few hundred yards. then Henry said he believed he wasn't hurt, and so he was going to swim back to the burning boat to help save the wounded. he wasn't unhurt. he was not remotely unhurt. they parted, and Henry returned.

beats.title: The Death Room
beats.modern: forty of them on pallets in a public hall in Memphis, every face packed in raw cotton. I watched there six days and six nights. once a day they carry someone out to a separate room, quietly, hidden behind a wall of assistants, and everybody knows exactly what it means and a shudder goes along the row like a wave. on the sixth evening his fingers started picking at the coverlet. his hour had struck. we carried my brother out.
beats.quote: His hour had struck; we bore him to the death-room, poor boy.

beats.title: Then The War Came
beats.modern: got my license. full pilot. I assumed I'd run this river until I died at the wheel with my mission finished. then the war came, the trade stopped, and the job simply ceased to exist. so: silver miner in Nevada, reporter, gold miner in California, reporter again, correspondent in the Sandwich Islands, correspondent in Europe, lecturer, and finally a man who writes books. twenty-one years, disposed of in one sentence.
beats.quote: But by and by the war came, commerce was suspended, my occupation was gone.

beats.title: Traveling Under An Alias
beats.modern: comeback tour, twenty-one years later, and I'm going incognito because rivermen feed beautiful lies to strangers and boring facts to friends. picked a fake name. immediately could not remember it. the hotel clerk took one look and told me he used to work in New York and knew exactly who I was. bagged in the lobby. imposters lecture under my name all over this country and nobody blinks. honest man tries one fraud and he's made instantly.

beats.title: The Levee Is A Graveyard
beats.modern: the change that gutted me was the levee. half a dozen boats asleep where there used to be a solid mile of them awake. a mile of empty wharf, no drays, no freight mountains, no shouting. the whole steamboat aristocracy just gone, absorbed into the crowd, grinding at the mill. steamboating was born about 1812, was enormous within thirty years, and was dead in under thirty more. a strangely short life for something that big.
beats.quote: Half a dozen sound-asleep steamboats where I used to see a solid mile of wide-awake ones!

beats.title: Alligator Boats
beats.modern: pilot doesn't recognize me so he's loading the tourist up. points at a dredge and says casually that's an alligator boat. for dredging out alligators. explains the alligator reefs, which shift constantly and can't be read like a wind reef, and lists the elite pilots who could SMELL good alligator water at fifteen hundred a month. says once you dredge an alligator he's convinced, he never comes back. also all government shoes are made of alligator hide, obviously.
beats.quote: 'To dredge out alligators with.'

beats.title: Take Her And Lie A While
beats.modern: I kept poking holes in his story until the timeline collapsed — the boat sank twice, it was daybreak and dark as Egypt, the moon rose instead of the sun — and he finally steps back from the wheel, wipes the sweat off, and says: here, YOU take her and lie a while, you're handier at it than I am. he'd clocked me inside seven words and let me run the whole bit to see what I was after. incognito: dead. six hours out of St. Louis.

beats.title: Rats To Your Holes
beats.modern: Vicksburg, six weeks of siege. twenty-seven thousand soldiers and three thousand civilians walled in, no mail, no boats, flour two hundred dollars a barrel. three in the morning, silence so complete you can hear one sentry's boots — and then the sky fills with crossing red lines and iron rains down on empty streets. the streets aren't empty a second later: women and children sprinting for caves in the clay while the soldiers shout rats, to your holes, and laugh.
beats.quote: 'Rats, to your holes!'

beats.title: The Gold Dust Follows Up
beats.modern: three months after I rode her, while I'm literally writing these chapters, the papers bring it: the Gold Dust exploded her boilers just outside Hickman. seventeen dead, forty-seven scalded. we wired for news. Lem Gray, the pilot, hurt but improving. then improving less. then a letter came saying he was dead. the river doesn't stop doing this. it just waits until you've stopped watching.

beats.title: The Happiest Man In Town
beats.modern: ran into a guy who used to look old and miserable and now radiates joy. he switched from insurance to undertaking. his pitch, chat: nobody haggles on a coffin. nobody says I'll shop around and come back. nobody downgrades from mahogany. nobody has to be chased for payment. no dull weeks either, because people don't wait for an example to die. he called it the dead-surest business in Christendom and put his hat back on at a jaunty angle.
beats.quote: there's one thing in this world which isn't ever cheap. That's a coffin.

beats.title: The Sir Walter Disease
beats.modern: hot take incoming and I'm not walking it back. the Revolution and Bonaparte at least broke the old chains and stripped the divinity off kings. then Sir Walter Scott shows up with his enchantments and single-handedly turns the whole thing around: sets people in love with sham grandeur, fake chivalry, bogus rank and caste, and the South caught it worst. whitewashed castles. inflated speech. the duel. he did measureless harm.
beats.quote: He did measureless harm; more real and lasting harm, perhaps, than any other individual that ever wrote.

beats.title: Where The Name Came From
beats.modern: lore drop, chat. old Captain Sellers used to publish little river notes in the Picayune signed Mark Twain. I was a cub. I burlesqued one of them a thousand words long and the pilots rushed it into print and it was funny and it went deep into a good man's heart. he never printed another paragraph and never signed that name again. he detested me until he died. and when the news of his death reached me on the Pacific coast I took the name he'd thrown away.
beats.quote: so I confiscated the ancient mariner's discarded one,

beats.title: Roll Call In Hannibal
beats.modern: back in my hometown, asking an old man what happened to everybody. the smartest boy in school: died defeated in the Territories. the brightest one: went to the dogs. the cheeriest boy alive: drink, gambling, Mexico, died without a cent for a shroud. my early sweetheart: three marriages, two buried, one divorce. one girl: died in the asylum after thirty-six years, put there by a prank. and for name after name after name, the same four words.
beats.quote: 'Killed in the war.'

beats.title: I Asked About Myself
beats.modern: so at the end of the roll call I asked the old man about one more local boy. me. verdict: oh, he did well enough — another case of damned fool, and if they'd shipped him to St. Louis he'd have succeeded quicker. chat I have never been so pleased with a decision in my life as I was right then about having told this extremely candid gentleman that my name was Smith.
beats.quote: 'Oh, he succeeded well enough--another case of damned fool.

beats.title: The Carpenter's Confession
beats.modern: my childhood hero was a carpenter who sighed over his plane and muttered things like O God, it is his blood. eventually he swore me to secrecy and confessed he was a red-handed murderer: thirty lives, all with the bowie knife he then produced. I spent an entire summer of Saturdays collecting fresh murders. names, dates, places, every quarter of the globe. it took me sixty confessions to notice that every single victim was named Lynch.
beats.quote: 'Look--with these hands I have taken the lives of thirty human beings!'

beats.title: Westward The Jug
beats.modern: final theory of civilization, and it holds every time. the first thing to arrive is never the steamboat or the railroad or the newspaper or the missionary. it's whiskey. then the missionary, then the immigrant with an ax, then the trader, then the gambler and the highwayman, then the smart man with an old land grant, which brings lawyers, and the vigilance committee brings the undertaker. then papers, politics, a railroad, a church and a jail. civilization, established.
beats.quote: Westward the Jug of Empire takes its way.

beats.title: Stream's Over
beats.modern: and that's the river, top to bottom and back up again: the boy who wanted to be a steamboatman, the cub who couldn't name one point, the pilot who was the freest man alive, the brother I carried out of a hall in Memphis, and a levee full of sleeping boats where a mile of them used to shout. home trail now. through Chicago, which is never the Chicago you last saw. five thousand miles. best trip I ever made. gg.

beats.title: Best Server, Worst Server
beats.modern: chat I'm covering two cities at once and I need you to understand the state of the patch. best of times. worst of times. age of wisdom, age of foolishness. everyone's going straight to heaven, everyone's going straight the other way. I'm not being cute. that is literally the year. 1775 is running two opposite realities on the same map and every authority insists it's the most of both.
beats.quote: It was the best of times, it was the worst of times,

beats.title: Recalled To Life
beats.modern: a guy on a foaming horse chases the night coach through the fog just to hand a banker one folded note. the note says wait at Dover for the girl. the banker reads it, doesn't explain anything, and sends back three words. RECALLED TO LIFE. that's the whole reply. even the messenger's out there in the mist going, that is a Blazing strange answer.
beats.quote: Jerry, say that my answer was, RECALLED TO LIFE.”

beats.title: Buried How Long
beats.modern: the banker dozes off and starts interviewing a ghost. buried how long. almost eighteen years. you gave up hope? long ago. you know you're being recalled to life? they tell me so. and when he asks, shall I show her to you, the ghost gives him a different answer every single time. wait, it would kill me. take me to her. I don't know her. same man. three answers. none of them okay.
beats.quote: “Buried how long?”

beats.title: The Cask In The Street
beats.modern: a wine cask falls off a cart in the poorest street in Paris and the entire neighbourhood drops to its knees in the mud to drink out of the cracks between the stones. cupped hands. broken mugs. rags squeezed into babies' mouths. people dancing, hugging strangers, toasting each other. it is the happiest these people have been in years and it lasts about nine minutes.

beats.title: BLOOD On The Wall
beats.modern: the wine was red. it stained the hands, the faces, the bare feet, the wooden shoes, the forehead of a woman feeding her baby. and one tall joker in a filthy nightcap dips his finger in the lees and writes one word on the wall. BLOOD. chat that's not a joke, that's a spoiler. remember which street this is. the wine gets spilled here again.
beats.quote: The time was to come, when that wine too would be spilled on the street-stones,

beats.title: One Hundred And Five, North Tower
beats.modern: upstairs over the wine shop there's a white-haired man making shoes in the dark. eighteen years in the Bastille and this is what came out. they ask him his name. he doesn't have one. he says the number of his cell. they ask again. same answer, exactly the same, no feeling in it. that's his name now, chat. that's what a cell does to a person.
beats.quote: “One Hundred and Five, North Tower.”

beats.title: The Lookalike Defense
beats.modern: treason trial, London, five years later. star witness swears on his life it was the defendant he saw. defence goes: look at my learned friend over there. the drunk one who's been staring at the ceiling all day. now take his wig off. ...it's the same face. the entire prosecution gets deleted in one move by a man who wasn't even trying.
beats.quote: Are they very like each other?”

beats.title: Acquitted
beats.modern: hour and a half of nothing. mutton pies, ale, the messenger falls asleep on a bench. then the whole building empties up the stairs at once and a paper comes through the crowd with one word on it. ACQUITTED. and Jerry, who's been running cryptic bank notes all year, goes: you could've just sent 'recalled to life' again, I'd have understood it this time.
beats.quote: Hastily written on the paper was the word “ACQUITTED.”

beats.title: Disappointed Drudge
beats.modern: the lookalike takes the man he just saved out for a drink and spends the whole meal being a dick to him. do you think I like you? no? correct. then, at the door: you think I'm drunk. yeah. then you should know why. 'I am a disappointed drudge, sir. I care for no man on earth, and no man on earth cares for me.' then he goes home, stares in a mirror, and tells his own face he hates it.
beats.quote: I am a disappointed drudge, sir. I care for no man on earth, and no man on earth cares for me.”

beats.title: The Jackal
beats.modern: here's the arrangement nobody talks about. the loud one gets rich in court, and Sydney sits up all night with wet towels wrapped round his head doing the actual work. he's been doing other people's homework since school and never his own. 'you were always somewhere, and I was always nowhere.' smartest man in the building, employed as equipment.
beats.quote: you were always somewhere, and I was always nowhere.”

beats.title: The Jolt At The Fountain
beats.modern: a noble's carriage takes a corner in a narrow street at full speed and there's a small sickening jolt. a tall man picks a bundle up off the stones and lies down in the mud howling over it like an animal. the man in the carriage leans out, mildly annoyed, and asks why the noise. is it his child. yes. it's dead.
beats.quote: Is it his child?”

beats.title: The Coin Comes Back
beats.modern: he throws a gold coin in the mud for the dead kid. throws another to the wine seller for being philosophical about it. drives off like a man who broke a plate and paid for it. then something rings on the carriage floor. the coin. thrown back. he threatens to have the thrower crushed under his wheels and nobody moves, nobody speaks. except one woman, knitting, who looks him full in the face. remember her.
beats.quote: “I would ride over any of you very willingly, and exterminate you from the earth.

beats.title: Drive Him Fast To His Tomb
beats.modern: morning at the chateau. bell ringing, servants running, horses saddled. the Marquis is still in bed. knife driven straight down through his heart into the mattress, and a frill of paper wrapped round the hilt. 'drive him fast to his tomb. this, from Jacques.' the father from the fountain signed it with the name they all share now.
beats.quote: “Drive him fast to his tomb. This, from Jacques.”

beats.title: Two Promises
beats.modern: the nephew is living in London under his mother's name and he asks the old prisoner for his daughter. gets a yes. then starts to say his real name and the doctor physically puts both hands over his own ears. STOP. tell me on your wedding morning, not one day before. that night his daughter hears hammering from his bedroom. the shoemaker's tools are out again.
beats.quote: you shall tell me on your marriage morning. Do you promise?”

beats.title: Any Sacrifice
beats.modern: the drunk one tells her he loves her and then immediately tells her it's useless, he's a heap of ashes, don't try to fix him, this conversation never happened. and then on his way out the door, quiet, no bit, no defence: 'for you, and for any dear to you, I would do anything.' there is a man who would give his life to keep a life she loves beside her. everyone forgets he said it. don't.
beats.quote: For you, and for any dear to you, I would do anything.

beats.title: The Honest Tradesman
beats.modern: the bank's messenger has a night job. his kid, walking at arm's length with a stool between them, asks: dad, what's a Resurrection-Man. 'he's a tradesman.' what's his goods. '...a branch of Scientific goods.' it's bodies, dad. it's people's bodies. and the boy says he wants to do that when he grows up and his father is visibly, genuinely proud.
beats.quote: “What’s his goods, father?”

beats.title: The Knitted Register
beats.modern: in the back room they're deciding who has it coming. the chateau. the whole race. extermination. and someone asks, are we sure the records are safe? no paper, no ink. she knits it. names and crimes, her own stitches, her own symbols, and she never drops a syllable. easier to erase yourself from existence than one letter out of her knitting. chat that's a kill list and it looks like a scarf.
beats.quote: It would be easier for the weakest poltroon that lives, to erase himself from existence, than to erase one letter of his name or crimes from the knitted register of Madame Defarge.”

beats.title: Preparing The Earthquake
beats.modern: her husband's getting tired. says it's taking a long time, might not even land in our lifetime. she doesn't blink. how long does it take to strike a man with lightning? fine. now tell me how long it takes to make and store the lightning. how long to prepare an earthquake. 'but when it is ready, it takes place, and grinds to pieces everything before it.' then she ties a knot like she's strangling a man.
beats.quote: “But when it is ready, it takes place, and grinds to pieces everything before it.

beats.title: Nine Days
beats.modern: the wedding is perfect. the bride leaves for her honeymoon glowing. two hours later the housekeeper meets the banker on the stairs with her hands in the air: he doesn't know me, and is making shoes. nine days. the doctor is gone and there's just a shoemaker in his room who won't look up. and the shoe he's making is a young lady's walking shoe. same one. it's always the same one.
beats.quote: He doesn’t know me, and is making shoes!”

beats.title: Tolerated Furniture
beats.modern: the drunk one asks the husband for the smallest thing anyone has ever asked for. permission to come round sometimes. to be allowed to sit in the corner of their home like an ugly useless chair that nobody looks at, tolerated for old service. he says he'd probably use it four times a year. he just wants to know it exists.
beats.quote: an useless (and I would add, if it were not for the resemblance I detected between you and me, an unornamental) piece of furniture, tolerated for its old service, and taken no notice of.

beats.title: The Bastille
beats.modern: July 1789. the whole quarter is arming itself with anything that has an edge and the wine shop is the eye of it. 'patriots and friends, we are ready! THE BASTILLE!' four hours at a cannon in the smoke, then four more. and his wife turns up with an axe in her hand, a pistol and a knife in her belt, shouting to me, women, we can kill as well as the men.
beats.quote: “What! We can kill as well as the men when the place is taken!”

beats.title: He Came For The Cell
beats.modern: fortress falls. everyone's looting, freeing prisoners, screaming. he grabs a turnkey by the shirt: show me the North Tower. one hundred and five. quick. and in the cell by torchlight, scratched into the stone: A. M. Alexandre Manette. a poor physician. a calendar. then he smashes the stool and the table to splinters, rips the straw bed open, and goes up the chimney with a crowbar. chat he did not come here for the revolution. he came for the paper.
beats.quote: “What is the meaning of One Hundred and Five, North Tower?”

beats.title: The Governor
beats.modern: they drag the governor of the fortress through the streets to be judged and the whole city is a howling mess around him. one figure in it never moves. she stays glued to his side the entire way, calm, pointing out her husband in the crowd, still there when the blows start landing, still there when he drops dead. then she puts her foot on his neck and takes his head off with the knife she'd had ready.
beats.quote: “See, there is my husband!”

beats.title: Old Foulon Is Alive
beats.modern: remember the man who told starving people they could eat grass? he faked his own death. mock funeral, the whole production, buried and mourned. they found him hiding in the countryside and walked him back into Paris alive. the wine shop hears it and the entire quarter is on its feet before the sentence finishes.
beats.quote: “Does everybody here recall old Foulon, who told the famished people that they might eat grass, and who died, and went to Hell?”

beats.title: Grass In His Mouth
beats.modern: they take him down the steps head first, on his knees, on his back, hundreds of hands stuffing grass and straw into his face the whole way while he begs. rope breaks, they catch him. rope breaks again, they catch him again. third one holds. she stood there the entire time and watched him like a cat watching a mouse and never said one word.

beats.title: Fire Rises
beats.modern: the chateau's burning and the rider begs the barracks for help. officers look at the soldiers, soldiers look at the fire, nobody gives an order. 'it must burn.' meanwhile two hundred and fifty villagers stand at the fountain with folded arms going, must be forty feet high, and don't move an inch. then they go home, put candles in every window to light the place up, and ring the church bell for joy.
beats.quote: “It must burn.”

beats.title: The Letter From Gabelle
beats.modern: the old estate manager is in a Paris prison for the crime of having worked for a lord who left. he collected no rent. he cancelled the taxes they couldn't pay. doesn't matter, he acted for an emigrant, and where is that emigrant. so he writes across the sea: I cry in my sleep asking where you are. 'my fault is, that I have been true to you.' be true to me.
beats.quote: My fault is, that I have been true to you.

beats.title: Drawn To The Loadstone Rock
beats.modern: so he sits up on the fourteenth of August and writes two letters he doesn't intend anyone to read until he's gone. lies to his wife's face all day. kisses her, kisses the kid, pretends he'll be back shortly, and walks out with a bag he hid earlier. an aristocrat by blood, riding into France in the year they started killing aristocrats by blood, for one old servant. he's not walking. he's being pulled.

beats.title: In Secret
beats.modern: he doesn't last five minutes in Paris. and the man walking him to prison is the wine seller himself. will you help me. no. will you get one message to my bank, just the address, nothing else. 'I will do nothing for you. my duty is to my country and the People. I am the sworn servant of both, against you.' filed as: in secret. no letters, no visitors, no date. buried alive, same as her father was.
beats.quote: I am the sworn servant of both, against you.

beats.title: The Grindstone
beats.modern: forty or fifty people in the courtyard working a grindstone and everything about them is red. the blades, the sparks, the wine being poured into their mouths, their hands, their eyes. fake eyebrows stuck on their faces. they're murdering the prisoners in the jails right now and this is the queue to get sharp enough to go back in.

beats.title: The Man They Can't Touch
beats.modern: here's the twist nobody saw coming. the old prisoner is now the most protected man in Paris. eighteen years in the Bastille is the best credential in the Republic. prisons open for him, tribunals listen, nobody questions him. one year and three months of walking through the Terror with a steady head because he is going to get his daughter's husband out. and he does. once.

beats.title: The Carmagnole
beats.modern: she stands at the same corner every day for months so he might see her from a window. then five hundred people come round the corner dancing and it's the worst thing she's ever seen. spinning, clutching, tearing at each other's hands and heads in perfect time, a healthy thing turned into this. they dance a ring around her and sweep off screaming. then the snow keeps falling, soft and white, like nothing happened.
beats.quote: No fight could have been half so terrible as this dance.

beats.title: Triumph
beats.modern: acquitted. the exact same crowd that wanted his head puts him in a chair with a red flag over it and carries him home on their shoulders, weeping and kissing him. five more people get condemned to death in the time it takes him to leave the building. and her father, who did this, holds her and says the words he's been climbing out of a grave for eighteen years to say. I have saved him.
beats.quote: I have saved him.”

beats.title: A Knock At The Door
beats.modern: same night. four men at the door with a warrant. arrested again, tomorrow's list. the doctor demands to know who denounced him. answer: the Defarges. 'and by one other.' who. and the man from Saint Antoine gets this strange look and says, do YOU ask, Citizen Doctor? you'll be answered tomorrow. now I'm dumb. chat. CHAT. he is looking right at him.
beats.quote: he is denounced--and gravely--by the Citizen and Citizeness Defarge. And by one other.”

beats.title: A Hand At Cards
beats.modern: the drunk one finally sobers up and sits down opposite a prison spy like it's a card table. card one: you're using a false name. card two: you used to work for the English government. card three: therefore, obviously, you still do, and everyone in this city is hunting exactly that man. 'I play my Ace. Denunciation of Mr Barsad to the nearest Section Committee.' look at your hand. don't hurry.
beats.quote: “I play my Ace, Denunciation of Mr. Barsad to the nearest Section Committee.

beats.title: Resurrection And The Life
beats.modern: he walks Paris all night by himself and the words from his father's funeral keep arriving on their own. I am the resurrection and the life. sixty-three people went under the blade today, tomorrow's are already in their cells, and the day after that's. he stops by the river and watches a little eddy turning and turning and going nowhere until the current takes it out to sea. 'like me.'
beats.quote: “I am the resurrection and the life, saith the Lord: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live:

beats.title: The Doctor Signs It
beats.modern: last line of the letter: them and their descendants, to the last of their race, I, Alexandre Manette, denounce to Heaven and to earth. the courtroom makes a sound with nothing in it but blood. because the man in the dock IS the last of that race, and the man who wrote his death sentence is his wife's father, from a cell, in 1767. and she turns to the room smiling. save him now, my Doctor. save him. unanimous. death in twenty-four hours.
beats.quote: “Save him now, my Doctor, save him!”

beats.title: That Family Is My Family
beats.modern: why her. why is this one woman so completely locked in. because the peasant family in that letter is HERS. the dying boy was her brother. the ruined girl was her sister. that father was her father, those dead are her dead, and the summons to answer for it came down to her. she's been knitting toward this since before anyone knew her name. her husband suggests maybe stopping. 'tell the Wind and the Fire where to stop; not me.'
beats.quote: “Tell the Wind and the Fire where to stop; not me!”

beats.title: The Swap
beats.modern: cell, twenty-four hours on the clock, and Sydney walks in past a turnkey he owns now. boots off. take mine. coat, cravat, ribbon out of your hair, shake it loose like mine. write what I dictate. 'it would be madness if I asked you to escape. but do I?' the pen stops. what's that vapour. nothing, there's nothing here, write faster. and the two identical faces change places.
beats.quote: “It would be madness if I asked you to escape; but do I?

beats.title: My Poor Sister
beats.modern: a girl in the holding room comes over and asks to hold his hand in the cart because she's little and weak and it would give her courage. then she looks at his face properly and stops. 'are you dying for him?' 'and his wife and child. hush. yes.' 'oh, you'll let me hold your brave hand, stranger?' 'hush. yes, my poor sister. to the last.'
beats.quote: “Are you dying for him?”

beats.title: Fifty-Two
beats.modern: the coach out of Paris, one drugged sleeping passenger with the wrong papers and the right face. guard shouts across at the last post: how many to the guillotine today? fifty-two. 'I said so! a brave number! I love it. hi forward!' and the coach runs, and the wind is rushing after us, and the clouds are flying after us, and the whole wild night is in pursuit of us. and so far, nothing else is.
beats.quote: The wind is rushing after us, and the clouds are flying after us, and the moon is plunging after us, and the whole wild night is in pursuit of us;

beats.title: Pross Versus Defarge
beats.modern: a housekeeper and the knitting woman alone in an empty flat. neither speaks one word of the other's language and they understand each other perfectly. one is buying minutes. the other wants what's behind that door. so she grabs her round the waist and lifts her clean off the floor: I am stronger than you, I hold you till one or other of us faints or dies. hands go for a pistol. flash, crash. love wins by simply not letting go, and the woman who won never hears another sound again.
beats.quote: I am stronger than you, I bless Heaven for it. I hold you till one or other of us faints or dies!”

beats.title: Twenty-Two
beats.modern: the cart. she asks him one last thing and apologises for being ignorant. she has a cousin in the country who'll never know what happened to her. if the Republic really does make the poor less hungry, that cousin might live to be old. will the waiting feel long to me? 'there is no Time there, and no trouble there.' they bless each other. she goes first. the knitting women count twenty-two.
beats.quote: “It cannot be, my child; there is no Time there, and no trouble there.”

beats.title: A Far, Far Better Thing
beats.modern: twenty-three. they said afterward it was the most peaceful face anyone in that city ever saw. and if he'd spoken what he was thinking, it was this: I see her grown old, crying for me on this day every year. I see a boy with my name and a forehead I know being told my story in a faltering voice. 'it is a far, far better thing that I do, than I have ever done; it is a far, far better rest that I go to than I have ever known.' he never told anyone. clip ends.
beats.quote: “It is a far, far better thing that I do, than I have ever done; it is a far, far better rest that I go to than I have ever known.”

beats.title: The Guy On The Couch
beats.modern: showed up to get painted and there's a stranger lying on the couch chain-smoking. thirty seconds in he's roasting his own aunt's piano playing to my face. chat I have never met a man this comfortable. Basil is openly begging him to leave. he is not leaving.

beats.title: All Influence Is Immoral
beats.modern: he says there's no such thing as a good influence. that virtue is just borrowed. that everyone alive is terrified of themselves. and then the finisher: the only way to get rid of a temptation is to lose to it. chat I stood there ten minutes not moving. a man just uninstalled my personality in front of my own portrait.
beats.quote: The only way to get rid of a temptation is to yield to it.

beats.title: The Countdown Timer
beats.modern: he says I've got a few years of being like this and then it's over. sallow. hollow-cheeked. dull-eyed. no triumphs left, just the memory of them, which is worse. chat he read out the patch notes for the nerf coming to my own face. I had never once thought about it before today and now it's the only thing in my head.
beats.quote: Youth! Youth! There is absolutely nothing in the world but youth!”

beats.title: I Would Give My Soul
beats.modern: the painting's finished and it's perfect and it stays like that forever and I don't. so I said it out loud with two witnesses in the room: let the picture go old, let me stay. I'd give everything. I'd give my soul for it. chat nobody flinched. they laughed and rang for tea.
beats.quote: I would give my soul for that!”

beats.title: Don't Touch The Canvas
beats.modern: Basil grabbed a palette knife to shred the thing because he thinks it's poisoning all three of us. I got there first, ripped it out of his hand and threw it across the studio screaming that it would be murder. he thinks I finally respect his art. chat that is not what happened. I'm in love with it.
beats.quote: “It would be murder!”

beats.title: The Girl In The Cheap Theatre
beats.modern: wandered east into a nowhere theatre with flaring gas jets and a guinea box seat. the scenery is a wedding cake, the Romeo is a beer barrel with drawn-on eyebrows, and then Juliet walks out. seventeen. voice like a violin deciding to hurt you. chat I could not see her for tears. I'm going back tomorrow. and the night after.

beats.title: She Named Me
beats.modern: went backstage. she's shy, she's tiny, she has no idea she's the most talented person in that building. the manager keeps calling me My Lord so I told her I'm nobody at all. she just looked up at me and said: you look more like a prince. I'll call you Prince Charming. chat write that name down. you'll need it.

beats.title: Juliet Falls Off
beats.modern: brought my two best friends to watch her and she is DREADFUL. flat, stagey, reciting like a kid at a school assembly. the pit starts whistling. Harry's putting his coat on. chat I hyped this girl for a month, I paid for the box, and she was a complete failure in front of the only two people whose opinion I wanted.
beats.quote: It was simply bad art. She was a complete failure.

beats.title: She Says I Cured Her
beats.modern: she comes offstage GLOWING. says she was bad on purpose, sort of: knowing me made the fake love unbearable, the painted moonlight looks like a lie now, she's sick of shadows. she wants me to take her away. chat she thinks she just handed me a gift. she's telling me she deleted the only part of her I was in love with.
beats.quote: I have grown sick of shadows.

beats.title: You Killed My Love
beats.modern: so I said it. you've killed my love. you were the art and without the art you're nothing, you're a third-rate actress with a pretty face. she's on the floor at my feet asking me to kiss her once more. I told her not to touch me and I left. chat I felt nothing walking out of that building. remember that for later.
beats.quote: A third-rate actress with a pretty face.”

beats.title: The Mouth Moved
beats.modern: got home at dawn. walked past the portrait, stopped, walked back. chat there is a line of cruelty round the mouth that was not there yesterday. I grabbed a hand mirror and checked. my face is perfect. his isn't.

beats.title: Harry Sat Down First
beats.modern: he came in, crossed the room, sat next to me and took both my hands, which he has never done in his life. then he told me Sibyl is dead. last night. after I walked out. chat his very next sentence was asking whether anyone at that theatre knows my name.
beats.quote: “Dead! Sibyl dead! It is not true! It is a horrible lie!

beats.title: The Roses Are Fine
beats.modern: so I murdered her. same as if I'd cut her throat with a knife. and chat here's the part I can only say to you: the roses in my garden look exactly as good as they did yesterday. the birds are going at it. and I'm dining out at eight.
beats.quote: Yet the roses are not less lovely for all that.

beats.title: The Old Schoolroom
beats.modern: got the key to the room I did lessons in as a kid, the one my grandfather kept me shut away in because I looked too much like my mother. carried the portrait up there wrapped in a cloth that has definitely covered a corpse before. it can rot in the dark. chat nobody has that key but me.

beats.title: The Book Harry Sent
beats.modern: yellow paper, no plot, one character: some Parisian working through every sin every century ever invented. read it until the light died and my valet gave up reminding me of the time. chat I told Harry I never said I liked it. I said it fascinated me. those are different words. I've ordered nine more copies in nine colours.
beats.quote: It was a poisonous book.

beats.title: The Room Goes Quiet
beats.modern: years of this now. men stand up and walk out of the smoking room when I come in. I nearly got blackballed from a club my own name built. women who torched their reputations for me go white when I enter. chat nobody can prove a thing because the proof is in an attic under a purple cloth, and I still look twenty.

beats.title: Basil Read The List
beats.modern: Basil turned up at midnight with a LIST. why does Berwick leave a room when you enter it. what about the boy in the Guards. Ashton. Kent's son. Perth. Adrian Singleton. chat he stood in my library and read me my own body count like a receipt and asked why my friendship is fatal to young men.

beats.title: You Want The Tour
beats.modern: he says he'd have to see my soul to really know me. chat. CHAT. he said the one thing you must never say in this house. so I picked up a lamp and told him fine, come upstairs, you made it, come and look at corruption face to face. he thinks I'm being poetic. he's about to learn I'm being literal.
beats.quote: You have chattered enough about corruption. Now you shall look on it face to face.”

beats.title: He Knows His Own Brushwork
beats.modern: tore the curtain off the thing and he made a sound I have never heard a human being make. then he goes hunting for the trick with a candle, checking the surface, checking the frame he designed himself. and there in the left corner is his own name in bright red where he put it. chat you can't argue with your own signature.

beats.title: The Face Of A Satyr
beats.modern: he's saying there was nothing evil in it, that this is the face of a satyr, that it has the eyes of a devil, that Christ, what a thing he must have worshipped. so I told him what it actually is. it's the face of my soul, Basil. each of us has heaven and hell in him. chat now he wants us to kneel down and pray together.
beats.quote: “It is the face of my soul.”

beats.title: The Knife On The Chest
beats.modern: he's praying AT me now. and the thing on the canvas is grinning like it's whispering instructions. there's a knife on the painted chest from weeks ago when I cut a piece of cord and never took it back down. chat I moved behind him and I did it and I kept doing it and then the room was silent except for something dripping onto the carpet.

beats.title: A Matter Of Life And Death
beats.modern: sent for Alan Campbell, who used to be my friend and now can't stand the sight of me. told him flat: there's a dead man sitting at a table at the top of this house, and your job is chemistry. turn him into a handful of ashes I can throw in the air. he said no. he said absolutely not. chat I'm not finished.

beats.title: The Paper Across The Table
beats.modern: so I took a piece of paper, wrote something on it, read it over twice, folded it and pushed it across the table. said nothing. watched his face go grey and his whole body drop back into the chair. chat I don't even have to tell you what's on it. he's doing it now. he was stern with me an hour ago. I dictate terms now.

beats.title: Five Hours And Acid
beats.modern: he came down after seven. pale, completely calm, said he'd done what I asked and that we should never see each other again. I went up. the room reeks of nitric acid and the thing that was sitting at that table is not there anymore. chat there is now no evidence anywhere in the world that Basil Hallward ever came to my house.

beats.title: Somebody Said The Name
beats.modern: down at the docks trying to buy oblivion, and a woman I paid to leave me alone screams Prince Charming at my back as I'm going out the door. chat a sailor who'd been face down on a table all night came up out of that chair like he'd been shot and went straight after me.

beats.title: Eighteen Years
beats.modern: hand on my throat in a dark archway, revolver against my head. he's Sibyl's brother. he's hunted me for years with nothing but a pet name to go on, and he's giving me one minute to make peace with God. so I asked when she died. eighteen years ago, he says. chat I told him to drag me under the lamp and LOOK at my face.
beats.quote: “Eighteen years! Set me under the lamp and look at my face!”

beats.title: Something At The Glass
beats.modern: house party, everyone laughing, Harry fencing with the duchess over nothing. I went to the end of the conservatory to cut her some orchids, looked up, and there was a white face pressed flat against the window watching me. chat I woke up on the tiles with the whole party standing over me. he found me.

beats.title: Don't Shoot It Geoffrey
beats.modern: a hare breaks cover and something about how it moved made me shout at him to leave it alone. he laughed at me and fired anyway. chat there were two screams out of that thicket. one of them was the hare.
beats.quote: There were two cries heard, the cry of a hare in pain, which is dreadful, the cry of a man in agony, which is worse.

beats.title: Under The Handkerchief
beats.modern: they laid him out on sacking in an empty stable because nobody wants a corpse in the house. I could not lift the cloth myself, made a farmhand do it. it's the sailor. it's her brother. chat I cried the whole ride home. from relief. the man hunting me walked in front of a gun by accident and I am safe.

beats.title: The Girl In The Orchard
beats.modern: I did a good thing. village girl, looked like Sibyl, laughing in an orchard with apple blossom falling in her hair. we were going to run off together at dawn and I let her go instead, left her exactly as flowerlike as I found her. chat I told Harry over strawberries and he said, without looking up: so you gave her good advice and broke her heart.

beats.title: I Told Him And He Laughed
beats.modern: asked him straight across the table: what would you say if I told you I murdered Basil. he said I was posing for a role that doesn't suit me. that all crime is vulgar and it simply isn't in me to do it. chat I confessed to my best friend and he told me I wasn't interesting enough to have done it.
beats.quote: It is not in you, Dorian, to commit a murder.

beats.title: The Street Preacher's Question
beats.modern: Harry heard some preacher in the rain yelling about gaining the whole world and losing your soul, and he brings it to me at the piano like a party trick. the music went wrong under my hands. I told him the soul is real, it can be bought and sold and bartered away. he told me anything you're certain of is never true.
beats.quote: The soul is a terrible reality. It can be bought, and sold, and bartered away.

beats.title: I Broke The Mirror
beats.modern: picked up the little mirror Harry gave me a lifetime ago and remembered a letter someone wrote me once, about how the curves of my lips rewrite history. then I put it on the floor and crushed it under my heel. chat my face was never a gift. it was a mask, and the youth was a joke, and it is the thing that ruined me.

beats.title: Checking For Improvement
beats.modern: went up to see if sparing the girl had cleaned anything off it. it hasn't. there's cunning in the eyes now and a hypocrite's wrinkle at the mouth, and MORE red on the hand, wet-looking, like it's fresh. chat I sat there and did the maths honestly for the first time in my life. vanity. curiosity. me acting the part of a good man. that's the whole of it.

beats.title: It Had Been Conscience
beats.modern: one piece of evidence left in the entire world and it's hanging in front of me. the knife's still up here, cleaned so many times there's not a mark on it, bright and shining. it killed the painter so it can kill the painting. kill the past and I'm free. chat I know exactly what this thing has been to me all these years. so I'm putting a knife in it.
beats.quote: It had been like conscience to him. Yes, it had been conscience.

beats.title: They Checked The Rings
beats.modern: one scream out of that room and a crash. the servants wake up. two gentlemen in the square below fetch a policeman, nobody answers the bell, so they go over the roof and in through the old bolts. inside: a portrait of a beautiful young man, flawless, exactly as he always was. and on the floor a withered hideous old stranger with a knife in his heart. they had to check the rings to work out who it was.
beats.quote: Lying on the floor was a dead man, in evening dress, with a knife in his heart.

beats.title: Restless By Design
beats.modern: chat I have tried everything. career, women, books, the whole checklist. nothing holds. and then it lands on me: you built me with a hole shaped like you. that is not a bug. that is the design doc. I have been restless my entire life and it finally makes sense.
beats.quote: our heart is restless, until it repose in Thee.

beats.title: The Book That Wrecked Me
beats.modern: I am eighteen, training to be a professional liar for money, and I pick up a Cicero book purely for the writing tips. did not take the style. took the WHOLE THING. put it down wanting truth more than a career and every plan I had became worthless in one sitting.

beats.title: I Thought The Bible Was Mid
beats.modern: finally opened the scriptures like fine, let us see the fuss. prose felt basic. no flourish. put it down like a critic reviewing a debut. chat it was not the book. the book sits low to the ground on purpose, for people willing to stoop. I was too busy being a great one to be a little one.

beats.title: What Am I Even Looking For
beats.modern: people keep asking what I mean when I say I love God. not a face. not a song. not a smell, not a taste, not a body. zero for five on the senses. and yet there is a light and a voice and a food in me that nothing outside me has ever been able to serve.

beats.title: Too Late Loved I Thee
beats.modern: late. so late. I was out here scanning every beautiful thing on earth for you and you were INSIDE the whole time. I stood outside my own house looking in the windows. you called, you shouted, you broke my deafness. you flashed and my blindness scattered. I touched it and I burned.
beats.quote: Thou wert with me, but I was not with Thee.

beats.title: The Envious Baby
beats.modern: watched a baby who cannot form a word go pale with rage at another baby feeding. milk flowing, plenty for two, and he could not stand it. we call that innocence. it is not innocence, it is short arms. give that one strength and see what he does with it.
beats.quote: The weakness then of infant limbs, not its will, is its innocence.

beats.title: Praying Not To Get Beaten
beats.modern: first prayer of my life, age seven: please do not let them hit me at school today. not answered. got beaten anyway. and the adults LAUGHED about it. grown men call their own idleness business, then flog a boy for playing ball. same disease, bigger budget.

beats.title: The Pear Tree Job
beats.modern: we did not want the pears. they were not even good pears. I had better ones at home. shook the tree at midnight, took the entire haul, threw it to the pigs. tasted maybe one. what sweetened it was the crime. I did not want fruit, chat. I wanted to be bad.
beats.quote: I loved to perish, I loved mine own fault, not that for which I was faulty, but my fault itself.

beats.title: Alone I Never Do It
beats.modern: here is the part that actually scares me. alone, I never would have. not once. the pears were nothing, the theft was nothing, the crew was nothing, and three nothings stacked up made me a thief. nobody laughs alone. turns out nobody steals alone either.

beats.title: Let's Go, Let's Do It
beats.modern: deadliest sentence in any group chat: let us go, let us do it. nobody actually wants the thing. everybody is waiting for one guy to flinch so they can all go home. and we would rather commit the crime than be that guy. we are ashamed of not being shameless.
beats.quote: when it is said, "Let's go, let's do it," we are ashamed not to be shameless.

beats.title: I Lied To My Mother
beats.modern: she would not let me sail unless she came, so I told her I was only seeing a friend off until the wind turned. then I left in the dark. she woke up on an empty shore. she had been asking, every day, on the ground, in tears, for exactly one thing. I took it.

beats.title: Chastity, But Not Yet
beats.modern: prayed for purity at nineteen with an asterisk the size of a house. make me good. LATER. I was genuinely scared he would answer on schedule. I did not want the disease cured, I wanted it fed. most honest fucking prayer I ever prayed and it kept working for twelve more years.
beats.quote: "Give me chastity and continency, only not yet."

beats.title: The Chain I Made Myself
beats.modern: nobody put me in irons. I did it link by link, on stream, in public. want it once. want it often. now it is a habit. now it is not a choice. that is the chain, and I forged every link personally and then complained about the weight.
beats.quote: For of a forward will, was a lust made; and a lust served, became custom; and custom not resisted, became necessity.

beats.title: Two Wills, One Me
beats.modern: there is a new me that wants the good life and an old me with seniority. two wills, both mine, both pulling. they do not cancel out. they tear. people call this being conflicted like it is a personality trait. it is just being ripped in half by yourself.

beats.title: My Hand Obeys, My Mind Doesn't
beats.modern: test this right now. tell your hand to move. it moves instantly, no gap between order and obedience. now tell your MIND to want something. nothing. total insubordination. the mind gives itself an order and gets ignored by itself. I am not fighting an enemy. I am the guy not doing what I say.
beats.quote: The mind commands the mind, its own self, to will, and yet it doth not.

beats.title: The Old Habits Whisper
beats.modern: my old habits did not scream when I tried to leave. worse. they tugged my sleeve from behind and muttered, so that is it forever? never again, not once, not ever? half audible. and then one of them asked the question that nearly ended me: you really think you can live without us?

beats.title: Tomorrow And Tomorrow
beats.modern: ended up face down under a fig tree crying so hard I had to walk away from my friend to do it properly. and all I could get out was how long, how long, tomorrow and tomorrow. why not now. why is there not an end to this in THIS hour. this one. the one happening right now.
beats.quote: How long, how long, "tomorrow, and tomorrow?" Why not now?

beats.title: Take Up And Read
beats.modern: I am on the ground sobbing and a kid's voice starts up next door, singing take up and read, take up and read. no game I know has that chant. so I took it as an order. opened the letters at random, read the first line my eyes hit, stopped. did not need more. the doubt just went out like a light.

beats.title: Crying Over Dido
beats.modern: hardest I ever cried in school was over a queen killing herself in a poem. FICTIONAL WOMAN. meanwhile my actual soul is dying in real time and my eyes are bone dry. I could grieve a character flawlessly and myself not at all. they gave me top marks for it.

beats.title: Why Do We Watch Sad Things
beats.modern: real question chat: why do we queue up content built to hurt us? nobody volunteers for actual grief. but stage it, and we pay, and we call the sting a good night out. I sat in those theatres feeding on other people's misery and told myself it proved I was sensitive.

beats.title: He Swore He Wouldn't Look
beats.modern: my friend got dragged to the arena and said, you can move my body, you cannot make me watch. eyes shut. mind locked. then the crowd roared at a kill and he opened them for ONE second. that was it. he drank it down. shouting, hooked, and within a week he was the one dragging others in.

beats.title: Why We Rubberneck
beats.modern: explain the crash on the shoulder of the road. nobody enjoys a mangled body. we go pale, we lose sleep over it, we are scared to see it again. and we still slow down and look. that is not pleasure. that is a hunger to KNOW, wearing a lab coat.

beats.title: The Lizard And The Spider
beats.modern: I quit the circus. I do not go watch dogs chase hares anymore. then a dog runs past me in a field and my entire train of thought is gone. sitting at home, a lizard picks off flies, a spider wraps one up, and I am just there. gone. it is one thing to get up fast. another thing not to fall.

beats.title: Is It Worship Or The Beat
beats.modern: problem I cannot solve. when the words are sung well I feel it burn, and I cannot tell if that is the truth landing or just good audio. the tune keeps sprinting ahead of the meaning it was hired to serve. I only notice I have sinned after the song ends.

beats.title: The Man Who Read Silently
beats.modern: went to see the bishop and the man was READING WITHOUT MOVING HIS LIPS. eyes gliding down the page, heart working, no sound at all. we stood there. nobody dared interrupt a man that locked in. we watched him read in silence, gave up, and left. every single time.

beats.title: The Speech And The Drunk Guy
beats.modern: walking to deliver a speech full of lies about the emperor, to a room that knows they are lies, and my chest is on fire with nerves. pass a beggar in the street who has had a few and the man is DELIGHTED. he got with pocket change the exact thing I have been scheming years for. he was merry. I was scared.

beats.title: Praise Still Moves Me
beats.modern: would I rather be right and hated, or wrong and adored? right. instantly. no hesitation. and yet a compliment still lifts my whole day and one bad word still lowers it, which means the dial is in other people's hands. every day, same furnace: the tongues of men.
beats.quote: Our daily furnace is the tongue of men.

beats.title: Evil Isn't A Thing
beats.modern: I spent years asking where evil came from like it was a substance with a supplier. it is not. everything that exists is good in the exact amount that it exists, and evil is the rot, the missing piece, the good that got eaten. strip all the good out and there is nothing left to be evil. it is not a thing. it is a hole.

beats.title: The Crying Fig Tree
beats.modern: reminder of what I actually used to believe: that a fig tree WEEPS when you pick it, and that if the right holy man eats the fig, he breathes out angels. divine particles trapped in fruit, released by his digestion. and I thought I was the sceptic in the room. I pitied produce and not hungry people.

beats.title: Blame Venus, Not Me
beats.modern: astrology is not selling you the future. it is selling you an alibi. the cause of your sin was fixed in the sky, says the chart. so I walk free and the one who made the stars takes the charge. very convenient. and I paid money for that verdict.

beats.title: Epicurus Would Have Won
beats.modern: honest receipt from my Epicurus phase: if nothing comes after death, he takes the whole argument, no contest. give me pleasure forever with no fear of losing it and what else would I even ask for. that was my ceiling. I could not see the one beauty that eyes do not pick up.

beats.title: The Palaces Of Memory
beats.modern: went walking through my own memory today and chat, it is HUGE. fields, halls, storerooms with no visible end. everything the senses ever brought home is filed in there, and I call for one and it sprints out, and I call for another and have to go digging for an hour. and that is only what forgetting has not swallowed yet.

beats.title: Remembering Forgetting
beats.modern: small thing quietly breaking my brain: I can remember forgetting. so forgetting is stored IN the memory. but if it is present in there, why am I not holding the thing it erased? and if it is absent, how do I recognise the word the second I hear it. memory is holding the one item whose whole job is losing items.

beats.title: Ask Me What Time Is
beats.modern: what is time? if nobody asks me, I know perfectly. the second someone asks me to explain it, I know nothing. we all say the word fifty times a day. try defining it out loud. the past is not. the future is not yet. and the present only qualifies as time because it is already leaving.
beats.quote: What then is time? If no one asks me, I know:

beats.title: Three Presents
beats.modern: hot take: there are not three times. past and future do not exist anywhere outside your head. what actually exists is three presents. a present of things past, which is memory. a present of things present, which is looking. a present of things future, which is expecting. all three live in the soul. I cannot find them anywhere else.

beats.title: What Was God Doing Before
beats.modern: classic reply guy question: what was God doing before he made the world? there is a joke answer going around, that he was preparing hell for people who ask that. funny. not using it. answering the question and ratioing the asker are two different jobs, and only one of them is honest. the real answer: there was no before. he made time too.
beats.quote: "He was preparing hell (saith he) for pryers into mysteries."

beats.title: I Am A Problem To Myself
beats.modern: here is the confession underneath all the confessions: I do not know myself. there are things about me that I will never have access to. I know what I have survived. I have no idea what would break me tomorrow. so I am posting what I know about me AND what I do not. the second list is longer.

beats.title: My Friend Died
beats.modern: my best friend since we were kids got sick and died in the same week I was still joking with him about it. after that, everything I looked at was death. my hometown turned into a torture device. I asked my own soul why it was so sad and my soul had nothing for me.
beats.quote: At this grief my heart was utterly darkened; and whatever I beheld was death.

beats.title: Half Of My Soul
beats.modern: somebody once called a friend half of my soul and I finally understand the phrase. one soul, two bodies. which is why I was terrified to die AND terrified to live, because living meant living halved, and dying meant the rest of him going too.

beats.title: I Loved Him Like He'd Last
beats.modern: why did losing him level me that completely? because I poured my whole soul out onto sand. I loved a mortal like the warranty was infinite. that is not devotion, that is a maths error, and grief is just the invoice arriving.

beats.title: Son Of These Tears
beats.modern: my mother spent years begging a bishop to come argue me out of my beliefs. he kept refusing, said leave him, he will read his way out. she would not stop asking. finally, a little fed up, he told her: go, it is not possible that the son of these tears should perish. she took that like it came from heaven.
beats.quote: it is not possible that the son of these tears should perish."

beats.title: The Window At Ostia
beats.modern: last real conversation with my mother. the two of us alone, leaning on a windowsill in a port town, waiting on a ship, talking about what forever is actually like. and for one second in the middle of it we touched the thing, both of us, together. then straight back down into sentences with a start and a stop.

beats.title: What Am I Still Doing Here
beats.modern: she said: son, personally, I am done. nothing in this life interests me anymore. the one thing I was staying for was seeing you come home, and I have got that plus more than I asked for. so what am I still doing here? chat she was not being dramatic. she meant it as a genuine scheduling question.

beats.title: I Closed Her Eyes
beats.modern: I closed her eyes. the grief came up like a flood and I ordered my own eyes to hold it, and they obeyed, and they stayed dry. everyone in the room thought I felt nothing. I was fighting a war behind my face and losing quietly.

beats.title: The Bath Didn't Work
beats.modern: somebody told me the word for bath comes from a Greek word about washing sadness out of the mind. so I went. I bathed. chat I came out exactly as sad as I went in. the sorrow would not sweat out of me. then I slept, and woke up, and it was a little lighter. sleep did the thing the bath could not.

the-adventures-of-tom-sawyer.title: The Adventures of Tom Sawyer, Complete
the-adventures-of-tom-sawyer.author: Mark Twain

beats.title: The Jam Situation
beats.modern: caught. jam on both hands, jam on my face, switch already in the air. so I go MY! LOOK BEHIND YOU, AUNT! and she turns. chat. she TURNS. I'm over a nine foot fence before the switch comes down. and the scary part isn't that it worked. the scary part is that it works every single time.
beats.quote: “My! Look behind you, aunt!”

beats.title: The Fence Meta
beats.modern: got sentenced to whitewash thirty yards of fence on a saturday. so instead of grinding it I made it look like the rarest job in town. wouldn't let Ben touch the brush. "does a boy get a chance to whitewash a fence EVERY day?" he paid me his apple for the privilege. chat I have accidentally discovered that if you gatekeep something worthless people will pay you to let them do your chores.
beats.quote: Does a boy get a chance to whitewash a fence every day?”

beats.title: New Girl Just Dropped
beats.modern: new girl in the Thatcher yard. blue eyes, yellow braids down to here. chat Amy Lawrence has been deleted from my heart with no ceremony and no goodbye. took me MONTHS to grind that relationship. gone in one frame. I did handstands at that fence for a solid hour and she walked inside without looking. then she threw a flower over the fence. WE ARE SO BACK.

beats.title: Dead On Her Lawn
beats.modern: new plan: lie down under her window at ten at night holding the wilted flower, perish of exposure, let HER find the body in the morning and carry that forever. hands folded. no shelter over my homeless head. absolutely flawless. then the window goes up and a servant dumps an entire bucket of water on the corpse. chat I got doused by an NPC.

beats.title: Two Thousand Verses
beats.modern: cashed my whitewash loot into sunday school tickets and walked up and demanded the Bible prize like a man with two thousand verses in the bank. huge ceremony. superintendent glowing. the county judge shakes my hand, calls me a fine manly little fellow, asks me to name the first two disciples. chat. I said DAVID AND GOLIAH. out loud. in front of her father.
beats.quote: “David and Goliah!”

beats.title: The Beetle Arc
beats.modern: sermon is dying so I release my pinchbug into the aisle. stray poodle finds it. plays with it. gets bit. plays with it MORE. then forgets it exists and sits directly down on it. that dog went up the aisle screaming like a comet, whole church behind their fans, preacher completely cooked. owner punted it out the window. only complaint: the dog left with my beetle.

beats.title: Mortified
beats.modern: monday. did not want school. so I diagnosed myself out loud with a mortified toe and started groaning until Sid ran for auntie. she came up the stairs WHITE. then she laughed, then she cried, then she told me to climb out of bed. and because I made the mistake of mentioning my loose tooth she tied silk thread to it and the bedpost and shoved fire at my face. tooth's on the bedpost. upside: I can spit in a brand new way and every boy in town is watching me do it.
beats.quote: “Oh, auntie, my sore toe’s mortified!”

beats.title: Huckleberry Finn
beats.modern: every mother in this town hates Huck Finn and every kid in this town wants to BE him. no school. no church. no shoes. sleeps on doorsteps in summer and in empty barrels when it rains. calls nobody master. swears beautifully. I am under strict written orders never to play with him, so obviously I play with him every chance I get.
beats.quote: In a word, everything that goes to make life precious that boy had.

beats.title: Worth The Switching
beats.modern: master asks why I'm late. I scan the room and there is exactly ONE empty seat in this building and it's next to the yellow braids. so I say it nice and loud: I STOPPED TO TALK WITH HUCKLEBERRY FINN. room stops breathing. he beats me until his arm gets tired and the switch supply runs low, and then he says now go and sit with the girls. chat. that was the play. that was ALWAYS the play.
beats.quote: “I stopped to talk with Huckleberry Finn!”

beats.title: The Slate
beats.modern: gave her a peach. drew her a house. drew her a man shaped like a crane. then I wrote something and covered it with my hand and said oh you don't want to see it. she pried my fingers off the slate herself. it said I LOVE YOU. she smacked my hand and went red and looked extremely pleased, and ten seconds later the master lifted me across the room by my ear and I did not care even slightly.
beats.quote: “I love you.”

beats.title: Engaged For Nine Minutes
beats.modern: got her to whisper it back, got the kiss, locked in the terms: never anybody else, ever never and forever. and then, riding the high, I said "why, me and Amy Lawrence—" out loud. with my mouth. chat I watched the whole thing burn down in real time. offered her my brass andiron knob as compensation and she knocked it on the floor.
beats.quote: “Oh, it’s ever so gay! Why, me and Amy Lawrence—”

beats.title: Midnight In The Graveyard
beats.modern: went to the graveyard at midnight with Huck and a dead cat to cure warts. that's it. that was the whole plan. then three men come up the hill with a lantern and start digging up Hoss Williams. the young doctor, Muff Potter, and Injun Joe. money argument turns into a fight, the doctor drops Muff with a headboard, and Joe picks up Muff's own knife and puts it in the doctor's chest. we ran. chat we ran and we did not stop.

beats.title: Signed In Blood
