beats.modern: Huck says a secret this size needs writing AND blood, so I scratched it on a pine shingle in red keel and we each pricked a thumb and signed and buried it by the wall. HUCK FINN AND TOM SAWYER SWEARS THEY WILL KEEP MUM ABOUT THIS AND THEY WISH THEY MAY DROP DOWN DEAD IN THEIR TRACKS IF THEY EVER TELL AND ROT. that's the contract. no patch notes. no take-backs.
beats.quote: “Huck Finn and Tom Sawyer swears they will keep mum about This and They wish They may Drop down dead in Their Tracks if They ever Tell and Rot.”

beats.title: The Wrong Man
beats.modern: they marched Muff Potter up to the body and he's crying he never done it. and then Injun Joe stood there and told the whole town, calmly, word for word, that Muff did it. then said it again at the inquest. under oath. me and Huck are standing there WAITING for the sky to open on him. nothing. clear blue. so now we're pretty sure he's sold his soul, and telling on a man like that is just a slower way to die.

beats.title: Painkiller
beats.modern: aunt polly has been treating my sadness with cold water and mail-order miracle cures, so I've been quietly feeding the Painkiller to a crack in the floorboards. today the cat begged for a taste. I warned him. I warned him TWICE. he went two feet straight up, ran laps, threw a couple of somersaults and exited through the window taking every flowerpot with him. I was on the floor dying. then she found the spoon.

beats.title: Cannon Over The Water
beats.modern: we're camped on Jackson's Island being pirates when the ferryboat starts firing a cannon over the river to float a drowned body up. we're all in the bushes guessing who died. and then it lands on me. boys. it's US. we're the drowned kids. chat they are MOURNING us at this exact moment and we are sitting here eating fried fish with our fingers. genuinely the best day of my life.
beats.quote: “Boys, I know who’s drownded—it’s us!”

beats.title: Under Her Bed
beats.modern: swam back across at night and crawled under aunt polly's bed to hear how my funeral was doing. she's telling Mrs Harper I warn't bad, only mischeevous. then she says I don't know how to give him up. then she knelt down and prayed for me with me lying six inches underneath her. I had the note in my pocket. the one that says I'm alive. I put it back, kissed her, and left.
beats.quote: Oh, Mrs. Harper, I don’t know how to give him up!

beats.title: We Attended Our Own Funeral
beats.modern: church is full. the preacher is crying in the pulpit. everybody is sobbing about what fine noble boys we were and remembering all our rascalities as beautiful now. and we're sitting up in the closed gallery listening to the whole thing. then we walked down the aisle. me first, Joe next, Huck in rags trying to become invisible. chat that is the greatest entrance this town will ever see and I know I will never top it.
beats.quote: They had been hid in the unused gallery listening to their own funeral sermon!

beats.title: The Prophetic Dream
beats.modern: auntie's hurt I never sent word I was alive. so I told her I DREAMED about her that night. and then I described it. the candle blowing. her saying the door was open. sending Sid to shut it. calling me no more responsible than a colt. Mrs Harper and the cream she threw out herself. she's calling it prophecy now. she's going straight over to Sereny Harper to brag about it. chat I was under the bed.

beats.title: I Done It
beats.modern: master's going down the row asking who tore his book. he gets to Becky and her face goes white, that exact look a rabbit gets with a gun on it. and I stood up and shouted I DONE IT. took the worst flogging Dobbins has ever handed out plus two hours after school. and the way she looked at me when I stepped forward was worth every stroke of it.
beats.quote: shouted—“I done it!”

beats.title: The Gilded Head
beats.modern: examination night. Dobbins is drawing a map on the board with unsteady hands, the whole room tittering, and he thinks they're laughing at the map. it is not the map. there's a cat coming down through the ceiling hatch on a string with her jaws tied shut, and she takes his WIG. and the signpainter's boy had gilded his bald head. GOLD. blazing at the entire town. vacation started right there.
beats.quote: And how the light did blaze abroad from the master’s bald pate—for the signpainter’s boy had gilded it!

beats.title: Called To The Stand
beats.modern: Muff's lawyer stands up, drops the drunk defense with no warning, and says CALL THOMAS SAWYER. chat I never told a soul. I walked to that lawyer's house alone at night and broke a blood oath in his parlor. so now I'm up there with Joe's iron face on me and I told all of it, and the second I said his name he went through the courtroom window and was gone.
beats.quote: “—and as the doctor fetched the board around and Muff Potter fell, Injun Joe jumped with the knife and—”

beats.title: Room Number Two
beats.modern: took auntie's tin lantern and a towel to hood it and went for the keys on room two. door wasn't even locked. I get in, pull the towel off the lantern, and chat I nearly put my foot on INJUN JOE'S HAND. flat out on the floor with a bottle beside him. I did not look for the box. I did not look for the cross. I grabbed the towel and I left.
beats.quote: “Huck, I most stepped onto Injun Joe’s hand!”

beats.title: The Revenge Job
beats.modern: this clip is Huck's, I only got it later. he tailed two men up Cardiff Hill in the dark and it's Joe, and the "revenge job" isn't a robbery at all. it's the widow Douglas. her dead husband once had him horsewhipped in front of the whole town. so Joe's plan isn't killing her, it's her face. the partner starts shaking and Joe tells him if he flinches he dies too.

beats.title: Huck Runs Downhill
beats.modern: so Huck backs out of the sumach bushes one careful foot at a time, snaps a twig, freezes, somehow does not die, and then he FLIES down that hill to the old Welshman's door and hammers on it. first thing out of his mouth: please don't ever tell it was me. three minutes later the old man and his two sons are up the hill armed. then Huck hears the guns and a cry and doesn't wait around for the details.

beats.title: We're Lost
beats.modern: took Becky off the tourist path in McDougal's cave to show her something nobody had seen. down and down, past the bats, past the lake. and I never made a single smoke mark the whole way because it never once entered my head that we'd need to come BACK. I shouted and the cave laughed at me. she's on the ground crying and I keep saying it's all right and it is not all right.
beats.quote: “Becky, I was such a fool! Such a fool! I never thought we might want to come back!

beats.title: The Last Candle
beats.modern: she said she was hungry so I got out the wedding cake she'd saved from the picnic to dream on. split it. spring water to wash it down. then I had to tell her the thing: we stay here, where the water is, because that little piece is our last candle. and we sat and watched it go. the half inch of wick standing alone. the flame climbing its own smoke. and then the dark.
beats.quote: “Well, then, Becky, we must stay here, where there’s water to drink. That little piece is our last candle!”

beats.title: A Hand With A Candle
beats.modern: crawling down a side passage on a kite string in total black, and twenty yards off a HAND comes around a rock holding a candle. I whooped for joy. then the body followed the hand and it was Injun Joe. and he ran. from ME. the echoes must have masked my voice or he'd have walked over and settled the courtroom business right there. I went back and told Becky I only shouted for luck.

beats.title: Every Bell In Town
beats.modern: every bell in St. Petersburg going off in the middle of the night, people pouring into the street half dressed shouting THEY'RE FOUND. because I'd followed a kite string down a third passage and seen a far off speck that looked like daylight, and pushed my head and shoulders through a hole, and there was the Mississippi rolling by. five miles below the cave. the men in the skiff flat out didn't believe us.

beats.title: Triple-Locked
beats.modern: judge tells me proudly that nobody will ever get lost in that cave again, because he had the big door sheathed in boiler iron and triple-locked it. two weeks ago. and he's got the keys. chat. two weeks. I went white and they threw water in my face and when I could speak I said it: oh judge, Injun Joe's in the cave.
beats.quote: “Oh, Judge, Injun Joe’s in the cave!”

beats.title: Under The Cross
beats.modern: took Huck back in the short way, by the hole I came out of. showed him the cross smoked on the big rock and he immediately wanted to leave because ghosts. I told him ghosts don't come where there's a cross. that fixed him. dug in the clay where the footprints were, hit boards, crawled under the rock, and there it was in a snug little cavern. fifty pounds of it. Huck with both hands in the coins going MY, BUT WE'RE RICH, TOM.

beats.title: Twelve Thousand Dollars
beats.modern: widow's throwing a whole party and she announces she'll take Huck in and school him and set him up in business. so I said Huck don't need it, Huck's rich. polite silence. slightly awkward. so I walked out, dragged in the sacks, and poured the entire thing across her supper table. nobody said a word. counted it up: a little over twelve thousand dollars. more cash than anybody in that room had ever seen at once.
beats.quote: “There—what did I tell you? Half of it’s Huck’s and half of it’s mine!”

beats.title: Rich Is Overrated
beats.modern: Huck lasted three weeks in the widow's house and then vanished. found him in a barrel behind the slaughterhouse in his old rags, breakfasted on stolen odds and ends, completely content. she makes him wash. she makes him wear shoes on sunday. she eats by a bell and sleeps by a bell. he says being rich ain't what it's cracked up to be, it's just worry and sweat and wishing you was dead, and he'd like to hand me his half back.
beats.quote: Looky-here, Tom, being rich ain’t what it’s cracked up to be.

beats.title: Terms Of The Gang
beats.modern: so I explained that robbers are high-toned, dukes and such, and I can't let him into the gang if he ain't respectable. he folded instantly. one more month at the widow's, and if she lets up on the roughest parts he'll smoke private and cuss private and crowd through or bust. initiation's tonight. midnight, swear on a coffin, sign it in blood. gg chat. that's the run.
beats.quote: I’ll stick to the widder till I rot, Tom;

the-importance-of-being-earnest.title: The Importance of Being Earnest: A Trivial Comedy for Serious People
the-importance-of-being-earnest.author: Oscar Wilde

beats.title: The Cigarette Case Incident
beats.modern: chat I left my cigarette case at Algy's flat and he has READ THE INSCRIPTION. 'from little Cecily, to her dear Uncle Jack.' he's holding it over his head like loot. yes I'm Ernest in town. yes I'm Jack in the country. no I did not think anyone would run forensics on my accessories.
beats.quote: ‘From little Cecily, with her fondest love to her dear Uncle Jack.’

beats.title: Bunburying
beats.modern: turns out Algy has an imaginary dying friend called Bunbury he visits whenever he needs to escape the city. I have an imaginary bad brother called Ernest I visit whenever I need to escape the country. we independently invented the same alibi. he says there are RULES to this and he wants to teach me them. I invented it too, Algy.
beats.quote: I have invented an invaluable permanent invalid called Bunbury, in order that I may be able to go down into the country whenever I choose.

beats.title: The Ernest Requirement
beats.modern: she loves me. huge. she also says her ideal has always been to love a man called Ernest, that the name inspires absolute confidence, that she was destined to love me the second she heard it. chat my entire relationship is running on a name I made up to get out of the countryside.
beats.quote: my ideal has always been to love some one of the name of Ernest.

beats.title: The Proposal, Interrupted
beats.modern: she tells me in advance she is fully determined to accept, then makes me get on my knees and say it properly anyway. I do. she accepts. she also reviews my technique. then her mother walks in and orders me to rise from my semi-recumbent posture. I'm on the carpet. she has a notebook out. chat, she has a LIST of eligible men and I'm not on it.
beats.quote: Rise, sir, from this semi-recumbent posture. It is most indecorous.

beats.title: Losing Both Parents
beats.modern: she asks about my parents. I tell her I lost both. she says losing one parent is a misfortune but losing both looks like carelessness. chat she is interviewing me for a husband slot and she just implied I misplaced my mother and father like a set of keys.
beats.quote: To lose one parent, Mr. Worthing, may be regarded as a misfortune; to lose both looks like carelessness.

beats.title: A Hand-Bag?
beats.modern: she asks where exactly I was found. I say in a hand-bag. she says 'A hand-bag?' the way you'd say a war crime. black leather, handles on it, completely ordinary. cloak-room, Victoria Station, Brighton line. that's my origin story, chat. I spawned in left luggage.
beats.quote: a hand-bag.

beats.title: An Alliance With A Parcel
beats.modern: denied. her advice is that I go acquire some relations before the season ends and produce at minimum one parent, either sex, she isn't fussy. she will not let her only daughter marry into a cloak-room and form an alliance with a parcel. chat I have just been rejected on the grounds of luggage.
beats.quote: care—to marry into a cloak-room, and form an alliance with a parcel?

beats.title: Death By Severe Chill
beats.modern: I'm deleting the alt. Ernest dies this week. I wanted apoplexy but Algy says apoplexy is hereditary and I'd be admitting a family defect to my future mother in law. so: severe chill. Paris. sudden. my brother, who has never existed for one second, is about to die of weather.
beats.quote: My poor brother Ernest is carried off suddenly, in Paris, by a severe chill.

beats.title: This World, The Next, Or Australia
beats.modern: I told my ward at dinner that my wicked brother would have to choose between this world, the next world, and Australia. she has now repeated that, word for word, to a man standing in my garden claiming to BE my brother. he says the reviews of Australia and the afterlife are both poor and he'll be staying here.
beats.quote: you would have to choose between this world, the next world, and Australia.

beats.title: The Mourning Fit
beats.modern: I come home in full black. crape hatband, black gloves, the complete grief fit. I tell the rector my brother is dead. Paris. severe chill. telegram from the hotel manager. the governess looks at me and says 'what a lesson for him. I trust he will profit by it.' chat she is ratioing a man who was never born.
beats.quote: What a lesson for him! I trust he will profit by it.

beats.title: Christen Me At Half-Past Five
beats.modern: still in mourning for my fake brother, I ask the rector to christen me. today. as Ernest. he says adults get sprinkled, sometimes fully immersed, and offers to do me alongside the Jenkins twins. I said no. I am not getting dunked with babies, that's childish. half past five, solo booking.
beats.quote: I don’t see much fun in being christened along with other babies.

beats.title: He Is In The Dining-Room
beats.modern: I'm standing in my own garden in FULL MOURNING and Cecily comes running out with a surprise for me. my brother is here. he arrived half an hour ago. he's in the dining room. chat the man I killed in Paris this morning is in my house and my ward is holding his hand.
beats.quote: Your brother Ernest. He arrived about half an hour ago.

beats.title: Engaged Since February
beats.modern: status update on the eighteen year old I am legally responsible for: she has been engaged to my imaginary brother since February the fourteenth. she accepted him alone, under a tree. she bought the ring herself in his name. there's a bangle. chat she ran a three month relationship with a man who does not exist and she was WINNING it.
beats.quote: Worn out by your entire ignorance of my existence, I determined to end the matter one way or the other,

beats.title: Both Engaged To Ernest
beats.modern: my fiancée has come down to the country and met my ward. within ten minutes they have established they are both engaged to Ernest Worthing. both produce diaries. both have timestamps. one says yesterday at 5.30, one says ten minutes ago. chat they are cross referencing receipts on a tea table and every single entry points at me.
beats.quote: I never travel without my diary. One should always have something sensational to read in the train.

beats.title: Sugar And Cake
beats.modern: Gwendolen says no sugar, sugar isn't fashionable. Cecily drops in four lumps. Gwendolen asks specifically for bread and butter, Cecily hands her a slab of cake. Gwendolen announces she is known for the gentleness of her disposition and then warns her she may go too far. chat this is the politest knife fight in England and it is happening over a teapot.
beats.quote: You have filled my tea with lumps of sugar, and though I asked most distinctly for bread and butter, you have given me cake.

beats.title: This Is Uncle Jack
beats.modern: I walk in. Gwendolen shouts 'Ernest! my own Ernest!' and gets an arm around her. then Cecily, very sweetly, explains to her that the gentleman currently holding her is her guardian, Mr. John Worthing. chat. the arm is mine. the name is not.
beats.quote: The gentleman whose arm is at present round your waist is my guardian, Mr. John Worthing.

beats.title: No Brother At All
beats.modern: they stand there arm in arm and ask me one question: where is your brother Ernest. so I do it. I tell the truth for the first time in my life. there is no brother Ernest. there is no brother. there never was one and I have no plans to obtain one. then they go inside and call us cowards. correct.
beats.quote: I have no brother Ernest. I have no brother at all.

beats.title: The Muffins
beats.modern: both our engagements have just detonated and Algy is eating muffins. I ask how he can sit there calmly eating muffins during a crisis and he says he can't eat muffins in an agitated manner, the butter would get on his cuffs. chat he then took the dish. off me. in my own garden.
beats.quote: Well, I can’t eat muffins in an agitated manner. The butter would probably get on my cuffs.

beats.title: Bunbury Exploded
beats.modern: Aunt Augusta arrives and asks whether Algy's invalid friend Bunbury lives in this house. Algy says Bunbury is dead. died this afternoon. cause of death: exploded. he means found out. chat he deleted his alibi live in front of the woman it was invented to dodge, and she took the whole thing completely seriously.
beats.quote: Oh! I killed Bunbury this afternoon. I mean poor Bunbury died this afternoon.

beats.title: The Charge Sheet
beats.modern: I refuse consent for Algy to marry my ward, and I read the charges into the record: entered my house under a false name, drank an entire pint bottle of the champagne I was saving for myself, alienated the affections of my only ward, stayed for tea, and devoured every single muffin.
beats.quote: He subsequently stayed to tea, and devoured every single muffin.

beats.title: The Bag Swap
beats.modern: she confesses. in a moment of mental abstraction she put the manuscript in the pram and the baby in the hand-bag. I ask which station. she says Victoria. the Brighton line. chat. the Brighton line. that's my bag. that's ME. I'm the baby.
beats.quote: I deposited the manuscript in the basinette, and placed the baby in the hand-bag.

beats.title: Yes . . . Mother!
beats.modern: I sprint upstairs and throw every trunk in the house around until I find it. I bring it down. she confirms the damage, the stain, her own initials on the lock. so I embrace her and say it: mother. and she recoils and says, with genuine heat, Mr. Worthing, I am UNMARRIED. wrong woman, chat. deeply wrong woman.
beats.quote: Mr. Worthing! I am unmarried!

beats.title: I Knew I Had A Brother
beats.modern: the one who actually knows is Aunt Augusta. I'm the son of her late sister. which makes me Algy's older brother. chat I invented a wicked younger brother out of nothing to get out of dinners, and the universe went ahead and assigned me a real one, and it's HIM, and he's been eating my muffins all day.
beats.quote: Then I have a brother after all. I knew I had a brother!

beats.title: It Was Ernest All Along
beats.modern: one thing left: my actual name. I rip the Army Lists out of the bookcase hunting my father. Moncrieff. General. christian names, Ernest John. chat I have been telling the truth by accident my entire life. Gwendolen forgives me on the grounds that I am sure to change. and that's the stream. turns out it does matter, being earnest.
beats.quote: On the contrary, Aunt Augusta, I’ve now realised for the first time in my life the vital Importance of Being Earnest.

the-odyssey.title: The Odyssey: Rendered into English prose for the use of those who cannot read the original
the-odyssey.author: Homer

beats.title: Dad's Channel, No Dad
beats.modern: guest host, chat. it's the son. dad's been gone twenty years and his channel is mine now by default. situation report: there are a hundred grown men living in my house. they killed our oxen, they're sitting on the hides, they're playing board games in my front yard and shouting for music. a stranger walks in and asks me if there's a wedding on. no sir. this is a siege with snacks.

beats.title: The Shroud Speedrun
beats.modern: so it finally comes out in front of the whole assembly. my mother has been running the greatest stall in recorded history. told them she'd pick a husband the day she finished weaving a burial cloth for my grandfather. wove it all day. UNPICKED IT EVERY NIGHT BY TORCHLIGHT. three years of fake progress bar. three years. then one of her own maids snitched and they caught her mid-unpick.

beats.title: Leaving, Nobody Tell Mom
beats.modern: a goddess fuddles their drinks until they're dropping cups and wandering home cross-eyed, then walks me down to a ship I chartered in secret. mom doesn't know. the house doesn't know. one servant knows and she's sworn. I'm a kid with a borrowed boat sailing off to ask old men whether my father is dead, and the wind gets up, and the foam hisses, and that's the whole plan.

beats.title: The Seal Blanket Stakeout
beats.modern: stopped in Sparta. Menelaus tells me how you catch a shape-shifting sea god: you lie in a pit on the beach for an entire morning under a DEAD SEAL SKIN. the smell nearly killed him. a goddess had to put perfume under his nose. then they jumped the old man and he became a lion, a snake, a leopard, a wild boar, running water, a TREE, and they just held on. that's the whole strategy. grip it until reality gets bored.

beats.title: Alive, Just Grounded
beats.modern: and then the old sea god drops the actual lore. my father is ALIVE. he's on an island in the middle of the sea. a goddess is keeping him there and he cannot leave because he has no ship and no crew and nobody is coming. so he's not dead, chat. he's worse than dead. he's stuck.

beats.title: Taking The Channel Back
beats.modern: dad here. taking my own channel back, seven years late. a messenger god just walked into this cave and said the word: let him go. and she went OFF. said you gods let male gods date mortals all day, one goddess keeps a man and suddenly it's a scandal. honestly? not wrong. also she's been keeping me for seven years. both things can be true.

beats.title: She Offered Me Forever
beats.modern: final offer on the table: stay here, never age, never die, immortal with a goddess, forever. and she asks if my wife is really worth it. and I look her in the face and tell her the truth.
beats.quote: I am quite aware that my wife Penelope is nothing like so tall or so beautiful as yourself.

beats.title: Ocean Boss Fight, No Ship
beats.modern: raft was fine for days and then the sea god gets back from holiday, spots me, and stirs the ocean with his trident like a pot. all four winds at once. mast snaps, sail's gone, I'm under. then a sea goddess surfaces like a gull, sits on my raft and says strip, take my scarf, swim. chat I do not accept free loot from strangers mid-storm. I stayed on the raft. the raft exploded. fine. scarf it is.

beats.title: Naked Guy In The Bushes
beats.modern: twenty days in the water. wash up with nothing. no ship, no crew, no clothes, crusted in salt, so hungry I'm shaking. and there's a princess doing laundry on the beach with her friends. so I break off a leafy branch, hold it where it counts, and walk out of the shrubs like a starving lion. every girl on that beach ran. she did not. she just stood there. absolute nerve.

beats.title: The Palm Tree Line
beats.modern: and then I run the smoothest thing I have ever said in my life. told her I once saw a young palm tree growing by Apollo's altar and had to stop walking, and that looking at her is that exact feeling. then I wished her a husband and a house and a marriage where two people actually agree with each other. I am naked, starving and covered in salt and I am STILL cooking.
beats.quote: there is nothing better in this world than that man and wife should be of one mind in a house.

beats.title: The Bard Sang My War
beats.modern: blind singer at dinner starts performing MY war. me and Achilles arguing at a banquet, the whole thing, note perfect. and I pull my cloak up over my head and sob into it like a child. nobody in the hall notices except the king, who hears me breathing wrong. they still don't know my name. I'm crying at a song about myself and they think the music just moved me.

beats.title: Don't Call Me A Merchant
beats.modern: local kid decides I don't look sporty. says I've got the build of a guy who does freight. so I stand up, don't even take my cloak off, grab the heaviest disc on the field and send it humming past every mark anyone has made all day. then I offer to box, wrestle or run against literally anyone present. was that necessary? no. did I need it? chat I needed it so badly.

beats.title: The Name Drop
beats.modern: you fed me. you gave me gifts. you watched me cry at your dinner table twice and never asked why. so here it is, the reveal. I'm the one from the songs. the horse was mine. and I'd trade every offer of immortality on this earth to see my own rocky little island again, because nothing beats where you're from.
beats.quote: I am Ulysses son of Laertes, renowned among mankind for all manner of subtlety, so that my fame ascends to heaven.

beats.title: The Flower That Deletes You
beats.modern: sent three men to scout the locals. no ambush, no fight, no threats. they just fed them a flower. and my guys came back with nothing behind their eyes. didn't want the ship. didn't want home. didn't want to come tell me what happened. had to drag them aboard crying and TIE THEM UNDER THE BENCHES. rowed out fast before anyone else got a taste.

beats.title: He Ate Two Of My Men
beats.modern: asked him for hospitality like a normal person. he answered by picking up two of my men like puppies and dashing them on the floor. ate them whole. bones, everything. washed it down with a drink of milk and went to sleep. I had my hand on my sword and then I did the maths: the door is a boulder we cannot move. kill him and we starve in here with the body. so I sat in the dark all night next to what was left of my crew.

beats.title: My Name Is Nobody
beats.modern: give him the good wine. three bowls, undiluted, and he's begging for more and asking my name so he can give me a present. so I tell him what I'm called.
beats.quote: my name is Noman; this is what my father and mother and my friends have always called me.’

beats.title: Nobody Is Killing Me
beats.modern: the other giants come running at the screaming, banging on the rock, asking who's hurting him. and he yells the setup and the punchline in one breath. and they stand outside and go: well, if NOBODY is attacking you then you're just ill mate, that's a god thing, nothing we can do, pray about it, goodnight. and they LEFT. I had to bite my own hand.
beats.quote: ‘Noman is killing me by fraud; no man is killing me by force.’

beats.title: Under The Sheep
beats.modern: he sits in the doorway with both hands spread to catch us on the way out. so we go under. tied the rams in threes, a man slung beneath the middle one, and I took the big one and hung off its belly by fistfuls of wool. and on the way out he STOPS my ram. starts talking to it. asks why it's walking last today, says it must be sad about his eye, says if it could talk it would tell him where I'm hiding. I am inches under his hand listening to that.

beats.title: The Worst Thing I Ever Said
beats.modern: safe. out of range. crew literally begging me to keep my mouth shut. and I stand up in the boat and give him my full legal name and home address, because I needed the credit.
beats.quote: ‘Cyclops, if any one asks you who it was that put your eye out and spoiled your beauty, say it was the valiant warrior Ulysses, son of Laertes, who lives in Ithaca.’

beats.title: Ten Feet From Home
beats.modern: wind god bottles every storm on earth in an ox-hide bag and hands it to me as a gift. nine days I steer, never once letting go of the rudder, no sleep. tenth day I can SEE the fires burning on my own island. and I close my eyes for one second. and my crew, absolutely certain the bag is treasure I'm not sharing, opens it. every wind at once. blew us all the way back. I woke up mid-ocean going the wrong direction.

beats.title: Eleven Ships In One Afternoon
beats.modern: harbour looked perfect. flat water, sheltered, cliffs all round. every captain took his ship inside. I moored outside on a rock and to this day I don't know why. then the giants came over the top throwing boulders down into the bowl, and they speared my men in the water like fish and carried them home for dinner. eleven ships. all of them. I cut my own cable with my sword and that is the only reason there is a stream.

beats.title: She Turned My Crew Into Pigs
beats.modern: she's singing at a loom, gorgeous voice, opens the door herself, sits them down, feeds them cheese and honey and wine with something in it. one tap of a stick and they're pigs. head, hair, grunt, everything. and here's the part that ruins me, chat: their minds stayed. they remembered every single thing. and she threw them acorns.

beats.title: God Hands Me A Cheat Item
beats.modern: meet a god on the mountain path who tells me the enemy's entire moveset before I fight it. then digs up a herb out of the ground: black root, white flower, and says mortals physically cannot pull this one. spell immunity in your pocket. plus the walkthrough: drink her drink anyway, and the second she raises the wand, draw on her.

beats.title: The Wand Doesn't Work
beats.modern: she mixes the drink. I drink it. she taps me and tells me to go get in the sty with the others. and nothing happens. and the LOOK on her face. I come at her with the sword up and she goes straight down, grabs my knees, asks who I am and how I'm spell-proof, then pivots instantly to "anyway let's go to bed and be friends." I made her swear a binding oath first. always get it in writing.

beats.title: A Whole Year Later
beats.modern: we stayed a year. a full year. good food, good wine, nobody counting days. and eventually the men take me aside and go, sir. respectfully. it's been a while. maybe home? and I go: oh. right. yeah. so I ask her for the exit and she says of course, one thing first, you have to go down to the land of the dead and interview a blind prophet. that's the side quest. that's what's between me and my house.

beats.title: The Prophecy
beats.modern: dead prophet drinks the blood and reads me my future like patch notes. the sea god's grudge is permanent, that's not getting fixed. you'll pass an island with cattle belonging to the sun. leave them alone: you get home late, broke, but alive. touch one: I lose the ship and every man on it. wrote it down. told the crew. remember this beat, chat.

beats.title: What Killed My Mother
beats.modern: she was alive when I left for the war. she is not now. so I ask her how it happened, was it an illness, was it quick, and she tells me it was missing me. that's the cause of death. that's it. then I tried to hold her three times and my arms went through her three times, and my own mother had to explain to me that this is simply what people are once they're gone.
beats.quote: my longing to know what you were doing and the force of my affection for you—this it was that was the death of me.’93

beats.title: Killed At His Own Party
beats.modern: the man who commanded all of us at Troy. survived ten years of war, got home, kissed the ground, cried with relief, and got butchered at his own welcome dinner like an ox in a shed. his wife and her boyfriend set it up. every man he brought with him died on that floor too. he says he lay there with the sword in him and heard Cassandra scream beside him. then he gives me a whole speech about not trusting your own house. filed that one away. filed it away hard.

beats.title: Achilles Rates Death
beats.modern: I tell Achilles the nice thing. you were worshipped alive, you're royalty down here among the dead, don't take it so hard. and he shuts me down flat, no pause.
beats.quote: I would rather be a paid servant in a poor man’s house and be above ground than king of kings among the dead.

beats.title: Ajax Won't Speak To Me
beats.modern: one ghost stands off at the edge and won't come near the blood. it's Ajax. still angry about a contest. we both went for Achilles' armour, I won it, and he didn't survive losing. so I go over and say all the right things. that we mourned him like we mourned Achilles. that it wasn't me, it was the gods. and he turns around and walks off into the dark without a single word. worst thing anyone's ever said to me and he said nothing.

beats.title: Tie Me To The Mast
beats.modern: wax in every ear on the ship. except mine. ropes, mast, standing upright, hands and feet bound, because I wanted to HEAR it. and they start singing and it isn't about love at all, it's about knowledge. they say they know everything that happened at Troy and everything that will ever happen anywhere. and I'm frowning at my own crew begging to be cut loose and they just row harder and tie me tighter. that's what a good crew is.

beats.title: Six Names I Still Know
beats.modern: I knew the monster was there. I didn't tell them, because if I had they'd have stopped rowing and we'd all have died. put my armour on, took two spears, stood in the bow, and watched the wrong side of the strait. she came down from above. took six. I looked up and saw their hands and feet in the air over my head and heard every one of them call my name once.
beats.quote: This was the most sickening sight that I saw throughout all my voyages.

beats.title: They Ate The Sun's Cows
beats.modern: one month of wrong wind, food gone, and I sleep for one hour. wake up to the smell of roasting beef. and then the meat starts LOWING on the spits. the hides crawl along the ground on their own. six days of eating steak that moos at you. then we sail and the first cloud finds us: lightning takes the ship, the falling mast takes the helmsman's skull, and every man goes into the water like gulls. I lashed the keel to the mast and rode the wreck alone.

beats.title: Their Ship Became A Rock
beats.modern: the people who finally gave me a lift home never made it back. the sea god waited until their ship was coming into their own harbour, in front of their whole town watching from the shore, and turned it to stone and pressed it into the seabed with the flat of his hand. they were still looking at it when it stopped being a ship. their entire crime was giving me a ride.

beats.title: New Look, Old Man
beats.modern: goddess taps me with a wand and takes all of it. skin goes to wrinkles, hair gone, eyes bleared over, clothes swapped for rags that stink of smoke, deer hide on top, a stick, and a bag with holes in it. twenty years away and I'm walking back into my own house as the thing people step around in a doorway.

beats.title: Telling My Son
beats.modern: he watched a filthy old beggar turn into a man his father's age in about one second, so naturally he decides I'm a god and starts praying at me. and I say it flat.
beats.quote: I am your father, on whose account you grieve and suffer so much at the hands of lawless men.”

beats.title: Argos
beats.modern: there's a dog on the manure heap by the gate. full of fleas, nobody's cared for him in years. I raised him as a puppy and shipped out before he was old enough to hunt with. he can't get up. he can't come to me. he just drops his ears and wags. and I have to turn my face away and ask the swineherd, casually, whose dog is that. because if I say his name out loud I lose everything.
beats.quote: but Argos died as soon as he had recognised his master.

beats.title: Beggar Cage Match
beats.modern: the house tramp wants me out of HIS doorway. the suitors are thrilled, they're putting up a prize, they're taking bets on two homeless men fighting for their entertainment. and I have to actively decide to hit him softly so nobody works out who I am. broke his jaw anyway. dragged him out by one foot, propped him against a wall, put his stick back in his hand and told him to go be king of the dogs somewhere else.

beats.title: The Scar
beats.modern: the old nurse washes my feet. the woman who fed me as a baby. and her hand closes on the boar scar I got as a boy hunting on the mountain and she drops my whole leg, kicks the basin over, water everywhere.
beats.quote: “My dear child, I am sure you must be Ulysses himself, only I did not know you till I had actually touched and handled you.”

beats.title: Tomorrow, The Bow
beats.modern: my wife, who does not know me, sits by the fire and tells the beggar what she's decided. tomorrow she sets up the twelve axes. whoever strings my bow and puts one arrow through all of them, she marries him and leaves this house forever. she thinks she's announcing the end of her life. she is actually scheduling a hundred funerals, and I'm sitting right there nodding.

beats.title: Heart, Be Still
beats.modern: can't sleep. lying on a bare hide in my own hall like a stray dog. the maids go past me giggling on their way to the suitors' beds and I nearly get up and finish all of them right there, and I feel my own chest growl at me like a bitch standing over her pups. so I lie there and talk to my own heart out loud.
beats.quote: “Heart, be still, you had worse than this to bear on the day when the terrible Cyclops ate your brave companions;

beats.title: The Room Laughs Wrong
beats.modern: a goddess gets into their heads and the whole room starts laughing and cannot stop. forced, wrong, mouths going while their eyes stream with tears. the meat on their plates goes bloody. and my guest the seer stands up and calmly describes what he can see in the room.
beats.quote: the walls and roof-beams drip blood; the gate of the cloisters and the court beyond them are full of ghosts trooping down into the night of hell;

beats.title: Strung It Like A Lyre
beats.modern: they've been sweating over that bow all afternoon. greasing it, warming it at the fire, taking turns, none of them can bend it an inch. then it comes to the old beggar in the corner. I turn it over once, check the horn for worm, and string it in one motion the way a musician fits a new string. then I flick it and it SINGS. the whole room changes colour. thunder outside on cue. and one arrow, clean through all twelve axe heads and out the far door.

beats.title: Rags Off
beats.modern: tear the rags off, jump onto the open floor, pour the arrows out at my feet.
beats.quote: “The mighty contest is at an end. I will now see whether Apollo will vouchsafe it to me to hit another mark which no man has yet hit.”

beats.title: Dogs
beats.modern: they still think it was an accident. they're on their feet shouting that I'll pay for shooting a guest, looking round the walls for weapons that I moved out days ago. so I tell them who I am, and the colour goes out of the room.
beats.quote: “Dogs, did you think that I should not come back from Troy?

beats.title: The Twelve
beats.modern: and then the part where I'm not the hero. the women who'd been sleeping with the suitors are made to carry the bodies out and scrub my floor clean of the blood. and when the hall is spotless my son takes them out to the yard and puts them on a ship's cable, strung high so their feet can't reach the ground.
beats.quote: Their feet moved convulsively for a while, but not for very long.

beats.title: The Bed
beats.modern: she's looked at me for hours and given me nothing. so she turns to the nurse and says fine, move our bed out of the bedroom and make it up outside. and I go OFF. because I built that bed. there was a living olive tree growing there and I built the room around it and cut the trunk itself into the bedpost. that bed does not move unless somebody cut the tree down. and she breaks. because that was the password, and nobody alive knows it but us two. she wasn't cold, chat. she was running a check.

beats.title: Proof For My Father
beats.modern: find my dad in the vineyard in patched rags and gardening gloves, and he's so far into grief he pours dirt over his own head while I'm standing right in front of him. so I say it: it's me, twenty years, it's done, they're dead. and he asks me for proof. so I show him the scar. and then I walk him down his own rows naming the trees he gave me when I was small: thirteen pears, ten apples, forty figs, fifty rows of vines. the scar didn't break him. the fruit trees did.

beats.title: GG
beats.modern: the families of the dead come up the road armed. my father, who hasn't lifted a spear in a generation, takes one and drops the man leading them, and shouts about what a day he's having. me and my son go straight at the front line and we would have killed every last one of them. and then a goddess shouts once and every weapon in that field falls out of every hand at the same time. thunderbolt in the dirt in front of me to make the point. so we stop. treaty on the spot. twenty years, and it ends with everyone just going home. gg.

beats.title: The Valley Build
beats.modern: welcome back chat. this is La Vallée. dad reads, mom gardens, the Pyrenees are RIGHT there. dad had a whole life out in the world and came home from it quieter, so now the plan is books, olives, and never wanting anything again. take a good look. this is the last time everything is fine.

beats.title: Mom Logs Off
beats.modern: mom's been fading for weeks and she keeps talking about the next world like she's already packed. dad keeps leaving the room to cry and coming back with his composed face on, which is worse. chat I held it together the entire time. and the second it was over I went down, and that's when I learned the thing holding me up wasn't strength. it was hope.

beats.title: Dad's Hidden Folder
beats.modern: 1am. dad's not in bed. I find him locked in his closet office reading papers and SOBBING. then he kneels and prays with a face I've never seen on him. then he takes out a little case with a portrait of a woman in it. not my mother. kisses it. presses it to his heart. chat I backed out of that room so fast. widowed two months and there's a whole other woman in a box.

beats.title: I Shot The Boyfriend
beats.modern: someone comes galloping up on our carriage in the dark yelling STOP, so my father draws the pistol and fires. groan. it's Valancourt. the mountain boy we've been road-tripping with all week. my dad shot my crush. I fainted in the carriage. and then the guy with the bullet in his arm got up to come check on ME. chat I'm marrying him. it takes four volumes.

beats.title: Music In The Woods
beats.modern: there's music in these woods and nobody is playing it. it stops, we listen, nothing comes back. the old man whose cottage we're staying at says he's been hearing it for eighteen years. same woods. no source. he says it the way you'd mention weather. dad went very quiet. filing this one away.

beats.title: The Dying Request
beats.modern: dad's dying and he's got one job for me. loose board in his closet, remarkable knot in the wood, press the line with your foot. under it, papers. burn them. do NOT read them. I asked why. he said if it were right to explain his reasons he wouldn't have needed the oath. so I'm now sworn to destroy a folder I'm not allowed to open.
beats.quote: “It is sufficient for you, my love, to have a deep sense of the importance of observing me in this instance.”

beats.title: GG Dad
beats.modern: he asked where I was. he couldn't see me anymore. I'd turned to the window so he wouldn't watch me cry. he blessed me, and it took everything he had left, and for one second when I kissed him his eyes came back and he was my father again. then he wasn't. three in the afternoon. no struggle, no sound.

beats.title: I Read One Line
beats.modern: my father made me swear on his deathbed to burn a stack of papers without reading them. I'm at the fire with them and my eyes just LAND on a sentence. one sentence. so bad I physically threw the stack away from me. and then I burned them anyway, chat, I watched them go, knowing the only explanation that will ever exist was going with them.
beats.quote: it is not my business to argue, but to obey.

beats.title: Who Is She
beats.modern: there was a purse under the board too. I go to put it away unopened and feel something bulky at the bottom. it's the portrait. HER. sweet face, sad eyes, total stranger. he never named her, never left instructions about her, so technically I'm allowed to keep it. so I'm keeping it. new lore item acquired.

beats.title: My Aunt Is A Hater
beats.modern: meet aunt Cheron, my legal guardian, whose entire personality is implying things. she's decided I was sneaking around at night, refuses to hear the explanation, and refuses to say why she refuses. then she pivots straight to how broke I am. with pity. out loud. at volume. she says she'll see how I behave in future. gracious.
beats.quote: “I never trust people’s assertions, I always judge of them by their actions;

beats.title: New Uncle Just Dropped
beats.modern: so my aunt married the Italian. secretly. this morning. the one Valancourt has told me twice he doesn't trust. and she's not just announcing it, she's taking MY wedding decorations for HER party, delaying MY wedding to fit hers in, and asking me to wear my own wedding clothes to it. congratulations auntie. huge day for you.
beats.quote: From this hour you must consider the Signor Montoni as your uncle—we were married this morning.”

beats.title: Engagement Cancelled
beats.modern: update: the new uncle has decided Valancourt is beneath me, so the engagement is dead and we're moving to Italy. my aunt delivered this like a weather report, then told me I'll enjoy the journey since I'm so fond of romantic country. she also explained that she only ever agreed to my wedding because my crying wore her down. ma'am.
beats.quote: the proposed connection between the families must from this time be thought of no more.”

beats.title: The Goodbye Clip
beats.modern: he keeps apologising for crying and then keeps crying. calls himself a wretch for making ME comfort HIM. I stop us at the gate because I cannot do the walk up the drive. he says trust me, we'll meet again, meet for each other, meet to part no more. chat he is off by four years and one gambling arc.
beats.quote: tenderness—“trust me we shall meet again—meet for each other—meet to part no more!”

beats.title: Venice Is A Trap
beats.modern: Venice: moonlight on the water, a gondolier singing to nobody, genuinely unreal. Venice also: Count Morano, whose entire personality is proximity. every evening he materialises at my elbow with a look of impatient delight. I look at the sea and think of home. I look at Morano and think of Valancourt. those are different feelings, Count.

beats.title: Pack Everything, Now
beats.modern: dawn, hammering on my door. Annette says the whole house is running and nobody knows why. Montoni's orders: be ready immediately, gondolas at the steps in minutes, we are leaving Venice. I asked if Morano was downstairs and nearly went under. nobody will say where we're going. chat we are going somewhere significantly worse.

beats.title: There Is Udolpho
beats.modern: road drops into a valley, last of the sun catches something on a cliff, and my stepuncle speaks for the first time in HOURS purely to say: there. that's Udolpho. then the light dies off the walls into purple, then nothing, and it just sits up there looking like it's daring the whole valley to try something. mood: I live there now.

beats.title: My Door Has No Lock
beats.modern: my room is at the far end of the castle, damp, enormous, no fire lit in it for years. there's a second door. it opens onto a black staircase going down. it HAS bolts. two of them. ON THE OTHER SIDE. I dragged a heavy chair against it. that's the security system, chat. one chair.

beats.title: The Black Veil
beats.modern: there's a picture in this castle with a black veil hung over it and I have thought about nothing else for two days. so I go in. hand on the veil. lift it. and it isn't a picture. I dropped it and then I dropped, chat, woke up on the floor. I'm not describing it. I am never lifting that again. (I find out what it was in six hundred pages and I promise you it's stupid.)

beats.title: Morano Kicks The Door In
beats.modern: 3am, Morano is in my room dragging me toward a hidden staircase, and then Montoni comes through the other door with half the household and it's SWORDS. in the corridor. nobody dares step in. Montoni wounds him, disarms him, stands over him and tells him to beg for his life. Morano faints instead. Montoni was going to finish it right there on the floor. these are my guardians.

beats.title: Auntie Won't Sign
beats.modern: my aunt has finally worked out that her husband has no money. none. he gambled away his own fortune, then hers, and the castle and the Venice house aren't even his if his debts were paid. now he wants her signature on the last thing she owns and she said no, at volume, calling him a vile deceitful cruel monster. chat I have never respected her more or been more frightened for her.
beats.quote: he is sunk deeply in debt, and that neither this castle, nor the mansion at Venice, is his own,

beats.title: He Runs A Gang Now
beats.modern: auntie said the quiet part out loud: he isn't serving any state, he's running a bandit crew out of this castle and looting the countryside. Montoni looked at her for one long second. then, flat, no volume: you're being moved to the east turret tonight, where perhaps you'll understand the danger of offending a man with unlimited power over you. he said it like he was booking a room.
beats.quote: he had only commenced a captain of banditti, to join the enemies of Venice,

beats.title: The Guy With The Torch
beats.modern: the porter says he'll take me to my aunt. leads me down through a ruined chapel, through the vaults, up a staircase in a dead tower, then says wait in this room while I go up and tell her. locks the door behind me. and then I hear his boots going DOWN. chat I am standing in a locked room I was walked into by a man who lied about which direction he was going.

beats.title: She's Still Alive
beats.modern: I climb the tower to sit with my aunt's body. there's a track of blood on the stairs. the room is dark. I get to the bed, pull the curtain, and the face in there is barely a face I know. I pick up the hand and it's cold as marble. and then it moves. and a voice says: where have you been so long. I thought you had forsaken me. she has been alive up here the entire time.
beats.quote: “I thought you had forsaken me.”

beats.title: Sitting Up With The Dead
beats.modern: she's gone. I decided not to tell Montoni till morning because I knew exactly what he'd say and I did not have it in me to hear it. so it was me and Annette doing the last small decent things for her, all night, in a castle full of armed men, with a storm shaking the walls. nobody else came up.

beats.title: He's Not Even Sad
beats.modern: told him in the morning. his one and only reaction was rage, because she died before signing. that's the grief. that's it. I sat with her body two days and thought about how she ended up here, and I couldn't be angry at her anymore. more in sorrow than in anger. she was awful to me and she deserved so much better than this.

beats.title: I Signed It Away
beats.modern: he swore, in the most solemn terms available to a human being, that if I gave up the estates he would let me leave. so I signed. it took me a long time to make my hand do it. and the second the ink was down he smiled and said it was necessary to deceive you, there was no other way of making you act reasonably. you'll go later. maybe. chat I sold the last thing I owned for nothing.
beats.quote: he,—“there was no other way of making you act reasonably;

beats.title: Someone Is Singing
beats.modern: there's a lute under my window at night and a voice with it and the song is FRENCH. Annette hears it, recognises it, and immediately starts yelling Monsieur Valancourt out the window like we are not surrounded by armed men. music stops instantly. her entire evidence is that the singer is French. and yet. chat what if.

beats.title: Wrong Guy
beats.modern: it isn't him. it's Monsieur Du Pont, a Frenchman from back home who has apparently loved me for years, stole a portrait of me off a table once, and is confessing all of it from inside this castle where he is also a prisoner. then he offers to help me escape. sir. you are in a cell. and he is still the single most decent man in this building.

beats.title: We Ride At Midnight
beats.modern: Ludovico talks a guard out of the courtyard, grabs two loose horses, and walks us straight through the gates. me, Annette, Du Pont, the woods. then shouting behind us and lights moving fast up by the castle. Du Pont whips the horse. we go. we look back and the lights are pinpricks and the voices are gone. chat I got out of Udolpho.

beats.title: New Château, Same Ghosts
beats.modern: we make it to Languedoc and Count De Villefort takes me in at Château-le-Blanc. his daughter Blanche adopts me on sight, having just escaped a convent and never had a friend. lovely family, lovely house, sea out the window. the whole north wing is locked and the servants change the subject. we're doing this again, aren't we.

beats.title: The Count Has Receipts
beats.modern: the Count sat me down about Valancourt in Paris. deep play with men he says he could hardly bear to look at. prison. TWICE. and a Parisian countess who bought him out and kept him. chat I fainted in the garden. woke up on the grass with the Count shouting for water. four years of holding onto someone who apparently stopped existing.
beats.quote: the Chevalier’s extravagance has brought him twice into the prisons of Paris,

beats.title: Breakup Stream
beats.modern: he came to say goodbye and instead tore himself apart in front of me. why was I forced to Paris. why did I take the bait. can you really give up a heart that loves you like mine. then, quiet: I'm going, Emily, I'm going to leave you, for ever. and every single thing I'd been angry about just fell out of my hands.
beats.quote: I am going, Emily, I am going to leave you—to leave you, for ever!”

beats.title: Dorothée's House Tour
beats.modern: the old housekeeper takes me into the dead Marchioness's room. twenty years untouched, black pall over the bed. she says she can see her lady lying on it. she says this is the spot, she held her hand right here and heard her last words. then she opens the closet and shows me the portrait. chat. it is the woman from my father's locket.
beats.quote: “it was here I sat on that terrible night, and held my lady’s hand,

beats.title: Ludovico Takes The Bet
beats.modern: the sealed wing of this château is supposedly haunted, so Ludovico volunteers to sleep in it. the whole household follows him upstairs like it's a title fight. the housekeeper turns the key, glances in, SCREAMS, and half the crowd evacuates the staircase. Ludovico walks in with a drawn sword and a basket of snacks, picks the bedroom at the far end, says he'll lie down when he gets bored of watching. king.

beats.title: The Room Is Empty
beats.modern: morning. no answer at the door. they force it. the Count goes room by room calling his name into total silence. bedroom's dark, a servant trips over the chair Ludovico was sitting in and the rest of them bolt. they open the shutters. bed empty. oriel empty. everything else exactly as it was left, outer door still locked from the INSIDE. Ludovico is gone.

beats.title: Montoni Is Dead
beats.modern: news from Venice. Montoni went to trial over a murder, walked on the charge because nothing stuck, and the senate locked him up anyway on the grounds that he was simply too dangerous to leave outdoors. he died in there. quietly. mysteriously. poison, they think. the man who took everything from me died offscreen in a cell and I found out by letter.

beats.title: It Was Pirates
beats.modern: Ludovico's alive. the haunted wing was PIRATES. smugglers running stores through the vaults, and one of them got caught in the bedroom, hid under the bedding, and lifted his face out of the sheet to scare the housekeeper off. it worked so well it bought them twenty years of ghost story. I was terrified of a man doing a bedsheet bit. the music in the woods though? even the pirates were scared of that one.

beats.title: The Nun Knows My Face
beats.modern: there's a dying nun at the convent, sister Agnes, who has been staring at me like she's seen me before. turns out she is Laurentini di Udolpho. the heiress who vanished out of that castle. the one Montoni was rumoured to have murdered. she's been here the whole time under a fake name, and her first real words to me are: you're the Marchioness's daughter.

beats.title: The Confession
beats.modern: she did it. she wanted the Marquis, so she talked him into believing his wife was unfaithful, and they poisoned her. and the exact instant it was done the revenge evaporated. he turned on her, cursed her as the one who'd dragged him into it, and spared her only on condition she spent the rest of her life on her knees. she got everything she wanted for about a minute and paid for it for twenty years.

beats.title: She Was My Aunt
beats.modern: the murdered Marchioness was my father's sister. my aunt. that's who was in the locket he wept over. the papers he made me burn were the letters about how she died, and he never said her name in front of me once in my life, and he made his other sister swear silence too. chat he wasn't hiding a mistress. he was hiding a grave.

beats.title: It Was Wax
beats.modern: and the thing behind the black veil? WAX. a wax corpse. some ancestor offended the church and got sentenced to sit and stare at a model of his own rotting body as penance, then put it in his WILL that his descendants had to keep it on the wall for the moral. if I had looked twice I'd have known in one second. I did not look twice. nobody looks twice.

beats.title: He Came Back
beats.modern: I'm up in the watch-tower with my lute singing the old songs, fully in my sad girl era, and there are footsteps on the stairs. it's him. I went cold on instinct and he just stopped and said: you don't know, do you. the Count found out the stories were lies and invited me here to explain. chat the man was slandered. I have spent a year mourning a crime that never happened.

beats.title: Stream Over
beats.modern: double wedding at Château-le-Blanc, me and Blanche, same day, old banners out of storage, music down every gallery. then home to La Vallée. the actual house. the one dad made me promise never to sell. he took me back to the plane tree where he first told me he loved me. four volumes, one castle, one wax corpse, and I ended up exactly where I started. gg.

beats.title: Cigar Diplomacy
beats.modern: some tourist rides into MY hidden spring with two horses and a book about Caesar. I have a blunderbuss and forty eight hours of nothing in my stomach. he offers me a cigar. chat, in Spain a cigar is a binding contract, so now I legally cannot rob him. then he feeds me ham and I ate it like a wolf. hospitality speedrun.

beats.title: Wrong Bandit, Buddy
beats.modern: so he starts telling me stories about Jose-Maria, the famous bandit. how brave he is. how generous. he is saying this out loud, at length, to a stranger holding a blunderbuss in the middle of nowhere. chat he thinks I am him. wrong bandit. and for the record that guy is a hack.
beats.quote: “Jose-Maria is nothing but a blackguard,”

beats.title: Your Guide Sold Me Out
beats.modern: I'm asleep across the doorway and the tourist shakes me awake to politely ask whether I'd enjoy six lancers walking in. his own guide rode off to sell me for two hundred ducats while I slept two feet away. this man had every reason to let me hang and he woke me up instead. only regret: I will never be able to pay him back.
beats.quote: “Your guide has betrayed me--but he shall pay for it!

beats.title: Wrong Door, My Guy
beats.modern: months later I kick her door in ready to end whoever is in that room and it's HIM. ham guy. cigar guy. the one man in Spain I owe. meanwhile she's behind me doing the little throat-cut motion at me, over and over, do him, do him. I walked him to the bridge instead. she lifted his gold watch anyway.
beats.quote: “The same as ever. There shall be an end to it!”

beats.title: The Medal
beats.modern: they garrotte me the day after tomorrow and he shows up to my cell with a bundle of cigars. I counted them, took a few, handed the rest back. chat I'm not going to need them. one ask: a little silver medal, an old lady in Navarre, tell her I'm dead. do not tell her how.
beats.quote: Tell her I am dead--but don’t tell her how I died.”

beats.title: The Flower Between The Eyes
beats.modern: guard duty at the cigar factory. I'm sitting on my bench twisting wire into a little chain because good soldiers stay busy. five hundred women walk past and I do not look up once. then she stops in front of ME and asks if the gentleman makes lace. everyone laughs. then she takes the flower out of her mouth and flicks it into my forehead. I picked it up off the ground and kept it. mistake one of about nine hundred.
beats.quote: I tell you, sir, I felt as if a bullet had struck me.

beats.title: The X On Her Face
beats.modern: stabbing call in the cigar room. I walk into three hundred women screaming in their shifts and one on the floor with an X freshly carved into her face. cause of dispute: the other girl said Carmen would be riding a donkey to the gallows soon. Carmen said she'd paint a checkerboard on her cheeks instead. that's the thing about her, chat. she says it and then she just does it.
beats.quote: ‘I’ll make troughs for the flies to drink out of on your cheeks,

beats.title: The Push
beats.modern: she goes, hey, what if you happened to fall over. I said try it and may our Lady help you through. she punches me in the chest, I go down ON PURPOSE, then I stick my lance sideways across the alley so my own men can't give chase. total cost: corporal stripes, one month in a cell, the sergeant arc deleted forever. and I'd do it again, which is the whole damn problem.

beats.title: The File In The Bread
beats.modern: jailer hands me a roll, says it's from my cousin. chat I do not have a cousin. knife hits metal: there is an English file baked into the loaf and a gold coin in the crumb. she mailed me a jailbreak inside a snack. I didn't use it. desertion is a crime and I still thought of myself as a soldier. just sat in there sniffing a dried flower like a lunatic.

beats.title: You Keep Guard Like A Recruit
beats.modern: busted down to private, posted at the colonel's door, entire town out front to watch it happen. carriage pulls up and out she steps in spangles and gold with a tambourine. walks past and says you keep guard like a recruit. then I stood there one full hour listening to officers flirt with her through the lattice. that's the hour I actually fell in love. sentry duty. through a grate. me.
beats.quote: It was on that day, I think, that I began to love her in earnest--for

beats.title: I Pay My Debts
beats.modern: she spent my last coin on sweets, made me carry every bag, then dumped the lot on the floor and said she pays her debts, it's the law. no castanets in the house so she smashed the old woman's only plate and danced with the pieces. best day I will ever have. next morning: we're quits, good day to you. the dog and the wolf can't live together, she says. she told me. I heard her. I stayed.
beats.quote: The dog and the wolf can’t agree for long.

beats.title: Canary Bird
beats.modern: she wants me to wave five smugglers through the breach I'm guarding. I say no, orders. she says fine, I'll go ask your officer, he'll post a sentry who knows how to not see things, bye canary-bird, I'll laugh the day they hang you. I folded in about four seconds. next day she called me cheap for having negotiated at all. I ended up crying in the dark corner of a church and she found me there and offered to bottle the tears.
beats.quote: “‘A dragoon in tears. I’ll make a philter of them!’

beats.title: The Lieutenant
beats.modern: she walks in with a lieutenant from my own regiment and tells me in Basque to get out. I couldn't move. he takes me by the collar, opens my forehead with his sword, I still have the scar. then he came on again and I put the point up and he ran onto it himself. chat that is the exact second the rest of my life was decided. back room. borrowed woman. one step I didn't take.

beats.title: Career Counselling
beats.modern: they drug me, dress the wound, and when I wake up she lays out my new career path. the king isn't feeding you now. you're too stupid to pickpocket. go be a smuggler. haven't I promised to get you hanged? hanging beats getting shot. chat she pitched me a life of crime like a job offer and I took it, because I thought the mountains meant I'd finally have her to myself.
beats.quote: Haven’t I promised to get you hanged? That’s better than being shot,

beats.title: Her Husband Walks In
beats.modern: captain goes, great news, new guy joining us, Carmen just broke her rom out of the galleys. her ROM. chat that word means husband. she has been married this entire fucking time. two years of working the prison surgeon to spring him. then Garcia turns up, one eye, worst man I've ever stood next to, and she calls him husband to my face while pulling little faces at me the second he looks away.

beats.title: Don't Lose The Stockings
beats.modern: ambush on the road. Remendado takes a bullet in the back and I'm hauling him up the rocks. Garcia yells don't lose the cotton stockings and puts his blunderbuss in the man's face. says nobody'd recognise him now. that night Garcia is playing CARDS by the fire like it's a normal evening. I'm on my back wishing I'd been the one who got shot. she crawls over and kisses me anyway. I said you are a devil. she said yes.
beats.quote: ‘what do we want with offal! Finish him off, and don’t lose the cotton stockings!’

beats.title: Orange-Seller
beats.modern: I go into Gibraltar undercover as a fruit guy and there she is on a balcony in silk beside an English officer with gold epaulettes. calls me up, tells me in Basque to act like I don't speak Spanish, then live-translates my death threats to him as small talk. I told her I'd love to get her milord alone on a mountain with a stick each. she told him I said I was thirsty. he laughed and ordered me a drink.
beats.quote: “‘He says he’s thirsty, and would like a drink,’

beats.title: The Card Game
beats.modern: her plan was for me to let Garcia walk in front so the Englishman would shoot him for me. I said no. we settle things Navarre style. so: I call him a cheat, throw the cards in his face, and he crouches Andalusian with his hat up to parry. I stand Navarrese, knife flat along my thigh. he flies at me, I turn off my left foot, he finds nothing there, and I go in at the throat until my hand is under his chin.
beats.quote: I felt I was stronger than any giant.

beats.title: Congrats, You're A Widow
beats.modern: next morning I take the Englishman apart on the road and win her back, and my opening line is congratulations, you're a widow. her response: you'll always be an idiot, Garcia should have killed you, your Navarrese stance is nonsense, it was just his turn. then she tells me she's read it in the coffee grounds more than once, the two of us finish together. and then she rattled her castanets about it.
beats.quote: ‘I’ve read in the coffee grounds, more than once, that you and I were to end our lives together.

beats.title: Two Doors From The Law
beats.modern: took a bullet, went down in the brush, thought I was going to die there like a shot hare. she rode in from Granada and did not leave me for a fortnight. never closed her eyes. patched me better than any army surgeon. then hid me in a house two doors from the magistrate hunting me and I watched him walk past my shutter. so I said let's go to America and live clean. she laughed in my face. we weren't born to plant cabbages.
beats.quote: “‘We were not born to plant cabbages,’

beats.title: The Picador
beats.modern: she comes back from the bullfight talking about a picador named Lucas. knows his horse's name. knows what his jacket cost. says he's a mark, we take his money or we recruit him. I said I forbid you to speak to him. she said careful, tell me not to do a thing and it gets done fast. later we fought over a stolen watch and I hit her, and she cried. first time ever. that landed worse than the bullet did.
beats.quote: It was the first time I had ever seen her cry,

beats.title: The Bull Avenged Me
beats.modern: there's a fete at Cordova, she says. she'll go scout who's carrying money, she says. then a peasant mentions there's also bullfighting. blood straight to the head, I run to the ring, and there's Lucas tearing the cockade off the bull and handing it up to her in the front row. she put it in her hair. and then the bull put Lucas on the ground with his own horse on his chest. third party. the bull avenged me.
beats.quote: “The bull avenged me.

beats.title: It Is Fate
beats.modern: I put her on the horse behind me and we rode all night without one word. at dawn I ask her to swear she'll come to America. no. I tell her I'm tired of killing her lovers so this time I'll kill her instead. she doesn't blink. says she's always known. says a priest was at her door the first day I saw her, says a hare crossed the road under my horse tonight. she was reading the omens like patch notes.
beats.quote: “‘I’ve always thought you would kill me.

beats.title: Me First, Then You
beats.modern: I'm begging now. there's a hundred and twenty gold ounces buried under an oak near here, we can go anywhere, we never have to be apart again. she doesn't answer. she's sitting cross-legged on a mat drawing in the dirt with one finger. then she smiles and says: me first, and then you. I know it will happen like that.
beats.quote: ‘Me first, and then you. I know it will happen like that.’

beats.title: The Mass And The Lead
beats.modern: I walked up to the hermitage and asked a holy man to say a mass for a soul that may be about to meet its Maker. he asked if something was on my conscience. I ran. came back praying she'd taken my horse and gone. she was still there. she had melted the lead out of her own hem and was reading it in a bowl of water, turning the little pieces over with a sad face, singing. she knew. she stayed anyway.
beats.quote: “‘Can you say a mass for a soul which is perhaps about to go into the presence of its Maker?’

beats.title: The Lonely Gorge
beats.modern: she jumps off the horse, throws her mantilla down at her feet, one hand on her hip, and says she can see I mean to kill her and I will never make her give in. I'm on my knees crying into her hands offering her everything. keep robbing, keep running, anything. she says no. she pulls the ring I gave her off her finger and throws it into the brush. I struck her twice. she fell without a sound.
beats.quote: “‘Love you again? That’s not possible! Live with you? I will not do it!’

beats.title: I Gave Myself Up
beats.modern: lay next to her an hour. she always said she wanted to be buried in a wood, so I dug it out with my knife. then I hunted the brush a long time for that ring and I found it and put it in beside her with a little cross. rode to Cordova, walked into the guard-room, told them I killed Carmen. wouldn't tell them where she is. that's the whole stream, chat.

beats.title: The Christmas Haul
beats.modern: Christmas Eve stream. Porter wanted sixpence, I gave him a shilling and said keep it, because this year we are RICH, chat. Torvald got the bank job. Then I stood in my own hallway eating macaroons like a criminal and shoved the bag in my pocket before he could hear the paper. He's calling through the door. lark. squirrel. eight years and this man has never once just said Nora.
beats.quote: Is that my little lark twittering out there?

beats.title: Pocket Money
beats.modern: he takes out his purse like it's a magic trick. ten shillings. a pound. two pounds. and I count it out loud and say thank you, thank you Torvald, that'll keep me going ages. and he beams. chat every coin of that is going straight into a hole in my life he doesn't know exists. I'm not spending it. I'm servicing it.
beats.quote: Is my little squirrel out of temper?

beats.title: Miss Sweet Tooth
beats.modern: he does a whole bit with the finger wag. has Miss Sweet Tooth been in town today? been to the confectioner's? been nibbling sweets? not even a bite at a macaroon or two? and I look my husband dead in the eyes and say no. no. certainly not. crumbs literally in my pocket. he laughs, says he was only joking, says a songbird must have a clean beak. chat I lie to this man so smoothly it frightens me.
beats.quote: Not even taken a bite at a macaroon or two?

beats.title: Christine Has Nothing
beats.modern: school friend turns up after ten years looking like she lived every one of them twice. husband dead. left her nothing. no kids. I go, so, nothing at all then? and she says not even any sorrow or grief to live upon. chat I did not have a reply to that. then she strokes my hair and says it happens sometimes, Nora. like I'M the one who needs comforting.
beats.quote: Not even any sorrow or grief to live upon.

beats.title: I Saved His Life
beats.modern: okay speak low, Torvald cannot hear this. everyone in this house believes my father paid for the Italy trip that saved my husband's life. papa gave us nothing. NOTHING. it was me. two hundred and fifty pounds, I found it, I did it, and my reward is that nobody is ever allowed to know. eight years of the biggest thing I've ever done, and you're the first people I've told.
beats.quote: It was I who saved Torvald’s life.

beats.title: Like Being A Man
beats.modern: how do you pay down a secret debt using money your husband hands you for dresses? you buy the cheap dress. every time. every year. and last winter I got copying work and locked the door and wrote until two in the morning, exhausted, and chat, I loved it. sitting there earning. it was like being a man. that is the saddest sentence I have ever said out loud and I didn't hear it until just now.
beats.quote: It was like being a man.

beats.title: Well I’m Damned
beats.modern: there is one thing I want to say more than anything on this earth. Rank says go on. Christine says Nora, dear. so I say it. WELL, I'M DAMNED. that's it. that's the whole rebellion. eight years of marriage and my most forbidden sentence is two words and a stolen biscuit.
beats.quote: I should just love to say—Well, I’m damned!

beats.title: Papa’s Signature
beats.modern: Krogstad takes the bond out of his coat, very calm, like a man reading a receipt. says there's just one small discrepancy. papa signed this three days after he died. long silence. I could lie again, I've been lying all week. instead I lift my head and look right at him. no. it was me. I wrote my dead father's name.
beats.quote: The discrepancy consists, Mrs Helmer, in the fact that your father signed this bond three days after his death.

beats.title: A Very Foolish Law
beats.modern: I told him: my father was dying, my husband was dying, I couldn't ask either of them. he said the law cares nothing about motives. so I said then it's a very foolish law and you must be a very poor lawyer. and chat, he didn't even get angry. he just said fine. if I go down a second time, you're coming with me.
beats.quote: The law cares nothing about motives.

beats.title: Deceitful Mothers
beats.modern: so my husband has THOUGHTS about forgers tonight. a man like that wears a mask in front of his own children, every breath in that house is full of the germs of evil. and then, unprompted, he says almost everyone who goes bad had a deceitful mother. holds out his hand. promise me you won't defend Krogstad. I take my hand out of his and walk to the other side of the tree. it's very hot in here. am I poisoning my kids? no. it isn't true. it can't possibly be true.
beats.quote: Almost everyone who has gone to the bad early in life has had a deceitful mother.

beats.title: Krogstad’s Dismissal
beats.modern: I made ONE mistake. I called his reasoning narrow-minded. wrong word, chat. he goes narrow-minded? and calls the maid, and hands her a letter, and says be quick. what was that, Torvald. answer: Krogstad's dismissal. call her back. Torvald call her back, for my sake, for the children's, you have no idea what that letter does to us. he says it's too late. then he hugs me, because he thinks the terror on my face is how much I love him.
beats.quote: Krogstad’s dismissal.

beats.title: The Black Cross
beats.modern: Rank came round to tell me he's dying. spine. inherited it off a father who ate and drank his way through everything, so he's paying a bill he never ran up. says within a month he'll be rotting in the churchyard. and when he's certain, he'll send a card with a black cross on it, and that's how I'll know it's begun. he's barring the door to Torvald. says Torvald can't stand anything ugly.
beats.quote: Probably within a month I shall lie rotting in the churchyard.

beats.title: Flesh-Coloured Stockings
beats.modern: showed Rank my silk stockings. flesh-coloured. told him he may only look at the feet. okay fine, the legs too. he goes hm. so I hit him on the ear with them and said that's your punishment. chat, in my defence, I am about to ask this man for an enormous amount of money and I was warming him up. not proud of it. not stopping either.
beats.quote: Oh well, you may have leave to look at the legs too.

beats.title: Rank Says It Out Loud
beats.modern: I'm two sentences from asking for the money. TWO. and he leans in and says Torvald isn't the only one who'd give his life for me. and just like that the door shuts.
