I can't ask him now, not ever, because taking it would mean something. so I stood up and called for the lamp. lights on. everybody see everybody. that was really horrid of you, Doctor Rank. he was only being honest and it cost me everything.
beats.quote: The only one who would gladly give his life for your sake.

beats.title: You Must Be My Witness
beats.modern: Christine. come here. see that letter in the box? you don't know all of it. I forged a name. now listen, because I need you for one thing: if I lose my mind, or if something happens to me, or if ANYONE stands up and tries to take this on themselves, you testify. I was in my right senses. nobody else knew. I, and I alone, did the whole thing. remember that.
beats.quote: I, and I alone, did the whole thing. Remember that.

beats.title: Dancing For My Life
beats.modern: shawl on, tambourine up, PLAY. he's at the piano shouting slower, slower, not so violently, that's not a bit right. hair comes down over my shoulders and I leave it. Christine is frozen in the doorway. Rank takes over the keys and I go harder. and Torvald says darling you're dancing as if your life depended on it. yeah. it does. every second he's watching me is a second he isn't opening that letterbox.
beats.quote: My dear darling Nora, you are dancing as if your life depended on it.

beats.title: Thirty-One Hours
beats.modern: five o'clock. seven hours to midnight. twenty-four more to the next one. so. thirty-one hours to live. and then from the doorway: where's my little skylark? and I put my arms out and walk in and say here she is.
beats.quote: Twenty-four and seven? Thirty-one hours to live.

beats.title: Two Shipwrecked People
beats.modern: lore drop I did not see coming: Christine and Krogstad were engaged once. she left him for a richer man because her mother and her brothers were starving. tonight she sits him down and offers to start again. two shipwrecked people on the same bit of wreckage do better than one. and this man, who has been squeezing my throat all week, just says he's never had such luck in his life. everyone in this house gets a second chance tonight except me.
beats.quote: Two on the same piece of wreckage would stand a better chance than each on their own.

beats.title: The Invisible Hat
beats.modern: Rank stopped in after the ball for one last cigar. Torvald asks what he'll wear to the next fancy-dress and he says: invisible. there's a big black hat, you put it on, nobody can see you. everyone laughed. I struck the match and held it for him. said sleep well, Doctor Rank. he said thank you for that wish. chat he is standing in that doorway saying goodbye forever and I am the only person in the room who knows it.
beats.quote: At the next fancy-dress ball I shall be invisible.

beats.title: Torvald Reads It
beats.modern: I had the shawl over my head and the black water in my mouth. never see my children again. never. and then his door opens and he's holding the letter. eight years of lark and squirrel and songbird, and tonight I am a miserable creature. a hypocrite. a liar. a criminal. my father's rot coming out in me. not one question about why I did it. and then the line that ended it: I have to sink to these depths because of a thoughtless woman. I saved his life and I'm the thoughtless one.
beats.quote: Miserable creature—what have you done?

beats.title: I Am Saved
beats.modern: second letter. Krogstad sent the bond back. it's over, we're clear, nobody's ruined. Torvald reads it and SHOUTS: I am saved! Nora, I am saved! and I said: and I? and he goes oh, you too, of course, obviously. then he throws my bond in the stove and stands there watching it burn and says the whole thing will be nothing but a bad dream to him. it ended for him in ninety seconds, chat. it had only just started for me.
beats.quote: Yes, it is true! I am saved! Nora, I am saved!

beats.title: Forgiven, Freely
beats.modern: now he's magnanimous. he forgives me. he says it about nine times. explains that forgiving your wife is one of the sweetest feelings available to a man, that it makes her doubly his, that he has basically given me a new life so now I'm his wife AND his child. broad wings. hunted dove. little scared helpless darling. I said thank you for your forgiveness, and went into the other room, and took the costume off.
beats.quote: There is something so indescribably sweet and satisfying, to a man, in the knowledge that he has forgiven his wife—forgiven

beats.title: The Doll House
beats.modern: sit down, Torvald. we have been married eight years and this is the first serious conversation we have ever had. papa called me his doll-child and played with me. then I was handed over to you and I performed for you. your opinions became my opinions. this was never a home, it was a playroom, and I was the doll-wife in it, and I made our children my dolls in turn. no I haven't been happy. I've been merry. those are not the same thing.
beats.quote: our home has been nothing but a playroom. I have been your doll-wife, just as at home I was papa’s doll-child; and here the children have been my dolls.

beats.title: Duties To Myself
beats.modern: he says leaving means deserting my most sacred duties, my duties to my husband and my children, and what will people say. I said I have other duties just as sacred. duties to myself. he says before all else you are a wife and a mother. I don't believe that anymore. before all else I am a person with a mind, exactly like him, and I am going out there to find out which of us is right, me or the entire world.
beats.quote: I believe that before all else I am a reasonable human being, just as you are—or,

beats.title: The Door
beats.modern: here is your ring. give me mine. keys are on the table. no you can't write to me. no I can't take anything from you, I don't take things from strangers. he asks what would have to change. both of us. so much that living together would be an actual marriage. I don't believe in wonderful things anymore, Torvald. goodbye. and I walk out, and behind me he's in a chair with his face in his hands going: the most wonderful thing of all—?
beats.quote: That our life together would be a real wedlock. Goodbye.

beats.title: The Guy Who Moved In
beats.modern: chat there is a brown old sailor standing in my dad's inn with a sea chest on a barrow and a sabre scar down one cheek, singing about dead men. throws gold on the floor. says you mought call me captain. drinks his rum slow like a wine guy while he scopes out the cliffs. congratulations to us. the Admiral Benbow has a resident now.
beats.quote: “Fifteen men on the dead man’s chest-- Yo-ho-ho, and a bottle of rum!”

beats.title: Weather-Eye Open
beats.modern: he pays me four pence a month for one job: watch the road for a seafaring man with one leg. that's the entire contract. now I dream about him every single night, hopping over hedges after me, sometimes with the leg in the MIDDLE of his body. worst paid gig in England and I'm doing overtime in my sleep.

beats.title: Black Dog As Ever Was
beats.modern: an old shipmate walks in and says Bill. the captain turns the colour of a corpse. two seconds later it's cutlasses out, table over, and the guy is sprinting up the road bleeding from the shoulder. then the captain asks me for rum and hits the floor. doctor takes one look: that's not a wound, chat. that's a stroke. he called it a week ago.
beats.quote: “Black Dog as ever was, come for to see his old shipmate Billy,

beats.title: Meat And Drink And Man And Wife
beats.modern: he's begging me for rum from his sickbed. says doctors is all swabs. says he's seeing old Flint standing in the corner behind me. says rum has been meat and drink and man and wife to him, which is the saddest bio I've ever heard. offers me a gold guinea for one glass. I brought him one and refused the money. he already owes my father months.
beats.quote: It’s been meat and drink, and man and wife, to me;

beats.title: Old Flint's First Mate
beats.modern: the lore drops out of him all at once. he sailed with Flint. he WAS Flint's first mate. Flint handed him the location at Savannah while he was dying, and now every pirate breathing wants what's inside that chest upstairs. if they tip him the black spot I'm to get on a horse and ride for the doctor. he offers me an equal share on his honour. sure.
beats.quote: He gave it me at Savannah, when he lay a-dying,

beats.title: The Blind Man's Grip
beats.modern: blind beggar on the road asks for a hand. I give him one. he clamps down like a vise and tells me to walk him in to the captain or he snaps my arm. chat I have never been more afraid of anything in my life, and I live with a pirate. I walked him in. my voice was shaking on the line he made me say.

beats.title: Six Hours
beats.modern: the blind man presses something into the captain's palm and taps away down the road. captain opens his hand. black spot. ten o'clock, six hours, we'll do them yet, he says, and stands up, and goes down face first from his full height. dead. I never liked him. I'd only just started pitying him. I cried anyway.
beats.quote: “Six hours. We’ll do them yet,”

beats.title: Not A Farthing Over
beats.modern: we are upstairs in a dead man's chest counting coins by candlelight and the blind man's stick starts tapping at our front door. I say take the whole bag and RUN. my mother says she will have exactly what she is owed and not one farthing over. mom. MOM. he is trying the handle.

beats.title: They Left Old Pew
beats.modern: his own crew hears the danger signal and scatters in every direction and just leaves the blind man standing in the road, tapping in circles, calling their names. Johnny. Black Dog. Dirk. you won't leave old Pew, mates. then the horses came over the hill and he ran the wrong way.

beats.title: Bulk Of Treasure Here
beats.modern: doctor cuts the stitches and out falls a map. island nine miles by five, shaped like a fat dragon standing up, big hill in the middle called the Spy-glass. three red crosses. and beside the last one, in small neat handwriting that isn't the captain's: bulk of treasure here. the squire is already buying a ship in his head.
beats.quote: “Bulk of treasure here.”

beats.title: The Sign Of The Spy-glass
beats.modern: meet the ship's cook. left leg gone at the hip, hops around on a crutch like a bird, face as big as a ham, whole tavern loves him. and I have spent two years watching the road for a one-legged sailor. one look at this clean, smiling, pleasant landlord and I cleared him. instantly. no notes. no follow-up questions.

beats.title: The Captain Hates This Cruise
beats.modern: new captain comes down to the cabin and opens with: I don't like this cruise, I don't like the men, I don't like my officer. says every hand before the mast knows more about the voyage than he does and the secret's been told to the parrot. everyone decides he's insufferable. he is right about every damn thing.
beats.quote: I don’t like this cruise; I don’t like the men; and I don’t like my officer.

beats.title: Cap'n Flint Wants Pieces Of Eight
beats.modern: the cook keeps his galley clean as a new pin and a parrot in the corner named after the worst pirate who ever lived. two hundred years old, present at every robbery in the Caribbean, screams PIECES OF EIGHT until he throws a handkerchief over the cage. he feeds her sugar out of his pocket. I thought he was the best man alive.
beats.quote: “Pieces of eight! Pieces of eight! Pieces of eight!”

beats.title: The Apple Barrel
beats.modern: climbed into the apple barrel for a snack and nearly fell asleep in it. then a heavy man sits down against the side and starts talking, and it's the cook's voice, and inside twelve words I understand that every honest life on this ship is now sitting in a barrel with me.

beats.title: Gentlemen Of Fortune
beats.modern: so he's not a cook. he was Flint's quartermaster, and he's out here pitching the business model to a teenager: the others blow it all on rum and die begging, but he banks it, some here some there, and at fifty he retires a gentleman. then the flex. some were feared of Pew. some were feared of Flint. Flint himself was feared of ME.
beats.quote: but Flint his own self was feared of me.

beats.title: I Give My Vote, Death
beats.modern: the kid asks what they'll actually do with us. maroon us, England's way? cut us down like pork, Flint's way? and Silver takes his time and says dooty is dooty, mates. I give my vote, death. then, pleasant as anything: Dick, jump up like a sweet lad and fetch me an apple. THE APPLE. THE BARREL. I stopped fucking breathing.
beats.quote: Dooty is dooty, mates. I give my vote--death.

beats.title: The Crutch
beats.modern: I stowed away in the pirates' boat and now I'm face down in a bush watching. an honest sailor tells Silver straight out: you killed Alan, kill me too, I defy you. turns his back and walks away. Silver grabs a branch, whips the crutch out from under his own arm and throws it like a spear. broke the man's back. then he was on top of him with a knife, twice, and I could hear him panting from where I lay.
beats.quote: If I die like a dog, I’ll die in my dooty.

beats.title: Ben Gunn Dreams Of Cheese
beats.modern: something is following me through the trees, running on two legs but bent almost double. bear? monkey? no. it's a man in goatskins who drops to his knees and says he's poor Ben Gunn and he hasn't spoken to another person in three years. marooned. living on goats and berries and oysters. and the first thing he asks me for isn't rescue. it's cheese. toasted, mostly.
beats.quote: “I’m poor Ben Gunn, I am; and I haven’t spoke with a Christian these three years.”

beats.title: Tom Redruth Goes Home
beats.modern: shot out of the bushes on our way into the stockade. old gamekeeper, oldest man in our party, never complained once the whole voyage. the squire is on his knees kissing his hand and crying like a child and begging to be forgiven, and Tom just says would that be respectful, sir, from me to you. his last request was that somebody read a prayer. it's the custom, sir.
beats.quote: “I wish I had had a lick at them with the gun first,”

beats.title: Silver's Embassy
beats.modern: he comes up under a white flag calling himself Cap'n Silver and offers us terms. the captain hears him out, stands up, knocks his pipe out on his palm and says: come up one by one unarmed and I'll take you home to a fair trial, or I put a bullet in your back next time I see you. then nobody would help Silver stand up. he spat in our spring on the way out.
beats.quote: I’ll put a bullet in your back when next I meet you.

beats.title: Cutlasses
beats.modern: they came over the fence like monkeys. house full of smoke, somebody opened my knuckles grabbing for a blade, the captain screaming get out and fight them in the open. I run round the corner straight into the boatswain with his hanger already coming down, miss my footing in the sand and roll all the way down the slope. by the time I stood up it was over and we'd won.

beats.title: I Cut The Cable
beats.modern: took a goatskin canoe roughly the size of a bathtub out into the fog and paddled at the ship. hawser tight as a bowstring. two drunks screaming at each other in the cabin, the whole pirate camp singing about dead men on the shore, and me sawing through the rope one strand at a time until two hundred tons of schooner swung loose in the dark.

beats.title: Cap'n Hawkins
beats.modern: the two watchmen killed each other over the rum. one is still breathing so I fetch him brandy and inform him that I have come aboard to take possession of this ship and he will please regard me as his captain until further notice. then I hauled down the Jolly Roger and threw it in the sea. God save the king. and there's an end to Captain Silver.
beats.quote: “And there’s an end to Captain Silver!”

beats.title: Dead Men Don't Bite
beats.modern: he came at me with the dirk so I went up the rigging and reloaded both pistols where he could watch me do it. one more step and I blow your brains out. dead men don't bite, I said, extremely pleased with myself. he says fine, you win, we'll sign articles, and while I'm grinning his hand goes back over his shoulder and I am nailed to the mast through the shoulder. both pistols went off on their own. he went into the water and stayed there.
beats.quote: Dead men don’t bite, you know,”

beats.title: Pieces Of Eight
beats.modern: walk into the block house in the pitch dark, smug as anything, planning to lie down in my usual spot and enjoy their faces in the morning. step over somebody's sleeping leg. and then out of the black: PIECES OF EIGHT PIECES OF EIGHT PIECES OF EIGHT. the parrot. a bird kept better watch than six grown men. then Silver's voice out of the dark: who goes.
beats.quote: “Pieces of eight! Pieces of eight! Pieces of eight! Pieces of eight!

beats.title: The Laugh's On My Side
beats.modern: six pirates, one me, back against the wall. so I told them everything. I was in the apple barrel and I heard every word you said. I cut your cable. I killed the men you left aboard her. I put your ship somewhere none of you will ever see it again. kill me or spare me, but spare me and you've got a witness when you're all in court. the whole room stared at me like sheep.
beats.quote: The laugh’s on my side; I’ve had the top of this business from the first;

beats.title: Half A Plank Of Death
beats.modern: they all file out to hold a council about killing us both. door shuts and he leans in and whispers: you're within half a plank of death, and a long sight worse, of torture. I stand by you now. you save your witness and he'll save your neck. back to back. and I shook on it with the man who murdered Tom in front of me.
beats.quote: Back to back, says I. You save your witness, and he’ll save your neck!”

beats.title: I Passed My Word
beats.modern: the doctor gets me alone at the fence and says jump. one jump and you're out and we run for it like antelopes. and I said no. I gave Silver my word. so instead I told him where I'd hidden the ship. he goes quiet and says every step of this it's been you saving our lives, and do you suppose we're going to let you lose yours.
beats.quote: Silver trusted me; I passed my word, and back I go.

beats.title: Flint's Pointer
beats.modern: skeleton at the foot of a pine. laid out perfectly straight, feet pointing one way, arms over the head like a diver pointing the other. Silver takes a compass bearing along the bones and it reads exactly at Skeleton Island. Flint killed all six of his diggers and then arranged one of them into a signpost. six they were, says Silver. and six are we.
beats.quote: Six they were, and six are we; and bones is what they are now.”

beats.title: The Voice Among The Trees
beats.modern: out of the middle of the trees, a thin high voice starts singing fifteen men on the dead man's chest. six grown pirates went white as paper. Morgan is flat on the ground. then it wails DARBY M'GRAW, FETCH AFT THE RUM, which were Flint's actual last words before he died. Silver's teeth are rattling in his skull and he STILL stands there arguing that no ghost has an echo.
beats.quote: sound--“Darby M’Graw! Darby M’Graw!”

beats.title: Seven Hundred Thousand Pounds
beats.modern: they sprint the last twenty yards and stop dead. there's a hole. old one, sides fallen in, grass growing in the bottom, a snapped pick shaft and busted packing cases with WALRUS branded on the boards. the cache was found and emptied. seven hundred thousand pounds, gone. every man's entire life plan deleted in one second.

beats.title: I Reckon I Settled You
beats.modern: Merry is mid-speech about cutting my heart out when three muskets go off in the thicket and he falls headfirst into the pit. Silver empties both barrels of a pistol into him while he's still moving and says George, I reckon I settled you. then the doctor, Gray and Ben Gunn walk out of the nutmeg trees with smoking guns. Silver has been on our side for approximately four seconds.
beats.quote: “I reckon I settled you.”

beats.title: Ben Gunn Had It The Whole Time
beats.modern: the maroon everybody laughed at found the skeleton, found the treasure, dug it up on his own and carried seven hundred thousand pounds on his back to a cave, load by load, weary trip by weary trip, two months before our ship ever showed up. that's why the doctor handed Silver the chart. the chart was worthless. Ben, Ben, says Silver. to think as you've done me.
beats.quote: “to think as you’ve done me!”

beats.title: Silver Was Gone
beats.modern: we anchor in a port in Spanish America, go ashore for one evening, come back at daybreak and Ben Gunn confesses he let Silver slip off in a shore boat hours ago. and the sea cook did not leave empty handed. he cut through a bulkhead and took a sack of coin worth three or four hundred guineas. honestly? every one of us was relieved.
beats.quote: “that man with the one leg had stayed aboard.”

beats.title: Pieces Of Eight, Forever
beats.modern: the bar silver and the guns are still buried out there and they can stay buried. oxen and wagon ropes wouldn't drag me back to that island. we all got our share and we all spent it exactly like ourselves. and the worst dreams I still have are the surf booming on those coasts, and that voice going PIECES OF EIGHT. PIECES OF EIGHT.
beats.quote: “Pieces of eight! Pieces of eight!”

beats.title: The Golden Apple Thief
beats.modern: king's got a tree that grows GOLD apples and he counts them nightly. one goes missing every night. gardener's youngest finally stays up, catches the thief mid-bite, shoots it. arrow does nothing. the thief is a bird made of solid gold and it drops ONE feather leaving. council says that feather's worth more than the entire kingdom. king says cool. I want the whole bird.

beats.title: Do Not Pick The Nice Inn
beats.modern: talking fox spawns with free advice: two inns in the next village, one gorgeous, one filthy. sleep in the filthy one. eldest brother goes what would a fox know, shoots at him, misses, then walks straight into the party house. eats, drinks, forgets the bird, forgets his country, forgets his whole quest. the tutorial hint was RIGHT THERE, chat.

beats.title: The Fox Was Family
beats.modern: years later the fox finds him in the wood and begs, with tears in his eyes, to be killed. cut off my head. cut off my feet. he finally does it and the fox stands up as a man: the princess's brother, missing for years. chat the helper NPC was a person the entire run and the only way to log him out was that.

beats.title: The Downgrade Speedrun
beats.modern: seven years of wages, traded for a horse. horse for a cow. cow for a pig. pig for a goose. goose for a ROCK. then he leans down for a drink, knocks the rock into the river, and falls on his knees crying with joy that it's gone. walks home with nothing and tells his mother how easy the road to good luck is. is he winning? chat I genuinely can't tell.

beats.title: Worst Band In The Forest
beats.modern: donkey, dog, cat and rooster stack themselves into one tall animal outside a robbers' house and start SCREAMING through the window, then fall through it in a shower of glass. robbers assume demon and evacuate the building at speed. four unemployed animals just cleared a house with vocals only, ate the whole dinner, and moved in permanently.

beats.title: The Thirteenth Fairy
beats.modern: twelve fairies show up and buff the baby one by one. eleven done, and then number thirteen kicks the door in furious about the guest list and hard-codes it: fifteenth year, spindle, dead. the last fairy can't delete the curse, only nerf it. not dead. asleep. a hundred years. king's fix is to burn every spindle in the kingdom, which is not how curses work.

beats.title: The Whole Castle Went AFK
beats.modern: she touches the spindle and drops. and the whole server drops with her. king, queen, court, horses in the stable, dogs in the yard, pigeons on the roof, the FLIES on the walls. the fire stops burning mid-blaze. the butler freezes with the jug at his lips. the cook was mid ear-slap on the kitchen boy and just stops there, hand up, for a century.

beats.title: Everyone Before Him Died
beats.modern: that thorn hedge ate every prince who tried it. they got grabbed like it had hands and died stuck in there. this guy walks up on the exact day the hundred years end and the thorns just open into flowers for him. zero skill. pure patch timing. he kisses her, and the whole castle boots back up: the flies buzz, the spit turns, and the cook finally lands that slap.

beats.title: Invisible At The Rave
beats.modern: soldier fakes the sleeping draught, throws on the invisibility cloak, and follows twelve princesses through a trapdoor under a bed. silver forest, gold forest, diamond forest, he snaps a branch off each for receipts. then he's in the boat, in the ballroom, dancing invisible, and drinking their wine so every cup is empty when it reaches their lips. the youngest keeps saying something's wrong. the eldest keeps telling her it's nothing.

beats.title: Lord Of Sun And Moon
beats.modern: she's already pope. throne two miles high, three crowns, the entire church stood round her. her husband goes babe, that's the ceiling, there is nothing above this. she lies awake all night about it, sees the sun come up without her permission, and sends him back to the sea in a black storm to demand control of the sunrise. fish says: go home to your pigsty. and that's where they live to this day.

beats.title: Three Nights On The Pillow
beats.modern: her dad makes her honour the deal, so the frog eats off her plate and sleeps on her pillow, and she hates every second of it. three nights. fourth morning she opens her eyes and there's a whole prince standing at the head of her bed with the best eyes she's ever seen. cursed by a spiteful fairy, unlocked by three nights of keeping your word.

beats.title: Top-off, Half-done, All-gone
beats.modern: the cat keeps getting invited to be godmother at christenings. she is not. she's going to the church to eat their shared winter fat, and she names the fake babies Top-off, Half-done and All-gone, which is just her narrating the pot draining. winter comes, jar's empty, and the mouse works it out and says the third name out loud. the cat eats her too. verily, that is the way of the world.

beats.title: Falada On The Gate
beats.modern: the maid took her horse, her clothes, her whole identity, and married the prince as her. then she asks her new husband for one small favour: kill the horse. because the horse WATCHED it happen. so the real princess pays the butcher to nail Falada's head above the dark gate she walks through twice a day. that's the only friend she has left and he's a head on a wall.

beats.title: She Sentenced Herself
beats.modern: the old king tells the whole story at the feast like it's just a story he heard once, then turns to the fake bride and asks what should be done to a woman like that. she doesn't recognise her own crimes. she picks something horrific: a cask stuck with nails, dragged through the streets by two white horses. and the king goes: thou art she. as thou hast judged thyself.
beats.quote: ‘Thou art she!’

beats.title: The Ladder Was Her Hair
beats.modern: the witch took the baby as payment for stolen greens, and at twelve she puts her in a tower with no stairs and no door. one window, way up. the only way in or out is the girl's own hair, twenty ells of it, wound round a hook and dropped. everyone remembers the rhyme. nobody remembers that the ladder is her body and someone climbs it daily.

beats.title: Snip, Snap
beats.modern: she blows it herself. asks the witch, out loud, why she's so much heavier to pull up than the young king's son. chat. CHAT. the witch grabs the braids, wraps them round her left hand twice, scissors in the right, snip snap, and the hair is on the floor. then she's dumped in a desert to live in misery. worst slip of the tongue in the entire book.

beats.title: He Jumped From The Tower
beats.modern: he climbs the hair and it's the witch at the top, smiling, telling him the bird is gone from the nest. he throws himself off the tower. survives the fall. the thorns take his eyes. years blind in the forest eating roots, and then he hears a voice he knows, and it's her, in the desert, with their twins. she cries onto his eyes and he sees again.

beats.title: Seven At One Stroke
beats.modern: flies land on his jam sandwich, he swats once, counts the bodies: seven. SEVEN. so he immediately cuts himself a belt, embroiders SEVEN AT ONE STROKE on it in big letters, and leaves town because the workshop is too small for his valour. he never actually lies. he just walks around letting the world assume he means men.
beats.quote: ‘Seven at one stroke!’

beats.title: The Bed Was Too Big
beats.modern: he squeezes a cheese and calls it a rock. throws a bird and calls it a stone. the giants buy every bit of it. at midnight one of them drives an iron bar clean through the bed he's supposed to be sleeping in. he's asleep in the corner. strolls out at dawn saying morning lads, and grown giants run for their lives from a man who makes trousers.

beats.title: The Birds Ate The Crumbs
beats.modern: night one he lined the path with white pebbles and walked them home by moonlight. night two the door's locked, so all he's got is his own bread, and he drops it crumb by crumb, telling his dad he's waving goodbye to a pigeon on the roof. moon comes up. path's empty. every bird in the forest ate the way home. two kids, three days, two berries between them.

beats.title: Show Me How You Get In
beats.modern: four weeks of the witch fattening him while his sister eats crab shells, and every morning he pokes a chicken bone through the bars because her eyes are bad. she runs out of patience and lights the oven. tells Gretel to climb in and check the heat. Gretel goes: I don't understand, how do I even get in? the witch leans in to demonstrate. push. bolt. done.

beats.title: The Job Swap Wipe
beats.modern: mouse, bird and sausage share a house with the chores split and it WORKS. then another bird tells the bird he's being played, so he demands a rotation. sausage goes out for firewood and gets eaten by a dog. mouse tries the sausage's job and dies in the soup. bird panics, sets the floor on fire, drops the bucket down the well and goes in after it. one shift change. total party wipe.

beats.title: Gold Girl, Pitch Girl
beats.modern: the hardworking sister came home covered head to foot in gold, so mum ships the lazy one down the well for the same payout. day one she's great. day two she's dawdling. day three she won't get out of bed or shake the feather beds. Mother Holle fires her and walks her to the same gate, and instead of gold she catches a full bucket of pitch. never came off. wore it the rest of her life.

beats.title: What Big Teeth
beats.modern: door's open, house feels wrong, and grandma is WRONG. big ears. big eyes. big hands. she asks about the mouth and gets an honest answer and one bound later she's gone. then the wolf naps so loudly a huntsman comes in to check on the old woman, sees who's in the bed, and instead of firing takes SCISSORS to the belly. two snips: red cap. two more: grandma. then they fill him with stones.
beats.quote: ‘The better to eat you with!’

beats.title: The Finger In Her Lap
beats.modern: she's crouched behind a barrel in her fiancé's cellar watching his crew drag in another girl, pour three wines into her, and cut her up on the table. one of them wants a ring off the dead girl's hand, can't get it, takes a hatchet to the finger, and the finger flies across the room and lands in HER LAP. they start searching. the old woman says eat first, the finger won't run away.

beats.title: This Is Only A Dream
beats.modern: wedding feast, every guest tells a tale, and she says she'll tell a dream. then she narrates his murder house room by room, in front of everyone he invited, while he sits there going my darling, this is only a dream after every single line, getting paler each time. she reaches the finger. says here is the finger. and puts it on the table.
beats.quote: ‘My darling, this is only a dream.’

beats.title: Places I Have Been
beats.modern: Tom's month, in order: mouse-hole, snail-shell, swallowed by a cow, cow gets killed for being haunted, thrown out on a dunghill, swallowed by a WOLF. so he talks the wolf into raiding his own parents' pantry until it's too fat to fit back out the drain, then screams the house awake. dad kills it, cuts it open, and Tom's first words are that he's glad of the fresh air.

beats.title: He Sang His Own Name
beats.modern: she signed away her firstborn for one more night of spun gold and now he's here to collect. three days to guess his name. she burns two of them on every name in the kingdom plus every joke name she can find. then a messenger sees a little man dancing round a fire in the woods SINGING HIS OWN NAME into the night air. she says it back to him. he stamps his leg through the floor.
beats.quote: Rumpelstiltskin is my name!”

beats.title: Just One, Just One
beats.modern: Gretel is roasting two chickens for her master's guest and taste-tests her way through both of them and half the cellar. guest knocks. she whispers that the master is sharpening that knife to cut off his EARS, run. guest runs. then she tells the master the guest stole both birds, and he sprints down the road with the knife shouting just one! just one! meaning chicken. the guest hears ear.

beats.title: The Little Wooden Trough
beats.modern: they put grandpa behind the stove because his hands shake and he spills. gave him a cheap wooden bowl after he broke the good one. then their four year old is on the floor fitting bits of wood together, and when they ask what he's making he says a little trough, for father and mother to eat out of when I'm big. they looked at each other and cried. grandpa ate at the table after that.

beats.title: One Side Was Good
beats.modern: the mirror will not stop ratting the girl out, so the queen comes to the dwarfs' door a third time dressed as a peasant with an apple. Snowdrop won't take it. so the queen bites half in front of her, because the apple was built for exactly this: one clean side, one poisoned side. one bite and she's on the floor. queen goes home, asks the glass, gets the answer she wanted, and her wicked heart is happy.

beats.title: A Coffin Made Of Glass
beats.modern: the dwarfs won't bury her because she still looks alive, so they build a coffin of glass, write her name on it in gold, and one of them sits with her at all times. an owl comes. then a raven. then a dove. a prince begs for the coffin, lifts it, and the piece of apple falls out of her mouth. she sits up asking where she is. the queen turns up to the wedding, sees the bride, and drops dead on the spot.

beats.title: The Pickaxe Doom Spiral
beats.modern: Elsie goes down for beer, spots a pickaxe left in the cellar wall, and reasons it out: if I marry Hans, and we have a son, and he grows up, and we send him down here for beer, that pickaxe kills him. then sits and SCREAMS. the maid comes down, agrees, joins in. then the boy. then the mother. then the father. five adults sobbing in a cellar over a hypothetical child, and Hans comes down, hears it, and marries her.

beats.title: Is It I, Or Is It Not I
beats.modern: she naps in the field instead of harvesting, so Hans quietly drapes a fowler's net of little bells over her while she sleeps and goes home. she wakes in the dark jingling with every step and genuinely cannot establish whether she is still herself. knocks on her own door and asks: Hans, is Elsie inside? he says yes. she accepts that as proof, and runs out of the village. never seen again.

beats.title: Dancing At The Gallows
beats.modern: the miser lied him onto the gallows, so with the rope basically on he asks for one last tune on the fiddle. the miser SCREAMS at the judge not to allow it and begs to be tied down. judge allows it. first note, the court starts capering. second note, the hangman lets go of his prisoner to dance. by the end of the bar it's judge, clerks, crowd and miser, all going, all begging him to stop. he gets his life and the hundred florins back.

beats.title: Stones In The Belly
beats.modern: mum goat comes home to a wrecked house and six missing kids, and one small voice from inside the clock case. they find the wolf asleep under a tree and his stomach is MOVING. she cuts it open with scissors and all six climb out alive because he was too greedy to chew. then they fill him with rocks and she sews him shut while he snores. he wakes up thirsty, rattles to the well, and goes straight in.

beats.title: The Millstone
beats.modern: the bird keeps singing that song outside the house until they come out one at a time. father gets a gold chain that lands perfectly round his neck. Marleen gets red shoes and dances in them. the stepmother says she'll go out too, saying she feels like the world is ending, and the second she crosses the threshold the bird drops a millstone. the fire and mist clear and the little brother is standing there, holding their hands.

beats.title: A Hundred Arts
beats.modern: fox brags he's master of a hundred arts plus a whole sack of cunning, and calls the cat a hungry mouse-hunter for knowing one trick. hunter arrives with four dogs. cat is up the tree instantly. the fox is still picking which of the hundred to use when the dogs get him, and the cat calls down: open your sack, Mr Fox. one trick you actually execute beats a hundred you theorise about.

beats.title: The Sticky Conga Line
beats.modern: Dummling shares his sad cinder-cake with an old grey man and gets a goose with golden feathers out of it. innkeeper's daughter grabs a feather: hand welds on. sister two touches her: stuck. sister three: stuck. the parson tries to pull them off: stuck. the sexton grabs the parson: stuck. two labourers: stuck. seven people dragged across the fields behind one guy and a bird, and the princess who has never laughed once in her life absolutely loses it.

beats.title: I Want To Learn Shuddering
beats.modern: everyone in this house gets the creeps off graveyards and ghost stories, and one kid sits in the corner genuinely baffled about what they all mean. so when dad says pick a trade, he says he'd like to learn how to shudder, since he doesn't understand that at all yet. his brother calls him a blockhead. his father sighs and says you'll learn it, but you won't earn your bread by it.

beats.title: A Bucket Of Fish
beats.modern: he out-wrestled a ghost, split an anvil, trapped an old spirit by the beard until it handed over three chests of gold, saved the castle, married the princess, became king. and still walks round the palace muttering if I could but shudder. his wife has had ENOUGH. pulls the blanket off him at night and dumps a bucket of cold water and live fish over him. he sits up: ah, NOW I know. quest complete.
beats.quote: ‘If I could but shudder--if I could but shudder.’

beats.title: His Beard Is A Mop
beats.modern: her father lines up every suitor by rank and she walks the row roasting all of them. too fat: round as a tub. too tall: maypole. too short: dumpling. too pale, too red, too bent. then she gets to a perfectly decent king and says his beard's like an old mop, and names him Grisly-beard in front of the room. her dad, watching this happen, swears she'll marry the next man through the door, prince or beggar.

beats.title: I Am The Fiddler
beats.modern: she's a kitchen maid now, carrying leftovers home in a basket, and the prince at the wedding takes her hand for a dance. it's Grisly-beard. the basket opens, the meat goes everywhere, the whole court laughs. he catches her on the steps and says: I was the fiddler. I was the drunk soldier who smashed your stall. all of it was me, because I loved you and your pride had to go. entire alt-account arc.

beats.title: Eat Them Instead
beats.modern: these two girls have now saved that dwarf from a tree, a fishing line and an EAGLE, and every single time he screams at them about his coat. then a bear comes out of the forest and he instantly offers them up: take these two wicked girls, they're tender, fat as young quails, eat them for mercy's sake. the bear doesn't even answer him. one swipe and he never moves again.

beats.title: The Bearskin Falls Off
beats.modern: the bear calls them back by name and the skin drops off him: king's son, dressed all in gold, cursed by the dwarf who stole his treasure and only free now that the dwarf is dead. Snow-white marries him, Rose-red marries his brother, and their mother takes the two rose trees with her and they flower white and red at her window every year. gg chat. that's the book.

the-extraordinary-adventures-of-arsne.title: The Extraordinary Adventures of Arsène Lupin, Gentleman-Burglar
the-extraordinary-adventures-of-arsne.author: Maurice Leblanc

beats.title: The Wireless Drop
beats.modern: chat someone just radioed the entire ship. Arsène Lupin is aboard, first cabin, blonde, wound on the right forearm, traveling alone under a name starting with R. then lightning eats the signal and the rest of the name never arrives. four hundred passengers now playing werewolf for five days straight. and yes. all four of those details are me.
beats.quote: “Arsène Lupin is on your vessel, first cabin, blonde hair, wound right fore-arm, traveling alone under name of R........”

beats.title: Thirteen Names On The List
beats.modern: so I volunteer to run the manhunt. pull the passenger list, thirteen names starting with R, nine of them traveling with family, that leaves four, three get cleared in about ten seconds. what remains is one quiet blonde man who has been sitting a little too close to Miss Nelly. he goes white and says fine, arrest me then. chat I have never been more helpful.
beats.quote: “Because, considering my name, my position as a solitary traveler and the color of my hair, I have already reached the same conclusion, and now think that I should be arrested.”

beats.title: Ten Thousand Francs Accepted
beats.modern: the man I framed posts ten thousand francs for anyone who unmasks Arsène Lupin. that night they find him in the dark end of the deck, head wrapped in a scarf, hands corded, pocketbook gone, and a card pinned to his coat accepting his own reward with pleasure. the pocketbook held twenty thousand. he paid the bounty and the tip.
beats.quote: “Arsène Lupin accepts with pleasure the ten thousand francs offered by Mon. Rozaine.”

beats.title: Ganimard At The Gangway
beats.modern: little old man at the bottom of the gangway, umbrella, olive green coat, bored expression. that is Ganimard and he has been standing on that pier the whole crossing. he steps in front of me and says my name like a question. I tell him I am Bernard d'Andrézy. he tells me d'Andrézy died in Macedonia three years ago and then hits my right arm. the arm from the telegram.
beats.quote: “Bernard d’Andrézy died in Macedonia three years ago.”

beats.title: The Camera Goes Overboard
beats.modern: every pearl and every franc is inside the Kodak I put in Nelly's hands ten seconds before the cuffs. she heard all of it. our eyes meet, she glances down at the camera, and I watch her understand the entire thing at once. then she walks a few feet down the gangway and lets it slip into the water between the ship and the pier. no evidence. no case. no Nelly.
beats.quote: “What a pity that I am not an honest man!”

beats.title: The Registered Letter
beats.modern: writing to a baron from my cell with a shopping list of his own house. the Rubens, the smallest Watteau, the tapestries, the cabinet of miniatures. pack them carefully, prepay the freight, deliver to Batignolles station within eight days, or I come collect in person on the 27th and take considerably more. PS keep the big Watteau, it is a copy and you paid thirty thousand for it.
beats.quote: S.--Please do not send the largest Watteau. Although you paid thirty thousand francs for it, it is only a copy,

beats.title: You Frighten The Fish
beats.modern: the terrified baron tracks down the one detective who ever caught me and finds him on the riverbank with a rod. thieves do not warn people they are about to rob them. go home. sleep soundly. you are scaring the fish. genuinely the best advice he was ever given. chat that man on the riverbank is not Ganimard. he is mine.
beats.quote: “Monsieur, it is not customary for thieves to warn people they are about to rob.

beats.title: I Cause Ganimard To Arrest Ganimard
beats.modern: the warning letter was never a flex, it was the engine. warn the man, the law laughs at him because I am visibly in prison, so he panics and hires the celebrated detective he just read about in his own local paper. my guy. pays him three thousand francs to guard the house while my crew lowers the paintings out a window into a boat. and if the real Ganimard ever solves it, his job is to arrest Ganimard.
beats.quote: I cause Ganimard to arrest Ganimard.”

beats.title: Check The Egg
beats.modern: Ganimard is sitting in my cell insisting the case is still open, so I tell him to crack my breakfast egg. inside the shell, a telegram. contract closed, hundred thousand delivered, all well. the baron has quietly bought his own paintings back and the charge dies with them. one hundred thousand francs. modest, honestly. living in the city is expensive.
beats.quote: “Contract closed. Hundred thousand balls delivered. All well.”

beats.title: Credit On The Name
beats.modern: stepped off a moving prison van in a traffic jam, strolled up the boulevard, took a café terrace, ordered a beer and cigarettes. no wallet. so I call the owner over and ask for credit loud enough for the whole terrace to hear. Lupin, prisoner at the Santé, currently a fugitive. surely the name is good for it. left in a wave of laughter and he never called anyone.
beats.quote: “Lupin, prisoner at the Santé, but now a fugitive. I venture to assume that the name inspires you with perfect confidence in me.”

beats.title: Let Me Back In
beats.modern: then I walked to the prison gate and asked the sentry to let me in. sorry, the van left without me, I would like my cell back. chat the whole escape was THEIR trap. a van rigged for the occasion, an obstruction staged at exactly the right corner, twenty agents on foot and bicycles waiting to follow me home to my friends. when I want out, I will not need help.
beats.quote: And if you prevent Arsène Lupin from entering the prison it will cost you dear, my friend.”

beats.title: Baudru, Désiré
beats.modern: trial day. everyone packed the benches to watch me do something spectacular. the guards bring in a stooped grey man, hollow cheeks, dead alcoholic eyes, and when the judge asks his name a thick slow voice says: Baudru, Désiré. the room murmurs. the judge decides it is simply another alias and carries on prosecuting him anyway.
beats.quote: “Baudru, Désiré.”

beats.title: That Is Not Arsène Lupin
beats.modern: and then my own hunter saves me under oath. Ganimard cannot settle in the witness box, asks permission to come closer, studies me for a long minute, walks back and tells the court that this man is not Arsène Lupin. and everyone believes him instantly, because he is the man who caught Arsène Lupin. I never opened my mouth. the trial dies right there.
beats.quote: “I declare, on oath, that the prisoner now before me is not Arsène Lupin.”

beats.title: The Laugh On The Bench
beats.modern: they release poor Baudru and put three men on him, hoping he leads them to me. Ganimard finally sits down beside me on a bench in the Bois and says it is a pleasant day. so I laugh. one laugh and his hair stands up, because he knows that laugh. he goes for my throat, I do one small jiu jitsu thing and his arm stops working. then the old man cries. real tears, over his damn career, on a park bench, next to me.

beats.title: He Is On This Train
beats.modern: the lady across the compartment leans in and whispers that Arsène Lupin is on this train. bought a first class ticket for Rouen, they are searching the carriages, her husband runs the prison service so she would know. I tell her he would never be reckless enough to show himself in public. she then describes me to me for the next hour and will not let me sleep.
beats.quote: “But he is on this train at the present moment,”

beats.title: Bound Like A Mummy
beats.modern: so I fell asleep. woke up with a stranger's knee on my chest and his hands around my throat, blood in my eyes, one minute from the end. by the time I can see again I am tied, gagged and lighter by twelve thousand francs plus every compromising paper I own. chat I got robbed. me. trussed up like a fucking parcel on a train that is pulling into a station full of police looking for Arsène Lupin.
beats.quote: Arsène Lupin seized and bound like a novice!

beats.title: Lupin Hunts Lupin
beats.modern: so I lend the police my car. the commissary hands me two officers, I take the wheel of my thirty five horsepower, and we go after the man who robbed me. twenty three kilometres in nineteen minutes, running side by side with the express, beat it by twenty lengths. Arsène Lupin going in search of Arsène Lupin, with a police escort, shouting directions from the back seat.
beats.quote: Arsène Lupin was going in search of Arsène Lupin!

beats.title: Colleagues Honoré And Gaston
beats.modern: cornered him in a hovel in the woods, took him down, knee on the chest, offered terms: hand back my pocketbook and the lady's jewels and I keep the police off you. he says yes and then goes for a knife, so he sleeps. then I read the envelope in his pocket. Pierre Onfrey. the man who cut the throats of a mother and her two daughters. left my two officers two hundred francs and a thank you card.
beats.quote: “I am Arsène Lupin. You are to deliver over to me, immediately and gracefully, my pocketbook and the lady’s jewels,

beats.title: The Bolted Room
beats.modern: the Queen's Necklace comes out for one night on the countess. afterwards the count hides it on a high shelf in the little cabinet off their bedroom, shuts the door, bolts the bedroom, sleeps like the light sleeper he is. morning, he opens the cabinet and asks his wife very calmly whether she moved it. they empty the room, dump the linen on the floor, light a candle. gone. bolted door, fastened window, no other way in.

beats.title: Then It Was A Child
beats.modern: years later a dinner guest solves it in about four minutes. the thief bridged the courtyard with a kitchen shelf, cut the glass, hooked the transom open with a bent poker. and no grown man fits through a transom that size. so it was not a man. it was a child. the seamstress's boy, asleep in the next room from his mother. Raoul. six years old.
beats.quote: “If the transom is too small to admit a man, it must have been a child.”

beats.title: A Thief At Six Years Of Age
beats.modern: the count is laughing now. what a debut, stealing the Queen's Necklace at six. and I agree with him warmly. nobody ever thought to check the window sill the boy had wiped clean of dust. he only had to want the thing and put out a hand. both hands, actually. and somewhere in that sentence the whole table works out exactly who they invited to dinner.
beats.quote: To steal the Queen’s Necklace at six years of age;

beats.title: Delicate And Chivalrous
beats.modern: the countess, who blamed his mother, moved her to the servants' floor and threw her out the next day, asks me to pass along a message. the mounting is theirs. it belongs to the house like their name and their honour. I tell her I will pass it on. four days later there is a red leather case on her table with the cardinal's arms on it, and a newspaper item praising Arsène Lupin for his chivalry.
beats.quote: “I shall tell him, madame.”

beats.title: Do Not Move, Do Not Cry
beats.modern: steered dinner onto brigands and murder all evening so my host would walk home with his nerves already gone. then a letter with five red seals waiting inside the book on his night table. from the moment you open this, whatever you hear, do not move and do not make a sound, or you are finished. he lay there until dawn watching an armed man in the curtains. there was no man. it was a fold in the fabric.
beats.quote: “From the moment you open this letter, whatever happens, whatever you may hear, do not move, do not utter one cry. Otherwise you are doomed.”

beats.title: Three Minutes Alone
beats.modern: a stranger reads the newspaper story, turns up at the house and asks to be left alone in that room for exactly three minutes. at two minutes fifty there is a pistol shot. that was Etienne Varin. he went straight to the hiding place, found it empty, and understood in one second who had been there first. second seven of hearts lying on the floor beside him, seven holes punched through the pips.

beats.title: Hearts Are Trumps
beats.modern: one shot knocks the revolver out of his hand and I take over the table. hearts are trumps and I play the seven. then I climb the chair, lay a little iron card along the sword of the mosaic king on their wall, push an awl through the seven holes in order, and the emperor's chest swings open. a steel safe hidden inside the decor. their entire leverage over two families lived in a wall.
beats.quote: Hearts are trumps, and I play the seven.”

beats.title: The Letters He Rewrote
beats.modern: the banker walks out of the room carrying his wife's love letters, and behind the curtain her hand goes cold in mine because she thinks I just sold her. so I hand her the real ones. what he is taking home I wrote myself last night, same hand, nothing in them worth a divorce. he watched them come out of the safe, so he will never suspect. there is no handwriting that cannot be imitated.
beats.quote: “There is no handwriting that cannot be imitated.”

beats.title: I Saved Him From My Own Guy
beats.modern: three in the morning, wealthy man walking home alone, mugger comes out of the trees, hero arrives with a cane and a boot and drives him off. the hero is me. the mugger is mine. I kicked my only friend in the leg for real to make it look right. now I have a breakfast invitation to the house with the safe in it and they call me their saviour.
beats.quote: I rescued Mon. Ludovic Imbert from certain death at your hands.

beats.title: They Were Counterfeit
beats.modern: six months of setup. staged rescue, job as their private secretary, a lead pipe drilled through my floor to watch the safe, a knotted rope off the balcony at midnight, two trips to empty it. chat the bonds were fake. four million francs of nothing, every single one. worse, they had been showing me off to their lenders as the rich dead uncle whose fortune never existed. I was the proof. and she borrowed fifteen hundred francs off me for charity and never paid it back.
beats.quote: Those bonds were false--they were counterfeit--every one of them--do you understand? THEY WERE COUNTERFEIT!”

beats.title: More Silent Than Silence
beats.modern: crawling across the countess's bedroom in the dark, listening to her breathe, telling myself the heartbeat in my ears is nothing. my hand finds a candlestick on the floor. then a clock on the floor. then hair. then a face, and the face is cold. lantern on. she is on the carpet in her own blood, the clock stopped at twenty past eleven, and the pearl case is empty.
beats.quote: He found that it was hair, human hair, and a human face; and that face was cold, almost icy.

beats.title: Between The Twelfth And Thirteenth
beats.modern: so I come back months later as an ex inspector named Grimaudan, holding his duplicate key, his knife, and a description of the bloody thumbprint he left on the plaster. the price of the pearl is his life. he breaks at the table, walks me back to the street he killed in, and counts paving stones from the sewer hole. the most famous pearl in Paris was ten centimetres down in the gutter.
beats.quote: “Count the paving-stones to the right from the sewer-hole. The pearl is between the twelfth and thirteenth.”

beats.title: I Left The Button
beats.modern: forty minutes locked in with a murdered woman and I used all of them. worked out it had to be one of her servants, then built his arrest for him. left his cloth button under her bed, carried off the knife and the key so nothing could ever be properly proved, wiped his thumbprint off the wall. arrest him, acquit him, ruin him, wait. a hollowed out man hands things over.
beats.quote: I also decided that, in order to get the pearl, that servant must be arrested,

beats.title: Tonight I Plunder Your Castle
beats.modern: my host spends dinner joking that I look exactly like Arsène Lupin, announces that Sherlock Holmes arrives tomorrow at four, and then, to keep the table entertained, hands over the one piece of the riddle I have been missing for weeks. so I thank him sincerely and tell him the truth. tonight, before Holmes gets here, I am robbing your castle. enormous laugh.
beats.quote: “To-night, before the arrival of Sherlock Holmes, I must plunder your castle.”

beats.title: Face To Face
beats.modern: a girl comes down the gallery stairs with a candle while my arms are full of his snuffboxes. she pulls the curtain aside and it is Nelly. the Kodak. the pier. that Nelly. watches start dropping out of my hands onto the floor one by one and I am standing there blushing like a thief caught in the act, which is the whole job description. so I put every single item down and give her a time. tomorrow, three o'clock, all of it comes back.
beats.quote: “To-morrow, at three o’clock, everything will be returned.

beats.title: The Ruby And The White Rose
beats.modern: I asked her to look at me for one moment the way she did on the boat. she looked. then she pointed at my finger, at the ruby ring I lifted off our host an hour ago and forgot I was wearing. nothing can be changed. Arsène Lupin is Arsène Lupin. she goes into the house without a word and that is the last of her. then I find the white rose she left behind on the flower box. some petals came off in my hand. I kept them.

beats.title: Holmes Gets His Watch Back
beats.modern: there is a small package in the car. addressed to Sherlock Holmes, from Arsène Lupin. it is his own watch. Devanne is howling. Holmes does not move a muscle the entire ride to the station, and that silence is louder than any shouting I have ever heard, and then he says that one day he will put his hand on my shoulder. the world is too small. we will meet. gg chat.
beats.quote: Sherlock Holmes’ watch stolen by Arsène Lupin!

beats.title: The Will Reading
beats.modern: my great uncle dies and leaves the entire estate to my four year old nephew. a TODDLER outbid us, chat. his qualifications, and I quote the will's vibes: can't talk properly, insists on his own way, extremely loud. beat out ten years of my mother actually taking care of him. me and my two sisters get a thousand pounds each. that's the whole loot table.

beats.title: Fanny's Nerf Patch
beats.modern: my half brother promised our dying father he'd look after us. he settled on three thousand pounds and felt AMAZING about himself for days. then his wife started talking. three thousand becomes fifteen hundred. becomes an annuity. becomes fifty quid occasionally. becomes: actually you should just send them fish. she ran him from three thousand to zero and he thanked her for the clarity.

beats.title: Introducing Edward
beats.modern: ok chat. Edward. not handsome. bad at talking until he's known you six months. his mother wants him in parliament, his sister wants him driving a fancy carriage, and what he actually wants is a small quiet house and to be left alone forever. and I am completely gone on him. I know. I KNOW.

beats.title: Marianne Reviews My Boyfriend
beats.modern: my seventeen year old sister is rating my man live to our mother. verdict: amiable. no fire in the eyes. read poetry aloud last night with DREADFUL INDIFFERENCE and she nearly left the room. she has a checklist, chat. every book, every song, every opinion has to match hers exactly. she says she'll never meet anyone who clears it. write that down.
beats.quote: I could not be happy with a man whose taste did not in every point coincide with my own.

beats.title: Goodbye To The Trees
beats.modern: we're broke and downsizing to a rented cottage in Devonshire. Marianne is outside in the dark saying goodbye to the house. then to the TREES. individually. asking them if they understand what she suffers. chat the trees do not understand. the trees are having a normal night. she's been out there an hour.

beats.title: The Landlord And His Mother
beats.modern: our landlord is a golden retriever in a hunting coat. sends baskets of fruit, sends game, sends his newspaper daily, will not stop inviting us to dinner. his mother in law's entire personality is shipping. one dinner in and she's already asking whether we left our hearts behind in Sussex and pretending she saw us blush. she is going to be a problem.

beats.title: Thirty Five Is Ancient
beats.modern: Colonel Brandon is thirty five. my sister has declared him legally deceased. he mentioned owning a flannel waistcoat once and she filed it as evidence of bodily decay. he complained about ONE shoulder on a cold wet day and she's now planning his palliative care. mum is forty and had to point out that by this system she's a relic.
beats.quote: But thirty-five has nothing to do with matrimony."

beats.title: Carried Down The Hill
beats.modern: Marianne went up the downs in threatening weather, got caught in the rain, ran for it, and ate absolute pavement. and a beautiful stranger with a gun and two dogs SCOOPED HER UP and carried her all the way into our parlour. wouldn't sit down, said he was too wet and dirty, and walked back out into the storm. she has not recovered. honestly neither have I.

beats.title: Queen Mab
beats.modern: he gave her a HORSE. chat we cannot afford a horse. we can't afford the second horse the servant would need, or the servant, or the stable to put them in. I make her give it back and Willoughby goes, quietly, so only I hear: the horse is still yours, I'm just holding it until you've got your own house. that's a proposal wearing a hat and a fake moustache.
beats.quote: When you leave Barton to form your own establishment in a more lasting home, Queen Mab shall receive you."

beats.title: The Lock Of Hair
beats.modern: Margaret, thirteen, reporting live from behind a chair: he took Marianne's own scissors, cut off a long lock of her hair, KISSED IT, folded it into white paper and pocketed it. that's it. that's an engagement in this country. except nobody has actually said the word engaged out loud. not to me, not to mum, not to anyone. remember that.

beats.title: Whitwell Is Cancelled
beats.modern: twenty of us packed and ready for a day out and Colonel Brandon gets ONE letter at breakfast, changes colour, and leaves for London within the hour. won't say why. won't delay a single day. Willoughby's read, whispered to my sister: he's soft, he faked it to dodge a picnic, fifty guineas says he wrote that letter to himself. clip that one, chat. keep it somewhere safe.
beats.quote: I would lay fifty guineas the letter was of his own writing."

beats.title: The Allenham Walkthrough
beats.modern: so those two spent that morning touring the house Willoughby stands to inherit. alone. while the elderly owner was INSIDE IT and had not invited them. Marianne's defence: if it had been wrong I'd have felt bad at the time, and I didn't feel bad, therefore it wasn't wrong. unbeatable. she's also already picked out which corner room they'd redo.

beats.title: He Just Leaves
beats.modern: came home to find Marianne running upstairs sobbing and Willoughby facing the fireplace. says his cousin is sending him to London on business. says he won't be back in Devonshire this year. couldn't accept mum's invitation. couldn't finish a sentence. couldn't look at her. then into the carriage and gone in under a minute. mum has already invented four innocent explanations. I have a bad feeling and zero evidence.

beats.title: The Ring
beats.modern: Edward finally visits and he's wearing a ring with a plait of hair set in it. Marianne, helpfully, asks whose. he goes crimson, glances at me, says it's his sister's and the setting changes the shade. chat that is MY hair. he took my hair. and I have decided this is the most romantic thing that has ever happened to anyone. note the word decided.

beats.title: Lucy Steele Drops It
beats.modern: a girl I have known for about a fortnight takes my arm on a country walk and casually mentions she may one day be very intimately connected with the Ferrars family. not Robert. the eldest brother. MY Edward. engaged four years. I did not scream. I did not faint. I asked a calm follow up question about how long. chat my face did absolutely nothing.
beats.quote: "We have been engaged these four years."

beats.title: She Brought Receipts
beats.modern: and she has PROOF, chat. a miniature of his face, carried in her pocket. a letter in his handwriting, produced casually, held just long enough. and then, sweetly: I gave him a lock of my hair set in a ring, perhaps you noticed it? I noticed it. I have been staring at that ring for weeks telling myself a story. she knew. she told me on purpose. and she made me swear to keep it secret.

beats.title: The Party
beats.modern: we've been in London a month. Marianne's sent him note after note, sealed with a big W, and got nothing back. tonight he's ten feet away talking to a fashionable woman. he sees us. he BOWS and carries on. she stands up and says his name in a voice that hurts to hear, holds out her hand, and he addresses ME instead. asks how long we've been in town. like a stranger. then he walks off.
beats.quote: "Good God! Willoughby, what is the meaning of this? Have you not received my letters? Will you not shake hands with me?"

beats.title: The Letter
beats.modern: he sent everything back. every note she wrote. the lock of hair. and a letter addressed DEAR MADAM, thanking her for hers, apologising if he'd accidentally given the impression of feeling anything, and mentioning that his affections have long been engaged elsewhere and the wedding is in a few weeks. every line an insult. she's face down on the bed and there is nothing I can do.
beats.quote: my affections have been long engaged elsewhere, and it will not be many weeks, I believe, before this engagement is fulfilled.

beats.title: The Colonel's Lore Drop
beats.modern: Colonel Brandon sits me down. the girl he loved since childhood was married off to his brother for her fortune at seventeen. it wrecked her. the marriage, then the divorce, then years he couldn't find her at all. he finally found her in a debtors' house, dying of consumption, unrecognisable. he paid for proper lodgings and sat with her every single day until the end. and this whole county thinks he's a dull old man with a bad shoulder.

beats.title: The Girl In February
beats.modern: there's a daughter. she was fifteen. she vanished last February. Willoughby took her, left her pregnant, with no money, no home, no way to even write to him. THAT is where Brandon went the morning he cancelled the picnic. the morning Willoughby joked he'd faked the letter for fifty guineas. and then the two of them met by appointment with pistols. both walked away. Willoughby never mentioned any of it.

beats.title: Miss Morton Is Lord Morton's Daughter
beats.modern: Edward's mother gets handed the screens I painted, is told they're mine, says hum, very pretty, and returns them without looking at them. then loudly admires the painting of Miss Morton, the heiress she's picked out for him. Marianne snaps, grabs the screens back, demands to know who on earth Miss Morton is to us. and the old woman draws herself up and fires the one line she'd been holding all night.
beats.quote: "Miss Morton is Lord Morton's daughter."

beats.title: Nancy Popped It
beats.modern: it's out. Lucy's sister blurted the four year engagement straight to Fanny, who was at that exact moment planning to marry Edward off to a lord's daughter. instant screaming hysterics. she tore into Lucy until the girl fainted, threw them both out of the house, and my brother had to get on his KNEES to beg his own wife to let them pack first. and Mrs. Jennings is telling me all of this as fun gossip, watching my face, with no idea.

beats.title: Four Months
beats.modern: Marianne finds out I've known since November. four months. four months of holding her while she cried about her heartbreak with mine folded up in my chest. she asks how I stayed so calm. I tell her: I promised Lucy I'd say nothing, and I owed my family not to make them worry about a thing none of us could fix. that's the whole answer. that's all it ever was.
beats.quote: "What!--while attending me in all my misery, has this been on your heart?--And I have reproached you for being happy!"--

beats.title: The Delaford Living
beats.modern: Edward's mother cut him off entirely for refusing to drop Lucy. so Colonel Brandon, who has met him maybe three times, hands him a parish worth two hundred a year so he can afford to get married. no relation. no obligation. purely because it's the decent thing. and then he asks ME to be the one to tell him. me. delivering the money that lets the man I love marry someone else. sure. absolutely. no notes.

beats.title: My Brother Runs The Numbers
beats.modern: John hears Brandon gave away a living for free and his brain refuses the input. no relationship? no connection? he immediately calculates what it could have been SOLD for. fourteen hundred pounds, he decides, unprompted. then concludes Brandon must have secretly sold it anyway and Edward's just keeping the seat warm. it is genuinely easier for this man to believe in a conspiracy than in one act of kindness.

beats.title: Is Mama Coming
beats.modern: she kept walking in the wet grass at Cleveland because she wanted to feel something. now there's a fever and she doesn't know where she is and she keeps sitting up asking if mum is coming, and telling me mum mustn't go by London or she'll never see her. everyone in this house has quietly started talking about her like she's already gone. Colonel Brandon doesn't wait to be asked. he's already ordering the horses.

beats.title: Around Noon
beats.modern: around noon her pulse shifts and I don't say it out loud for a long time because if I say it and I'm wrong I will not survive it. then her breathing. then her skin. then she turns her head and LOOKS at me. properly looks at me. the doctor comes at four and says she's past the worst and that is the exact moment I stop holding it together.

beats.title: He's At The Door
beats.modern: it is the middle of the night, my sister is upstairs barely out of danger, and WILLOUGHBY is standing in the drawing room. rode from London in one go, out of the chaise for ten minutes all day. I try to leave. he blocks the door. first thing out of his mouth is is she safe, is it true. second thing is: honestly, do you think me more a villain or more an idiot.
beats.quote: "do you think me most a knave or a fool?"

beats.title: The Full Confession
beats.modern: and then he just tells me all of it. he was in debt, always had been, always planned to marry money. he went after my sister for sport with no intention of anything. then he actually fell in love with her. he was days away from proposing. and that same week his cousin found out about the girl, offered to forgive him if he married her, and cut him off when he refused. so he picked the fifty thousand pounds. he loved her and he chose the money and he knows exactly what he traded.

beats.title: He Copied It Out
beats.modern: and that letter. the one that broke her. his wife wrote it. spotted Marianne's note at breakfast, opened it herself, read it, and then made him copy her words out in his own handwriting so it would land properly. and he sat down and did it. he did it. he's telling me this like it's a defence.

beats.title: She Compares It To Mine
beats.modern: first walk since the fever. she stops in the lane, points at the exact mound on the hill, and says: there. that's where I fell, that's where I first saw him. then says she's finished with regret. I ask if she's comparing her conduct with his. she says no. she's comparing it with mine. chat I didn't have anything to say back.

beats.title: Mrs. Ferrars, Vastly Contented
beats.modern: our servant comes back from town and mentions, over the tablecloth, that he ran into Mrs. Ferrars in a carriage. Lucy. married. Edward sitting beside her, leaning back, not looking up. she sent us her best compliments and said she'd changed her name. she looked, he says, vastly contented. nobody at this table eats another bite. mum won't look at me. I say nothing, because what is there.

beats.title: Mrs. Robert Ferrars
beats.modern: Edward rides up to the cottage, white as paper. I make myself ask after Mrs. Edward Ferrars. he looks blank. then confused. then picks up a pair of scissors and starts shredding their sheath while he explains that I must mean Mrs. ROBERT Ferrars. she married his BROTHER. the one who got the money. last week. I got out of that room before I made a sound and then I cried so hard I thought it would never stop.
beats.quote: "Perhaps you do not know--you may not have heard that my brother is lately married to--to the youngest--to Miss Lucy Steele."

beats.title: Three Hours
beats.modern: he went out for a walk to work up the nerve, chat. came back. and by the time we sat down to dinner, about three hours after he arrived, he'd asked me, got my mother's blessing, and become the single happiest man in England. four years of Lucy Steele undone in one afternoon. I have been calm for eighteen months. I am done being calm.

beats.title: The Flannel Waistcoat Wins
beats.modern: and my sister. who ruled thirty five a terminal condition. who said a woman of twenty seven could only ever hope to be a nurse. who required a husband to share every single opinion she held. marries Colonel Brandon. at nineteen. willingly. patroness of a village. and the man is STILL wearing the flannel waistcoat.

beats.title: And Willoughby Is Fine
beats.modern: and Willoughby? his cousin forgave him afterwards. told him that if he'd married a woman of character he'd have had the money AND the girl. so he sold her for nothing. did he then die of a broken heart, flee society, waste away? no. he did not. he got some horses and some dogs and a wife who isn't always in a mood, and he's basically fine. that's the ending. that's genuinely the ending.

thus-spake-zarathustra.title: Thus Spake Zarathustra: A Book for All and None
thus-spake-zarathustra.author: Friedrich Wilhelm Nietzsche

beats.title: The Saint In The Woods
beats.modern: old man in the forest, still writing hymns, still singing them, still weeping and mumbling at the sky. we talked for ten minutes and I could not do it. could not tell him. walked away and said it to myself instead: this guy hasn't heard yet. GOD IS DEAD. he's out here grinding dailies on a server that shut down.
beats.quote: “Could it be possible! This old saint in the forest hath not yet heard of it, that GOD IS DEAD!”

beats.title: Revenge On The Witness
beats.modern: met the man who killed god. asked him why. it wasn't hate, chat. god SAW him. saw the dirtiest corner of him, every private ugly thing, and never looked away. you cannot live under a witness like that. so he removed the witness. that's not blasphemy, that's shame with a weapon.
beats.quote: The God who beheld everything, AND ALSO MAN: that God had to die!

beats.title: Sing Me A Better Song
beats.modern: you want me to buy what you're selling? then the saved ones have to LOOK saved. sing me a better song. right now your choir sounds like a support group in a basement. and I'd want them naked, because only beauty gets to preach at me about repentance.
beats.quote: more like saved ones would his disciples have to appear unto me!

beats.title: God Died Of Pity
beats.modern: the devil told me once that god has a hell too, and it's loving humans. then later I heard him drop the patch note: god didn't get murdered. he watched us. and the pity killed him. died of empathy damage looking at what we are.
beats.quote: “Even God hath his hell: it is his love for man.”

beats.title: You Are Still Worm
beats.modern: look at a monkey. embarrassing, right? that is exactly what you look like to whatever comes next. you climbed all the way up from worm and there's still worm in you. I'm not insulting you. I'm telling you you're a rough draft and the final version isn't out yet.
beats.quote: What is the ape to man? A laughing-stock, a thing of shame.

beats.title: A Rope Over An Abyss
beats.modern: you are not the destination. you're the tightrope. animal on one end, something better on the other, and underneath there's nothing but drop. the good part of you isn't where you're standing. it's that you're crossing at all.
beats.quote: Man is a rope stretched between the animal and the Superman—a rope over an abyss.

beats.title: Remain True To The Earth
beats.modern: anyone selling you a better world after this one is selling poison, and half of them don't even know they're doing it. stay on the ground. the dirt under your feet is the only real thing anyone will ever hand you.
beats.quote: I conjure you, my brethren, REMAIN TRUE TO THE EARTH,

beats.title: Chaos And The Dancing Star
beats.modern: you need chaos inside you to give birth to a dancing star. good news, chat: you're a disaster. that's the raw material. bad news: there's a version of humanity coming that has everything sorted, calm, optimised, and it will never make anything again.
beats.quote: I tell you: one must still have chaos in one, to give birth to a dancing star.

beats.title: The Hour Of Great Contempt
beats.modern: the best thing that will ever happen to you is the night your own happiness makes you sick. when you look at your comfort, your reasoning, your tidy little virtue, and go: this is it? this is what I settled for? that disgust isn't a breakdown. it's the door.
beats.quote: What is the greatest thing ye can experience? It is the hour of great contempt.

beats.title: Heavy Drops Before Lightning
beats.modern: my type: the one who goes quiet when the dice land in his favour and asks if he cheated. who promises small and delivers huge. who's so full he forgets himself entirely. every one of them is a heavy drop falling out of a black cloud. they're not the lightning. they announce it and then they're gone.
beats.quote: I love him who scattereth golden words in advance of his deeds, and always doeth more than he promiseth:

beats.title: The Last Man Blinks
beats.modern: here's my actual nightmare and it isn't hell. it's a guy who's FINE. earth's gone small and he hops around on it making everything smaller. asks what's love, what's a star, and BLINKS. he says he discovered happiness. he'll outlive every one of us.
beats.quote: The earth hath then become small, and on it there hoppeth the last man who maketh everything small.
beats.group: The Last Man And The Cold Monster

beats.title: A Little Poison Now And Then
beats.modern: a little poison now and then for nice dreams. a lot at the end for a nice death. they moved out of everywhere hard to live because they need warmth, so they rub against the neighbour for it. they still work but only as a hobby, and carefully, in case the hobby hurts.
