beats.quote: A little poison now and then: that maketh pleasant dreams. And much poison at last for a pleasant death.
beats.group: The Last Man And The Cold Monster

beats.title: Worst Focus Group Ever
beats.modern: I described the most contemptible creature I could imagine, in detail, as a WARNING. and the crowd cheered. make us that, they said, you can keep the Superman. they smacked their lips, chat. they heard the horror and read it as a fucking product pitch.
beats.group: The Last Man And The Cold Monster

beats.title: The Coldest Cold Monster
beats.modern: the state is the coldest of all cold monsters and its favourite lie is: I am the people. it isn't. peoples were made by creators who hung a faith over them. the state was built by destroyers who needed somewhere to put the surplus. it bites with stolen teeth. everything in it is stolen.
beats.quote: “I, the state, am the people.”
beats.group: The Last Man And The Cold Monster

beats.title: They Call It A Newspaper
beats.modern: they steal what the inventors built and call the theft culture. they're sick permanently, they throw up bile and print it as a newspaper, they eat each other and can't even digest themselves. they chase money because money is the lever, and they get poorer doing it. this is the discourse. this is what it is.
beats.quote: Sick are they always; they vomit their bile and call it a newspaper.
beats.group: The Last Man And The Cold Monster

beats.title: Where The State Ceaseth
beats.modern: break the window. jump out. the air past the monster's breath is still open. wherever the state STOPS is exactly where a person who isn't spare parts begins, and that's where the one song only you can sing starts playing. everything before that line was somebody else's throat.
beats.group: The Last Man And The Cold Monster

beats.title: The Praise Is The Sting
beats.modern: the praise IS the sting. they buzz in close because they want your skin and your blood, and they flatter you the way you'd flatter a god or a devil, which means they already decided you're not a person. and the friendly ones? that's just cowardice being smart. you are not built to be a fly swatter. leave.
beats.quote: They want to be close to thy skin and thy blood.
beats.group: The Last Man And The Cold Monster

beats.title: Your Soul Is A Nickname
beats.modern: your soul is a nickname for part of your body. that's the whole thing. the ego says I and struts about it; the body doesn't say it, the body just DOES it. there's more intelligence in your gut than in your best idea, and behind every thought you're proud of there's a landlord you have never once met.
beats.quote: “Body am I entirely, and nothing more; and soul is only the name of something in the body.”

beats.title: The Dogs In Your Cellar
beats.modern: you didn't kill the worst parts of yourself. you AIMED them. the wild dogs in your basement turned into songbirds. you brewed balm out of your own poison and milked the cow called suffering and now you're drinking it. every virtue you own is a devil that got a job.
beats.quote: Once hadst thou wild dogs in thy cellar: but they changed at last into birds and charming songstresses.

beats.title: Will To Power
beats.modern: everywhere there's life I find the same engine, and it isn't survival. it's power. even obedience is a hidden reach for mastery: the weak serve the strong to get power over the weaker. and the strongest one stakes his own life on it, because by then that's the only chip he has left to push in.
beats.quote: Wherever I found a living thing, there found I Will to Power; and even in the will of the servant found I the will to be master.

beats.title: Life Told Me Her Secret
beats.modern: Life pulled me aside and told me what she actually is: the thing that has to keep beating itself. every leaf that falls she's sacrificing for power. and whatever I build, however much I love it, I'll have to turn on eventually. that's not betrayal. that's the job description.
beats.quote: where there is succumbing and leaf-falling, lo, there doth Life sacrifice itself—for power!

beats.title: The Last Art You Learn
beats.modern: self love is not a vibe you wake up with. it's the hardest craft there is. finest, subtlest, most patient, and the LAST one you'll ever learn. not the sick version either, that one stinks. the healthy kind, where you can sit alone with yourself and not go wandering off looking for a distraction you can call brotherly love.
beats.quote: One must learn to love oneself—thus do I teach—with a wholesome and healthy love:

beats.title: The Way Does Not Exist
beats.modern: someone asked me for the way. I told them: this is MY way, where's yours? because THE way? doesn't exist. never did. I got here down a hundred crooked routes and I never once asked directions, I interrogated the roads themselves. asking felt disgusting to me. still does.
beats.quote: “This—is now MY way,—where is yours?”

beats.title: Tarantulas Of Equality
beats.modern: you preach equality. I hear a tarantula. touch the web and out it comes, black triangle on its back, and the bite leaves a mark that calls itself justice. it isn't fairness talking. it's the tyrant-craving of people who couldn't get power, wearing virtue as a costume. I ripped your web open on purpose.
beats.quote: Tarantulas are ye unto me, and secretly revengeful ones!

beats.title: Distrust The Punishers
beats.modern: rule I'd tattoo inside my eyelids: distrust anyone whose urge to punish runs hot. look at their face long enough and a hangman looks back out of it. and anybody who talks constantly about their own justice? there's more than honey missing in there.
beats.quote: distrust all in whom the impulse to punish is powerful!

beats.title: Pity From A Distance
beats.modern: people whose entire joy is feeling sorry for you have zero shame left. if I ever pity you I'd rather you never hear about it, and I'd rather do it from far away with my hood up. helping a man to his face wounds his pride, and I was ashamed on his behalf the whole time.
beats.quote: If I must be pitiful, I dislike to be called so; and if I be so, it is preferably at a distance.

beats.title: Our Actual Original Sin
beats.modern: the original sin isn't pride and it isn't lust. it's that humans have not ENJOYED themselves nearly enough. that's the whole fall. and here's the part nobody tells you: the better you get at enjoying your own life, the worse you get at inventing pain for other people.
beats.quote: Since humanity came into being, man hath enjoyed himself too little: that alone, my brethren, is our original sin!

beats.title: The Grudge Against Time
beats.modern: here's what your will is chained to: it cannot go backwards. every it was is a stone it can't roll. so it turns petty and starts rolling stones down onto anything that can still feel. that grudge against time is the entire mechanism of revenge. every cruel thing you've ever done grew out of it.
beats.quote: This, yea, this alone is REVENGE itself: the Will’s antipathy to time, and its “It was.”

beats.title: Thus Would I Have It
beats.modern: redemption isn't being forgiven. it's taking every it was in your life and turning it into: I wanted that. not accepting it. not making peace with it. WILLING it, backwards, on purpose. that's the only version of the word I recognise.
beats.quote: To redeem what is past, and to transform every “It was” into “Thus would I have it!”—that only do I call redemption!

beats.title: They Hate The Breaker
beats.modern: ask the good and just who they hate most. it's whoever smashes their table of values. they call him a criminal, a law-breaker. he's the creator. I'm not building a flock here. I want people who can sharpen their own scythe and who'll get called destroyers for it.
beats.quote: Companions, the creator seeketh, not corpses—and not herds or believers either.

beats.title: Free For What
beats.modern: you say you're free. cool. I do not care what you escaped. plenty of people threw away the last worthwhile thing about them the day they threw off the leash. tell me the thought that RULES you. free from what, sure, whatever. free FOR what?
beats.quote: Free from what? What doth that matter to Zarathustra!

beats.title: Burn Yourself To Ashes
beats.modern: the road to yourself runs straight past yourself and all seven of your demons. you'll be a heretic to your own beliefs, a fraud, a fool, a doubter, a villain. and at some point you have to be willing to burn in your own fire. you don't get to be new without first being ash.
beats.quote: Ready must thou be to burn thyself in thine own flame; how couldst thou become new if thou have not first become ashes!

beats.title: Lose Me And Find Yourselves
beats.modern: you believe in me? that's the problem. you hadn't found yourselves yet, so you found me instead. careful: a statue can fall on you. so here's the ask. lose me. find yourselves. deny me completely. and only then do I come back.
beats.quote: Now do I bid you lose me and find yourselves; and only when ye have all denied me, will I return unto you.

beats.title: I Slammed The Door
beats.modern: left the academy and slammed the door behind me. sat hungry at their table for years. they sit in the cool shade because what they actually want is to be spectators, never where the sun burns the steps. and they gawk at thoughts other people had the way you gawk at traffic going past.
beats.quote: I have departed from the house of the scholars, and the door have I also slammed behind me.

beats.title: We Lie Too Much
beats.modern: somebody said the poets lie too much. correct. WE lie too much. we know almost nothing and we're terrible students, so lying is the only move we've got left. every one of us has watered the wine. things have happened in our cellars I'm not going to describe.
beats.quote: the poets lie too much: he was right—WE do lie too much.

beats.title: An Ear As Big As A Man
beats.modern: first time I crossed that bridge I saw an ear. an ear the size of a full grown man. underneath it, a thin little stalk, and on the stalk a tiny envious face with a bloated soullet dangling off it. people told me that's a GENIUS. no. that's a reversed cripple. too little of everything, way too much of one thing.
beats.quote: “That is an ear! An ear as big as a man!”

beats.title: The Gateway Called This Moment
beats.modern: two roads meet at a gate. one runs backwards forever, one runs forwards forever, and the name carved over the gate is This Moment. if everything that CAN happen has already happened, then this gate has already stood here. you and me whispering. the spider. the moonlight. all of it. again. and again.
beats.quote: And are not all things closely bound together in such wise that This Moment draweth all coming things after it?

beats.title: Bite Its Head Off
beats.modern: kid on the ground, black snake down his throat, my hands can't pull it out. and something screams out of me that isn't a decision: BITE. bite its head off. he bites. spits. stands up. and he isn't a shepherd anymore, he's lit from the inside and LAUGHING. nothing human has ever laughed like that. I've been thirsty for that sound ever since.
beats.quote: No longer shepherd, no longer man—a transfigured being, a light-surrounded being, that LAUGHED!

beats.title: The Small Man Returns
beats.modern: seven days flat on my back, animals bringing me fruit I wouldn't touch. and it wasn't because man is evil that broke me. it's that man is SMALL. because if everything comes back forever, then the small man comes back forever too. the pettiest person you know, on loop, for eternity. that's what crawled down my throat.
beats.quote: All too small, even the greatest man!—that was my disgust at man!

beats.title: Joy Wants Eternity
beats.modern: if you ever said yes to ONE moment of joy, congratulations, you just said yes to every horror as well. it's all laced together, all of it. you cannot ask for one instant back without asking for the whole thing back. joy doesn't want children or heirs. joy wants ITSELF. forever. on repeat.
beats.quote: Said ye ever Yea to one joy? O my friends, then said ye Yea also unto ALL woe. All things are enlinked, enlaced and enamoured,—

beats.title: Was That Life Once More
beats.modern: the ugliest man on earth. the one who killed god. he stood up at midnight and said one day with us made his entire life worth living. and then he said the sentence: was THAT life? well. once more. chat I have never been prouder of anything.
beats.quote: ‘Was THAT—life?’ will I say unto death. ‘Well! Once more!’

beats.title: Learn To Laugh At Yourselves
beats.modern: the higher the type, the more often it fails. so yes, every one of you is a failure. so what? learn to laugh at yourselves the way you're SUPPOSED to laugh. then go collect small perfect finished things and set them around you. their little gold ripeness fixes something in the chest. finished things teach you to hope.
beats.quote: Learn to laugh at yourselves, as ye ought to laugh!

beats.title: I Crowned Myself
beats.modern: nobody alive was qualified to crown me so I did it myself. laughter crown, roses on it. I consecrated my own laughing. Zarathustra the dancer, the light one, the sooth-LAUGHER, the one who loves leaps and side-leaps. I checked the whole field. nobody else could carry it.
beats.quote: This crown of the laughter, this rose-garland crown: I myself have put on this crown, I myself have consecrated my laughter.

beats.title: He Searched Badly
beats.modern: biggest sin ever committed on this planet? a man looked at the whole earth and said woe to you who are laughing now. he couldn't find one single reason to laugh out here. a TODDLER can find one. he searched badly.
beats.quote: “Woe unto them that laugh now!”

beats.title: Arise Great Noontide
beats.modern: my last temptation wasn't power or comfort. it was feeling sorry for the good ones. done with that. do I chase happiness? no. I chase my WORK. the lion showed up at my door and the doves came with him, my children are close, I'm ripe. this is my morning. get up.
beats.quote: Do I then strive after HAPPINESS? I strive after my WORK!

ecce-homo.title: Ecce Homo: Complete Works, Volume Seventeen
ecce-homo.author: Friedrich Wilhelm Nietzsche

beats.title: Nutrition Beats Salvation
beats.modern: everyone wants to argue about the soul. chat. CHAT. what are you EATING. that is the question the salvation of humanity actually runs on, not one single piece of theological trivia. how must you feed yourself to hit your maximum power? I got to this question absurdly late and my results up to then were as bad as results get.

beats.title: German Cooking Broke German Philosophy
beats.modern: german philosophy is german digestion, I said what I said. soup FIRST. meat boiled into threads. vegetables drowned in fat and flour. pastry with the structural density of a paperweight. then the ancestral drinking. and you wonder where german intellect came from? sadly disordered intestines. german intellect is indigestion. it cannot assimilate anything.
beats.quote: German intellect is indigestion; it can assimilate nothing.

beats.title: Tea Rules, Coffee Lies
beats.modern: patch notes for the body. nothing between meals. coffee deleted, coffee makes you gloomy. tea in the morning only, small cup, strong enough to fight back. and I need you to hear this: weak tea will indispose you for the ENTIRE day. everyone has his own limit and it is narrower than you think.

beats.title: No Thought Born Sitting Down
beats.modern: sit as little as humanly possible. do not trust a single thought that was not born outdoors with the body moving, ideally with the muscles throwing a party. every prejudice you own started in your intestines. sitting still is the one sin against the holy spirit I actually believe in.
beats.quote: All prejudices take their origin in the intestines.

beats.title: Genius Needs Dry Air
beats.modern: make a list of every place that ever produced a mind worth reading. paris. provence. florence. jerusalem. athens. now check the weather on all of them. dry air, every time. clean sky, every time. genius is not a gift, chat, it is a climate. you are not blocked. you are damp.

beats.title: Every Address Was Wrong
beats.modern: I ran the numbers on where I have lived and it is genuinely horrifying. naumburg. pforta. leipzig. bâle. venice. every single one wrong for this body. my entire life until the last ten years was spent in the exact places most forbidden to me, and I called that a career.

beats.title: Both Sides Of The Ladder
beats.modern: riddle for chat. as my own father I am already dead. as my own mother I am still alive and getting older. top rung and bottom rung of the ladder in one body. that is why my nose reads decline on anything before anyone else smells it. I am not describing both sides. I AM both sides.
beats.quote: as my own father I am already dead, as my own mother I still live and grow old.

beats.title: My Worst Year Shipped My Best Book
beats.modern: my father died at 36. at 36 my own life bottomed out, eyes so bad I could not make out anything three paces away. resigned the professorship. spent the summer like a shadow in st moritz and the most sunless winter of my life like a shadow in naumburg. that is the year I wrote The Wanderer and His Shadow. I was, let us say, conversant with shadows.

beats.title: Three-Day Headache Clarity
beats.modern: day three of the headache, violent nausea, and my brain has never been sharper. absolutely cold blood. I thought things out in that state that healthy me cannot reach, because healthy me is not enough of a climber, not subtle enough, not cold enough. the pain is not the tax on the work. some days it is the equipment.

beats.title: It Is Simply I Who Am Nervous
beats.modern: specialist treats me as a nerve patient for months. finally he sits me down and goes: no, there is nothing wrong with your nerves, it is simply I who am nervous. chat I broke my doctor. no one has ever detected a fever in me either. slow circulation, undefeated record.
beats.quote: "No! there is nothing wrong with your nerves, it is simply I who am nervous."

beats.title: What Does Not Kill Him
beats.modern: how do you spot one of nature's lucky rolls? he only enjoys what is good for him and stops the second it stops being good. he turns serious accidents into loot. that which does not kill him makes him stronger. he believes in neither bad luck nor guilt. and he knows how to forget. that last one is the actual cheat code.
beats.quote: that which does not kill him makes him stronger.

beats.title: I Stopped Being A Pessimist
beats.modern: here is the part nobody expects. the years my body hit its absolute floor are the years I QUIT being a pessimist. the recovery instinct simply refused to let me hold a philosophy of poverty and desperation. I could not afford the doomposting anymore. out of my will to health I made my philosophy.

beats.title: Russian Fatalism
beats.modern: when you are sick the one poison you cannot afford is resentment. so I run what I call russian fatalism: the soldier who cannot take another day of the campaign and simply lies down in the snow. accept nothing. undertake nothing. absorb nothing. stop reacting entirely. if reacting is what uses you up, then you do not react. that is the whole build.

beats.title: Buddha Ran A Hygiene Program
beats.modern: buddha was not founding a religion, he was running a hygiene protocol. step one of recovery: get resentment out of the soul. hostility does not put hostility to flight, friendship does. that is not a moral rule, chat. that is physiology. nothing on earth burns a man down faster than the passion of resentment.
beats.quote: "Not through hostility is hostility put to flight; through friendship does hostility end":

beats.title: Four Rules Of Engagement
beats.modern: my war tactics, since everyone asks. one: I only attack what is already winning, and if it is not winning yet I wait. two: I attack alone, no allies, nobody compromised but me. three: never personal. I use a person as a magnifying glass to make a general rot visible. four: no private grudge allowed anywhere in it. attacking is how I show respect.

beats.title: All Silent People Are Dyspeptic
beats.modern: the rudest letter you could possibly write is more good natured than silence. people who go quiet are always short on subtlety and heart. swallowing a grievance sours the temper and then it goes for the stomach. all silent people are dyspeptic, chat. rudeness is a public service.
beats.quote: All silent people are dyspeptic.

beats.title: I Can Smell Your Soul
beats.modern: my sense of cleanliness is not a metaphor. I can physiologically smell the entrails of a human soul. whatever is rotting at the base of a character, whatever your education painted over, I have it at first glance. and they always sense that I have clocked them. it does not make them any more fragrant.

beats.title: No Books While I'm Cooking
beats.modern: while I am deep in the work there is not one book within arm's reach. I would not let a person speak in the room, or even think in the room. because that is what reading IS. you are pregnant with a thought and you want a stranger climbing quietly over the wall to say something? absolutely not.

beats.title: The Scholar Is A Decadent
beats.modern: your average scholar handles two hundred books a day and forgets how to think completely. no book in his fingers, no thoughts in his head. everything he produces is a yes or a no to something already thought by somebody else. his self defence instinct has rotted, otherwise he would defend himself AGAINST books. the scholar is a decadent.
beats.quote: The scholar is a decadent.

beats.title: Reading At Dawn Is Vicious
beats.modern: I have watched gifted, free spirited people get READ TO RUINS by thirty. brilliant kids turned into matchsticks you have to rub before they give off a spark. and to get up at break of day, full strength, whole dawn in front of you, and open a book? that is not discipline, chat. that is a vice.

beats.title: Illness Deleted My Library
beats.modern: my eyes gave out and that was the end of philology. no more books, for years. and the self at the bottom, the one that had been buried alive under everybody else's voices, woke up. shy at first, unsure, and then it spoke again. I have never rejoiced over my condition more than in the sickest and most painful part of my life.

beats.title: Six Thousand Feet Beyond Man
beats.modern: walking the woods by the lake of silvaplana, stopped near a huge rock standing up like a pyramid, and the eternal recurrence just LANDED on me. I wrote it on a scrap of paper with one line underneath: six thousand feet beyond man and time. I did not go looking for that. it arrived.
beats.quote: "Six thousand feet beyond man and time."

beats.title: What Inspiration Actually Feels Like
beats.modern: you want to know what the older poets meant by inspiration? something becomes visible and audible with total certainty and it convulses you. one hears, one does not seek. one takes, one does not ask who gives. the strain gets so large it comes out of you as crying. I have never once had a choice in the matter.
beats.quote: One hears--one does not seek; one takes--one does not ask who gives:

beats.title: I Walked Eight Hours And Danced
beats.modern: when the creative energy was flowing hardest my body was moving most. seven, eight hours over the hills with no fatigue. I was dancing in those days. the body is inspired, we can leave the word soul out of this entirely. slept well, laughed a lot, perfectly robust. that is the whole secret and nobody wants it.
beats.quote: The body is inspired: let us waive the question of "soul."

beats.title: The Rancour Of Greatness
beats.modern: nobody warns you about this one. everything great turns on its author the moment it is finished. being the one who made it is exactly what makes you weak in front of it. you cannot look at it. you carry it on your back forever and it nearly crushes you. a man pays dearly for being immortal. he has to die many times first.
beats.quote: A man pays dearly for being immortal: to this end he must die many times over during his life.

beats.title: Solitude Has Seven Skins
beats.modern: solitude has seven skins and nothing gets through them. you go among people, you greet friends, and it is just more desert. the looks coming back no longer carry a greeting. nothing wounds a person deeper than suddenly being made to feel your distance. that is what they punish you for. not the ideas. the distance.
beats.quote: Solitude has seven skins which nothing can penetrate.

beats.title: I Left Bayreuth Mid-Festival
beats.modern: walked into bayreuth and recognised nothing. barely recognised wagner. what happened? wagner had been TRANSLATED INTO GERMAN. german art, german master, german beer. the wagnerite had become master of wagner. so halfway through the festival I packed my trunk, left a charming parisian lady trying to comfort me, and sent wagner one fatalistic telegram. gone.

beats.title: Wagner Was My Hashish
beats.modern: I could not have survived my own youth without wagner's music. I was sentenced to the society of germans. if a man needs to get out from under something unbearable he takes hashish. I took wagner. he is the counter poison to everything essentially german. that he is also a poison, I do not deny.
beats.quote: Wagner is the counter-poison to everything essentially German--the fact that he is a poison too, I do not deny.

beats.title: I Have Loved Wagner
beats.modern: everyone is waiting for me to open fire on wagner. old artillery man, the heavy guns are right there, I could level him this afternoon. I am not going to. everything decisive in this question I kept to myself. I have loved Wagner. that is the whole post.
beats.quote: Wagner?--Everything decisive in this question I kept to myself--I have loved Wagner.--After

beats.title: The Night Song
beats.modern: light am I. that is the whole problem. I wanted to be night. I am girdled in my own light and I drink back my own flames and I have never once known what it is to receive. my hand never rests from giving and it has gone hard from it. oh the solitude of all givers. oh the silence of all beacons.
beats.quote: Oh, the solitude of all givers! Oh, the silence of all beacons!

beats.title: Do Not Confuse Me With Anyone
beats.modern: I am about to put the greatest demand ever made on human beings in front of them, so first, formally: who and what I am. and apparently this needs saying, because people have neither heard me nor seen me. I live entirely on credit I issued to myself. talk to any scholar summering here and you will be convinced I am not alive.

beats.title: The Air Up Here Is Thin
beats.modern: if you can breathe the air of my writings you already know it is mountain air. you have to be built for it or the odds are it just chills you. the ice is near. the loneliness is genuinely terrible. and then look how serenely it all lies in the sunshine, how freely you can breathe, how much of it lies beneath you.

beats.title: Some Are Born Posthumously
beats.modern: my time has not come. some people are born posthumously. one day there will be institutions where men live and teach the way I mean it, maybe even endowed chairs just for interpreting Zarathustra. right now nobody listens, nobody knows how to receive anything from my hands, and honestly? correct. that seems to me quite the proper thing.
beats.quote: My time has not yet come either; some are born posthumously.

beats.title: Six Sentences Is Enough
beats.modern: von stein tells me honestly that he could not understand a single word of Zarathustra. I told him that is exactly as it should be. understand six sentences of that book, meaning LIVE them, and you are already standing higher among mortals than any modern man gets. I am not writing for readers. I am writing for survivors of six sentences.

beats.title: You Read Superman Wrong
beats.modern: Superman means one of nature's rarest and luckiest strokes, the exact OPPOSITE of modern men, good men, christians and other nihilists. and everyone reads it as an ideal type, half saint half genius. learned cattle suspect me of darwinism. others heard carlyle hero worship, which I mocked on the page. I once told a man to look for the Superman in a Borgia rather than a Parsifal and he could not believe his ears.

beats.title: The Grape Ladies Of Turin
beats.modern: germany has not discovered me. vienna has, petersburg, stockholm, copenhagen, paris, new york. but here is the thing that has flattered me more than anything in my life: wherever I go in turin every face brightens, and the old market women will not rest until they have picked out the sweetest of their grapes for me. that is the review that counts.

beats.title: Satyr Over Saint
beats.modern: for the record I am not a bogey man and not a moral monster. I am the exact opposite in nature to everything that has ever been honoured as virtuous, and between us, that is precisely what I am proud of. disciple of the philosopher Dionysus. given the choice I take satyr over saint every single time.
beats.quote: I am a disciple of the philosopher Dionysus, and I would prefer to be even a satyr than a saint.

beats.title: I Don't Build Idols
beats.modern: the very last thing I would ever promise is to improve mankind. I am not setting up new idols. I would just like the old ones to find out what legs of clay cost. knocking idols over is the job, and idols is my word for ALL ideals. every time an ideal world got assumed, reality got robbed of its value and its meaning.

beats.title: Error Is Cowardice
beats.modern: the only test of values I trust: how much truth can a mind endure, and how much can it DARE. because error, the belief in the ideal, is not blindness. error is cowardice. every step forward in knowledge comes out of courage and hardness toward yourself. I do not even refute ideals. I just put my gloves on around them.
beats.quote: Error (the belief in the ideal) is not blindness; error is cowardice....

beats.title: Unfollow Me
beats.modern: go away from me. arm yourselves against Zarathustra, and better still, be ashamed of him, maybe he deceived you. you honour me? careful, a statue can fall on you. you had not sought yourselves yet when you found me, which is exactly why believing is worth so little. lose me. find yourselves. when every one of you has denied me, then I come back.
beats.quote: "Now I bid you lose me and find yourselves; and only when ye have all denied me will I come back unto you."

beats.title: I Am Dynamite
beats.modern: I know my destiny. one day my name will be attached to something formidable, a crisis with no precedent on earth, the deepest collision of consciences there has ever been, and a sentence passed on everything that was believed and demanded and held holy. I am not a man. I am dynamite.
beats.quote: I am not a man, I am dynamite.

beats.title: I'd Rather Be A Clown
beats.modern: there is nothing of the religion founder in me. religions are for the mob and I wash my hands after meeting a religious man. I want zero believers. I am far too full of malice to believe even in myself. my actual nightmare is being pronounced HOLY one day, which is why I am publishing this in advance. I refuse to be a saint. I would rather be a clown.
beats.quote: I refuse to be a saint; I would rather be a clown.

beats.title: Good Men Never Speak The Truth
beats.modern: the optimist is just as degenerate as the pessimist and probably does more damage. here is the line nobody forgives me for. good men never speak the truth. false shores and false harbours are what the good taught you. you were born and raised inside their lies. everything went crooked from the roots.
beats.quote: "Good men never speak the truth. False shores and false harbours were ye taught by the good.

beats.title: Morality As Vampirism
beats.modern: when the lightning of truth hits the thing that stood highest, check whether you are still holding anything at all. everything that was called truth up to now turns out to be the most spiteful and most subterranean form of life. and the holy pretext, the improvement of man? a device for draining the blood out of him. morality as vampirism.
beats.quote: the holy pretext, which was the "improvement" of man, has been recognised as a ruse for draining life of its energy and of its blood.

beats.title: The Maiwand Patch
beats.modern: chat I took a bullet at Maiwand. shoulder, straight through the bone, and my orderly threw me over a packhorse like a sack of grain to get me out. then I caught fever in the hospital and nearly ran out of health bar entirely. the government's official response: nine months of leave and a boat home. thanks for the patch notes.
beats.quote: There I was struck on the shoulder by a Jezail bullet, which shattered the bone and grazed the subclavian artery.

beats.title: Stamford's Warning
beats.modern: asked my old colleague about this guy who needs someone to split rent with. he goes, oh he's fine, he's just a little too scientific for my taste. define scientific. "well, he beats the corpses in the dissecting room with a stick. to check whether you can still bruise a dead man." and you tell me this AFTER I said I'm in.
beats.quote: “Yes, to verify how far bruises may be produced after death. I saw him at it with my own eyes.”

beats.title: The Flatmate Disclosure Round
beats.modern: before we sign, he wants us to trade red flags up front. his: chemicals everywhere, strong tobacco, and sometimes he goes days without speaking and I'm not allowed to take it personally. mine: I keep a bull pup, I get up at cursed hours, I'm extremely lazy. we shook on it. this is apparently how you choose the person you live with.
beats.quote: I get in the dumps at times, and don’t open my mouth for days on end.

beats.title: The Brain Attic
beats.modern: my flatmate did not know the earth goes round the sun. I told him. he said he'd do his best to forget it. his theory: your head is a small attic with fixed shelf space, and every useless fact you shove in pushes a useful one out the door. so the entire solar system got deleted to make room for cigar ash. and infuriatingly, the build works.
beats.quote: “I consider that a man’s brain originally is like a little empty attic, and you have to stock it with such furniture as you choose.

beats.title: I Wrote It Myself
beats.modern: I'm reading this insufferable magazine article about reading a stranger's whole life off his shirt cuffs, and I absolutely go off. armchair twaddle. I'd bet a thousand to one against him. and my flatmate says, flat, not looking up: you would lose your money. I wrote it myself. then explains he invented a job. when the actual police are stuck, they come to HIM.
beats.quote: I’m a consulting detective, if you can understand what that is.

beats.title: The Brixton Letter
beats.modern: letter comes in. empty house off the Brixton Road, dead American on the floorboards, blood in the room but not one wound on him, nothing stolen, no way to tell how he died. Scotland Yard is literally begging my flatmate for help and he's on the sofa going, eh, they'll pocket the credit anyway. then he grabs his coat mid-sentence. get your hat.
beats.quote: There had been no robbery, nor is there any evidence as to how the man met his death.

beats.title: No Data Yet
beats.modern: ask him what he's thinking on the way to a murder and he talks to me about violins. Stradivarius versus Amati. mate. FOCUS. he says: no data yet. says forming a theory before you have the evidence quietly bends everything you look at afterwards. then makes the cab stop a hundred yards short so he can walk the last bit and read the ground.
beats.quote: “It is a capital mistake to theorize before you have all the evidence. It biases the judgment.”

beats.title: The Face And The Ring
beats.modern: the dead man is staring at the ceiling with the worst expression I have ever seen on a human face. horror and hatred, frozen there. I've watched men die at Maiwand and none of them looked like this. no wound on him. blood all over the room and none of it is his. then they lift him onto the stretcher and something small hits the boards and rolls. a wedding ring.
beats.quote: “It’s a woman’s wedding-ring.”

beats.title: RACHE
beats.modern: Lestrade hauls us into the darkest corner of the room, strikes a match on his boot, and there it is scrawled on bare plaster in blood: RACHE. he's glowing. announces the killer was writing RACHEL and got interrupted, mark his words, find the woman named Rachel. my flatmate laughs so hard he has to formally apologise to him.
beats.quote: it means that the writer was going to put the female name Rachel, but was disturbed before he or she had time to finish.

beats.title: The Tape Measure
beats.modern: twenty minutes on his hands and knees with a tape measure and a magnifying glass, whining to himself like a dog on a scent. then he stands up and reads the killer out loud like a character sheet: over six feet, small feet, square-toed boots, long nails on the right hand, red face, Indian cigar, arrived in a four-wheeler whose horse had one new shoe. and on the way out, over his shoulder: Rache is German for revenge. stop looking for Rachel.
beats.quote: “‘Rache,’ is the German for ‘revenge’; so don’t lose your time looking for Miss Rachel.”

beats.title: What John Rance Saw
beats.modern: the constable who found the body swears the street was empty. except, oh, yeah, there was one absolutely paralytic bloke draped over the railings singing his head off. tall. red face. they propped him up and let him wander home. my flatmate hands him half a sovereign and tells him he had the killer in his arms and let go. that head of yours should be for use as well as ornament.
beats.quote: That head of yours should be for use as well as ornament.

beats.title: A Study In Scarlet
beats.modern: he's not worried at all. the killer came back for that ring, so the ring is bait, so he already has him. then he leans back in the cab and names the case: a study in scarlet. one scarlet thread of murder running through the plain grey wool of ordinary life, and the job is to pull it out and hold up every inch of it. then he starts SINGING. we're going to a concert.
beats.quote: There’s the scarlet thread of murder running through the colourless skein of life, and our duty is to unravel it, and isolate it, and expose every inch of it.

beats.title: Old Woman Be Damned
beats.modern: we advertise the ring as found, I load my service revolver, we wait for a desperate man. in shuffles somebody's ancient granny with a forty-minute saga about her daughter Sally. takes the ring, blesses us, leaves. he tails her cab clear across London and when it finally stops the cab is EMPTY. old woman be damned, he says. that was a young man in costume and WE were the old women.
beats.quote: “Old woman be damned!”

beats.title: Stangerson Too
beats.modern: second American, found at dawn. a thin red ribbon of blood curling out from under a locked hotel door, window wide open, ladder standing in the lane behind, one stab straight to the heart. and Lestrade builds up to the big reveal, what do you think was written above the body, and my flatmate answers before he can: RACHE. in blood. nobody said anything for a while after that.
beats.quote: “The word RACHE, written in letters of blood,”

beats.title: The Two Pills
beats.modern: two pills in a little box from the dead man's windowsill. he halves one, dissolves it in milk, feeds it to the poor old terrier downstairs the landlady wanted put out of its pain. nothing happens. he's PACING, it can't be a coincidence, it can't. then: AH. HE HAS IT. cuts the other pill. dog is gone in a second flat. one pill kills, one does nothing. somebody was making men gamble for their lives.
beats.quote: Of the two pills in that box one was of the most deadly poison, and the other was entirely harmless.

beats.title: Just Help Me With This Buckle
beats.modern: he sends the street kid down for a cabman to help carry his luggage. bloke kneels to do up a strap. click. and my flatmate stands up smiling and introduces the room to Jefferson Hope, who killed both Americans. the cabman goes THROUGH the window, glass and woodwork, and it takes four grown men to drag him back and pin his feet.
beats.quote: “let me introduce you to Mr. Jefferson Hope, the murderer of Enoch Drebber and of Joseph Stangerson.”

beats.title: Twenty Years Earlier
beats.modern: hard cut, chat. twenty years back, salt desert, other side of the world. a man is dying of thirst carrying a five year old girl, because every other person in their party is already dead, including her mother. she asks if they're dying too. he says yes. she LAUGHS, because that means she gets to see her mum again. three buzzards land on the rock above them and wait.
beats.quote: Why, of course, now as long as we die we’ll be with mother again.”

beats.title: Join Or Bleach
beats.modern: then ten thousand people come over the horizon and pull them both out of the sand. their leader offers exactly one deal: come with us, but only as believers, we keep no wolves in the fold. better your bones bleach out here than you rot the whole fruit. the old man says he'll take any terms going. his name is John Ferrier. he keeps the girl and calls her Lucy.
beats.quote: Better far that your bones should bleach in this wilderness than that you should prove to be that little speck of decay which in time corrupts the whole fruit.

beats.title: Rescued From A Stampede
beats.modern: twelve years on. Lucy rides into town, gets swallowed by a cattle drive, horse panicking, horns in its flank, one slip and she goes under the hooves. a hunter shoves through the herd, grabs her bridle, hauls her out. she looks up at this dark, savage-looking man and says, deadpan, who'd have thought Poncho would be so scared of a few cows. his name is Jefferson Hope. hold onto it.
beats.quote: “whoever would have thought that Poncho would have been so scared by a lot of cows?”

beats.title: Two Months At The Outside
beats.modern: he has silver mines to get working in Nevada. he takes both her hands at the gate and says two months at the outside, then I come back and claim you. her father already said yes. he rides off without looking back once, because looking back would break him. she goes inside the happiest girl in Utah. write that line down, chat. we're going to need it.
beats.quote: In two months you shall see me.”

beats.title: The Prophet's Deadline
beats.modern: the Prophet himself walks into the farmhouse and gets to it: your daughter is the flower of Utah and she cannot marry outside the faith. Stangerson has a son. Drebber has a son. she picks one. she gets a month. and on his way out the door he says it would be better for the pair of you to be bleached skeletons on the Sierra Blanco than to set your weak wills against the Holy Four.
beats.quote: “that you and she were now lying blanched skeletons upon the Sierra Blanco, than that you should put your weak wills against the orders of the Holy Four!”

beats.title: The Suitor Auction
beats.modern: two lads turn up at the farm to bid for her, feet on the stove, whistling a hymn. one opens with: I only have four wives and Drebber here has seven, so my claim is stronger. the other counters with his father's mills. they do this in front of her father. he stands up and offers them two exits, the door or the window, and they take the door promising he'll rue it.
beats.quote: As I have but four wives and Brother Drebber here has seven, it appears to me that my claim is the stronger one.”

beats.title: Nine From Seven
beats.modern: they go out the side window in the dark, past two watchers hooting like owls at each other, and into the mountains. then a voice from a rock over the trail: who goes there. by whose permission. nine from seven. and Hope gives back the countersign he happened to overhear in Ferrier's own garden an hour ago. seven from five. pass, and the Lord go with you. I have never been so tense about arithmetic.
beats.quote: “Pass, and the Lord go with you,”

beats.title: The Camp Was Empty
beats.modern: Hope goes out to shoot dinner, gets turned around in the gorges, comes back five hours late shouting into the dark. nothing answers but his own echo. fire cold. horses gone. old man gone. girl gone. and off to one side, a low heap of fresh red soil with a stick in it and a sheet of paper: JOHN FERRIER. that's it. that's the whole epitaph.
beats.quote: There was no mistaking it for anything but a newly-dug grave.

beats.title: Married Yesterday
beats.modern: he walks back down into the valley half dead and there are FLAGS up. bunting. a festival. he grabs a man he knows and asks what happened to Lucy Ferrier. married yesterday. to Drebber. and the reason it's Drebber and not Stangerson is that Stangerson shot her father, which they argued gave HIM the better claim, and the council voted it the other way. the man says he saw death in her face.
beats.quote: “She was married yesterday to young Drebber.

beats.title: The Ring Off Her Finger
beats.modern: she never lifts her head again. dead inside a month. the husband who married her for the farm doesn't bother pretending to grieve. his other wives sit up with the body the night before the burial, and the door bangs open, and a wrecked weather-beaten man walks past every one of them without a word, kisses her forehead, and takes the wedding ring off her finger. she shall not be buried in that. that ring is the one that rolls across the floorboards in Brixton, twenty years later.
beats.quote: “She shall not be buried in that,”

beats.title: Two Continents
beats.modern: then he hunts them. for twenty years. his black hair goes grey doing it. one glimpse of a face in a window in Cleveland and Drebber has him ARRESTED to buy time, and by the time he's released the pair have sailed for Europe. St Petersburg, Paris, Copenhagen, always days behind them, taking any menial job that pays the next leg. London is where he finally runs them down.
beats.quote: Year passed into year, his black hair turned grizzled, but still he wandered on, a human bloodhound,

beats.title: The Clock In His Chest
beats.modern: at the station he says he'd like to make a statement, and also, doctor, put your hand here. I do. his chest is HUMMING. aortic aneurism, days from bursting, and he's known for years. he says he doesn't care how soon it goes now the work is done, he just doesn't want to be remembered as a common cut-throat. then he tells us all of it. judge, jury and executioner, all rolled into one, and you'd have done the same.
beats.quote: I determined that I should be judge, jury, and executioner all rolled into one.

beats.title: Choose And Eat
beats.modern: he drives a blind drunk Drebber to the empty house, lights a candle, holds it up to his own face and asks: who am I. watches it land. watches the man understand. then puts the box on the table. two pills. one kills, one is nothing. choose and eat, I'll take whichever you leave, let's see if there's justice on this earth or whether we're just ruled by chance. Drebber chose. Drebber lost.
beats.quote: Choose and eat. There is death in one and life in the other. I shall take what you leave.

beats.title: Why He Wrote Rache
beats.modern: and RACHE? the clue that had every newspaper in London screaming about secret societies, that had the Yard hunting German revolutionaries? his nose was bleeding from sheer excitement, he remembered reading about a case in New York, and he thought it would be funny to send the police the wrong way. that's it. that's the whole fucking reason. then he went for the secretary, offered him the same two pills, got jumped, and used the knife instead.
beats.quote: I guessed that what puzzled the New Yorkers would puzzle the Londoners,

beats.title: Thursday Came
beats.modern: trial was set for the Thursday. Thursday came and there was nothing for us to testify to. the thing in his chest burst the night after we took him, and they found him in the morning stretched on the floor of the cell with a calm smile on his face. like a man looking back on a job he came a long way to finish.
beats.quote: A higher Judge had taken the matter in hand,

beats.title: They Get A Testimonial
beats.modern: and the papers? the papers say the credit for the whole capture belongs entirely to Lestrade and Gregson, and mention a Mr Sherlock Holmes as an amateur who may hope in time to reach their level. he just laughs. told you at the start, he says. all our study in scarlet, and they get a testimonial. so fine. I'm writing every fact of it down myself. you're reading it.
beats.quote: It is an open secret that the credit of this smart capture belongs entirely to the well-known Scotland Yard officials, Messrs. Lestrade and Gregson.

the-anabasis-of-alexander.title: The Anabasis of Alexander: or, The history of the wars and conquests of Alexander the Great
the-anabasis-of-alexander.author: Arrian

beats.title: Day One Of The Grind
beats.modern: dad's dead. I'm twenty. inherited a war nobody thinks I can run. rode down to Peloponnesus and asked every Greek state to hand me command against Persia. all yes except Sparta, who said they don't follow, they lead. cool. noted for later. back to Macedonia to pack for Asia.

beats.title: Thebes Revolts
beats.modern: Thebes flipped on me so we brought everything. Perdiccas jumps the wall before the signal, the line breaks, and the Thebans run so hard they can't get their own gates shut behind them. and then it stops being us doing the killing. the Phocians and Plataeans had two hundred years of grudge saved up. nobody spared. not one.

beats.title: One House Left Standing
beats.modern: the allies voted: raze it, sell the survivors, split the farmland. I pulled exactly one house out of the wreckage. the poet's. chat, I deleted an entire city off the map and kept Pindar's address because I like his work. sit with that.

beats.title: Lucky Guy, Achilles
beats.modern: laid a wreath on Achilles' grave. Hephaestion did Patroclus, obviously. and standing there I said the quiet part: lucky man, he got Homer. that's the flex, chat. not the kills. the coverage. you can win everything and still lose if nobody clips it.
beats.quote: Alexander pronounced Achilles fortunate in getting Homer as the herald of his fame to posterity.[115]

beats.title: The Granicus Helmet
beats.modern: spear shatters mid-charge. ask my guard for his, his is snapped too. Demaratus hands me one and I put Darius's son-in-law on the ground with it. then a scimitar takes a chunk off my helmet, and there's a SECOND blade already up behind my head. Clitus takes the man's arm off at the shoulder, sword still in the hand. remember that name.

beats.title: Except The Lacedaemonians
beats.modern: shipped 300 suits of Persian armour back to Athens to hang in the Acropolis with a plaque on it. read the plaque. from Alexander and all the Greeks. EXCEPT the Lacedaemonians. Sparta said they don't follow, they lead. fine. then they don't get their name on the trophy.
beats.quote: “Alexander, son of Philip, and all the Greeks except the Lacedaemonians, present this offering from the spoils taken from the foreigners inhabiting Asia.”

beats.title: The Knot
beats.modern: there's a wagon in the citadel tied with a knot that has no ends and no beginning, and the prophecy says whoever unties it rules Asia. nothing to pull. nothing to pick at. so I drew my sword and untied it. that's the word I used. untied. thunder that night, so the gods signed off.

beats.title: Drink While He Reads
beats.modern: swam in a freezing river, now I'm convulsing with fever and every doctor has written me off except Philip. he's mixing the cup. mid-mix, a letter arrives from Parmenio: your doctor is bought and paid for by Darius. so I take the cup, hand HIM the letter, and drink it while he reads. eye contact the whole way down.

beats.title: Into The River At A Run
beats.modern: went into the river at a sprint to get inside their arrow range and their left wing folded on contact. but our centre snagged on the bank, the phalanx split, and Darius's Greek mercenaries poured into the seam like they'd been waiting for it. the line everyone calls unbeatable nearly lost its name in that gap. 120 good men gone in it.

beats.title: Wrong Man, Right Answer
beats.modern: took his tent and there's women weeping inside. they think he's dead because we've got his bow and his cloak. his mother comes out and bows to Hephaestion, because Hephaestion is taller. she realises, she's mortified, she starts backing away. I told her she made no mistake. he's Alexander too.
beats.quote: the king told her she had made no mistake, for Hephaestion was also an Alexander.

beats.title: Seven Months For An Island
beats.modern: they were on an island so we built a road through the sea to reach them. seven months. halfway through they dragged our captured men onto the wall where the whole camp could watch and cut them down into the water. so when the wall finally came apart, nobody was in a listening mood. 8,000 dead in the streets. 30,000 sold.

beats.title: If I Were Parmenio
beats.modern: Darius offers 10,000 talents, his daughter, and everything west of the Euphrates. Parmenio says if he were me he'd take it. I said yeah, if I were Parmenio I'd take it too. wrote back that I don't want money that's already mine, or a slice of what's already mine, and if I want the daughter I'll take her without his permission.
beats.quote: So would he also do, if he were Parmenio, but as he was Alexander he replied to Darius as he did.

beats.title: Bird Drops A Rock On Me
beats.modern: engineers said the mound's too high, can't be stormed. perfect. impossible is the entire reason I'm here. then mid-sacrifice a bird flies over and drops a rock straight on my head, and my prophet goes: you'll take the city, but watch yourself today. thanks. love the specificity.
beats.quote: “O king, thou wilt indeed capture the city, but thou must take care of thyself on this day.”

beats.title: Drawn In Barley
beats.modern: found the spot for the city and there's nothing to mark the walls with. no chalk, no rope, no lime. so we tip out the soldiers' barley and I walk the outline while they pour. prophets took one look and said the city would be rich above all in the fruits of the earth. we drew it in food, chat.

beats.title: Into The Sand To Ask
beats.modern: walking into the Libyan desert to ask a god who my father actually is. the wind wipes the road out, no trees, no hills, guides admit they're lost. then it rains. in the desert. and something goes out in front of us the whole way. Ptolemy swears they were talking snakes. Aristobulus says two ravens. either way we came back out.

beats.title: Heard What I Wanted
beats.modern: went in alone. asked. came out. official statement: I heard what I wanted to hear. no I'm not telling chat the question. no I'm not telling chat the answer. no hints. clip ends here and we ride for Memphis.

beats.title: No Stealing In The Dark
beats.modern: night before the big one, Parmenio comes to the tent: hit them in the dark, they're standing to arms, they're terrified, they'll break. and he's right, it would work. that's the problem. I said stealing a victory is mean. we do it at noon in front of everybody so nobody gets to say I won by trick.
beats.quote: it would be mean to steal a victory, and that Alexander ought to conquer in open daylight, and without any artifice.

beats.title: The Gap At Gaugamela
beats.modern: their line opens for one second to plug the flank and I take the wedge straight into the hole, straight at him. maybe a minute of face-to-face and he's the first man on his own field to turn and run. AGAIN. second time this man has left the building before his own army knew it lost.

beats.title: I Burned The Palace
beats.modern: burned the palace at Persepolis. Parmenio said don't, it's your house now, and the locals will decide you're only passing through. I said it's for Athens, for the temples they burned first. chat, I've had a long time to think about it, and even the man writing this down says I got it wrong.

beats.title: I Never Got To Speak To Him
beats.modern: rode four hundred stades through the night on borrowed horses and caught them at first light, unarmed, strung out on the road. they had him in a covered cart. when they heard us coming his own officers stabbed him and rode off. he bled out before I reached the cart. the King of Asia, dumped by his staff in a wagon. I never got to say one word to him.

beats.title: The Father Too
beats.modern: Philotas heard there was a plot on my life and said nothing. in my tent twice a day, every day, nothing. the army speared him. then I sent riders ahead to Media with letters and had his father killed too. Parmenio. who commanded half of everything I own. because you do not leave alive the man whose son you just executed.

beats.title: Nose And Ears
beats.modern: brought the man who chained Darius in front of everyone, had his nose and ears cut off, and sent him to Ecbatana to die in front of the Medes. and I'm standing there saying it in Persian clothes. my own historian stops the story here to tell you I was becoming the thing I beat. conquered the empire, got conquered by the wardrobe.

beats.title: This Hand
beats.modern: drinking party, everyone racing to tell me I outrank actual gods. Clitus won't play. says the wins were the army's. says my father did more. then he throws his right hand out at me: this hand saved you at the Granicus. the hand. the actual hand. I called for my guards and not one man moved, so I picked up a pike and did it myself.
beats.quote: said:—“This hand, O Alexander, preserved thee on that occasion.”

beats.title: One Kiss Poorer
beats.modern: new format: you bow Persian style, you get a kiss from me. cup goes round, everyone bows, everyone gets kissed. Callisthenes drinks, skips the bow entirely, and strolls up for his kiss anyway. someone snitches on him mid-walk. I turn my head away. he just shrugs and says he's leaving one kiss poorer. whole room heard it.
beats.quote: said:—“I am going away only with the loss of a kiss.”

beats.title: The Pages Read My Receipts
beats.modern: my own pages planned to knife me in my sleep. at the trial Hermolaus stood up and read my list back to my face: Philotas, Parmenio, Clitus, the bowing, the drinking. said he couldn't live under it. they stoned him. Callisthenes died in chains, or on the rack, depending which of my closest friends you ask. they don't agree. that's its own answer.

beats.title: Winged Soldiers
beats.modern: asked the rock to surrender on good terms. they laughed in my face and said come back when you've got soldiers with wings. so 300 men went up the worst face of a frozen cliff in the dark on tent pegs and flax rope. thirty fell and we never found the bodies. at dawn I sent a herald to the gate: look up. the winged men are here.

beats.title: Roxana
beats.modern: the rock came with a family in it. saw her once and that was the whole event. and before chat starts: she was a prisoner and I married her instead, properly, and I wore the criticism. same reason I never went near Darius's wife. you can take a continent and still not take that.

beats.title: Ships Backing Water
beats.modern: never fought anything like it. their cavalry backs into their own elephants for safety, we swarm the elephants, and the elephants lose it and start flattening both armies equally. no favourites. at the end they backed off slow, still facing us, like ships rowing backwards, making this thin high whistling noise. I still hear that noise.

beats.title: In A Kingly Way
beats.modern: he's over seven feet, shot through the shoulder, still upright on the elephant, still not running. I ask him how he wants to be treated. he says: treat me in a kingly way. I ask if he wants to add anything to that. he says that covers everything. gave him his kingdom back and more land on top.
beats.quote: “Treat me, O Alexander, in a kingly way!”

beats.title: Bucephala
beats.modern: he was thirty. no wound. just old, and done, and finished on the same day as the biggest fight of my life. he never let anyone else on his back. once when he was stolen I told an entire country I'd kill every person in it unless he came home, and he was back the same day. built a city on the river and named it after my horse.

beats.title: There's More River
beats.modern: there's another river, and past it better land, better fighters, more elephants than anyone's seen, and I want it so badly my teeth hurt. and the camp has gone quiet in the wrong way. men saying out loud they won't follow even if I go first. so I called the officers in: talk me forward, or talk me home. those are the options.

beats.title: The Only Army That Beat Me
beats.modern: Coenus said it out loud for all of them and the room started crying. so I sulked. told them fine, go home, tell your families you left your king in enemy country. three days in the tent, no visitors, waiting for the mood to turn. it didn't. then the sacrifice came back bad and I announced the retreat. the only army that ever beat me was mine.

beats.title: Somebody Broke The Ladder
beats.modern: ladder crew was too slow so I took one off a man, put it up myself and went first under my shield. then the guards all piled on behind me at once and SNAPPED it. so now it's me, alone, standing on top of an enemy wall while a whole city shoots at me. options were: climb down and look ridiculous, or jump in. chat, you know me.

beats.title: Air Out Of The Wound
beats.modern: arrow through the breastplate into the chest. Ptolemy says air came out of the hole with the blood every time I breathed. I kept swinging while the blood was still warm and then the ground tilted and I went down onto my own shield. Peucestas stood over me with the shield from Troy. up on the wall the whole army heard itself start screaming.

beats.title: Take The Cover Off
beats.modern: they think I'm dead and being shipped home in a covered boat. so I have the awning stripped off the stern and lift my hand as we come in. then I refuse the stretcher and get on a horse. then I get OFF the horse so they can watch me walk to my own tent. men touching my knees, my hands, my clothes. one old Boeotian just says: great deeds, great suffering, that's the deal.

beats.title: Sixty Days Of Sand
beats.modern: took the desert route on purpose because Cyrus lost his army here and came out with seven men, and I wanted to be the one who didn't. the sand swallows your leg to the knee like fresh snow. the pack animals go first, then the men. reach water by dawn and you lived. get caught out there by the sun and nothing about you mattered.

beats.title: The Helmet
beats.modern: scouts find a puddle in a crack in the rock. they scrape it together and run it to me in a helmet like they're carrying gold, the whole army watching their king get water while they get none. I thanked them. I held it up so everyone could see it. then I poured it into the sand. and the whole army got up like every man had drunk.

beats.title: They Just Stamped
beats.modern: Indian philosophers watch my whole army come over the hill and their response is to stamp on the ground. I ask what that means. they say: every man owns exactly this much earth, the patch under his feet. you're a man like us, just noisier and more of a nuisance, and you'll die owning exactly enough dirt to be buried in.
beats.quote: thou also wilt soon die, and possess only as much of the earth as is sufficient for thy body to be buried in.”

beats.title: Calanus Books It
beats.modern: Calanus got ill and decided he was done, and no illness was going to make the decision for him. I argued for weeks and lost. he rode out on a litter singing, gave his horse away, handed his cups to his students, lay down on the pyre and did not move once. not once. I gave the order, the trumpets went up, and the elephants screamed for him.

beats.title: Eighty Weddings At Once
beats.modern: married Darius's daughter. gave her sister to Hephaestion so our children would be cousins. eighty of my officers married Persian and Median noblewomen the same day, Persian rite, all of us seated in a row, dowries on me. then I found out 10,000 of the lads had already married local women and paid for those too. apparently the most popular thing I ever did.

beats.title: No Names On The Table
beats.modern: told the army I'd clear every man's debts. barely anyone signed up, because they were certain it was a test to find out who was bad with money. fair. so I put tables of silver out in the camp instead: bring the bond, take the cash, nobody writes your name down. 20,000 talents gone. they were happier about the anonymity than the money.

beats.title: What Did I Keep
beats.modern: you want to go home? go. but first, the tape: my father found you in animal skins running from Illyrians and put cloaks on your backs. I inherited 60 talents and 500 in debt and handed you Egypt, Babylon, Susa, and the sea at both ends. you're governors now. you're generals. what did I keep out of all of it? this robe and this hat. I eat what you eat and I stay awake so you can sleep.

beats.title: All Of You, Kinsmen
beats.modern: so I handed the commands to Persians and called THEM my kin. two days later my Macedonians are lying in the dirt outside my gates, weapons on the ground, saying they won't move until I come out. old Callines says what hurts is the word kin, and the kiss that comes with it. I said all of you, without exception, are my kin. then 9,000 of us drank out of the same bowl.
beats.quote: said:—“But all of you without exception I consider my kinsmen, and so from this time I shall call you.”

beats.title: Day Seven Of The Fever
beats.modern: he got a fever. day seven I'm sitting at the boys' games with a full stadium when word comes that it's bad. I went straight there. he was already gone. lay on him most of a day. cut my hair off for him like Achilles did. sent an offering to the healing god with a message attached: you did not treat me fairly.
beats.quote: remark:—“Although Asclepius has not treated me fairly, in not saving the life of my Companion, whom I valued equally with my own head.”[906]

beats.title: Don't Enter The City
beats.modern: Chaldaean priests pull me off the road outside Babylon. their god says walking into that city will not go well for me. I quoted Euripides at them, the best prophet is the one who guesses right, and kept walking. they said fine, at least don't come in facing west. the ground made facing east impossible. so. west it was.
beats.quote: “He the best prophet is that guesses well.”[923]

beats.title: The Diary
beats.modern: the log reads like this. drank at Medius's. bathed. slept. fever. carried out to the sacrifices on a couch. gave the fleet its sailing date anyway. bathed. fever. orders. bathed. fever. orders. day after day of a man scheduling a voyage he is not going on. at the end they came in and I knew every single face and couldn't produce one word.

beats.title: To The Best
beats.modern: they let the whole army file past the bed. I couldn't speak, so I lifted my head for each man and moved my eyes. that was the goodbye. somebody asked who gets the empire. to the best. and I told them there'd be a funeral contest over it like nothing they'd ever seen. chat. I was right about that.
beats.quote: “To the best.”[969]

beats.title: Stream's Over
beats.modern: thirty-two years and eight months. twelve years and eight months of it on the throne. that's the whole run. gg. Ptolemy's got the VODs and he's the one writing them down.

beats.title: Kansas Is Gray
beats.modern: welcome to the stream, chat. this is Kansas. the grass is gray, the dirt is gray, the house used to be painted and now it's gray. my aunt is gray. my uncle is gray from his beard down to his boots and he has never once laughed. Aunt Em screams when I laugh because she forgot people do that. render distance infinite, content zero.

beats.title: The House Goes Up
beats.modern: wind from the north, wind from the south, and Uncle Henry says cyclone and runs for the cows. Aunt Em drops into the cellar. I go back for my dog and the floor throws me. chat the HOUSE is in the air. we're in the exact middle of the storm where it's calm, riding it like a feather, and I'm being rocked like a baby in a cradle. this is not how houses work.

beats.title: Dog Overboard
beats.modern: TOTO FELL DOWN THE TRAPDOOR. mid flight. a thousand feet up. ...and then he just stops, chat. the air pressure holds him there like a cork with one ear sticking out of the hole. I grabbed the ear. dragged him back in. shut the door. never opening that again.

beats.title: New Map Just Dropped
beats.modern: we landed. hard, but the bed took it. I open the door and chat there is COLOR. green grass, trees with fruit actually on them, birds that look expensive, a brook doing brook noises. yesterday I was looking at cracked dirt all the way to the edge of the sky. new map just dropped and it isn't gray.

beats.title: Manslaughter By Real Estate
beats.modern: a tiny old woman in a star covered gown bows to me and thanks me for the murder. what murder. she points at the corner of my house. there are FEET sticking out from under it. silver shoes, pointed toes, very much attached to a dead witch. chat I committed manslaughter with real estate and an entire village is throwing me a parade for it.
beats.quote: We are so grateful to you for having killed the Wicked Witch of the East, and for setting our people free from bondage.”

beats.title: She Dried Up In The Sun
beats.modern: the Munchkins start yelling and pointing and the body is GONE. she was so old she dried up in the sun the second it hit her. all that's left in the loot pile is the silver shoes, which the good witch shakes the dust out of and hands to me. they say there's a charm on them. they say nobody ever knew what it does. unidentified item. equipping anyway.
beats.quote: “that she dried up quickly in the sun. That is the end of her.

beats.title: The Slate Told Me To Go
beats.modern: so I ask how to get home. desert east. desert south. desert west. desert north. the old lady's professional opinion: guess you live here now. I start crying and every single Munchkin pulls out a handkerchief and cries WITH me. then she balances her hat on her nose, counts to three, and it turns into a slate with my quest written on it. kisses my forehead, says the mark makes me untouchable, points at a yellow road, and vanishes.
beats.quote: “LET DOROTHY GO TO THE CITY OF EMERALDS”

beats.title: The Guy On The Pole
beats.modern: there's a scarecrow on a pole in the corn and chat he WINKED at me. I pull the pole out of his back and he says being up there was very tedious. sir. that is the entire job. then he tells me he has no brains and can't stand people thinking he's a fool, so he's coming to see the wizard with me. I ask if there's anything he's afraid of. he says a lighted match.
beats.quote: “it’s a lighted match.”

beats.title: The Rusted Man
beats.modern: something's groaning in the woods. it's a man made entirely of tin, frozen mid swing with the axe still up over his head. he says he's been groaning for over a year and nobody ever came. first request out of his mouth is an oil can, and chat, it's on a shelf in his own cottage. he's been ten feet from the fix the whole time and couldn't turn his neck to look.
beats.quote: I’ve been groaning for more than a year, and no one has ever heard me before or come to help me.”

beats.title: The Axe Was Enchanted
beats.modern: the tin man tells me why he's tin. he was flesh, he was in love, and the girl's guardian paid the Wicked Witch of the East to stop the wedding. the Witch enchanted his AXE. it took a leg. tinsmith made a new one. then the other leg. then both arms. then his head. then it cut him in half. every time, a tin replacement. and the last one came without a heart, so he just stopped loving her. he tells me this like a weather report.

beats.title: I Slapped A Lion
beats.modern: a LION comes out of the trees. one swipe and the scarecrow is cartwheeling, one swipe and the tin man is flat on the road, and then he goes for my dog. so I hit a lion. on the nose. with my hand. and I called him a coward and chat he didn't even argue. he hung his head and said I know. I've always known it. how do I help it.
beats.quote: “You are nothing but a big coward.”

beats.title: The Beetle Incident
beats.modern: the tin man stepped on a beetle. one beetle. he cried so hard about it that his JAW RUSTED SHUT and we had to oil his face open. now he walks with his eyes on the ground and steps over ants. the guy with no heart is the most careful creature in this forest and he thinks that's the flaw.

beats.title: Chop The Bridge
beats.modern: two Kalidahs. bear bodies, tiger heads, claws that could open the Lion like a can. we're halfway across a chopped down tree over a canyon and they follow us onto it. the scarecrow, the one with NO BRAINS, tells the tin man to chop off the end we're standing on. the log goes and they go with it. chat the fool solved it in four seconds.

beats.title: Pole In The River
beats.modern: the raft got swept, the scarecrow shoved his pole too hard into the mud, and the raft left without him. so now he's stranded on a stick in the middle of a river, thinking about how at least in the cornfield he got to pretend to scare crows. then a stork flew by, asked what was wrong, and just went and got him. he hugged everyone including the lion and sang the whole rest of the walk.
beats.quote: “I am now worse off than when I first met Dorothy,”

beats.title: The Poppy Field
beats.modern: the flowers get redder and redder until it's poppies to the horizon and chat the smell puts you to sleep forever. Toto goes down first. then me. straw and tin don't breathe, so they carried me out in a chair made of their hands. the Lion made it almost to the edge and dropped. too heavy to lift. the tin man's verdict was to leave him there and hope he dreams he found courage.

beats.title: Towed By Mice
beats.modern: the tin man saved a field mouse from a wildcat and it turned out to be the QUEEN. so she brings thousands of them, every single one carrying a piece of string in its mouth, and they harness themselves to a wooden cart and drag a full grown lion out of the poison field. the King of Beasts, towed to safety by mice. he woke up and laughed about it.

beats.title: The Glasses Lock On
beats.modern: gate guy says the Emerald City is so bright it will blind you, so everyone has to wear green glasses. then he LOCKS them onto our heads. golden bands, one key, hanging around his neck. he put a pair on my dog. chat nobody in this city has seen anything without a green filter in years. remember that.

beats.title: The Great And Terrible Head
beats.modern: the throne room has a giant floating HEAD in it. no body, no arms, eyes that track you across the floor. I tell it I'm Dorothy, the Small and Meek, and I just want to go home. it says in this country everyone pays for what they get. the price for my ride home is killing the Wicked Witch of the West. chat I'm a kid from Kansas with a dog.
beats.quote: “I am Dorothy, the Small and Meek. I have come to you for help.”

beats.title: Four Different Faces
beats.modern: we all go in one at a time and chat, he's a DIFFERENT THING for each of us. I got the floating head. the scarecrow got a beautiful winged lady. the tin man got a five eyed rhino monster with five arms and five legs. the lion got a ball of fire that singed his whiskers. same demand every time: kill her first, gifts after. he doesn't even care which of us does it.

beats.title: Forty Of Everything
beats.modern: the Witch runs three waves at us. forty wolves: the tin man stands in front and swings forty times, then sits down like he mowed a lawn. forty crows: the scarecrow stands up alone and wrings forty necks. then a swarm of bees, so he has his own straw pulled out and buries us under it, and the bees break every stinger on tin and die in little heaps like coal. chat the fool and the heartless one are running our entire defense.

beats.title: The Monkeys Take Everything
beats.modern: she burns her last Golden Cap wish and the sky fills with Winged Monkeys. they drop the tin man on a field of rocks until he can't move or groan. they pull every piece of straw out of the scarecrow and throw his clothes into a tree. they tie the lion up like cargo. then the leader comes for me, sees the kiss mark on my forehead, and stops dead. can't touch me. so they just deliver me to her doorstep.

beats.title: Scullery Duty
beats.modern: I'm a kitchen slave now. pots, kettles, floor, keep the fire fed. every night I sneak food out to the Lion in the yard so he can keep refusing to be harnessed like a horse. she waves the umbrella at me but never lands it, because of the kiss. she did hit my dog once. Toto bit her leg and chat, she didn't bleed. she's been wicked so long the blood in her dried up years ago.

beats.title: The Bucket
beats.modern: she tripped me with an invisible iron bar to steal one of my silver shoes. so I got mad and threw the water bucket at her. chat she started MELTING. screaming that water is the end of her, asking didn't I know. I didn't know. I said sorry while she went brown and shapeless across my clean kitchen floor. then I swept her out the door and put my shoe back on.
beats.quote: “Didn’t you know water would be the end of me?”

beats.title: The Castle Is Mine Now
beats.modern: first thing I did with the castle was tell the Winkies they aren't slaves anymore. they still keep the day as a holiday. then we went and got my friends. tinsmiths hammered the tin man back into shape over three days and four nights, and we chopped down the tree holding the scarecrow's clothes and restuffed him with clean straw. both of them cried and one had to be wiped down so his face wouldn't rust. also I looted a gold cap out of her cupboard because it was pretty.

beats.title: The Screen Falls Over
beats.modern: the Lion roars to scare the wizard, Toto jumps, and knocks over a SCREEN in the corner. behind it: a little bald old man with a wrinkled face, looking exactly as shocked as we are. no head. no lady. no beast. no fireball. he says please don't hit me and I'll do anything you want. chat the Great and Terrible has been making believe this entire time.
beats.quote: “I have been making believe.”

beats.title: Born In Omaha
beats.modern: his lore drop: born in Omaha, trained as a ventriloquist, became a circus balloon guy, floated off one day and couldn't get down. lands here, the locals see a man come out of the clouds and decide he's a wizard, and he lets them. has them build a city, calls it Emerald, and locks green glasses on every face so the name checks out. I asked if everything here is green. he said no more than in any other city.
beats.quote: “No more than in any other city,”

beats.title: Bran, Silk And A Green Drink
beats.modern: and then the fake wizard delivers anyway. the scarecrow's head gets emptied and refilled with BRAN and a fistful of pins and needles, which stick out the top, and the Lion says that proves he's sharp. the tin man gets a silk heart stuffed with sawdust soldered into his chest. the Lion drinks something green out of a dish and declares himself full of courage. none of it is real. all of it works.

beats.title: The Balloon Leaves Without Me
