beats.modern: every armed prophet won. every unarmed one got wiped. people are easy to convince and impossible to keep convinced, so build for the day the belief runs out. Savonarola owned this whole city on words alone, the mood turned, and he had no way to hold the believers or force the rest. that is the entire mechanic.

beats.title: They Fly Up And Fall Off
beats.modern: the ones handed a state have no trouble climbing, because they never climb, they fly. all the difficulty is waiting at the top. no idea how to command, having lived private their whole lives. no loyal troops. and the whole thing rests on the mood of the man who gifted it. anything that grows that fast has no roots and the first storm takes it.

beats.title: The Block And The Knife
beats.modern: Romagna was lawless, so Borgia sent in the cruelest man he owned with unlimited authority. peace in weeks. everybody hated the enforcer, which was the design. then one morning Borgia had him executed and left in the square at Cesena, the block on one side and the bloody knife on the other. the people went home satisfied AND terrified at the same time. he outsourced the cruelty and then executed the outsourcing.
beats.quote: he took Ramiro, and one morning caused him to be executed and left on the piazza at Cesena with the block and a bloody knife at his side.

beats.title: He Planned For Everything
beats.modern: the day Julius got elected, Borgia told me this to my face: I thought through every single thing that could happen when my father died, and I had a remedy ready for all of it. the one scenario I never ran was that I would be dying at the same time. he had a counter for the entire board and got removed by a fever.

beats.title: One Meeting, One City
beats.modern: a potter's son calls the people and the senate of Syracuse together like it is a routine governance session. gives a signal. his soldiers kill every senator and every rich man in the room. he walks out holding the city and there is not one riot afterwards. one meeting. that is the whole coup.

beats.title: Empire, Not Glory
beats.modern: before you clip that: I said it worked, I never said it was greatness. he climbed on real ability, through a thousand dangers, nothing handed to him. but slaughtering your own citizens, betraying friends, no faith, no mercy, no religion? that route buys an empire. it does not buy glory. two separate accounts and you can only fund one.
beats.quote: to slay fellow-citizens, to deceive friends, to be without faith, without mercy, without religion; such methods may gain empire, but not glory.

beats.title: All The Damage At Once
beats.modern: do all the harm in one night. every bit of it, at once, then never again. drip it out daily and you are holding the knife forever, nobody can relax around you, and nobody ever attaches. rewards run the opposite direction: hand those out slowly, in small pieces, so the taste stays in the mouth longer.
beats.quote: For injuries ought to be done all at one time, so that, being tasted less, they offend less; benefits ought to be given little by little, so that the flavour of them may last longer.

beats.title: Kinder Than Mercy
beats.modern: Borgia got labelled cruel. his cruelty gave Romagna peace, unity and loyalty. Florence protected its nice-guy reputation and let Pistoia tear itself apart instead. so who was actually merciful. a few examples early is mercy at scale. mercy that lets the murders and the robberies start hits everybody. one offends an individual, the other guts a whole people.

beats.title: Good Arms Make Good Laws
beats.modern: two foundations under every state: good laws and good weapons. but there are no good laws in a state that cannot defend itself, so really there is one foundation and it is the weapons. where the arms are good the laws follow automatically. so I will be skipping the law section entirely.
beats.quote: as there cannot be good laws where the state is not well armed,

beats.title: Cowards You Pay
beats.modern: hired soldiers: brave in front of you, cowards in front of the enemy. no unity, no discipline, no loyalty, no fear of god. the only thing keeping them on the field is a small wage, and nobody dies for a small wage. peacetime they rob you. wartime the enemy robs you. you are paying twice for zero defence.
beats.quote: they are disunited, ambitious, and without discipline, unfaithful, valiant before friends, cowardly before enemies;

beats.title: Chalk In Hand
beats.modern: the King of France took the entire length of Italy with chalk. chalk. his quartermasters walked ahead marking which houses his men would sleep in. that is what our rented armies were worth. the preachers said our sins caused it and they were right about the word and wrong about the sin. and since it was the princes' sin, the princes got the bill.

beats.title: Winning Makes You Their Prisoner
beats.modern: borrowing another ruler's army is worse than hiring mercenaries. lose and you are finished. WIN and you belong to them. mercenaries are dangerous because they are cowards, auxiliaries are dangerous because they are good, and they are all one unit taking orders from someone who is not you. with auxiliaries the ruin arrives pre-assembled.
beats.quote: for losing, one is undone, and winning, one is their captive.

beats.title: David Took It Off
beats.modern: Saul put the royal armour on David before the Goliath fight, to help. David got it on his back, said he could not use it, took the whole thing off and went with a sling and a knife. other people's equipment either slides off you, or crushes you, or ties you up. there has never been a fourth outcome.
beats.quote: the arms of others either fall from your back, or they weigh you down, or they bind you fast.

beats.title: One Subject Only
beats.modern: a ruler studies one subject and the subject is war. that is the entire syllabus. being unarmed does not just make you weak, it makes you contemptible, and no armed man has ever willingly obeyed an unarmed one. Sforza went from private citizen to Duke of Milan by being martial. his sons found soldiering uncomfortable and went from dukes back to private citizens.

beats.title: How People Actually Live
beats.modern: other writers built imaginary republics that have never existed in any place at any time. I am doing the real one. how people actually live is nowhere near how they ought to live, and if you run your rule off the ought version you get eaten. a man fully committed to being good, surrounded by men who are not, is a countdown.
beats.quote: how one lives is so far distant from how one ought to live,

beats.title: Learn How To Do Wrong
beats.modern: you have to learn how to do wrong. not do it constantly. LEARN it, hold it, deploy it only when the situation demands. nobody gets to have all the good qualities anyway, humans are not built with that many slots. so triage: dodge the vices that would cost you the state, and about the rest, stop agonising.
beats.quote: it is necessary for a prince wishing to hold his own to know how to do wrong, and to make use of it or not according to necessity.

beats.title: Generosity Is A Treadmill
beats.modern: being known as generous is a treadmill with no off switch. you spend everything holding the title, then you tax people to keep spending, so now they hate you and you are broke. offended many, rewarded few. and the moment you slow down they call you cheap anyway. you were always going to get called cheap. you just chose the expensive route there.

beats.title: Feared Over Loved
beats.modern: loved or feared? ideally both, but you cannot hold both, so: feared. men are ungrateful, fickle, liars, cowards and greedy. while you are winning they will offer you their blood, their property, their children. the second the need is actually close they are gone. love is a link THEY can snap whenever it profits them. fear is a link you hold.
beats.quote: it is much safer to be feared than loved, when, of the two, either must be dispensed with.

beats.title: Keep Your Hands Off The Money
beats.modern: be feared, never hated, and the line between them is boringly simple: stay off their property and stay off their women. if a man has to die, do it with a public reason everyone can see. but never touch assets, because excuses for seizing property are infinite and the appetite grows. a man forgets his murdered father faster than his stolen inheritance.
beats.quote: quickly forget the death of their father than the loss of their patrimony.

beats.title: The Fox And The Lion
beats.modern: two ways to fight: by law, which is human, and by force, which is animal. the first runs out constantly, so learn the second. and pick both beasts, because the lion cannot see a trap and the fox cannot survive a wolf pack. be the fox to spot the snare and the lion to scare the wolves. the pure lions have no idea what game they are in.
beats.quote: be a fox to discover the snares and a lion to terrify the wolves.

beats.title: Faith Has An Expiry
beats.modern: a promise binds you only while the reason you made it still exists. if men were all good this would be vile advice. men are not good, they will break faith with you first, so you are not bound to keep it with them. and you will never once run short of a respectable reason for the breach. those are free and unlimited.

beats.title: You Only Need The Appearance
beats.modern: you do not need the virtues. you need to appear to have the virtues. actually holding them at all times is the harmful build. be merciful, faithful, humane, upright, religious, convincingly, with a mind constructed to flip to the opposite the moment flipping is required. the wind changes and you turn with it.
beats.quote: it is unnecessary for a prince to have all the good qualities I have enumerated, but it is very necessary to appear to have them.

beats.title: Everyone Sees, Nobody Checks
beats.modern: everyone can see you. almost nobody gets close enough to verify you. men judge by the eye, not the hand, and by the result, not the method. the few who actually know better will not say it out loud, because the majesty of the state is standing behind the story. hold power and every method you used gets graded honest afterwards.
beats.quote: Every one sees what you appear to be, few really know what you are,

beats.title: Conspiracy Math
beats.modern: plenty of conspiracies, almost no successful ones, and here is why. a plotter cannot act alone. so he has to recruit, and the only people he can approach are malcontents. the instant he opens his mouth he has handed that man a guaranteed reward for reporting him. conspiring is offering a stranger a sure win to protect your risky secret.

beats.title: Outsource The Beatings
beats.modern: France runs this correctly. the king wanted the nobles bridled and the people shielded, but he did not want the blame from either side. so he built a separate body to do the beating down and the favouring, sitting between him and everyone. the rule generalises: hand the reproach jobs to somebody else, keep the gift-giving in your own hands.

beats.title: Hated For Good Works
beats.modern: Pertinax tried to make the army live honestly after Commodus let them run feral. they killed him for it, with a side of contempt for his age. you can earn hatred with good behaviour exactly as fast as with bad. if the group holding you up is corrupt, you have to feed the corruption, and doing right will get you removed.

beats.title: The Bodyguard You Insulted
beats.modern: Caracalla killed a centurion's brother in a humiliating way, kept threatening the man daily, and then kept him on the personal bodyguard. died in the middle of his own army, by that centurion. you cannot defend against someone who has stopped fearing death. so the entire defence is upstream: never seriously wrong the people standing next to you.

beats.title: The Best Fortress
beats.modern: build castles, do not build castles, I will praise either. but the best fortress is not being hated. hold every wall you like: if the people want you gone there will always be some foreigner delighted to hand them the ladder. the castle of Milan has caused the Sforzas more grief than any other single thing they own.
beats.quote: the best possible fortress is—not to be hated by the people,

beats.title: Never Stay Neutral
beats.modern: when two neighbours go to war, pick a side, loudly. stay neutral and the winner eats you while the loser enjoys it, and you will have no argument and nowhere to shelter. the winner does not want friends who sat out. the loser will not house the man who would not stand with him. neutrality is being disliked by everybody at the exact moment you need somebody.

beats.title: Your Staff Is The Tell
beats.modern: people read you through the people around you. capable and loyal staff means you are wise, because recognising them and holding them is the actually hard part. bad staff and the verdict is already in, because choosing them was your first decision as a ruler and you fumbled it in public.

beats.title: The Truth Committee
beats.modern: courts are stuffed with flatterers because men are hopeless about themselves. the only guard is letting it be known that the truth does not offend you. but if EVERYONE can tell you anything whenever they feel like it, respect leaks out the bottom. so: pick a few wise ones, give them the licence, only on what you ask about, then decide alone and stay decided.

beats.title: Fortune Gets Half
beats.modern: a lot of people have decided the world is run entirely by fortune and God, so why bother steering. some days I almost agree. but I refuse to kill our free will, so here is my ruling: fortune arbitrates half of what we do. maybe a bit more than half. she leaves us the rest, and the rest is where everything I have written lives.
beats.quote: Fortune is the arbiter of one-half of our actions,[1]

beats.title: The River
beats.modern: fortune is a river in flood. trees gone, buildings gone, the soil itself relocated, nothing on earth standing in front of it. and yet. in the dry season you can dig channels and raise banks so the next flood goes where you put it. she only wrecks the places where nobody prepared. Italy is open country with no banks at all.

beats.title: Nobody Changes Course
beats.modern: here is the trap. almost nobody can change method. your nature will not let you, and worse, the method WORKED for years, so you cannot believe in dropping it. then the careful man reaches the moment that demands boldness and simply cannot do it. that is the whole ruin. fortune did not turn on him. he refused to turn.

beats.title: Italy Waits For A Banner
beats.modern: Italy is lying there without a pulse. more enslaved than the Hebrews, more scattered than the Athenians. beaten, stripped, torn, overrun, no head, no order, every sore left to fester. one man looked like the answer and fortune dropped him at the top of his run. and she is still standing ready to follow a banner. any banner. there is just nobody holding one up.
beats.quote: ready and willing to follow a banner if only someone will raise it.

beats.title: You Do The Rest
beats.modern: the sea split. a cloud went ahead. water came out of the rock. manna fell. everything has already been done for you, so you do the rest. God deliberately does not do all of it, because doing all of it would take our free will and the share of the glory that belongs to us. he left you the last part on purpose. pick it up.
beats.quote: God is not willing to do everything, and thus take away our free will and that share of glory which belongs to us.

beats.title: Server Lore Recap
beats.modern: before we start, chat, quick lore. the Danes' first king washed up as a baby with nothing. no name, no family, no gear. ended his run taking tribute off every kingdom within sailing distance. when he dies they load him back onto a boat with more treasure than most nations own and shove him out to sea. nobody knows where he landed. that's the kind of server we're logging into.

beats.title: Heorot Goes Up
beats.modern: the current king builds the biggest hall anybody has ever heard of and names it Heorot. gold on the walls, rings for everyone who walks in, music every single night. he shares out everything he's been given except two things: his own life, and his men. hold onto that detail.

beats.title: Something In The Swamp
beats.modern: and there's a thing out in the marsh that can HEAR all of it. every night. laughter, harp, singing, drifting over the water to whatever is lying in the dark taking it personally. Cain's bloodline. banned by the devs at patch zero, never actually deleted. chat it has been listening for years.

beats.title: Night One, Thirty Gone
beats.modern: he waits for the sun to go down, walks into the hall after the party, and leaves with THIRTY men. thirty. and he's laughing on the way home. nobody finds out until sunrise, when the king sits down and starts counting. that's not a raid, chat. that's a wipe.

beats.title: Twelve Years Of This
beats.modern: twelve years. the best building in the world stands empty every night because nobody will sleep in it. he won't take gold, won't take a truce, won't hear terms from anyone. he just walks the fog route every night forever and no council meeting has ever fixed it.

beats.title: I'm Taking A Boat
beats.modern: I hear about it back home and I'm going. strongest guy alive, might as well be useful. I pick fourteen, I get a boat, and here's the part I like: nobody tries to talk me out of it. they know me. they read the omens, told me to go get it, and pushed us off the sand.

beats.title: Send My Gear Home
beats.modern: and if he wins, don't plan a funeral. there won't be a body. he'll carry me off dripping and eat me out in the marsh, so nobody has to dig anything. just ship my mail shirt back to my king. it's an heirloom. it's the only piece of me worth keeping.
beats.quote: Goes Weird as she must go!"

beats.title: Beer Boasts, Morning Bodies
beats.modern: the old king tells me how it usually goes. his guys get loaded, swear on the ale bench they're staying up to fight it, huge speeches, everybody cheering. then morning comes and the benches are painted and he's counting who's missing. twelve years of the same two scenes.

beats.title: Unferth Opens His Mouth
beats.modern: some guy sitting at the king's feet decides tonight's the night he tries me. opens with: aren't you the one who lost a swimming race as a kid? brother. you have had twelve years to walk out to that swamp yourself and your big move is pulling up my VOD from when I was fifteen.

beats.title: The Swim Story
beats.modern: for the record. we were kids, we both said we'd do it, we both did it. five nights out there in winter with swords drawn against the sharks, north wind in our faces, and neither of us would leave the other. then something dragged me to the bottom and I put a blade through it. that's the run you're using as a dunk.

beats.title: Brother Killer
beats.modern: one more thing, since we're going through history. you killed your own brothers. your own blood. that's the guy giving me notes tonight. and here's the actual number: if your heart matched your mouth, that thing would never have gotten twelve free years in your king's hall.

beats.title: The Queen's Cup
beats.modern: the queen comes down the hall with the cup and puts it in my hands herself, thanking God out loud that somebody finally showed up. so I say it in front of the whole room. tonight I do what your people need, or I don't leave this hall alive. no take-backs. chat is the witness.
beats.quote: Or the last of my life-days live in this mead-hall."

beats.title: Fair Fight Rules
beats.modern: armor off. helmet off. sword handed to my guy, hold it, I won't need it. he doesn't know what weapons are, so we're going raw and God can pick a winner. then I lie down on the bench in a dark room I know something is walking toward.
beats.quote: "I hold me no meaner in matters of prowess, In warlike achievements, than Grendel does himself;

beats.title: He Comes From The Moor
beats.modern: he's moving. off the moor, under the clouds, walking a road he's walked a hundred times to a door he's opened a hundred times. touches it and it comes off the hinges. and chat, his eyes. there's light coming out of them. he counts a room full of sleeping men and he is HAPPY.

beats.title: The Grip
beats.modern: he takes a sleeping man before I can move. eats him. all of him. then he reaches for me and I catch the hand. and I feel the exact second he understands, chat. this thing has been farming people for twelve years and it just found out it's in the wrong room. now it only wants the door.

beats.title: The Whole Hall Screaming
beats.modern: the building is coming apart around us. benches ripped off the floor, gold fittings flying, walls holding only because they were bolted with iron. and outside every Dane in the country is awake listening to a sound they've never heard before: that thing crying. twelve years of screaming, finally coming out of the right throat.

beats.title: The Arm
beats.modern: he pulls for the door and I don't let go. and the shoulder gives. sinews going one at a time, then the whole arm tearing loose. he runs off into the dark to die in his own swamp. I'm standing in a wrecked hall holding an arm.

beats.title: Trophy Under The Roof
beats.modern: I hang it up under the roof beams. arm, shoulder, whole claw. by sunrise there are riders coming in from other kingdoms just to look at the tracks. they follow the drag marks to the lake and the water is red and boiling. he made it home, chat. that's all he made.

beats.title: Adopted On Stream
beats.modern: the king walks in, sees the hand hanging under his own roof, and says it in front of everybody. from today you're my son. I'll love you like my own body. whoever your mother is, God was good to her. chat, I've fought sea monsters. that one got me.
beats.quote: I'll love thee in spirit As bairn of my body;

beats.title: Mom Aggro
beats.modern: chat. CHAT. there's a second one. his mother. she comes into the hall while everyone's sleeping off the party, takes the king's oldest friend, and grabs the arm back off the wall on her way out. one man, then gone. she wasn't there to fight anybody. she was there to collect.

beats.title: The Water Nobody Swims
beats.modern: the old king describes where they live and it's the worst place on the map. a lake under stone cliffs, frost-covered trees leaning over it, fire on the surface at night, and no one alive has ever found the bottom. a deer with hounds on it will stand on that shore and die rather than go in. that's my next stop.

beats.title: Avenge, Don't Mourn
beats.modern: he's falling apart so I say it straight. don't sit here crying over your friend, get up. every one of us has a last day already on the calendar. the only thing you pick is what's on the record before it. she doesn't get to hide in the ground, the woods, or the water. I promise you that.
beats.quote: "Grieve not, O wise one! for each it is better,

beats.title: A Full Day Down
beats.modern: I go in wearing everything and it takes an ENTIRE DAY of sinking before the bottom shows up. she's on me the second I arrive. claws can't get through the mail so she just carries me, while sea beasts bite at my armor the whole way down. then a roof over my head, no water, and firelight.

beats.title: The Sword That Failed
beats.modern: I swing the famous borrowed sword down on her head and it does NOTHING. first time in its whole life that blade has failed anyone. so I throw it away. we wrestle. I put her down, she puts me down harder, and then she's sitting on my chest with a knife out, and the only thing between us is a shirt of iron rings.

beats.title: The Giant's Sword
beats.modern: and then I see it on the wall. a sword from the giant age, too big for any man alive to carry into a fight. except. I get up, I take it down, and I put it through her neck, straight through the bone. she goes down and stays down, and the blade is lit up in my hand like the sun. chat I am SHAKING.

beats.title: Taking The Head
beats.modern: I find him laid out in the back of the cave, already dead from the arm. so I take his head, for the fifteen men he ate and the fifteen he carried off. and the blade melts in my hand like ice in spring, chat, his blood was that hot. all I bring back up is the hilt. up top, the Danes see the water go black, decide I'm dead, and go home. my guys stay sitting there watching the water.

beats.title: Beware Of Arrogance
beats.modern: the old king pulls me aside with the whole hall listening. you're strong now. you won't be. it comes for everyone: sickness, a blade, fire, flood, old age, or your eyes just going dark one morning. and he's saying this to me while thanking God he lived long enough to see that head on his floor.

beats.title: The Old King Cries
beats.modern: when I leave he kisses me, holds onto my neck and cries in front of his entire court. fifty years a king. he keeps telling himself we'll sit and talk again someday. chat, we both know how far Denmark is, and how old he is.

beats.title: Hondscio And The Glove
beats.modern: detail I left out for my own king. the first man taken that night was Hondscio, and it was over before anybody woke up. and the thing was carrying a bag, chat. a pouch stitched out of dragon skin by some old craft nobody uses anymore, sized for people. I was supposed to go in the bag.

beats.title: They Thought I Was A Bum
beats.modern: worth saying out loud. for years my own people wrote me off. thought I was slow, lazy, a bench-warmer, and the hall gave me nothing when the cups went round. one trip fixed the entire record. every slight got paid back with interest, and I got land, a sword, and a title out of it.

beats.title: Fifty Winters, King
beats.modern: time skip, chat. my king dies. his son dies. the crown lands on me and I hold it for fifty years. I'm old now. and then one night, up on a grey cliff over a stone path nobody knew was there, something starts guarding a pile of gold.

beats.title: The Last Survivor
beats.modern: before the dragon there was a man. the last one of his people left alive. he carried all of their gold down into the ground himself and told the earth to hold it, since his men couldn't. nobody left to polish the cups. nobody left to wear the mail. no harp, no horses, no one in the yard. then he lay down on top of it and died.
beats.quote: "Hold thou, O Earth, now heroes no more may,

beats.title: One Cup, Whole Country
beats.modern: three hundred years it sits on that gold. then one guy on the run from his own lord finds the path, panics, and takes a single cup to buy his way back into favor. that's it. one cup. the dragon wakes up, counts, finds a footprint, and decides my entire country pays for it in fire.

beats.title: It Burned My Hall
beats.modern: it goes up at night and burns the country from the air, then slides back under the rock before daylight. and chat, it burned MY hall. the gift-seat. best building in the land, gone. and for the first time in fifty years I'm sitting there wondering what I did wrong that this landed on me.

beats.title: The Empty House
beats.modern: before I go in I think about the worst thing I know. an old man watching his son hang, singing over him, too old to do anything but stand there while the birds wait. and then going home to a house full of wind. no riders, no harp, nobody in the yard. and it starts again every morning when he wakes up.

beats.title: Wait On The Barrow
beats.modern: last thing I tell my men. this one isn't yours. sit on the ridge in your armor and watch which of us walks out. I'd go bare-handed like I did with the other one, but this thing breathes fire, so I'm taking the iron shield. I'm getting that gold, or the gold's getting me.
beats.quote: 'Tis no matter of yours, and man cannot do it,

beats.title: First Exchange
beats.modern: I shout under the stone arch and the ground answers me. steam first, then him. shield up. I swing the old heirloom sword and the edge skids off bone, barely bites, less than I needed. and now it's awake, it's furious, and everything around us is on fire.

beats.title: They Ran
beats.modern: chat. my eleven picked men. the ones I fed, armed, paid, and chose personally for this. they went to the TREES. left me in the fire with a broken sword and an iron shield. one didn't.

beats.title: Wiglaf Walks In
beats.modern: Wiglaf. young, first real fight of his life. he stands in the smoke and reminds the other ten what they swore on the mead-bench when the rings were being handed out, and when nobody moves he goes in alone. says he'd rather burn next to me than carry a clean shield home.
beats.quote: God wot in me, 'tis mickle the liefer The blaze should embrace my body and eat it With my treasure-bestower.

beats.title: Nægling Shatters
beats.modern: I hit it in the head hard enough that my own sword breaks. Nægling. every blade I've ever owned has failed me, chat, my hand is too heavy for iron. and while I'm standing there holding a handle, it comes in a third time and takes my neck in its teeth.

beats.title: Cut The Worm In Half
beats.modern: the kid goes low, under the fire, hand burning off, and puts his blade in where the neck isn't armored. the flames drop. and I get the knife off my belt and open the worm up through the middle. we did it together, him and me. and that's the last thing I will ever do.
beats.quote: The Weder-lord cut the worm in the middle.

beats.title: The Poison
beats.modern: then the bite starts to swell and burn and I know what's in me. I sit down against the wall and look up at stone arches holding the whole earth over our heads. the kid's washing the blood off my face. chat, I'd hand this armor to my son right now. I never got one.
beats.quote: "My son I would give now my battle-equipments,

beats.title: Fifty Years, No Ambushes
beats.modern: here's my whole record and I'm at peace with it. fifty years ruling. no neighbor ever dared come test me. I never went looking for trouble, never swore a crooked oath, never killed my own kin. now go, quick, bring the gold out where I can see it. I want to know what I bought.

beats.title: Build My Barrow
beats.modern: he brings it out, cups and plates and an all-gold banner, and I look at it and thank God I got that for my people before I went. now do this for me. burn me, then stack a mound on the headland where the ships pass, high enough that sailors out on the dark water call it Beowulf's barrow.
beats.quote: Aloft it shall tower on Whale's-Ness uprising, That earls of the ocean hereafter may call it Beowulf's barrow,

beats.title: Last Of The Line
beats.modern: I take the gold ring off my neck and give it to the kid, with the helmet and the mail. you're the last of our family, Wiglaf. fate took every one of my kin ahead of me and I'm going after them now. that's my last sentence, chat. channel's his.
beats.quote: "Thou art latest left of the line of our kindred,

beats.title: Wiglaf Reads Them
beats.modern: the ten come back out of the trees when the fire's out, shields clean, and stand there looking at the body. Wiglaf doesn't even raise his voice. gift-giving is over for your families. no more rings, no more land, and every man in your line loses his rights the day the neighbors hear what you did.
beats.quote: Death is more pleasant To every earlman than infamous life is!"

beats.title: Raven, Eagle, Wolf
beats.modern: and none of that gold gets worn. not one piece. no man wears it, no woman gets a ring for her neck, it all burns with him and the women get exile instead. no harp in the hall now. just cold spears in hands at dawn, and a raven telling an eagle how the eating went while the wolf listens in.

beats.title: The Pyre
beats.modern: they build it on the headland and hang it with helmets, shields and bright mail, exactly the way he asked. then they light it. black smoke going straight up, the fire roaring, everyone underneath it crying, until the bone-house burns through and there's nothing left to burn.

beats.title: The Gold Goes Back
beats.modern: ten days to raise the mound, high and wide so ships can see it from far out. and then they put the whole hoard in with him. all of it. every ring anybody died for goes back into the dirt, exactly as useless to people as it was the whole time it was buried.

beats.title: Twelve Riders
beats.modern: twelve of them ride around the mound, sons of chiefs, saying his name out loud and listing what he did, because that's what you owe a man when he leaves his body. they praise him the way you're supposed to: in measure, out loud, with love. gg. stream's over.

beats.title: Genoa And Lucca
beats.modern: chat I'm at a Petersburg party where the host greets her first guest by threatening to unfriend him unless he agrees Napoleon is the literal Antichrist. he agrees instantly. then they discuss whether Russia goes to war like it's the weather. everyone in this room is speaking French about killing French people. it's 1805 and the server is about to catch fire.
beats.quote: They have decided that Buonaparte has burnt his boats, and I believe that we are ready to burn ours.”

beats.title: The Window Ledge Bet
beats.modern: Dólokhov bets an English officer fifty imperials he can drink a full bottle of rum sitting on a THIRD FLOOR window ledge. legs hanging out. no hands. we ripped the window frame out of the wall so nobody could claim he was holding on. he does it. the whole bottle. the Englishman just quietly gets his wallet out.

beats.title: Bring The Bear
beats.modern: so obviously I announce I'm doing it too. no bet, no reason. they try to restrain me and I send four grown men flying. Anatole talks me down by promising a different party. fine. but the bear's coming. yes there's a bear. I pick up the bear and dance around the room with it. chat this is why I got exiled from Petersburg.
beats.quote: “Come on!... And we’ll take Bruin with us.”

beats.title: The Inheritance Drop
beats.modern: my father died. I never got to call him that out loud. and before the body's cold there's a woman gently explaining that I am now one of the richest men in Russia. every single person who looked past me at that party suddenly knows my name. a title, an empire, and absolutely no idea who I am. terrible patch notes.

beats.title: Why Are They Running At Me
beats.modern: cutting to Nikolai's POV. he charges the French screaming, then actually SEES them, and his brain goes: wait. why are they running at me. to kill ME? whom everyone is so fond of? he throws his pistol AT a guy instead of firing it and runs like a hare. arm shattered. entire hero fantasy deleted in nine seconds.

beats.title: Je Vous Aime
beats.modern: her father locked us in a room and announced the engagement to the whole house before I said one word. so I said the line. I love you. it came out like a dead battery and I felt ashamed of myself for saying it. six weeks later I'm married to the most beautiful woman in Russia and I have never felt more alone inside a building.

beats.title: The Sky Over Austerlitz
beats.modern: Andrei grabs a fallen standard, runs at the guns doing the full hero cinematic, and gets clubbed in the head. and then he's on his back and there's just sky. gray clouds sliding by. quiet. the man who wanted glory more than oxygen finds out the glory was nothing and the sky was everything.
beats.quote: How was it I did not see that lofty sky before? And how happy I am to have found it at last!

beats.title: That's A Fine Death
beats.modern: his hero rides up, looks down at him bleeding out, and says nice death. Andrei hears it like a fly buzzing. the man he built his entire personality around is standing over him and Andrei is thinking about clouds. biggest deratification in recorded history. Napoleon shrunk to the size of a bug by a sky.
beats.quote: “That’s a fine death!”

beats.title: The Duel
beats.modern: I have never fired a pistol in my life. I shoot Dólokhov in the side. he goes down in the snow, sits up, eats a mouthful of it, and aims at me anyway. and I just stand there. broad chest, arms out, free target. he misses. I walk off into the trees muttering folly, folly, death, lies, like an NPC whose script broke.

beats.title: Forty-Three Thousand
beats.modern: Dólokhov isn't playing cards with Nikolai, he's executing him. he picked the number 43 in advance because that's his age plus Sónya's, the girl who turned him down. so Nikolai loses forty-three thousand rubles, an amount that eats his family alive, and Dólokhov just stretches and mentions he's tired of sitting so long.
beats.quote: “You owe forty-three thousand, Count,”

beats.title: Freemason Onboarding
beats.modern: met a strange old man at a coach station who looked at my entire life and told me, calmly, that it was garbage. he was right. I paced my room till dawn like someone who just found religion, because I had. chat I'm joining the Masons. I'm going to fix my soul AND serfdom. give me six months.

beats.title: The Raft Talk
beats.modern: me and Andrei stuck on a ferry raft mid-river arguing about God until the sun goes down. the ferrymen are waiting. the horses are already unhitched on the far bank. we don't move. I tell him there's a whole universe of truth above this dirt, and he says nothing, and then he steps off and looks up and it's the same sky from Austerlitz. I watched a man come back to life.

beats.title: Night At The Window
beats.modern: Andrei's staying at the Rostóvs' and there's a girl at the window above him who cannot sleep because the moon is too good. she wants to hug her knees and fly away. she has zero idea that a broken thirty-one-year-old is lying awake directly underneath her getting completely rewired by it.
beats.quote: “There never, never was such a lovely night before!”

beats.title: The Oak Again
beats.modern: in spring he rode past a dead-looking old oak and thought: same, king. no leaves, no point, life's over at thirty-one. he rides back past it weeks later and it has EXPLODED into green. and he decides no, actually. life is not over. chat a tree fixed this man.

beats.title: Her First Ball
beats.modern: Natásha's first ball and nobody asks her. she's standing by the wall doing the math on whether she's actually invisible, while my wife glides past as the most looked-at woman in the empire. so I grab Andrei by the arm and tell him to dance with her. he does. second couple onto the floor. chat, I did that. remember I did that.

beats.title: A Whole Year
beats.modern: he proposes. she says yes before he finishes the sentence. then the fine print: his father won't allow a wedding for a year. she just keeps repeating why a year, why a year, and he can't answer, because the real answer is my dad hates this. chat that year is the crack everything else gets in through.

beats.title: The Wolf In The Gully
beats.modern: Nikolai's POV and this is the happiest moment of his life: the wolf comes out of the copse, the dogs pile in, and old Karáy has her by the throat in a gully. hand on the saddlebow, dagger ready, it's done. and she rips loose and walks off. he screams at the sky. old dog crawls out bleeding. that's hunting.

beats.title: The Russian Dance
beats.modern: Natásha was raised by a French governess and has never been taught one step of this. Uncle strikes a chord, she throws off her shawl, sets her arms, and does it PERFECTLY. everyone in the room was braced for her to embarrass herself for about half a second. where did she get it? nobody knows. it was in the air she breathed.

beats.title: Three Sleighs At Night
beats.modern: mummers, costumes, three troykas racing flat out across a moonlit field with everyone screaming and snow in their teeth. Nikolai looks around and doesn't recognize the countryside anymore. it's somewhere new and enchanted. chat hold onto this clip. bookmark it. it doesn't come back.

beats.title: Anatole Sits Down
beats.modern: a handsome man sits down beside Natásha at the opera and within five minutes there is no wall left between them. she keeps checking her father's face, my wife's face, anyone's face, for someone to tell her this is wrong. nobody does. my WIFE arranged the introduction. that's Hélène. that's who I married.

beats.title: The Elopement Gets Busted
beats.modern: sleigh's idling, maid's at the gate, Anatole walks up the porch steps to steal her, and the door opens on a gigantic footman with orders to bring him inside. Dólokhov is screaming BETRAYED from the street and physically drags him back out through the wicket. Sónya told. Sónya saved her life and lost her the friendship.

beats.title: I Shook Him By The Collar
beats.modern: found him in my own house. asked him straight: you promised to marry her and tried to elope with her. he says he doesn't answer questions in that tone. so I picked him up by the collar and shook him until his face agreed to cooperate. I had a heavy paperweight in my hand. I put it back down. that was close, chat.

beats.title: The Arsenic
beats.modern: she found out he was already married. already MARRIED. and that night she took poison, then got frightened and woke Sónya and told her what she'd done. they got the antidotes in on time. she's alive. too weak to move. I'm standing in that house understanding that every man in it, me included, failed this girl.

beats.title: If I Were The Best Of Men
beats.modern: she tells me everything is over for her. and I hear myself say: if I were the handsomest, cleverest, best man in the world, and free, I would be on my knees right now asking for your hand. she cried. I ran out of the house so she wouldn't see that I was crying too. chat I am extremely married.
beats.quote: “If I were not myself, but the handsomest, cleverest, and best man in the world, and were free, I would this moment ask on my knees for your hand and your love!”

beats.title: The Comet
beats.modern: drove out into Arbát Square and the entire sky is one enormous comet, the one everyone swears means plague, war, end of the world. and I'm standing in the street crying with joy at it. everyone else sees doom. I'm looking at the exact shape of whatever just happened in my chest.

beats.title: Uhlans In The River
beats.modern: Napoleon points at a river. the Polish colonel BEGS for permission to swim it instead of using the ford a third of a mile away, purely so the Emperor can watch. forty of his men drown. Napoleon never looks up. he's mildly annoyed they're distracting him from his map. then he calls for his horse and rides home. that's the man.
beats.quote: were proud that they were swimming and drowning in this river under the eyes of the man who sat on the log and was not even looking at what they were doing.

beats.title: I Am 666
beats.modern: okay so I converted the letters of Napoleon's name into numbers and got 666. beast confirmed. then I did mine and it didn't work, so I changed the spelling. still no. so I added my nationality. 671. five too many. so I deleted a letter that should not be deleted and got EXACTLY 666. chat I am the designated counterplay. this is airtight. no further questions.

beats.title: Put On Your White Dress
beats.modern: the old prince spent Marya's whole life being cruel to her, and last week she caught herself wishing he would die. now he's had the stroke and he's crying and saying thank you, daughter dear, forgive, thank you, forgive. and the last thing he ever gets out is: put on your white dress, I like it. then the second stroke.
beats.quote: “Put on your white dress. I like it,”

beats.title: Bind Him
beats.modern: the Boguchárovo peasants won't let Marya leave and the French are hours out. Nikolai rides in alone, knocks a man's cap off, screams bind him, and the entire mutiny folds in about ninety seconds. they end up tying each OTHER up and handing over their own belts. he walks her out. chat, hold that thought.

beats.title: War Is Not Courtesy
beats.modern: night before Borodinó, Andrei's shed, and he is DONE with the theater of it. take no prisoners. stop pretending war has manners. they burn your house, kill your father, then lecture you about chivalry and flags of truce. he says the aim of war is murder, out loud, and every man in that room knows he's right and none of them says so.
beats.quote: War is not courtesy but the most horrible thing in life; and we ought to understand that and not play at war.

beats.title: The White Hat On The Knoll
beats.modern: I attended the largest battle in the world as a TOURIST. white hat, green tailcoat, no weapon. climbed a little mound with ten guns on it, sat down on the edge of the trench, and smiled at everybody. turns out that mound is the single most fought-over spot on the field. the gunners looked at me the way you look at weather.

beats.title: Can This Be Death
beats.modern: Andrei's regiment stands under artillery for hours doing nothing, which is the worst thing you can ask of men. a shell lands and spins in the grass like a top in front of him. the adjutant hits the dirt. Andrei stays standing because people are WATCHING, because lying down would be shameful. then it goes off.
beats.quote: “I cannot, I do not wish to die. I love life—I love this grass, this earth, this air....”

beats.title: The Amputation Tent
beats.modern: in the field hospital the man on the next table is sobbing like a child while they show him his own severed leg with the boot still on it. Andrei looks over. it's Anatole. the man who tried to steal Natásha. and instead of hatred he gets hit by this enormous ruinous pity and starts crying for him. he finally understands the thing his sister kept telling him about love. and he knows he found it about four hours too late.
beats.quote: But now it is too late. I know it!”

beats.title: The Broken Crockery
beats.modern: war council in a peasant hut, and a six-year-old girl watching from on top of the stove is the only one who understands it: it's Granddad versus Long-coat. and Granddad wins. Kutúzov sighs, stands up, and orders the retreat. Moscow goes. he says out loud that he'll be the one who pays for the broken crockery. then the generals file out like people leaving a funeral.
beats.quote: “Well, gentlemen, I see that it is I who will have to pay for the broken crockery,”

beats.title: The Carts Argument
beats.modern: an officer asked the old count for a few carts for the wounded. the countess does the math out loud: that's a hundred thousand rubles of the children's property, it's the government's job, the neighbors already cleared out two days ago. and he has no counterargument. he flaps his arms and leaves the room. that's the fight. men bleeding in your own yard versus the china.

beats.title: Forgive Me
beats.modern: they took the wounded out of Moscow on those carts and one of them was Andrei. she didn't know. she finds him in a hut at Mytíshchi, goes down on her knees, and just says forgive me, forgive me. and he says I love you. more, better than before. chat they got a year of silence and about three weeks of this.
beats.quote: “I love you more, better than before,”

beats.title: The Kid In The Fire
beats.modern: Moscow is burning and a French soldier points at a courtyard and says there's your child. three-year-old in a pink dress under a bench. I grab her and she screams and bites my hands the entire way because she has no idea I'm the rescue. carried her through the garden anyway looking for a way out.

beats.title: I Am Your Prisoner
beats.modern: stopped by a patrol with a dagger under my coat and a plan to assassinate Napoleon. officer asks who I am. I say I'm not telling you, I'm your prisoner, take me. the peasant woman is shouting about the little girl and I announce she's bringing me my daughter that I saved from the flames, which is a lie I don't remember deciding to tell. then I march off between the soldiers, thrilled.

beats.title: Hélène Is Gone
beats.modern: my wife is dead. officially: a terrible attack of angina. privately, in the good drawing rooms: a very large dose of something she had been taking in small doses. she wrote to me. I never answered. I did not love her, chat. I did not want this.

beats.title: The Executions
beats.modern: they lined us up and shot them in pairs. I was in the sixth pair and they never fired. I watched a factory boy get cut down off the post and pushed into the pit with his shoulder still rising and falling while they threw earth on him. and the men doing it KNEW. one said it'll teach them to start fires and couldn't finish the sentence.

beats.title: Andrei Goes
beats.modern: Marya and Natásha sit with him at the end and neither of them cries, because he already left and this is just the body. he kisses his son and blesses him because that's what's required, then looks around to see if there's anything else he's supposed to do. and then it's over, and Natásha closes his eyes and asks where he went. nobody in that room has the answer.

beats.title: My Immortal Soul
beats.modern: sat down by a cart wheel in the middle of a prison camp and started laughing so hard men came over to see what was wrong with me. THEY shut me up? they hold ME captive? me? my immortal soul? ha-ha-ha. barefoot, lousy, no name, no shoes, and I have never been this free in my entire life.
beats.quote: They took me and shut me up. They hold me captive. What, me? Me? My immortal soul? Ha-ha-ha! Ha-ha-ha!...”

beats.title: Pétya
beats.modern: the kid begged his way onto the raid. sixteen. Denísov gives the signal and Pétya just GOES, straight past everyone, into the courtyard, screaming hurrah. and then his arms are waving wrong and he's sliding off the saddle. bullet through the skull. Dólokhov says done for, twice, like it's nothing. Denísov makes a sound like a dog and grabs hold of the fence.
beats.quote: “I am used to something sweet. Raisins, fine ones... take them all!”

beats.title: The Dog Howled
beats.modern: Platón couldn't keep up anymore. I saw him sitting under a birch and I did not go over. two soldiers ran past me, one carrying a lowered and smoking gun. behind me the little blue-gray dog started howling and I thought, what a stupid beast, why is it howling. I knew. I made myself not know. every man walking beside me did the same thing.

beats.title: The Globe
beats.modern: dreamed my old geography teacher showed me a globe made of moving drops of water, every drop shoving to take up space, merging, vanishing, coming back. God's in the middle and each drop is just trying to reflect him. and the old man says: there now, Karatáev has spread out and disappeared. that's when I let myself know.
beats.quote: There now, Karatáev has spread out and disappeared.

beats.title: It Was Natásha
beats.modern: there's a thin woman in black sitting in Marya's room and I do not recognize her at all. then Marya says her name, and the face opens like a door grown rusty on its hinges, and she SMILES. chat it was Natásha. and I loved her. I found that out at the exact same second everyone else in the room did.
beats.quote: When she smiled doubt was no longer possible, it was Natásha and he loved her.

beats.title: Write To Her Parents
beats.modern: Marya tells me she thinks Natásha will love me and I'm instantly on my feet holding her hands going you think I may hope? you think? she says write to her parents, go to Petersburg, leave the rest to me. and I keep saying it can't be, how happy I am, no it can't be. thirty years of being wrong about my own life and it lands here.

beats.title: The Green Stain
beats.modern: epilogue: Natásha doesn't sing anymore, doesn't do society, is jealous of literally every woman alive including the governess, and will come striding out of the nursery in a dressing gown with her hair everywhere to show you that the stain on the baby's napkin turned yellow instead of green, GLOWING about it. everyone says I'm under my wife's thumb. correct. no notes.

beats.title: The Kid Picks It Up
beats.modern: Andrei's boy is fifteen now and wakes up cold and shaking from a dream where he and I were leading an army made of cobwebs toward glory. then I'm gone and his father is standing there instead, with no shape at all, loving him. so he lies back down and decides he is going to do something someday that even his father would have been satisfied with. that's the stream, chat. the kid picks up the thread.
beats.quote: Everyone shall know me, love me, and be delighted with me!”

beats.title: The Graveyard Guy
beats.modern: chat I'm at my parents' grave, which is where I hang out, because they're dead and so are all five of my brothers. and a man comes UP out of the ground with a chain on his leg and grabs me by the chin. turns me upside down, shakes me out like a piggy bank. one piece of bread falls out. he eats it in front of me.
beats.quote: “Keep still, you little devil, or I’ll cut your throat!”

beats.title: File And Wittles
beats.modern: the ask: a file and food by sunrise or he takes my heart and liver out. also there's a second guy hiding with him, way worse than him, who can creep into your bed while you're tucked up warm and open you right up. locking your door does nothing. I am seven years old. obviously I said yes.
beats.quote: “Or I’ll have your heart and liver out.”

beats.title: The Pantry Job
beats.modern: robbed my own house before dawn, chat. bread, cheese rind, half a jar of mincemeat, brandy (topped the bottle back up with water, sorry), a meat bone, and a whole pork pie that was extremely for guests. every floorboard in the place screaming STOP THIEF at me. grabbed a file out of Joe's forge on the way out and ran into the fog.

beats.title: He Ate The Pie
beats.modern: they drag him back in irons and he looks straight past me at Joe and says he stole the food himself. eats the entire charge so nobody suspects me. and Joe, my brother in law, actual saint, says he's welcome to it, we wouldn't have him starve for a pie. I said nothing. I just stood there letting a convict cover for me.
beats.quote: me,—“so you’re the blacksmith, are you? Than I’m sorry to say, I’ve eat your pie.”

beats.title: Twenty Minutes To Nine
beats.modern: so this rich woman lives in the dark in her wedding dress. one shoe on, veil half done, jewels half out of the box. every clock in the house frozen at twenty minutes to nine. she takes my hand, puts it on her chest and says BROKEN with a proud little smile like it's her whole brand. then she told me to play. play WHAT
beats.quote: “You are not afraid of a woman who has never seen the sun since you were born?”

beats.title: Coarse Hands, Thick Boots
beats.modern: the girl reads my hands and my boots out loud like a diagnosis. coarse hands. thick boots. also I said jacks instead of knaves so my entire class background got exposed in one card game. and chat, her contempt was so strong I caught it off her. I looked down at my own hands and agreed with her.
beats.quote: “And what coarse hands he has! And what thick boots!”

beats.title: Bread And Meat In The Yard
beats.modern: she brought me food and set the mug down on the stones without looking at me, like I'm a dog in disgrace. then she saw my eyes go wet and looked absolutely THRILLED about it. so I got behind a gate in the brewery lane and cried into my own sleeve and kicked the wall. same hands, same boots, brand new problem.

beats.title: Come And Fight
beats.modern: some pale kid at the window goes halloa, then who let you in, then "come and fight" like it's on the calendar. brings a sponge and a water bottle for BOTH of us. does a whole footwork routine. laws of the game, regular rules. then I drop him. and again. and again. he keeps getting up like a boss with three health bars until he throws the sponge and announces that I won. brother I never wanted this.
beats.quote: “Come and fight,” said the pale young gentleman.

beats.title: The Kiss Worth Nothing
beats.modern: she's waiting at the gate with a glow on her face like something wonderful just happened, which I think was me getting punched repeatedly. then: you may kiss me, if you like. I'd have crawled over glass for that. and she handed it over like loose change to a beggar. worth nothing, and we both knew it.
beats.quote: “Come here! You may kiss me, if you like.”

beats.title: Ashamed Of Home
beats.modern: the ugly part out loud: one year around money and my own kitchen looks cheap to me. the forge, the parlour, the front door, all downgraded in my head. Joe hasn't changed one bit. I have. and I would die before I let those two see where I sleep.

beats.title: The Leg-Iron
beats.modern: someone came up behind my sister in her own kitchen and put her down with something heavy. she never even turned round. and the thing lying on the floor beside her was a convict's leg iron, filed apart. chat. I know that iron. I'm the one who brought the file that opened it.

beats.title: Telling Biddy
beats.modern: Biddy asks what I actually want and I say it out loud: there's a beautiful girl and I want to be a gentleman on her account. and Biddy, completely calm, asks whether it's to spite her or to win her, because to spite her I should just stop caring, and to win her, well, she wasn't worth winning. she's right. I knew she was right. I did it anyway.
beats.quote: I want to be a gentleman on her account.”

beats.title: Great Expectations
beats.modern: a lawyer walks into the pub and informs me I have great expectations. anonymous benefactor. removed from my present sphere of life. brought up as a gentleman. terms: I keep the name Pip and I never ask who. chat I did not need to ask. rich lady, dead wedding, gorgeous girl she keeps around like a pet. it's obviously her. obviously.
beats.quote: the communication I have got to make is, that he has great expectations.”

beats.title: The Finger-Post
beats.modern: walked out of the village whistling like it cost me nothing. got as far as the finger post at the end of the road and broke completely. said goodbye out loud to a wooden sign. then on the coach I kept planning to get off and walk back and do the goodbye properly, and I kept not doing it, until it was too far to go back. mists up. world open. end of part one.
beats.quote: “Good-bye, O my dear, dear friend!”

beats.title: The Prowling Boy
beats.modern: CHAT. my new roommate opens the door in London and it's the pale kid from the garden. the one I beat up. we just stood there laughing at each other. and then he apologises to ME for knocking me about so much. brother you spent that entire fight on your back.
beats.quote: “The idea of its being you!”

beats.title: The Day Came, Not The Groom
beats.modern: Herbert drops the lore. dress bought, tour planned, guests invited. the day arrives and the groom does not. he sent a LETTER, and it landed while she was dressing at twenty minutes to nine, which is why every clock in that house says twenty minutes to nine. she never let daylight in again. oh and he was running it with her own half brother. they split the money.
beats.quote: The day came, but not the bridegroom. He wrote her a letter—”

beats.title: A Capitalist
beats.modern: asked Herbert what he does. "a capitalist. insurer of ships." amazing. then it's life assurance shares, a little mining, chartering a few thousand tons, trading to the East Indies for silks and spices, tusks from Ceylon. profits? TREMENDOUS. so which ships are you insuring at the moment. "I haven't begun insuring yet. I am looking about me." he's an unpaid intern.
beats.quote: “I haven’t begun insuring yet,” he replied. “I am looking about me.”

beats.title: The Castle
beats.modern: Wemmick lives in a tiny cottage he has converted into a castle. moat. actual drawbridge. real cannon that he fires at nine every night for his deaf dad, who I communicate with exclusively by nodding, that's it, that's the whole protocol, you just nod harder. his boss has never heard of any of this. office Wemmick and home Wemmick are two different men and he asked me to respect that.
beats.quote: When I go into the office, I leave the Castle behind me, and when I come into the Castle, I leave the office behind me.

beats.title: Let Them See Your Wrists
beats.modern: dinner at my guardian's and he ends an arm wrestling argument by clamping his housekeeper's hand to the table like a trap and making her show us both wrists. she says master, please. he says show them. one wrist is scarred to ribbons. he traces the muscle with his finger, tells the table she has been admired, and dismisses her. nobody said a word. me included.
beats.quote: Molly, let them see your wrist.”

beats.title: Ever So Many Partings
beats.modern: Joe came to London and I was embarrassed of him the entire visit and he felt every second of it. so he leaves. and the sir drops out of his voice and he says life is made of ever so many partings welded together, and that he is wrong out of the forge, and I will never see him in these clothes again. then GOD bless you dear old Pip. he was gone before I got down the stairs.
beats.quote: life is made of ever so many partings welded together, as I may say,

beats.title: I Have No Heart
beats.modern: walked her round the old brewery and pointed out exactly where she made me cry, and she said, and I quote, I don't remember. then explained very calmly, like reading out a spec sheet, that she has no heart. no softness. no sympathy, no sentiment, no nonsense. I told her I didn't believe her. I believed her.
beats.quote: “that I have no heart,—if that has anything to do with my memory.”

beats.title: Don’t Know Yah
beats.modern: the tailor's boy from my hometown clocked the new clothes and ended me in public. faked fainting from my sheer dignity. staggered round me on his knees begging mercy. then came back wearing his bag like my coat, strutting with an entourage, going don't know yah, don't know yah, 'pon my soul don't know yah. then followed me over the bridge crowing like a chicken. flawless. no notes.
beats.quote: “Don’t know yah, don’t know yah, ’pon my soul don’t know yah!”

beats.title: Memorandum Of Pip’s Debts
beats.modern: the budgeting system: buy nice stationery, write MEMORANDUM OF PIP'S DEBTS across the top of a clean sheet, list what we owe, tie the bills into a neat bundle. that's the whole system. writing them down feels so much like paying them that I genuinely lose track of the difference. Herbert says his are mounting up. I told him to stare them out of countenance. they're staring back.
beats.quote: “They are mounting up, Handel,”

beats.title: The Black Seal
beats.modern: letter comes through the door with a black seal and I know before I open it. my sister died Monday at twenty past six. and now she is everywhere. I keep thinking she's coming at me down the street, or about to knock. she was never once in these rooms. she's in them now.

beats.title: The Secret Sponsor
beats.modern: I bought my best friend a career and he has no idea. paid half my money into a partnership through a clerk and a middleman so it could never trace back to me. he came home glowing about how some merchant had taken a shine to him. I nearly cracked in front of him. cried in bed that night because for once my money did something that wasn't about me.

beats.title: I Am What You Have Made Me
beats.modern: she raised the girl as a weapon to break men, and now the weapon is cold to HER and she cannot cope. calls her a stock and a stone, a cold cold heart. and the girl never once raises her voice. just: I am what you have made me. take the praise, take the blame, take the success, take the failure, take me. built the thing herself and got shocked when it wouldn't hug her.
beats.quote: “I am what you have made me. Take all the praise, take all the blame; take all the success, take all the failure; in short, take me.”

beats.title: Moths And Candles
beats.modern: asked her why she lets the worst man in England orbit her all evening. she says moths hover around a lighted candle, can the candle help it. I said can the Estella not help it. she laughed and said sure. yes. anything you like. that's the answer. every single time.
beats.quote: “hover about a lighted candle. Can the candle help it?”

beats.title: Second Father
beats.modern: he's on one knee holding my hands, kissing them, calling me his son. says he is my second father. says he pictured my face in a shepherd's hut until he forgot what other faces looked like. this man loves me more than anyone alive ever has and every part of me is recoiling like he's a snake. that's the beat, chat. I'm the villain of this stream.
beats.quote: I’m your second father. You’re my son,—more to me nor any son.

beats.title: Sharpest And Deepest
beats.modern: let's total it up. the rich lady was never my sponsor. the girl was never for me, I was a practice dummy she wound up to torment her relatives with. and none of that is the worst part. the worst part is that I threw away Joe, the one person who was purely good to me, for THIS. and there's no undo button on it.

beats.title: In Jail And Out Of Jail
beats.modern: he gives me his entire life in one line: in jail and out of jail, in jail and out of jail, in jail and out of jail. no idea where he was born. first memory is stealing turnips to eat. got labelled a hardened case at the age other kids get called cute. he says he regularly grew up took up.
beats.quote: In jail and out of jail, in jail and out of jail, in jail and out of jail.

beats.title: Two Men In The Dock
beats.modern: him and his partner get tried together and it isn't a trial, it's a fashion show. the partner has curly hair, a white handkerchief and schoolfriends in the gallery. my guy has a record and no coat, because he sold his clothes to afford the lawyer. defence goes: look at these two side by side, which one do you think did it. partner gets seven years. he gets fourteen. same crime.
beats.quote: ain’t it him as gets seven year, and me fourteen,

beats.title: The Rejection
beats.modern: told her I love her, have loved her since I first walked into that house, know I'll never have her, still love her. she KNITTED through the entire speech. then explained that when I say love she understands the words but nothing arrives. you address nothing in my breast, you touch nothing there. and then the kill shot: I did warn you though. didn't I.
beats.quote: You address nothing in my breast, you touch nothing there.

beats.title: Married To Him
beats.modern: then she says it. she's marrying the brute. the dull one, the money one. I ask why she'd fling herself away and she says on whom should she fling herself away, someone who might actually feel that she brought them nothing? and no, it wasn't the old woman's idea. she's just tired of the life she's been living. there. it's done. say no more.
beats.quote: “Why not tell you the truth? I am going to be married to him.”

beats.title: Part Of My Existence
beats.modern: you'll get me out of your thoughts in a week, she says. chat. she's in every line I have read since I was a kid. she's on the river, on the sails, in the marshes, in the clouds, in the dark and in the streets. she's part of the good in me and part of the bad and that is not changing. God bless you. God forgive you. that's the last thing I ever said to her.
beats.quote: Estella, to the last hour of my life, you cannot choose but remain part of my character,

beats.title: Don’t Go Home
beats.modern: night porter stops me at the gate at midnight with a note. PLEASE READ THIS, HERE written on the outside. I open it under his lantern. three words inside, in Wemmick's handwriting. DON'T GO HOME. that's the entire message. and chat, I have a wanted man asleep in my rooms.
beats.quote: “DON’T GO HOME.”

beats.title: Her Mother’s Hands
beats.modern: at dinner the housekeeper's fingers move and it's a knitting motion and my whole skull lights up. those hands. those eyes. that hair. take the face I love, add twenty years of a violent husband, and you get the woman pouring my wine. she is Estella's mother. nobody in that room knows but me.

beats.title: What Have I Done
beats.modern: she asks me to write I FORGIVE HER under her name someday, long after her broken heart is dust. I told her I could do it right now. and the woman in the dead wedding dress went down on her knees on the floor in front of me and just said what have I done, what have I done, over and over, fifty times, until it stopped being words.
beats.quote: If you can ever write under my name, “I forgive her,” though ever so long after my broken heart is dust pray do it!”

beats.title: The Fire
beats.modern: went back up to check on her one last time. she's in her chair with her back to me and then the room goes bright. she comes at me screaming with fire standing feet above her head. got her down under my coat and the table cloth and everything else in that rotten room, and we fought each other on the floor like enemies. the tinder floating in the smoke was her wedding dress. didn't notice both my hands were burnt until someone told me.

beats.title: Estella’s Father
beats.modern: Herbert retells the story he got out of him. a jealous woman tried for murder, a little girl destroyed, twenty odd years ago. and the arithmetic lands on me all at once. I made him look at me. I made him touch me. I asked him if I sounded feverish. then I said it out loud. the man we have hidden down the river is Estella's father.
beats.quote: And the man we have in hiding down the river, is Estella’s Father.”

beats.title: The Limekiln
beats.modern: Orlick has me tied to a ladder in a shack on the marsh with a limekiln outside to erase whatever's left of me. he's drinking himself up to it and I can see every mouthful is a mouthful of my life. and then he tells me who put my sister down. it was him. except in his head it was ME, because I was favoured and he was beaten. you done it, now you pays for it.
beats.quote: It was you as did for your shrew sister.”

beats.title: The Four-Oared Galley
beats.modern: we almost made it. rowing him out to the steamer when a four oared galley slides alongside and calls his real name. he lunges and rips the cloak off the man sitting in it and it's the partner. the one who sold him out twice. big cry, big splash, boat goes out from under me. they pull him out of the tide swimming badly and clap irons on his wrists and ankles. the other one never came up.

beats.title: Thirty-Two And The Judge
beats.modern: thirty two of them sentenced to death in one go. sun coming through the courtroom windows in one big shaft, lighting up the judge and all thirty two together like they're on the same road, which they are. he stands up in it, one speck of a face in the light, and says he has already had his death sentence from the Almighty, but he bows to this one. then sits down. they had to help him walk out. he held my hand the whole time.
beats.quote: “My Lord, I have received my sentence of Death from the Almighty, but I bow to yours,”

beats.title: She Is Living Now
beats.modern: day ten in the prison infirmary and his eyes lit up when I came through the door. they let me stay past time. so I told him. you had a child once you loved and lost. she lived. she found powerful friends. she's a lady, she's beautiful, and I love her. he got my hand up to his lips with the last strength in him. then his head went down and that was it.
beats.quote: “She lived, and found powerful friends. She is living now. She is a lady and very beautiful. And I love her!”

beats.title: The Receipt
beats.modern: came out of months of fever with Joe nursing me the whole way, calling me old chap again like nothing ever happened. and the moment I could stand on my own, he was gone. left a note. not wishful to intrude I have departured fur you are well again dear Pip and will do better without. P.S. ever the best of friends. folded inside it, the receipt. he paid my debts. all of them.
beats.quote: Ever the best of friends.”

beats.title: It’s My Wedding Day
beats.modern: walked back to the forge to ask Biddy to marry me. curtains up, flowers in the window, and the two of them come out arm in arm. it's her wedding day. she married Joe. I put my head down on the old kitchen table and thanked God the question never made it out of my mouth. then I asked them both to say out loud that they forgive me. they did. instantly.
beats.quote: “It’s my wedding-day!”

beats.title: No Shadow Of Another Parting
beats.modern: eleven years later I go back to the ruined house and she's standing there in the mist. everything else has gone from her. she kept this one piece of ground and nothing else. she says suffering taught her what my heart used to be, that she has been bent and broken but into a better shape, and asks if we're friends. I took her hand. we walked out of the ruins together and I saw no shadow of another parting. gg.
beats.quote: I have been bent and broken, but—I hope—into a better shape.

king-arthur-and-the-knights.title: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
king-arthur-and-the-knights.author: Malory, Thomas, Sir

beats.title: The Dragons Under The Tower
beats.modern: channel lore from before I exist, chat. a usurper keeps building a tower and it keeps falling down overnight. his wizards say the fix is obviously human sacrifice. so they drag in a kid with no father, and the kid says: drain the pool. two dragons down there. red one, white one. tearing the foundations apart every single night. red one loses. we are the red one.

beats.title: The Stone In The Churchyard
beats.modern: a stone appears outside the church with a sword in it and gold letters on the blade. every lord in the country queues up. every single one yanks like he's starting a lawnmower. nobody shifts it a hair. so they post ten guards and open it to the entire realm. months of this. nothing. the sword is just sitting there insulting everybody.
beats.quote: "Whoso pulleth out the sword from this stone is born the rightful King of England."

beats.title: Errand Boy Pulls The Sword
beats.modern: my brother forgets his sword. I ride home for it, house locked, everyone's at the tournament. and I think: hang on, there's a free sword in that churchyard. no guards either, they all went to watch the jousting. so I pull the crown of England out of a rock because my brother needed a loaner. chat I did not read the writing.

beats.title: My Father Kneels To Me
beats.modern: then my father kneels. then my brother kneels. and Ector tells me we were never blood. one afternoon: I gain a kingdom and lose a family. and he doesn't ask me for land or gold. he asks me to still be kind to him when I'm king. I would have given him anything he named.
beats.quote: "I have in one day lost my father and my mother and my brother."

beats.title: The Arm In The Lake
beats.modern: chat there is an ARM coming out of the lake holding a sword. just an arm. Merlin is completely normal about this. a lady floats over and says the sword's hers, I can have it, I just owe her one favor whenever she asks. no details. no terms. and I said yes. I said yes immediately. remember that I said yes.
beats.quote: "that sword is mine, and if thou wilt give me in return a gift whenever I shall ask it of thee,

beats.title: Merlin Calls The Kill
beats.modern: we're ankle deep in bodies and Merlin rides into the middle of the battle to tell me to stop. sixty thousand men this morning. fifteen thousand now. he says they've got nothing left but their honor, so what exactly am I taking. so I call it. and I hand every scrap of the plunder to the two kings who came to help me and keep nothing.
beats.quote: now they are sore beaten, and have nothing left them but their honor; and why shouldest thou slay them to take that?"

beats.title: The Questing Beast Guy
beats.modern: a thing comes down to drink: snake head, leopard body, lion tail, deer feet, and thirty hounds barking INSIDE ITS STOMACH. then some knight jogs up, says he's been chasing it a full year, and takes my horse. takes it. tells me it's not my quest and rides off on my mount. that's Pellinore. we come back to him and it does not get better.
beats.quote: "thy desire is utterly in vain, for it shall never be achieved but by me, or by my next of kin."

beats.title: Badon Hill Killstreak
beats.modern: they took the peace deal, sailed off, then turned the ships around a few hours later and started burning the coast. so we take the hill. two days of it, uphill the whole way. and the number they put on me alone that day is four hundred and seventy. chat I did not count that. somebody else counted that.
beats.quote: "red as the rising sun from spur to plume,"

beats.title: The Giant On The Mount
beats.modern: I climb the mountain alone because a giant took my cousin's wife. get to the top, he's at dinner, and chat I am not describing what's on that fire. he wears a coat stitched from the beards of fifteen kings he killed. we go down the whole mountain wrestling, rock to rock, all the way to the sea, and he dies with his arms locked around me.

beats.title: The Beard Mantle Demand
beats.modern: messenger walks in. his king has beaten eleven kings and made every one of them shave. he has TRIMMED A CLOAK with the beards. he needs one more to finish the set. and he's asking for mine. chat there is a man out there doing arts and crafts with royal facial hair and I have made the shortlist.
beats.quote: My beard is yet too young to trim that mantle of thy master's with;

beats.title: Only The Clean Can Draw It
beats.modern: girl walks in wearing a sword she can't take off. only a knight with a completely clean record can draw it. I go first, in public, so nobody feels singled out, and I fail, and I know exactly why I failed. then every baron fails. then a broke guy in bad clothes at the back asks for a turn and it slides straight out. she begs for it back, warns him it will kill his best friend. he keeps it.
beats.quote: "worthiness and brave deeds are not shown by fair raiment but manhood and truth lie hid within the heart.

beats.title: Beheaded At My Own Table
beats.modern: and then the lake lady walks into my hall to collect that favor. she wants a head. I tell her no, I don't do that, ask for anything else. and before I can fix it, Balin walks past, clocks her as the witch who had his mother burned, and takes her head off in front of my entire court. under my protection. at my table. I banish him and I hate every word of it.
beats.quote: Thou desirest my head, therefore shalt thou lose thine";

beats.title: The Prophecy On The Road
beats.modern: Merlin catches Balin on the road purely to read him his future. you will strike the worst blow struck since the one struck at Christ. you will wound the best living knight and he will not heal for years. three kingdoms go to famine. and Balin says: if I believed you I'd kill myself right now just to make you a liar. then Merlin vanishes. no follow-up. no help.
beats.quote: thou shalt strike the most Dolorous Stroke that ever man struck, save he that smote our Lord.

beats.title: The Dolorous Stroke
beats.modern: Balin's weaponless, sprinting room to room, and he grabs the only weapon in sight: a spear standing beside a golden bed. he swings. and chat the CASTLE COMES DOWN. walls, towers, all of it, three days he's pinned in the rubble. that bed had Joseph of Arimathea in it. that spear was THE spear. and the cup goes out of the world. one panicked swing and my kingdom loses its heart.
beats.quote: in this castle and that chamber which thou didst defile, was the blood of our Lord Christ!

beats.title: Balin And Balan
