beats.modern: so I said it out loud, in a pub, to men who hate me. force and hatred and history, that's not life for men and women. everybody knows the very opposite of that is what life is. what's that, says Alf. love, I said. and then I left. behind me they're already doing impressions of me.
beats.quote: —Love, says Bloom. I mean the opposite of hatred.

beats.title: Christ Was A Jew Like Me
beats.modern: he's shouting slurs at me from the pub door so I turned around and gave him the list. Mendelssohn. Marx. Spinoza. your saviour was a jew, his father was a jew, your GOD was a jew. Christ was a jew like me. chat he went back inside to get the biscuit tin.
beats.quote: Your God was a jew. Christ was a jew like me.

beats.title: Ascension By Biscuit Tin
beats.modern: he threw a biscuit tin at my head in broad daylight and missed. the car pulled off, the dog came after us. and chat, the way this town will be telling it tonight? a great brightness came down and Elijah ben Bloom ascended into glory at an angle of fortyfive degrees over Little Green street like a shot off a shovel.
beats.quote: ben Bloom Elijah, amid clouds of angels ascend to the glory of the brightness

beats.title: The Roman Candle
beats.modern: girl on the rocks leans back to watch the fireworks. keeps leaning. she knows I'm looking. she lets me. and the roman candle goes up and up and everyone shouts O! and it bursts and comes down in green dewy stars, soft, gold, falling. then it all melted away in the grey air and everything went silent. chat.

beats.title: Tight Boots? No.
beats.modern: she gets up to leave and she's walking slow, very careful, down the strand. tight boots? no. chat she's lame. she was sitting the whole time and I never knew. and now I'm doing the maths on myself, and the maths says: worst man on this beach.
beats.quote: Tight boots? No. She’s lame! O!

beats.title: A Bouncing Boy
beats.modern: maternity hospital update: three days in labour and she's had the boy. everyone's fine. meanwhile the medical students downstairs are hammered, roaring about birth and God and contraception, and the young poet in the corner is buying every round with money he doesn't have. chat I came to ask after the mother. I stayed because someone has to watch him.
beats.quote: she had borne with a laudable fortitude and she had given birth to a bouncing boy.

beats.title: Mabbot Street Entrance
beats.modern: one in the morning and I'm following the drunk poet into nighttown. skeleton tram tracks. red and green lights in the dark. children fighting over ice. a man with no words jerking past with kids hanging off his arms. chat something is wrong with the air down here and I am going in anyway.

beats.title: Arrest Him, Constable
beats.modern: I'm on trial now. no idea when that started. a queue of society ladies I have never touched are giving evidence: anonymous letters in a disguised hand, indecent proposals, and one flower I sent from a mountain that turned out to be a potato blossom stolen off a model farm. chat nobody is doing this to me. my own head is doing this to me.
beats.quote: Arrest him, constable.

beats.title: Hound Of Dishonour
beats.modern: the madam of the house has turned into a man and I have turned into a woman. he calls me hound of dishonour and I call him Empress. Hugeness. Magmagnificence. he taps me with a fan and says on the hands down and chat, I go down. adorer of the adulterous rump, he calls me. he's not wrong. that's the horror.
beats.quote: Adorer of the adulterous rump!

beats.title: Non Serviam
beats.modern: my mother is in the room. green bile at the corner of her mouth, breath like wet ashes, telling me to repent, praying for my soul, dying in front of me a second time. NO. break my spirit if you can, all of you, I'll bring you to heel. with me it's all or not at all. I will not serve. so I took the stick and smashed the light out of the ceiling.
beats.quote: With me all or not at all. Non serviam!

beats.title: The Coward's Blow
beats.modern: he can barely stand, never mind fight, and he's arguing philosophy with two drunk soldiers in the street. I'm trying to walk him out of it. one of them breaks loose and hits him full in the face and he goes down flat, out cold, hat rolling off to the wall. chat I picked up the hat.

beats.title: Rudy
beats.modern: he's flat on the ground and I'm standing over him with his hat and his stick, not letting anyone near him. his face looks like his mother's. he's murmuring something about a white breast and a dim sea. and then, chat. against the dark wall. a boy about eleven, little suit, glass shoes, reading a book and kissing the page, not looking at me. Rudy.
beats.quote: (Wonderstruck, calls inaudibly.) Rudy!

beats.title: Showing Him The Photo
beats.modern: four in the morning in a cabman's shelter, feeding him coffee and a bun he won't touch, talking about Spain. so naturally I take out my wallet and show him a photograph of my wife in a low cut evening dress and ask him, thoughtfully, whether he'd call her a Spanish type. chat. I did that. on purpose.

beats.title: The Keyless Couple
beats.modern: get him back to my house and I have no key. it's in the other trousers. the ones I didn't wear to the funeral. options: knock and wake her, or don't knock. so a grown man in mourning clothes climbed over his own railings, hung by his hands, and dropped into his own basement. eleven stone four. chat I fell.
beats.quote: To enter or not to enter. To knock or not to knock.

beats.title: The Heaventree
beats.modern: we went out the back door into the garden and pissed under the stars. both of us. at the same time. and I looked up, chat, and there it was: the heaventree of stars hung with humid nightblue fruit.
beats.quote: The heaventree of stars hung with humid nightblue fruit.

beats.title: The Preceding Series
beats.modern: he's gone home and I'm alone in the dark doing the maths. the full list. Mulvey, Penrose, an italian organgrinder, a bootblack at the post office, on and on to no last term, and him at the end of it today. and every single one of them thought he was the first. chat none of them were the first. none of them will be the last.

beats.title: Melons
beats.modern: so what's the retribution, chat? murder: no. duel: no. divorce: not now. hush money: possibly. I ran every option and picked none of them. I got into bed the wrong way round, head at her feet, and kissed her. the plump mellow yellow smellow melons of her rump. each one. that's the revenge. that's it.
beats.quote: He kissed the plump mellow yellow smellow melons of her rump,

beats.title: Where?
beats.modern: she asks me where I've been all day. I give her a version of it. edited. and now I'm going under, curled up like a child, and the whole day is coming apart in my head into nonsense: Sinbad the Sailor and Tinbad the Tailor and Darkinbad the Brightdayler. he rests. he has travelled. when? going to dark bed. where?
beats.quote: He rests. He has travelled.

beats.title: Yes Because He Never
beats.modern: my turn, chat. he asked for breakfast in bed. eggs. HE never asks for anything, so something has happened today, I can smell it. last time he pulled this he was doing the sick voice at the hotel to impress that old miser Mrs Riordan who left us nothing and talked about earthquakes and the end of the world. let's have a bit of fun first.

beats.title: 3 Or 4 Times
beats.modern: so. this afternoon. three or four times, and I lit the lamp after and thought the vein was going to burst, the size of it, like a crowbar. he must have eaten oysters. great singing voice, no conversation, straight in. and I'm lying there thinking: whats the idea making us like that with a big hole in the middle of us.

beats.title: The Sun Shines For You
beats.modern: sixteen years ago on Howth head. grey tweed suit, straw hat, rhododendrons, and I gave him the bit of seedcake out of my own mouth. after that kiss I near lost my breath. he told me I was a flower of the mountain, and that the sun shines for you today. chat that was the one true thing he said in his whole life.
beats.quote: first I gave him the bit of seedcake out of my mouth

beats.title: Yes I Said Yes
beats.modern: he kissed me under the Moorish wall and I thought: well. as well him as another. so I asked him with my eyes to ask me again. and he asked. and I made him wait a second. and then I put my arms around him and pulled him down to me and his heart was going like mad and I said it.
beats.quote: and yes I said yes I will Yes.

beats.title: Colour Isn't In The Apple
beats.modern: the red is not in the apple, chat. out there it is only motion shoving your eyeball around. the colour happens inside you. press your eye with a finger and you see light with nothing in front of you, exact same trick. the object is one thing and the picture in your head is another thing, and you have only ever had the picture.

beats.title: Sudden Glory
beats.modern: figured out laughter. it is sudden glory: you spot something deformed in another person and instantly applaud yourself by comparison. which is exactly why the hardest laughers at other people's defects are the ones with the least going on. they have to keep themselves in their own favour somehow. big minds do not dunk. they pull people out of the mud and only measure themselves against the best.
beats.quote: Sudden glory, is the passion which maketh those Grimaces called LAUGHTER;

beats.title: Curiosity Is A Lust
beats.modern: wanting to know why and how is a passion, not a virtue, and it is the one no animal has. call it what it is: a lust of the mind. and it outlasts every other lust, because it never gets tired of itself the way the body does. the thing keeping you up at 3am reading is older than your morals.

beats.title: Panic Is A Group Project
beats.modern: panic terror: fear where nobody can tell you what of. and notice it only ever happens in a crowd. one guy actually saw something. everyone else is running because the person beside them is running, each one assuming the other knows why. that is the entire mechanism of a stampede, and of a bank run, and of most of history.

beats.title: The Man In Bedlam
beats.modern: madness is not a separate substance from passion. it is passion at a volume nobody else is running. if a man in the asylum holds a perfectly sober conversation with you and then, as you are leaving, tells you politely that he is God the Father, you do not need to wait around for him to do something wild. the claim was the whole diagnosis.

beats.title: Words Are Counters
beats.modern: nature cannot be wrong. only sentences can. which is why the more language a man has, the wiser or the crazier he gets, no middle option. words are counters to wise men, chips they push around to keep the reckoning straight. to fools they are actual money, valued by whichever name is stamped on them. Aristotle said it, therefore it is true. that is not thinking. that is currency worship.
beats.quote: For words are wise mens counters, they do but reckon by them: but they are the mony of fooles,

beats.title: Round Quadrangle
beats.modern: if you are wrong about a fact, fine, that is error, the most prudent men get there. but if you say round square, or immaterial substance, or free will, you have not said something false. you have made a noise. there is no thought under it to be right or wrong about. that is absurdity, and no creature on earth can do it except us.

beats.title: The Privilege Of Absurdity
beats.modern: humans got one bonus feature no animal has: we can be absurd. we can say things with zero meaning inside them and then defend them for forty years. and the world record holders, by a distance, are the professional philosophers. Cicero said it and he was one of them. cause of death is always the same: not one of them settles what his words mean before he starts reasoning with them.
beats.quote: there can be nothing so absurd, but may be found in the books of Philosophers.

beats.title: The Scarecrow Argument
beats.modern: why do I bother attacking their invisible separated essences? because it is crowd control. they use empty words to frighten you out of obeying the actual laws of your actual country, the same way a farmer frightens birds off the corn with an old coat, a hat and a bent stick. there is nobody in the coat. there is nobody in the words either.

beats.title: Read Thy Self
beats.modern: everyone repeats that wisdom comes from reading men, not books. and the people who say it mostly use it to run their neighbours down behind their backs. the older instruction is better: read thy self. watch what you actually do when you hope, fear, reason, want. congratulations, that is what everyone else is doing too. I am not guessing about you. I am filing a report on me.

beats.title: Reputation Of Power Is Power
beats.modern: reputation of power IS power, because everyone who needs protecting walks toward whoever looks like they have some. same with a run of good luck: win a few and people start believing in you, which makes you genuinely stronger. friends are power. servants are power. and eloquence is power for the bleakest reason available, which is that it looks like wisdom.
beats.quote: Eloquence is Power; because it is seeming Prudence.

beats.title: The Buyer Sets Your Price
beats.modern: your worth is a price, and a price is not a property you own. a commander is worth a fortune in wartime and nothing in peace. a good judge, the reverse. and here is the part that stings: not the seller but the buyer determines the price. you may rate yourself as high as you like, most men do. your real value is whatever other people will give for it.
beats.quote: For let a man (as most men do,) rate themselves as the highest Value they can; yet their true Value is no more than it is esteemed by others.

beats.title: There Is No Final Level
beats.modern: there is no greatest good. no final level where you arrive and stop wanting. the old moral philosophers sold a mind at rest, and no such mind exists, because a man whose desires are finished is a man who is finished. happiness is the moving, not the arriving. everything you get is only the road to the next thing you will want.

beats.title: Power After Power
beats.modern: general inclination of all mankind, and I do mean all: a restless desire for power after power, that stops only at death. it is not simple greed. it is that you cannot secure what you already have without getting more. kings, who have the most, spend it locking it down by law at home or by war abroad, and the second it is safe a new appetite shows up. the treadmill has no off switch. it has an obituary.
beats.quote: a perpetuall and restlesse desire of Power after power, that ceaseth onely in Death.

beats.title: Nature Made Us Equal Enough
beats.modern: nobody is far enough ahead to be safe. yes, some of you are stronger, some quicker. does not matter. the weakest man in the lobby has strength enough to kill the strongest, either by getting him in his sleep or by teaming up with three other people who are frightened of the same guy. that is the whole equality argument. it is not a compliment. it is a threat assessment.
beats.quote: the weakest has strength enough to kill the strongest, either by secret machination, or by confederacy with others,

beats.title: Everyone Thinks They're The Smart One
beats.modern: people find the equality claim insulting, because every single one of you believes he is wiser than the crowd. you will happily admit others are funnier, better read, better speakers. you will not admit anyone is wiser. and why? you see your own wit up close and everyone else's from across the room. honestly the best proof we all got an equal share of brains is that nobody has ever asked for a refund.
beats.quote: For they see their own wit at hand, and other mens at a distance.

beats.title: Three Reasons People Fight
beats.modern: three causes of quarrel in human nature and that is the whole list. gain, safety, reputation. the first takes your things, the second is scared you will take his, and the third will burn your house down over a WORD. a smile. a different opinion. any sign at all that you value him lower than he values himself, or that you slighted his family, his friends, his country, his trade, his name. most of the violence you will ever see is the third one.

beats.title: War Is Weather, Not A Storm
beats.modern: war is not the fighting. war is the forecast. foul weather is not one shower of rain, it is the stretch of days when rain is always on the table. same here: war is the whole time everyone knows everyone is willing, with nothing to rule it out. you are not at peace because nobody swung today. all the other time is peace.

beats.title: Solitary Poor Nasty Brutish And Short
beats.modern: with no common power there is no point building anything, because why plant a crop somebody else harvests. so: no trade, no ships, no decent housing, no clocks, no maps, no arts, no letters, no society. and worst of all, non stop fear of dying badly. what comes out the other end is a life solitary, poor, nasty, brutish and short. that is not me being dramatic. that is just the arithmetic with nobody holding the sword.
beats.quote: continuall feare, and danger of violent death; And the life of man, solitary, poore, nasty, brutish, and short.

beats.title: You Lock Your Own Door
beats.modern: think I am too dark about people? you arm yourself before a journey. you lock your door at night. you lock the chest INSIDE your locked house, in a country with laws and armed officers paid to avenge you. what opinion of your neighbours is the lock stating? of your children and servants, the chest? you accuse mankind with your actions every single night. I only wrote it down.

beats.title: Force And Fraud, The Two Virtues
beats.modern: in that condition nothing can be unjust, and I mean nothing. no common power, no law. no law, no injustice. out there force and fraud are the two cardinal virtues, openly. and there is no mine and thine either: property is whatever you can take and hold for exactly as long as you hold it. justice is not a faculty inside a man like eyesight. it is a thing between men, and only once somebody is enforcing it.
beats.quote: Force, and Fraud, are in warre the two Cardinall vertues.

beats.title: Seek Peace, Or Take Everything
beats.modern: rule one, and every other rule hangs off it: go for peace as far as you have any hope of getting it, and where you cannot get it, use every help and advantage of war. that is the deal in one line. the first half is the fundamental law of nature. the second half is the reason you are still alive to read the first half.
beats.quote: "To seek Peace, and follow it."
beats.group: The Way Out Is A Contract

beats.title: The Right You Cannot Sign Away
beats.modern: some rights cannot be handed over no matter what you signed. resisting people who come to take your life is one of them. why? every transfer is voluntary, and every voluntary act aims at some good to yourself, and there is no good to you in that one. same for wounds and chains and prison. and when men come at you with violence you cannot know whether they mean to stop short of killing you, so the law does not pretend you agreed.
beats.group: The Way Out Is A Contract

beats.title: The Fool's Argument
beats.modern: the Fool says in his heart there is no such thing as justice, and sometimes out loud too. his case: your survival is your own business, so keeping or breaking a covenant is only a question of what pays. if the wickedness pays big enough that nobody can touch you afterward, it was reasonable, and what is reasonable cannot be unjust. that is how successful wickedness got the name of virtue. men who condemn breaking faith everywhere else make one exception: when a kingdom is the prize.
beats.quote: The Foole hath sayd in his heart, there is no such thing as Justice;
beats.group: The Way Out Is A Contract

beats.title: Nobody Lets You Back In
beats.modern: here is the answer to him, and it is not be nice, it is arithmetic. nobody survives out there on his own strength, you need confederates. so a man who announces that cheating the people who help him is rational cannot be received into any group except by their mistake, and cannot be kept once they see the mistake. cast out, he dies. left in, he is alive purely on other people's errors, which is not a strategy you can plan around.
beats.group: The Way Out Is A Contract

beats.title: Covenants Without The Sword
beats.modern: justice, equity, modesty, mercy, do unto others: all correct, all completely useless on their own, because every one of them runs against what our passions actually want. covenants without the sword are just words, and words secure nobody at all. that is not contempt for morality. it is a note about enforcement. a rule with no consequence behind it is a suggestion wearing a costume.
beats.quote: And Covenants, without the Sword, are but Words, and of no strength to secure a man at all.
beats.group: The Way Out Is A Contract

beats.title: Why Bees Manage And We Don't
beats.modern: people keep asking why bees and ants run a functioning society with no coercion and we cannot. five reasons. bees do not compete for honour. a bee's private good IS the common good. no bee thinks it could run the hive better than management. no bee has the art of words, so no bee can dress good up as evil on a stream. and last one, my favourite: man is most troublesome exactly when he is most at ease. comfort is when he starts correcting the government.
beats.group: The Way Out Is A Contract

beats.title: I Authorise And Give Up My Right
beats.modern: here is the move. every person hands their whole strength to one man or one assembly, and each says to each: I authorise and give up my right of governing myself to this man, on condition you do the same. that is more than agreement, more than everyone happening to cooperate. it is a real unity, all of you fused into one person. and that person is Leviathan. a mortal god, which is where your peace and defence actually come from.
beats.quote: "I Authorise and give up my Right of Governing my selfe, to this Man, or to this Assembly of men, on this condition, that thou give up thy Right to him,
beats.group: The Way Out Is A Contract

beats.title: The Artificial Man
beats.modern: so I built a machine out of people. sovereignty is its artificial soul. magistrates are the joints, reward and punishment are the nerves, everyone's wealth is the muscle, counsellors are the memory, law is its reason, and the safety of the people is its job. concord is health. sedition is sickness. civil war is when it dies. I called it Leviathan because nothing on earth is bigger, and you are all cells inside it.
beats.quote: For by Art is created that great LEVIATHAN called a COMMON-WEALTH, or STATE,
beats.group: The Way Out Is A Contract

beats.title: The Powers Do Not Split
beats.modern: the essential rights cannot be divided up and parcelled out. hand off the army and your courts are decoration. hand off taxation and the army is decoration. hand off who may teach what, and men will be frightened into rebellion by stories about spirits. a kingdom divided against itself cannot stand, and I want you to notice the order of events: the division in opinion comes first. the division into opposing armies is second. England is running the demonstration right now.

beats.title: Fear And Freedom Get Along Fine
beats.modern: fear and liberty are consistent, and here is the proof. a man throws his cargo into the sea so the ship will not sink. he is terrified and he chose it, willingly, and could have refused. same when you pay a debt only because prison is the alternative: nobody was physically stopping you from keeping the money. everything men do under law is still their own action. free does not mean unpressured. free means nothing external stopped you.
beats.quote: Feare and Liberty are consistent;

beats.title: Chains From His Lips To Your Ears
beats.modern: laws are artificial chains, and you forged them. one end is fastened to the sovereign's lips, the other end to your own ears. that is the entire apparatus. and physically they are feeble, easiest thing in the world to snap one. they hold by the danger of breaking them, never by the difficulty.
beats.quote: fastned at one end, to the lips of that Man, or Assembly, to whom they have given the Soveraigne Power; and at the other end to their own Ears.

beats.title: LIBERTAS On The Turrets
beats.modern: the city of Lucca has LIBERTY cut into its towers in letters you can read from the road. does one man in Lucca have a single ounce more freedom from the state than a man in Constantinople? no. the liberty in all those Greek and Roman books is the CITY's liberty to do what it likes to other cities, not yours. monarchy, republic, does not move your number.
beats.quote: There is written on the Turrets of the city of Luca in great characters at this day, the word LIBERTAS;

beats.title: Obedience Lasts As Long As Protection
beats.modern: before anyone files me as the absolutism guy: your obligation lasts exactly as long as his power to protect you, and not one hour longer. the right to save yourself when nobody else can be signed away by no covenant ever written. sovereignty is the soul of the body politic, and when the soul departs the limbs stop moving. the end of obedience is protection. wherever a man sees protection, in his own sword or another man's, that is where his obedience goes.
beats.quote: The Obligation of Subjects to the Soveraign is understood to last as long, and no longer, than the power lasteth, by which he is able to protect them.

beats.title: Hedges, Not Walls
beats.modern: laws are not there to stop you moving. they are hedges along a road, set not to halt travellers but to keep them from wandering off and wrecking themselves on their own impulses and haste. which means a law that is not needful is not a good law at all. it is a trap for money. and where the right of the sovereign is not acknowledged, extra laws will not save anybody anyway.
beats.quote: as Hedges are set, not to stop Travellers, but to keep them in the way.

beats.title: No Impunity For The Great
beats.modern: in a court of law the great man and the poor man stand as level as kings do before the King of Kings. and when a great man does harm, his greatness does not soften it, it makes it worse, because he needed to do it least of anyone. let him walk and watch the chain run: impunity makes insolence, insolence makes hatred, and hatred will pull down every oppressive greatness in reach even if it brings the whole commonwealth down too.
beats.quote: Impunity maketh Insolence; Insolence Hatred; and Hatred, an Endeavour to pull down all oppressing and contumelious greatnesse,

beats.title: Charity Is Not A Mood
beats.modern: men who through accidents they could not avoid can no longer keep themselves should not be left to whether strangers feel generous this month. that is the commonwealth's job, in law. exposing them to the hazard of uncertain charity is the same unkindness as walking past them yourself, only with extra steps in between. the strong bodied are another matter entirely. those you put to work, and you make sure there is work to be found.

beats.title: Multiplying Glasses
beats.modern: every one of you is issued a magnifying glass at birth, namely your passions and your self love, and through it every small payment looks like an enormous grievance. what you are not issued is the telescope. that would be moral and civil science, the thing that lets you see the disaster hanging in the distance which the payment is quietly preventing. so the cost is vivid and the catastrophe is invisible. every single time.
beats.quote: For all men are by nature provided of notable multiplying glasses, (that is their Passions and Self-love,) through which, every little payment appeareth a great grievance;

beats.title: Two Masters, One Seizure
beats.modern: if one power gets to declare what sin is and another declares what law is, you have two kingdoms wearing one country, and every subject serving two masters who both want their commands obeyed as law. that cannot hold. one has to sit under the other. when they collide instead, the body politic goes into convulsions, like a man in a falling sickness thrashing into fire and water, because the nerves are receiving two sets of signals at once.

beats.title: The Books That Teach Regicide
beats.modern: young men read the Greek and Roman histories, see the glorious campaigns, and conclude the glory came from the form of government rather than from a handful of extremely ambitious individuals. they skip straight past the constant seditions and civil wars in the same pages. then they learn that killing a king is a crime but killing a TYRANT is admirable, and the entire trick turns out to be which word you say first.

beats.title: Tyrannophobia
beats.modern: there is a disease you get from a mad dog's bite where you are dying of thirst and cannot bear the sight of water. a monarchy bitten by the democratical writers catches the same illness. it desperately needs a strong government, and the instant it has one it recoils in horror at being strongly governed. call it tyrannophobia. dying of thirst, screaming at the cup.

beats.title: Prometheus Brain
beats.modern: man is the animal that cannot stop asking what caused this, which means he cannot stop dreading what is coming. that is Prometheus, whose name means the prudent man: chained on a hill with an excellent long view, an eagle eating his liver by day and the liver growing back overnight. anyone who looks too far ahead has his heart gnawed all day by fear of death or poverty, and gets no pause from it except sleep.

beats.title: Four Seeds
beats.modern: four seeds, and all four are planted in everybody. believing in ghosts. not knowing what actually causes anything. devotion toward whatever you are afraid of. and taking coincidences for omens. grow those in different soil, with different fancies and passions, and you get ceremonies so different that each group finds the other's completely ridiculous. same four seeds every time though.
beats.quote: Opinion of Ghosts, Ignorance of second causes, Devotion towards what men fear, and Taking of things Casuall for Prognostiques,

beats.title: The Ghost Of The Roman Empire
beats.modern: trace where that great church power actually came from and it is unmistakable. the Papacy is the ghost of the dead Roman Empire, sitting crowned on its own grave. it rose out of those ruins the moment the empire went cold. even the language is a ghost: nobody in the world speaks Latin, and there it is, still walking the halls at night.
beats.quote: the Papacy, is no other, than the Ghost of the deceased Romane Empire, sitting crowned upon the grave thereof:

beats.title: Protection And Obedience
beats.modern: that is the book. if you take one thing out of it, take this: the relation between protection and obedience runs both directions and neither end survives alone. you owe obedience because you are protected. he holds the power because he protects. cut either side and there is no commonwealth left, only armed men who used to be neighbours. now I am going back to my study of bodies natural, which offends fewer people.

beats.title: The Interview
beats.modern: chat I am twenty years old, I am a country vicar's daughter, and I just got hired by the most handsome man in London to raise his dead brother's two orphans in a giant house in Essex. sight unseen. pay is way above my level. and the one condition: never contact him. never write, never complain, never ask. handle everything myself and let him alone. he held my hand and thanked me and I said yes to all of it.
beats.quote: “That she should never trouble him—but never, never: neither appeal nor complain nor write about anything;

beats.title: The Headmaster's Letter
beats.modern: day two. postbag comes late. letter from my employer, and sealed inside it is one from the school. his note says: read him, deal with him, do NOT report back. not a word. so I open it alone at midnight and the school will not take Miles back. ever. no reason given. no reason given is the worst kind of reason. the boy is ten.
beats.quote: “What does it mean? The child’s dismissed his school.”

beats.title: Nothing, Nothing, Nothing
beats.modern: then I actually meet Miles and he is the sweetest creature alive, glowing, incapable of a bad thought. so the housekeeper asks the obvious. what do I write to the school? nothing. what do I tell his uncle? nothing. what do I say to the boy? nothing. we shook on it like a blood oath. chat I just chose the vibes over the evidence.
beats.quote: “Then I’ll stand by you. We’ll see it out.”

beats.title: The Man On The Tower
beats.modern: so I'm on my evening walk doing my little daydream where my gorgeous boss appears on the path and tells me I'm doing great. and there IS a man. up on the tower. hatless, both hands on the ledge, staring straight down at me. the rooks stop cawing. the whole evening goes muted, like someone cut the audio. and chat, it isn't him.
beats.quote: An unknown man in a lonely place is a permitted object of fear to a young woman privately bred;

beats.title: He Came For Someone Else
beats.modern: sunday. I go back for my gloves and he is at the dining room window. face right against the glass. same man, closer, and this time I watch his eyes leave me and go around the room. checking. looking past me for something else. that is the detail that took my legs out. I'm not the one being haunted. I'm not even the point.
beats.quote: He had come for someone else.

beats.title: Quint Is Dead
beats.modern: I give the housekeeper the full police sketch. red hair, tight curls, little red whiskers, long pale face, small fixed eyes, tall, no hat. dressed smart in clothes that are not his. she goes white and says those are the master's clothes. then she gives me the name: Peter Quint, the valet, in charge here after the master left. cool. where is he now. and she squares up like she needs both feet planted to say it: he died last winter.
beats.quote: “Peter Quint—his own man, his valet, when he was here!”

beats.title: Too Free With Everyone
beats.modern: she asks who he was looking for and I hear my own mouth say Miles. no proof. total certainty. and she doesn't argue, which is so much worse. then the lore drop: neither child has ever once said his name. and when Quint was alive he had that boy to himself for hours, for months, nobody stopping him, because the master handed him everything. she puts it as gently as she can. he was much too free.
beats.quote: “Quint was much too free.”

beats.title: The Sea Of Azof
beats.modern: hot afternoon at the lake. Flora's playing, I'm sewing, and I know without looking that there is a third person on the far bank. before I look up I check the kid. and chat: she has gone completely silent, she has turned her back to the water, and she is calmly jamming a stick into a piece of wood to make a toy boat. eight year olds do not perform casual. she is performing casual.
beats.quote: My heart had stood still for an instant with the wonder and terror of the question whether she too would see;

beats.title: They Know
beats.modern: I throw myself at the housekeeper screaming they know, they know. Flora saw and said NOTHING, kept it to herself, an eight year old holding a secret that clean. and it wasn't the man this time. a woman in black on the other side of the lake, beautiful and dreadful, not looking at me once, just fixed on the child with a kind of fury of intention. I already know who. my predecessor. the one who left and died. Miss Jessel.
beats.quote: a woman in black, pale and dreadful—with such an air also, and such a face!—on

beats.title: The Staircase Standoff
beats.modern: 4am. I'm reading, the house feels wrong, I take a candle out to the landing and the flame dies. and Quint is on the stairs. halfway up, in the grey light, looking right at me. and chat here's the part that scares me: I am not afraid. we stand in total silence like two people who already know each other. then he turns and walks down into the dark like a servant who was given an order.
beats.quote: I had plenty of anguish after that extraordinary moment, but I had, thank God, no terror.

beats.title: The Curtain Trick
beats.modern: get back to my room and Flora's bed is empty, curtains pulled across it so it reads as full. then she pops out from behind the window blind, barefoot, and scolds ME. you naughty, where have you been. so I ask why she staged the bed to look slept in. she gives me the little divine smile: because I don't like to frighten you. she is eight. that answer was written in advance.
beats.quote: “Because I don’t like to frighten you!”

beats.title: The Boy On The Lawn
beats.modern: eleventh night. Flora's at the window again, so I sneak to an empty room in the old tower to see what she's looking at. big moon, clear as anything. there's a figure on the lawn staring up, and not at me. at something above me. there is someone on the tower over my head. and the kid standing on the grass in the middle of the night, face turned up to it, is Miles. I felt sick as hell.
beats.quote: There was clearly another person above me—there was a person on the tower;

beats.title: Think Me Bad
beats.modern: I march him upstairs and demand the truth. why were you outside at midnight. he smiles that smile and says he did it so that for once I would think he was bad. that was the entire plan. he set it up with Flora, she got up and looked out the window, I followed her eyes, I saw. then he kissed me and asked how else was he supposed to be bad enough. chat I got outplayed by a ten year old and I thanked him for it.
beats.quote: “How otherwise should I have been bad enough?”

beats.title: They're His And They're Hers
beats.modern: here's what I finally worked out. the children were never good. they were ABSENT. all that sweetness is a policy and a fraud, they're living a whole second life I'm not in. they're not mine and they're not ours. they're his and they're hers. and the two dead ones keep showing up on towers and roofs and the far side of ponds because they're trying to get close enough. what can they even do, she asks. they can destroy them.
beats.quote: They’re not mine—they’re not ours. They’re his and they’re hers!”

beats.title: Who's Going To Make Him
beats.modern: housekeeper's fix: their uncle has to come take them away. great. who makes him? me, apparently. so I write to the man and say what exactly, sir your house is poisoned and your niece and nephew are insane, regards, the governess you told never to bother you? she suggests I make him come for MY sake. absolutely not. I told her if she ever appeals to him on my behalf I leave that same day, him and her both.
beats.quote: “By writing to him that his house is poisoned and his little nephew and niece mad?”

beats.title: When Am I Going Back
beats.modern: walking to church. Miles, sweet as anything, tosses it out like a rose: when in the world am I going back to school? chat I stopped dead like a tree fell across the road. weeks of neither of us touching it and he opens in public where I can't do anything. then he keeps going. he's a fellow. he can't be with the same lady always. he's getting on. he wants to see more life. that is not a child talking, that is a negotiation.
beats.quote: “Look here, my dear, you know,”

beats.title: I Will
beats.modern: then in the churchyard, standing over the graves, he asks the question that put me on the ground. does my uncle think what you think. does he know the way I'm going on. I said your uncle doesn't much care. and Miles goes: don't you think he can be made to? by coming down here. and who's getting him down, Miles? I will. then he walked into church and left me sitting on a tomb.
beats.quote: “Then don’t you think he can be made to?”

beats.title: She's In My Chair
beats.modern: I nearly quit on the spot. skipped the service, went back to the empty house to grab my things, opened the schoolroom door and there is a woman sitting at MY table in full noon daylight, head in her hands, writing nothing. the dead governess. she stands up, unbothered, and looks at me like her right to that chair is as good as mine to hers. like I'm the intruder. I screamed you terrible, miserable woman at her and the room went back to sunshine. and I stayed.
beats.quote: her—“You terrible, miserable woman!”—I

beats.title: The Candle
beats.modern: night of the storm. I'm on the edge of his bed begging him to tell me anything. I say I'd rather die than hurt a hair of you, I just want you to help me save you. and the room goes freezing, a blast of dead air, the whole house shakes like the window came in, and the boy SCREAMS. chat I could not tell if that was terror or celebration. then darkness. why, the candle's out. it was I who blew it, dear.
beats.quote: “It was I who blew it, dear!”

beats.title: She Took The Boat
beats.modern: Flora is gone. we walk the entire lake and there's no girl and no boat, and that missing boat is the proof. she rowed herself across and hid it in the trees behind a bank. all alone, that child? she is not alone. and at times like this she is not a child. she's an old, old woman.
beats.quote: “She’s not alone, and at such times she’s not a child: she’s an old, old woman.”

beats.title: She's There, She's There
beats.modern: we find Flora on the grass smiling like a finished performance, and I finally say the name out loud: where is Miss Jessel. and she IS there, across the water, exactly where she stood before. one second of pure joy, chat. proof. I'm not cruel and I'm not mad. I'm pointing, screaming she's as big as a blazing fire, LOOK. and the woman looks straight through a person standing forty feet away and asks where on earth I see anything. that's when my whole fucking floor went out.
beats.quote: She’s as big as a blazing fire!

beats.title: Take Me Away From Her
beats.modern: and Flora never even turns her head to look. she stares at ME with a face I have never seen on her, hard and old and common, and she says it flat: I see nobody. I see nothing. I never have. I think you're cruel. I don't like you. then she buries her face in the housekeeper's skirt and starts wailing take me away, take me away from HER. from me, chat. she means me.
beats.quote: I think you’re cruel. I don’t like you!”

beats.title: The Letter Never Went
beats.modern: I send them both to London, and on the way out the housekeeper drops it: my letter to the uncle never arrived. it never went. it wasn't on the hall table where I left it, Luke never touched it. Miles took it. read it. and she says out loud the thing neither of us wanted to be true: now she knows what he did at school. he stole.
beats.quote: “Your letter won’t have got there. Your letter never went.”

beats.title: Yes, I Took It
beats.modern: just me and the boy in the house now. I ask him, offhand, like it's a small thing: did you take my letter off the hall table. and Quint arrives at the window. white face of damnation against the glass, standing there like a guard outside a prison. so I grab him, turn his back to it, hold him with his own heart hammering in my hands, and I fight for that soul without letting him see what I'm fighting. and out of him comes: yes. I took it.
beats.quote: It was like fighting with a demon for a human soul,

beats.title: I Said Things
beats.modern: so what got you expelled, Miles. did you steal? no. he said things. not to everyone. to a few boys, the ones he liked. and they repeated them to the ones THEY liked and it went round until it reached the masters and they threw him out and never told anyone what for. he can't remember the words. he can't remember the names. that's it. that's the entire crime. and chat, standing there, it hits me: what if he's innocent. what does that make me.
beats.quote: “They thought it was enough!”

beats.title: Peter Quint, You Devil
beats.modern: he's at the glass one last time and I'm shrieking no more, no more, no more. Miles can't see it. he guesses wrong, asks is SHE here. no. it's at the window, straight in front of us. and the boy screams the name I never once said to him: Peter Quint, you devil. WHERE. I turn him round to show him and there's nothing. clear sky. quiet day. I tell him Quint has lost him forever. then I feel what it is I'm holding. gg chat.
beats.quote: “Peter Quint—you devil!”

gullivers-travels-into-several-remote.title: Gulliver's Travels into Several Remote Nations of the World
gullivers-travels-into-several-remote.author: Jonathan Swift

beats.title: Woke Up Tied Down
beats.modern: woke up and I cannot move. arms, legs, HAIR, all pegged to the ground. then something walks up my chest and it's a guy. six inches tall. bow and arrow. forty of his friends behind him. I yell, they scatter, they come back, and they unload a hundred arrows into my hand like needles. lying still now. chat, the tutorial is hostile.

beats.title: The Feast
beats.modern: they built scaffolding up my ribs and now a hundred of them are marching meat into my mouth. shoulders of mutton smaller than a lark's wing, I'm doing three at a time. bread loaves the size of musket bullets. they winch up a whole barrel of wine and it's half a pint. I ask for more. they're out. chat I drank the national reserve.

beats.title: They Found My Watch
beats.modern: the search team inventories my pockets and files a report to their emperor. my comb is a palisade fence. my pistols are hollow iron pillars. and my pocket watch, which ticks like a water mill, they conclude is either an unknown animal or THE GOD I WORSHIP, because I check with it before I do anything. chat. they are not wrong.
beats.quote: it pointed out the time for every action of his life.

beats.title: Promotion by Rope Trick
beats.modern: here's how you get a cabinet post in this country. a job opens, five candidates dance on a rope, highest jump without falling takes the ministry. the treasurer clears an inch above every lord in the empire. he'd have broken his neck last year if a royal cushion hadn't happened to be lying there. this is the government. this is the entire hiring process.
beats.quote: whoever jumps the highest, without falling, succeeds in the office.

beats.title: Terms and Conditions
beats.modern: to get unchained I have to accept the terms. no leaving without a permit. no lying down in a field. carry the royal courier once a moon. destroy the Blefuscu fleet. pace out the entire coastline and file a survey. his official title is delight and terror of the universe and his empire is twelve miles around. I signed. cheerfully.
beats.quote: monarch of all monarchs, taller than the sons of men; whose feet press down to the centre, and whose head strikes against the sun;

beats.title: High Heels and Eggs
beats.modern: two parties here. high heels and low heels. they will not eat or speak with each other. the heir has one of each so he walks with a limp and everybody reads the limp as a policy position. meanwhile there's a war on. thirty thousand dead, forty ships gone, eleven thousand executed, over which end of a fucking egg you crack first.
beats.quote: ‘that all true believers break their eggs at the convenient end.’

beats.title: I Stole a Navy
beats.modern: strip off, wade in, fifty hooks on fifty cables. they shoot my face full of arrows so I put on my SPECTACLES, the pair their search team never found, and keep working. cut the anchor cables, gather the knot, pull. fifty warships walking across the channel behind me. I come up out of the water holding an entire navy on a string.

beats.title: The One Time I Refused
beats.modern: now he wants the rest of their ships, the whole island as a province, and every big-endian dead. I say no. that's it, that's the crime. the man I personally handed a navy to starts building a case against me that same week. turns out services weigh nothing the second you decline the favour.
beats.quote: I would never be an instrument of bringing a free and brave people into slavery.”

beats.title: The Fire
beats.modern: empress's apartment is burning, their buckets are thimbles, my coat's at home. but I drank a LOT of a very diuretic wine last night and I have not gone since. three minutes. fire out. palace saved, chat. ...it is a capital offence to make water inside the palace walls. I did not think of that until just now.
beats.quote: in three minutes the fire was wholly extinguished,

beats.title: Articles of Impeachment
beats.modern: they read out the charges. article one: did maliciously, traitorously and devilishly extinguish a fire by discharge of his urine. article two: declined to commit a genocide when instructed. that's the treason. saving the palace the wrong way, and refusing to wipe out a nation. they wrote it down themselves, chat. VOD receipts.

beats.title: The Merciful Option
beats.modern: my best friend at court stands up FOR me: don't kill him, just put out both his eyes. sharp arrows into the eyeballs, twenty surgeons attending, and everyone agrees this is the gentle option. the treasurer then costs it out: cut my rations quietly until I waste away, cart off the meat, keep the skeleton as a monument. that's the mercy here. that's my fucking friend.

beats.title: Six Hundred Pounds of Sheep
beats.modern: made it home with live tiny cattle in my coat pockets. rats got one of the sheep on the voyage, found her bones picked clean. showed the rest to gentlemen for money, then sold the herd for six hundred pounds. two months with my wife and children and I'm signing onto another ship. I never learn. that's the whole channel.

beats.title: Picked Up Like a Bug
beats.modern: new country, corn forty feet tall. a reaper nearly steps on me so I scream, and he lifts me between finger and thumb the way you grab something that might bite. sixty feet up, pinching my ribs. I don't struggle. I look at the sun and put my hands together and beg. last patch I was a god here. now I'm vermin with good manners.

beats.title: Rats the Size of Dogs
beats.modern: locked in a room the size of a cathedral and two rats come up the bedcurtains. one gets his forefeet on my collar. I rip his belly open before he can do anything and put a wound in the other on his way out. measured the tail: two yards. chat, if I'd taken my belt off before that nap I'd have been eaten in my sleep.

beats.title: My Little Nurse
beats.modern: the farmer's nine year old made me seven shirts, taught me the language, built me a bed out of her doll's cradle and named me Grildrig. forty feet tall and small for her age. she calls me hers. I owe her everything I have here. and I already know I am going to be the thing that ruins her.

beats.title: Ten Shows a Day
beats.modern: they put me on a table in an inn and charge at the door. I walk, I bow, I drink from a thimble, I do the sword bit, I say you are welcome in their language. twelve sets of company before I can't stand up. a schoolboy throws a hazelnut the size of a pumpkin at my head. it misses. he gets beaten and thrown out. and we go again tomorrow.

beats.title: Sold to the Queen
beats.modern: my owner reckons I'm about to die from the workload, so he sells me to the queen for a thousand gold while I'm still worth something. I ask for one thing: Glumdalclitch comes with me. granted. she can't hide how happy she is. he says farewell and I don't answer him. he sold me exactly like he sold her lamb to the butcher.

beats.title: Whig or Tory
beats.modern: I'm laying out our trade, our wars, our religion, our parties, and he picks me up, strokes me, laughs, and asks whether I'm a whig or a tory. then turns to his minister: look how contemptible human grandeur is, when insects can imitate it. they have titles. they build little nests. they love, they fight, they cheat, they betray. I went red. and I could not name one thing he got wrong.

beats.title: Dropped in the Cream
beats.modern: the queen's dwarf is thirty feet tall and I'm the only thing in the palace beneath him, so we have a problem. today he lifts me mid-dinner and drops me headfirst into a bowl of cream. swallowed a quart before my nurse fished me out. last week he wedged me into a marrow bone and left me sticking out of it. sound whipping both times. worth it, apparently.

beats.title: The Monkey Fed Me
beats.modern: a monkey drags me out of my box, tucks me under his arm like a baby and takes me up onto the palace ROOF. sits on the ridge cramming food out of his cheek into my mouth and patting me when I won't swallow. the entire court laughing in the yard below. a footman finally carries me down in his trouser pocket. threw up for an hour, bed for a fortnight.

beats.title: Odious Little Vermin
beats.modern: so the king takes everything I've told him. our courts, our wars, our laws, our last hundred years. holds me in his hand. strokes me. and delivers the verdict: my people are the most pernicious little vermin ever to crawl on the face of the earth. said kindly. chat, I have no rebuttal.
beats.quote: I cannot but conclude the bulk of your natives to be the most pernicious race of little odious vermin that nature ever suffered to crawl upon the surface of the earth.”

beats.title: I Offered Him Guns
beats.modern: to win him back I offer him gunpowder. explained all of it: the tubes, the balls, walls coming down, ships with a thousand men going under, bodies dropping out of the clouds for the entertainment of the spectators. free. a gift. he goes white, says he'd give up half his kingdom before knowing that secret, and orders me never to mention it again on pain of death. and I sat there thinking: what a small fucking mind.
beats.quote: he would rather lose half his kingdom, than be privy to such a secret;

beats.title: Eagle Delivery
beats.modern: napping in my box by the sea and something yanks the ring on the roof. wings overhead. an eagle has me and it means to drop me on a rock like a tortoise and open me up. then a fight starts up there. and I fall. a full minute straight down and a crash louder than Niagara. box floating. me inside it. four hours in the ocean waiting to die.

beats.title: Everyone Got Small
beats.modern: home. and everyone is TINY. I'm shouting at travellers on the road to stand clear before I tread on them. I duck under my own front door like a goose. my wife runs out to embrace me and I stoop below her knees so she can reach my mouth. told her she'd starved herself and the girl down to nothing. they all think I've lost my wits. it's just habit, chat. it's only ever habit.
beats.quote: I began to think myself in Lilliput.

beats.title: Set Adrift
beats.modern: pirates take my sloop. the Japanese captain hears me out and says I live. the DUTCHMAN, my fellow christian, spends an hour trying to get me thrown into the sea, fails, and settles for having me set adrift alone in a canoe with four days of food. stood on the deck cursing me the whole way out. I found more mercy in a heathen than in a brother christian, and I said so out loud, which is what started this.

beats.title: An Island in the Sky
beats.modern: dying on a rock. no food, no plan. then the sun goes out and there's not a cloud in the sky. something solid, two miles across, flat and shining underneath, moving toward me. I get the glass out and there are PEOPLE on it. walking up and down the sides. an island. in the air. with a population. I am waving my handkerchief at a floating country.

beats.title: Men Hired to Hit You
beats.modern: everyone up here is so deep in thought they can neither speak nor listen unless somebody hits them. so the rich keep a servant with a bladder on a stick whose whole job is to bop your mouth when it's your turn to talk, and your ear when someone's talking to you. also your eyes, so you don't walk off a ledge. they offered me one. I declined and the entire court decided I was stupid.

beats.title: Dinner in Triangles
beats.modern: dinner arrives: mutton cut to an equilateral triangle, beef as a rhomboid, pudding in a cycloid, bread in cones and cylinders. then a tailor takes my height with a QUADRANT, plots my whole body with rule and compasses, and six days later hands over a suit that fits nobody, because he fumbled one figure in the calculation. happens constantly here. nobody minds.

beats.title: How to Handle Rebels
beats.modern: here's how the flying island deals with a town that won't pay. park over it. no sun, no rain, crops fail, people sicken. still stubborn? drop rocks through the roofs. still stubborn? land the entire island on the city and everyone in it. he rarely does it, and it isn't mercy. the bottom might crack on impact.

beats.title: Country in Permanent Beta
beats.modern: forty years ago some men spent five months on the flying island, came home with a smattering of maths and a head full of ideas, and got a royal patent for an academy. now every town has one. new methods for everything. one man doing the work of ten. a palace built in a week. only snag: not one project has ever finished, and the country beneath them is starving in the ruins. so they push HARDER.
beats.quote: the whole country lies miserably waste, the houses in ruins, and the people without food or clothes.

beats.title: Sunbeams Out of Cucumbers
beats.modern: first room of the academy: a man eight years into extracting sunbeams out of cucumbers, to be sealed in phials and released in bad summers. eight more years and he'll have it, he says, could I contribute something, cucumbers were dear this season. next room the smell nearly drops me. senior fellow, turning human excrement back into the food it came from. they issue him a barrel of it a week.

beats.title: The Content Machine
beats.modern: a professor has built a frame of wooden blocks with every word in the language pasted on them. forty students crank handles, the words shuffle, and the boys write down any three that look like they belong together. six hours a day. he has volumes of broken sentences already, and out of that he'll assemble a complete body of all arts and sciences. no genius required. he'd like public funding for five hundred more.

beats.title: I Asked the Dead
beats.modern: on the sorcerers' island I can summon anyone who ever lived and they physically cannot lie. so I went through modern history. every famous victory won by a coward. every wise decision made by a fool. traitors written up as patriots, honest men on the gibbet. a general confessed he won purely through cowardice and bad judgement. three kings admitted they never once promoted a man on merit. chat the record is fake. all of it.

beats.title: Immortality Is a Nerf
beats.modern: they have people here who never die. I gave a whole speech about what I'd do with forever. then they explained it. you don't stop ageing, you just stop stopping. at eighty you're legally dead, estate handed over, can't own, can't testify. at ninety no teeth, no taste, no memory to reach the end of a sentence. the language moves on without you and you're a foreigner in your own town. they envy funerals.
beats.quote: I grew heartily ashamed of the pleasing visions I had formed;

beats.title: My Own Crew
beats.modern: my own men rush the cabin, bind me hand and foot and chain my leg to the bed with a sentry ordered to shoot. months of that, waiting to be murdered. then they row me to a shore nobody will name, tell me the new captain wanted rid of me at the first land they saw, and shove off. told me to hurry inland before the tide. that was the goodbye.

beats.title: Welcome to the Neighbourhood
beats.modern: meet the local wildlife. hairy, clawed, goat-bearded, the most disagreeable animal I have ever seen in my life. one comes at me so I hit it with the flat of my sword, and forty come howling out of the next field. I get my back against a tree while they climb the branches above me and shit on my head until I'm nearly stifled with it. that's the welcome. that's hour one.

beats.title: That Thing Is Me
beats.modern: the horse has his servant drag one of the creatures out of the kennel and stand it beside me for comparison. face. hands. feet. every part. and I'm looking at it and it is a person. it's ME with longer nails and dirtier palms. the only thing separating us is clothing they don't understand and the fact that I wash. chat I am the animal in the shed.

beats.title: No Word for Lying
beats.modern: I tell my master I crossed the sea in a hollow vessel made from the bodies of trees. he says I must be mistaken, or else I have said the thing which was not. that's the phrase. that's the whole construction they've got. there is no word for lying in this language. nobody ever needed to invent one.
beats.quote: “that I must needs be mistaken, or that I said the thing which was not;”

beats.title: Why We Fight
beats.modern: he asks what starts a war. so: ambition. ministers needing a distraction from their own theft. disagreements over whether a berry's juice is blood or wine, what colour a coat should be, whether whistling is a sin. we invade allies for a conveniently placed town. we invade the weak because they're weak and the strong because they're strong. and the soldier is the most honourable trade we have. hired to kill people who never did a fucking thing to him.
beats.quote: poor nations are hungry, and rich nations are proud; and pride and hunger will ever be at variance.

beats.title: White Is Black
beats.modern: then he asks about law. so I explain there is a whole class of men trained from boyhood to prove that white is black and black is white, depending on who is paying that day. if my neighbour wants my cow, he hires one to prove the cow was always his. I hire another to defend it, because I am not permitted to speak for myself. every other person in the country belongs to them.
beats.quote: “there was a society of men among us, bred up from their youth in the art of proving, by words multiplied for the purpose, that white is black, and black is white, according as they are paid.

beats.title: The River
beats.modern: bathing in the river, stark naked, and a young female of the local species watches from the bank and comes in after me. grabs hold of me. I roared until the nag came galloping over and she let go, then stood howling on the far bank the whole time I dressed. and that's the proof, chat. their females want me because I am one of them. I can't argue it anymore.

beats.title: The Exhortation
beats.modern: the assembly has ruled that my master keeps me too much like an equal. so: work me like the rest of my kind, or send me swimming back where I came from. they don't command here. they exhort. because no rational creature can disobey reason, so nobody ever needed the word. he told me gently, first thing in the morning. I fainted at his feet. he assumed I'd died.
beats.quote: either to employ me like the rest of my species, or command me to swim back to the place whence I came:

beats.title: The Hoof
beats.modern: boat's stitched out of skins, the wind's right, and I'm going. I knelt to kiss his hoof and he lifted it to my mouth himself. people say I made that part up, that no one so far above me would stoop to it. they've never met one. I paid my respects to the rest of them, got in the canoe, and pushed off.
beats.quote: he did me the honour to raise it gently to my mouth.

beats.title: The Kindest Man Alive
beats.modern: a Portuguese captain picks me up. Don Pedro. gives me his cabin, chicken, good wine, clean shirts, passage home, twenty pounds, asks nothing back. the kindest person in five voyages. and I crept out of bed to throw myself into the sea rather than sit near him, because he smelled like my own species. he had me chained in the cabin for my own good.

beats.title: My Wife Touched Me
beats.modern: home. my wife takes me in her arms and kisses me and I pass out cold for almost an hour. a full year before I could stand them in the room. they still don't touch my bread or drink from my cup. first money I spent was on two horses, and I talk to them four hours a day. the groom is my favourite person in the house because he smells of the stable.
beats.quote: I fell into a swoon for almost an hour.

beats.title: How a Colony Works
beats.modern: here's the pattern, and I've seen enough of the world to say it. a storm blows a crew somewhere. a boy spots land from the topmast. they go ashore, meet a harmless people who feed them, set up a rotten plank as a memorial, claim the place for their king, murder two or three dozen locals, take a couple home as samples, and get pardoned. then the ships come. that's a colony.
beats.quote: this execrable crew of butchers, employed in so pious an expedition, is a modern colony, sent to convert and civilize an idolatrous and barbarous people!

beats.title: Pride
beats.modern: last thing and then I'm done. a lawyer, a pickpocket, a colonel, a lord, a gambler, a politician: fine. that's nature, that's the course of things, I'm not provoked. but a lump of disease and deformity in body and mind that is also PROUD of itself breaks every measure of my patience. the horses have no word for that vice. they couldn't find it in the animals. I could. so if you carry any of it, do not come near me.
beats.quote: when I behold a lump of deformity and diseases, both in body and mind, smitten with pride, it immediately breaks all the measures of my patience;

beats.title: Midlife Crash Out
beats.modern: chat I'm 35 and I woke up in a forest with no path, no map, no idea how I got here. one second I'm living my life, next second: dark trees, zero light, genuine fear. this is not a bit. I looked up and there's a mountain with sunrise on it and for one second I thought ok, maybe I climb out of this.

beats.title: Three Beasts, Zero Skill Issue
beats.modern: started the climb. immediately a leopard blocks me. then a LION. then a she-wolf, and chat, the wolf is the one that broke me. she's starving and she never stops being starving no matter how much she eats. I backed all the way down the mountain. run ended. back into the dark.

beats.title: My Favourite Author Spawns In
beats.modern: a guy walks out of the dark and chat. CHAT. it's Virgil. the Aeneid Virgil. dead a thousand years, my literal favourite writer, standing in front of me. I told him his book is the only reason I know how to write. he goes: yeah, you can't take that road. we're going the long way. through hell.

beats.title: The Door Has Patch Notes
beats.modern: there's writing over the gate. it's written FROM the door's perspective, which is already unhinged, and it ends with the single hardest line ever carved into anything. Virgil goes, in here you leave all doubt behind. then he takes my hand like I'm five and walks me in.
beats.quote: “All hope abandon ye who enter here.”

beats.title: The Fence Sitters
beats.modern: first thing inside hell isn't even hell yet. it's the people who never picked a side. never did good, never did evil, just vibed. heaven won't take them and hell won't take them because hell has STANDARDS. they chase a blank flag forever getting stung by wasps. Virgil's review: don't talk about them. look and keep walking.

beats.title: Charon Denies Entry
beats.modern: old man with burning coal eyes rows up and starts screaming at me specifically because I'm ALIVE and his boat is not for me. Virgil hits him with the line that ends every argument down here: it is willed where will and power are one, ask no more. instant silence. then the dead drop into the boat like autumn leaves off a branch, all of them somehow eager.

beats.title: Limbo Is Just Sighing
beats.modern: first circle. no screaming, no fire. just sighing. men, women and infants, forever. Virgil says these people did nothing wrong. that's the whole charge sheet. wrong century, wrong paperwork. then he says it quietly: and I'm one of them. we live wanting something we will never get. that's the punishment.

beats.title: Sixth Man Of The Year
beats.modern: four shades walk up: Homer carrying a sword, then Horace, Ovid, Lucan. the actual greatest poets who ever lived. they greet Virgil, then they turn and wave ME over and make me one of them. I was the sixth. chat I am putting this in my bio. I am never recovering from this.

beats.title: They Read One Book
beats.modern: I called two of them out of the storm. Francesca and her guy, still together in the wind. she tells me they were reading a romance out loud, alone, and at the kissing part they stopped reading. that's the whole confession. her husband killed them both. and chat, she says the worst part of hell isn't the wind, it's remembering being happy. I passed out cold.
beats.quote: “No greater grief than to remember days Of joy, when mis’ry is at hand!

beats.title: Cerberus Gets Fed Dirt
beats.modern: three-headed dog, crimson eyes, greasy beard, currently shredding souls in the freezing rain. it sees us and opens all three mouths. Virgil calmly scoops up two handfuls of DIRT and throws it down its throat. the dog chokes on it like a lab getting a treat and forgets we exist. that is my guide. that is the greatest mind in poetry.

beats.title: F In The Swamp
beats.modern: guy covered in filth lunges at our boat asking who I am. I clocked him instantly. Filippo Argenti, the most arrogant man in Florence, now a mud creature. I told him stay there and cry. Virgil literally shoved him off the boat, hugged me, and said blessed is the woman who bore you. then the other mud people mobbed him and he started biting HIMSELF. we left.

beats.title: The Server Locks Us Out
beats.modern: we reach the walls of Dis. iron walls, red-hot towers, a thousand fallen angels on the gate. they'll let Virgil in for a chat. not me. then they slam the door in his face. chat. MY GUIDE got denied. he came back with his eyes on the ground and no confidence left in his face. he says he's angry, not scared, and someone is already on the way down to open this.

beats.title: Heaven Sends One Guy
beats.modern: someone walks across the swamp. WALKS. doesn't get wet. spirits scatter in front of him like frogs off a snake. the only thing bothering him is the smell, he keeps fanning it away from his face. he touches the gate with a stick and it just opens. then he tells a thousand demons off for being stupid, reminds them Cerberus still has no fur on his throat from last time, and leaves without a word to us.

beats.title: The Wrong Tense
beats.modern: a head pops out of a burning tomb looking past me for someone. it's Guido's dad. he asks where his son is, why isn't he with you. I said my friend Guido HAD him in contempt. past tense. one word. he screamed is he dead, does he not see daylight anymore, and I hesitated half a second too long. he fell back into the fire and never came up again. chat I killed a man with grammar.

beats.title: I Broke A Twig
beats.modern: black forest, no leaves, thorns instead of fruit, harpies nesting in it. Virgil says snap a branch. I snap a branch. the tree SCREAMS. why are you tearing me. dark blood comes out of the break, hissing like green wood on a fire, blood and words coming out of the same wound. chat these aren't trees.

beats.title: The Loyal Secretary
beats.modern: the tree talks. he was the emperor's right hand, held both keys to his heart, and jealous courtiers ran a smear campaign until his honours turned to ruin. so he killed himself. his words: I was just to everyone and unjust to myself. and he swears by his own roots he never betrayed his lord once. his only ask is that I go up there and clear his name.

beats.title: Sir, Brunetto
beats.modern: burning sand, fire falling like snow, and a troop of scorched souls squinting up at us like old tailors threading a needle. one grabs my hem. it's my TEACHER. the man who taught me how a person makes himself last. he can't stop walking or he lies down a hundred years, so he walks beside me with his head at my knee and warns me my own city will turn on me for doing good.

beats.title: Fraud Has A Face
beats.modern: our ride to the next level surfaces. face of an honest man. kind, gracious, trustworthy looking. everything below the neck is serpent, paws and painted patterns fancier than any tapestry ever woven. and the tail is up behind him with a scorpion's fork on it. that's fraud, chat. the face is the whole scam.

beats.title: Popes Upside Down
beats.modern: holes in the rock like baptism fonts, and out of each one a pair of legs with the feet on fire, kicking. these are the men who sold church offices. I lean down to talk to one and he starts yelling at me thinking I'm a DIFFERENT pope arriving early. he's stacked head-down on his predecessors, and when the next crooked one dies he gets pushed deeper. I asked what price Christ charged Peter for the keys.

beats.title: Ulysses Speedruns The Map
beats.modern: a flame with two tips walks up and it's Ulysses. HE talks. not his son, not his old father, not his wife could beat the urge to see what was out there. so he took one ship and the last loyal crew past the pillars where humans are told to stop. his speech to a boat of old men: you weren't made to live like animals, you were made for knowledge. chat he talked them into it in five sentences.
beats.quote: Ye were not form’d to live the life of brutes But virtue to pursue and knowledge high.”

beats.title: Five Months Of Ocean
beats.modern: they turned the stern to sunrise and rowed into open water for five moons. then a mountain appeared, tallest thing any of them had ever seen, and they cheered. the joy lasted about ten seconds. a whirlwind came off the new land, spun the ship three times, and on the fourth lifted the stern and drove the prow under. the sea closed over them. he tells it from inside a flame with zero self pity.

beats.title: The Lantern Guy
beats.modern: a body walks past me with no head. it's carrying the head by the hair, swinging it like a lantern, and the head LOOKS UP AT ME AND TALKS. he lifts it higher so I can hear better. he split a father and son against each other in life, so now his brain walks around separated from its own source. he calls it the law of retribution. chat I have never been more awake.

beats.title: The Tower
beats.modern: deepest ice. a man chewing on another man's skull looks up, wipes his mouth on the guy's hair, and tells me. locked in a tower with his four boys. door nailed shut. he watched their faces and turned to stone inside, and the children, the CHILDREN, offered him their own bodies so he'd hurt less. they died one by one over six days. then he went blind and crawled over them calling their names for three days. then hunger did what grief couldn't.

beats.title: Final Boss Is Crying
beats.modern: the bottom. and chat, the devil isn't scheming. he's stuck. frozen from the chest down, three faces, six bat wings, and the wind off those wings is what keeps the ice frozen. he built his own prison by flapping. and he is WEEPING out of six eyes, tears and bloody foam down three chins. the most powerful rebel ever and he's a windmill in a lake he made himself.

beats.title: Climbing Down God's Enemy
beats.modern: the exit is CLIMBING SATAN. Virgil tells me to hold his neck, waits for the wings to open, grabs the fur, and we go down the devil hand over hand. then at the hip he flips himself upside down and starts climbing UP and I thought we were going back into hell. we weren't. I looked back and Lucifer's legs were pointing up. we passed the centre of the earth. gravity flipped.

beats.title: Again Beheld The Stars
beats.modern: there's a stream running down through the rock and we follow it up in the dark. no resting, no talking, just climbing, him first, me behind. and then a round hole of light at the end of the cave. we came out on the other side of the world. first thing I saw was stars.
beats.quote: Thus issuing we again beheld the stars.

beats.title: The Beach Bouncer
beats.modern: new island, new mountain, sunrise, and four stars nobody up north has seen since Eden. an old man with a white double-fold beard stops us wanting to know how two souls escaped the pit. Virgil doesn't argue, he grabs me, bends my knees for me and makes me bow. hell's over, chat. we are doing therapy mountain now.

beats.title: Three Failed Hugs
beats.modern: a boatload of new souls lands and one comes sprinting at me with his arms open and it's Casella, my musician friend. I go to hug him. arms pass through. try again. through. third time, through, and my hands hit my own chest. he smiled and stepped back. so I asked him to sing instead, and he sang one of my own songs back to me, and the sweetness of it is still in me.

beats.title: One Tear, One Tug Of War
beats.modern: guy named Buonconte died bleeding out in a river valley with Mary's name on his lips. so an angel took him. and the devil showed up FURIOUS: you're robbing me over ONE TEAR. so he took the body instead, cooked up a storm, flooded the whole valley, and rolled the corpse down the river until it was buried in mud. lost the soul, griefed the body.

beats.title: Remember Me
beats.modern: a third soul speaks and it's the shortest life story anyone has ever given. Siena made me, Maremma unmade me, and the man who put the ring on my finger knows how. that's it. that's the whole thing. she doesn't even name him. and she asks me to rest from the road first, and THEN remember her.

beats.title: Seven Scars, One Door
beats.modern: three steps up to the actual gate: white marble you can see your face in, then a cracked scorched black one, then blood red. angel on top with a sword. I crawl and beg. he carves the letter P into my forehead SEVEN TIMES with his sword point, one per deadly sin, and says: when you're inside, wash these off. that's the assignment. seven scars, seven levels.

beats.title: Do Not Look Back
beats.modern: two keys, silver and gold. he says if either one jams in the lock nobody gets in, and that he'd rather err by opening than by keeping people out. then he shoves the door and it grinds like a rusted vault. one rule on the way through: whoever looks behind him goes straight back out. and as it opened I heard singing far off, coming and going like an organ under voices.

beats.title: Cimabue Got Ratioed
beats.modern: the proud are all folded under boulders sized to their own egos. under one of them is Oderisi, the best illustrator alive when he was alive, and he immediately hands the crown to the guy who replaced him. Cimabue thought he owned painting, now everyone says Giotto and nobody says Cimabue. one Guido took the language off the other Guido. your name is a gust of wind.

beats.title: Skill Issue, Not Star Issue
beats.modern: I asked Marco why the world is so cooked. is it the heavens? he sighs the deepest sigh in the poem and says brother, the world is blind and you clearly come from it. if the stars ran you there'd be no free choice, and no justice in reward or punishment either. the soul comes out like a baby chasing whatever tastes nice, so it needs laws and a leader, and nobody is leading.
beats.quote: If then the present race of mankind err, Seek in yourselves the cause, and find it there.

beats.title: Biggest Fan Meets Idol
beats.modern: a soul who just finished his sentence joins us and starts gushing about the Aeneid. calls it the breast he nursed at. says he'd do another whole lifetime in exile just to have lived when Virgil lived. chat. VIRGIL IS STANDING RIGHT THERE giving me the do-not-say-anything face. I smiled. he clocked the smile. I had to tell him. he drops to hug Virgil's feet and Virgil goes: brother, don't. you're a shadow hugging a shadow.

beats.title: Starving Under A Fruit Tree
