beats.modern: souls so thin their eye sockets look like rings with the stones pried out. a fruit tree and a waterfall right there, and the smell of them is what starves these people. one of them recognises ME and I couldn't recognise him back until he spoke. it's Forese. I cried at that face when he died and I'm crying at it again.

beats.title: He Said Her Name
beats.modern: last obstacle is a wall of fire and I have to walk through it. I clasped my hands and pictured every burned body I've ever seen. Virgil promises not one hair will singe, reminds me he got me past Geryon, says trust me. I don't move. so he tries one more thing. he says Beatrice is on the other side of this wall. and I turned like a dying man hearing the name he loves.

beats.title: Crown And Mitre
beats.modern: top of the stairs. Virgil turns to me and says you've seen both fires now, and my sight goes no further. I brought you as far as skill and art can bring anyone. take your own pleasure for a guide from here. don't distrust yourself anymore. then he says the words. I crown and mitre you, sovereign over yourself. that's the last thing he ever says to me.

beats.title: The Old Flame
beats.modern: a woman in a white veil, green mantle, robed in living flame. I can't even see her face yet and something wakes up in me that's been asleep since I was nine. so I turn left like a scared kid running to his mother, ready to say the old flame is back, every drop of blood in me is shaking. and Virgil is GONE. he left. no goodbye. I stood in Eden and cried, and a voice said: don't cry about that yet.
beats.quote: “Dante, weep not, that Virgil leaves thee: nay,

beats.title: Look At Me, I Am Beatrice
beats.modern: she doesn't hug me. she says my name, tells me to look at her properly, says I am, in fact, I AM Beatrice, and asks how I finally deigned to climb the mountain. I looked down at the water, saw my own face, and couldn't stand it. then she tells the angels the whole case: I led him with my eyes, then I died, and he immediately went after cheaper things. I froze solid. then the singing melted me.

beats.title: Second River, Full Reset
beats.modern: one river already took the memory of everything I did wrong. then they walk me into a second one, Eunoe, which gives back every good thing I'd forgotten I did. I drank and I would never have stopped drinking. I came out of that water remade, like a plant with new leaves, ready to go up.
beats.quote: Pure and made apt for mounting to the stars.

beats.title: She Stared At The Sun
beats.modern: Beatrice locks her eyes on the sun like no eagle ever has. I copy her. and I hold it, and the sky goes so bright it's like a second sun got hung up there. and something changes in me that language does not have a word for, so I use the closest myth I've got: Glaucus tasting the herb and turning into a sea god. after that I could hear the wheel of the heavens turning.

beats.title: In His Will Is Our Peace
beats.modern: lowest heaven. I ask a soul the rude question: do you want a higher spot? and she SMILES like she's in love and says no. love settles the will so you only want what you already have. wanting more would mean disagreeing with the one who placed us, and that can't happen here. and then she drops the line that reorganised my whole understanding of heaven.
beats.quote: And in his will is our tranquillity;

beats.title: Francis Married Poverty
beats.modern: a light in the sun tells me about a kid from Assisi who married a woman nobody had wanted in eleven hundred years, against his father's will, in front of a court and in front of his dad. the woman is POVERTY. widowed since Christ, zero suitors the whole time. and once people saw the two of them together and how happy they were, men started kicking off their shoes to follow.

beats.title: Great Great Grandpa Spoils It
beats.modern: I asked my ancestor to just tell me the exile straight, because an arrow you see coming flies slower. and he does, no riddles. you will leave everything you love. that's the first shot from the bow of exile. you'll learn how salty other people's bread is and how hard other people's stairs are. and the part that hurts most will be the worthless idiots you're exiled WITH.
beats.quote: Thou shalt prove How salt the savour is of other’s bread, How hard the passage to descend and climb By other’s stairs,

beats.title: The Little Threshing Floor
beats.modern: she told me to look down before going higher. so I looked back through all seven spheres and there's earth. and chat, it made me LAUGH. that's it? that pitiful little thing? that's the patch of dirt we are all so vicious about? I saw the whole thing from harbours to hills in one glance. anyone who thinks least of it is the wisest person alive.

beats.title: Viva Voce With Saint Peter
beats.modern: chat I am being examined ON FAITH. BY PETER. he asks what faith is and Beatrice gives me the look that says unlock it. I quote his own colleague back at him: the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen. he says correct. then he goes: nice coin, right weight, right alloy. but do you actually have it in your purse? examiners are the same in every century.

beats.title: Peter Turns Red
beats.modern: all of paradise is singing and then Peter's light changes colour and he goes OFF. my seat, MY seat, is empty in the sight of God, and the man sitting in it on earth has turned my grave into a sewer of blood. the whole sky flushed red like a sunset behind him. and he wasn't finished.

beats.title: The River Of Light
beats.modern: a river made of light. amber waves, banks covered in impossible spring, sparks flying out of it into the flowers like rubies set in gold and then diving back in. she says drink first. so I bent to it like a baby who slept through a feed, and the second the light touched my eyes the river turned from a stream into a CIRCLE. it was never a river.

beats.title: She Went To Her Seat
beats.modern: I turned to ask Beatrice one more thing and there's a smiling old man standing there instead. Bernard. I said where did she GO. he says look up, third circle from the top. and there she is, further from me than the sea floor is from the sky, with a crown of eternal light on her. and her look still comes down across all that distance clean and unblurred.

beats.title: One Volume, Everything In It
beats.modern: I looked into it. and in that depth I saw the entire universe bound together in one book. everything scattered across all of reality, every substance and every accident, gathered and stitched into a single light. I'm telling you what I saw and my tongue is doing worse than a baby still at the breast.

beats.title: Squaring The Circle
beats.modern: three circles, three colours, one space. the second reflected off the first like a rainbow off a rainbow, the third breathing out of both. and inside the middle one I saw OUR FACE. a human face, painted in that light. I stared at it like a geometer trying to square the circle who cannot find the one principle he needs. my wings weren't built for it. then a flash went through my mind and handed me the thing.

beats.title: gg
beats.modern: my imagination tapped out right there. couldn't render it. but my wanting kept turning anyway, smooth, like a wheel that's already balanced, and something else was doing the turning. same thing that turns the sun. same thing that turns every star. stream's over, chat. that's the whole map, bottom to top.
beats.quote: That moves the sun in heav’n and all the stars.

beats.title: Woke Up As A Bug
beats.modern: chat. I woke up and I'm a bug. not a mood, not a metaphor. armour plate back, brown belly with ridges across it, about forty legs waving around doing their own thing. and my brain's first move is to check the room. same walls. same fabric samples on the table. it's not a dream. cool. cool cool cool.
beats.quote: “What’s happened to me?”

beats.title: It Can All Go To Hell
beats.modern: let me tell you about my job. trains at five, hotels, food that hates me, a new city every week so I never get an actual friend. my boss sits UP on a raised desk and talks down at me because he's hard of hearing. five more years and my parents' debt to him is cleared and then I quit so hard he falls off it. anyway. train's at five.
beats.quote: It can all go to Hell!”

beats.title: My Voice Isn't Mine
beats.modern: mom knocks. asks if I wasn't going somewhere. I say yes mom, thank you, getting up now. except something else says it with me. there's a squeak riding under every word like a second thing is using my throat. and she just accepts it and shuffles off. she couldn't hear it, chat. I could.
beats.quote: “Yes, mother, yes, thank-you, I’m getting up now.”

beats.title: They Sent Management
beats.modern: doorbell. it's not a trainee. it's not a phone call. it is the CHIEF CLERK, in person, at my house, because I missed one train after five years of never being sick once. I get so mad thinking about it that I fling myself out of bed on pure spite. thud. bang my head. worth it.

beats.title: Astonished, Quite Astonished
beats.modern: and now he's doing the manager voice through my bedroom door. my numbers are down. my position isn't secure. there's a little hint about money I was trusted with, said loud enough for my PARENTS to hear. bro I have an exoskeleton. I'm getting a performance review through a locked door from a man who has never once considered that a person could simply become a bug.
beats.quote: I am astonished, quite astonished.

beats.title: The Voice Of An Animal
beats.modern: so I go all in through the door. just a dizzy spell sir, I'll be on the eight o'clock train, please put in a good word with the boss, please don't make my parents suffer. cleanest grovel I have ever delivered. and out in the hall he says it flat: that was the voice of an animal. mom starts screaming for a doctor. dad screams for a locksmith. not one word landed.
beats.quote: “That was the voice of an animal”,

beats.title: Opening The Door With My Face
beats.modern: no hands, so the key gets turned with my mouth. no teeth either, just jaw, so I hang my entire body weight off it and chew until the lock gives. brown stuff running out of me down the door. nobody out there is saying keep going, Gregor. I wanted one voice. one well done. did it anyway.
beats.quote: “So, I didn’t need the locksmith after all”.

beats.title: The Reveal
beats.modern: door swings open. the chief clerk says oh and starts walking backwards like something invisible is dragging him out. mom takes two steps toward me and folds straight down onto the floor into her skirts. dad makes fists like he wants to punch me back into the room, then covers his eyes and cries so hard his chest shakes. nobody says my name.

beats.title: Driven Back With A Stick
beats.modern: dad grabs the clerk's walking stick and a newspaper and starts herding me. hissing at me. actual hissing, like I'm a stray in the yard. I can't do reverse, and I'm too wide for the doorway, so one side of me scrapes open and leaves brown streaks on the white paint. then he SHOVES. I go flying in, bleeding. door slams. quiet. day one of the new me.

beats.title: Milk Doesn't Work Anymore
beats.modern: wake up in the dark and there's a bowl by the door. sweet milk with bread floating in it, my favourite thing since I was a kid. she remembered. I put my whole face in it and... nothing. it tastes like nothing I want. I crawl away from the only kind thing anyone did today, because my mouth isn't mine now.

beats.title: The Sample Platter
beats.modern: my sister comes back with a newspaper laid out with options. half rotten vegetables. old bones in sauce gone hard. cheese I personally called inedible two days ago. she's testing what I eat now, like I'm a new pet. and chat, I went for the rotten cheese FIRST. eyes watering. sucking it down. genuinely the best meal of my life.
beats.quote: “Am I less sensitive than I used to be, then?”,

beats.title: They Had Savings
beats.modern: pressed against the door listening to dad walk them through the finances and. chat. there's money. there's been money this whole time, sitting quiet, earning interest, plus a chunk of everything I ever handed over. five years of trains and hotel beds and that boss, for a debt that could have been gone sooner. and I'm behind the door nodding along. proud of them.

beats.title: Ceiling Guy
beats.modern: discovered I can hang upside down off the ceiling. it's better up there. body swings a little, breathing's easier, and sometimes I just let go for fun and hit the floor and nothing breaks. free. actually free. took becoming a bug to get a hobby.

beats.title: When Gregor Comes Back
beats.modern: they're clearing the furniture out so I get more room to crawl, and I'm honestly into it, until mom whispers the thing. leave the room exactly how it was. so when Gregor comes back to us he'll find everything unchanged. she still thinks I'm coming back. that one sentence is what reminded me I used to be a person.
beats.quote: I think it’d be best to leave the room exactly the way it was before

beats.title: Not The Picture
beats.modern: they're taking everything, so I pick one thing to save: the picture of the lady in the fur. climb up, press my whole body flat on the glass. nobody is getting this one. then mom walks back in, sees a huge brown patch on the wallpaper, and screams oh God oh God before her brain even reaches my name. out cold on the couch. grete shakes a fist at me. first thing she's said straight to me since it happened.
beats.quote: “Oh God, oh God!”

beats.title: The Apple
beats.modern: my dad has a JOB now. blue uniform, gold buttons, standing up straight. this is not the man who couldn't get out of his armchair to greet me. he chases me round the room, then starts throwing apples. actual apples out of the fruit bowl, no aim, and one lands IN my back and stays there. can't move. last thing I see is mom running at him with her skirts sliding off her, begging him not to kill me.
beats.quote: It was an apple; then another one immediately flew at him;

beats.title: The Old Dung Beetle
beats.modern: new cleaning lady, and she's the only person in this flat who isn't scared of me. cracks my door twice a day purely to greet the old dung beetle. one morning I go at her out of spite and she picks up a CHAIR, holds it over me, mouth open, waiting. not coming any closer then? then puts it back in the corner. respectfully, she'd win.
beats.quote: “come on then, you old dung-beetle!”,

beats.title: And Here I Am, Dying
beats.modern: we rent rooms out now. three bearded men eat at MY table, in the spot where I used to sit with my parents, and the only thing I can hear over the entire meal is teeth. chewing. that's the whole sound. you need teeth to eat. I've got jaws that hold nothing.
beats.quote: And here I am, dying!”

beats.title: Was I Ever An Animal
beats.modern: my sister is playing violin for the tenants and they're BORED, hands in pockets, blowing smoke at the ceiling, and she's playing beautifully with her face tilted into it. and I'm crawling out onto the clean floor covered in dust and hair and old food because I have to be closer to it. chat, if music does this to me, what am I? first thing that's fed me in months.
beats.quote: Was he an animal if music could captivate him so?

beats.title: The Tenants See Me
beats.modern: middle tenant just points. no words, one finger, at me. and my dad's first instinct is to protect THEM, arms spread, walking three grown men backwards while blocking their view of his own son. the guy stamps his foot, gives notice on the spot, mentions damages given the conditions in this flat. the other two: and we also give immediate notice. door slam. we lost the rent because I wanted to hear my sister play.
beats.quote: “And we also give immediate notice.”

beats.title: It's Got To Go
beats.modern: my sister is at that table calling me it. get rid of the idea that that's Gregor. if it were Gregor he'd have worked out long ago that people can't live with an animal, and he'd have left on his own. we'd have no brother but we could remember him with respect. dad is nodding. chat, she's the one who brought me the cheese.
beats.quote: You’ve got to get rid of the idea that that’s Gregor.

beats.title: At Last
beats.modern: so I turn around. takes everything I've got left, knocking my head against the floor to help me pivot, and for once nobody's rushing me. I crawl the whole distance back to my room and there's not one sound behind me. last look: mom's fallen asleep. and the second I'm through the doorway it slams, bolts, locks, and I hear her say it to them. at last. she'd been standing there waiting.
beats.quote: “At last!”.

beats.title: Three In The Morning
beats.modern: chat I can't move anymore and honestly it's alright. the pain is fading out. can't even feel the rotten apple in my back now. I'm thinking about my family and it's all love, no anger, none of it, and I agree with her. I should go. I want it more than she does. clock tower strikes three. sky starts going light outside the window.
beats.quote: If it was possible, he felt that he must go away even more strongly than his sister.

beats.title: Stone Dead
beats.modern: the cleaner pokes the body with a broom, finds it slides across the floor with no resistance at all, and yells into the bedrooms that it's dead, just lying there. dad crosses himself and says let's give thanks to God for that. all three of them copy him. then grete looks down and says just look how thin he was, he hadn't eaten in so long. that's the eulogy. that's the entire eulogy.
beats.quote: “Just look how thin he was. He didn’t eat anything for so long.

beats.title: The Tram Ride
beats.modern: and then the three of them take a tram out to the country. first day out together in months, whole carriage to themselves, warm sun. they compare jobs and discover all three are doing well with real prospects. first item on the list: move somewhere smaller and cheaper than the flat I picked for them. then mom and dad watch grete stretch in her seat and think, she's turned out beautiful, time to find her a husband. that's the ending. it's theirs.

beats.title: All Children Except One
beats.modern: every kid on this server grows up. it's a forced patch, no opt-out. Wendy figured out hers when she was two, holding a flower, and her mum said oh why can't you stay like this. that's the moment the timer starts for you people. two is the beginning of the end. anyway chat. I found the exploit.

beats.title: The Shadow Incident
beats.modern: so the mother screams, and the family DOG comes at me, and I bail out the window. chat. the dog got my shadow. window slammed on it, clean amputation, dog's standing there holding my shadow in her mouth like a sock. she hung it out the window for me. very polite. the mum rolled it up and put it in a drawer.

beats.title: Crying On Her Floor
beats.modern: update: shadows do not reattach. I tried SOAP. then I sat down on a stranger's nursery floor and cried, which I have never done and did not do. and the girl in the bed sits up, completely unbothered by the intruder sobbing on her carpet, and goes: boy, why are you crying? so I stood up and bowed. manners, chat.
beats.quote: “Boy,” she said courteously, “why are you crying?”

beats.title: Second To The Right
beats.modern: she gives me the full government name. Wendy Moira Angela Darling. I say Peter Pan and she goes "is that ALL?" ...it is now. thanks. then she asks my address so I said second to the right and straight on till morning, and she said what a funny address, and for one second, chat, I thought maybe it IS a funny address. she asked what they put on the letters. I don't get letters.
beats.quote: “Second to the right,” said Peter, “and then straight on till morning.”

beats.title: The Cleverness Of Me
beats.modern: she sewed my shadow back onto my foot with an actual needle. said it might hurt. didn't cry, never cry, don't have the feature. and then I looked down at that shadow behaving perfectly and I said it out loud to the whole room: how clever I am. oh, the cleverness of me. she pointed out she did it. she did a LITTLE of it.
beats.quote: “How clever I am!” he crowed rapturously, “oh, the cleverness of me!”

beats.title: Ran Away Day One
beats.modern: she asked how old I am. don't know. don't track it. what I do know is I heard my parents talking about what I'd be when I was a MAN. so I ran away the day I was born. day one. uninstalled before the tutorial. went and lived in the gardens with the fairies instead. I don't want ever to be a man, chat, and I'm not going to be.
beats.quote: “I don’t want ever to be a man,” he said with passion.

beats.title: Fairy Patch Notes
beats.modern: fairy lore for the new viewers: the first time a baby ever laughed, the laugh broke into a thousand pieces, and that's fairies. also, every time a kid says "I don't believe in fairies" one of them drops dead somewhere. that's a real mechanic. remember it. anyway I couldn't find Tink for ten minutes and it turns out I shut her in the drawer.
beats.quote: every time a child says, ‘I don’t believe in fairies,’ there is a fairy somewhere that falls down dead.”

beats.title: The Recruitment Pitch
beats.modern: closing her now, chat, watch the pitch. you could be flying instead of lying in a silly bed. there are MERMAIDS. we'd all respect you so much. you could tuck us in at night, nobody has ever tucked us in. you could darn our clothes and make us pockets, we don't have pockets. ...her arms went out. she's coming.

beats.title: Lovely Wonderful Thoughts
beats.modern: flight tutorial: think lovely wonderful thoughts. that's the whole guide. (I did not mention the fairy dust. you need the dust. I had dust on my hand the entire time and let them faceplant off the beds for a while first.) little one lets go, screams "I FLEWED," now all three are bonking their heads on the ceiling. heavenly, she called it.

beats.title: Just Say I'm Wendy
beats.modern: she's worried out loud that I'll forget her, since I forget mermaids by the time I land. fair. so I gave her the fix: if you ever see me forgetting you, just keep saying "I'm Wendy" and then I'll remember. chat I thought that was a great fix. she did not look like she thought it was a great fix.

beats.title: I Cut Off A Bit
beats.modern: they asked who runs the pirates now. Hook. yeah, that Hook. is he big? not as big as he was. I cut off a bit of him. the right hand. flung it to a crocodile that happened to be swimming past, and the croc liked it so much it has followed him from sea to sea ever since, waiting on the rest of him. he's got an iron claw now. house rule: if we meet him in open fight, he's MINE.
beats.quote: “I cut off a bit of him.”

beats.title: Shoot The Wendy
beats.modern: I get separated for five minutes, chat. FIVE. and Tink tells the boys that I want them to shoot the big white bird coming in over the trees. and they believe it, because I'm captain and nobody on this island questions the captain. Tootles has a bow. Tootles fires. the girl I brought home for them comes down out of the sky with an arrow in her chest.

beats.title: Why Do You Not Cheer
beats.modern: I land in front of my whole crew crowing and NOBODY cheers. I said it out loud: I am back, why do you not cheer. then they stood back and let me see. Tootles goes on his knees, bares his chest, tells me to strike true. I raised that arrow twice and something stopped my hand both times. and then her arm moves. the arrow hit the acorn button I gave her, the one she wore on a chain. my kiss stopped it. she's alive.
beats.quote: “I am back,” he said hotly, “why do you not cheer?”

beats.title: Be Our Mother
beats.modern: so we built a house around her while she was unconscious. red walls, moss roof, a hat knocked out for a chimney, sole of a shoe for a knocker. I told the boys look your best, first impressions are awfully important. then I knocked politely on the door of the house we had built around a girl, and all of us went down on our knees and asked her to be our mother. she said yes. we have a mother now, chat.

beats.title: Doing The Voice
beats.modern: pirates rowing a tied-up prisoner out to the drowning rock. easy play: wait for them to leave. instead I did Hook's voice. "set her free." but captain— "at once, d'ye hear, or I'll plunge my hook in you." they cut her loose and she slid between Starkey's legs into the water like an eel. flawless. no notes. am I not a wonder.

beats.title: I Am Peter Pan
beats.modern: then the real Hook starts a guessing game with the mystery voice in the dark, and chat, I have never once resisted a game. animal? yes. man? NO. boy? yes. ordinary boy? absolutely not. wonderful boy? ...yes. and then he says do you give it up, and I shouted "well then, I am Peter Pan." gave them my name. in the water. surrounded. take him dead or alive, he says.

beats.title: He Bit Me
beats.modern: I'm on the rock with his own knife, about to finish it, and I stop. because I'm higher up than him and that isn't fair fighting. so I gave him a hand up. and he BIT me. not the pain, chat. the unfairness. it just deleted my brain, I stood there staring like an NPC while the iron hand went through me. twice.

beats.title: An Awfully Big Adventure
beats.modern: tide's coming up over the rock. she can't swim, I can't fly, he clawed me twice. one kite floats past and it lifts one person. she wanted to draw lots for it. no. and you a lady, never. tied it round her, said good-bye Wendy, and pushed her off the rock. water at my feet now. mermaids calling to the moon. and honestly chat? to die will be an awfully big adventure.
beats.quote: “To die will be an awfully big adventure.”

beats.title: A Devoted Son
beats.modern: she asked me what my exact feelings toward her are. I said: those of a devoted son. she said "I thought so" and got up and went and sat by herself at the far end of the room. right before that I had checked with her that it's still only make-believe that I'm their father, and when she said yes I heard myself sigh with relief. she heard it too.
beats.quote: “Those of a devoted son, Wendy.”

beats.title: The Window Was Barred
beats.modern: she's telling my boys that mothers always leave the window open, love conquers all, fly home whenever. so I groaned out loud and told them the truth. I stayed away for moons and moons and moons believing exactly that. then I flew home. the window was BARRED. she'd forgotten all about me. there was another little boy asleep in my bed.

beats.title: I'm Not Coming
beats.modern: so they're all leaving. fine. I skipped up and down the room playing my pipes so she could see exactly how unmoved I am. she keeps saying come with us, find your mother. no. maybe that one would look at me and say I was old too. I just want always to be a little boy and to have fun. that's the entire build, chat. not respeccing.

beats.title: I Taught Them The Signal
beats.modern: I told the kids the signal: if our side wins up top, they beat the tom-tom. said it out loud, underground, with a pirate crouched at the mouth of every single tree. so Hook has Smee beat the tom-tom. I hear it and I shout VICTORY, and my whole crew climbs up the trees cheering, one at a time, into their hands. I gave them the signal, chat.

beats.title: Five Drops
beats.modern: and I slept through it. all of them taken, and I'm face up on the bed with my mouth open. Hook came down MY tree, saw the medicine she left out for me, and put in five drops of a poison he blended himself out of every ring he'd ever taken off a dead man. then he stood there and had one long gloating look at me and wormed back up the tree.

beats.title: She Drank It
beats.modern: Tink's screaming that the cup is poisoned. I said don't be silly, how would Hook get down here, besides I never fell asleep. I raised it. and she got between my lips and the cup and drank the whole thing. "it was poisoned, Peter, and now I am going to be dead." she landed on my shoulder, bit my nose, whispered you silly ass, and went to lie down in her little room.
beats.quote: “It was poisoned, Peter,” she told him softly; “and now I am going to be dead.”

beats.title: Clap Your Hands
beats.modern: her light is going out, chat. she says she could get well if children believed in fairies. so I'm asking everyone. everyone dreaming of this place, everyone in their nighties, everyone listening right now: IF YOU BELIEVE, CLAP YOUR HANDS. DON'T LET TINK DIE. ...many clapped. some didn't. and some of you HISSED. she's up. she's flying. we're going to talk about the hissing later.
beats.quote: “If you believe,” he shouted to them, “clap your hands; don’t let Tink die.”

beats.title: Hook Or Me This Time
beats.modern: moving alone now. snow's covered every footprint, the whole island has gone dead quiet, everyone I have is on that ship. only thing that passed me was the crocodile. so I swore it out loud where the trees could hear: Hook or me this time. crawling like a snake, finger on my lip, dagger ready. chat I have never been happier in my life.
beats.quote: “Hook or me this time.”

beats.title: Not The Crocodile
beats.modern: whole deck hears ticking and Hook just comes apart, clipped at every joint, crawling across his own ship on his knees begging his crew to HIDE him. they all turn their faces away from the rail because they think it's Fate coming aboard. it is not Fate. it's me. I'd been ticking for an hour and forgot I was doing it. don't cheer, don't cheer, I'm signing at them, do NOT cheer.

beats.title: Peter Pan The Avenger
beats.modern: Hook decides the ship's bad luck is the girl and tells them to throw her overboard. except she's hidden with the others and I'm the one at the mast in her cloak. "there's none can save you now, missy." there's one. "who's that?" PETER PAN THE AVENGER. cloak off. he tried twice to speak and couldn't, chat. I watched his heart break in real time.
beats.quote: “Peter Pan the avenger!”

beats.title: I'm Youth, I'm Joy
beats.modern: mid-duel he stops and asks what I actually am. Pan, who and what art thou. so I said the first thing in my head: I'm youth, I'm joy, I'm a little bird that has broken out of the egg. total nonsense, chat, I made it up on the spot. and it wrecked him. because it proved I don't know what I am, and apparently not knowing is the highest form there is.
beats.quote: “I’m youth, I’m joy,” Peter answered at a venture, “I’m a little bird that has broken out of the egg.”

beats.title: Bad Form
beats.modern: he lit his own powder magazine to take the ship with us. I walked in, picked up the shell, threw it in the sea. so he climbs the rail to jump, looks back at me coming through the air, and gestures at me to use my foot. so I kicked him. that's what he wanted, chat, that was his last win. "bad form," he says, and goes content to the crocodile.
beats.quote: “Bad form,” he cried jeeringly, and went content to the crocodile.

beats.title: Two Tears
beats.modern: flew ahead of them and barred her window so she'd think her mother had locked her out and come back to me forever. good plan. flawless plan. then I peeped in and there's the lady at the piano with two tears just sitting on her eyes. I'm fond of her too, lady. we can't both have her. she wouldn't make the best of it, and even when I stopped looking she was inside me, knocking. ...fine. I unbarred it.
beats.quote: “I’m fond of her too. We can’t both have her, lady.”

beats.title: The One Joy
beats.modern: she got them back. all three of them out of the beds and into her arms, dad awake, dog running in, everyone crying at once. nobody in that room looked at the window. I've had a hundred thousand things those kids will never have, chat. that one's barred to me forever.

beats.title: Who Is Captain Hook
beats.modern: she came back for spring cleaning and started talking about the arch enemy, so I asked: who is Captain Hook? she goes, you KILLED him, you saved all our lives. yeah I forget them after I kill them. then she got excited about Tinker Bell and I had to ask who that was. there's such a lot of them. I expect she's no more.
beats.quote: “I forget them after I kill them,” he replied carelessly.

beats.title: I Am Old, Peter
beats.modern: came for spring cleaning and she wouldn't turn the light on. chat, I was afraid. actually afraid, first time I can remember. don't turn up the light, I said. she turned it up. "I am old, Peter. I am ever so much more than twenty. I grew up long ago." you PROMISED not to. she said she couldn't help it. she's married.
beats.quote: “I am old, Peter. I am ever so much more than twenty. I grew up long ago.”

beats.title: Boy, Why Are You Crying
beats.modern: so I'm sitting on the floor of that same nursery crying, and my sobs wake the kid in the bed. she sits up. and she says: boy, why are you crying? chat. CHAT. same room. same words. I stood up and bowed and she bowed back from the bed. I said my name is Peter Pan and she said yes, I know. I have been waiting for you.
beats.quote: “Boy,” she said, “why are you crying?”

beats.title: Gay And Innocent And Heartless
beats.modern: and off we went, the new one flying better on night one than her mother ever managed. the mother stayed at the window watching us shrink to the size of stars. this one will grow up too. then it's her daughter. then hers. and it goes on forever, chat, so long as children are gay and innocent and heartless. stream never ends. I just get new chat.
beats.quote: so long as children are gay and innocent and heartless.

walden.title: Walden, and On The Duty Of Civil Disobedience
walden.author: Henry David Thoreau

beats.title: Quiet Desperation
beats.modern: chat I have to say the quiet part. most of you are not fine. you are not even sad. you are RESIGNED, and resignation is just despair that stopped filing complaints. and no, the hobbies don't count. there's no play in them because they come AFTER work. that's not fun, that's recovery.
beats.quote: The mass of men lead lives of quiet desperation.

beats.title: The Inherited Farm Debuff
beats.modern: everybody congratulates the guys who inherited farms, barns, cattle, tools. that is a DEBUFF. you can acquire that stuff so much easier than you can get rid of it. bro is pushing a seventy-five-foot barn down the road of life like a boulder, stables never cleaned, hundred acres strapped to his back. the guy who inherited nothing has exactly one job: cultivate the few cubic feet of flesh he's standing in.

beats.title: Another Mans Brass
beats.modern: some of you reading this cannot pay for dinners you have already eaten. you're on this page spending borrowed time, robbing your creditors of an hour. the Romans called debt aes alienum, another man's brass. you are living inside somebody else's metal. always promising to pay tomorrow, dying today. and the loop is: make yourself sick earning money to have on hand for the day you get sick.

beats.title: The Overseer Is Inside
beats.modern: hard to have a boss over you. worse to have a subtler one. worst of all when the slave driver is YOU. public opinion is a weak little tyrant compared to the opinion you hold of yourself at 3am. and that private opinion is not describing your fate. it is WRITING it.
beats.quote: Public opinion is a weak tyrant compared with our own private opinion.

beats.title: The Elders Have Nothing
beats.modern: I am thirty years old and I have never once heard a useful syllable from anyone older than me. not one. they tell you what can't be done, you go do it. their experience was partial. their lives were, by their own private admission, kind of a wash. life is an untried experiment for ME. it does not help me one bit that they ran it.

beats.title: Ask The Bank Who Owns It
beats.modern: asked the town assessor how many people here actually own their farm, no debt. he could not name twelve. I doubt there are three. want the real history of any house in Concord? don't ask the family, ask the bank holding the mortgage. ninety-seven merchants in a hundred fail. this entire civilization is doing tricks off a bankruptcy springboard.

beats.title: Tools Of Their Tools
beats.modern: we used to camp. tent in the world, moving through it. then the guy who picked fruit when he was hungry became a farmer, and the guy who stood under a tree became a homeowner, and now look: men have become the tools of their tools. we stopped camping for the night and settled down and forgot heaven. built a mansion for this world and a tomb for the next. two houses. neither one you can walk out of.
beats.quote: But lo! men have become the tools of their tools.

beats.title: Twenty-Eight Dollars Twelve Cents
beats.modern: full build cost, because nobody ever posts it. boards 8.03. refuse shingles 4.00. laths 1.25. two secondhand windows 2.43. a thousand old bricks 4.00. two casks of lime 2.40, that was high. hair 0.31, more than I needed. nails 3.90. chalk one cent. transport 1.40, I carried most of it on my back. total twenty-eight dollars and twelve and a half cents.
beats.quote: I intend to build me a house which will surpass any on the main street in Concord in grandeur and luxury,

beats.title: The Cost Of A Thing
beats.modern: here is the only price tag that means anything. the cost of a thing is how much LIFE you hand over for it. house around here runs eight hundred dollars. labor pays a dollar a day. that is ten to fifteen years, and that's if nobody's depending on you. you spend more than half your life before the shelter is yours. now explain to me again how this is the upgrade.
beats.quote: the cost of a thing is the amount of what I will call life which is required to be exchanged for it, immediately or in the long run.

beats.title: Enterprises That Require New Clothes
beats.modern: beware of any project that requires new clothes instead of a new wearer of them. if there is no new man, how exactly do you expect the new fit to work? got a big plan? run it in the old jacket first. people don't want something to do WITH. they want something to DO. actually they want something to BE.
beats.quote: beware of all enterprises that require new clothes, and not rather a new wearer of clothes.

beats.title: The Head Monkey At Paris
beats.modern: asked my tailor for a specific cut. she says, totally deadpan, "they do not make them so now." not emphasizing the THEY at all. like she's quoting the Fates. who are They. what is their jurisdiction over my shoulders. we do not worship the Graces, we worship Fashion, and the head monkey in Paris puts on a cap and every monkey in America puts on the cap.

beats.title: The Toolbox Apartment
beats.modern: there's a box by the railroad where the crew locks their tools. six feet by three. costs about a dollar. drill some air holes, hook the lid down at night, and congratulations: no landlord, no rent, stay up as late as you want, wake up and just go. I am not joking. plenty of men are being harassed to death paying for a bigger box who would never have frozen in this one.

beats.title: I Ate Eight Dollars
beats.modern: eight months of food: eight dollars and seventy-four cents. rice, molasses, rye meal, corn meal, twenty-two cents of pork. separate column for FAILED EXPERIMENTS: flour, sugar, lard, apples, one pumpkin six cents, one watermelon two cents. I'm publishing my guilt only because yours would look worse in print. also I ate a woodchuck once, for research. musky. would not run it back.

beats.title: Forty Days A Year
beats.modern: day labor is the freest job that exists. thirty or forty days a year funds an entire life. sun goes down, you are DONE, the rest belongs to you. meanwhile your employer is speculating month to month with no off switch from January to January. keeping yourself alive on this planet is not a hardship, it is a pastime, if you'd stop buying things. nobody has to earn bread by the sweat of his brow unless he sweats easier than I do.

beats.title: I Bought Every Farm In My Head
beats.modern: I have bought every farm within twelve miles. in my head. walked the property, tasted the wild apples, talked husbandry with the owner, took his price, mortgaged it mentally, enjoyed it a while, then handed it back and let him carry it on. my friends think I'm a real estate broker. wherever I sit, the landscape radiates out from me. a man is rich in proportion to the number of things he can afford to leave alone.

beats.title: Why I Moved Out
beats.modern: moved to the woods for exactly one reason: to see the actual game instead of the tutorial. I did not want to hit the death screen and discover I never played. wanted to live DEEP. drive life into a corner, reduce it to lowest terms. and if it turned out to be cheap, fine, I'd get the whole genuine cheapness of it and publish it. if it turned out sublime, I'd know firsthand.
beats.quote: I went to the woods because I wished to live deliberately, to front only the essential facts of life, and see if I could not learn what it had to teach,

beats.title: Simplicity Simplicity Simplicity
beats.modern: your life is being frittered away by DETAIL. an honest man barely needs to count past ten fingers, twenty in a real emergency, lump the rest. simplicity. simplicity. SIMPLICITY. two or three affairs, not a thousand. keep the accounts on your thumbnail. three meals a day? eat one. hundred dishes? five. scale everything else to match.
beats.quote: Simplicity, simplicity, simplicity! I say, let your affairs be as two or three, and not a hundred or a thousand;

beats.title: Morning Is When I Am Awake
beats.modern: morning is not a time. the clock does not get a vote. morning is when I am awake and there is a dawn IN me. millions are awake enough for physical labor. one in a million is awake enough to actually think. one in a hundred million for anything divine. I have never yet met a man who was fully awake. how would I even look him in the face.
beats.quote: Morning is when I am awake and there is a dawn in me.

beats.title: The Highest Of Arts
beats.modern: most encouraging fact I know: a person can raise his own life on purpose. anybody can paint a picture or carve a statue and make two or three objects beautiful. it is far rarer to paint the AIR you are looking through. to affect the quality of the day. that is the highest art there is and it has no gallery and nobody claps.
beats.quote: To affect the quality of the day, that is the highest of arts.

beats.title: The Realometer
beats.modern: wedge your feet downward. through the mud and slush of opinion and prejudice and tradition and delusion and appearance. through Paris and London, through New York and Boston and Concord, through church and state and poetry and philosophy and religion. keep going until you hit rock and can say THIS IS, no mistake. then set a gauge there. not a Nilometer. a Realometer. so future ages can read how deep the flood of shams got.

beats.title: Time Is A Stream
beats.modern: time is just the stream I go fishing in. I drink from it, and while I'm drinking I can see the sandy bottom and how SHALLOW it is. the thin current slides off. eternity stays. I want to drink deeper. fish in the sky, where the bottom is pebbly with stars. I cannot count one of them. I do not know the first letter of the alphabet. I have spent my whole life regretting I am not as wise as I was the day I was born.
beats.quote: Time is but the stream I go a-fishing in.

beats.title: A Broad Margin
beats.modern: did not read a single book my first summer. hoed beans. often did better than that: sat in the sunny doorway from sunrise to noon doing absolutely nothing, birds flying silently through the house, until the sun hit the west window and told me hours were gone. I love a broad margin to my life. I grew in those stretches like corn at night. that was not time subtracted. that was EXTRA.
beats.quote: I love a broad margin to my life.

beats.title: No Companion So Companionable
beats.modern: it is healthy to be alone most of the time. company, even good company, gets tiring fast. I have never found a companion as companionable as solitude. and honestly you are lonelier out among people than you ever are in your own room. a man thinking or working is alone wherever he happens to be standing.
beats.quote: I never found the companion that was so companionable as solitude.

beats.title: Society Is Too Cheap
beats.modern: society is commonly too CHEAP. we meet at such short intervals that nobody has time to become worth anything to anyone. three meals a day handing each other another taste of the same musty cheese we already are. we invented etiquette purely so this can happen daily without open war. we live thick, we trip over each other, and I think we lose respect that way. a man's value is not in his skin. you do not have to touch him.
beats.quote: Society is commonly too cheap.

beats.title: Three Chairs
beats.modern: three chairs in this house. one for solitude, two for friendship, three for society. bigger crowd shows up, there's still only the third chair, so they stand, and it works. I have had twenty-five or thirty souls in here at once, bodies included. it is genuinely shocking how many great people a small house holds.
beats.quote: I had three chairs in my house; one for solitude, two for friendship, three for society.

beats.title: The Rain Fixed It
beats.modern: I have felt lonely exactly once. a few weeks in, for about an hour, I seriously wondered if being near people was required to stay sane. I could feel it was a slight insanity in the mood and I could feel the recovery coming. then a gentle rain started, and every single drop of it was company. every pine needle swelled with sympathy. an unaccountable friendliness holding me up like an atmosphere. no place has been strange to me since.

beats.title: Earths Eye
beats.modern: a lake is the best feature any landscape has. it is earth's EYE. you look into it and what you are actually measuring is how deep you go. the trees along the shore are the lashes. the wooded hills and cliffs behind them are the brow. it has been looking back this whole time.
beats.quote: It is earth’s eye; looking into which the beholder measures the depth of his own nature.

beats.title: The Ganges In My Well
beats.modern: morning routine: bathe my brain in the Bhagavad Gita, next to which our entire modern world and all its literature reads like a group chat. then I put the book down and walk out to my well for water and meet the servant of a Brahmin priest who is still sitting on the Ganges reading the Vedas. our buckets grate together in the same well. Walden water, Ganges water. same well.

beats.title: Maine And Texas Have Nothing To Say
beats.modern: we are in a MASSIVE hurry to run a telegraph from Maine to Texas. Maine and Texas may have nothing to say to each other. it's the guy who begged to be introduced to a famous deaf woman, and then they put the ear trumpet in his hand and he had nothing. we're tunneling under the Atlantic to get the old world weeks closer, and the first thing through the wire will be that some princess has a cough.
beats.quote: We are in great haste to construct a magnetic telegraph from Maine to Texas; but Maine and Texas, it may be, have nothing important to communicate.

beats.title: It Rides Upon Us
beats.modern: we do not ride on the railroad. it rides upon US. have you ever thought about what the sleepers under the track actually are? each one is a man. rails laid across him, covered with sand, cars running smooth over the top. sound sleepers, I assure you. every few years a fresh lot goes down and gets run over too. some have the pleasure of riding on a rail. others have the misfortune of being ridden upon.
beats.quote: We do not ride on the railroad; it rides upon us.

beats.title: Whats The News
beats.modern: man cannot nap thirty minutes after dinner without waking up and going "what's the news?" like the rest of humanity was standing sentry for him. some ask to be woken every half hour purely for this. then he reads over coffee that somebody had his eyes gouged out on a river three states away, never once considering that he himself lives in a dark unfathomed cave and has barely the rudiment of an eye.

beats.title: Running The Gauntlet
beats.modern: the vital organs of a village: the grocery, the bar, the post office, the bank. plus the necessary machinery, a bell, a big gun, and a fire engine. and the houses are laid out in lanes facing each other so every traveller has to run the GAUNTLET and every man, woman and child gets a lick in. the spots at the head of the line, where you can see and be seen and land the first blow, cost the most rent. obviously.

beats.title: That Government Is Best
beats.modern: the motto is "that government is best which governs least" and I heartily accept it, and I would like to see it actually applied, because carried all the way out it lands on "that government is best which governs not at all," which is the government men will get the moment they're ready for it. government is an expedient. most are usually inconvenient and all of them are sometimes.
beats.quote: motto,—“That government is best which governs least;”

beats.title: Men First Subjects After
beats.modern: does a citizen have to hand his conscience over to the legislature, even for a second? then why does he have one. we should be men FIRST and subjects after. do not cultivate a respect for the law, cultivate a respect for the right. law never made anybody one bit more just, and through their respect for it the well-meaning people get turned into the daily agents of injustice.
beats.quote: I think that we should be men first, and subjects afterward.

beats.title: Small Movable Forts
beats.modern: watch a whole file of them march over hill and dale to a war. colonel, captain, corporal, privates, powder monkeys, all of them. against their own will. against their common sense and their conscience. makes for very steep marching and a palpitating heart. they all know it's a damnable business, they are peaceable men. so what ARE they. men? or small movable forts at the disposal of some unscrupulous guy in power.

beats.title: Voting Is Gambling
beats.modern: voting is gambling. checkers with a moral tint. you play right and wrong for chips and betting follows naturally. the voter's own character is never on the table. I cast my vote for what I think is right and I am not actually staking anything on it, I am leaving it to the majority. even voting FOR the right does nothing for it. it just tells people, weakly, that you'd prefer it.
beats.quote: All voting is a sort of gaming, like chequers or backgammon, with a slight moral tinge to it,

beats.title: A Counter Friction
beats.modern: if the injustice is just the friction of the machine, let it go, it'll wear smooth, and anyway the machine wears out. but if the injustice has its own spring and pulley and crank built specifically for it, and it requires YOU to be the agent of harm to another person, then break the law. let your life be a counter friction to stop the machine. my whole job is to not lend myself to the wrong I condemn.
beats.quote: Let your life be a counter friction to stop the machine.

beats.title: One Night In Jail
beats.modern: have not paid the poll tax in six years. they put me in jail for a night. I stood there looking at two feet of stone and a foot of wood and iron, and the funny part is they genuinely thought my chief desire was to be on the other side of that wall. they locked the door on my meditations, which walked out anyway, and those were the only dangerous thing in the room. couldn't reach me, so they punished my body, like boys who can't get at a man kicking his dog instead. lost my last respect for the State that night. pitied it.
beats.quote: I saw that the State was half-witted, that it was timid as a lone woman with her silver spoons,

beats.title: The Huckleberry Party
beats.modern: got jailed on my way to pick up a mended shoe. let out the next morning, finished the errand, put the shoe on, joined a huckleberry party that had been waiting on me to lead it, and half an hour later I was standing in a berry field on one of our highest hills two miles out. and from up there, the State was nowhere to be seen.

beats.title: Explore Thyself
beats.modern: everybody wants to go chase a giraffe in southern Africa. that's not the game you're actually after. be the Lewis and Clark of your own streams. explore your own higher latitudes, bring preserved meat if you have to and stack the empty cans sky-high as a marker. be a Columbus to whole continents inside you, opening new channels, not of trade, of THOUGHT. every man is lord of a realm next to which the Czar's empire is a hummock the ice left behind.
beats.quote: be a Columbus to whole new continents and worlds within you, opening new channels, not of trade, but of thought.

beats.title: Foundations Under Them
beats.modern: here is what the experiment taught me. move confidently toward the thing you actually imagined and you will meet a success that does not happen in ordinary hours. you'll leave things behind, cross a boundary you can't see, and the rules start getting interpreted in your favor. simplify and the universe gets less complicated, and solitude stops being solitude and poverty stops being poverty. built castles in the air? GOOD. that is exactly where they belong. now put the foundations under them.
beats.quote: If you have built castles in the air, your work need not be lost; that is where they should be. Now put the foundations under them.

beats.title: A Different Drummer
beats.modern: why are we in such desperate haste to succeed, and at such desperate things. if somebody isn't keeping pace with the group, maybe he is hearing a different drummer. let him step to the music he actually hears, however slow it is, however far away. nobody is required to ripen on the same schedule as an apple tree.
beats.quote: If a man does not keep pace with his companions, perhaps it is because he hears a different drummer.

beats.title: Sell Your Clothes Keep Your Thoughts
beats.modern: however mean your life is, meet it and live it. do not shun it and call it hard names. it is not as bad as you are. it looks poorest when you are richest. the setting sun hits the poorhouse windows exactly as bright as the rich man's, and the snow melts at that door just as early in spring. cultivate poverty like a garden herb, like sage. don't chase new things, clothes or friends. turn the old ones. things do not change, WE change. sell your clothes and keep your thoughts.
beats.quote: Cultivate poverty like a garden herb, like sage.

beats.title: The Sun Is But A Morning Star
beats.modern: I am not saying you personally will get there. that is just the nature of a tomorrow that mere passing time can never make arrive. the light that puts out our eyes is darkness to us. only that day dawns to which we are awake. there is more day to dawn. the sun is but a morning star.
beats.quote: Only that day dawns to which we are awake. There is more day to dawn. The sun is but a morning star.

beats.title: Cheap Ancestral Halls
beats.modern: we got an entire colonial mansion for the summer, chat. ancestral halls. hedges, gates that lock, the works. rent was suspiciously cheap and nobody has lived here in YEARS. my husband says great deal. I say there is something queer about it. one of us is a doctor and one of us is right.

beats.title: He Doesn't Believe I'm Sick
beats.modern: my husband laughs at me. of course he does, that's marriage. here's the problem: he's a physician, I'm the patient, and his professional opinion is that nothing is wrong with me. chat. he does not believe I am sick. and he's the one writing the prescriptions.
beats.quote: John laughs at me, of course, but one expects that in marriage.

beats.title: The Prescription
beats.modern: official treatment plan: phosphates, tonics, air, exercise, and absolutely forbidden to work until I'm well. banned from my own job. personally I think work and a little excitement would fix me faster than any of this. nobody asked. my brother's also a doctor of high standing and he says the same thing. rigged panel.

beats.title: Writing In Secret
beats.modern: so I write anyway. it wipes me out, but not from the writing, from the sneaking. and he says the worst possible thing for my condition is thinking about my condition, which means I can't fix it and I can't mention it. fine. we'll talk about the house instead.

beats.title: He Shut The Window
beats.modern: told him one moonlit night that I could feel something strange in this house. he said what I felt was a draught. and then he closed the window. that's the entire marriage in one move, chat. I report a haunting, he adjusts the airflow.

beats.title: We Took The Nursery
beats.modern: I wanted the downstairs room with roses on the window. we're in the old nursery at the top of the house instead, because air. count the details with me: windows barred for little children. rings bolted into the walls. paint gouged, floor splintered. he says it's the best room in the house.

beats.title: I Never Saw A Worse Paper
beats.modern: the wallpaper. chat, I need you to understand this wallpaper. sprawling flamboyant pattern committing every artistic sin available. the lines wander a little and then destroy themselves, plunging off at outrageous angles. the color is a smouldering unclean yellow, lurid orange in spots, sickly sulphur in others. no wonder the children in here hated it.
beats.quote: I never saw a worse paper in my life.

beats.title: Blessed Little Goose
beats.modern: asked him to repaper the room. he said if he gave me that I'd move on to the bedstead, then the barred windows, then the gate at the top of the stairs, and he's not renovating a house for a three month rental. asked to move downstairs then. he called me a blessed little goose and offered to whitewash the cellar. denied, but affectionately.

beats.title: The Eyes Go All The Way Down
beats.modern: there's a spot where the pattern lolls over like a broken neck and two bulbous eyes stare at you upside down. they're everywhere. up, down, sideways, crawling. where two strips of paper didn't line up, the eyes run crooked down the whole seam, one a little higher than the other. and I'm supposed to be resting in here.

beats.title: There's Something Under It
beats.modern: update. there's a second pattern under the first one. a sub-pattern, different shade, and you can only catch it in certain lights and not clearly even then. something almost like a figure, sulking around back there behind the loud stupid front design. I see you.

beats.title: Escalation Threat
beats.modern: new terms: if I don't pick up faster he's sending me to a specialist in the fall. I knew a woman who went through that man's hands. she says he's exactly like my husband and my brother, only more so. meanwhile I cry at nothing, most of the day, and only ever when the room is empty.

beats.title: Pattern Gymnastics
beats.modern: the bed is nailed to the floor, so I lie on it and follow the pattern for hours. it's as good as gymnastics, honestly. no radiation, no symmetry, no law of any kind. the curves go waddling up and down in isolated columns of fatuity and then swerve into great slanting waves of optic horror, like seaweed in full chase. anyway. nap.

beats.title: Use Your Will
beats.modern: tried to have one real, earnest, reasonable conversation. just asked to visit my cousins. I was crying before I finished the sentence, so there goes my case. he carried me upstairs, laid me on the bed, read to me until my head hurt, called me his darling and his comfort. then told me nobody can help me but myself and I must use my will. that's the whole treatment.

beats.title: It's A Woman
beats.modern: the dim shapes behind the front pattern get clearer every day and chat, it's always the same shape. it's a woman. stooping down. creeping around back there. I don't like it a bit. I wonder. I begin to think. I wish John would take me away from here.

beats.title: Three Weeks More
beats.modern: woke him up and said it plainly: I'm not gaining here, take me away. he says the lease runs three more weeks, I'm gaining flesh and color, he's a doctor and he knows. I said I weigh less than when we came. he hugged me and said I could be as sick as I pleased. I started with better in body perhaps and the look on his face closed my mouth mid sentence.
beats.quote: “she shall be as sick as she pleases!

beats.title: At Night It Becomes Bars
beats.modern: here's the thing nobody else has noticed: the paper changes with the light. twilight, candlelight, lamplight, and worst of all moonlight, the front pattern becomes BARS. and the woman behind it is as plain as can be. by daylight she goes subdued and quiet. I think it's the pattern that keeps her so still.

beats.title: Caught Jennie With Her Hand On It
beats.modern: I'm getting a little afraid of John. he's been looking at the paper when he thinks I'm not watching. Jennie too, I caught her with her HAND on it. she jumped like she'd been caught stealing, then said the yellow stains everything and we should be more careful. innocent, right? she's studying my pattern. nobody finds it out but me.

beats.title: A Yellow Smell
beats.modern: the smell. it creeps all over the house. hovering in the dining room, skulking in the parlor, hiding in the hall, lying in wait for me on the stairs. it gets into my hair. I did seriously consider burning the house down to reach it. I'm used to it now. best description I've got: it smells like the color of the paper. a yellow smell.

beats.title: She Shakes The Bars
beats.modern: solved it, chat. the front pattern moves because SHE shakes it. sometimes there are a great many women back there, sometimes only one, and she crawls so fast the whole wall shivers. in the bright spots she holds still. in the shady spots she takes the bars and shakes them hard. she's always trying to climb through, and the pattern strangles whoever tries. that's why it has so many heads.

beats.title: Creeping By Daylight
beats.modern: she gets out in the daytime. I've seen her, out of every window in this room: creeping up and down the shaded lane, creeping through the grape arbors, and when a carriage comes she hides under the blackberry vines. I don't blame her. it must be very humiliating to be caught creeping by daylight. that's why I lock the door when I do it.

beats.title: The Last Night
beats.modern: last day and it's enough. John stays in town overnight. Jennie wanted to sleep in here, the sly thing, so I told her I'd rest better alone. clever of me, because I wasn't alone a bit. soon as the moonlight hit and that poor thing began to crawl and shake the pattern, I got up and ran to help her. I pulled and she shook. I shook and she pulled. yards of it came down before morning.

beats.title: Not Alive
beats.modern: Jennie stares at the wall and I tell her merrily I did it out of pure spite at the vicious thing. she laughs and says she wouldn't mind doing it herself. she BETRAYED herself right there, chat. she wants the paper. she tried to get me out of the room, far too obvious. but I'm here, and no person touches this paper but me. not alive.

beats.title: I Threw The Key Away
beats.modern: door locked. key thrown out into the front path. nobody comes in until John does, because I want to astonish him. also I have a rope up here that Jennie never found. if that woman gets out and tries to get away, I can tie her.

beats.title: The Bars Are Too Strong
beats.modern: the bed will not move. I tried to lift it until I was lame, then got angry and bit a piece off the corner, which hurt my teeth. I'm angry enough now to do something desperate. jumping out the window would be admirable exercise, but the bars are too strong to even try. besides I wouldn't. of course not. a step like that is improper and might be misconstrued.

beats.title: My Shoulder Fits The Smooch
beats.modern: it's so pleasant to be out in this great room and creep around as I please. I won't go outside. outside you creep on the ground and everything is green instead of yellow. in here I creep smooth along the floor, and my shoulder fits exactly into that long smudge worn around the wall, so I can never lose my way. chat. think about who wore that groove.

beats.title: I've Got Out At Last
beats.modern: there's John at the door. calling, pounding, crying for an axe. I tell him very gently that the key is down by the front steps under a plantain leaf, and I say it slowly, over and over, until he has to go and get it. he opens the door and stops dead. I keep creeping and look at him over my shoulder. and then the man faints, right across my path by the wall, so I have to creep over him every single time.
beats.quote: “I’ve got out at last,” said I, “in spite of you and Jane! And I’ve pulled off most of the paper, so you can’t put me back!”

around-the-world-in-eighty.title: Around the World in Eighty Days
around-the-world-in-eighty.author: Jules Verne

beats.title: Nothing Ever Happens Here
beats.modern: welcome back. today's content: I fired my valet. the shaving water arrived at 84 degrees. the standard is 86. two degrees. that is the entire incident. I don't travel, I don't have friends, I have a clock that displays the year and I watch it. mods, take the sub goal off screen, there is nothing to fund.

beats.title: You Are Four Minutes Slow
beats.modern: new hire walks in and lists the whole résumé: street singer, circus rider, gymnastics professor, Paris fireman. fine. I asked him the time. he is four minutes slow. told him so, hired him at 11:29 exactly, put my hat on and left. he came here for a quiet life, chat. he has no idea.
beats.quote: “You are four minutes too slow. No matter; it’s enough to mention the error.

beats.title: The Unforeseen Does Not Exist
beats.modern: club argument about where a bank robber could possibly hide. Stuart says the world is big. it isn't. it's eighty days now, rail and steamer, the paper printed the table. he said prove it. so: twenty thousand pounds, half of everything I own, train to Dover at 8:45 tonight. he listed storms, wrecks, delays, people pulling up the rails. all included.
beats.quote: “The unforeseen does not exist,”

beats.title: We Leave In Ten Minutes
beats.modern: walked home four hours early and told him we leave in ten minutes to go round the world. no trunks. one carpet bag, two shirts, three pairs of stockings each, we buy the rest on the way. his face did something I have never seen a face do. also there are twenty thousand pounds in the bag. he is carrying it.
beats.quote: “We’ll have no trunks; only a carpet-bag, with two shirts and three pairs of stockings for me, and the same for you.

beats.title: Somebody Left The Gas On
beats.modern: somewhere past Sydenham he lets out a cry like a wheel came off. it did not. he left the gas burning in his bedroom. eighty days of gas, lit, in an empty locked house. I told him it burns at his expense. remember this one, chat, it comes back at the end.
beats.quote: “To turn off the gas in my room!”

beats.title: Now I Am The Bank Robber
beats.modern: update from home: I am the man who robbed the Bank of England. some detective wired Scotland Yard from Suez asking for a warrant to meet me in Bombay. my odds went to two hundred to one against. one paralysed lord is still betting on me. that is the entire fanbase, chat. one man who cannot stand up.
beats.quote: I’ve found the bank robber, Phileas Fogg. Send without delay warrant of arrest to Bombay.

beats.title: So Much The Worse For The Sun
beats.modern: someone finally explained to my valet that his watch is two hours off because we have left London. he refuses to move the hands. not once, not for the whole planet. his official position is that the sun is wrong.
beats.quote: “So much the worse for the sun, monsieur. The sun will be wrong, then!”

beats.title: Is This Rabbit, Sir
beats.modern: Bombay. station dinner. the landlord recommends his jungle rabbit. I asked whether the rabbit mewed when it was killed. he started swearing oaths. I told him not to swear, and to remember that cats were once sacred here. good times. for the cats. possibly for travellers too. then I finished the plate.
beats.quote: “And this rabbit did not mew when he was killed?”

beats.title: The Shoes In The Temple
beats.modern: sent him out for shirts. he went sightseeing instead, walked into a temple with his shoes on, got jumped by three priests, dropped two of them with his fists, and sprinted. arrives at the train with no hat, no shoes, no shirts. I said I hope this does not happen again. chat, it is going to cost us in about four days.

beats.title: The Railway Simply Stops
beats.modern: train halts in a forest. conductor: the railway is not finished. fifty miles of nothing between here and Allahabad. the papers announced the line was open; the papers were wrong. the general is shouting, my valet wants to fight the conductor. I have two days in hand and this is what they are for. nothing is lost.
beats.quote: “I mean to say that the train isn’t going on.”

beats.title: Two Thousand Pounds For An Elephant
beats.modern: there is exactly one vehicle in this village and it is an elephant. the owner won't rent. ten pounds an hour, no. twenty, no. forty, no. a thousand to buy him outright, no. twelve hundred. fifteen. eighteen. two thousand pounds and he takes it. my valet has gone completely white. the elephant's name is Kiouni and he is now mine.

beats.title: There Is A Widow In That Procession
beats.modern: a procession came through the trees and we hid in the thicket for it. drums, priests, a dead rajah carried on a litter, and behind him a young woman loaded with jewels, drugged senseless on hemp and opium, walking to the temple where she sleeps tonight. at dawn they burn her with him. the guide says everyone in Bundelcund knows she did not choose it.
beats.quote: “A suttee,” returned the general, “is a human sacrifice, but a voluntary one.

beats.title: Sometimes, When I Have The Time
beats.modern: I have twelve hours in hand. I am spending them on her. the general said, why, you are a man of heart. I said sometimes. when I have the time.
beats.quote: “Suppose we save this woman.”

beats.title: The Rajah Sits Up
beats.modern: we could not get through the wall. guards never slept. dawn came, they carried her out, laid her on the pyre beside the corpse, and lit it. I had a knife open and was about to run into the fire when THE DEAD RAJAH SAT UP. stood. picked up his wife. walked down through the smoke. a thousand people put their faces in the dirt. chat. it was my valet.

beats.title: A Thousand Pounds A Shoe
beats.modern: arrested in Calcutta. not for the rescue. for the temple, weeks ago, in a different city, and the evidence on the clerk's desk is his shoes. fifteen days for him, a week for me, and my steamer leaves at noon. so I put two thousand pounds on the desk as bail and we walked out. he wants the shoes back, obviously.
beats.quote: “Ah, these are pretty dear shoes!”

beats.title: It Is An Accident, Madam
beats.modern: valet never came back last night. this morning the Carnatic had already sailed, twelve hours early, without notice, and without him. I told madam it is an accident, nothing more. chat is spamming that the little man from the boat poured opium into him in a bar on the quay. I do not read chat.
beats.quote: “It is an accident, madam; nothing more.”

beats.title: Twenty Tons To Shanghai
beats.modern: no steamer for a week, so I am buying my own weather instead. pilot boat 43, twenty tons, hundred pounds a day and two hundred more if we make it: eight hundred miles to Shanghai in ninety-six hours, in November. I asked madam whether she would be afraid. she said not with you. we sail within the hour.
beats.quote: “Not with you, Mr. Fogg,”

beats.title: Glad It Is A Typhoon
beats.modern: the pilot came to me grey in the face and asked permission to speak freely. there is a squall coming. I asked which direction. south. so it is a typhoon and it is behind us. good. it will carry us forward. we spent the whole day being thrown north on one scrap of sail, twenty waves nearly took us, and she never once complained.
beats.quote: “Glad it’s a typhoon from the south, for it will carry us forward.”

beats.title: My Valet Has A Six Foot Nose
beats.modern: Yokohama. paid into a theatre to kill an hour. the finale is fifty acrobats stacked in a pyramid balanced on each other's noses. the base wobbles, one nose leaves the formation, the entire human monument comes down like a house of cards. and the man responsible clears the footlights, climbs into my gallery, and lands at my feet crying master. he boarded the steamer still wearing the wings.

beats.title: Justice Of The Peace
beats.modern: San Francisco. walked into a crowd. boots and canes in the air, revolvers going off, banners used as clubs. a red-bearded man swung at my head and the detective stepped in and took it in the face for me. we exchanged names. Colonel Stamp Proctor. afterwards I asked a porter what the riot was about. election of a justice of the peace.
beats.quote: “No, sir; of a justice of the peace.”

beats.title: One, And That Was Enough
beats.modern: Salt Lake City. as we pulled out a man came sprinting down the track, jumped the rear platform and collapsed into a seat. he was fleeing a domestic scene. my valet, who has been staring at this town all afternoon, asked him very politely how many wives he had. answer: one. and that was enough.
beats.quote: —“one, and that was enough!”

beats.title: Full Speed At The Broken Bridge
beats.modern: the bridge at Medicine Bow is falling apart, so the engineer's plan is to reverse a mile and hit it at a hundred miles an hour. my valet suggested we walk across first and let the empty train follow. they called him a coward for it. we crossed so fast nobody saw the bridge. it fell into the rapids behind us.

beats.title: I Play The Spade
beats.modern: mid rubber, a voice behind me says I should play a diamond. it is the colonel. he informs me I understand nothing about whist and reaches for my card. I played the spade. he wants satisfaction now, not in six months. next station, ten minutes, revolvers. I said very well, and sat back down to finish the hand.
beats.quote: “And who plays it,” replied Phileas Fogg coolly, throwing down the ten of spades.

beats.title: The Sioux Get On At Full Speed
beats.modern: the duel never happened. a hundred Sioux swung onto the moving train, clubbed the engineer, and opened the throttle wide by mistake. we are doing a hundred miles an hour with a fight in every carriage. madam is firing through a broken window like she was born to it. the conductor goes down shouting that we have five minutes. then my valet went out the door, under the cars, hand over hand along the chains, and unhooked the whole train from the engine. we stopped at the fort. counted heads. he was gone.
beats.quote: “Unless the train is stopped in five minutes, we are lost!”

beats.title: Living Or Dead
beats.modern: they have him and two others. the fort captain says he cannot risk fifty men for three. I told him I don't know whether he can, but he ought to. then I said I would go alone. thirty of his men stepped forward at once. this is the wager, chat. one day lost is the whole thing. I am not calculating.
beats.quote: “I don’t know whether you can, sir; but you ought to do so.”

beats.title: A Sledge With Sails
beats.modern: got him back alive. twenty hours behind, no train until evening, and the fix comes from the detective of all people: a sledge rigged like a sloop. mast, brigantine sail, jib, a rudder at the back. two hundred miles of frozen prairie to Omaha at forty miles an hour. nobody could speak, too cold. best travel of the entire trip.

beats.title: Now Money Failed
beats.modern: missed the Liverpool steamer by forty-five minutes. found a trading boat, the Henrietta, sailing for Bordeaux. asked to charter her, no. asked to buy her, no. money stopped working, chat. first time this whole lap. so I booked four passages to Bordeaux at two thousand dollars a head and told him we would be aboard at nine.
beats.quote: Up to this time money had smoothed away every obstacle. Now money failed.

beats.title: I Am In Command
beats.modern: day two, noon, I took the ship's position from the bridge myself. the captain is locked in his own cabin, screaming. I spent thirty hours buying his crew with banknotes and they came over in a body. the Henrietta is now pointed at Liverpool. also, and nobody asked: I know how to sail.

beats.title: Burn Her For Fuel
beats.modern: coal is gone. so I had the captain brought up on deck and offered to buy his ship. he called me a pirate. I explained that I would then have to burn her, at least the top half. he said she is worth fifty thousand dollars. I handed him sixty. we tore out the cabins, bunks, masts, railings and deck and fed the whole thing into the furnaces.
beats.quote: “Captain Fogg, you’ve got something of the Yankee about you.”

beats.title: Arrested On The Quay
beats.modern: Liverpool. twenty to twelve on the eightieth day, six hours from London, wager in hand. a hand lands on my shoulder. it is him. the little man who has been on every boat since Suez, who ate at my table, whose passage I paid. police detective. warrant with my name on it.
beats.quote: “I arrest you in the Queen’s name!”

beats.title: The Only Punch Of My Life
beats.modern: three hours on a bench in a customs cell with my watch on the table, watching the wager die. then the door opens and he is standing there, out of breath, hair everywhere: wrong man. they caught the real robber in Edinburgh three days ago. I am free. so I made the only quick movement of my life and put him on the floor.
beats.quote: “sir—forgive me—most—unfortunate resemblance—robber arrested three days ago—you are free!”

beats.title: Five Minutes Late
beats.modern: special train, hired locomotive, paid the driver whatever he wanted. every clock in London was striking ten minutes before nine as I stepped down. the club needed me at a quarter before. I went round the entire planet and finished five minutes late.

beats.title: Will You Have Me For Your Wife
beats.modern: told her I am ruined and offered her the little that is left. she asked what becomes of me. nothing, I said. no friends. no relatives left. she said misery shared by two can be borne. then she stood up, took my hand, and asked me to marry her. forty years of composure, chat. I said I love you.
beats.quote: “Mr. Fogg,” said Aouda, rising and seizing his hand, “do you wish at once a kinswoman and friend? Will you have me for your wife?”

beats.title: Here I Am, Gentlemen
beats.modern: fortieth second, nothing. fiftieth, nothing. fifty-fifth, the street outside starts roaring. fifty-seventh, the saloon door opens. the pendulum has not beaten sixty. here I am, gentlemen.
beats.quote: “Here I am, gentlemen!”

beats.title: Today Is Saturday
beats.modern: rewind ten minutes, because you deserve to know how. he came back from the clergyman with no hat and no breath and got it out eventually: the wedding cannot be tomorrow, because tomorrow is Sunday. today is Saturday. going east I crossed three hundred and sixty degrees at four minutes a degree and gained a whole day without noticing. then he dragged me out of the house by the collar.
beats.quote: “You have made a mistake of one day! We arrived twenty-four hours ahead of time; but there are only ten minutes left!”

beats.title: The Whole Point
