beats.modern: won twenty thousand, spent nineteen getting here, split the last thousand between my valet and the detective who arrested me. I did deduct the gas he left burning for nineteen hundred and twenty hours. for the sake of regularity. this morning he calculated we could have done it in seventy-eight days by skipping India. no doubt. and I would not have her. stream's over, chat.
beats.quote: “No doubt,” returned Mr. Fogg, “by not crossing India.

oedipus-king-of-thebes.title: Oedipus King of Thebes: Translated into English Rhyming Verse with Explanatory Notes
oedipus-king-of-thebes.author: Sophocles

beats.title: The City Is On My Lawn
beats.modern: chat the entire city is camped on my steps again. crops dead. herds dead. women dying in labour. a priest is out here telling me the ship is going down and I'm the only one who can steer. no pressure. I solved one riddle ten years ago and I have been the customer support line for Thebes ever since.

beats.title: Patch Notes From Delphi
beats.modern: Creon's back from the oracle with the fix. and the fix is vague as hell: there's an unclean thing living in Thebes, rotting the soil, and we have to cast it out. how? find whoever killed the last king and make them bleed. that's it. that's the whole ticket. no name, no suspect, no date. thanks, Apollo. very actionable.
beats.quote: An unclean thing there is, hid in our land, Eating the soil thereof:

beats.title: The Cold Case
beats.modern: so I ask the obvious question. your king got murdered on a public road and nobody investigated? and Creon goes: the Sphinx was here, we were dealing with more immediate problems. BUSY. a riddle monster showed up so the murder of your actual king slid straight to the bottom of the queue and stayed there for a decade. this city runs on vibes.

beats.title: The Curse I Wrote
beats.modern: going live with the curse. whoever did this: nobody speaks to him, nobody shelters him, nobody gives him water, no prayers when he dies. let his days rot the way his soul rots. AND, listen, if it turns out he's been living under my own roof this whole time, then every word of it lands on my head too. that's how sure I am.
beats.quote: even as his soul Is foul within him let his days be foul,

beats.title: The Prophet Won't Talk
beats.modern: I fly in the blind prophet, top of his field, and the first thing out of his mouth is 'knowing is a terrible thing when knowing helps nothing.' then he tries to LEAVE. sir. I paid for that trip. he says the darkness is his and mine. mine and HIS. what does that mean. he will not tell me what that means.
beats.quote: All without light!--And never light shall shine On this dark evil that is mine ... and thine.

beats.title: Thyself Art He
beats.modern: so I lose it and accuse HIM. you're blind so you didn't swing it, but you planned it, and if you had working eyes I'd say you did it alone. and he turns around, completely calm, no volume at all, and says: the man of blood you're hunting is you. ...he's lying. he has to be lying. he's mad because I yelled.
beats.quote: Thou seek'st this man of blood: Thyself art he.

beats.title: Red String Moment
beats.modern: got it, chat. Creon told me to summon the prophet. prophet accuses me. Creon takes the crown. that's not prophecy, that's a coup with extra steps. and while we're here: where was this all-seeing genius when the Sphinx was eating people? no bird signs. no flames. it took ME, no magic, no training, just a guy with a brain, to shut her up forever.

beats.title: Eyes Hast Thou
beats.modern: I called a blind man blind. mistake. he straightens up and says: you have eyes and you cannot see what you're doing, where you are, or WHO YOU ARE LIVING WITH. you don't even know who your parents are. then he tells me nobody in the history of falling has fallen as far as I'm about to. cool. great stream.
beats.quote: Eyes hast thou, but thy deeds thou canst not see Nor where thou art, nor what things dwell with thee.

beats.title: He Spoils The Ending
beats.modern: before he lets his kid lead him out he drops the entire ending in one breath. the killer is standing here right now. thinks he's a foreigner, turns out he's Theban. rich now, begging later. seeing now, blind later. brother AND father to his own children. and then he tells me to sit and think about that. sir. SIR.
beats.quote: Blind, who once had seeing eyes, Beggared, who once had riches, in strange guise,

beats.title: My Wife's Reassuring Story
beats.modern: my wife tells me to relax, prophets are frauds, and her evidence is UNHINGED. an oracle told Laïus his own son would kill him. so they took the newborn, drove iron through both his feet, and left him on a mountain to die. and Laïus got jumped by robbers at a crossroads anyway. see? she says. see how prophecy means nothing? chat. chat go back to the crossroads part.
beats.quote: Through both his feet A blade of iron they drove. Thus did we cheat Apollo of his will.

beats.title: Where The Three Roads Meet
beats.modern: I start asking questions I do not want the answers to. where did it happen. how long ago. what did he look like. and she says: tall, grey just coming in, built pretty much exactly like you. five men, one chariot, he rode alone. I'm doing arithmetic in my head live on stream and I need every number to come out wrong.

beats.title: The Guy At The Party
beats.modern: lore drop. years ago some drunk at a feast yells that I'm not my father's real son. my parents deny it, they beat the guy, but it never stopped itching. so I went to Delphi alone to ask. and the god didn't answer my question at all. he just said: you will lie with your mother, and you will kill your father. so I ran. picked a direction by the stars and never went home. that's why I'm in this city at all.
beats.quote: I must know My mother's body and beget thereon A race no mortal eye durst look upon, And spill in murder mine own father's blood.

beats.title: The Road Rage Incident
beats.modern: here's the part I never told anyone. walking in a daze, three roads meet. herald up front, old man in a chariot. his groom shoves me off the path so I hit him. then the old man waits until I'm level with him and cracks me on the skull with his goad. so I swung, and he went backwards off the cart in blood. and then I killed the rest of them too. all of them. one road, one bad minute, ten years ago.

beats.title: One Man Or A Band
beats.modern: my whole life now hangs on a plural. the one survivor said ROBBERS. a great band. if he sticks to that, I'm clean, because one man is not a band, that's just arithmetic. but if he says one lonely traveller on foot... then that's the finger of god coming down out of the sky and pointing at me. get the shepherd. get him now.

beats.title: Goodbye Before I Go
beats.modern: she's begging me to stop. drop it, don't ask, for the sake of your own life stop asking. and I think she's just scared I'll turn out to be some slave's son and embarrass her. so I tell her she can go be royal on her own. and she says goodbye. not see you inside. goodbye, this once, and never never more. then she walks in and shuts the door. and I keep asking questions.
beats.quote: O child of woe, I pray God, I pray God, thou never know!

beats.title: Fortune's Child
beats.modern: every face in this courtyard has gone grey and I'm up here going LET IT BREAK. I want the roots, however low they go. I'm not man's child, I'm Luck's child, the months raised me high and low like brothers. what's a birth record going to do to me? that's my lineage, nobody can take it. this is the most confident I have ever been. remember this exact moment.
beats.quote: I am Fortune's child, Not man's; her mother face hath ever smiled Above me,

beats.title: The Witness Won't Talk
beats.modern: the old shepherd arrives already terrified. can't recall. doesn't know. that was so long ago. begs me, says he's old, says please. so I have my men pull his arms back. yeah. I threatened to torture a frightened old man for a story, on stream, in front of everyone. and he breaks: fine, I gave the baby away. and then he says he wishes God had let him die today instead.

beats.title: I Solved The Case
beats.modern: the baby was Laïus's. the queen handed it to him herself and told him to destroy it, because of a prophecy that the child would kill his father. he felt sorry for it and passed it to a stranger instead. so. the old man at the crossroads was my father. the woman inside is my mother. I solved the case, chat. I did what nobody in this city could do for ten years and the answer is me. sky, put the lights out. I'm done being looked at.
beats.quote: Oh, on these eyes Shed light no more, ye everlasting skies That know my sin!

beats.title: She Was Hanging There
beats.modern: she ran for the old bedroom and the doors slammed. we could hear her in there talking to Laïus, dead twenty years, about that bed. then I came through with a sword screaming for her. the oak bar bent under me and gave. and she was hanging there. swinging. like a bird already dead.

beats.title: The Gold Pin
beats.modern: I loosed the knot and laid her on the floor. then I took the gold pin off her dress, the big flat one, and drove it down into my own eyes. and again. and again, like a song, until it was over. because these eyes watched all of it and understood none of it, and they were never going to see anything worth seeing again.
beats.quote: "Out! Out! Ye never more shall see Me nor the anguish nor the sins of me.

beats.title: All Of It Was Apollo
beats.modern: they keep asking who made me do it. Apollo did. all of it, the whole route, planned out and waiting for me years before I got there. but nobody held my wrist. he wrote it and I walked it and the hand was mine. and what did I want eyes for anyway, when there was nothing left in front of them worth looking at.
beats.quote: I knew not; I did but follow His way; but mine the hand And mine the anguish.

beats.title: Enforcing My Own Curse
beats.modern: I wrote the exile law myself. everyone heard me do it. so enforce it on me, right now, quick, before anyone has to look at my face. put me out on Kithairon, the mountain my parents picked as my grave when I was three days old. let them finish what they started. I've known for a while that nothing ordinary is allowed to kill me.

beats.title: My Two Girls
beats.modern: my daughters come in and I can't see them, I can only hear them crying. and I have to say it out loud: no one will marry you. you'll leave every festival early, in tears, before the dancing starts. your whole inheritance is my name. the only thing I've got left to hand you is this, and it isn't much: try to live an easier life than your father did.
beats.quote: Who shall dare wed you, whose heart rise above The peril, to take on him all the shame That cleaves to my name

beats.title: Count No Man Happy
beats.modern: and the old men close the stream out. look at him, they say. he read the riddle no one could read, he stood above every living man, people turned in the street to watch him pass. now look at him. so never call anybody's run a win until the run is finished and they're through it without pain. doors close. gg.
beats.quote: no man's life account as gain Ere the full tale be finished and the darkness find him without pain.

beats.title: Two Babies, One Day
beats.modern: born the same morning as the Prince of Wales. same city. England threw a week of bonfires and free wine for HIM. my family looked at me like a bill they couldn't pay. two babies, one face, and only one of us got a parade. keep that in your notes, chat.

beats.title: The Nightly Routine
beats.modern: come home with no coins and dad beats me. then grandma beats me AGAIN, harder, because she's the specialist. then in the middle of the night mom sneaks me a crust she starved herself to save, and when he catches her he beats her too. that's the routine. I thought everybody lived like this.

beats.title: Open The Gates
beats.modern: a kid put his face to the bars just to look at me and the guard threw him into the mud like garbage. that is my father's subject. OPEN THE GATES. bring him in. and watch that same crowd that laughed at him snatch their hats off the second I raise my voice.

beats.title: The Swap
beats.modern: we traded clothes for a laugh. we're standing at the mirror. chat. CHAT. same hair, same eyes, same face, same everything. strip us both and nobody in England could tell you which one is the Prince of Wales. and now that I'm in his rags I can see the bruise the guard put on his hand.
beats.quote: Doff thy rags, and don these splendours, lad!

beats.title: Beggar's Spawn
beats.modern: went out in the rags to go yell at that guard. he did not recognise me. he backhanded me into the road and called me beggar's spawn. I told him my person is sacred and he will hang for touching me. the whole street laughed. chat I am locked out of my own life.
beats.quote: “Take that, thou beggar’s spawn, for what thou got’st me from his Highness!”

beats.title: Ho, There, Lion
beats.modern: walked into the orphanage MY FATHER FUNDED and told them who I am. they knelt in a circle and did mock worship of my royal rags, and then somebody called for the dogs. the heir to the throne of England, beaten by hands and torn by dogs, in a charity yard my dad paid for.
beats.quote: Down on your marrow bones, all of ye, and do reverence to his kingly port and royal rags!”

beats.title: Claimed By A Drunk
beats.modern: a drunk just collared me in the rain, announced he's my father, and promised to find where the soft places in my bones are. I told him take me to the king and he'll be rich beyond his dreams. he decided I'm Bedlam mad and dragged me home anyway. chat, this is Tom's dad.
beats.quote: Take me to the king my father, and he will make thee rich beyond thy wildest dreams.

beats.title: The Prince Hath Gone Mad
beats.modern: he's been gone half an hour and I'm alone in a palace wearing his clothes. opened the door, eight servants bowed, I slammed it. a girl came in and I fell on my knees begging her to let me go home and she ran out in horror. the whisper is already down every corridor: the prince hath gone mad.

beats.title: Mad Or Sane, Still Shall He Reign
beats.modern: they walked me in front of Henry the Eighth. I told the most dangerous man in England that I'm a pauper born and begged him for my life. he took my face in his hands and decided his son has lost his mind. then he made it a hanging offence to mention it. mad or sane, I'm still getting crowned.
beats.quote: “He is mad; but he is my son, and England’s heir; and, mad or sane, still shall he reign!

beats.title: No Hereditary Scratcher
beats.modern: dinner comes with three hundred and eighty-four staff. one lord's entire inherited job is my napkin. then my nose started itching and NOBODY KNEW WHAT TO DO. there is no Hereditary Scratcher in all of English history. I cried at the table. then I scratched it myself. also I drank the finger bowl and said it lacked strength.
beats.quote: Alas! there was no Hereditary Scratcher.

beats.title: Someone Is Wearing My Life
beats.modern: dove through a forest of drunk legs and got loose. chat, the whole river is on fire with fireworks because the Prince of Wales is being feasted at Guildhall tonight. that is not me. some pauper took my window and ran with it. he gets a reasonable time to make his peace with God, and then hanged, drawn and quartered.

beats.title: One Guy Drew A Sword
beats.modern: I'm screaming at a mob that I am the Prince of Wales and getting nothing but spit, and one man steps out, puts his back to a wall and starts swinging a rapier at all of them for me. Miles Hendon. he does not believe one word I say. he defends me anyway. that's the difference between people.
beats.quote: thou might’st have a worser friend than Miles Hendon and yet not tire thy legs with seeking.

beats.title: The King Is Dead
beats.modern: a bugle cut the banquet dead and the messenger said the King is dead. then a thousand people dropped to their knees and stretched their hands toward ME. so I leaned over and asked: if I command a thing, does it just happen? he said your word is law. first thing I did with absolute power was cancel an execution.
beats.quote: “Then shall the king’s law be law of mercy, from this day, and never more be law of blood!

beats.title: He Asked For A Chair
beats.modern: told Miles to name his reward. anything inside my power. remember, he thinks I'm insane. so he goes off, thinks HARD about it, comes back, kneels, cites four hundred years of legal precedent, and asks that he and his heirs forever may SIT DOWN in the presence of the King of England. granted. his legs were tired.
beats.quote: that I and my heirs, for ever, may sit in the presence of the Majesty of England!”

beats.title: My Back Is My Bread
beats.modern: a boy came in and introduced himself as my whipping-boy. when the prince fails his Greek they can't hit the prince, so they hit HIM. that is his job. that is his family's income. he begged me not to quit studying, because his back is his bread. I made the office hereditary and promised to fail on purpose.
beats.quote: “My back is my bread, O my gracious liege! if it go idle, I starve.

beats.title: Boiled Alive
beats.modern: condemned man on his knees begging me for a favour, and the favour is not his life. he wants to be HANGED. because the sentence for poisoners in this country is boiled alive, lowered by rope, slowly, feet first. granted instantly, and the law dies with it. then I read his case and the whole conviction was a rumour, so he walked.
beats.quote: “O good my liege, not so! It is ordered that I be boiled alive!”

beats.title: Make Me A Storm
beats.modern: a woman and her nine-year-old, sentenced to hang for selling their souls and raising a storm by pulling their stockings off. the storm flattened her own house. so I pardoned her, told her she's untouchable, and then asked her to do it. live. nothing happened. shocking. if the power ever comes back, fetch me a storm.
beats.quote: “Exert thy power--I would see a storm!”

beats.title: An English Slave
beats.modern: a man at this fire just listed what my kingdom did to his family. mother burned as a witch for nursing a sick man who died. wife whipped through three towns until it killed her. children starved while he sat in the stocks. both ears cut off. branded and sold. an English slave. I stood up out of the straw. that law ends today.
beats.quote: An English slave!--that is he that stands before ye.

beats.title: Foo-foo The First
beats.modern: told a barn full of thieves that I am Edward, King of England. they crowned me with a TIN BASIN. robe, a torn blanket. sceptre, the tinker's soldering iron. throne, a barrel. new title, carried unanimously: Foo-foo the First, King of the Mooncalves. I offered these people nothing but a kindness and this is what they did with it.
beats.quote: “Long live Foo-foo the First, King of the Mooncalves!”

beats.title: The Thing In The Dark
beats.modern: something touched me in the pitch dark of this barn. twice. I decided I would rather find it than lie here waiting for it, so I put my hand out. hair. then a warm rope. chat the rope was a TAIL. it's a calf. I'm curled up against it under horse blankets and I have never slept better in Westminster.

beats.title: I Draw The Line At Kittens
beats.modern: the widow made me wash the dishes. fine. Alfred the Great watched the cakes, so I essay it. then apples. then grinding a knife. then carding wool for HOURS. then she handed me a basket of kittens to drown and chat, that is where the King of England draws the line. I walked out the back door with the basket.
beats.quote: “Alfred the Great watched the cakes; doubtless he would have washed the dishes too--therefore will I essay it.”

beats.title: The Archangel
beats.modern: found a hermit in the deep woods. holy man, hair shirt, candle, human skull on the box. very welcoming. then he leaned right into my face and whispered that he is an archangel, that I have just touched a hand shaken by Abraham, and that he would have been POPE if my father hadn't dissolved his monastery.
beats.quote: “I am an archangel!”

beats.title: Pray The Prayer For The Dying
beats.modern: woke up with my ankles tied, my wrists tied and my jaw bandaged shut. he did it so gently I slept through the whole thing. now the archangel is kneeling over the bed with the butcher knife he has been sharpening all night, asking the son of Henry the Eighth if he has prayed. I cannot make a sound.
beats.quote: “Son of Henry the Eighth, hast thou prayed?”

beats.title: King Of The Game-Cocks
beats.modern: Hugo stepped on my foot for the third time so I put him on the floor with a cudgel. what this gang forgot: I was trained in single-stick and every trick of swordsmanship by the first masters of Europe. fifteen minutes later he crawled off and they carried me around on their shoulders. Foo-foo is retired. I'm King of the Game-Cocks.

beats.title: Eightpence For A Life
beats.modern: framed for stealing a pig. the pig is worth three shillings eightpence, and anything over thirteenpence ha'penny is a hanging. so the judge quietly cleared the room and asked the woman if she'd like to revalue it. eightpence, she sobbed. then the constable followed her into the hall and bought the pig for eightpence, using the noose as leverage.
beats.quote: dost know that when one steals a thing above the value of thirteenpence ha’penny the law saith he shall hang for it?”

beats.title: I Know Him Not
beats.modern: we finally reach Miles's home and his younger brother looks at him like a stranger who wandered in. father dead. good brother dead. the girl Miles loved is married to this snake now, and Hugh brings her in to inspect him. she goes grey, looks him full in the face, and says I know him not. he sat down and covered his face.
beats.quote: “I know him not!”

beats.title: The Stake In The Yard
beats.modern: two women were chained near me in that cell and they were kind to me when I had nobody left. I woke up and they were gone and I thought, good, they're free. they were in the yard, tied to posts, with the faggots already stacked. their daughters came screaming through the gate and one caught fire holding her mother. I turned my face to the wall.
beats.quote: “That which I have seen, in that one little moment, will never go out from my memory,

beats.title: He Took My Lashes
beats.modern: they had Miles in the stocks and an egg burst on his face, so I ordered them to release my servant. the officer ordered me lashed instead. a king may take stripes but a king cannot beg. then Miles said let the child go, I'll take his, and took twelve on a bare back without one sound. I picked up the bloody scourge and made him an earl with it.
beats.quote: Let him go--I will take his lashes.”

beats.title: They Faded Out Of My Head
beats.modern: being honest with chat because nobody else will ever hear it. I stopped waiting for the real king. he turned into a ghost that only made me feel guilty, so I stopped thinking about him. then my mother and my sisters went the same way. I got scared they'd turn up in rags and kiss me in public. I trebled my servants instead.

beats.title: I Do Not Know You, Woman
beats.modern: riding through London and the entire country is screaming for me. then one face in the second row. she tears past the guards, grabs my leg, covers it with kisses, calls me her darling. a guard hurls her back into the crowd. and I hear my own mouth say I do not know you, woman. everything after that was just noise.
beats.quote: “I do not know you, woman!”

beats.title: Stop The Coronation
beats.modern: the Archbishop is holding the crown of England over his head, every noble in the abbey has a coronet raised and paused, and I walk up the middle aisle barefoot in rags and forbid it. hands go on me instantly. and then the boy in the cloth of gold stops the entire room to say HE is the King, and drops to his knees in front of me.
beats.quote: “I forbid you to set the crown of England upon that forfeited head.

beats.title: The Seal Hath No Place In It
beats.modern: then they ask the one question only the true prince could answer: where is the Great Seal. every lord in England watching. and I could not remember. it was gone. the court drifted away from me like I was plague. and then the pauper walked me back through that morning, detail by detail, until I saw it: the Milanese armour on the wall.
beats.quote: “I call the scene back--all of it--but the Seal hath no place in it.”

beats.title: To Crack Nuts With
beats.modern: so the King asks me, kindly, in front of the assembled nobility of England, what exactly I had been doing with the Great Seal of England for three weeks. chat I went red. I said it very quietly. to crack nuts with. the whole abbey came apart laughing, and after that nobody doubted I'd been living as their king.
beats.quote: “To crack nuts with!”

beats.title: He Sat Down
beats.modern: Miles walks into my throne room still in rags, works out that his little lunatic is the actual King of England, and then just fetches a chair and SITS DOWN in front of the entire court. hands go on him. touch him not, it is his right. he bought that right with a boon back when he thought I was mad. Earl of Kent.
beats.quote: “Touch him not, it is his right!”

beats.title: The King's Ward
beats.modern: the pauper who wore my crown ran my kingdom with mercy the whole time I was being whipped in my own streets. my Protector wanted him stripped and thrown in the Tower. no. he keeps the robes, he keeps the honour, nobody else may copy that dress, and his mother and sisters are cared for. title: the King's Ward.

beats.title: Justice And Retribution
beats.modern: went back for every one of them. the branded slave. the old lawyer with no ears left. the daughters of the two women who burned. the boy they were hanging over a stray hawk. the woman who took a yard of cloth. I was too late for the man who killed a deer. and I tell this whole story out loud for the rest of my life, on purpose, so the pity never dries up.

beats.title: New Server New Me
beats.modern: moved towns, chat. left behind everyone I love and I feel AMAZING, which is probably a red flag about me. also there's a girl back home whose heart I maybe wrecked by accident. was that my fault? did I encourage it? ...we're not doing that today. new rule starting now: I enjoy the present and the past stays buried.

beats.title: Touching Grass Literally
beats.modern: lay face down in the tall grass by the stream for an hour and felt the presence of God in a bug, chat. genuinely. I am the greatest artist alive right now and I physically cannot draw one line. every time I try to describe it my brain just browns out. that's the stream today. bugs and God.

beats.title: The Farmhand's Whole Heart
beats.modern: met a farmhand who works for a widow and is completely gone on her. older, treated badly by her first husband, says she'll never marry again, and he'd wait forever anyway. chat I have never heard a man talk about anyone like that. purest thing I've ever witnessed. clipping it. remember this guy.
beats.quote: I have never in my life witnessed or fancied or conceived the possibility of such intense devotion, such ardent affections, united with so much purity.

beats.title: The Bread Scene
beats.modern: showed up to collect a girl for a ball and there she is in white with pink ribbons, slicing a loaf for SIX children, portioned by age and appetite, every one of them shouting thank you with their hands out. chat. that's it. that's the exact frame my entire life stopped on.
beats.quote: She was holding a rye loaf in her hand, and was cutting slices for the little ones all around, in proportion to their age and appetite.

beats.title: The Waltz Vow
beats.modern: the aunt literally warned me in the carriage. engaged. don't lose your heart. filed under later. then we waltzed and chat I left my body. and somewhere around the third turn I privately swore that no woman I ever love will waltz with anyone but me, even if it sends me to hell. normal thought. mentally well.
beats.quote: Never did I dance more lightly. I felt myself more than mortal, holding this loveliest of creatures in my arms,

beats.title: Who Is Albert
beats.modern: some woman in the line points at her, waggles a finger, and says one name twice. ALBERT. so I ask. she says he's a worthy man she's engaged to. chat I ALREADY KNEW THIS. I was told in the carriage before I met her. and I still fumbled the steps so badly she had to grab me and physically shove me back into position.
beats.quote: "Albert is a worthy man, to whom I am engaged."

beats.title: One Word
beats.modern: storm passes, we're at the window, rain smell coming off the whole valley. she looks at the sky, then at me, eyes full, puts her hand on mine and says one word. a poet's name. that's the entire sentence. and I got the whole poem instantly. I bent over her hand and sobbed. ONE WORD, chat.
beats.quote: Divine Klopstock! why didst thou not see thy apotheosis in those eyes?

beats.title: The Bonnet
beats.modern: they were all laughing by the carriage and her eyes went round every single guy in that group and never once landed on me. I'm standing there seeing nothing but her. carriage drives off. and then the bonnet leans out the window and she turns back. at me? chat I will never know and I have decided to live inside that maybe permanently.
beats.quote: suddenly I saw Charlotte's bonnet leaning out of the window, and she turned to look back, was it at me?

beats.title: She Loves Me
beats.modern: reading her eyes like patch notes and the data is THERE, chat. she loves me. I respect myself more as a person purely because she loves me. and then she says his name with that warmth in her voice and I'm a soldier getting his rank read out and his sword taken off him in front of everyone.
beats.quote: That she loves me! How the idea exalts me in my own eyes!

beats.title: Her Song
beats.modern: there's one tune she plays. simple, nothing, barely anything. and on the nights I'm sitting there seriously working out how to end it, she plays that and the fog just lifts and I can breathe again. chat I am being kept alive by a piano. I'm fully aware of it. I have no plan for when she stops.
beats.quote: Sometimes, when I am ready to commit suicide, she sings that air;

beats.title: The Loadstone Mountain
beats.modern: every night I swear I'm not going tomorrow. every morning I find the reason. she needs an answer delivered in person. the weather's good. Walheim's only half a league from her door and I'm already in Walheim. my grandmother used to tell us about a magnet mountain that pulls every nail out of a passing ship until the crew drowns in loose planks. yeah. that.

beats.title: Albert Is Arrived
beats.modern: he's here. the fiance. and chat, he RULES. calm, decent, hasn't kissed her once in front of me out of respect for how I'm doing. I'm supposed to hate him and instead I like him, which is so much worse. lucky I missed the reunion. that would have ended me on the spot.
beats.quote: Fortunately I was not present at their meeting. It would have broken my heart!

beats.title: The Pistol Bit
beats.modern: borrowed Albert's pistols for a trip. he starts the whole story about why he keeps them unloaded, ramrod through a maid's thumb, surgeon's bill, and while he's mid-lecture I just put the barrel to my forehead. it's not loaded. it's a bit. he goes white and says he cannot comprehend how a man could be mad enough to shoot himself. hold that thought, chat.
beats.quote: With a sudden motion, I pointed the mouth of the pistol to my forehead, over the right eye.

beats.title: The Girl In The River
beats.modern: so I told Albert about the village girl who drowned herself. small life, one boy, everything she had riding on him, and he left. everyone says she should have waited, she'd have found someone else eventually. chat you don't stand over a man dying of fever and say he should have waited for his blood to calm. it's the same thing. it is exactly the same thing.
beats.quote: See here, Albert, the history of thousands; and tell me, is not this a case of physical infirmity?

beats.title: The Curtain Drops
beats.modern: something's flipped, chat. the exact same hills that used to feel like heaven now read as a machine eating itself. one walk kills a thousand insects. one step wrecks an ant city. every moment is chewing through the one before it. nature isn't a garden. it's a monster devouring its own children and I can't unsee it now.
beats.quote: Nature has formed nothing that does not consume itself, and every object near it:

beats.title: The Pink Ribbon
beats.modern: birthday package from Albert. inside: the pink ribbon she wore the first night I saw her, the one I kept asking for, plus the little pocket Homer I'd been wanting. they KNOW me. these two know exactly what I want and hand it over. kissed the ribbon a thousand times. later I climbed her pear tree and shook them down and she stood underneath catching them.
beats.quote: I kissed the ribbon a thousand times, and in every breath inhaled the remembrance of those happy and irrevocable days

beats.title: Adieu, Charlotte
beats.modern: last night before I go. moonlight, the three of us in the dark recess, and she asks whether the dead know each other again. I said yes. here and after. then I said adieu, maybe forever, and she smiled and said 'yes: tomorrow, I think.' TOMORROW. she has no idea. I watched her white dress disappear at the gate and put my arms out at nothing.
beats.quote: Adieu, Charlotte; adieu, Albert. We shall meet again."

beats.title: They Got Married
beats.modern: took a government post in another city to survive being away from her. thanks for the heads up on the wedding, Albert. really. I had a plan: the day it was fixed I'd take her portrait off my wall and bury it with my papers. you're married. it's still hanging. I hold second place in her heart and I intend to KEEP it. if she ever forgot me I'd lose my mind.
beats.quote: I hold the second place therein; and I intend to keep it.

beats.title: Thrown Out Of The Party
beats.modern: dined with the count, stayed into the evening, completely forgot that people of my rank aren't supposed to be in a room like that. the whispering started with the women, spread to the men, and eventually the count had to walk me to the window and tell me the company would rather I left. I smiled. bowed. got in a carriage and watched the sunset. by supper the whole town had it.
beats.quote: "I perceive the company is rather displeased at your being here.

beats.title: The Farmhand Again
beats.modern: quit the post, wandered, came back to her town, and found my farmhand on the road. remember the purest love I ever witnessed? he stopped eating, stopped sleeping, followed her upstairs one day, and when she said no he forced it. dismissed. shunned by everyone. she's marrying the new servant now. and he told me plainly he does not intend to survive that. chat, I read his story back and it is mine.
beats.quote: As she proved deaf to his entreaties, he had recourse to violence.

beats.title: The Canary
beats.modern: she's got a canary now. lets it kiss her on the mouth, then holds it out to me and its beak goes from her lips straight to mine. then she takes seed in her mouth and feeds it, smiling, all innocence. chat I had to turn my face away. she should not do this. she KNOWS how much I love her.
beats.quote: His little beak moved from her mouth to mine, and the delightful sensation seemed like the forerunner of the sweetest bliss.

beats.title: They Cut The Trees
beats.modern: THEY CUT DOWN THE WALNUT TREES. the ones we sat under. planted by the old vicar generations back. the new vicar's wife had them felled because the leaves made the yard dirty and boys threw stones for the nuts and the noise disturbed her READING. chat I would have fucking killed the man who swung first. the whole village is in revolt. I will never forgive it.
beats.quote: I could, in my wrath, have slain the monster who struck the first stroke.

beats.title: Ossian Over Homer
beats.modern: Homer's out. Ossian's in. traded sunlit islands and hot dinners for fog, dead heroes, gray hair, and girls dying on the tombs of their warriors. full personality patch, chat. I'm on the part where the bard knows the traveller will come looking for him and walk right over his grave and find nothing. yeah. that's the one I keep rereading.
beats.quote: Ossian has superseded Homer in my heart.

beats.title: Flowers In Winter
beats.modern: met a man out by the river hunting for flowers. in winter. says they're for his love, she's very rich, she has jewels and crowns. his mother comes to call him in for dinner and tells me he spent a whole year raving, chained in a madhouse. and the happy time he keeps talking about, the one he begs to get back to? that year. chat. that was the good part for him.
beats.quote: "he means the time when he was completely deranged, a time he never ceases to regret,

beats.title: Henry's Lore Drop
beats.modern: the flower guy. the one whose madness I said I envied. turns out he was secretary to Charlotte's father. he loved her, hid it, got found out, got dismissed, and it broke his brain. that's the entire road, chat, with a sign on it and a man standing at the end of it waving. Albert told me this like he was reading out the weather.
beats.quote: an unhappy passion for her which he cherished, concealed, and at length discovered, caused him to be dismissed from his situation. This made him mad.

beats.title: Stop Playing That Song
beats.modern: sat with her, her little sister dressing a doll on my lap, and I ended up staring at her wedding ring until my tears landed on it. so she played the song. that song. I paced the room until my chest went tight and then begged her to stop playing it. she looked at me and said, kindly, you are ill, your favourite food is disgusting to you now. I left.
beats.quote: "For Heaven's sake, play that air no longer!"

beats.title: The Body At The Door
beats.modern: a man's been murdered in Walheim. found dead at his own doorstep, the widow's new servant. armed peasants march the killer through the crowd and chat it's him. my farmhand. I get in front of him and ask what he's done and he says it completely calm: no one will marry her now, and she will marry no one. that threshold where the kids used to play is stained.
beats.quote: "No one will now marry her, and she will marry no one."

beats.title: You Cannot Be Saved
beats.modern: I tried. offered to defend him, wrote the whole speech out loud on the road, then asked the judge to just look away and let him run. rejected flat. Albert sided with the judge. I left furious and wrote one line down when I got home: you cannot be saved, unfortunate man. I see clearly that WE cannot be saved.
beats.quote: "You cannot be saved, unfortunate man! I see clearly that we cannot be saved!"

beats.title: Plunge
beats.modern: thaw came fast, the whole valley's underwater at midnight, moon silvering the black clouds, every field I know turned into one roaring lake. I stood over the torrent with my arms out and shouted PLUNGE. for one second it was the most beautiful idea I have ever had. then my feet went to stone. not my hour, chat. not yet.
beats.quote: For a moment my senses forsook me, in the intense delight of ending my sorrows and my sufferings by a plunge into that gulf!

beats.title: Not Before Christmas Eve
beats.modern: she's drawing the line. do not come here again before Christmas Eve, she says, for my own peace. then she takes my hand and tells me to be a man and get over an attachment to a woman who can only pity me. go take a trip. find someone who's actually free. come back and we'll all be friends. chat I told her that speech should be printed and handed out to teachers.
beats.quote: Be a man, and conquer an unhappy attachment toward a creature who can do nothing but pity you."

beats.title: One Of Us Three
beats.modern: wrote it this morning, calm, no drama, no poetry: I am going to die. by the time you read this the ground will be over me. and Charlotte, why shouldn't I say it out loud, one of us three has to die and it is going to be me. because I've had the other thought. about him. about you. that's exactly why it has to be me.
beats.quote: One of us three must die: it shall be Werther.

beats.title: Read To Me
beats.modern: she asked if I'd brought anything to read. said my own Ossian translation is in her drawer and she's been saving it because she wanted to hear me say it out loud. chat I picked up that manuscript and my hands were shaking before I opened it. star of descending night. three lines in and my eyes were already gone.
beats.quote: "Star of descending night! fair is thy light in the west!

beats.title: The Last Time
beats.modern: we got to the father who loses every child and we both broke at once. she's sobbing into her handkerchief, my head is on her arm, and then her warm cheek touched mine and the world just left. I kissed her. she pushed me off saying my name, twice weak, the third time steady. it is the last time, Werther. you will never see me again. door locked. I stood at it begging for one word. silence.
beats.quote: "It is the last time, Werther! You shall never see me any more!"

beats.title: Give Him The Pistols
beats.modern: sent a note over asking to borrow the pistols for a journey. chat, HE handed the note to her. told her, give him the pistols, and wish him a pleasant trip. she went half-faint, walked to the wall, took them down with a shaking hand, wiped the dust off them slowly, stalling, until his impatient look made her hurry. handed them to my servant. couldn't get a single word out.
beats.quote: "Give him the pistols. I wish him a pleasant journey,"

beats.title: Past Eleven O'Clock
beats.modern: all quiet, chat, and I'm calm. looked at the Great Bear one last time, my star, the one that was always over your door when I walked home. asked your father for the corner of the churchyard under the two lime trees. bury me in these clothes, don't search my pockets, the ribbon goes in the ground with me. they're loaded. clock's striking twelve. amen. farewell, farewell.
beats.quote: "They are loaded—the clock strikes twelve. I say amen.

beats.title: No Priest Attended
beats.modern: stream cuts here, chat. six in the morning the servant comes in with a candle and finds him on the floor by the window in full dress, still breathing. the ball went in over the right eye. Charlotte hears the bell ring and drops. he holds on until noon. the steward's eldest boy has to be pulled off the bed by force. buried that night at eleven under the lime trees, carried by labourers. Albert couldn't come. no priest attended.
beats.quote: At twelve o'clock Werther breathed his last.

beats.title: The Wrong Kid At Bright River
beats.modern: they ordered a boy from the orphanage and the shipment was me. stationmaster wanted to park me in the ladies' waiting room, chat. declined. outside has more scope for imagination. so I sat on a pile of shingles for half an hour building a backup plan involving sleeping in a wild cherry tree. and the old man they sent SIDLES PAST ME. doesn't look. bro I am the only human on this platform.
beats.quote: ‘There was more scope for imagination,’

beats.title: All My Worldly Goods
beats.modern: he tried to take my bag. I said no, everything I own is in here and it isn't heavy. chat that sentence did something to my chest on the way out. then I told him the truth at full speed: I've never belonged to anybody. not really. four months in an asylum, which is the worst, because there's no scope for imagination in there except the other orphans. and then I asked him if he'd ever imagined having dimples in his elbows.
beats.quote: I’ve never belonged to anybody--not really.

beats.title: The White Way Of Delight
beats.modern: we rounded a curve and there was half a mile of apple trees arched clean over the road, all white bloom, purple air underneath, sunset at the end like a rose window. chat I went SILENT. me. it is the first thing I have ever seen that my imagination could not improve. they call it "the Avenue." absolutely not. renaming it live: the White Way of Delight.
beats.quote: It’s the first thing I ever saw that couldn’t be improved upon by imagination.

beats.title: They Ordered A Boy
beats.modern: stood in their kitchen while they discussed me like a mis-delivered parcel and then it landed: they wanted a BOY. for the farm. chat I said it out loud, all of it — you don't want me because I'm not a boy, I might have expected it, nobody ever did want me — and then I burst into tears on their table. she said don't cry. sorry, no. this is the most tragical thing that has ever happened to me.
beats.quote: “You don’t want me because I’m not a boy! I might have expected it. Nobody ever did want me.

beats.title: Anne Spelled With An E
beats.modern: she asked my name. I said please call me Cordelia. she said is that your name. no. it is Anne. but chat if we're doing Anne then we are doing A-n-n-e. A-n-n looks dreadful. the E is the entire personality. I will trade away Cordelia for the E. that is the deal, take it.
beats.quote: A-n-n looks dreadful, but A-n-n-e looks so much more distinguished.

beats.title: The Depths Of Despair
beats.modern: they put supper in front of me and I physically cannot. I asked her plainly: can YOU eat when you are in the depths of despair? she said she has never been in the depths of despair. chat. she has never even TRIED to imagine being in the depths of despair. that explains this entire kitchen.
beats.quote: I’m in the depths of despair. Can you eat when you are in the depths of despair?”

beats.title: Bald Facts Only
beats.modern: she wanted facts, no imagining. fine. fever took my mother when I was three months old and my father four days after her. then the Thomases: four kids under me, drunk husband, and he died under a train. then the Hammonds: eight kids, twins THREE TIMES. then the asylum, who didn't want me either, they said they were overcrowded already. I'm eleven, chat. that's the save file.
beats.quote: They didn’t want me at the asylum, either; they said they were overcrowded as it was.

beats.title: The Barn Verdict
beats.modern: the ruling happened at the cow barn where I couldn't hear it. she told him she's never brought up a child, expects to make a terrible mess of it, will do her best anyway — and then: so far as I'm concerned, Matthew, she may stay. chat I'M STAYING. and she isn't even telling me tonight because she knows I wouldn't sleep a wink. correct. I would not have.
beats.quote: So far as I’m concerned, Matthew, she may stay.”

beats.title: Yours Respectfully, Anne Shirley
beats.modern: turns out I was supposed to have been praying this whole time. she made me kneel, which is strange, personally I'd go out into a big field and look up until I FELT a prayer. anyway I improvised live: thank you for the White Way of Delight and the Lake of Shining Waters. two asks — let me stay at Green Gables, and let me be good-looking when I grow up. signed it yours respectfully. apparently the correct outro is "amen." noted for next stream.
beats.quote: “Gracious heavenly Father, I thank Thee for the White Way of Delight and the Lake of Shining Waters and Bonny and the Snow Queen.

beats.title: I Hate You, Mrs. Lynde
beats.modern: the neighborhood watch came to inspect me and announced to the room that I'm terrible skinny and homely and my hair is red as CARROTS. so I crossed the kitchen in one bound and told her she is rude, impolite and unfeeling, and I hope I hurt her feelings, and I will never forgive her. NEVER. stamped my foot on every single one. this woman has raised ten children and nobody has ever done that to her. sent upstairs. chat, worth it.
beats.quote: “How dare you call me skinny and ugly? How dare you say I’m freckled and redheaded?

beats.title: The Apology Performance
beats.modern: ordered to apologize, so I did NOT half-send it. down on my knees, hands out, whole speech: I am a dreadfully wicked and ungrateful girl, I deserve to be cast out by respectable people forever. she forgave me in about nine seconds AND told me red hair sometimes darkens to auburn when you grow up. I came for punishment and left with a HOPE. Marilla noticed I was enjoying myself. I was.
beats.quote: I’m a dreadfully wicked and ungrateful girl, and I deserve to be punished and cast out by respectable people forever.

beats.title: The Bosom Friend Oath
beats.modern: secured a bosom friend, chat. Diana Barry. black hair, laughs before she talks. I made her join hands over a garden path we agreed to imagine was running water and swear it properly: faithful as long as the sun and moon shall endure. she said I'm a queer girl, she'd heard that already, and she believes she's going to like me real well. FRIEND ACQUIRED. permanently.
beats.quote: I solemnly swear to be faithful to my bosom friend, Diana Barry, as long as the sun and moon shall endure.

beats.title: Carrots
beats.modern: boy across the aisle wants my attention. can't get it. so he picks up my braid and stage-whispers CARROTS. CARROTS. chat I stood up and brought my slate down on his head and cracked it clean across — the slate, not the head. he tried to take the blame, didn't matter. master wrote my name on the blackboard with the E MISSING and made me stand under it all afternoon. I will never look at Gilbert Blythe again.
beats.quote: “Carrots! Carrots!”

beats.title: Three Tumblers Of Cordial
beats.modern: hosting solo, adults out, full house-keeping responsibilities on my mind. found the raspberry cordial on the top shelf and poured Diana a generous tumbler. she loved it. said it's nicer than Mrs. Lynde's, doesn't even taste like hers. she had a second. then, chat, at my own encouragement, a third. I didn't have any myself because of all the apples. remember that.
beats.quote: “The nicest I ever drank,”

beats.title: It Was Not Cordial
beats.modern: IT WAS NOT CORDIAL. the cordial was in the cellar. what I served my bosom friend three tumblers of was three-year-old currant wine. she went home dizzy, laughed silly at her mother, slept for hours, woke up with a head. now Mrs. Barry is telling the whole road that I set Diana drunk on purpose and I am never to play with her again. chat. I have been outplayed by a PANTRY.
beats.quote: “She says that I set Diana drunk Saturday and sent her home in a disgraceful condition.

beats.title: Croup At Three In The Morning
beats.modern: middle of the night, Minnie May can't breathe, both doctors out of town, parents away, and the girl minding the house has completely frozen. good news chat: I raised three sets of twins and every one of them had croup on a schedule. ipecac, hot water, flannel, all night. doctor finally rolls in at three and says I saved her life, it'd have been too late otherwise. I take back everything I said about Mrs. Hammond having twins.
beats.quote: I tell you she saved that baby’s life, for it would have been too late by the time I got there.

beats.title: Something Was In The Bed
beats.modern: we raced for the spare room bed in the dark, both of us, and landed on it at the exact same second. and then, chat, the bed said MERCIFUL GOODNESS. it was Diana's great-aunt. seventy years old. arrived early. we were out of that room before she finished the sentence and neither of us can explain how.
beats.quote: “Merciful goodness!”

beats.title: We Built The Haunted Wood
beats.modern: Diana and I got tired of everything around here being commonplace so we upgraded the spruce grove into the Haunted Wood. lore: a white lady who walks the brook wringing her hands before a death in the family, the ghost of a murdered child that lays cold fingers on your hand, a headless man on the path, skeletons in the boughs. we invented all of it in April. and now chat I will not go in there after dark. for anything.
beats.quote: A haunted wood is so very romantic, Marilla.

beats.title: The Liniment Cake
beats.modern: baked a layer cake specially for the minister's wife. she takes a bite and her face does something complicated and then she just... keeps eating it. KEEPS EATING IT. chat the vanilla bottle had anodyne liniment in it. rubbing liniment. in the cake. I had a cold so I couldn't smell a thing. I am upstairs on the bed refusing to be comforted and I will be here some time.
beats.quote: “Mercy on us, Anne, you’ve flavored that cake with Anodyne Liniment.

beats.title: The Ridgepole Dare
beats.modern: Josie Pye dared me to walk the ridgepole of a kitchen roof so obviously I climbed the ladder. willed my pearl bead ring to Diana on the way up, for the record. got several steps. then gravity. chat I fell off a roof, broke my ankle, fainted for real — and the first thing Marilla saw was me being carried up the slope in Mr. Barry's arms. that's the moment she found out how much she loves me. brutal way to learn it. let us look on the bright side.
beats.quote: “I shall walk that ridgepole, Diana, or perish in the attempt. If I am killed you are to have my pearl bead ring.”

beats.title: Puffed Sleeves
beats.modern: Matthew bought me a dress. brown gloria with the gloss of silk, frills, lace at the neck, and chat — PUFFED SLEEVES. two puffs. divided by shirring. with ribbon. this man who cannot speak to women walked into a store and did that for me, and then stood there going "well now, well now" because I was crying at a chair.
beats.quote: “Matthew, it’s perfectly exquisite. Oh, I can never thank you enough.

beats.title: Live Up To Those Sleeves
beats.modern: concert night. they call my name, a million eyes turn, and for one dreadful moment I am certain I cannot start at all. then I remembered the sleeves. chat I had to LIVE UP TO THOSE SLEEVES. voice came out from somewhere far away, hit every groan, old Mrs. Sloane wiped away actual tears. Diana confirms I groaned lovely.
beats.quote: I knew that I must live up to those sleeves, Diana.

beats.title: The Hair Is Green
beats.modern: bought hair dye off a peddler with my chicken money. warranted raven black, wouldn't wash off. used the ENTIRE bottle. chat it is green. dull bronzy green with streaks of the original red coming through for texture. I thought nothing on this earth could be worse than red hair and I was wrong by a factor of ten. and he was honest about one thing at least: it does not wash off.
beats.quote: “I thought nothing could be as bad as red hair. But now I know it’s ten times worse to have green hair.

beats.title: The Barge Springs A Leak
beats.modern: we're playing Elaine so I'm lying in a flat draped in black shawl, iris folded on my chest, dead and beautiful, drifting downstream to Camelot. then the barge starts LEAKING. big crack. oars left at the landing. chat I did not have time for a flowery prayer, I said dear God take the flat close to a pile and I'll do the rest, and then I climbed a bridge pile like a cat. the barge sank in midstream without me in it.
beats.quote: ‘Dear God, please take the flat close to a pile and I’ll do the rest,’

beats.title: I Shall Never Be Friends With You
beats.modern: guess who rows under the bridge while I am clinging to a slimy pile, soaked, holding a wet crepe scarf. Gilbert Blythe. pulls me into the boat. says he's sorry about the carrots thing, says my hair is awfully pretty now, asks if we can be friends. and chat, my heart did a strange little beat and then I said NO. never, and I don't want to be. he rowed off. I have made a mistake I'm going to be paying on for years.
beats.quote: “I shall never be friends with you, Gilbert Blythe; and I don’t want to be!”

beats.title: A Foeman Worthy Of My Steel
beats.modern: we're both in the Queen's class now and it is open war for first in class. he's a foeman worthy of my steel, chat, nobody else even tries to compete. he talks to every other girl in Avonlea and looks straight through me. and here's the part I'd delete if I could: the grudge is GONE. I forgave him ages ago without noticing. found out just in time for it to be too late.
beats.quote: He was a foeman worthy of her steel.

beats.title: The Pass List Is Out
beats.modern: three weeks of haunting the post office and then Diana comes FLYING over the log bridge with a newspaper. Entrance results. chat: I passed. first. tied with Gilbert and my name printed on top of a list of two hundred. my hands shook so badly I burned half a dozen matches lighting the lamp. that moment was worth living for.
beats.quote: “passed the very first--you and Gilbert both--you’re ties--but your name is first.

beats.title: We Are Rich
beats.modern: everyone in the buggy home is sighing about the diamonds those hotel ladies wore. chat. we ARE rich. we've got sixteen years apiece, we're happy as queens, and we've all got imaginations. you wouldn't trade into any of those women and you know it. I'm content to be Anne of Green Gables with my string of pearl beads — Matthew put as much love in those as ever went with anybody's jewels.
beats.quote: “I’m quite content to be Anne of Green Gables, with my string of pearl beads.

beats.title: Winner Of The Avery
beats.modern: results day at Queen's. I hid in the dressing room because I do not have the moral courage to read a board in front of people. then the hall starts roaring HURRAH FOR BLYTHE, MEDALIST and I take one clean hit of defeat straight to the chest — Matthew will be so sorry. and THEN somebody yells three cheers for Miss Shirley, winner of the Avery. chat that's four years of college. I have to write home this minute.
beats.quote: “Three cheers for Miss Shirley, winner of the Avery!”

beats.title: Rather Than A Dozen Boys
beats.modern: walking the cows home with Matthew at sunset and I finally said the thing I've carried since I was eleven: if I'd been the boy you sent for, I could actually help you now. and he patted my hand and said he'd rather have me than a dozen boys. mind you that, Anne. and it wasn't a boy took the Avery — my girl. my girl that I'm proud of. chat write that one down.
beats.quote: “Well now, I’d rather have you than a dozen boys, Anne,”

beats.title: The Folded Paper
beats.modern: he came in from the yard holding a folded newspaper, face gray and drawn, and he went down across the threshold before either of us could reach him. Mrs. Lynde listened at his heart and then just looked at us. the paper was the bank failing. every cent they had. doctor says it was instant. chat. he was at the gate with me yesterday.
beats.quote: “Child, yes, I’m afraid of it. Look at his face.

beats.title: Then The Tears Came
beats.modern: I couldn't cry all day. everyone else could and I just had the ache. then I woke in the dark and heard him saying my girl, my girl that I'm proud of, and it broke open. Marilla crept in and held me and told me she's been strict and harsh maybe, but she loves me as dear as if I were her own flesh and blood, and I've been her joy since the day I came. she has never once said it before. it took this.
beats.quote: I love you as dear as if you were my own flesh and blood

beats.title: I'm Not Going To Redmond
beats.modern: the specialist's terms for Marilla: no reading, no sewing, no crying, glasses on — or stone-blind in six months. the savings went down with the bank. then a man came up the lane asking to buy Green Gables. chat I've had the plan since the night she got home and I said it out loud today: I'm not taking the scholarship. I'm not going to Redmond. she is not staying in this house alone. I'll teach at Carmody and we keep the place.
beats.quote: But if I don’t he says I’ll certainly be stone-blind in six months.

beats.title: The Bend In The Road
beats.modern: when I left Queen's my future was a straight road and I could see the milestones going on for miles. now there's a bend in it. I don't know what's around the bend, chat, and I'm going to believe the best is. it has a fascination of its own, that bend. what green glory, what new landscapes, what curves and hills and valleys further on.
beats.quote: Now there is a bend in it. I don’t know what lies around the bend, but I’m going to believe that the best does.

beats.title: He Gave Me The School
beats.modern: found out why the Avonlea school came to me. the trustees had already promised it to Gilbert. the second he heard I'd applied he went to their meeting, withdrew his own application and told them to take mine. he's teaching at White Sands now, paying board out there, out of money he needs to put himself through college. chat he did that and never said a word to me about it.
beats.quote: he withdrew his application, and suggested that they accept yours.

beats.title: Five Years Of Lost Conversations
beats.modern: caught him on Barry's hill, scarlet in the face, and made myself hold out my hand and thank him. he asked if I'd really forgiven the old fault and chat — I forgave him that day at the pond landing, I just never told anybody, including myself. what a stubborn little goose. we stood at that gate half an hour. Marilla clocked it. we've got five years of lost conversations to catch up on. gg. God's in his heaven, all's right with the world.
beats.quote: “We haven’t been--we’ve been good enemies.

the-romance-of-tristan-and.title: The Romance of Tristan and Iseult
the-romance-of-tristan-and.author: Joseph Bédier

beats.title: The Child Of Sadness
beats.modern: lore drop before the stream even starts, chat. my dad rode off to a war and got killed in an ambush. my mom didn't scream, didn't cry, just stopped working. three days later she has me, holds me once, names me, and dies. she named me after how it felt. that's my whole name. she looked at a newborn and called it Sadness.
beats.quote: your name shall be called Tristan; that is the child of sadness.”

beats.title: Stolen By Merchants
beats.modern: Norwegian traders invite me aboard to look at the goods and then just sail away with me still on it. kidnapped, chat. except the sea starts throwing hands on my behalf for eight days straight until they're praying and begging and lowering me into a rowboat. wind drops instantly. the ocean got me out of a hostage situation and asked for nothing.

beats.title: The Stag Tutorial
beats.modern: wash up in a strange country, first thing I see is grown men about to hack a stag into four lumps like firewood. absolutely not. I get down and do it properly, every cut in order, then teach them how to ride home ranked by which piece you're carrying. chat I got hired at a castle for correcting strangers' technique unprompted.
beats.quote: Is it fitting to cut up so noble a beast like any farm-yard hog?

beats.title: Three Hundred Kids A Year
beats.modern: Ireland sends a giant to collect the tax and the tax is three hundred boys and three hundred girls. every baron in the hall suddenly finds something fascinating on the floor. so I kneel and take it. we row out to an island, one on one, and I kick my own boat off the sand so it drifts away. no exit for either of us.
beats.quote: “One of us only will go hence alive. One boat will serve.”

beats.title: Pay In Splinters
beats.modern: purple sail comes back and the whole beach screams his name. then they see who's standing on the prow. my sword's got a chunk missing, chat, and the chunk is in his skull. I told his men to take that piece home and call it the payment. what I did not clock: his niece pulled it out of his head and locked it in a box.
beats.quote: Take you that steel, my lords; it is the tribute of Cornwall.”

beats.title: The Wound That Cleared The Room
beats.modern: turns out the spear was poisoned. the wound smells so bad that everyone I have ever fought for leaves the room. three people stay. three. so I ask them to put me in a boat with no sail, no oar, no food, just my harp, and shove me out. if the sea wants to finish it, fine. if it wants to heal it, also fine. I just can't lie here rotting in front of people.
beats.quote: I would have the sea bear me far off alone, to what land no matter, so that it heal me of my wound.”

beats.title: Healed By The Enemy
beats.modern: seven days adrift playing harp to nobody. fishermen hear it over the water and haul me in. chat. CHAT. of all the harbours on earth the current picked the one harbour where the man I killed is lying in state, and the only healer alive who can fix me is his niece. she saves my life over forty days without ever learning my name. I ran the second I could walk.
beats.quote: She alone, being skilled in philtres, could save Tristan, but she alone wished him dead.

beats.title: The Hair Of Gold
beats.modern: the barons keep saying I bewitched my uncle to steal the crown, so they force him to marry. he's sitting there stuck when two swallows fight above his window and drop a single long gold hair. he holds it up and says: her. that one. no other. it's the most obvious dodge in history and the barons know it and glare at me. so I take the oath: I bring her back or I die trying.
beats.quote: “she whose hair this is; nor will I take another.”

beats.title: Dragon, Tongue, Ditch
beats.modern: bear head, coal eyes, lion claws, serpent tail. my lance shatters, my sword bounces off the hide, it breathes fire and my horse dies under me. so I go down its throat on foot and split the heart. then I cut out the tongue for proof, shove it in my boot, and the venom drops me face first in the grass. while I'm out cold, the guy I stopped on the road doubles back, saws off the head, and claims the reward.

beats.title: The Splinter Fits
beats.modern: she's drawing me a bath. she picks up my sword to polish it, being kind, and stops. there's a notch in the blade. chat she walks away, opens the box where she keeps the splinter she pulled out of her uncle's skull, and lays it in the gap. perfect fit. she comes back holding my own sword over me while I'm too weak to sit up.
beats.quote: “You are that Tristan of the Lyonesse, who killed the Morholt, my mother’s brother, and now you shall die in your turn.”

beats.title: Talking Under The Blade
beats.modern: so I argue. my life is yours twice over, I say. you healed me once, you found me in the marsh twice, kill me now and you'll spend forty years telling yourself you stabbed a wounded guest who fought a dragon for you. then I show her the gold thread in my coat where I sewed her hair. she puts the sword down. she kisses me for peace. neither of us knows what that starts.
beats.quote: See here, amid the threads of gold upon my coat your hair is sown: the threads are tarnished, but your bright hair still shines.”

beats.title: Won Her For Someone Else
beats.modern: I stand in front of all Ireland, show the tongue, offer the coward trial by combat, and he won't look at me. so she's mine by right of the kill. and then I say the words: I'm not keeping her. I won her for my uncle. I take an oath, out loud, in front of a hundred knights, to deliver her to him loyally. bookmark this clip, chat.

beats.title: I Found You Wine
beats.modern: wind dies, everyone goes ashore, it's just us and a little serving girl and it's hot. she goes looking for a drink and comes back thrilled: I found you wine! chat it was not wine. her mother brewed that for the wedding night. we drank the whole thing between us. Brangien walks in, sees our faces, throws the empty jug in the sea and starts screaming that we just drank our own deaths.
beats.quote: Now she had found not wine — but Passion and Joy most sharp, and Anguish without end, and Death.

beats.title: Well Then, Come Death
beats.modern: two days of not eating, not sleeping, walking past each other on a boat you can cross in nine steps. third day she calls me lord and I say don't, I'm your servant, and she says no. you're my master and I'm the slave, and I only found that out today. and Brangien is on the deck at our feet begging us to turn back and there is no turning back. so I said the only thing left.
beats.quote: “Well then, come Death.”

beats.title: The Wedding Night Swap
beats.modern: I walk her down the gangway and put her hand in my uncle's hand myself. he blesses the swallows. he blesses me. he blesses the ship. eighteen days later he marries her, and in the dark Brangien gets into that bed in her place, because the guilt is eating her alive and this is what she has to give. nobody noticed. chat, nobody ever noticed.

beats.title: Someone Is In The Tree
beats.modern: I'm dropping bark in the spring like always and the moonlight shows me a second face in the water. he's up the pine. with a bow. and she's already walking out to me. so we improvise: I stand there formal as a stranger, begging her to ask the King why he hates me, and she says how dare you call me out here, my husband would scatter my ashes. flawless. we never break. and up in the branches the man smiles, because he believes us.
beats.quote: “Queen, I would have you pray the King for me.”

beats.title: Four Farthings Of Flour
beats.modern: the dwarf buys flour, hides it in his coat, and scatters it across the floor between my bed and hers to catch footprints. I watch him do it. easy, I'll just jump the gap. what I forgot: a boar opened my leg that morning. I clear the flour clean and land bleeding. no prints, chat. just a trail of blood on her sheets, on the boards, and pressed into that flour like a signature.
beats.quote: “It is to mark my footsteps, but there shall be no marks to show.”

beats.title: The Chantry Leap
beats.modern: they're walking me to a fire made of thorns. no trial, no sentence, nothing. I ask to pray one last time in the little chapel on the cliff. I point out there's one door and every one of you has a drawn sword, so where exactly am I going. they let me in. I went out the window. the wind caught my cloak, a rock caught me. and then I'm running along the sand and I can still see the smoke coming off her fire.
beats.quote: There is but one door to the place, my lords, and each of you has his sword drawn.

beats.title: Worse Than The Fire
beats.modern: a hundred lepers come to watch her burn and their leader tells my uncle that fire is too quick, the ash blows away by evening, give her to us instead and she'll spend a whole life asking for death. and he thinks about it. and he says yes, that's better justice. she's screaming burn me, burn me instead, and the entire crowd is sobbing, and he hands her over anyway.
beats.quote: “Burn me! rather burn me!”

beats.title: Ambush On The Road
beats.modern: they drag her right past the bush I'm hiding in. I ride out and give the man one chance to let go. he throws off his cloak and calls for crutches in the air. singers will tell you I killed him. I didn't, I don't fight men like that. Gorvenal did it with an oak sapling. I cut the ropes off her wrists and we go into the deep wood, and by nightfall she's asleep on me, and honestly? we liked it there.

beats.title: Two Years Of Roots
beats.modern: we live like hunted animals. clothes in strips, faces gone white, eating whatever I can shoot. a hermit finds us and tells me there's a hundred marks of gold on my head and I should repent. repent of what, old man. you weren't on that boat. you don't know what was in the cup. I'd rather beg for the rest of my life with her than be king of anywhere without her.
beats.quote: I would rather beg my life long and live of roots and herbs with Iseult than, lacking her, be king of a wide kingdom.”

beats.title: The Sword Between Us
beats.modern: he found the hut. he came in alone with the sword out, ready, and we were asleep. but I'd laid my bare blade down between us the way you do, and he saw it and couldn't do it. so instead: he swaps his sword for mine, slides his ring onto her finger, and there's a sunbeam falling on her face so he plugs the gap with his glove so it won't wake her. then he leaves. that is so much worse than being killed, chat.
beats.quote: And still the sunbeam fell upon the white face of Iseult, and the King took his ermined gloves and put them up against the crevice whence it shone.

beats.title: A Dog For A Ring
beats.modern: so I gave her back. that's the deal, that's the writ, that's the ford. before we ride out she asks for my dog, so she has something that looks at her the way I do. I give her Toothold. she gives me a green jasper ring and says if you ever send anyone, send this, and no wall and no royal order on earth will stop me from coming. we kissed. then I handed her bridle to a king.
beats.quote: there is no power or royal ban that can prevent me from doing what you bid—wisdom or folly.”

beats.title: The Oath With A Loophole
beats.modern: they make her swear on holy relics and carry red hot iron, so I show up as a filthy pilgrim begging on the riverbank. she needs carrying to shore, picks me, and whispers: fall. so I fall, with her in my arms, in front of two kingdoms. then she strips off every jewel, walks out barefoot, and swears no man has ever held her but King Mark and that poor pilgrim. she carries the iron nine steps. opens her hands. not a mark on them.
beats.quote: I swear that no man has held me in his arms saving King Mark, my lord, and that poor pilgrim.

beats.title: The Bell That Deletes Pain
beats.modern: a duke had a fairy dog with a little bell, and anyone who hears it stops hurting. instantly. all of it, gone. so I killed a giant to win it and shipped it to her, because if one of us gets to not feel this it should be her. she works out what it is. and she leans out the window and throws it in the sea. said if he's still suffering then so am I.
beats.quote: Friend, while you suffer, so long will I suffer also.”

beats.title: I Married The Name
beats.modern: two years of no word from Cornwall. I fight a war in Brittany, win it, and the duke offers me his daughter. her name is Iseult. chat, her name is Iseult. I said yes to a name. that night my valet pulls my sleeve off and the green jasper ring hits the stone floor and rings, and I remember exactly who gave it to me and why. so I told my brand new wife I'd made a holy vow to spend the wedding nights praying. she said aw, that's a good vow.
beats.quote: I made a vow to Her that, should I ever wed, I would spend the first holy nights of my wedding in prayer and in silence.”

beats.title: Madness As A Strategy
beats.modern: new plan: be a fool. I shave my head into a bald cross, rub my face with herbs until the colour changes, trade clothes with a fisherman, cut a club off a hedge, and walk barefoot through the front gate of the castle that wants me dead. servants throw stones and I play along laughing. then I sit at the King's feet and he asks my name and I tell him the truth. Tristan. the whole hall laughed.
beats.quote: I will seem mad, but with a madness that shall be great wisdom.

beats.title: She Doesn't Know Me
beats.modern: I list everything. the harp, the poison, the dragon's tongue in my boot, the sword she held over my throat, the cup on the high seas. she calls me a drunk and tells them to throw me out. she looks straight at me and there is nothing there. so I say the ring. the jasper ring, the day we parted, I kept it and I've been asking it for advice. and then she knows. and she goes down.
beats.quote: “Heart, you should have broken of sorrow not to have known the man who has suffered so much for you.

beats.title: White Sail, Black Sail
beats.modern: poisoned spear, second time in my life, and this one is not healing. I send my brother in arms with the ring to fetch her, forty days, and I set the signal: coming back with her, run the white sail. coming back without her, black. and I don't know it yet, but my wife is on the other side of that wall with a maid keeping watch, hearing every single word.
beats.quote: if you bring Iseult, hoist the white sail; but if you bring her not, the black.

beats.title: She Kept Smiling
beats.modern: she heard all of it. that I married her for a name, that there's another woman, that the whole marriage was a vow I invented. and she doesn't scream. she waits for the door to open, comes in with food, feeds me by hand, kisses me on the mouth, and asks sweetly whether her brother will be back soon with someone who can heal me. and then she thinks about it all day. every day.

beats.title: Five Days Sideways
beats.modern: she's coming. she's so close the cliffs are in sight. and then the wind turns and hammers them backwards for five days, rigging snapping, the sky going black, the little boat torn off the stern so they can't even row in when it stops. she's screaming at heaven that all she wanted was one more conversation. that night she dreams she's holding a boar's head in her lap and it's bleeding all over her skirt, and she knows.
beats.quote: “God does not will that I should live to see him, my love, once—even one time more.

beats.title: What Colour Is The Sail
beats.modern: the wind comes back, the white sail goes up, all the way to the masthead so I'll see it from miles out. I'm too weak to reach the cliff now. my wife comes in and tells me a ship is coming and she knows it's her brother's. I ask her the only question I have left. what colour is the sail. she says she saw it plain and well. she says it's black. I turned to the wall. I said her name three times. on the fourth, I was gone.
beats.quote: “I cannot keep this life of mine any longer.”

beats.title: She Lands To Bells
beats.modern: the same wind that killed the lie drove her straight in. she steps off the ship into a town full of tolling bells and can't understand why everyone is crying, so she asks, and an old man tells her Tristan is dead and it's the worst thing that ever happened here. she walks up to the palace without a word. she tells the other wife to move: I have more right to this than you, I loved him more. then she lay down next to him and gave it up.
beats.quote: I have more right to mourn him than have you—believe me. I loved him more.”

beats.title: The Briar
beats.modern: my uncle crossed the sea for us. cut two coffins, chalcedony for her, beryl for me, sailed us home to Tintagel and built our tombs on opposite sides of the chapel. one night a briar came out of my grave, climbed the whole chapel, and rooted itself in hers. they cut it down. it grew back. three times they cut it, three times it came back stronger and in flower. and then the King said leave it.
beats.quote: Thrice did the peasants cut it down, but thrice it grew again as flowered and as strong.

beats.title: Nobody Lets Me In
beats.modern: day one out of nineteen years inside. I walk into the nicest place in town, I have MONEY, I show my papers like a good boy. dude takes one look, writes a note, sends a kid running to the cops. chat I haven't done anything yet. the paperwork does the crime for me now.

beats.title: The Bishop Sets Another Place
beats.modern: so I lead with it. name, sentence, all nineteen years, I am a convict, do NOT let me in. and this old priest doesn't even look up. set another place, he says. I say it AGAIN, louder, waving the yellow paper. he says put the good sheets on. chat I have been thrown out of a dog kennel this week. by the dog.
beats.quote: “you will put white sheets on the bed in the alcove.”

beats.title: Nineteen Years For A Loaf
beats.modern: lore drop, since chat keeps asking what I did. my sister had seven kids. no work that winter, no bread, literally none. I punched through a bakery window and grabbed one loaf. dropped it running. never even ate it. five years. that was the opening offer.

beats.title: The Escape Math
